description: How does it work? Makes the car shop lifts functional, removing the need for a car jack when the car is near the lift. There is no obvious effect besides the "car jack" item being removed from the list of "Required tools" on the "Vehicle Mechanics" window. Move the lift to your own car shop! Enabling the option to convert the vanilla tiles, you will be able to pick-up the world car lifts and place them on your own base. It requires a screwdriver and Electrical Level 3, and will result in four heavy parts. Be careful, it can break! Improve your chances with more Electrical level. (Mechanical or Metalworking requirements were not possible with how moveable tiles work.) Sandbox options - Range: The distance range from the vehicle where the car lift operates (radius from the driver door tile). - Require Power: Indicates if the car lift requires available power to operate, whether it is from hydro (world power) or a generator. - Convert to Movable Tiles: Convert vanilla tiles into moveable tiles. This process can be undone with the revert option. - Revert to Vanilla Tiles: Revert moveable car lift tiles into vanilla tiles. To succesfully revert, this option must be kept enabled until ALL tiles are reverted. Frequently Asked Questions - Can I install it to an existing save? - Yes, by default the mod just makes the existing lift tiles on the map functional. If you want to craft them, you will have less chances to find a magazine since the loot spawns at map discovery. - How do I learn the recipe? - Find and read the "Carzone Commodities: Car Lift" with Mechanics 4 and Metalworking 3, or learn the recipe automatically at Mechanics 6 and Metalworking 4. - How should I place the lift tiles? - The tiles must be placed in the form of a complete lift with the correct orientation, with both columns and center pieces. It doesn't matter how many center pieces to place, it could be 1 or 10 (for wide vehicles). - How can I pick lift? - You just pick the individual pieces as you would any furniture (if you meet the skill and tool requirements). To be able to pick vanilla car lifts (the ones that spawn at car shops), you need to enable the "Convert to Movable Tiles" Sandbox option. This will convert the vanilla tiles into the mod tiles (the same you can craft) as they are discovered. Be mindful, there is a chance to break the pieces that will decrease with better Mechanics level. - Why does my vehicle don't fit in the lift? - Some vanilla car lift on small repair shops have only 2 tiles without hitboxes, so the fit is TIGHT. Big repair shops' lifts are wider (3 tiles without hitboxes), and you can build your own custom width car lift. Some modded cars also are very tall, and collide with the top bars. description: Bandit creator Bandit Creator is an extension of the Bandits mod, allowing you to fully customize Bandits and their Clans. Want to decide how your future killer looks? Now you can! Accessible from main screen menu or in game using debug mode in single player. Compatibile with B42 version for single and multiplayer. Customization Options Here's what you can modify: Outfit – Clothing, jewelry and accessories for each body part. Physical appearance – skin tone, hair / beard style and color, makeup. Attributes: Health, Sight (affects weapon accuracy), Endurance (determines when they need to stop to catch their breath) Strength (affects melee combat, shoves, and barricade damage) Weapons – melee, primary, and secondary weapons, plus ammo count. Bag type – the contents are auto-generated based on their expertise. Bandit special skills (expertise) Clan spawn settings: Define AI behavior, spawn location, time frame, and group size. Problems After the game starts, some assets are loading in parallel for a short while. As a result if you open the Bandit Creator, it is possible that some of the clothing may be missing. Simply reload the creator again. Sometimes the creator may load longer than expected and freeze the game for 5-15 seconds. Just be patient Be mindful about screen resolution and font size. Creator adapts to resolution to a degree, but if the resolution is very low and font size is very big, you will experience problems. Bandit Expertise Each bandit can have up to three unique skills, called expertises. Some are not yet implemented and are marked accordingly: Assassin – Only approaches if unseen; can kill with one stab; silent. (Not implemented) Breaker – Breaks barricades/doors quickly; carries extra tools. Electrician – Sabotages generators and electrical devices; carries tools. Cook – Steals or sabotages crops; carries food. Goblin – Performs mischievous (but non-lethal) actions in your base. (Not implemented) Infected – Can bite the player like a zombie, with the same consequences. Mechanic – Sabotages cars and steals fuel; carries tools and a gas can. Medic – Heals themselves or allies; carries medical gear. (Not implemented) Recon – Moves faster than others. Thief – Specializes in stealing from the player. Repairman – Carries useful tools and supplies. Tracker – Tracks the player more easily; carries maps. Trapper – Plants bear traps. (Not implemented) Traitor – May pretend to be a friend. (Not implemented) Sacrificer – Explodes on death. (Not implemented) Zombiemaster – Attracts zombies to the player. (Not implemented) Mod integrations The mod comes with several pre-built clans and bandits using vanilla items. However, it also supports external mods that add new weapons and clothing. Just enable the mods, and Bandit Creator will let you use those items. Note: If you disable those mods later, affected bandits will spawn without their gear. Your configurations will remain intact unless you re-save them. Here is a nice set of mod integrations. How creations are stored The configuration files of bandit creations (and their clans) consist of two text files (bandits.txt and clans.txt) that are saved on your local computer. There are two different storage place types for these files, and you must decide which one to use for every individual bandit profile you create. Understanding this is crucial and while this may look complicated at first, it gives the necessary flexibility. Local storage This is a single storage that exists outside of mod folders. Every bandit created in local storage will not be impacted by future mod updates. This is the best storage for players who want to: create their bandits for single player games server admins who want to decide how bandits will look like for every players on that server. Local files reside in /Zomboid/Lua/bandits folder. If you are not a modder you may stop reading here. Mod storage This storage ties every bandit creation to a specific mod and puts its configuration files in that mod. You should only tie your creations to a mod that you own. Just like I tied default bandit creations to Bandits mod. If you edit this creations your changes will get overwritten when I update the mod on Steam. So the only situation when you would chose this storage is when you are the mod author who controls the updates. For example: You created a weapon or clothing mod and you also want to create some bandits using them. This way if someone uses Bandits and your mod they will get some new fresh bandits using items from your mod. You want to create an integration mod that only defines the bandits and sets the dependency to both Bandits mod and the mod providing with the clothing / weaponry. Files reside in /<modid>/common/bandits folder. You will be able to save to a mod only if if these folders exist in the mod folder and bandits.txt and clans.txt empty files are created in there. Configuration files from mods and local storage are loaded simultaneously and merged in memory. Local is loaded last. The merging process allows you even to have bandits from the same clan defined in different storages. So you don't need to make clans, you can just expand what there already is. If you like my work, be sure to give it a LIKE and Credits Ravense - art Workshop ID: 3469292499 Mod ID: BanditsCreator

description: Compatible with Project Zomboid Build 42.12.3 – 42.20.2 SP/MP Fast shortcuts for items, crafting recipes, and building projects The Shortcut adds a customizable shortcut bar for items, crafting recipes, and building projects. Add what you use most, then double-click to use, craft, or build instantly when requirements are met. You can also right-click a shortcut to jump directly to the relevant menu with the entry selected. Requires NeatUI Framework. Make sure NeatUI Framework loads before The Shortcut. Controls Default hotkey: TAB. Use the hotkey to show or hide the shortcut panel. Use the mouse wheel over the panel to switch pages. Hotkey, size, layout, position and transparency can be changed from the settings page. Main Features Shortcut pages for items, crafting recipes, and building projects. Double-click shortcuts for fast actions. Right-click shortcuts to open the relevant vanilla menu. Customizable rows, columns, slot size, transparency, position, and hotkey. Supports large layouts, up to 16x16 slots. Designed for the Build 42 crafting and building systems. Build 42.20+ config migration to ShortcutConfig.txt. Item Page Drag items from your inventory into shortcut slots. Double Click — quickly perform supported actions, such as drinking, eating, smoking, or reading. Right Click — open the item’s context menu. Crafting Page In the crafting interface, press the + button to add recipes to shortcut slots. Double Click — craft immediately if requirements are met. Green checkmark — the recipe can currently be crafted. Right Click — open the crafting panel and select the recipe. Mouse over — view basic recipe information. Building Page In the building interface, press the + button to add building projects to shortcut slots. Double Click — start building if requirements are met. Green checkmark — the project can currently be built. Red preview — shown when the project cannot currently be placed or built. Right Click — open the building panel and select the project. Mouse over — view basic project information. Settings You can customize rows, columns, slot size, widget position, panel transparency, slot transparency, hotkey, and reset settings. Build 42.20+ config note Starting with version 1.2.7, The Shortcut saves settings to: ShortcutConfig.txt Older versions used: ShortcutConfig.lua Old Lua config files are still read for migration, but TXT is now the current save file. Troubleshooting If settings do not save, slots reset, the panel returns to its default position, or only default slots appear, try this with Project Zomboid closed: Unsubscribe from The Shortcut. Wait until Steam fully removes the old Workshop download. Subscribe again. Verify game files in Steam: Project Zomboid > Properties > Installed Files > Verify integrity of game files Then reset the config files in: C:\Users<YourUser>\Zomboid\Lua Current file: ShortcutConfig.txt Old file, if present: ShortcutConfig.lua You can back up and delete both files to fully reset settings. If the issue continues, test a new save with only NeatUI Framework + The Shortcut. If it works there, add other mods back in small groups. Detailed bug reports should go here: Bug Report Please include PZ build, mod version, SP/MP mode, OS, console errors, mod list/load order, and reproduction steps. Compatibility Notes Compatible with Build 42.12.3 – 42.20.2. Requires NeatUI Framework. Make sure NeatUI Framework loads before The Shortcut. Works in single-player and multiplayer host testing. Does not add items, recipes, traits, map content, or permanent world data. Possible conflicts are more likely with mods that heavily modify crafting, building, inventory, or UI systems. Vanilla moodles Hiding the vanilla moodles on the right side is not a feature of The Shortcut. You can do that with Modern Status. The Shortcut and Modern Status are compatible. Performance / Gamepad Notes Very large layouts, such as 16x16, may have some FPS impact. If needed, use fewer slots or a smaller layout. Gamepad support is not currently implemented. The mod is mainly designed for mouse and keyboard. More Mods & Support If you enjoy this mod and your circumstances allow, it would be amazing if you could buy the original author a cup of coffee — but first and foremost, enjoy your game! Credits Original mod by Rocco: PZ Workshop Items Maintenance and compatibility updates for newer B42 builds by Afyrmo: PZ Workshop Items Workshop ID: 3470659758 Mod ID: TheShortcut

description: This Volume is now compatible with B42.20 Stable, single and multiplayer! FROCKIN SPLENDER PHASE 2 IS UNDERWAY!! Announcing: collaboration between the Frockin' Splendor! franchise and Tomb's Player Body! My mate Tomb just published a goth skin, makeup and hairstyle mod, which pairs perfectly with the Frockin' Splendor! franchise. Go check it out! Every piece of high quality, fishnet, nylon and lace accessories you will ever need to complete a gothic, punk or otherwise edgy and eye-catching look: bodysuits, leotards, tops & crop tops, boleros, shorts, skirts, leggings, gloves, corsets and stockings. At launch there are 113 different items, 1568 variants in total. All can be found in containers at reasonable places, and in "gift boxes". Use context menu options to adjust the appearance of the outfits. Certain items also have an alternative, ripped appearance, use context menu option to rip some holes. Naturally, you cannot un-rip them. A new tech has also allowed a structural system that defines fishnet and nylon as their own distinctive fabric types. You will be able to salvage them for scraps similar to the vanilla functions. Fishnet scraps can be recycled into threads, and nylon scraps can be disposed of to gain tailoring xp. This mod is the second part of a multi-stage project to improve and expand a certain B41 mod and bring it to B42. With all major branches being brought over to B42, this concludes most of the effort, and makes Volume 4 the final instalment in the mainline series. There will be an epilogue after this one to tie every volume and Shirts & Ties together with zombie outfits that utilises the combined varieties of the franchise, and bring over any leftover items. Currently there are at least 22 zombie outfit archetypes and 12 famous zombie outfits planned for the epilogue. Q: Is this mod save compatible? A: YES. Q: I can't find the stuff in containers! A: While the mod is save compatible, you will need to go to areas previously unexplored for the new items to start spawning in. A new tech has allowed this mod to place items in custom containers, or, "gift boxes", inside other containers such as wardrobes or crates. This way all Frockin Splendor! clothes can be found in reasonable quantities, while not crowding out the loot tables for vanilla and other modded items. These "gift boxes" have between 0.55% and 1.19% chance to spawn. Q: Why didn't you port the crafting system to B42? A: At the current stage B42 crafting is in a very unfinished state. There are placeholder codes and recipes and are clearly subject to change. It would be unwise to overhaul the old crafting recipes only to have to redo it when The Indie Stone inevitably changes things. Crafting will come later. With that being said, I have built a structural framework to define fishnet and nylon as separate fabric types, so you will be able to salvage the items for threads and xp. Q: Mod compatibility issues? A: All Frockin Splendor! mods are guaranteed to be compatible with each other. There should be no conflicts with other mods, to the best of knowledge. Please report any error you encounter in the BUG REPORT post. Q: What about character model mods? A: All but one clothing items do not have a separate mesh, meaning that they can be used with various character model mods without issue. Q: Can I use your mod in my mod pack? A: Ask for permission! Q: Can I translate your mod or port it back to B41? A: Feel free to do translation, and I'd be happy to incorporate them into the mod, but I kindly ask that back-ports are NOT to be made. Q: Will you port the new functions and items back to B41 yourself then? A: After Frockin' Splendor! Epilogue is published I will think about porting everything new back to B41. Naturally, this will make Kink It Up! Extra obsolete, so I will need to think about the logistics of things. If MP comes to B42 beforehand then there would be no need anyway. Liking the mod? Give it a rating to show your support! This mod is part of the Frockin' Splendor! Phase 1 Series. description: Welcome to my another small mod! I created this because I couldn’t find a properly working PDA on the Workshop — and because I wanted something meaningful to complement my Stalker Occupation mod. While the mod is still freshly "cooked," I plan to refine it further and add more complex features over time, especially if it gains some popularity. So stay tuned, rate it and spread the word to help support future updates! The PDA comes packed with several features, including: Fully custom 3D model that can be held or placed in the world. Well known authentic sound effects, from the STALKER series. Custom texture for a unique look. Current Implemented Features Players start with a PDA (fully configurable via sandbox options). Supports all functions of the vanilla walkie-talkie (requires the PDA to be equipped as the primary item). Map access through the PDA, while regular map access can be disabled completely by the sandbox option of the mod. Do not disable Allow World Map Option in vanilla Sandbox options! Numpad 0 shortcut for quick map access when vanilla map access is disabled and the player has a PDA in their inventory Draw, create symbols, write, and erase freely in all colors directly on the map via the PDA. Mini Map access through the PDA, while regular access can be disabled completely by the sandbox option of the mod. Do not disable Allow Mini Map Option in vanilla Sandbox options! Option to play an iconic track from the STALKER series - which one exactly, you’ll have to find out yourself! Caution: Playing it will attract the undead. Accurate weather forecast for the next day, including average daytime and nighttime temperatures, and warnings for extreme conditions (e.g., heavy rain, storm, blizzard, fog, tropical storm, and more). The PDA emits a soft glow when equipped, simulating the light of a real electronic display. Where to Find It? Whispers tell of these high-end military devices turning up around military zones. The army surplus store owner might have pulled some strings to get a few... or maybe he just got lucky. There are even rumors that some high rank officers at the Police Departments have been seen with one clipped to their belts. Keep your eyes open, survivor - with a bit of luck, you might just score one of these rare and valuable gadgets. More complex features are planned for future updates, especially if the mod gains popularity. description: This is a personal quality-of-life modpack: a collection of small, targeted tweaks that make everyday gameplay smoother without changing the core experience. This is a modpack. Please do not use other mods that overlap with features already included here. Most error reports I receive are caused by duplicate or overlapping mods being used alongside this pack. TwisTonFire QoL Modpack Choose a version below to view its complete feature overview: Standard Edition Rat Race Edition Compatibility This pack is designed to work smoothly alongside most mods and to avoid unnecessary overlap wherever possible. If certain inventory-related mods are detected, overlapping features from this pack will automatically stay disabled and be hidden from Mod Options. This includes features such as the inventory name header, container reordering, and inventory icon scaling. Important: if you are using mods that override the inventory UI, then my inventory changes are supposed to not load or appear. That is intentional behavior, not a bug. The goal is to prevent conflicts, broken layouts, and useless settings in Mod Options. Known examples include CleanUI, Reorder Containers, and Better Containers. Some settings are also intentionally limited to singleplayer. In multiplayer, options that have no real effect are hidden automatically, so you only see settings that are relevant to your current environment. Previously saved values are preserved. If you return to a compatible setup later, your earlier settings will still be there. My main Project Zomboid philosophy is to keep the game as original and authentic as possible. That said, I do want to improve small details where it makes sense. I do not intend to change the fundamental nature of Project Zomboid or turn it into something completely different from what the developers created. As mentioned, this is a Quality of Life modpack. It supports the vanilla game instead of completely changing it. It is meant to make everyday gameplay and usability feel smoother, while still staying true to the original Project Zomboid experience. Your support helps me keep going — thank you! Compatibility Workshop ID: 3480305875 Mod ID: twistresting Mod ID: twistqolrr

description: Constown, KY This mod adds the town of Constown to the standard map. This is a small town in Knox County, the center of which is pierced by a four-lane highway, which is the main source of income for local residents. Any traveler passing through the town can stay at our wonderful "Summer tree" motel. And if your car suddenly breaks down, there are two auto repair shops along the highway where you can inexpensively repair your vehicle. Unfortunately, time makes its own adjustments and small businesses are unable to compete with large entrepreneurs. Therefore, in Constown you can find restaurants and shops that have recently been the pearls of the city, closed forever. But despite the fact that now is not the most favorable period, Constown is a town where you want to stay. The town is divided into 4 areas: Commercial area along the highway. Residences divided into new houses of the same type and the old private sector. Trailer park. Farms. Town Location: Constown is located west of Rosewood on the main highway. Description: When I created this map, my goal was to make a town that would not stray from the style of vanilla towns. Each building was created by me personally, but with an eye on existing buildings in the game, so that the feeling of the integrity of the map is not lost. Some shops and restaurants have already been found in the game, while others were invented by me and this is my special pride. In Constown you will find unique elements of furniture, interior decor and simply elements of everyday life that you will not find in any other town in Knox County! And also on the walls you will find paintings by local artist Konstantin Ananas. description: A compact, lightweight weapon holding 20+1 rounds. Weighing only 400 grams unloaded it's easy to put it in a pocket (or ankle holster) and forget about it until it's needed. Just be aware of the slow reloading, as you insert rounds one-by-one through the breach into the internal magazine. My goal with weapon mods is to add weapons that fill a niche not readily available; In this case a gun you can use a non-primary weapon that won't take up much of your carry capacity, has a little bit more stopping power and easier handling than an M9 but a drawback that prevents it from being an overly-good primary gun. Credits Weapon design, reference images and main texture by KelTec arms. Parts of the texture are from Keltech PR57 by Brahian SG FAQ Does this mod work in B41? No, B42 only. Is this mod compatible with Rain's firearms? Yes, the PR-57 supports attachments from Rain's Firearms but does not require Rain's Firearms to work. Is this mod compatible with <other firearm mod>? The weapon is built using only vanilla features so probably. Can this mod be added to/removed from existing games? Yes, but when adding the gun will only show up as loot in new map areas. Are you going to add support for stripper clips? No, because that would require too much reworking of the reloading code because the base game doesn't support multiple reload options. I may revisit this once B42 firearms are more stable. Why does this gun use 5.56mm rounds instead of 5.7mm? Because I didn't want to add a whole new ammo type just for one gun. Both rounds use the same diameter bullet and look similar. Sure, a 5.56mm round has approximately four times more kinetic energy... but if "battery" can simultaneously be a AAA and a heavy duty lantern battery then a 5.56x45mm round works as a 5.7x28. (This mod also adjusts the weight of a 5.56mm round from 25 grams to a more accurate 10grams, otherwise the weight of the ammunition ends up higher than the weight of the gun!) Does it fit in an ankle holster? Yes; it can placed in normal holsters, shoulder holsters, ankle holsters and any modded attachment points that support HolsterSmall items. Is this weapon appropriate for 1993? The distinctive reloading system was developed in the 1920s, the PR-57 was developed in the 2020s, so on average this weapon is appropriate for any game set after 1970s. description: Compatible with Project Zomboid Build 42.10–42.20 — SP / MP Project Cook adds a dedicated cooking interface for Project Zomboid while keeping the underlying cooking rules as close to vanilla as possible. Its main focus is Base Cooking: evolved recipes where you start with a base item and add compatible ingredients or seasonings — soups, stews, salads, stir-fries, burgers, sandwiches, pasta-style meals, and more. Project Cook helps you choose valid base items, browse nearby ingredients, queue several additions, check cooking and nutrition information, and manage nearby cookers through a cleaner and more accessible UI. Required Mod & Load Order Project Cook requires [B42] NeatUI Framework. Recommended order: [B42] NeatUI Framework Project Cook Project Cook Pixel Icon Pack — optional The Pixel Icon Pack only replaces some Project Cook icons. If enabled, load it after Project Cook and restart the game after changing icon packs. Base Cooking Use this tab for vanilla-style evolved-recipe cooking. You can: choose or automatically detect a valid base item browse compatible ingredients and seasonings from your inventory and nearby containers double-click an ingredient or use + to queue several additions right-click ingredient stacks to choose a specific item when several are available fill supported containers from nearby water sources empty supported recipe containers and recover the empty container rename finished foods view recipe rating information when available Project Cook follows vanilla evolved-recipe rules for ingredient use, Cooking-skill modifiers, frozen ingredients, burnt food, rotten food, seasoning limits, and maximum ingredient counts. Partially-used and full items in the same ingredient stack are tracked separately so repeated additions can continue across the available items instead of getting stuck on one fragment. Ingredients, Seasonings & Nutrition ingredients and seasonings are handled separately each base item keeps its vanilla ingredient limit each seasoning type can only be added once unusable burnt/frozen/rotten ingredients cannot be queued frozen or rotten ingredients remain usable whenever the vanilla recipe/skill rules allow them Nutrition information is revealed progressively: Cooking 2: categories become readable Cooking 4: rough values Cooking 6: closer estimates Cooking 8: exact values Nutritionist: full nutrition details and nutrition sorting Cooker — WIP The Cooker tab can manage nearby ovens, microwaves, gas/charcoal barbecues, fireplaces, campfires, and other supported cookers. Depending on the cooker, you may be able to turn it on/off, adjust supported settings, add fuel, insert/remove propane tanks, move food into the cooker, return food to its previous container, and browse nearby food through All Containers. This tab is usable but still being improved. You can always use the normal inventory/loot interface instead. Cooking By Recipes — WIP This tab is for normal crafting-style cooking recipes. Some cooking actions belong to Project Zomboid's regular Crafting system rather than evolved recipes. For those, you can also use vanilla Crafting or Neat Crafting, then continue in Base Cooking if the result supports evolved-recipe ingredients. Project Cook 1.3.2 Recent fixes include: better repeated additions from ingredient stacks and partially-used food ingredient consumption and queue handling closer to vanilla evolved-recipe behavior correct handling of unusable burnt/frozen/rotten ingredients fixed ingredient transfers from nearby containers improved MP handling for fully-consumed seasonings fewer repeated inventory scans for better performance fixed Project Cook being marked with [ERRORS] in the in-game loaded-mod list Compatibility Project Cook mainly uses vanilla cooking, crafting, inventory, and evolved-recipe systems. Mods that register ingredients through vanilla evolved recipes should normally be detected automatically. Mods that add normal craft recipes can work alongside Project Cook, but those recipes may belong in Crafting / Cooking By Recipes instead of Base Cooking. For inventory-overhaul compatibility reports, please provide the exact mod/fork and Workshop ID. description: This mod adds a variety of weapons that don't align with the era's setting. If you value realism, please consider carefully before subscribing to this mod. Current total number of weapons : 79 Mod Overview This mod is inspired by my childhood obsession: the mobile shooter Crisis Action, first released in 2014 and still active today, now approaching its 10th anniversary. B42 weapons were notably underpowered in the original version, so their damage has been significantly buffed. B41 weapons largely retain the original stats. Note: The B41 version of this mod contains multiple unresolved issues. Since this version is nearing deprecation, I'm not planning further fixes — even though B42's stable multiplayer release may still take a while. For the best experience, it's recommended to pair with the Ammo Maker mod. (Only B42) Gameplay Mechanics - Firearms You can acquire modded firearms from diverse locations — police stations, gun shops, survivors, and even school lockers. Once obtained, firearms can be upgraded using Upgrade Points. Each weapon has its own upgrade cap and unique attribute bonuses. Some firearms, when dismantled, yield Weapon Fragments, which can be used to enhance matching weapons or be broken down into Upgrade Points. - Melee Weapons Melee weapons can be found in tool shops, warehouses, garages, and similar locations. Unlike firearms, most melee weapons cannot be upgraded — they are already at max level upon acquisition. Their stats closely mimic the original game's values. - Weapon Enhancement Upgrade Points are required to strengthen weapons. You can acquire them by dismantling firearms, melee weapons, weapon parts, or fragments. Additionally, some weapons (firearm or melee) require specific Weapon Fragments to be eligible for upgrading. - Weapon Fragments These can also be acquired randomly from loot boxes or zombie drops. Weapon Fragments can themselves be dismantled into Upgrade Points if needed. - Weapon Parts Attachable to firearms, these parts grant specific attribute enhancements — such as increased fire rate or slight weight reduction. - Weapon Codex The Weapon Codex is the most important item in this mod. It can be obtained from gun shop magazine racks, bookshelves — or occasionally from general bookstores. Only after acquiring this codex does gameplay officially begin. The left panel of the codex displays weapon series; collecting all weapons in a series yields rewards. When you open a weapon's detailed view (with the 3D model), weapons marked with a check are collectible targets. Right-clicking a marked weapon allows you to "Register in Codex" — some firearms only become registerable after being upgraded. Available Translations: • English • Traditional Chinese • Simplified Chinese ❗Known Issues - Stuttering when right-clicking enhancement points is caused by vanilla code for recipe lookups; items with more applicable recipes cause more lag. Expecting official optimization for this part. FAQ Q: Is this mod compatible with other firearm mods? A: I'm not certain; no tests have been conducted yet, but it should theoretically be compatible. I'll update this FAQ as soon as I confirm. Q: Can I enable this mod in an existing save file? A: Yes — but items will not respawn in areas that have already been explored. You'll need to venture into new zones for mod items to spawn. Q: What should I do if an error occurs? description: Find the Perfect Fit! Adds clothing sizes to Project Zomboid for a deeper and more realistic looting experience. High tailoring skill lets you adjust clothes to your own body size. 1. Size System Clothing now comes in 6 sizes: XS, S, M, L, XL, XXL. Each size corresponds to a weight class: Emaciated, Very Underweight, Underweight, Normal, Overweight, Obese. Not all clothing have size, but if you find an item that should have size but doesn't, comment below and I'll consider it. Your current size appears on the Character screen, next to your weight. Size distribution: Penalties for ill-fitting clothing: Tight clothes take longer to wear and might be impossible to equip. Tight clothes cause muscle soreness and slow post-exercise recovery. Tight clothes have a higher chance of tearing when climbing fences or windows. Tight pants and skirts cause stiffness in legs while running and sprinting Loose clothes reduce insulation and combat speed. Loose clothes increases the chance that you can trip after climbing fences Loose pants/skirts may fall off if not secured with a belt. 2. Check Size You can inspect clothes to see their size. With low tailoring skill, you get a rough estimate: tight, loose, or perfect fit. With high tailoring skill, you see the exact size. Successful checks reward a small amount of tailoring XP. 3. Resize Clothes With enough tailoring skill, you can resize clothes up or down by 1 size. Requires proper tools and materials, and only some clothes can be resized. Resize result: Failure: clothing may lose condition. Success: clothing may gain a bit of condition. Success always grants tailoring XP. 4. Condition Decreases Over Time Clothing will slowly lose condition over time. Wet, dirty and bloody clothes will degrade faster. Clothes with high wind resistance and water resistance can last longer. Higher maintenance and tailoring help reduce the degrading rate. You can increase condition by reconditioning them, similar to repairing weapons. Some clothes can be reconditioned using just strips, for others, you will need a spare one. Reconditioning mechanics: Success chance and durability restored increase with Tailoring and Maintenance levels. Failure can reduce condition. Each recondition attempt lowers future success rate and amount restored. 5. Clothes crafting (B42 only) B42 introduces some clothing items which can be crafted. You can choose sizes of the output items in the crafting window beforehand (by clicking on the size tag). Notes This mod is based on Size Labels, with more added features. Most features can be customized via sandbox settings. Compatible with multiplayer and existing saves. Should be compatible with all clothing mods. Just remember, not all clothes have size. Smart Radial Menu A smart radial menu for quick access to common item actions. Supports controllers and the Steam Deck. Also supports split-screen, displaying a radial menu for each player. B42 Stable Only If you are still playing the Unstable version of the game, please use this instead: Smart Radial Menu [B42.19/Unstable]. That version will stay as is and will not be updated. Features Dynamic Radial Menu: Scans inventory and proximities, displaying the following relevant options: eating, drinking, smoking, using meds, reading, setting alarms, researching and crafting. Controller Support: Designed for mouse + keyboard, gamepad, and Steam Deck navigation. Item Filtering: Excludes spoiled, hazardous, and poisonous items (if known to the player), as well as literature already read and skill books you cannot read yet. Tainted water and food is optional. Learning Craft Recipes: Displays recipes that can be researched from items. Evolved Recipes Support: Craft advanced cooking recipes directly from the menu. Clothing Actions: Adds actions to wear, unequip, and inspect clothes, as well as the item's extra actions if available. Crafting: Adds recipes you can craft from your inventory and nearby containers. Weapons: Adds options to equip, attach, reload, load/unload magazines, change fire mode, and repair weapons. Submenus for ingredients, maps and equipped clothes: Added submenus to separate spices from other food, maps from other literature, and the currently equipped clothes from the rest. Integration: Safe to add and remove from existing saves. Localization: Translated for multiple languages. Menu Navigation *Keybind is customizable Minimum Recommended Settings Item stacking and use Consumable items are grouped and consumed from least to most uses, nutrition, or liquid amount. Evolved recipes use the opposite order, helping prioritize ingredients that need using. Floor fluid containers can be drunk directly, as in vanilla. Large containers such as buckets cannot be drunk from directly in inventory, like in vanilla. Skill Books, magazines, schematics and recipes are prioritized over other literature. Clothing is sorted head-to-toe, prioritizing better condition and more uses where applicable. Renamed bags are also prioritized. Inventory items appear first, clockwise from the top. Unwanted and unreachable items appear last, behind frozen items, except equipped clothing, which remains head-to-toe, and in other menus like crafting and weapons. Crafting items prioritize inventory items, then sort alphabetically. The worst condition item is selected first, then uses remaining; filters, tanks and batteries use the opposite order. Batch crafting is supported when allowed by vanilla. The Weapons slice expands vanilla weapon handling with equip, upgrade, attachments, ammo and weapons from other containers. Root-inventory weapons get their own slice like in vanilla, and the flashlight follows vanilla selection. Update 2.1 Added a Weapons Slice. Added an option to display this menu before or after vanilla radial menus (useful if vanilla menus get in the way often). Added the functionality to rip all clothes (optional). Added a wring out all wet clothes functionality (optional). Added option to load/unload all magazines (optional). Added Sandbox Options to disable these 3 functionalities. Added colors to tooltips. Added experience gained from evolved recipes to the tooltip. Added status icons when about to eat or drink frozen or known poisoned items. Added compatibility with Better Sorting B42 and Better Sorting Reborn. Improved efficiency for large inventories even more. If you are having missing file errors try resubscribing. Fixed minor bugs. Mod compatibility TidyUp Meister Drink Smart Eat Smart organizedCategories: Core Extended categories (B42) Better Sorting Better Sorting Reborn No additional compatibilities are currently planned. Known bugs This is my biggest mod project to date, so bugs may be expected. Extra mouse buttons on gaming mice can't be used to hold the menu open due to how the game code works, but it works in toggle mode. When items are marked as favorite, some recipes will be unavailable. This is a vanilla limitation. 'Insert battery' has an option that can insert multiple batteries into a flashlight and waste extras. This is a vanilla bug, just avoid it. The Weapon Slice is the last biggest addition and may have bugs. Please report them if you find any. Please use the 'Bug Reports' discussion to report and paste error logs. This mod is not and will never be a replacement for the right-click menu or tile interaction. If you can and would like to support me by buying me a coffee, I'd greatly appreciate it - but most of all, I hope you enjoy the mod! Workshop ID: 3494108029 Mod ID: SmartRadialMenu

description: Ever felt like vitamins in Project Zomboid just aren’t worth the stash space anymore? Yeah - me too. Back in Build 41, they had 10 uses and gave a reliable -2 fatigue, which made them almost useless. But in Build 42, the system changed. Vitamins were reworked into caffeine pills and while that’s a cool direction, they still feel too limited, too rigid and still not quite worth carrying around. Since I couldn’t find a mod that offered the flexibility I wanted, I built Hephas Vitamins. A lightweight, customizable mod that puts the power back in your hands, with tweakable effects, optional healing and some extra flavor if you want it. Whether you're a survival purist looking to fine-tune fatigue recovery, or just want vitamins to feel useful again, this mod has you covered. Thanks for checking it out! And if you like what I’m doing, feel free to take a peek at my other mods too! Fully customizable vitamin effects through sandbox settings Delta Usage – Set how many uses each vitamin(coffeine) bottle has Fatigue Reduction – Adjust how much fatigue is restored Stress Change – Adjust stress increase for each vitamin (coffeine) use Healing Chance & Amount – Optional bonus healing effects Custom Quotes Toggle – Turn off the vitamin sayings if they’re not your vibe Optional Healing Support A fun little bonus feature (added by a request) that gives vitamins (coffeine pills) a chance to restore health. Custom Flavor Quotes to bring a little more personality to pill-popping Your character will occasionally comment when pills work their magic, but only when healing is triggered, so you won't get spammed with quotes every time you pop one. Non-Invasive Implementation No full vanilla item overrides via hardcode. That means better compatibility with other mods. More complex features and additional add-ons for other pills may follow later down the road if the mod gains popularity. And if you have any suggestions for new vitamin sayings or ways to improve the mod, feel free to share them in the suggestion thread! The vehicle system also has a point: find a wreck, work out what is broken, bring it back. This mod already leans on it plenty. Tools About The code is free to take. This mod gets the hours left over, which some weeks is a few and other weeks is none. Fixes and features do come, just not on your schedule. It's simple, but it's honest work. description: Looted the 14th pipe wrench because you forgot you already had 13? Didn't take that sledgehammer because you already had one but now you realized that was on your previous character? This mod allows you to designate zones in your home(s) or base(s). A list of all items in those zones will be displayed in the new Home Inventory tab, available in the Character Info panel (Health screen). Safe to add/remove mid campaign; doesn't overwrite any game files. Update 1.8.0: Zones can have their colors customized. Players can choose between a floating window (inspired by Home Inventory Improved), or the current tab embedded in the Character Info panel. For more/other features, check out Sam's improved version here (unfortunately, outdated, but might work). Description The Home Inventory mod allows the player to create and manage custom zones: "home" zones; similar to how the Animal system works in B42. The items inside home zones are fetched and saved, and can be seen as a list in a new tab called "Home Inventory" located in the Character Info panel (the heart icon). Home zones can cover multiple bases, and can also cover different areas of each base. It's up to you to decide how you will organize your bases and the items inside them. The list of items is only fetched when you add or remove zones, or when you click the "Home Inventory" tab, so the mod has virtually no effect on performance. If you are too far from a zone, their tiles will not be loaded, and the game will think your items don't exist. To prevent this, the mod saves the items of each zone to a cache, so you can keep checking your home inventory while you are away. Examples *New!* Hover over items to see how many you have in your own zones without having to open the panel: Double-click on an item entry in the list to walk to that [strike]zone[/strike] container (added in v1.5) automatically: Zones and their names are drawn on the map when the zone manager is open: Check items in your base as a list even while away: Designate zones which can be used to further organize your base: To-do [strike]Zones with configurable colors[/strike] done [strike]Filters[/strike] done [strike]Decouple completely from Animal Zone system[/strike] no longer a goal [strike]Workshop description[/strike] done [strike]Show home zones in world when the manager window is open[/strike] done [strike]Show items inside container items (for now only furniture is supported)[/strike] done [strike]Mouse hover highlights container[/strike] done [strike]Support translations[/strike] done [strike]4K monitor support[/strike] done [strike]Display friendly name for containers rather than the technical/object name ("Metal Shelves" are currently displayed as "metal_shelves")[strike] done [strike]Increase column width of the zone name in manager window to support longer names[/strike] done Repository Source code is hosted in GitLab. description: Compatible with Build 42 up to Build 42.20.0+ Show Key Origin helps you identify what a key belongs to by showing the distance and direction to its origin directly in the inventory tooltip. It can also display a visual origin line in the world, pointing from your character toward the related building or the original spawn position of the linked vehicle. This makes keys much easier to identify, sort and keep organized. Main Features Shows the distance to a key’s origin. Shows the direction toward that origin. Adds a context-menu option to show or hide a visual origin line. For house/building keys, the line points toward the related building. For vehicle keys, the line points toward the vehicle’s original spawn position. Optional compass requirement through Sandbox settings. Optional thicker origin line when TchernoLib is enabled. How It Works Hover over a key in your inventory to see its origin information. Right-click a key and use the context menu to show or hide the origin line. Use the information to identify duplicate keys, sort useful keys, and figure out which building or vehicle each key belongs to. Optional Sandbox Setting You can enable a Sandbox option that requires having a compass in your inventory. When enabled: Tooltip origin information only appears if you have a compass. The visual origin line can only be shown if you have a compass. Optional TchernoLib Support If you enable TchernoLib, the origin line can be displayed thicker for better visibility. TchernoLib is optional. Show Key Origin works without it. Compatibility Works from Build 42 up to Build 42.20.0+. Safe to enable or disable in both new games and existing saves. Lightweight, UI-focused mod. Compatible with most mod setups. Possible conflicts are mainly expected with mods that heavily modify inventory tooltips or key/item context-menu behavior. Localization Show Key Origin includes expanded localization support with: Legacy TXT translations for earlier Build 42 versions. JSON translations for Build 42.15+. Updated and reviewed wording for key origin, distance, direction, compass requirements and display-line options. description: Build Support: B42.0.2 to B42.20.x — Build 42 only NeatUI Framework is a lightweight shared UI framework for Project Zomboid Build 42 mods. You usually do not use this mod directly. Install and enable it when another mod lists NeatUI Framework as a requirement. Important: if another mod depends on NeatUI Framework, load NeatUI Framework BEFORE that mod. What This Mod Does NeatUI Framework provides shared UI tools used by other Project Zomboid mods. It helps dependent mods keep their interfaces cleaner, more consistent, and easier to maintain across different Build 42 versions. Shared UI framework / library for Build 42 mods Reusable UI helpers, widgets, layout tools, rendering utilities, and styling support Compatibility helpers for UI changes across different B42 builds Cleaner and more consistent interfaces for supported mods Less duplicated UI code between related mods This framework does not add gameplay features by itself. Its visible effects depend on the mods that use it. Who Needs This Mod? You need this mod only if another mod requires it. If none of your enabled mods depend on NeatUI Framework, you can leave it disabled. Mods That Use NeatUI Framework NeatUI Framework is used by several UI-focused mods originally created by Rocco and maintained / updated for newer Build 42 versions by Afyrmo, including: CleanUI Modern Status The Shortcut Neat Crafting Neat Building Project Cook It is also used by: Neat Crafting & Neat Building – XP & Mod Display — created by Afyrmo Neat Rocco's UI — created by ArtNod NeatUI Hairstyler — created by Gimmi NeatUI XPDrop — created by Gimmi You may also like Clean HotBar, which follows a similar clean UI approach. How to Enable It Single Player Enable NeatUI Framework in your mod list and place it before any mod that depends on it. If the mod is subscribed but does not appear in the in-game Mods tab, please check that you are running Build 42. This mod is not for Build 41. Multiplayer / Host / Dedicated Server For multiplayer, NeatUI Framework must be added to both server lists: Mods: NeatUI_Framework Steam Workshop: 3508537032 You can check this in your server config: Zomboid\Server<YourServer>.ini It should include: Mods=NeatUI_Framework;... WorkshopItems=3508537032;... NeatUI Framework must be loaded before any mod that depends on it. If a dependent mod works in Single Player but not when hosting a server, this is one of the first things to check. Compatibility Build 42 only Supports Build 42.0.2 to 42.20.x Intended for SP / MP Host / Dedicated Server setups Includes compatibility maintenance for UI changes introduced across newer Build 42 versions This framework is a library; visible behavior depends on the mods that use it Linux Dedicated Servers / Lua Checksum Recent versions include cleanup intended to improve compatibility with Linux dedicated servers using: DoLuaChecksum=true Lua file paths and line endings have been normalized to help avoid checksum issues on case-sensitive servers. description: Overview : Say goodbye to becoming a jack-of-all-trades! This mod introduces a new skill development system that encourages balance and decision-making by setting a cap on total skill levels. Designed with multiplayer and RP servers in mind, this mod promotes role specialization and interdependence. Confirmed to work with Build 41/42. Split-screen play is not supported. May be considered upon request. Features : Skill Cap System You can level up freely until your total skill level reaches the cap. Once the cap is reached, skill leveling behavior depends on the cap setting. If there are skills marked as reducible, one will be randomly chosen to decrease, allowing the new skill to level up. If there are no reducible skills, skill level-up will be suppressed. Skill Cap Buttons Cap control buttons are added to the skill panel in the character info window. Each button has three toggle states that can be switched by clicking: : Gain XP and level up freely until the total cap is reached. : XP gain and leveling are disabled; skill may be reduced if over the cap. : XP gain and leveling are disabled; skill is protected from reduction. Skills without a cap button are excluded from the system. You can customize which skills are excluded via Sandbox settings. Sandbox Options : These options are available in Sandbox Options. Seesaw Game > Total Skill Cap : Sets the total level cap across all skills. Once the combined level exceeds this value, no further skill gains are allowed. Seesaw Game > Excluded Skill Cap : Sets a semicolon-separated list of skills to exclude from the total skill cap. These skills will not be affected by the cap and can continue to level up freely. Options : These options are available with Mod Options in B41. Level Down XP Rate : Sets how much XP is reduced when a skill is leveled down due to reaching the total skill cap. Show Skill Cap Info : Displays total skill cap information in the Skill Panel. Known Issues : Setting a high EXP multiplier may cause the total skill count to become inaccurate when multiple levels are gained from a single exp acquisition. This is currently a limitation, but I plan to consider addressing it if there is significant demand in the future. If leveling up is disabled due to exceeding the cap limit, any recipes acquired through that level-up will remain learned. Beta Notice for MP: This mod has been updated to support multiplayer on the current stable Build 42 release. Due to changes in Build 42's XP and multiplayer handling, the mod's internal architecture has been substantially revised. XP control, which was previously handled mainly on the client, is now handled primarily by the server. The intended gameplay features have been tested successfully on a dedicated server, including skill locking, level reduction, per-player settings, reconnecting, and changing the Level Down XP Rate during play. However, performance with multiple concurrent players has not yet been tested extensively. description: Red Days Players will now have a menstrual cycle and need to find and stockpile feminine care products Current Major Features: The basic menstrual cycle including the following phases: - Menstrual - Follicular - Ovulation - Luteal Character generates discharge outside of the menstrual cycle. Debuff effects during the Menstrual Phase: - Reduced Endurance - Increased Fatigue - Groin bleeding and muscle strain (to simulate cramps) - Lower torso muscle strain (to simulate cramps and increase pain level so the moodle shows up) - Increased discomfort levels - Painkillers negates debuffs (6 ingame hours default) Feminine Hygiene products: - Boxes of Sanitary Pads - Boxes of Tampons - Boxes of Panty Liners - Bandages will work as a quick stop gap if regular feminine hygiene products are not available. Custom 3D models for Hygiene Products - Special thanks to "sudodski" who stepped up and created the 3D models for this mod. Thank you very much! We appreciate you :) - Craftable cycle tracker calendar: - If tracker book is in equipped bag or inventory and page 14 ID matches character ID - Everytime player unequips or replaces a sanitary item, it as assumed the player inspected the item and results are automatically logged in the book. - If data isn't being written, delete all contents on page 14 or craft a new book. - IDK how to make a custom UI and I have 0 artistic talent so a text based calendar is the best I've got. - The inspirational quote changes everytime you unequip/replace a sanitary pad item. Let me know if there are any you'd like to add. Just make sure the quote and the author credit would fit in the character limits. Refer to existing quotes as a guideline. - Writing tools aren't needed for now, but will be made necessary later. - If you are on a new character and delayed phase is enabled, no data will be recorded until your first period occurs. After that however, everything should work normally. - Moodles - Moodles reminding players to change out products - Pre-Menstrual Symptoms (PMS) - Characters spawn with 3 randomly selected PMS symptoms that remain consistent throughout their life. Enable random symptoms per cycle in sandbox options if you prefer variety. - PMS severity varies each cycle and can be reduced by 75% with painkillers. - Effects gradually increase during late luteal phase, peak just before menstruation, then quickly subside within 24 hours of bleeding. PMS Effects: - Agitation (A): Uses default unused anger moodle (may conflict with other mods). Doubles stamina/endurance recovery at peak severity. Cancels out Fatigue debuff. - Fatigue (F): Halves stamina/endurance recovery and doubles fatigue gain at peak severity. Cancels out Agitation buff. - Sadness/Depression (U): Depression level tracks PMS severity. Antidepressants provide relief, but depression naturally subsides as PMS fades. - Tender Breasts (T): Causes upper torso muscle strain scaling with severity. Reduced by 50% if Cramps are also active. May interfere with sleep at high severity without painkillers when combined with cramps. - Cramps (C): Causes lower torso and groin muscle strain scaling with severity. Stacks with Tender Breasts. May require painkillers for sleep at high severity. - Food Cravings (Y): Player always wants to eat. Not wearing hyginene items increases "dirtiness/bloodiness" for certain clothing locations and drops small amounts of blood on ground when fully saturated - - Potential for interaction with other mods that have dirt/blood attracts zombies ============ WARNING! ================= ====== TSS IS LETHAL BY DEFAULT! ========= Toxic Shock Syndrome (TSS) - Neglecting your hygiene items for too long can develop into a progressive infection, starting with mild warning symptoms and, if ignored long enough, escalating all the way to full Toxic Shock. - Early on it's just stamina/fatigue penalties and a nagging feeling something's off. Left unchecked, it can spiral into a dangerous late stage where your health itself starts draining -- made worse by stress, exhaustion, thirst, body temperature, and hunger. - Changing your hygiene items regularly keeps it from ever starting. Once infected, removing the source lets your body recover on its own over time -- no medication strictly required, just patience. However once the infection crosses over into TSS, you must take 2 doses of antibiotics daily for 5-6 days 8-12 hours apart. - Antibiotics (a regular food item) speed up recovery and are your best safety net if things get bad. - Known limitation: TSS is currently disabled automatically when playing on a true multiplayer/dedicated server, due to an unresolved sync bug -- it works as described above in singleplayer. Will be revisited in a future update. I've tested SP to work fine, but for both MP and SP, if you encounter something that doesn't seem right. You can reset the TSS. - RESET TSS: - You can reset TSS by launching the game in debug mode, and running this command: rd.goToTSSStage(0) - COLLECT REPORT: - Go to your zomboid user data files, usually here: C:\Users\<your username>\Zomboid\console.txt - Find a block of lines that look like : f:5891> =========================== Generated menstrual cycle details ============================== - Submit the bug report, what you did leading up to the bug, what you expected, what you got and then the error. Planned features: Feminine Hygiene products: - Craftable re-usable cloth pads - Menstrual cups Traits: - Hygiene product consumption and stat decrement rates vary by cycle trait: - Light, Normal, Heavy Cycle Traits - Endometriosis by popular request - Health affects menstrual cycle - Severe underweight/malnutrition can stop the cycle - Severe stress can alter the cycle - PMS symptoms as traits - Interactions with things like hot drinks, chocolate, ice cream, etc. - Menopause Debuffs for insufficient hygienic care: - TSS or other sickness and debuffs FAQ: - Menstrual bleeding is visual only and should not kill you. - Only female characters will experience the menstrual cycle by default, but you can enable for all genders in sandbox options - This should be safe to add mid save, however feminine hygiene items won't spawn in places you've already looted, but can spawn on corpses. - The follicular, ovulation and luteal phase doesn't have any other effect besides generating discharge, which is completely a visual thing with no status effects that requires a 1-2 times a day change of panty liners. ___________________________________________________ NOTICE 2025-07-07: Regarding Controversy in the Comments I am completely OK with criticism of the mod, it helps me figure out what to do better. I created this mod with respectful intent and to be as accurate as I can and with what I know and within the limitations of the game. Nearly 50% of our population have no choice but to deal with this completely natural biological cycle and it shouldn't be a weird taboo subject. Women do exist, and they do not have cooties, grow up please. What I'm NOT OK with is sexism and or misogyny. I will keep all comments critical of me and the mod, but going forward, I'll be deleting comments I deem to be sexist, misogynist or otherwise excessively immature. description: Being the 'Common Sense' of vehicles, this mod adds A LOT of Features and QOL/Rebalancing Changes, I urge you to read the full list below! Trust me, you'll be wishing some of these options were in the vanilla game. [WIP Mod for Multiplayer/Singleplayer B42.20 Stable]. Supports all modded vehicles. Can be added/removed mid-save safely. Almost everything can be selectively disabled/enabled (the important stuff at least), most options are enabled by default. Climbable Vehicles does not currently work for multiplayer, requires enabling in the sandbox settings, and will be moved to a different mod page when enough vanilla bugs are fixed. I only recommend using it for screenshots as it's very outdated and I cannot, nor will I, confirm if it works since it's basically abandoned, for now. Don't ask about it in the comments either, I'll finish it when I finish it. NEW FEATURES: - Adds vehicle zones across the entire map (literally thousands) including vehicles in garages, gas station, more traffic in your traffic jams, farms, and more. - Adds a new custom vehicle spawn rate, chance to spawn burnt, damaged, and more customization in the sandbox settings. - Spawns more corpses in cars, you'll find quite a few here and there on car seats. - Some vehicle zone types, like parking lots, can spawn vehicles facing in random directions to simulate the initial waves of chaos of the apocalypse. - Improves junkyards and traffic jams by adding back wrecked vehicles, removal of random parts, rebalanced vehicle qualities, and randomly opened doors/windows. - Bombs can now trigger car alarms AND be planted on vehicles to explode them (smoke, pipe, aerosol, remote detonators, plant on doors, above wheels, and in the ignition, etc.). - A new system for refueling vehicles from pumps at gas stations, which includes, but is not limited to, not needing to stand still for a minute while pumping gasoline, repairing the pump you just ripped out after driving away with it still attached, sounds, fuel station status, etc. - Adds the ability to exit from a moving vehicle, but I'd be careful at higher speeds! - Weather affects players with an open door, a window open, or a windshield smashed (more detailed than worth explaining). - Adds Jackie Jaye's LBMW Radio Van. It will only spawn at her trailer north of the main LV military checkpoint. - Adds vehicles hoods, trunks, and trailers as a generic crafting surfaces; for crafting recipes that require a table. - Adds a crafting recipe to clone a car key, either as a backup or for a friend. It is very similar to the 'Copy Building Key' recipe and it requires reading the same magazine from it. - Adds several scripts for smelting vehicle parts into steel, crafting tires and windows/windshield glass, and repairing tires and mufflers. - Adds the ability to open/close and unlock/lock your own door while in a vehicle. - Adds the ability to enter/exit some vehicles through the trunk (assume for most heavy-duty vehicles it will work). Only works if you can see the "Trunk" container icon from the seat you're in (usually the rear row). That feature, that is accessing the trunk from the inside if you're in a specific seat, is vanilla and I made this to work based on that. - As the driver of a vehicle, you can electronically open/close any window. Press "Z", or enter the Vehicle Seats UI another way, then hold LEFT or RIGHT ALT to see your options. From there, you can either click an individual window or press a number on your keyboard to open the corresponding window. - You can now unhotwire (rewire?) hotwired vehicles at level 3 electrical and level 2 mechanics. - Adds a TWD reference, a flipped prison bus in Rosewood (if you have the correct KI5 vehicle mod enabled), there's more potential here (WIP). - Normal trailers have the ability to add and remove their cover (right-click trailer part in the trailer's mechanics ui). - Advert trailers now have trailer storage (access from either open side, still the same storage). - Adds extra seating to the back of Pick Up Trucks, great for transporting friends AND corpses, which may be the same thing if they died... (no visible player model is shown, vanilla bug would make it look weird unfortunately). - Adds context menu option to cut tire pieces from tire stack world objects, most commonly found at 'Irvington Speedway' as bumper barriers. Supports the vanilla red, white, and black tire stacks. - Adds context menu option to take propane from the large world propane tanks, which can be commonly found at newer/updated gas stations and basements in B42.20 stable. SANDBOX SETTINGS: - General spawn rate defaults to vanilla if no value is entered. Junkyards, traffic jams, and special traffic jams ignore this setting. - Spawn rate for traffic jams (otherwise recognized as bumper to bumper traffic) is defaulted to very high, but the vanilla Vehicle Spawn Rate value slightly alters it. - The Traffic Jams in LV toggle enables/disables all the new traffic jams I added in LV specifically. - The Traffic Jams outside LV toggle enables/disables all the new traffic jams I added everywhere else. - Random Vehicle Angles is a toggle for if some specific types of car zones, such as parking lots and ambulances, will be rotated around at random. Basically, it is a slight immersion thing. - Corpses Spawning in Vehicles can be set to "None", "Rare", "Normal", and "Common" (default is 'Normal' which is about 8%). - Bombs interacting with vehicles can be toggled off/on. - The new system for refueling vehicles from pumps at gas stations can be toggled off/on. - Weather affects players in vehicles can be toggled off/on. - Jumping out of a fast moving vehicle can toggled off/on and the damage received can be reduced/increased. - The ability to turn all vehicle zones into burnt wrecks, completely configurable at a set rate. - The ability to completely customize the quality of cars you find for all vehicle zones. - The ability to prevent 'Good' vehicles from spawning ('Good' vehicles are a VANILLA thing). - MIN / MAX propane amounts in industrial propane tanks, it is a multiplier counted in number of propane tanks for easy understanding. Each propane tank is 81 units (propane torches contain 10), so the default maximum would be 170 X 81 = 13770 units of propane (with a minimum of 0). - The 'Climbable Vehicles' addon (read at the top of the workshop description for 'use warning'). LOAD ORDER INSTRUCTION!!!: In general, treat this mod like a map mod for load order (at the top), but still place after normal map mods. For more detailed MILITARY VEHICLE ZONES options: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3436499337 If you use or want a mod that removes/replaces vanilla vehicles, please use either of these two: Kraz's No Vanilla Vehicles (B42) - (may not remove all vehicle story event vanilla vehicles): https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2535461640 OR Vanilla Vehicles Replacer (KI5) - (may cause unexpected spawns, possibly leading to floating vehicle shadows): https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3423424077 Shoutout to KI5's (year accurate / lore friendly) vehicle mods which are primarily supported (but not the only ones) in this mod for balancing and special treatment (I still take suggestions for other vehicles like the W900 trucks mod): https://steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/?id=2490220997 ...and if you want corpses to spawn in KI5 vehicles specifically, install this mod and follow THEIR load order instruction which allows me to spawn the corpses on KI5's vehicles' seats. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3457132019 EXTRA SPECIAL SHOUTOUT TO (Alex) @RedChili FOR HELPING ME WITH CLIMBING ANIMATIONS https://steamcommunity.com/id/mreastman/myworkshopfiles/?appid=108600 Workshop ID: 3520758551 Mod ID: WayMoreCars

description: This is a complete rewrite using the original Home Inventory as reference. Quoted from maraganina: Looted the 14th pipe wrench because you forgot you already had 13? Didn't take that sledgehammer because you already had one but now you realized that was on your previous character? This mod allows you to designate zones in your home(s) or base(s). A list of all items in those zones will be displayed in the new Home Inventory [strike]tab[/strike], available [strike]in the Character Info panel (Health screen)[/strike] by clicking a new button in the sidebar. Safe to add/remove mid campaign; doesn't overwrite any game files. ... The Home Inventory mod allows the player to create and manage custom zones: "home" zones; similar to how the Animal system works in B42. The items inside home zones are fetched and saved, and can be seen as a list in a new [strike]tab[/strike] panel called "Home Inventory" located in the [strike]Character Info panel (the heart icon)[/strike]. Home zones can cover multiple bases, and can also cover different areas of each base. It's up to you to decide how you will organize your bases and the items inside them. The list of items is only fetched when you add or remove zones, or when you click the [strike]"Home Inventory" tab[/strike] "Manage" button, so the mod has virtually no effect on performance. If you are too far from a zone, their tiles will not be loaded, and the game will think your items don't exist. To prevent this, the mod saves the items of each zone to a cache, so you can keep checking your home inventory while you are away. What's new? This mod adds many extra features in addition to the currently existing ones in the original mod, which includes: Vehicles Storage: Any items in a vehicle or trailer inside a zone should now be accounted for. (since 0.7.0) (thanks for the idea, @Sophia (Sophel) and @Crystalmancer!) After a long drive, you can open the items list and hit refresh to show your newly acquired loots. The name of vehicle is displayed alongside its specific part for easier search. Improved UI (again, hopefully) (since 0.6.0) The Zone panel can now be resized, and it's also made more compact. Quick Search: Right-click on an item will show whether you have collected that item and the current amount stored in your Home Inventory. (since 0.4.0) NOTE: The amount of items collected for the default option is now placed in the tooltip of an item, visible when hovered. (since 0.5.0) Container Tooltip: Hover over the container name of an item to show its inventory icon. (since 0.3.0) Integration with Smarter Storage (since 0.3.0) (Thanks for the idea, @ivmakk!) The "Container" column will now display the custom name set by the mod if it exists. The custom icon and background will be used in the container tooltip when hovered. Improved UI (since 0.2.0) The items panel can now be opened with a new button next to the "Designated Zones" button. (A new custom icon is also used.) A refresh button to reload items without needing to re-open/close any panels. Items sorting with ascending and descending order by clicking on the header text. Selectable filter criteria with a drop-down list next to the search bar. Resizable panel to expand all truncated texts to your heart's content. Mod options: some previously hard-coded values (such as zone colors) can be adjusted and all changes made can be applied mid-game. (since 0.2.0) A key can be set to open/close the items panel (KP_ADD or "Numpad +" by default) A number of bugs in the original mod is also fixed (hopefully): Incorrect size reported by the zone manager panel. (A 1-cell zone will show up as 4) (might be the same as the previous one) Zones bleeding into each other. (Two non-overlapping zones that are right next to each other will cause an item in one zone to show up in the other as a duplicate entry) Interference to the display designated zones for animals. This mod does not hide or show them. Incompatibilities This mod only conflicts with the original one, but that's mostly because having 2 different items system is kind of redundant in my opinion. It is planned that a special function to import mod data from the original mod for migration. Final notes A special thanks and all respects to the original mod's creator maraganina, I've been using your mod for a few months now, and it has been a convenience in every run of mine ever since, and of course, this mod would have never existed without your contribution to the Steam Workshop. For everybody else, if you like this mod, be sure to check out the original one, too! GLHF and keep on surviving! :3 Workshop ID: 3522009163 Mod ID: cf_home

description: How long can you blend in? Slow Burn transforms Project Zomboid into a stealth-focused survival experience inspired by Bobby Adair's acclaimed post-apocalyptic novel series. You're infected—but unlike everyone else, the transformation never fully completed. As long as you suppress your human instincts and behave like the infected around you, the dead will accept you as one of their own. Combat is no longer your first option. Survival depends on patience, deception, and knowing exactly when your disguise begins to fail. Keep an eye on the custom Suspicion Moodle to gauge how well your disguise is holding up. Running, fighting, and other obviously human behaviour will give you away. Move slowly, stay quiet, and let the infected believe you belong. Controls Tab — Toggle the Debug HUD (Suspicion/Fever tracking) Z — Devour a corpse while crouched over it (resets Suspicion at a cost) G — Cover yourself in guts over a corpse (reduces Suspicion gain at a cost) N — Toggle Zombie Walk Mode Q — Shout (blows your cover instantly), or Whisper while crouched to lure a nearby zombie toward you V — Grunt like a zombie to slightly lower suspicion (30 second cooldown) Custom Profession: Infected Survivor Starting Stats Sneaking +2 Lightfooted +2 Nimble +2 Night Vision Bandaged bite wound (left forearm) Suspicion Levels HIDDEN (0–24) — Perfect mimicry. Completely ignored. SUSPICIOUS (25–49) — The infected begin watching you more closely. EXPOSED (50–74) — Your disguise is failing. Zombies begin circling. HUNTED (75–89) — Nearby infected converge from within 30 tiles. BLOWN (90–100) — Full aggression. Zombies swarm from up to 70 tiles away. Suspicion decays fastest while crouched, alone, and out of sight—especially indoors. Survive long enough, and the infected will once again accept you as one of their own. Infected Survivor Profession — Immune to zombie bites. Dynamic Suspicion System — Stay hidden until your cover is blown. Indoor & Outdoor Awareness — Hiding indoors reduces Suspicion faster. Line-of-Sight Detection — Walls and objects help conceal suspicious behaviour. Five Custom Moodles — Instantly display your current cover level. Environmental Influence — Weather, time of day, and your behaviour all affect detection. Zombie Escalation — Nearby infected begin hunting you as Suspicion rises. Whisper Mechanic (Q while crouched) — Lure a nearby zombie toward your position for a controlled, strategic kill. Smart Ones — A small chance for certain zombies to see through your disguise no matter how you act. Naked Hordes — Occasional roaming packs of naked zombies led by one of the rare "smart ones." Unlike the rest of the infected, a horde is fully alert and will hunt you down if it spots you — the only safe option is to keep your distance and let it pass. Naked Zombies — A small percentage of the ordinary population also spawns naked, purely as a cosmetic look — unlike Naked Hordes, these are just as harmless as any other zombie. Zombie Walk Mode (N) — Shuffle like the infected for a major Suspicion reduction while walking, running, vaulting fences, or climbing through windows. Sprinting still gives you away. Infected Window Break — While in Zombie Walk Mode, right-click an unbroken window to claw and thump your way through it like one of the dead for far less Suspicion than smashing it normally, at the cost of a chance to cut yourself. Gloves greatly reduce that risk. Nakedness Discount — Stripping down makes you read as more convincingly infected, reducing Suspicion gain further and stacking with Zombie Walk Mode. Devour (Z) — Consume a corpse to completely remove Suspicion at the cost of increased fever. Guts (G) — Smear yourself in blood and gore to reduce Suspicion gain while increasing fever and stress. Grunt (V) — Groan like the infected to shave a little off your Suspicion, on a cooldown. Fever System — An optional slow-building survival mechanic requiring medicine and rest to prevent your infection worsening. Zombie Bleed-Out — A solid hit from a bladed weapon, piercing tool, or firearm can open a wound that bleeds a zombie out over time on top of normal damage, while it keeps coming after you. Wound severity ranges from a minor graze that may clot shut to an always-fatal devastating wound, with your odds improving the more skilled you are with the weapon in hand.
