Yes. It's a pure loot/item addition mod — it doesn't touch existing world data, so you can safely add it mid-save. Keep in mind newly placed loot only spawns in areas not yet "seen"/loaded by the game, so you may need to explore new zones to start finding duffel bags. ▶ What can I put in the webbing slots? Small utility items only — things like a flashlight, knife, canteen, or walkie-talkie. Bulkier items (like scissors) won't fit; the webbing slots are meant for compact gear, not general storage. ▶ I dropped the backpack (or died) and now I can't pick it up / equip it. Is it a bug? No, this is how weight reduction works. While equipped, the backpack's weight reduction bonus is active — so a bag holding 18kg of items might only "weigh" 7kg on your back. The moment it hits the ground (dropped or after death), that bonus disappears and it reverts to its full real weight. If that's more than your character can lift, the game won't let you pick it up. Fix: take a few items out of the backpack (or drop some of your own inventory) until you're under the 50kg carry limit, then pick it up and equip it — you'll be able to add the items back in afterward. ▶ I set the bag/magazine spawn probability to 0.00 in Sandbox and they still spawn. Is this a bug? This was a known issue in earlier versions, caused by how/when the mod read your Sandbox settings during world generation. Fixed as of v3.0.0. If you're still seeing it, make sure you're on the latest version and report it with your mod version number so I can confirm. ▶ Are the Legendary mods (Backpack, DuffelBag, Fanny Pack, Satchel, etc.) compatible with each other? Yes, all my legendary mods are designed to work together safely. ▶ Does it work on the current stable build (42.20)? Yes, confirmed working on 42.20 stable, both singleplayer and multiplayer (dedicated and hosted/LAN). ▶ Can I go over the 49 capacity cap with another capacity-overwrite mod? No — 49 is the hard limit set by the base game itself, not something this mod can bypass. It's already set to the maximum vanilla allows. ▶ The bags/magazines feel too common — how do I make them rarer? Open the Sandbox options and lower the Common/Rare drop weight sliders for bags and magazines (you can even set them to 0 to disable spawns entirely). description: Break Big Rocks – Enhanced Mining & Crafting Update Break massive rocks, gather valuable resources, and experience a deeper and more immersive mining system in Project Zomboid. Giant Rock Crusher turns heavy tools into true mining equipment, introducing a balanced survival-focused mining loop built around endurance, skill progression, and vanilla-friendly crafting. Mine smarter, manage your endurance, and build a sustainable resource chain with Break Big Rocks. Dynamic mining time based on your equipped tool and Strength level. Mining now consumes physical endurance through the vanilla metabolism system. Vanilla-style tool durability checks respect each tool's resistance instead of removing condition deterministically. Strength, Maintenance, and Masonry XP awarded for mining actions. Custom sounds for a better mining experience. Expanded mining loot table with rare, sandbox-configurable resources. New and expanded Sandbox options to fine-tune mining balance and rarity. Event-driven Blacksmith recipe progression removes recurring player recipe polling and checks only on load or skill advancement. description: Restore your vehicle's engine quality with a Wrench, Spare Engine Parts, and Mechanical skill 4+ Unlike vanilla engine condition (which affects durability), engine quality determines starting reliability, fuel efficiency, and cold weather performance. This mod lets you restore quality from any percentage up to 100%. Why Use This Mod? Have you ever found a great military vehicle, but its engine quality is completely ruined? Have you already repaired and fully upgraded a car for long trips, but starting the engine still requires minutes of attempts? Then this mod is for you - restore the engine to its day-one state, just like it was set from the factory. Key Features Engine Quality Restoration: Improve quality from any percentage up to 100% Skill-Based Mechanics: Higher Mechanics skill = better quality increases per iteration (just like vanilla engine repairing works) Configurable Resource Cost: Adjust engine parts consumption multiplier in Menu -> Options -> Mods -> Restore Engine Quality (1-5 per restoration, default: 2) How to Use Requirements: Wrench (or Ratchet Wrench), Spare Engine Parts, appropriate Mechanics skill level (4+) Access: Right-click vehicle Engine → Restore Engine Quality (the same context menu where "Repair Engine" located) Process: Each restoration consumes engine parts and improves quality based on your skill Resource Cost By default, requires 2x more Spare Engine Parts than regular engine repair (making it more challenging but not grindy). You can adjust this multiplier in mod options from 1x (same as repair) to 5x (very expensive). Engine Quality Effects Starting Reliability: Lower quality = higher chance to fail starting Fuel Efficiency: Lower quality = up to 50% more fuel consumption Cold Weather Starting: Quality ≤65% struggles in cold weather Engine Power: Higher quality = more horsepower (affects reverse speed) Requirements Wrench (or any WRENCH-tagged tool, e.g. Ratchet Wrench) Spare Engine Parts Minimal Mechanics level 4/5/6 for standard/heavy-duty/sports vehicles respectively. The percentage each (2) engine parts restore depends on your mechanics skill and car type (modded vehicles can use their own required mechanics level). For example, at level 10 mechanics, 50 spare engine parts will restore a standard car's engine quality from 0% to 100%. Based on your Mechanics level, each 2 Spare Engine Parts will restore 1-5% Engine Quality. 1 + (<Mechanics Level> - <Required Level>) / 2 Motivation Inspired by Easy Engine Rebuild (B41 only), but fully developed from scratch as a new mod with a focus on a lore-friendly way to restore the engine. Unlike Easy Engine Rebuild, this mod gives you the ability to restore the engine iteratively, similar to how vanilla engine repair works. Compatibility Supported builds: 42.17+ (tested on b42.20.3 SP & MP) Safe to add/remove mid-game Works with all vanilla vehicles Works with Vehicle Repair Overhaul, AutoMechanics and other popular mechanics mods Works with KI5, Autotsar vehicles, and should work with most other vehicle mods as well (please let me know in the comments if you find any unsupported modded vehicle) Feedback Found a bug or have suggestions? description: Vampirism – Survive as a Creature of the Night Step into the apocalypse as something more than human… This mod lets you experience Project Zomboid as a true vampire, trapped between eternal hunger, fragile blood reserves, and the dangers of a dying world. In this update, blood is no longer just something you drink — it is something you must manage, protect, and sometimes risk. Core Features Blood Thirst HUD (v2.0): A redesigned gothic interface that tracks your blood level — a constant reminder that hunger never sleeps. Feed on the Dead: Drink directly from zombie corpses (once per body) to survive the night. Blood Storage System (NEW): Extract blood into transfusion bags to save it for later — but stored blood is fragile. Blood Degradation: Blood spoils over time if not refrigerated, transitioning through Fresh → Coagulated → Rotten. Risk-Based Feeding: Old blood causes unhappiness; rotten blood can make you sick — just like spoiled food. Animal Feeding: Hunt and feed on animals, including baby animals (Build 42 entities). Unpredictable Blood Extraction: You never know how much blood a corpse will give — like siphoning fuel from a wreck. No Human Food: Bread, cans, and crops are useless to you. Blood is your only sustenance. Low-Blood Consequences: Severe debuffs at low blood levels; death awaits at 0%. Weakness to Sunlight: Daylight burns your flesh. The night is your ally. Night Power: Stronger at night, weaker during the day. Sandbox Customization: Adjust thirst decay, sunlight damage, healing, extraction balance, and more — from casual to hardcore vampirism. Vampire Profession (Build 42 Ready): Start as a vampire directly from character creation, fully integrated with the new profession system. Blood Is Not Power — It Is a Resource Being a vampire does not make you invincible. Blood can be: Fresh: Safe and effective. Rancid: Still usable, but unpleasant. Rotten: Dangerous — drink at your own risk. Fail to refrigerate your supplies, and your reserves will betray you. Plan poorly, and hunger will force desperate choices. Survival is no longer about feeding once — it’s about planning ahead. Traits Your vampirism is not a single curse, but a combination of strengths and burdens. Choose how you endure the night — and the day. Blood Thirst: The core curse of all vampires. You no longer feed on normal food — only blood can sustain you. Sun-Tolerant: Allows limited survival under direct sunlight. Solar damage is reduced and burns are prevented, but the sun remains deadly over time. Night Hunter: Feeding and recovery are more effective at night, but daylight becomes even more punishing. Night Thirst: Blood Thirst consumption increases during the night, demanding constant feeding to maintain stability. Day Torpor: Your blood slows during daylight. Blood Thirst consumption is reduced while resting, encouraging a more cautious daytime rhythm. Ascension – The Lord Vampire Path When a vampire masters the art of killing, a darker power awakens. At 1500 zombie kills, you ascend and gain unique passive abilities: Controlled Thirst: Blood decay slows by 25%. Hunger becomes easier to manage. Carnal Dominion: +15% melee damage while well-fed (above 50% blood). “The Lord Vampire does not fear hunger; he commands it.” Immersion & Compatibility Atmosphere: Feeding includes subtle sound cues — dangerous in crowded areas. description: Adds a new skill in the survival category called toughness. This is your character's mental resilience to the hardships of the apocalypse, with each level reducing the amount of panic, pain and discomfort they'll feel. Toughness XP can be earned by killing zombies. It will take about 4450 total zombie kills to reach max level in toughness at x1 XP rates. The new positive trait "tough" provides a starting toughness level of +1 and a x4 XP multiplier, reducing the total number of zombie kills for max level to only around 1000. Each level of toughness reduces the total amount of panic felt by your character by -10%, pain by -5%, discomfort by -5% and an extra 10% added to the discomfort nullification threshold. This means a character with level 2 toughness will not gain any discomfort at all if the total combined discomfort of their clothes and moodles is at or below 20%. Since the total discomfort pecentage level can go above 100%, level 10 toughness won't completely remove discomfort if enough uncomfortable clothes are being worn. If these values are not to your liking the XP rate and stat reduction from toughness can be configured in the sandbox. This mod can be seen as an alternative to the "become desensitized" mod, providing a more gradual increase in panic reduction as the playthrough progresses rather than suddenly granting the desensitized trait after a set number of zombie kills. description: These zombies... you kill them again, and again, and again, and again. Yet, all they ever have on them are clothes and absolutely nothing useful. After slaying over 5,000 zombies in CDDA, I've come to a sincere conclusion: these zombies are flat broke. I just can't believe that after the Cataclysm broke out, people would leave their homes with nothing. It's impossible that they wouldn't have picked up a weapon to fight back, even if they were doomed to die right at the outset. That's why I made this mod—to enrich the loot drops from zombies and to make it look like they had actually lived a life and did something before they turned. Effects: Make zombies have a chance to drop weapons, daily necessities (including mod items), and some materials. By default, between 25 and 75 liters per hour can fill a 10,000 liter well in 7 to 10 days. ☣ Contamination System • If you leave rotting zombie corpses near wells, each in-game hour there is a chance the well water will become contaminated by the bodies. • The chance increases with both the number of corpses nearby and the time they remain unremoved. • It is possible to clean a contaminated well using charcoal. The goal of this mod is simple: give "excess ceramics" a purpose. You can recycle common pottery loot (and your own crafted ceramics) into shards/powder, then choose a path: Reclaim clay (lossy) by converting recycled ceramics into Modeling Clay and kneading it back into base Clay. Make new decor by sculpting masters, making plaster molds, and slip-casting hollow ceramic pieces. This mod is built for Build 42.13.2 and plugs directly into the base game pottery + kiln workflow (clay tools + kiln firing), with an added slip-casting fluid chain. Most steps can be done on any crafting surface unless the recipe says otherwise: Smash fired clay/ceramic items (looted or crafted) into shards Grind shards into powder (grog) Mix pottery fluids (Slip / Grog Slurry / Grogged Slip) Make Modeling Clay from Grogged Slip + an additive Sculpt masters → make plaster molds → cast hollow pieces Kiln fire and optionally paint the finished ceramics What's New / Core Features (42.13.2) 3 custom fluids integrated with B42's fluid system: Clay Slip (light) Grog Slurry (dark) Grogged Slip (tempered mix) Controlled blending: Slip + Grog Slurry blend into Grogged Slip. Slip-casting workflow: build a Casting Frame, create Slip Cast Plaster Molds, then cast unfired ceramics using Slip or Grogged Slip. Two in-world magazines that teach the recipe sets (you still need Pottery skill to craft): HydeCo. Slip Casting HydeCo. Ceramic Decorations Expanded smash list for recycling the stuff you keep finding in kitchens, shelves, and storage (examples): bowls, jars (including glazed), mugs, plates, pots, bricks/shingles/tiles, molds/casts, crucibles, teacups, pipe segments, and more. Everything feeds back: even the mod’s own fired/painted decorations can be smashed back into shards when you’re done with them. Modeling Clay (Additives) To keep the loop interesting, Modeling Clay is made from Grogged Slip plus an additive: Beeswax option (from HydeCo. Bees!) Vanilla alternatives: Sandbag or Dirtbag Decor & Cosmetic Uniques Custom decor items follow the same multi-stage pottery workflow: Modeling Clay → Plaster Mold → Unfired → Fired → Painted. description: This mod adds M998 HMMWV (Humvee) with Animated Doors and a fully functioning Turret to Project Zomboid. It is necessary to have the Military Tool Kitinstalled. *Only for B42 SP and MP *✅B42.20 *Compatible with old saves *Compatible with KI5 vehicles Resources Animated Doors Animated Addons Turret The turrets have heavy coding that adds a completely new ballistics system that is independent of the systems in the Standard Game, performing calculations for each projectile independently, calculating its energy, ability to cause damage and transfix bodies, vehicles and walls. Doors, hoods, trunk lids and more. They have their own colors, so you can assemble your Humvee with the color variation of the parts you want. How to use the Machine Gun The machine gun must be installed in the vehicle You must sit in the Gunner's seat You must place the 12.7x99mm (.50 BMG) Ammo Box already loaded with 12.7x99mm (.50 BMG) Round in the gun compartment. Press the Right Mouse Button to aim and the Left Mouse Button to fire. ATTENTION, the projectile will be fired where the barrel of the machine gun is pointing and not necessarily where you are aiming, so for more precise shots it is recommended that you wait for the turret stop before firing. (It is still possible to fire with it moving) ATTENTION, when the projectile is fired, it will travel all the way until it completely loses its synergy and stops, so if there are vehicles in its path and the projectile has enough synergy, it will cause damage and may or may not transfix them. The same logic applies to walls, just as in real life a .50 BMG projectile can transfix some walls and still have the energy to destroy things in its path. So use with caution, a Browning M2HB is not a toy. It is necessary to have the Military Tool Kit installed. description: Tired of zombies magically appearing out of nowhere? With this mod you can disable respawn but still face an endless threat. Clear the streets by destroying corpses (burn, bury, or stash them) or leave the corpses alone, and zombies will keep rising again forever. SANDBOX SETTINGS GUIDE: Revival Chance (%) – Sets the probability that a zombie will revive at all. For example, if set to 40%, there is a 40% chance the zombie will revive and a 60% chance it will remain dead. Fixed Revival Time – Set the number of in-game hours before a zombie revives. Note: If Random Mode is enabled, this value is ignored, and only the Min/Max Revival Time settings are used. Random Mode – When enabled, zombies revive after a random period instead of the fixed time. The revival time is calculated between the Min Revival Time and Max Revival Time settings. Min Revival Time – Defines the minimum number of in-game hours that must pass before a zombie can revive. For example, if Min is 5 and Max is 20, the zombie will revive somewhere between 5 and 20 hours. Max Revival Time – Defines the maximum number of in-game hours before a zombie can revive. Works together with Min Revival Time to create a random revival window. Workshop ID: 3555199477 Mod ID: UndyingZombies Workshop ID: 3555199477 Mod ID: UndyingZombies

Yes. It's a pure loot/item addition mod — it doesn't touch existing world data, so you can safely add it mid-save. Keep in mind newly placed loot only spawns in areas not yet "seen"/loaded by the game, so you may need to explore new zones to start finding duffel bags. ▶ I dropped the bag on the ground and now I can't pick it back up. Is it a bug? This is a vanilla PZ weight limit, not a bug. Your character always picks up the FULL weight of the bag first (before the mod's weight reduction applies), then equips it. If your total carry weight would go over 50 with the bag's real weight, the game blocks the pickup. Fix: drop a few items from your inventory (or take some out of the bag first) until you're under the limit, pick up the bag and equip it, then pick your items back up. Once worn, the weight reduction applies normally. ▶ Does it work on the current stable build (42.20)? Yes, confirmed working on 42.20 stable, both singleplayer and multiplayer (dedicated and hosted/LAN). ▶ Can I go over the 49 capacity cap with another capacity-overwrite mod? No — 49 is the hard limit set by the base game itself, not something this mod can bypass. It's already set to the maximum vanilla allows. ▶ The bags/magazines feel too common — how do I make them rarer? Open the Sandbox options and lower the Common/Rare drop weight sliders for bags and magazines (you can even set them to 0 to disable spawns entirely). description: Preserve 'evolved recipe' foods such as soup, stew, etc. in jars using the vanilla jarring method, for an immersive expansion to the game's preservation mechanics. Optional - remove requirements for salt and vinegar. Optional - sandbox settings: days until stale/rotten for all jarred food. Description: 1. Cook your evolved recipe. 2. Place into canning jar. 3. Cook sealed jar for an hour. 4. Store and enjoy at a later point in time. Auto-learning of jarring process lowered from level 8 to level 4 cooking. At default settings, jarred food (including vanilla preserved vegetables) lasts 300 days before going stale and 400 days before rotting at normal spoilage setting when kept without refrigeration (vanilla: 60 and 90 days). Note that the vanilla mechanic accounts for the age of produce, so make sure to can your produce at its freshest and as soon as possible after jarring. Please see my Realistic Distributions: Alcohol, Cigarettes, Clutter mod for more jars, lids, salt, and vinegar spawns. Additionally, see Rebalanced Yields: Butchering for more homesteading tweaks. Extra Info: -Compatible with all modded items as long as you can use them in the evolved recipes. -Jars allow you to store more produce than in a cooking pot or bowl as they are lighter. -Jars and lids returned in all expected scenarios, unless the lid is at low condition and gets broken. -The opened soup/stew/rice/pasta jars do not count as metal and can be microwaved. -Even though the jar is briefly displayed as 'uncooked', you will correctly receive cooked food if you decide to open it without canning. -The spice and seasoning icons are now transferred to the jar as of version 1.1.2 of this mod - they do not do so in vanilla when e.g. portioning soup from cooking pot into bowls. Future Plans: -Potentially create a realistic version - as the vanilla method is not safe for canning most of the things players are going to be canning. This will do for a video game for now, enjoy the expanded functionality. A pressure canner is used to reach higher than boiling temperatures (kills botulism spores) and preserve food that does not have naturally high acidity and/or salinity, and would otherwise be rendered unpalatable. The developers intended to allow the player to preserve high acidity vegetables in a water-bath canning method - this is suitable for many pickled vegetables, tomato sauces, relishes, jams, and chutneys. -Maybe a check for how big the food is, potentially allowing or requiring the player to use two jars. Compatibility: Lua implementations were used when possible to avoid overwriting vanilla scripts and functions. Only the vanilla canning 60/90 days script was affected. This mod will potentially extend the shelf life of any mods that allow more jarring and preservation as long as they use the vanilla script. Translations are provided for: DE, EN, ES, FR, IT, PL, PTBR, RU, and UA. Thanks to Refúgio Z for PTBR, and WRex for UA translations. Permissions: Please do not modpack or reupload. If this mod is deleted, you are welcome to reupload to Steam Workshop only. Thanks and enjoy! description: Changes the animal yields to provide more realistic, immersive quantities of meat from butchering. Build 42.12 note: Compatible with the latest update. Description: As you can see from the screenshots, vanilla butchering for larger animals (i.e. not chickens) is a complete waste of time as of the latest unstable build. I have balanced the functions that create the resulting loot by hand to provide a balance between realism and immersion for gameplay. An actual, fully grown cow would certainly provide more beef than this mod, but it certainly should provide more than three chickens, as it currently stands in vanilla gameplay. I strongly recommend you use the Butcher Hook Animal Size Fix mod as it provides further balancing to the butchering aspect of gameplay, the developers have missed out a vital parameter related to animal size when factoring in the butcher hook. From the author: To make a long story short, since build 42 came out any and all animals would have a static size of 0.6 on the hook due to being resized for the UI, the issue is that this ALSO affected the value used for butchering and harvesting meat from them. As such all this mod does it add an additional parameter to be passed to the butchering util file that uses the correct animal size rather than the static 0.6 that was used before. No animal meat values are changed or modified by this mod in any way, this only affects animals butchered on the hook. If this changes - being true as of the latest unstable build (October 2025), I will update the description accordingly. Similarly, if butchering is rebalanced by the developers, I shall make sure my mod is still relevant. You can use the mod Bug Zapper 9000 instead, but please load my mod after, by placing Rebalanced Yields: Butchering lower on the load order. This mod already includes one of the bug fixes, and the same script needed to be modified to rebalance butchering. Extra Info: -Cuts of meat, from all animals, weighing more than 0.4 can be halved with a craft recipe. -Overall, this mod does not focus on just increasing the amount of meat pieces that animals provide by butchering, but making sure that you do not get stacks of small unusable pieces. You will be getting larger cuts weighing up to several kilograms, you can process these in recipes and your aim upon butchering a large animal should switch to preservation. -Pigs have a moderate chance of providing lard, allowing the player to establish a sustainable source of cooking fat into the apocalypse. -Additionally, this mod tweaks the amounts of bones that animals, particularly small animals, have a chance to drop. Larger animals will still drop small bones (cows did not drop small bones, I have changed this so they do), and you should know that in vanilla it is possible to break larger bones with hammers to create fragments that can be used in recipes as small bones. -Penalty for not using the butcher hook reduced, as in vanilla, the lack of a butcher hook meant that large animals would yield half the pieces of meat, therefore twice as little in terms of hunger reduction and calories. Also, no leather. Using a butchering hook still provides a 20% bonus to base-defined animal values, so you would, in theory, benefit from 20% increase in meat yield by using it. -Vanilla roadkill would result in mangled scraps, as both the minimum and maximum yields for number of items would be halved, and the "meat ratio" (i.e. meat to nothing ratio, based on theoretical yield of the animal weight and your butchering skill) would be randomly set to a low amount. I have reduced the penalty for roadkill, however it is still sizeable, so you should avoid running over any animals that you can shoot or otherwise kill in melee. -This mod does not add any items that did not exist in the base game, however as hunger reduction/calories/protein/fats, etc. are governed by the base items as well as the scripts that spawn them, I had to use a lua implementation to tweak the calories of base meat items to real life values, and this should not conflict with mods that alter these items. Future Plans: -Make sure that rodents and raccoons (which use the Base.Smallanimalmeat item) are balanced further as it really is anyone's guess as to what is going on between the butchering and the animal trapping system. -Bacon from pigs maybe? Compatibility: Load this mod after the Butcher Hook Animal Size Fix and/or Bug Zapper 9000 by placing Rebalanced Yields: Butchering lower on the load order. This mod overwrites the AnimalPartsDefinitions.lua file responsible for the butchering loot and so will almost always be incompatible with other mods that affect the butchering loot. Additionally, this mod tweaks 2 functions in ButcheringUtil.lua (to make changes to "no butchering hook" and "roadkill" penalties) and therefore will probably be incompatible with other butchery balancing mods. Permissions: Please do not modpack or reupload. If this mod is deleted, you are welcome to reupload to Steam Workshop only. Thanks and enjoy! description: Compatibility: Build 42.12.3 to Build 42.20.1+ Trap Manager is a clean and practical interface for monitoring, comparing, and understanding your traps in Project Zomboid Build 42. It gathers your traps into one clear window, shows their current status in a sortable table, explains key values with helpful tooltips, and includes a built-in simulator to preview vanilla catch chances by animal, trap, bait, zone, and Trapping skill. Trap Manager does not change vanilla trap mechanics. It only reads, organizes, and explains trap information. Sidebar shortcut: hover the Zone icon on the left sidebar to reveal the matching Trap button, then click it to open or close Trap Manager. What Trap Manager Does Shows all your traps in one window instead of checking them one by one. Displays trap data in a clear, sortable table. Adds tooltips that explain what each value means. Includes a built-in catch chance simulator. Helps compare traps, bait, zones, and skill levels more easily. Keeps vanilla gameplay untouched: no changes to capture logic, items, recipes, animals, loot, or odds. Trap List Window View all your traps in one place. Sort rows by clicking column headers. Resize columns by dragging separators. Hide or show columns from the header context menu. Use per-row visibility toggles to temporarily hide rows from the list. Check practical details such as bait, freshness, distance, catch chance, hours alive, trap status, and more. Built-in Catch Chance Simulator The simulator lets you preview vanilla trapping chances by combining: Animal Trap Bait Zone Trapping Skill Selecting an animal can automatically populate other fields with valid values, and tooltips help explain how each factor affects the result. Note: displayed chances are based on vanilla trapping logic. They are best understood as base vanilla candidate/catch chances. Mods that change trapping rules, cold modifiers, nearby-player behavior, bait logic, or trap processing may affect the real result in-game. Window Controls Refresh — updates the trap list immediately. Auto — enables hourly in-game auto-refresh while the window is open. Vector — draws a line from your character to the trap currently hovered in the table. Reset — restores your default column layout. Full — shows every column and resizes the window to fit them. Show all — temporarily shows rows you previously hid. Mod Options Choose the hotkey used to open or close the window. Enable or disable hourly auto-refresh. Enable or disable longer explanatory tooltips. Choose which columns should be shown after pressing Reset. Restore factory defaults for the reset layout at any time. How to Open Trap Manager Left sidebar: hover Zone, then click the slide-out Trap button. Hotkey: use the key configured in ModOptions. Compatibility Compatible with Project Zomboid Build 42.12.3 to 42.20.1+. Designed specifically for Build 42. Works in Singleplayer and Multiplayer. Safe to add or remove from existing saves, since it is UI-focused. Does not alter vanilla trap mechanics. Generally compatible with other UI mods. Mods that heavily change vanilla trapping internals may affect simulator accuracy or trap data display. Languages Includes translations for: AR, CA, CH, CN, DA, DE, EN, ES, FI, FR, HU, ID, IT, JP, KO, NL, PH, PL, PTBR, RU, TR, UA If your language is not available, the mod falls back to English. Translation suggestions and corrections are welcome. FAQ Does Trap Manager change catch chances or trap mechanics? No. It only reads, organizes, and explains trap information. Are the simulator chances exact? They are based on vanilla trapping logic and are intended as practical guidance. If several animals are valid candidates at the same time, vanilla may choose between candidates, so the displayed value should be read as a base chance estimate rather than a guaranteed final outcome. What is the difference between “Shown columns” and “Default columns”? Shown columns are the columns visible right now. Default columns are the columns restored when you press Reset. What does “Apply factory defaults” do? It restores the original default column setup used by Reset. What does “Vector” do? It draws a line from your character to the last trap you hovered in the table, helping you orient yourself more easily. Is the mod performance-heavy? No. It is lightweight, and auto-refresh only runs once per in-game hour while the window is open. Feature Summary One clean window for all your traps. Sortable, resizable, and hideable columns. Helpful tooltips across the interface. Built-in catch chance simulator. Sidebar shortcut and hotkey support. Native Build 42 ModOptions. Save-safe and gameplay-safe. Multilingual support. Install it, open the panel, and understand your traps at a glance. Feedback & Bug Reports Feedback, bug reports, balance suggestions, compatibility reports, and translation improvements are always welcome. Useful reports include: Project Zomboid build. Trap Manager version. Singleplayer, MP Host, or Dedicated Server. Relevant mod list and load order. Whether another mod changes trapping behavior. Steps to reproduce the issue. Console errors or logs, if available. More Mods & Feedback You can find my other Project Zomboid mods here If you find Trap Manager useful, please consider leaving a thumbs up and adding it to your favorites — it helps other players discover the mod. description: A simple b42 port of my "Item Stories" b41 mod. I've bundles all item stories into an All-In-One package, as requested. This mod makes buildings more "lived in" by spawning items inside them. It is picking what to spawn randomly from a 'story' system. If you've tried my "'immersive barricaded start" mod , this will spawn items in a similar way, but for every building, and at a much lower chance. Since this mod will spawn extra items, it is recommended you play with LOWER loot than usually would. I'd say it's pretty balanced so far, but I'm open to feedback. Start and Peak sandbox settings : start settings are applied before the start day, peak settings applied after the peak day, and proportionally scaled settings are applied between start day and peak day. Other stories can easily be added via submods, to spawn specific items in specific rooms and/or on specific furniture sprites for example. List of Item Stories included : "Room Loot": Spawns an item picked from the loot table of the room the item will spawn in. Kitchen items in kitchens, bedroom items in bedrooms, etc. Chance are low and customizable through sandbox settings, and it can trigger in ALL rooms and on ALL furniture sprites. Propane Tanks in Garages :Triggers in garages, basements, and sheds, spawns propane tanks ZuperCart's Supermarket Carts in Stores: Triggers in a variety of stores. Spawns Zupercart's supermarket carts. (Requires Zupercart mod, this story isn't used if you don't enable Zupercart) ZuperCart's Trolleys in Warehouses & Factories : Triggers in a variety of factories & storage areas. (Requires Zupercart mod, this story isn't used if you don't enable Zupercart) Pool cues and balls on billiard tables : self explatnatory Pallet crates in warehouses : Triggers in a variety of factories & storage areas. (Requires Forklift mod, this story isn't used if you don't enable Forklift) (New for this version) Rideable stories : Spawns a bicycle/skateboard/kick scooter sometimes in garages, basements, and some other rooms. (Requires Bicycle or Skateboard or Kick Scooter mod, this story isn't used if you don't enable one of them) I've removed the "Tire Racks in Mechanics and Garages" story , it was too much of a pain in the ass to deal with. Taking suggestions If you have an idea for an item story, you want an item to have a chance to spawn in some rooms or furnitures, leave it in the comments. Or better yet, simply make a mod yourself that uses the framework. You only need to know how set up a lua table, how building rooms are named (Click here for a list of PZ's rooms), and how to check furniture sprite names using the Brush Tool of PZ's debug mode. Though keep in mind that stories can only spawn inside a building (or basement). 'Forest' stories aren't possible, for example. Limitations Randomized Houses: Item stories are only generated in rooms that have not generated a vanilla randomized house story event. So if you absolutely want Item Stories to trigger on every room, you'll need set the Sandbox Setting "Meta" -> "Randomized House Chance" to "Never". Tilesets with no surface offsets : Some mods use tilesets that haven't properly mapped their tiles' furniture surface offsets, which means some of their furniture tiles will be considered as floor instead of furniture. Which generally means much lower chances of item story spawns. Even some furniture in vanilla don't have their surface offset mapped. One example would be the strongbox tiles, the I can't really do anything about it. The devs have said they're going to implement a sudo-3d map for each sprite, but it'll be a while before they release it in a build. These sprites can be recognized easily by simply trying to "Place Item" on one of these tiles to see that it's not working. description: -Personal Notice (Update)- Thank you all for the support! Hey everyone, I've been away for a while taking a long break from being online and gaming, been mostly focusing on my family and my dad especially with his cancer, however I'm happy to report his cancer psa levels have dramatically reduced these past couple of months thanks to the injections he's been receiving, while he's still unable to walk he's recovered dramatically and is faring MUCH better than back in December when this whole nightmare unraveled. I wanna give a much heartfelt thank you to everyone who donated and provided support with your kind prayers or words my way, thank you! I will be returning to update my mods here. Are you disappointed that Generators no longer light up the outside world? Does it feel like darkness just consumes every corner of the world? Do you miss when generators would light up the city or your base? Well darkness no more! Bring the lights back to nights! This mod, restores a feature intentionally removed in B42 by TIS, where streetlights and world lights like shops, signs, and billboards, turn on when a nearby generator is connected and running. Streetlight colors are customizable too! Choose from several different presets (Neutral White, Defective LED, Crimson Red, etc.) or set your own RGB colors! Important Note: Generator Streetlights Restored, uses its own lighting system and is not tied to the vanilla power grid or vanilla lighting system... for now. This also means the mod can affect client-side performance, however i've optimized it as much as possible to prevent that, but there's only so much Optimization i can do with a system like this (thanks TIS, sigh). Consider this mod a WIP Project, so expect bugs and issues. Features Generator Streetlights Restored works in single-player with multiplayer support. Decorative world signs and billboards light up too. Supports several languages! Chinese, Japanese, Russian, Turkish, Thai, Portuguese, Spanish, Polish and Korean! Custom streetlight colors support! Use any of the presets or use your own RGB colors! Adjustable tile radius for lighting, set how far each generator powers world lights. Intensity and glow radius, tune overall brightness and glow size. Customize all this and more in Sandbox Options! Known Issues and Bugs - The tile lighting range in Sandbox Options is a bit bugged and won't actually "respect" a value past a certain amount. Afaik values 10 - 60 work fine. - Performance degrades when more than 1 generator is placed an area, you may notice hitching or micro stuttering if using multiple generators near each other in one area, i recommend you place generators far away from each other in different areas, if you want it to light up more of an area, raise the tile lighting range however raising this value too much can also cause performance problems, so test whatever feels best for you. Additional Note: I will most likely end up rewriting the entire lighting logic and just use the vanilla lighting system instead (since that's native and far better for performance) but we'll see, i have to look at what's possible first, as im not sure if TIS removed the original coding for generators powering world lighting. - A few bugs remain with the lighting. For example, Color Presets are actually only supposed to apply to streetlights exclusively but for now it's applying to a lot of other world lights which wasn't intended. May or may not fix that since it's not really much of a problem and some people may like it so we'll see. - Besides that, there's probably more bugs that i didn't notice or didn't catch, i did try to test this system a lot and fix whatever i could but nothings perfect. As always report them down below in the comments or on a post. Incompatibilities - Any mod that does something similar to my mod. (Lighting mods, Generator overhaul mods etc) Possible list of incompatible mods: Light Switch Plus (B42): https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3418843205 Ultimate Generator Overhaul: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3478628177 Reporting Bugs - This mod is complex, i need exact details of your bugs, so please provide detailed reports in the Discussions section. No promises to fix all issues. Consider donating and buy me a coffee! (Click on the image below to donate) Workshop ID: 3578735933 Mod ID: GenStreetlightRestore

description: Quick'n'Auto Mark TL;DR Quick'n'Auto Mark automatically marks buildings on your map when you enter them and gives you a compact, slide-up dock for fast manual marking, quick color selection, easy symbol placement, symbol scaling, and nearby mark cleanup. If you also use Where Is My Car?, you can now assign a separate vehicle-only favorite color by right-clicking a color in the Quick'n'Auto Mark dock. If you like using the map a lot, I also highly recommend my companion minimap mod: TwisTonFire - minimap What this mod adds Automatic building marks When you enter a building, the mod can automatically place a marker at its center. Configurable auto-mark delay Choose whether buildings are marked immediately or after a delay of 1 / 2 / 3 / 5 / 10 in-game minutes. Manual marks take priority If you manually place your own symbol inside a building, that building’s automatic mark is suppressed so your own map notes stay in control. Slide-up quick dock A small dock appears at the bottom of the screen when you hover there, giving you fast access to colors, common symbols, erase tools, settings, scale controls, and minimap access. Full symbol picker Open a full tabbed symbol picker for more icons beyond the quick-access buttons. Smart color handling Your available colors depend on the pens and pencils you actually carry. Mixed colors become available when you carry the right combination of writing tools. Separate vehicle color support If Where Is My Car? is active, you can right-click a color in the dock to assign a separate vehicle-only favorite color without changing your normal Quick'n'Auto Mark color. Marker size control Use the built-in slider to adjust symbol size, reset it back to default, and fine-tune nearby marks more easily while playing. Nearby manual mark eraser Carry an eraser and you can remove nearby manual marks placed through the mod without wiping your entire map clean. Vanilla minimap integration Open the vanilla minimap directly from the dock, or combine this mod with TwisTonFire - minimap for an even better experience. Sidebar map popup support Adds an extra dock toggle to the map popup for quick access. Why it feels good to use The dock is compact, fast, and stays out of the way until you need it. The mod is built around the vanilla map and symbol system, so using it feels natural instead of intrusive. Your favorite color, dock state, and related settings are remembered. If you use Where Is My Car?, you can keep a separate vehicle color without changing your normal marking color. You can combine auto-marking with manual notes instead of being forced into one style. It is designed as a practical quality-of-life tool for players who actually use the minimap during normal gameplay. Settings included Turn automatic building marks ON/OFF Choose the delay before a building is marked Choose the auto-mark symbol Adjust the symbol scale Reset the scale back to its default value Quick Dock features Fast color swatches One-click quick symbols Right-click color support for Where Is My Car? Full symbol picker button Nearby manual mark erase button Scale slider + reset button Settings button Minimap button Compatibility & performance Designed to be lightweight and practical during normal gameplay. Built around the vanilla world map, map symbols, and minimap systems. Generally compatible with most mods, but mods that heavily replace the map UI, map popup, minimap behavior, or world map symbols may conflict. Best experience if you are already used to marking loot spots, bases, vehicles, generators, gas stations, or points of interest on your map. FAQ Do I need pens or pencils? Yes. Your available colors depend on the writing tools you carry. Can I still place marks manually? Absolutely. Manual marking is a core part of the mod, and your own manual marks can override building auto-marks. Can I change marker size? Yes. Use the size slider or the reset button. Can I remove marks again? Yes, nearby manual marks can be erased with an eraser. Can I use a separate vehicle color with Where Is My Car? Yes. Right-click a color in the Quick'n'Auto Mark dock to assign a vehicle-only favorite color. If no separate vehicle color is set, it will fall back to your normal favorite color. What if auto-marking does not happen? Make sure Auto Marks are enabled, make sure you are actually inside a building, and make sure you have a valid writing tool available. Will removing the mod erase existing marks? No. Symbols already placed on your map remain saved as map symbols. Controller? No, just no. Recommended companion mod For the best experience, pair this with: TwisTonFire - minimap It makes using map-based QoL mods feel much more comfortable during actual gameplay. description: You're bitten. You have two choices. Wait until you succumb to the virus or take matters into your hands. Cut off that infected part and live to die another day. This version of The Only Cure has been rebuilt from scratch to support future additions and to feel as close as possible as a vanilla mechanic. Supports Single Player and Multiplayer. Host Mode may work but is UNSUPPORTED! Setup [strike]Use it with the following mods for the intended experience: Fancy Handwork Brutal Handwork Place them BEFORE The Only Cure in your mod list![/strike] At the moment, the mods listed here aren't compatible with B42. Quick guide Amputation Get some kind of Saw, Axe, or Machete, right click on it, and choose which limb to amputate. You can also drag n' drop the item directly into the afflicted area to start cutting it off. If you have some bandages and\or stitches in your inventory you will automatically use them, multiplying the chances of your survival. If you have a tourniquet, place it on the correct side to dampen the amount of damage you will take after you're done amputating the limb. Keep in mind that if you amputate your upper arm, you won't be able to equip any prosthesis. After you've amputated a limb, you will gain skill points for the amputated side, making timed actions faster in due time. Cicatrization You can check the cicatrization status of an amputated limb from your Health Panel From time to time, you should clean your wounds with a bandage to help the cicatrization process. If your limb isn't completely cicatrized, you can still equip prosthetic limbs, but that can trigger random bleedings from that area. Prosthetics If you're missing a hand, you won't be able to do a lot of things, such as equipping two-handed weapons. With prosthetics limbs, you can fix that. There are two prosthesis type that can be crafted\found in medical areas: Hook Prosthesis Arm Prosthesis The main difference between the twos is that your actions will take longer with the Hook Prosthesis. When you equip a prosthetic limb, you will slowly gain skill points in the Prosthesis Familiarity perk, making actions more speedy in due time. Admin tools If something strange happened, an admin can reset TOC mechanics on any player by right clicking on them and select "Reset Amputations". They could also do the opposite by clicking on "Force Amputation" for each amputable limb. Issues and bugs? Got any issues or found some pesky bugs? Report them on GitHub! Credits Want to support me? Yes, confirmed working on Build 42.20 Stable. ▶ Is the Naginata one-handed or two-handed? It's a two-handed weapon. ▶ How do I repair my Naginata? Once repaired, sharpening with the whetstone will work normally again. ▶ Why does my Naginata keep losing its edge so fast? The lower a weapon's condition, the faster it loses sharpness during combat. Keeping the weapon's condition topped up through regular repairs will slow this down — letting condition drop too low creates a cycle where it dulls faster and faster. ▶ Where do I find a Naginata, or how do I craft one? Find the recipe magazine in the world, or unlock it automatically by leveling up your MetalWelding skill. ▶ Does the vanilla melee weapon rarity setting in Sandbox affect how often Naginatas spawn? Yes — both the vanilla weapon rarity sandbox setting and this mod's own drop chance settings affect spawn frequency together. ▶ Can I adjust how common they are? Yes — every item in the mod has its own configurable drop chance in the Sandbox options, in addition to the vanilla rarity setting above. ▶ Is it compatible with your other Legendary mods (Backpack, DuffelBag, Satchel, Cap, etc.)? Yes, all Legendary mods are designed to work together safely. ▶ Does it work in multiplayer? Yes, confirmed working in multiplayer. 🔄Updates 🔹[v.3.0.0] Updated and optimized for 42.20 stable. description: Unseasonal Weather – Dynamic Climate Events & Radio Forecasts Does the weather feel predictable after a few in-game weeks? Unseasonal Weather adds a layer of unpredictable, season-aware climate events on top of the vanilla system — now enhanced with an immersive radio-based weather awareness system. The world no longer tells you exactly what’s coming. You’ll have to listen, interpret, and decide. What this mod does Dynamic seasonal weather events: each season has its own pool of climate anomalies (heat waves, blizzards, fog banks, tropical rains, cold fronts…). New Radio Forecast System (v1.3): weather hints are broadcast over radio frequencies using ambiguous, human-like reports. Imperfect information: forecasts can be normal, false, erroneous or interrupted — just like in real life. Automatic start & recovery: events trigger naturally and fade back into vanilla climate after several in-game hours. Soft randomness: every event receives subtle intensity variations — no two events feel the same. Rare & ultra-rare cinematic events: extremely uncommon atmospheric phenomena with unique visual tone. Radio Forecasting – How it works (v1.3) The weather is no longer obvious. Once per in-game day, the system may schedule a radio forecast. [* ]Forecasts are broadcast on a dedicated frequency and must be actively listened to. Messages are intentionally ambiguous: they describe air pressure, humidity, wind, heat or cold — never exact events. Some forecasts are misleading, incomplete or interrupted by interference. Silence is also possible — no broadcast doesn’t mean safety. Not all radios receive the signal from Unseasonal Weather Network. You are not told what will happen. You are given clues — and survival depends on how you interpret them. How to Use the Radio Forecast System Find a working radio or walkie-talkie. Equip it or place it nearby and make sure it is powered on. Tune the device to the Unseasonal Weather Network frequency (112.2 MHz). Set the volume high enough to hear broadcasts clearly. Wait for a scheduled forecast window: Morning broadcasts: typically between 08:00 and 11:00. Night broadcasts: typically between 20:00 and 23:00. (The active window depends on your Sandbox settings.) Listen carefully to the message — tone, wording and uncertainty matter. Important: Forecasts are not guaranteed every day. Some broadcasts may be false, erroneous or interrupted. Silence does not mean safety — sometimes there is simply no signal. Radio Teasers – Signal Noise & Early Warnings Sometimes the radio speaks before it knows what to say. Short, ambiguous broadcasts may appear days or hours before a real forecast — hinting that atmospheric conditions are being monitored. These messages do not guarantee an upcoming transmission. Some are vague. Some are precise. Some are simply wrong. They are not alerts. They are not schedules. They are fragments of information. Listening is a choice. Understanding is never guaranteed. Note about walkie-talkies: Even if a frequency is set, walkie-talkies do not receive automated radio broadcasts. This is a vanilla engine limitation. Use a radio device to listen to forecasts. Radio starts tuned automatically How climate events work Each in-game day rolls a chance for a special weather event. If triggered, an event is selected based on the current season (or from rare global pools). Temperature, fog, wind, rain and cloud density are overridden using the vanilla ClimateManager. Events last several in-game hours (sandbox configurable). Once finished, all overrides are cleanly removed and vanilla weather resumes. Rare Global Events Uncommon atmospheric phenomena that can occur in any season: SuperFog – extremely dense fog with near-zero visibility. Crystal Clear Day – unnaturally clean skies and sharp light. Moonlit Clarity – bright, cold nights with no fog. Blood Sky – heavy reddish clouds and oppressive atmosphere. Static Storm – storm clouds without rain. Ashfall / Dustfall – drifting grey haze. Frozen Dawn – icy sunrise with pale fog. Silver Skies – metallic-bright overcast skies. Ultra-Rare Cinematic Events Extremely unlikely. Not shown in sandbox settings. Solar Hellburst – a harsh red-orange solar glare, dune-like and oppressive. White Death – a polar-blue atmospheric freeze with piercing cold tones. If you see one… you were unlucky. Or lucky. Hardcore Temperature Extremes For players who enable hardcore settings: Extreme heat can force you indoors. Extreme cold can become lethal without shelter. The world won’t kill you instantly — but staying outside is a mistake. All temperature changes are additive and scale with sandbox intensity. Debug Commands UW.startEvent() UW.endEvent() Useful for testing, servers, and admins. Compatibility & Performance Build: Project Zomboid Build 42 Singleplayer / Multiplayer: supported (server-side install required for MP). Performance: extremely lightweight — periodic checks only. Compatibility: works with most weather mods unless they hard-override climate every tick. description: Airdrops This mod allows you to spawn airdrops containing valuable loot or animals (in a living or deceased state). A clear marker will appear on the map showing the drop zone. When the crate lands, a signal fire will light up at the exact location to help players locate the drop. Key Features Advanced Sandbox Customization: Set the drop frequency your way: from 1 hour to 1 whole year. Progressive Drop Timer: Dynamic interval adjustment based on a multiplier (-5.0 to +5.0). Each airdrop can make the next one more or less frequent! Configure spawn-near-player settings (chance, min/max radius). The airdrop can now land anywhere on the map, no matter how far from the player! (try a radius of 1000–2000). Visual Effects Control: Choose drop site effects - none, fire with lighting, smoke, or both for enhanced immersion. Explosive Cleanup System: Configure what happens when airdrops expire - explosion with sound, zombie spawn, aggressive animal spawn, or nothing. Effect Power Scaling: Adjust the intensity of cleanup effects from subtle (1) to maximum (200) for dramatic finales. Turn off the map marker for a true challenge and hunt down the airdrop before it vanishes! All sandbox changes (presets, defaults, intervals) apply in real-time without a restart. Diverse & Configurable Loot: 11 Loot Presets: Medical, Survival, Tools, Weapons (with ammo), Materials, Food & Drinks, Kitchenware, Junk + Accessories + Bags, Clothing, Animals, and Books. Animals Preset: The crate includes hay and animal feed. Exactly one animal (live or corpse) will spawn 2–3 tiles from the crate. Mod-Friendly: Loot is drawn from ProceduralDistributions for maximum variety and mod compatibility. Full Control: Override loot lists via AirdropCategories.ini or use custom tables for coordinates and loot distribution. Immersive Gameplay Mechanics: Your character says one of five random lines when a nearby drop occurs (EN/RU). Game speed returns to normal on airdrop touchdown. If sleeping, your character will wake up (only if not drunk and fatigue < 80%). Visual Effects: Configurable drop site effects - fire with lighting, smoke, or both for up to 2 in-game hours. Explosive Cleanup: Airdrops now explode when their timer expires! Choose from explosion, zombie spawn, or aggressive animal spawn effects. Radio messages alert you to the airdrop zone. A beeper shows your distance — follow the signal! Daily Schedule Broadcasts: Automatic radio notifications from 03:00 to 06:00 every day, informing you of the time remaining until the next airdrop. Messages are fully localized with proper grammar for all supported languages. World Interaction & Dangers: The airdrop crate can be smashed open with a Sledgehammer. Zombies may appear near the airdrop site. If the "Bandits" mod is active, bandits may appear near the drop. Progressive Timer Examples Based on default settings: Airdrop Frequency = 5%, Min Interval = 24h How it works: Airdrop Frequency (5%): Each hour, there's a 5% chance to spawn an airdrop (if interval allows) Min Interval (24h): Minimum time between airdrops (base interval) Progressive Multiplier: Modifies the interval after each successful airdrop Formula: New interval = Current interval + (Current interval × Multiplier) Note: Intervals are capped between 1 hour (minimum) and 8760 hours (1 year maximum). Save Compatibility & Airdrop Cleanup The mod maintains full save compatibility — installing or removing it will not corrupt your existing saves. Airdrop Lifecycle & Cleanup: Configurable Timer: Airdrops automatically expire after a set time (1-8760 hours, default 24h). Explosive Cleanup: When the timer expires, airdrops can explode with sound, spawn zombies, spawn aggressive animals, or simply disappear based on your settings. During explosions, nearby players will be knocked back and damaged, potentially suffering fractures, wounds, and other blast effects depending on their distance from the airdrop and the explosion power. Effect Power Control: Adjust cleanup effect intensity from subtle (1) to dramatic (200) for the perfect finale. Manual Destruction: You can destroy airdrop crates instantly with a Sledgehammer before they expire. Upon mod removal: Automatic Cleanup: All mod-spawned airdrops are scheduled for automatic removal after a total of 25 hours (a 24-hour cooldown period + a 1-hour buffer). Manual Cleanup: You can destroy the airdrop crates instantly in-game before removing the mod. Fallback Behavior: If ignored, the airdrops will eventually despawn via natural game mechanics. This may trigger a single, non-critical LUA error but will have no impact on gameplay or your save file. Note: Your saves remain safe at all stages of installation and removal. description: If you encounter minor issues or bugs, please first test this mod in isolation or with a minimal mod list. Then, please report the issue. Doing so makes it easier to investigate the cause of the issues. This mod was developed with this theme in mind. Bathing and showering in Project Zomboid should feel meaningful. This mod adds fully playable bath and shower mechanics, and gives them a real place in day-to-day survival. Bathing is not just flavor. It can become part of how you stay comfortable, clean, and in good condition over time. Is washing yourself in a sink, or even a toilet, really enough to feel clean? You might survive without proper bathing, but it should not feel ideal. Detailed feature notes are listed in the guide because of the Workshop character limit. This Mod Guide Features Adds an invisible body dirt parameter called Grime. The Grime system can be disabled in the sandbox options. Bathtubs function as fluid containers. Includes a dedicated bathtub UI. Adds "Take Shower" options to white showers and wall-mounted showers. Adds a "Take Bath" option to white bathtubs. Bathing Benefits: bathing can help relieve various negative stats. Items Body Shampoo: an alternative to soap. (Currently shower-only.) Bath Salt: can be added to tub water. There are currently 6 types, each with different bathing benefits. Automatic Clothing Change: includes a wide range of options. Improved Plumbing: bathtubs and showers can calculate available water from the total amount stored in all water collectors in the 3x3 area above them. Advanced Prep Location Detection: the character can better detect where to prepare for bathing. Toilets, cabinets, and other awkward tiles are given lower priority even if they are technically usable or closer. Bathtubs have four sprite variations: with shower (vanilla), cleaned with shower, without shower, and cleaned without shower. You can always climb over the edge of a bathtub. This can sometimes result in zombies ending up in the bathtub. Bathtubs and showers can be separated through the context menu. (Requires a pipe wrench.) Shower parts can be removed from bathtubs and deluxe showers. Removed shower parts can be packed, unpacked, and placed as wall-mounted showers. Deluxe showers can be crafted using shower parts and wall-mounted showers as materials. Separated bathtubs can have shower parts or wall-mounted showers attached again. Adds recipes for packing and unpacking shower parts and wall-mounted showers. Clean Tub variants are available for both attached-shower and separated-shower types. The improved Deluxe Shower can rotate in all four directions. The vanilla version only supports S and E. Recommended Mods Moodle Framework Bath Towels Overhaul Starlit Library I intentionally did not make these required, but I strongly recommend them because they support important parts of this mod. Compatible Mods Included Patches Ra's Body Mod - dedicated compatibility patch included. Lifestyle: Hobbies - bath and shower interactions are replaced by this mod's versions, and bathing can also reduce `hygieneNeed`. WaterPipes - bathtubs and showers can be connected to WaterPipes pipes. General Compatibility Automatic clothing change is designed to work with most body mods. Tomb's Player Body Overhaul - one of my personal favorites, and the one used in the screenshots. Wash or Rot - its grime system is similar but not identical, so the two mods can coexist and may work well together. Anthro Survivors - Although a patch is included, there is no guarantee that it will work correctly with the latest version. More Damaged Objects - [Important] Please be sure to perform an Auto Sort. Melos Tiles for Miles Tilepack - Various bathtubs and showers are available. Companion Dogs - Your following companion dog will wait while you bathe or shower. Please see Here for details. My mods are not compatible with mods that directly overwrite the base game's files or functions. Using them together may cause unexpected bugs. Incompatible Mods A mod that constantly control the character's state or animations. FAQ I filled the bathtub with water, but I can't see the water. When I get into the bathtub, my lower body disappears. A: Make sure "Take A Bath And Shower: DepthMap fix" is at the top of the mod list. Known Issues Uninstalling this mod while saving is not recommended, as it will leave a large amount of junk in the game. Some features may still behave oddly in split-screen mode. The bathtub and shower faucet menus are currently limited because the vanilla fluid menu is broken. If you speed up the game during the movement or clothing-change steps before or after showering, the action may stop midway. This happens because WalkAction and PathFindBehavior can be canceled at high game speeds. Translations EN ES - thanks to Kasualidad. FR - thanks to Bukaroo_Fr. IT - thanks to [ITA] D4rk JP KO - thanks to Reeul2. PL - thanks to Marcus Vallerdon. PTBR - thanks to SIMBAproduz. RU - thanks to phxntom1213. TR - thanks to xeotN. UA - thanks to SilentSalo. Please help support additional translations. Future Plans More balance adjustments. Additional polishing and expansion of bathing-related content. Metal barrel bathing. If you like my mod, please consider buying me a ko-fi. It helps support future modding work. Workshop ID: 3592172476 Mod ID: ATakeABathAndShowerDepthMap Mod ID: TakeABathAndShowerNew

description: Compatible with Project Zomboid Build 42.12.3 – 42.20.2 Formerly: Foraging Light Fix & Tuning Foraging Light Tuning lets you control how much flashlights help during Search Mode / Foraging in Project Zomboid Build 42. In newer B42 builds, an active flashlight can make foraging behave almost like full daylight. That avoids older light fluctuation issues, but it can also make night foraging feel too forgiving. This mod restores configurable control over flashlight brightness for foraging, so a flashlight can help a lot without necessarily removing the darkness penalty completely. Safe for existing saves. Can be enabled or disabled anytime. The Workshop name changed, but the internal mod ID remains ForagingLightFix to preserve save/server compatibility and existing sandbox settings. What This Mod Does Adds configurable flashlight support for Search Mode / Foraging. Lets you control the minimum effective light provided by an active flashlight. Allows flashlights to reduce the foraging Darkness Effect without always acting like full daylight. Keeps foraging light calculations stable while using flashlights. Allows stronger nearby light sources, such as daylight, ambient light, street lights, or lit rooms, to still improve visibility. Affects both the real Search Radius and the Investigate Area tooltip. How It Works Minimum-Light Mode OFF If a flashlight is equipped and turned on, foraging uses the newer vanilla-style behavior: Effective light can reach 1.0. Darkness Effect becomes 1. The flashlight removes the darkness penalty. Use this if you prefer the current vanilla flashlight behavior. Minimum-Light Mode ON If a flashlight is equipped and turned on, the flashlight provides at least the configured Min Light (Flashlight) value. Default value: 0.8. Higher value = less darkness penalty. Lower value = harsher night foraging. Nearby stable light sources can still raise the effective light level above the flashlight minimum. The mod keeps tuned flashlight behavior stable while avoiding older square-to-square light spikes. This is the recommended mode if you want flashlights to help at night without making darkness behave exactly like daylight. Sandbox Options All options appear under Foraging Light Tuning: Minimum-Light Mode — enables the tuned flashlight behavior. Min Light (Flashlight) — minimum effective light while using a flashlight when Minimum-Light Mode is enabled. Suggested Presets Easy: 1.0 — flashlight removes the darkness penalty. Moderate: 0.8 — default; useful flashlight support without fully replacing daylight. Tough: 0.5 — flashlights help, but night foraging remains punishing. Compatibility Notes Designed for Project Zomboid Build 42. Reviewed through Build 42.20.2. Compatible with Build 42.12.3 – 42.20.2. Does not add items, traits, recipes, map content, or permanent world data. Safe to add or remove from existing saves. Internal mod ID remains ForagingLightFix for compatibility with previous versions. Possible Conflicts Conflicts are more likely with mods that also change: Search Mode / Foraging light calculations. Foraging Darkness Effect behavior. Flashlight handling specifically for foraging. Translations Includes translations for: CH, CN, CS, DA, DE, EN, ES, FR, HU, IT, JP, KO, NO, PL, PT, PTBR, RO, RU, TR and UA Suggestions and corrections are welcome. More Mods & Feedback You can find my other Project Zomboid mods here If you find this Workshop item useful, please consider leaving a thumbs up and adding it to your favorites — it helps other players discover it. Feedback, bug reports, balance suggestions, and translation improvements are always welcome. Workshop ID: 3596478900 Mod ID: ForagingLightFix

description: PoweredBuildings V2 Singleplayer + Multiplayer alpha Originally I just wanted to make a small mod that makes it possible to power an entire building with generators. Zomboid had other plans. Turn standard generators into whole-building power systems. Generator Powered Buildings lets you connect generators to a building and run that building as one managed power network instead of relying only on the normal nearby-generator coverage. You can link multiple generators into one pool, keep their vanilla outdoor radius, auto-refuel from linked storage, and monitor the whole setup from a dedicated Building Power Info window. You can access the full Building Power Info window from a light switch once the building has power (Generator -> Connect to Building -> Turn On). Main features Link up to 10 generators to one building. Generators still keep their vanilla 20x20 outdoor radius, so you can place them around the building for more coverage outside. Supports powered coverage from Z-3 to Z+16. Multi-level Generator placement Access building power management from generators and from supported light switches in powered buildings. Live Building Power Info window with pool fuel, condition, strain, power draw, active consumers, linked barrels, and heating data. Click a generator in the info window and your character will walk to it. Share power load and fuel usage across connected generator pools. Power strain system: if the building is too large for the active generators, fuel usage goes up. Link petrol barrels and compatible storage mods to the same generator pool for extra fuel storage and automatic refueling. Power grid extends about 3 tiles beyond the building footprint, so some appliances outside can still stay powered. Heating controls with target temperature support. Deactivate heating in the thermostat while grid power is still on to save fuel. Upper-floor heating placement support. Powered player-built buildings and player-built annexes on vanilla buildings. Automatic rebuilding of building consumer data on chunk load to avoid stale save data. Working placeable vanilla light switches. Generators have special multipliers What you do in game Place a generator near the building you want to power. Connect the generator to the building. Turn it on and let the mod scan the building's powered consumers. Open the Building Power Info window from the generator or a supported light switch in the powered building. Optionally link petrol barrels or compatible storage to the same generator pool for automatic refueling. Use the window to monitor pool fuel, strain, active lights and appliances, and heating settings. Building mode currently still inherits the vanilla generator outdoor radius outside the building footprint. High strain currently increases fuel usage, but extra generator damage from strain is not final yet. How It Works Place rain barrels and connect them with pipes. The system assigns a group ID to each pipe network and "marks" adjacent barrels. On each interval, pipes check for nearby crops and water them using the group's shared water. After watering, the mod balances water across all barrels in that group to avoid draining a single barrel first. description: About this mod: This mod makes temperatures more realistic, it completely changes how the air temperature feels, even when indoors. So at winter time you have to make sure to layer up, find some heaters, and close all doors and windows. In the summer time you can't be wearing too much clothing and run around in the heat or you'll risk overheating! Credit to my buddy NikoTM for making the custom heater models and textures! ------------------------------ FEATURES ------------------------------ Advanced simulation system for indoor temperatures. Warm air will flow out or in, depending on the outside temperature, if there's open doors, windows, or missing walls. It will also flow out of gaps under doors/around windows, so no house is fully sealed. Fully MP compatible, with specific code that makes sure that all players see the same temperatures. To save on performance and to make the simulation easier to apply, the indoor temperatures are updated every 1 minute of in-game time. Rooms in the same building will equalize towards the same temperature based on room sizes and their temperatures, if they have open or closed doors between them, and which floors they are on. Offline simulation system so even if you leave a building and return later, it will have updated temperatures based on the openings to the outside, and active heaters inside. If the world power is on then buildings still have active HVAC/Central heating systems that keep the building warm, but when the power goes out they will cool down based on the outdoor temperature. Supports huge buildings like malls, hospitals, and the airport New body temperature simulation which changes the efficiency of clothing, you will need to layer up with warm clothing to be fully protected. Hypothermia is now deadlier, and you will become hypothermic quickly if you don't have appropriate clothing. Supports player-made buildings. 4 new custom heaters, 2 electricity powered, 2 propane powered, with a custom UI to control the power and automatic shut-off timer. Vanilla heat sources are included in the simulation, so fireplaces, campfires, grills and ovens can be used to warm up. Standing near a heat source will warm you up faster. Car heaters also works for the simulation, so if you have gas in your car it can be used to stay warm (except in extremely cold temperatures). [EXPERIMENTAL] Food Freezing, this feature needs to be enabled in the sandbox settings and will cause some slight stutter. Simulated temperatures affects food, so food can now freeze at any point when the temperature is below freezing. You can put food outside, inside, in containers, or in your inventory, and they will freeze as long as the temperature is below freezing. ---------------------------- MOD INCOMPATIBILITIES ---------------------------- It's FULLY COMPATIBLE with other temperature mods that directly affect the outdoor temperatures, like Cold Winters or Unseasonal Weather or Cryogenic Winter INCOMPATIBLE with mods that change the digital watch UI as I had to implement my own to make my temperature values show up properly. If you use a mod to set the alarm by right clicning the UI, that feature has been added to my watch UI. Should be compatible with all clothing mods as long as they use proper insulation values. ---------------------------- FAQ ---------------------------- Is it safe to add mid-save? Yes it can be added/removed mid-save. In very rare cases when removing the mod mid-save there could be an issue with NaN values for temperature and wetness. To fix that use this mod: NaN Values Fix Also due to how my mod disables the thermoregulator, you need to fully restart the game after uninstalling the mod to make sure the thermoregulator resets to the default values. Does it make winters colder/summers warmer? No this mod does not actually change the outdoor temperatures, it uses the outdoor temperatures to set indoor temperatures. To have colder winters/warmer summers you need to combine it with other mods that changes the outdoor temperatures (like Cold Winters for example) Why am I getting cold so quickly even when wearing many layers of warm clothing? Most likely it's because the clothes are wet or have holes in them, or there's a strong wind causing you to get colder faster. Wet clothing is your number one enemy for staying warm, it lowers the insulation values a lot, so make sure to stay nice and dry with many layers! All the doors and windows are closed, so why is the room I'm in still getting colder? There is a small passive heat loss due to no house being 100% insulated, so it loses about 1 degree of heat per hour. ------------------------------ PLANNED FEATURES ------------------------------ Add more heater types and an air conditioner ---------------------------- KNOWN ISSUES ---------------------------- In rare cases it's possible that this mod triggers a vanilla bug that sets wetness and temperature values to NaN when it's uninstalled mid-save. To fix that, use this mod: NaN Values Fix If you have any issues, please join my Discord and post in the Support channel: ------------------------------ TRANSLATIONS ------------------------------ English Polish (Credit to Slav3106) French (Credit to Bonstalin) Ukrainian (Credit to Сonceived in a sock) Russian (Credit to Doctor Sex and Jackson Frost) German (Credit to Jackson Frost) Turkish (Credit to @Caesar) Spanish (Credit to @Ciro2020) This mod can only be added to and extended with the express permission from the original creator.
