description: NOTE: NOT MULTIPLAYER COMPATIBLE FOR 42.20 STABLE, SINGLEPLAYER USE ONLY Goose's Kentucky National Guard Professions Authentic 1993 KYNG professions, loadouts, and equipment for the Knox Exclusion Zone. This mod adds seven historically grounded professions drawn from the units and equipment the Kentucky National Guard would realistically have deployed during the 1993 Knox Exclusion Zone operation. Each profession comes with a profession-appropriate loadout with realistic ammo counts, rations and field equipment that are designed to be balanced, immersive and true to the era. If you want your playthrough to actually feel like you survived the first hours of the apocalypse as a member of the military, this is where you start. Professions CBRN Specialist (MOS 74D, -10 Points) Chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear specialist from the 103rd Chemical Battalion. Combat Engineer (MOS 12B, -16 Points) Field engineer from the 201st Engineer Battalion trained in demolitions and obstacle clearance. Equipped for breaching, fortification and improvised munitions. Combat Medic (MOS 91B, -12 Points) Medical specialist from the 917th Medical Company of the 201st Engineer Battalion. Carries a full trauma kit and field pharmaceuticals enough to give field care and sustain a squad of four. Infantryman (MOS 11B, -10 Points) Standard light infantryman from the 1st Battalion, 149th Infantry Regiment. Carries a full combat load with appropriate rations, protective equipment and standard issue weapons. Military Police (MOS 95B, -12 Points) Perimeter security and law enforcement specialist from the 198th Military Police Battalion. Equipped for checkpoint duty and civil control operations within the KEZ. Motor Transport Operator (MOS 88M, -10 Points) Logistics driver and vehicle operator from the 2123rd Transportation Company. Keeps convoys moving and knows how to get an engine running without a key. Single Channel Radio Operator (MOS 31C, -12 Points) Radio operator assigned to the 201st Engineer Battalion. Carries a Manpack radio for frontline communication. NOTE: MOS designations reflect 1993 U.S. Army classifications. Some are outdated by modern standards, this is intentional for period accuracy. Features Each profession awards a unique, era-accurate loadout on spawn with realistic ammo counts, rations, gas masks, and field gear where applicable. Loadouts can be toggled in Sandbox Settings (enabled by default). Loadouts are designed to be balanced and not overpowered, let me know of any balancing suggestions. Equipment reflects what KYNG units would actually have been issued during a 1993 containment deployment. This mod adds several unit identifiers and a military id card as items (not spawning as loot, yet). Flavour text included for those who appreciate it, more lore to come :) Compatibility Sandbox Settings to enable loadout and lore items NOT Multiplayer compatible yet Can be added to already existing saves, but not removed from them Recommended: Alice Gear If the Alice Gear mod is active, this mod will automatically swap applicable equipment to the gear that mod adds, significantly improving immersion. Finally, a mod where your body count actually matters. Look, I'm not here to judge your... numbers. Kill zombies, hit milestones, earn trait rewards. Higher trait cost = lower drop chance. Simple. Compatible with B42.20+ (Stable) | SP and MP because your body count shouldn't depend on your social life. The spiritual successor to Circuit's Kill Milestones (Zombies) B42. His mod gave me the idea, I wanted more features and control for my server, so I built my own from scratch. Circuit has since moved on from PZ modding and linked this mod on his page. Thanks for the inspiration! Features Stats UI: Three tabs for progress tracking, full reward history, and a trait catalog with rarity and conflict info Right-click context menu: Quick-check kills and distance to next milestone. Toggleable in Mod Options. Smart trait conflicts: Mutually exclusive traits are resolved automatically. The Catalog tab shows exactly why any trait is unavailable. 43 traits in the pool (21 earnable, 22 removable). Every single one individually toggleable in sandbox settings. Third-party addon API: Other mods can register their own traits via BCR.RegisterCustomTraits(). See the addons below for working examples. Toggleable context menu: Mod Options in the ESC menu lets you disable the right click context menu. Sandbox Options All configurable in-game by the host. No file editing needed. Kill threshold per milestone (2 to 10,000) Progressive or linear scaling Reward priority: Remove negatives first, add positives first, or coin flip Grant Missed Opportunities: Install mid-game with thousands of kills? Get all owed rewards at once Positive rewards, negative removal, or both. Your body count, your rules Individual trait toggles: Enable or disable any of the 43 traits Drop chances scale with trait cost: cheap traits (1-2 pts) drop often, expensive ones (7-8 pts) almost never. Check the Catalog tab for more info. Available Addons Want even more traits? These BCR addons integrate other trait mods into the reward system: I Am Not Your Mom - 6 vanilla traits the base mod skips (Brave, Desensitized, Deaf, etc.) MoreTraits - 77 traits from the MoreTraits mod SomewhatTraits - 32 traits from the SomewhatTraits mod FAQ Q: Do I keep rewards if I remove the mod? A: Yes. Traits are permanently saved to your character. Q: Thousands of kills but only 1 reward? A: Enable "Grant Missed Opportunities" in sandbox options and kill one more Z to trigger the update. Q: Why can't I get trait XY? A: Right click > BodyCountRewards > Catalog tab. It tells you exactly why. Q: Linear vs Progressive? A: Linear = same kills per milestone. Progressive = each one needs more kills. Scaling factor controls how steep it gets. Q: Athletic/Strong/Fit? A: Maybe. Those grant perk points, so they need extra work. If enough people want it, I'll look into it. Q: Works with mod traits? A: Yesn't. Not out of the box, but modders can use the addon API. Check out the addons linked above. Languages English | Deutsch | Espanol | Pyccknn | Portugues (BR) | 简体中文 | 한국어 | Turkce | Francais | Polski | Ykpaiнcbka Translations are automatically translated. If something reads awkwardly in your language, open an issue on GitHub or leave a comment below. Native speakers are welcome. Compatibility Build 42.13+ (Unstable Branch). SP and MP. Safe to install mid-game (reads existing kill count). Safe to remove (earned traits stay permanently). No vanilla file overwrites. Works with Skill Recovery Journal. AI Transparency I designed the architecture and wrote the core logic myself. AI assisted with coding, debugging, unit tests, and this workshop page. I believe in being upfront about tools used. To modders: Consider adding a similar note. Be honest about what's yours. To users: If AI-assisted dev isn't your thing, don't use the mod. But please don't downvote transparency. The mod will now work in all versions of B42. Hopefully. What It is It enables you to create a crossbow from a bunch of junk. What It Do It do: - Be a (short-ish)-ranged weapon - Be quiet to fire - Be good at hunting animals (if you're sneaky enough) - Be making you feel sneaky and cool as hell - Be accessible to create (even to wilderness playstyles with no access to other ranged weaponry) - Be giving you a reason to collect/save some otherwise less than useful items - Be scaling decently with critical chance and range as aiming level increases - Be allowing ammo to be retrieved from dead zombies (configurable in sandbox settings) - Be rarely spawning the items themselves as well as the recipe magazine in appropriate places/denizens throughout the world - Be able to be added to multiplayer servers and existing saves Alright, I'm done with the 'be' thing, promise. What It Don't It don't: - Reliably one-shot zombies, especially at low aiming levels. It's made of scraps- temper your expectations. - Handle hordes well. Probably best to pick zombies off one at a time. If you attract a crowd, then good luck. - Reload quickly. Custom (sorta) reload animation means it takes a second or two to ready another shot. NO MAGAZINES! Crafting Requirements A magazine will be required in order to learn the recipes. Researching an existing item or reaching the auto-learn level of the respective skill will also teach the recipes if a magazine cannot be found. - Makeshift Crossbow: Requires Maintenance level 4; recipe auto-learned at Maintenance level 6 - Makeshift Bolt: Requires at least Carving level 2 in order to carve bolt shafts. The recipe itself can be auto-learned at Carving level 4. Learning the recipe for assembling the bolt will also teach the recipe for crafting its constituent parts (flights and shaft). "Why... ...does firing the crossbow fill the area with light?" At the moment, ranged weapons are hard-coded to emit light when fired. Smarter, handsomer modders than myself have tried to tackle this and so far no dice. Maybe some day I will find a solution for this! ...doesn't it train my aiming skill?" It does, just much more slowly than most conventional firearms. Aiming XP is based on damage done per shot, and seeing as this is essentially a rubberband nail gun, it's gonna be a bit slow to train aiming. Not much I can do about that one, sorry. ...does my reloading skill go up so fast?" Opposite situation, but similar issue: you gain ~1 reloading XP per reload of most weapons/magazines. Since you reload between shots with this thing, that's sorta just how it works. Your reloading arm is going to be absolutely YOKED, though. ...does it not fire after reloading sometimes in MP?" Because I'm a bit of a hack and can't find a way to overcome some of the desync issues multiplayer causes the weapon. If you can't seem to reload it, just set it down, then pick it back up. Should put it back to normal operation. ...are the requirements to craft everything so high?" Because I like the idea of you having to survive with only rocks and sharp sticks for a while before you can start using ranged weapons. This mod is meant to bridge the gap between low-tech, abundant melee weapons and high-tech, rare firearms. It can't really replace either, so it is what it is. Enjoy. description: 좀보이드에서 더 다양한 디저트를 먹고 싶은 빵순이, 빵돌이들! 좀보이드에서 꿈빛 파티시엘을 하고 싶은 사람들, 모여라! 좀비를 잡느라 지쳤나요? 캐릭터가 우울한가요? 달콤함이 부족한가요? 그럴 땐 디저트를 먹으며 당분을 보충해 보세요. 기분이 조금 나아질 거예요. ‘간단한’ 과정만 거치면 디저트들을 쉽게 만들 수 있습니다. 예를 들어, 호박이나 해바라기를 재배해 씨앗을 얻고, 맷돌에 갈아 만든 견과류 파우더로 마카롱을 만들 수도 있고, 용광로에서 스패튤러나 케이크 돌림판을 제작해 케이크 도구로 사용할 수도 있습니다. 또한 버터 교반기를 이용해 우유로 생크림을 만들 수도 있습니다. 간단하죠? 하지만 이런 ‘간단한’ 과정들이 귀찮다면, 월드에서 파밍해도 됩니다. 몇몇은 상해 있을 수도 있지만, 어차피 뱃속에 들어가면 똑같을거예요. 배가 조금 아프고 기분이 살짝 나빠질 수도 있겠지만요. 아포칼립스 세상에서 달콤한 롤케이크와 슈크림을 먹을 수 있는데 그게 뭐 별건가요? 달콤한 디저트만 먹다 보면 짭짤한 음식도 생각날 수 있어요. 다들 단짠단짠 아시죠? 그럴 때는 든든하게 돼지국밥을 먹거나, 양은냄비에 얼큰한 라면을 끓여 먹을 수도 있습니다. 좀비를 잡으러 가는 소풍(?)에는 김밥 도시락을 싸 가면 훨씬 즐거울 거예요. ---제작자 코멘트 안녕하세요! 코딩을 전혀 모르는 상태에서 머리를 싸매고 주먹구구식으로 처음 만들어 본 모드입니다. 아직 어설픈 부분이 있을 수 있지만… 너그럽게 봐 주시면 감사하겠습니다! 앞으로 더 나아지도록 계속 개선해 나가겠습니다. 다양한 디저트와 식재료도 차근차근 추가하고 있습니다. 좀보이드에서 꿈빛 파티시엘을 구현하는 것이 목표입니다. 가능한 한 현실적인 요소를 살리면서, 바닐라 아이템도 함께 활용할 수 있도록 구성하려고 노력했습니다. 그럼 재미있게 플레이하세요! Want more desserts in Project Zomboid? Calling all dessert lovers and aspiring pastry chefs—come join the fun! Tired of fighting zombies? Is your character feeling down? Craving something sweet? Then treat yourself to some desserts and get that sugar boost—you might feel a little better. With just a few “simple” steps, you can easily make a variety of desserts. For example, you can grow pumpkins or sunflowers, collect seeds, grind them into nut powder using a mill, and make macarons. You can also craft tools like spatulas or cake turntables in a furnace and use them for baking. Or use a butter churn to turn milk into whipped cream. Simple, right? But if those “simple” steps feel like too much work, you can always find desserts while looting the world. Some might be spoiled, but hey—once it’s in your stomach, it’s all the same, right? You might get a stomachache or feel a bit worse… but come on, in an apocalypse, being able to enjoy sweet roll cakes and cream puffs isn’t such a bad deal. After eating too many sweet desserts, you might start craving something savory. You know—sweet and salty balance. When that happens, you can enjoy a hearty bowl of pork soup or cook up some spicy ramen in a metal pot. And if you're heading out on a zombie-hunting “picnic,” packing some kimbap will make it even more enjoyable. ---Developer’s Note Hello! This is my first mod, made from scratch with zero coding experience and a lot of trial and error. There may still be rough edges… but I hope you’ll be kind and enjoy it anyway! I’ll continue improving it over time. I’m also gradually adding more desserts and ingredients. My goal is to bring a full “pastry chef” experience into Project Zomboid. I’ve tried to keep things as realistic as possible, while also making use of vanilla items wherever I can. Have fun and enjoy the game! Workshop ID: 3663132395 Mod ID: HDsFoodRecipes

Progression table Thresholds Bonuses Values are meant for medium difficulty Speed caps at level 6. Damage and crit continue to grow up to level 10. description: Every night could be your last. Siege Night turns your base into a battleground. Every few nights, the dead march on your position from a single direction -- wave after wave, growing stronger as the night goes on. Build your walls. Stock your ammo. Survive until dawn. Built for fortress defense. Solo or multiplayer. Mod ID: SiegeNight | Workshop ID: 3669589584 Workshop URL: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3669589584 Wave Cycles -- WAVE (dense assault), TRICKLE (stragglers), and BREAK (patch up and reinforce). 3 to 7 waves per night, escalating as midnight approaches. Directional Attacks -- every siege picks one of 8 compass directions and all zombies come from that angle for the entire night. Different directions each siege force real decisions about where your walls go. Siege Scaling -- zombie count scales with sieges survived and players online. Early game: 3 waves, ~75-150 zombies. Late game: 6-7 waves, up to 1,500. Siege Modes (MP) -- Per-Base (independent sieges per group) or Unified (one global siege targeting the busiest area). Configurable in sandbox. Safehouse Anchor Mode -- zombies target your claimed safehouse instead of your player position. They attack your base even if you leave. Dawn Survival -- make it to sunrise and your character announces the kill count. The siege panel tracks everything. 30+ Sandbox Options -- tune siege frequency, zombie count, scaling, spawn distance, anchor mode, special zombie rates, mini-horde thresholds, and more. Spread across 3 sandbox pages. Kill Tracking -- a Siege Night tab in your character info (press H) shows wave/phase, kills this siege, lifetime totals, and full siege history for the last 20 nights. Sprinters -- fast. Blend in with the horde until they're already on you. Breakers -- construction gear. Built to smash through your barricades and walls. Tanks -- military outfits, 5x normal health. description: Jeeve's Hordes Surviving the apocalypse just got a whole lot harder. Jeeve's Hordes adds dynamic, unpredictable horde night events to your server that will keep every player on edge. You never know exactly when the next horde is coming — only that it is coming. How It Works Hordes strike at night on a randomized schedule. The server picks a random interval between events (configurable from every few days to once a month), then picks a random time during the night window to unleash the dead. When the horde arrives, zombies spawn around every online player and are drawn toward them by a pulsing sound lure. A warning moodle appears on the morning of a horde day so you know tonight is the night — giving you just enough time to prepare, barricade, and arm yourself. Survivor Escalation Every horde you survive makes the next one more dangerous — just for you. Each survival adds to your personal zombie multiplier, meaning veteran survivors face increasingly brutal waves while newer players get a fair fight. Your multiplier caps at a server-configurable maximum. The global horde count also grows over time. Each event adds more zombies to the base count, so the entire server faces a rising threat as the days go on. Death resets your progression. If you die, your personal multiplier goes back to zero. High risk, high reward. Rotten Flesh & Zombie Stew Zombies have a chance to drop Rotten Flesh when killed. Collect it to craft Zombie Stew — a foul concoction made by combining Rotten Flesh, water, and a cooking pot. Eating Zombie Stew before a horde grants you immunity for that event. The horde ignores you entirely — no zombies will spawn around you and the lure won't pulse near you. Perfect for nights when you're undergeared or just want to sit one out. But be careful: Using Zombie Stew for 5 consecutive horde nights triggers a streak penalty that resets your entire survivor progression back to zero. You can't rely on stew forever. Fragrance à la Jeeves Found rarely in the world, Fragrance à la Jeeves is a mysterious cologne with a very different effect. Using it doesn't protect you — it attracts the dead. On a non-horde day, the fragrance triggers a personal horde just for you — a solo event using the same spawning and progression mechanics as a normal horde night. On a horde day, the fragrance grants a 200% zombie spawn multiplier — tripling your wave size. Survive it, and you'll earn double progression plus a boosted military airdrop (when Jeeve's Drops is installed). It's the fastest way to climb the ranks — if you can handle the heat. Horde Reward Scaling: Every 10 hordes survived increases the loot multiplier on your completion airdrop by +0.2×, capping at 3.0×. Fragrance doubles this progression rate and guarantees a military crate type. The longer you survive, the better your rewards. Using fragrance for 5 consecutive horde nights increases your lure radius by 50%, drawing zombies from further away during future hordes. The penalty resets on death or any horde night where fragrance was not used. Stew and fragrance share a 7 in-game day cooldown — using one blocks the other. Fully Configurable Every aspect of the mod is adjustable through sandbox options: Scheduling — Set the earliest start day, frequency range, and night hours Zombie Count — Base count per player, increment per event, and maximum cap Spawn Behavior — Min/max spawn distance, safe radius, lure range and volume Progression — Survivor multiplier cap Items — Rotten Flesh drop chance, Zombie Stew immunity toggle Fragrance — Toggle Fragrance à la Jeeves on/off, configure world spawn rate Warnings — Toggle player warning moodles on/off Discord Integration Designed to work seamlessly with the Jeeves Discord Bot (part of the Jeeves server stack) for full server management. When paired with JeevesBot, your Discord server receives: Notifications when a horde is scheduled Alerts when the horde begins Summary when the event ends, including survivor count Admin commands to trigger, stop, or check horde status from Discord Discord integration is optional — the mod works perfectly as a standalone. Compatibility Build 42 — Multiplayer and singleplayer. Note: Jeeve's Integration is required and must load before Jeeve's Hordes. It provides the custom moodle framework for horde warning, immunity, and fragrance indicators. If using Jeeve's Drops as well, ensure the load order is: Integration Drops Hordes. The mod.info enforces this automatically via loadModAfter. Part of the Jeeves Ecosystem Jeeve's Integration — Discord chat relay, player ranks, custom moodles, and server commands Jeeve's Claims — Safehouse, land, and vehicle claim protection Jeeve's Drops — Airdrop and supply drop events with guarded loot Jeeve's Journals — Skill recovery journals Jeeve's Patches — Compatibility fixes for popular mods Jeeve's QoL — Quality-of-life improvements bundle Jeeve's Personal Computer — In-game computers, arcade games, training disks, and skill backup Jeeve's Zones — Admin-defined map zones with per-zone rules Jeeve's Build — Buildable furniture and structures from licensed tile packs Jeeve's Solar Arrays — Solar power generation (Immersive Solar Arrays for Build 42) Workshop ID: 3672042113 Mod ID: JeevesHordes

description: Revamped and updated version of the mod: The Calm Before The Storm Built for version B41.78+ and B42.13+! DESCRIPTION - SAFE TO ADD/REMOVE MID-GAME! - WORKS IN MULTIPLAYER! Nowhere is safe forever. "Horde Rush" is a survival-focused mod designed to keep you on your toes and test your base defenses when you least expect it... Are you prepared to hold the line? PREREQUISITES For this mod to function correctly, you must adjust a few specific Sandbox Options. You can find these settings under `Advanced Zombie Options` (if editing in-game) or under the `ZombieConfig` section (if editing your server's SandboxVars file). 1. Enable Zombie Respawn The mod relies on zombies existing in the world. Make sure respawning is turned on by setting the following values to greater than zero. Default Values here are pretty good enough. Respawn Hours = 72 Respawn Unseen Hours = 16 2. Adjust Population Multipliers To ensure the horde events feel appropriately challenging and intense, I highly recommend tweaking your population levels. Default values here are also pretty good: Population Multiplier = 2.0 Population Start Multiplier = 1.0 Population Peak Multiplier = 1.5 3. Increase Sound Follow Distance Zombies need to be allowed to travel long distances when they hear any in-game events' sounds. Follow Sound Distance = 450 Note: If you set the "Horde Distance" in the mod options higher than 300, you must increase this sandbox value to match it using formula: Follow Sound Distance = Horde Distance * 1.42 HOW IT WORKS * No Artificial Spawns: This mod does not spawn new zombies out of thin air. It only attracts the undead that are already roaming nearby in your world. * Sandbox Scaling: Because it uses the existing local population, the difficulty and size of these waves are directly tied to your game's default Zombie Config in the Sandbox options. Play with high population multipliers, and you'll face massive, overwhelming hordes. Play on lower populations, and the rushes will be more manageable. The event cycles through three phases: * The 'Cooldown' Phase - The time between events. Gameplay is normal and zombies will behave as usual. * The 'Calm' Phase - The period in which mass zombie migration occurs. Towns and cities will seem deserted and eerily quiet. This gives players the opportunity to scavenge and build defenses before the inevitable horde arrives. * The 'Storm' Phase - Zombies return in massive hordes and persistently hunt down the player(s). It will take some time... quite some time for the horde to actually march toward your location, providing a window to prepare your defenses. The event begins with smaller waves of stragglers and escalates into larger groups as the main horde arrives. Zombies are, by default, always aware of the player's position, which can be changed in the sandbox options. FOUND AN ISSUE? Please, raise this issue on my GitHub: https://github.com/drag0no/PZ_Rin_HordeRush/issues CREDITS Massive thanks to socialtroglodyte for the brilliant core logic of this mod and permission to use his code! description: Advanced Health System Survive your own body. Advanced Health System is a complete physiological overhaul for Project Zomboid focused on progressive, realistic health deterioration based on player decisions. This is not a random illness mod. This is a systemic survival framework. Your body reacts to: Sleep neglect Poor nutrition Dehydration Stress accumulation Physical exhaustion Infection Weight Temperature Poison Health conditions develop gradually through defined stages: Mild → Moderate → Severe → Peak → Recovery No instant deaths. No unfair spikes. No invisible RNG. Core Features Progressive 3–8 day health episodes No phase skipping Only one dominant critical condition at a time Immunity cooldown after recovery Critical conditions can affect vitality Integrated with Vanilla First Aid skill First Aid Reworked First Aid is no longer reactive — it is preventive. Gain XP by maintaining proper hygiene Gain XP by sleeping correctly Gain XP by preventing severe episodes Auto-examination system with skill-based diagnosis High skill reveals dominant conditions and true severity Low skill means limited perception. High skill means informed survival. Health Interface You can open the interface with the H keybind or by using the mod button on the vertical buttons of your screen. Minimalist body silhouette Color-coded severity based on medical knowledge No numbers, no bars, no artificial stats Clean and immersive visual feedback The body tells a story — if you know how to read it. Advanced Medical Items This mod introduces a set of advanced medical items designed to expand survival possibilities without replacing the vanilla system. Electrolyte Drinks – Improve hydration recovery and help stabilize the body under stress. Broad Spectrum Antibiotics – More effective against infections compared to standard treatments. Beta-blockers – Help control stress-related physiological responses. Anti-inflammatory Medication – Reduce internal strain and inflammation effects. Medical Thermometer – Useful for tracking body condition and detecting abnormalities. Vanilla medical items are still fully functional and remain a viable option. However, AHS medical items are generally more effective and suited for advanced or critical conditions. Dynamic Traits System AHS introduces a fully dynamic health trait system driven by your character's habits and physical condition over time. Traits are not static – they evolve based on how you play. Poor habits (dehydration, stress, infections, exhaustion) may lead to negative traits. Maintaining good health over time can grant positive adaptations. Your body reacts to accumulated strain through hidden systems such as: Hydration Sleep Stress Physical Bacterial Poison Weight Temperature You are not given exact values. Instead, your character provides subjective feedback based on their First Aid skill. Diagnosis & Perception The diagnosis system is designed around uncertainty and interpretation. Low First Aid → vague and unreliable feedback Higher First Aid → more precise and consistent observations Symptoms may overlap or appear gradually Not all conditions are immediately obvious “You feel better… but something is still not right.” Design Philosophy AHS is not a numbers-based system. No visible stats or exact condition values No instant clarity on what is happening Focus on immersion, interpretation, and survival decision-making Your character does not know everything. You must observe, interpret, and adapt. AHS does not punish single mistakes. It punishes accumulated neglect. Three days without proper care will have consequences Ignoring warning signs will escalate risk Recovery takes time — there are no instant fixes Your worst enemy might not be the zombies — it might be your own body. Compatibility ✔ Multiplayer supported ✔ Designed for long-term survival runs ✔ Does not replace vanilla health system Stay alive. Stay aware. FAQ Is it safe to add mid-save? description: A fully-featured smartphone mod for Project Zomboid Build 42. Find phones in houses, offices, and stores. Use them to navigate, message other players, and more. Install xPhone Sound Pack (separate Workshop item) to unlock GPS voice guidance with spoken directions in English and Spanish. == PHONE MODELS == xPhone Disposable — The cheapest model. Found commonly in houses. Has a fixed internal battery that cannot be replaced or recharged. Once the battery dies, the phone is permanently dead. Use it wisely. xPhone Standard — Mid-tier model found in offices and stores. Uses a replaceable battery (xPhone Battery item). When the battery runs low, swap it for a fresh one from your inventory through the phone's settings menu. xPhone Solar — Rare high-tier model. Its built-in battery automatically recharges when you are outdoors during daytime. The longer you stay in sunlight, the more charge it recovers. Nearly self-sustaining for light usage. == BATTERY SYSTEM == Every phone has a 0-100% battery that drains realistically based on what you do: - Music Playback: moderate drain (~8h on Disposable, ~11h on Standard, ~20h on Solar) - GPS Navigation: lightest drain (~11h on Disposable, ~16h on Standard, ~33h on Solar) - Idle: no drain while the phone is in your inventory and not in use The Solar model recharges automatically when you walk outdoors during daylight hours. == APPS == Messages (Text Messaging) Each phone gets a unique 5-digit number assigned when first activated. Save contacts by name and send private text messages to any player at any distance. Conversations are displayed in a chat-style interface with timestamps. A Global Chat channel lets everyone with an active xPhone communicate together. You receive real-time toast notifications for incoming messages from any screen — click to jump directly to the conversation. GPS / Maps A full navigation system with a real-time rendered map showing 1,000+ named streets, buildings, points of interest, and city labels. Features include: - Search: type any place name or street to find it instantly - Navigate: select a destination and get A* pathfinding with an optimal route drawn on the map - Voice guidance: turn-by-turn directions spoken aloud in Spanish or English (requires Sound Pack) - Mini-map: always visible on the GPS home screen while navigating - Full-screen map: zoomable and pannable world map, click anywhere to set a destination - Nearby POIs: discover nearby locations sorted by distance - City quick-access: jump to any city from a sorted list with distances - Off-route detection: automatic recalculation if you stray from the path - Vehicle awareness: detects if you are driving and adjusts speed estimates and arrival voice lines xPottify (Music Player) A built-in music streaming app that automatically detects all installed True Moozic-compatible cassette and disc mods. Browse by collection, pick a song, and listen while you loot and survive. Music plays through your character's position in the world — other players nearby can hear it and the volume changes in real time based on distance and your volume slider. With earphones connected, music is private. Without earphones, it attracts zombies. If no compatible music mods are installed, xPottify shows a friendly message explaining how to add them. Settings - Connect/disconnect earphones from your inventory. With earphones connected, all phone sounds (music, GPS voice) play privately — zombies cannot hear you. Without earphones, sound plays through the phone speaker and attracts nearby zombies. - Adjust voice guidance volume - Swap batteries (Standard model only) - View phone number, battery level, and phone model info == MULTIPLAYER == Fully works in multiplayer. Phone numbers are synced across the server. Players can exchange numbers and send private text messages from anywhere on the map. The global chat channel connects all active phones. The server tracks all phone numbers and persists global chat history. == LOOT == Phones and spare batteries spawn naturally in the world through the distribution system. Disposable phones are common, Standard phones are uncommon, Solar phones are rare. Spare batteries can be found in electronics stores and offices. == LANGUAGE == Supports English and Spanish. Switch language in Settings — all UI text updates instantly. 📋 Changelog v1.1 — March 3, 2026 Phone Identity & Persistence - Phone registration (number, contacts, dead state) now persists across save/load via player ModData backup - Picking up a different phone shows the activation/login screen correctly (SIM swap logic) - Four clean activation cases: your phone → activate, someone else's → login, unowned + have account → auto-bind, unowned + no account → first-time setup Battery System - Battery level now backs up to player ModData — survives drop/pickup and save/load without resetting to 100% - Context menu shows the real battery value instead of always showing 100 Volume System - Volume setting now persists across ModData loss (backed up to player ModData) - Fixed volume resetting to max when songs auto-advance or are manually changed - Volume changes are now heard by nearby players in real time via the broadcast system Multiplayer Audio (Major Fix) - Fixed double audio bug: nearby players were hearing each song twice (one from PZ engine propagation + one from custom broadcast) - Music playback now uses client-only SoundManager instead of player emitter, eliminating engine-level sound duplication - Remote players hear music exclusively through the custom broadcast system with proper distance-based volume falloff - Fixed song restarting for the listener when the emitter changed volume — remote sound instances are now muted instead of destroyed - Fixed stop/pause not working for nearby listeners — the broadcast now distinguishes pause (mute, keep position) from full stop (destroy) - Fixed low volume (1/10) making music inaudible for nearby players — minimum hearing range of ~8 tiles regardless of volume setting - Volume changes are now heard by nearby players in real time via the broadcast system xPottify Music Player - xPottify now dynamically scans all installed True Moozic-compatible mods (cassettes, discs, CDs, vinyl) - No longer hardcoded to specific genres — works with any music mod that uses GlobalMusic - Shows a helpful message when no compatible music mods are installed ☕ Support the Developer Thank you so much for downloading and playing my mods! Every subscriber, comment, and rating means the world to me. If you enjoy this mod and want to support my work, you can buy me a coffee! Your support helps me keep creating and improving mods for the community. ☕ buymeacoffee.com/XaviChang Every coffee fuels another late-night coding session! ☕🎮 Workshop ID: 3675737813 Mod ID: xPhone

Dead Man's Dossier [B42][MP] Build 42 multiplayer-safe. A collectible objective system: zombies drop torn pages, assemble a dossier, follow coordinates to a hidden stash. Works in multiplayer 42.1.17. Police, military, medical, firefighter, and ranger zombies drop torn document pages. Collect all pages for a tier, assemble a dossier, and follow the coordinates to a hidden supply stash. The loot spawns on the ground at the stash location — gear up and survive. How It Works Kill zombies wearing police, military, medical, firefighter, or ranger outfits They have a chance to drop torn document pages Collect all pages for a tier, then right-click a page to Assemble Dossier A progress bar plays while your character reads and assembles the pages The completed dossier reveals coordinates to a hidden supply stash A colored marker appears on your world map showing the stash location Travel to the stash and right-click the dossier to Verify Stash Location Proximity hints guide you in — color-coded "getting warmer" feedback When you're close enough, loot drops on the ground at the stash tile for you to pick up If your map marker disappears (e.g. after a server restart), Verify Stash Location or View Stash Map will restore it automatically Don't want the mission? Right-click the dossier and choose Abandon Mission to discard it and start fresh Five Tiers Police (2 pages) — Pistols, shotguns, ammo, police clothing, bulletproof vest, holster, walkie-talkie Military (3 pages) — Assault rifles, pistols, magazines, scopes, ammo, camo gear, military backpack, ALICE webbing, bulletproof vest Medical (2 pages) — Antibiotics, bandages, suture needles, painkillers, surgical tools, scrubs Firefighter (2 pages) — Axe, sledgehammer, crowbar, fireman gear, blow torch, bolt cutters, welding mask Ranger (2 pages) — Hunting rifle, shotguns, knife, hatchet, scopes, ranger clothing, compass, rope, trap box Each page has immersive lore text — internal memos, classified reports, incident logs, and field notes that tell the story of Knox County's fall. Where to Find Pages Pages drop from zombies wearing the matching outfit. They also spawn in relevant containers: Police pages in police station lockers, desks, and gun storage Military pages in army hangars, surplus stores, and military storage Medical pages in hospital drug cabinets, clinics, and medical storage Firefighter pages in fire department lockers Ranger pages in ranger outfit containers and tool storage Map Markers When you assemble a dossier, a colored marker is placed on your world map at the stash location. Each tier has a distinct color. Markers persist across saves and can be toggled on/off with a button on the map screen. Sandbox Options Server admins can tune everything under Dossier Mod in Sandbox Options: Page drop chance per tier — High (30%) / Normal (15%) / Low (8%) / Very Low (3%) Page container spawn rate — How often pages appear in world containers (Common / Uncommon / Rare / Very Rare) Stash reward rarity — Multiplier for reward drop chances (Generous 2x / Normal 1x / Scarce 0.5x / Minimal 0.1x) Stash proximity radius — How close you need to be to collect rewards (5-50 tiles, default 15) Use Custom Rewards — Load reward items from a config file instead of the built-in tables (see below) Custom Rewards (Admin Config) Server admins can fully customize what items each stash tier drops: Start the server once — a config file is auto-generated at Zomboid/Lua/DeadMansDossier_Rewards.cfg Edit the file to add, remove, or change items and their drop chances Enable Use Custom Rewards in Sandbox Options Restart the server — custom rewards are now active The config file uses a simple format: [Police] Base.Pistol = 0.40 Base.Shotgun = 0.25 # Base.Sledgehammer = 0.05 (commented out = disabled) [Military] Base.AssaultRifle = 0.05 SomeMod.CustomWeapon = 0.10 (cross-mod items work too) The Reward Rarity sandbox multiplier still applies on top of custom chances. Items from uninstalled mods are silently skipped. If the config file is missing or has errors, the mod falls back to the built-in defaults. Cross-Mod Support Military stash caches can drop X-Virus and Medical stash caches can drop Knox Antidote. Works with or without those mods installed — if the mod isn't active, the item is silently skipped. Translations Item names are now routed through PZ's translation system (thanks to feedback from Shahin·Wolf). Translators can add new languages by copying Translate/EN/ItemName.json to a language folder (e.g. Translate/CH/) and translating the values. Same goes for DeadMansDossier.json (UI + lore) and Sandbox.json (option labels). Submit translations via Workshop comments and they'll be added to the next release. Compatibility Build 42 — works in multiplayer (updated for 42.20) Mid-save compatible — can be added to an existing save Changelog — 42.20 Updated for Project Zomboid 42.20. Nothing the mod relies on changed, so existing servers need no action. Fixed: many stash rewards never actually spawned. Around a fifth of the reward list still used Build 41 item names that no longer exist — the game silently created nothing, and the server log even reported them as delivered. All reward items are now validated against the live game files. Fixed: several zombie types never dropped pages at all. Four of the outfit names the mod watched for do not exist in Build 42, so those zombies were invisible to it. Replaced with real ones, and added SWAT, sheriff deputies, prison guards, army instructors and full-suit firefighters to the drop pool. New: the document lore now actually appears. Every page and completed dossier has hand-written in-world lore that was never hooked up to anything — hover an item to read it. Fixed: 42.20 blocked Assemble / Verify / Abandon while dragging a corpse. They work again. Fixed: map markers did not come back if you disconnected and rejoined without restarting the game. Fixed: mod icon and Workshop metadata were missing their root-level copies. All on-screen text now goes through the translation system, so translations can be contributed. English only for now. Roadmap Stash loot currently drops on the ground — planning to add a supply crate container in a future update Feedback and suggestions welcome! If a stash location seems off, please let us know and we'll fix it. Support Found the stash? Help me hide the next one: My Mod Collection This is the list of mods I use on the server I play with my friends: Faitas' PZ MP Mod Collection Workshop ID: 3675740871 Mod ID: DeadMansDossier

description: Fine tune loot spawns and respawns by area and time by reducing their chance of spawn Setup Open the configs window by clicking the PhunLewts button in the Admin or Debug window This is a list of all your different configurations. The Default profile is the configuration used if you are not using with PhunZones or if the zone you are in does not specify a configuration. It's the perfect place for your global defaults! Let's make ammo really rare. To do so, I'll edit the default config, click the Categories tab, edit the Ammo category and set it to 90 That makes ALL items in that category reduce their spawn by 90%. Now, let's say I want no ammo spawning in certain places. To do this, I create a new config, inherit from default (which has the 90% reduction for ammo) and change the Ammo value to 100 I can then assign that config to a zone via the PhunZones editor IMPORTANT This mod only reduces loot when the game spawns or respawns items in a container. It cannot reduce loot in containers that are already filled (eg a custom map that ships with loot already in containers). However it will apply when those containers restock. That also means that changes in your config will not affect containers that have already been stocked It cannot force loot to respawn in custom maps that are missing or have broken forage zones. Basically if the game won't restock the container, this mod won't be able to change that There are no longer dependencies required, however it is strongly suggested that you use PhunZones. Without it, only your default config is used Remember, the values reduce loot spawns. 100 = 100% reduction and 0 = no reduction! description: PhunSprinters 2 the sequel to the Academy Award winning PhunSprinters. PhunSprinters is the ultimate sprinter mod for Zomboid. PhunSprinters does not simply add sprinters. It calculates risk and that risk can change depending on where you are, how long you’ve survived, the moon cycle, and the environment. 🧠 How Sprinter Risk Is Calculated Sprinter behaviour is determined by stacking modifiers in this order: Global Base Risk (in your settings) Zone Override (if PhunZones 2 is installed) Hours Discount (Ease-In) Moon Phase Modifier Darkness / Night Rules Light Suppression Final Sprinter Chance & Behaviour 🌑 Modes There are four different modes that determine when sprinters will run 🔦 Light Suppression (Flashlights Matter) When enabled, bright light can force sprinters to walk This creates emergent gameplay: Flashlights become tactical tools Base lighting matters Night travel becomes a risk vs reward decision It brings some of the Phun of mode #4 to the other options (this option doesn't do anything if using Mode 4) ⚠️ Some limits exist to prevent performance issues in dense areas. ⏳Hours Discount (Difficulty Easing) The Hours Discount slowly ramps difficulty over time. Instead of applying full risk immediately, sprinter chance increases gradually. Example: Zone Risk: 50% Hours Discount: 100 Player Hours: 50 ➡️ Effective Risk = 25% Risk increases linearly until the discount hours are reached. This is ideal for fresh servers, new characters, and multiplayer balance. 🌕 Moon Phase Modifiers Moon phases multiply the current risk. Example: Zone Risk: 20% Full Moon Modifier: 200 → will effectively double (200%) the risk to 40% New Moon Modifier: 50 → will effectively half (50%) the risk to 10% Moon modifiers scale risk, they do not replace it. Unless you set it to 0, then it means there is no risk! Key differences to version 1 Support for PhunZones 2 Removed requirements for dependencies (PhunZones and PhunLib are no longer required) Unified the UI and core mods (UI is no longer a separate mod) Drop B41 support (current version of PhunSprinters will continue to work for B41 but this greatly simplifies things) Improve performance Reduce amount of "Why they no sprint" moments More Phun Stuff Coded with love for our awesome PhunZoid community. GitHub repo and more info Workshop ID: 3676252110 Mod ID: phunsprinters2

description: Dynamic Evolution Z Adaptive World & Horde System The world is no longer static. Dynamic Evolution Z introduces a persistent, invisible behavioral system that reshapes zombie activity over time. The longer you survive — and the more aggressively you reshape the map — the more the infection reorganizes itself. No UI. No mutation gimmicks. No arcade bosses. Just systemic pressure. Core Systems Persistent Global Evolution Zombies evolve individually as days pass and player activity increases. Evolution is saved per zombie — some adapt faster, others stagnate. Individual Identity Each zombie develops independently. Different evolution baselines, different growth rates, different outcomes. No synchronized scaling. No artificial difficulty spikes. Leader Archetypes Rare evolved zombies can emerge as Leaders. Leaders: Increase group cohesion Improve persistence of nearby zombies Make dispersal harder Influence horde structure They are not bosses. They are behavioral catalysts. Ambient Wander Layer The world breathes even when you are not fighting. Subtle population drift occurs across chunks over time, preventing long-term stagnation and creating slow territorial pressure. Migration System Large-scale clearing has consequences. Under certain conditions, groups may begin relocating across nearby chunks — especially after heavy player activity. Safe areas do not remain safe forever. Layered Behavior Priority Meta-events, player pursuit, leadership influence and ambient drift follow a clear priority structure. Systems do not conflict or override vanilla behavior. Leader Archetypes Leaders are not all the same. When a zombie reaches advanced evolution, it may develop a distinct behavioral archetype. These archetypes do not grant artificial health or damage bonuses. They alter group behavior. HIVE Strong group cohesion Keeps nearby zombies tightly clustered Maintains formation longer than normal Harder to split apart HUNTER Improved tracking persistence Better memory of last known player position Groups remain engaged longer during pursuit Less likely to abandon a chase FRENZY Higher reaction to noise events Increased tendency to investigate distant sounds May redirect nearby zombies toward disturbances SHADOW Enhanced path persistence More likely to follow remembered routes Difficult to shake off once detected SPLIT Weaker cohesion Encourages group fragmentation Spreads pressure across multiple directions Creates unpredictable dispersal patterns STALKER Selects and follows a single prey Uses memory instead of direct pursuit Relentless but not fast — it never truly loses you Builds long-term tension and presence HOWLER Acts as a living signal node Calls and gathers nearby zombies Pushes hordes toward detected players Creates escalating pressure in waves Leaders are rare. Not every group has one. Not every evolved zombie becomes one. You may never know which type you are facing — until the horde behaves differently. Debug Commands -- List of commands: DynamicZ.DebugSetEvo(0.5) DynamicZ.DebugAddKills(500) DynamicZ.DebugSetStage(3) DynamicZ.DebugMakeLeader() DynamicZ.DebugForcePulse() DynamicZ.DebugCommand("/dz_set_evo 0.9") DynamicZ.DebugMakeLeader("SPLIT") DynamicZ.DebugInspect() DynamicZ.DebugStatus() DynamicZ.DebugUntrack() DynamicZ.DebugReset() DynamicZ.DebugHelp() DynamicZ.DebugCommand("/dz_inspect") -- Available commands on server: /dz_set_evo <0..1> /dz_add_kills <amount> /dz_set_stage <0..3> /dz_make_leader [HIVE|HUNTER|FRENZY|SHADOW|SPLIT] /dz_force_pulse /dz_reset /dz_inspect /dz_status /dz_untrack /dz_debug on /dz_debug off Sandbox Options Fully modular system: Enable Evolution Layer Enable Leader System Enable Migration Layer Enable Ambient Wander Layer Play it subtle — or turn the world hostile. Design Philosophy Dynamic Evolution Z does not add mutations. It adds adaptation. The infection does not become stronger through raw stat boosts. It becomes more organized, more persistent, and less predictable. You are not fighting stronger zombies. You are fighting a system that reacts. Performance & Multiplayer Build 42 Compatible Multiplayer Safe Server-side logic Optimized update throttling No global constant map scanning Layer conflict prevention system It is not compatible with Wandering mod, Starving mod, Thump with Friends. Designed to scale without heavy FPS impact when properly configured. Official compatibility layer for They Fear The Light. Intended Experience Early Game: Near-vanilla behavior. Mid Game: Subtle pressure and increasing cohesion. Late Game: Organized movement, territorial shifts, adaptive persistence. Clearing a town is no longer a permanent solution. description: Multiplayer compatible. Safe to add to existing saves. Armor Makes Sense replaces vanilla armor discomfort with realistic physical costs: endurance drain, heat buildup, breathing restriction, muscle strain, and worse sleep recovery. No stress penalties. Just physics. Why This Exists I spent days grinding blacksmithing to craft full plate armor. When I finally equipped it, the game punished me with discomfort and stress. My character was miserable. That felt wrong. Armor should cost stamina, mobility, heat, and fatigue, not sanity. So I replaced the system. What This Mod Does Armor Makes Sense removes vanilla's psychological discomfort and replaces it with physical costs. Protective gear now drains endurance, strains muscles, restricts breathing, traps heat, and slows recovery through existing vanilla systems. Despite the name, this is not just an armor tweak. To make the system behave consistently, I had to treat clothing as a whole ecosystem. The name stuck. Features Discomfort removed Vanilla's discomfort modifier is set to zero on all wearable items. Armor no longer causes stress. Speed rebalance Run speed and combat speed modifiers are reassigned by body region. Leg armor affects running. Arm and shoulder armor affect combat speed. Light pads stay neutral. Endurance drain Heavier armor increases endurance usage during movement and combat. Walking is almost free. Sprinting in full plate is not. Thermal pressure Armor traps heat. In hot weather you overheat faster. In cold weather, insulating armor helps. Breathing restriction Gas masks and respirators reduce airflow. The penalty scales with exertion: negligible at rest, noticeable under heavy effort. Muscle strain Heavy arm and shoulder protection adds fatigue per swing. A chest plate does not slow your swing, but gauntlets and shoulder pads do. Better-crafted armor restricts less than crude scrap. Sleep recovery Sleeping in rigid armor slows fatigue recovery. It is an emergency choice, not a default. Layering overhaul Vanilla limits some combinations in ways that do not make much sense. This mod re-slots 79 items across 8 custom body locations so layering works more naturally. In-Game UI Tooltips show burden level and breathing restriction Burden tab breaks down total loadout cost Help button explains each mechanic in plain language Compatibility Game version: Build 42.20 Other armor mods: should generally work through automatic item classification based on defense stats, weight, and item properties More in the Makes Sense series Translations Russian Spanish Source: GitHub Workshop ID: 3677430162 Mod ID: ArmorMakesSense

description: Chopper Drop [B42][MP][SP] Periodic military supply drops that create high-risk, high-reward hotspots. Works in singleplayer and multiplayer. How It Works On a configurable timer (default: every 3 hours), a helicopter flies over and drops a military supply crate A map marker appears showing the drop location to all players The helicopter sound attracts zombies from a wide radius A zombie horde (default: 30 zombies) spawns at the drop site when the first player arrives Players race to reach the crate, fight through zombies, and claim the loot After the despawn timer expires (default: 45 minutes), the crate disappears and the event ends Drop Location Drops are placed near the center of all online players (not biased to one player) Locations are biased toward towns and cities — urban areas are more likely to be picked, but rural drops can still happen The crate always lands on a valid walkable tile (ground floor) — avoids water (lakes, rivers, ocean) and shifts up to 30 tiles to find dry land. If no land is found, the drop is cancelled and retried automatically Min/max distance from players is configurable The Crate Reinforced military crate — zombies cannot destroy it Randomized loot from a pool of 250+ items — weapons, armor, ammo, medical, food, crafting supplies, and more Fully customizable loot pool — enable "Use Custom Loot Config" in sandbox options and edit ChopperDrop_Loot.cfg in your Zomboid/Lua/ folder to add, remove, or comment out items Loot quantity per crate is configurable (default: 15 items) Uncollected crates disappear after the despawn timer expires When the Event Ends The crate is removed (if not already looted) The helicopter sound stops The map marker is removed Zombies that spawned at the site remain — the area stays dangerous Sandbox Options Enable/disable supply drops (master kill switch) Enable/disable random drops only (keeps radio + admin commands working — useful for radio-only / pure on-demand setups) Timer mode: Real Time or Game Time Event frequency (minutes between drops) Despawn timer (minutes before crate disappears) Use custom loot config (load items from ChopperDrop_Loot.cfg) Loot quantity (number of random items per crate) Zombie horde size (0 to disable) Helicopter sound radius Helicopter volume (%) Zombie attraction radius Chopper pattern (Static or Orbit — orbit circles the sound around the drop site, spreading zombies out) Chopper leaves on arrival — when enabled, the helicopter flies off as soon as a player reaches the drop zone (configurable radius). Rotor sound stops and zombies are no longer pulled in. Crate, marker, and already-spawned zombies remain. Lets players push through the horde and reclaim the area. Minimum players online (default: 0 — works solo out of the box) Min/max distance from players Enable/disable Chopper Drop Radio Radio drop chance from military zombies Radio charges (Tune In uses) Early intel head start (seconds) Enable/disable Request Airdrop Request Airdrop cooldown (minutes between called airdrops) Enable/disable screen alerts (large centered text when events start/end) Customizable alert messages (supports {x} and {y} placeholders for drop coordinates) Spawn retry delay (minutes before retrying after a bad landing zone) Enable/disable spawn fail alert (notify players when a drop is cancelled) Customizable spawn fail alert message Custom Loot Config Want to control exactly what drops in the crate? You can fully customize the loot pool: Start the server once — a file called ChopperDrop_Loot.cfg is auto-generated in your Zomboid/Lua/ folder Open the file in any text editor — it contains every item in the default pool, one per line Add, remove, or comment out items with # to build your own loot table Enable "Use Custom Loot Config" in Sandbox Options Restart the server — your custom loot is now active Items from uninstalled mods are silently skipped, so cross-mod items (like Knox Antidote or X-Virus) are safe to include. The LootQuantity sandbox option still controls how many items are picked per crate. Chopper Drop Radio A rare tactical radio that drops from military zombie corpses. Gives you two abilities: Tune In — Check how long until the next supply drop. Each use costs one charge. The radio shows remaining charges in its name. When the charges run out, the radio is destroyed. Early Intel — Radio holders receive the drop coordinates immediately when the event starts. Everyone else is notified after a delay (default: 60 seconds), meaning the event is already underway by the time they find out. Request Airdrop — If the radio is fully charged, you can sacrifice it to call in an immediate supply drop. The radio is destroyed on use. Only works when no other drop is active. Cooldown between called airdrops is configurable. (New — first version, may have bugs. Disable via sandbox option "Enable Request Airdrop" if needed.) All radio features are fully configurable. The entire radio system can be disabled if you prefer the base experience. Admin Commands /chopperdrop — Type in chat to force an immediate supply drop near players (admin only) /chopperdrophere — Type in chat to force a supply drop at your own location (admin only) /chopperdropend — Type in chat to terminate the active supply drop (admin only) ChopperDropForceEvent() — Force a drop from debug console (~) or server console (/lua ChopperDropForceEvent()) ChopperDropForceEventHere() — Force a drop at your location from the debug console (~) ChopperDropEndEvent() — End active drop from debug console (~) or server console (/lua ChopperDropEndEvent()) Singleplayer & Multiplayer Fully server-authoritative. All spawning, loot, and despawn logic runs server-side. Works in singleplayer, Host & Play, and dedicated servers. Translations Russian translation included, contributed by RedLink-kam. Translators are welcome to submit other languages — copy Translate/EN/Sandbox.json and Translate/EN/ContextMenu.json into a language folder (e.g. Translate/RU/) and translate the values. Submit translations via Workshop comments and they'll be added in the next release. Support If this mod made your squad fight over a crate, help me call in the next drop: My Mod Collection This is the list of mods I use on the server I play with my friends: Faitas' PZ MP Mod Collection Workshop ID: 3678109350 Mod ID: ChopperDrop

The original Equipment UI Workshop mod is not required. Features include: Paper-doll-style equipment interface. Drag & Drop equipment management. Support for vanilla and modded BodyLocations. Build 42.20 compatibility. Performance and stability improvements. Optimized clothing, equipment and Hotbar updates. Correctly scaled equipment icons. Support for larger icon textures without slot overflow. UI scaling from 0.5x to 4.0x with additional intermediate steps. Option to hide equipped items from the normal inventory. Do not keep both Workshop items installed. Both provide Equipment UI under the same Mod ID and overlapping Lua files. description: Companion mod for Solar Floodlight by alexander.ronin13. Extends solar floodlights with car batteries, motion sensors, and lightbulb slots. Never modifies Solar Floodlight files. Safe to add or remove mid-save. Credits All credit for Solar Floodlight goes to its original author, alexander.ronin13. This is a companion add-on only — it does not include, modify, or redistribute any Solar Floodlight code. Solar Floodlight on Steam Workshop Features Extended Batteries — Car batteries, lighter batteries, and ISA mod batteries work in floodlights. Drain scales with capacity (car batteries last multiple nights). Condition-based degradation. Larger batteries boost light radius (+2 to +6 tiles). Condition preserved on removal. Motion Sensor — Install a motion sensor for proximity-activated lighting. Configurable detection radius, detection targets (players/zombies/both), and optional passive drain. Requires Electrical skill (configurable). Lightbulb Slot (off by default) — When enabled, floodlights require a lightbulb to operate. Accepts any vanilla lightbulb. Bulbs degrade over time and eventually burn out. Condition preserved on removal. Operating Modes — ON (always on), OFF (always off), AUTO (night only). All parameters fully configurable via sandbox options. Custom battery and bulb types can be added without a mod update. Full multiplayer/dedicated server support. Quick Reference — Nights to Empty (8h nights, 100% condition) - CarBattery1 (50 Ah): ~3.4 nights — sustainable ~4 PZ months - CarBattery3 (75 Ah): ~4.2 nights — sustainable ~5.4 PZ months - CarBattery2 (100 Ah): ~4.8 nights — sustainable ~6.4 PZ months - DeepCycleBattery (200 Ah): ~6.8 nights — sustainable ~9.5 PZ months - SuperBattery (400 Ah): ~9.7 nights — sustainable ~13.5 PZ months Setup 1. Subscribe to this mod and Solar Floodlight 2. Add both to your server's mod list (this mod loads AFTER Solar Floodlight) 3. That's it — works automatically Server Config WorkshopItems=3680577450;3683488496 Mods=SolarFloodlight;SLBatteryPack Sandbox Options Battery: CondLossPerNight (1.5), CondLossOnZero (3.0), ConditionMin (0), EnableRadiusBonus (on), ReferenceAh (2.5), BatteryTypes (registry string) Sensor: SensorSkillLevel (4), SensorRadius (15), SensorPassiveDrain (0) Bulbs: EnableBulbs (off), BulbLifespanMult (1.0), BulbTypes (extra types string) See the README in the mod folder for detailed descriptions, scaling formulas, tuning guides, and technical documentation. ISA Battery Support ISA batteries (WiredCarBattery, DeepCycleBattery, DIYBattery, SuperBattery) are supported out of the box. Capacity is read from ISA's ModData when available. Mid-Save Safety Safe to add or remove mid-save. All data is stored in Solar Floodlight's own ModData and is simply ignored without this mod. Workshop ID: 3683488496 Mod ID: SLBatteryPack

description: Multiplayer Here (Do not report bugs if you have other mods installed) NECROA - THE KNOX EVENT REIMAGINED If you ever unleashed the Necroa Virus in Plague Inc. and watched civilization collapse beneath an unstoppable tide of infection, this is your chance to experience the aftermath firsthand. Necroa brings the spirit of the iconic Necroa Virus into Project Zomboid, transforming the Knox Event into a far more dangerous and unforgiving apocalypse. The infected are no longer static enemies that remain unchanged throughout your playthrough. As time passes, they evolve into increasingly aggressive, resilient, and unpredictable threats. These evolutions are not limited to statistics. New zombie variants feature unique appearances, equipment, and behaviors, making the progression of the outbreak visible throughout the world. What begins as a familiar zombie apocalypse gradually develops into a nightmare where the infection itself feels alive and constantly adapting. Inspired by Plague Inc.'s most infamous plague, Necroa expands upon the concept with additional infection systems, advanced zombie mechanics, and a growing sense of dread designed to keep players under constant pressure. Survival becomes harsher, mistakes become more costly, and the undead become a threat that can never be underestimated. WARNING This mod is not designed to be beginner-friendly. Many of its mechanics are intentionally built to create a more realistic and hostile environment. Actions that are normally safe in vanilla Project Zomboid may carry significant risks when Necroa is enabled. Protective equipment matters. The airborne strain of the virus is fully simulated, and your character is not immune to it. Exposure without proper protection can result in infection and death. Players who prefer a less punishing experience can disable the Air Infection mechanic through the Necroa settings. While the infected may appear manageable during the early days of a playthrough, they become substantially more dangerous as the outbreak progresses. By the mid and late game, zombies evolve from a simple obstacle into a persistent and escalating threat. Fortifications, safehouses, protective gear, and long-term planning are no longer optional luxuries. They are essential survival tools. Barricade your windows. Reinforce your doors. Prepare for the outbreak to get worse. Because it will. FEATURES • Progressive zombie evolution system • Multiple unique infected variants • Fully modeled airborne infection mechanics • Expanded survival and containment gameplay • Visual progression of the outbreak through equipment and zombie appearances • Increased difficulty and long-term threat escalation • Additional systems inspired by the Necroa Virus from Plague Inc. • Customization options If you want to know a bit more about the Zcom lore, want the Zcom hazmat suit separately or is having problems with textures of the hazmat suit, try: CREDITS & ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS Some early versions of Necroa incorporated concepts and code originating from inactive or abandoned Project Zomboid mods, including Sense of Smell and Susceptible. Over time, several of these systems have been rewritten, modified, or replaced with custom implementations. For example, the original Sense of Smell functionality was replaced by a custom version beginning with Update 1.6. Unfortunately, I was unable to establish contact with the original creators before release. If you are one of the original authors and would prefer your work not be referenced or utilized in this project, please contact me and I will gladly update the mod and replace the affected systems with entirely original implementations. Special thanks to: Phil J Herman Spyjack Notloc Mr Sunshine babybobo (Translations) SimKDT Fernitelearnite (Writer) And above all, Ryuku. Thank you for your support, feedback, inspiration, and contributions throughout development. ABOUT THE PROJECT Necroa was developed over the course of approximately eight months and represents one of the most ambitious projects I have undertaken for Project Zomboid. Every system, model, texture, mechanic, and update was created with the goal of delivering a unique zombie apocalypse experience that feels increasingly desperate, immersive, and oppressive as the world falls apart around you. Thank you for playing. ROADMAP The following features are planned for future (some will be added only in the Necroa Outbreak mod that will come in the future): • New unique zombie animations (Outbreak) • Zombie vocalizations and lament sounds (Outbreak) • Restoration of zombies consuming corpses • Zombies capable of breaking small fences • Spitter-type infected variants • Acid-type infected variants • Advanced zombie migration mechanics (Outbreak) (More features are planned and will be announced in future updates.) description: Dead Magic introduces a full-featured spellcasting system to the zombie apocalypse. Craft grimoires, learn spells, perform rituals, and enchant your gear. Grimoires are equipable spellcasting weapons: store multiple spells, cycle between them, and cast on the move. Progress a custom Magic perk through 5 volumes of skill books, grimoire crafting tiers (Apprentice → Master), per-spell mastery, meditation, and rare relic artifacts with unique built-in effects. A full casting system: spellbooks found in world loot, spell cooldowns, endurance costs, and visual effects. Higher progression reduces costs and improves consistency. Timed ritual casting with powerful, long-duration effects paid for in fatigue and health. Rituals require remaining stationary while channeling. Most unlock by reading ritual manuals; Arcane Cache unlocks via Magic level. Enchant weapons, jewelry, clothing, footwear, gloves, and containers via the crafting menu or context menu. Bonuses scale with your Magic level. Convert eligible books and manuals into Research Points, then unlock permanent upgrades across a 24-node tree. Individual spells also improve as you cast them, and meditation offers level-scaled recovery benefits. Enable the mod and start/load a character (If needed) Find and Read the Magic Talent magazine to gain magical affinity Craft a grimoire which contains Mage Bolt for free, and/or find at least one spellbook Right-click spellbook → Add Spell to Grimoire Equip the grimoire and cast your first spell. Active spell can be selected via Grimoire context menu, or via holding hotkey (Default R). Read a ritual manual to unlock your first ritual Open Review Grimoire via Context menu or Hotkey and begin a ritual while standing still Start enchanting gear once your Magic level increases via the crafting menu or Context menu for appropriate items Multiplayer is supported and actively tested. If you hit an issue, please post in the Bug Report thread. For server hosts — add to your server config: WorkshopItems=3686883520 Mods=DeadMagic Fatigue costs and minimum cost floor Ritual cast time multiplier Meditation gain/recovery multipliers Mastery gain and enchantment quality multipliers Artifact drop rate multiplier Why can’t I cast? You may be on cooldown, out of endurance/fatigue, or missing an active spell in your equipped grimoire. Why is a ritual locked? Read its ritual manual first (except Arcane Cache, which is level-based). Why does a ritual fail mid-cast? You moved or were interrupted; rituals require staying on the same square while channeling. Why can’t I research an item? Research only works on supported items in your main inventory. Can I change keybinds? Yes, all Dead Magic controls are rebindable. Can I add this to an existing save? Yes — enable the mod and load your save. Find and read the Magic Talent magazine if needed, then craft a grimoire to get started. Can I remove it mid-save? Not recommended. description: Multiplayer compatible. Safe to add to existing saves. Nutrition Makes Sense Nutrition Makes Sense rebuilds how hunger, food, and weight work so maintaining yourself feels more intuitive in normal play. In vanilla, staying on top of weight usually means monitoring calories and checking body weight. NMS was made to reduce that kind of number-watching by giving the player earlier, more useful feedback through ordinary gameplay. Food values have also been adjusted across around 600 vanilla items to have more realistic nutritional values. Weight changes are also less wobbly and more grounded in sustained eating patterns. The goal is not to make nutrition harsher. It is to make it more readable, more responsive, and easier to manage without turning it into a numbers chore. What changes Hunger reflects energy state If you're not eating enough, hunger starts to show it earlier, instead of leaving weight change as the main thing to monitor. Food values are rebuilt Satiety, calories, and macros are authored per item based on the actual food. You do not need to lean on a few outlier foods just to maintain yourself. Weight follows sustained patterns Missing one meal will not meaningfully change your weight. Repeated overeating or undereating will. Deprivation takes sustained neglect Ordinary inconsistency will not wreck you. Serious deprivation only sets in if you stay underfed for too long, at which point stamina recovery slows, fatigue rises, and melee damage starts to fall. Protein matters too Protein is tracked across multiple days. Going too long without decent protein intake slows healing. What you see Reworked food tooltips with simple readouts for satiety, energy density, and dominant macro. A malnourished moodle when nutritional deprivation starts kicking in. Health panel entries showing active penalties from deprivation or protein deficiency, and whether things are getting better or worse. Weight trend with exact number shown on the character screen. More in the Makes Sense series Source: GitHub Workshop ID: 3690404044 Mod ID: NutritionMakesSense

DESCRIPTION Tougher Vehicles is a simple, highly customizable utility mod that lets you adjust how much damage your vehicle takes. Say goodbye to your car turning into paper after hitting a few zombies! Everything is designed to be "plug-and-play" without breaking core mechanics or causing conflicts with other custom vehicle mods. KEY FEATURES - Dual Compatibility: Natively supports both Project Zomboid Build 41 and Build 42. - Global Durability: Tweak the overall durability multiplier from 2x stronger up to completely unbreakable. - Per-Part Customization: Fine-tune specific parts individually! You can set Tires, Windows, Doors, Engine, Trunk, and Lights to have their own separate durability, or just let them follow the Global setting. - Tire Auto-Inflation: Keep your tires automatically at maximum air pressure (PSI) so they never deflate. - Battery Saver: Significantly slow down the car's battery drain rate when using the radio, heater, or headlights. - 100% Safe: The battery drain setting ONLY applies to actual Car Batteries attached to the vehicle. It does NOT affect normal small batteries used for flashlights or portable electronics. SANDBOX OPTIONS Options are clearly organized into GLOBAL and PART settings: • [GLOBAL] General Durability Multiplier: 1x | 2x | 3x | 5x (Default) | 10x | Unbreakable • [GLOBAL] Battery Drain Rate: Vanilla | 2x Slower | 5x Slower (Default) | 10x Slower • [GLOBAL] Tire Auto-Inflation (Pressure): Vanilla | Always Fully Inflated (Default) • [PART] Tires Durability: Default (Use Global) | 2x | 3x | 5x | 10x | Unbreakable • [PART] Windows Durability: Default (Use Global) | 2x | 3x | 5x | 10x | Unbreakable • [PART] Doors Durability: Default (Use Global) | 2x | 3x | 5x | 10x | Unbreakable • [PART] Engine Durability: Default (Use Global) | 2x | 3x | 5x | 10x | Unbreakable • [PART] Trunk Durability: Default (Use Global) | 2x | 3x | 5x | 10x | Unbreakable • [PART] Lights Durability: Default (Use Global) | 2x | 3x | 5x | 10x | Unbreakable FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (FAQ) Q: Why do my car windows still break when surrounded by a horde of zombies? A: The durability multiplier applies to every single part of the car, including the windows. However, windows in Zomboid naturally have very low base health (often just 10-20 points). description: Connected Generators B42 Connected Generators B42 allows nearby generators to operate as a managed power cluster in Project Zomboid Build 42. Instead of relying on a single generator, active generators in the same cluster share the network's fuel demand. If one generator runs out of fuel, generators that still have fuel can absorb the remaining demand. The mod also adds computer terminals, persistent Network IDs, custom generator groups, remote monitoring, an interactive network map, pager alerts, and range visualization tools. Supports Singleplayer, hosted Multiplayer, and Dedicated Servers. Requires Project Zomboid Build 42.10 or newer. Main Features Generator Clusters Nearby connected generators operate as a shared power cluster. Fuel demand is distributed across active generators. Available generators can absorb the share of a generator that runs dry. Supports generators across multiple floors. Named generators remain tracked while their chunks are unloaded. Remote simulation accounts for time spent outside loaded chunks. Chunk unloading does not remove generators from the network. Default connection settings: Horizontal link range: 15 tiles. Vertical link range: 3 levels above and below. Both connection ranges are configurable in Sandbox Options. Electricity coverage follows Project Zomboid's vanilla generator range settings. Computer Terminal Turn compatible desktop computers into generator management terminals. Computers require electricity and shut down when power is lost. Powered computers contribute to electrical demand. Assign unique Network IDs to generators. Monitor fuel, condition, state, usage, runtime, floor, and connected devices. Turn authorized generators on or off remotely. Access is restricted to the computer owner and authorized faction members. Generator Groups Create, rename, and delete custom groups. Move generators between groups. Unassigned generators appear under Ungrouped. Expand or collapse individual groups. Search by Network ID, owner, faction, group, or state. Filter by group and Online, Offline, or Disconnected state. Groups and assignments are stored on the computer and persist with the save. Authorized players using the same computer share its organization. The groups are merely organizational for separating the list of generators; placing generators in the same group does not guarantee that they are sharing the load. Visualization Tools Display direct connection lines between generators. Show numbered generator markers. View fuel, condition, usage, runtime, and floor information in tooltips. Display generator link ranges. Display full electricity coverage. Display currently energized areas. Display combined cluster coverage. Identify generators above or below the current floor. Network Map Interactive world map integrated into the computer terminal. Display generator locations, direct links, and coverage overlays. Search by generator Network ID. Search the bundled street database by street or city name. Center the map on the player's current location. Show or clear a local route to the selected generator. Monitoring and route display are independent: monitoring changes the networks saved on the computer, while route controls only affect the local player's overlay. Pager Alert System Link a pager to one or more named generator networks. Receive alerts when generators turn on or off. Receive alerts when generators disconnect. Configure low-fuel and low-condition thresholds. Alerts are delivered through the pager with an audible notification. Sandbox Options Horizontal generator link range. Vertical generator link range. Desktop computer power consumption. Enable or disable the computer system. Enable or disable the Network Map. Enable or disable the pager system. Compatibility and Important Notes Client and server should use the same mod version. Fully restart the game after updating; Lua reload is not sufficient for every handler. Dedicated servers must be restarted after updating the mod. Loaded generator condition remains governed by Project Zomboid's vanilla generator system and is not artificially redistributed by the mod. Search and filter state is local to the current terminal window. Generator groups and assignments are persistent data stored on each computer. This mod is under active development. Bug reports and suggestions are welcome. When reporting a problem, please include whether it happened in Singleplayer, hosted Multiplayer, or on a Dedicated Server, along with any relevant console or server logs.
