description: Slide Bite You picked up a semi-auto pistol for the first time, what could go wrong? ───────────────────────────────────────── In vanilla Project Zomboid, a character who has never touched a gun in their life handles a semi-automatic pistol with perfect form every time. Slide Bite fixes that. Semi-automatic pistols have a reciprocating slide that travels rearward over the grip on every shot. An inexperienced shooter who holds the gun too high gets the web of their hand caught by that slide. The result is a cut. It bleeds. It can get infected. It hurts. ───────────────────────────────────────── What Happens When It Triggers A laceration is applied to your right hand — treated like any other cut in the game. Clean it, bandage it, watch it for infection. Ignore it and it compounds. Your character says something. They noticed. ───────────────────────────────────────── Risk by Skill Level Aiming 0 — 10% chance per shot Aiming 1 — 5% chance per shot Aiming 2 — 2% chance per shot Aiming 3+ — 0%. Muscle memory. You've got it now. ───────────────────────────────────────── How to Stop It Pick the right profession — Police and Veterans start knowing how to hold semi-auto pistols correctly. Level up — reach Aiming 3 and the risk disappears entirely Wear gloves — any gloves in the hand slot protect you fully, including modded ones Read the manual — find the Pistol Technique Manual in gun stores, police stations, and army surplus to permanently learn proper grip at any skill level Learn the hard way — get slide bitten enough times and your character figures it out on their own ───────────────────────────────────────── Revolvers Are Now a Real Choice Revolvers have no slide. There is nothing to bite you. A complete beginner can pick up a revolver on day one and fire it without consequence. This makes early gun selection meaningful. The revolver is forgiving — low capacity, slow to reload, but safe to use while your skills are zero. The semi-automatic is more capable, but it will punish you for holding it wrong until you learn. Choose based on your confidence, not just your loot. ───────────────────────────────────────── Works With Modded Weapons and Gloves Any semi-automatic pistol with a detachable magazine is automatically eligible. Any item in the hand clothing slot automatically protects. No patches needed for weapon or clothing packs. ───────────────────────────────────────── Multiplayer Ready All wound application and stat tracking run server-side. Works on hosted and dedicated servers without configuration. ───────────────────────────────────────── Mod ID: SlideBite Build: 42.16 Version: 1.1 Workshop ID: 3693775109 Mod ID: SlideBite

No hooking, no metatable juggling, no layout lifecycle. require "TooltipLib/Core" TooltipLib.registerProvider({ id = "MyMod_WeaponStats", target = "item", enabled = TooltipLib.Filters.weapon, cacheable = true, description = "Weapon damage stats", callback = function(ctx) ctx:addKeyValue("Damage:", "+15%", nil, TooltipLib.Colors.GREEN) ctx:addProgress("Mastery:", 0.75, nil, TooltipLib.Colors.GOLD) end, }) The framework handles the hook, the layout, the error handling, and the caching. Your callback adds content. Error isolation. Every callback runs inside pcall. Provider A fails, providers B through Z keep rendering. Circuit breaker benches repeat offenders after 10 consecutive errors. Cleanup phase runs unconditionally — if your preTooltip modified item state and your callback divided by zero, cleanup still fires. Filtering. 14 item filters, 3 world object filters, factory functions for custom cases, combinators (allOf, anyOf, negate). Every filter is pcall-hardened. Context methods. Ten common methods for all surfaces: addLabel addKeyValue addProgress addInteger addFloat addPercentage addSpacer addHeader addDivider addText Layout surfaces (item, itemSlot, object) add texture rendering. Rich text surfaces (skill, vehicle) add line-level formatting. 5-phase lifecycle. preTooltip → callback → textures → postRender → cleanup. In order. Multiplayer Item, skill, vehicle, and recipe surfaces are fully client-side. Zero server traffic. World objects use a request-response pipeline on dedicated servers. Client sends one request per object. Server reads whitelisted methods only — getters and boolean checks. No mutations, no arbitrary invocation. Responses cached client-side. Sandbox option EnableMPSync lets admins disable the pipeline. Singleplayer and listen servers read directly. No network overhead. Compatibility Works alongside mods that hook ISToolTipInv.render directly — deferred mode detects the foreign hook and renders provider content below it. Works with Inventory Tetris, Equipment UI, and other UI-replacing mods. Multiple mods can bundle TooltipLib — version guard ensures newest copy loads, older ones skip silently. VorpallySauced — Weapon progression tooltips. Affixes, mastery, kill tracking. description: Sauce Tooltips A good safehouse has labels on things. What it is, what shape it's in, how much is left. Vanilla's generator tooltip says "Generator." That's the whole thing. You're hovering the one machine keeping your food cold, and the game tells you its name. Not the fuel. Not whether it's even running. Sauce Tooltips fills in the label. Hover a thing and it tells you what you'd actually want to know: world objects, items, vehicles, crops, crafting. Everything is client-side, nothing touches your save, and every label has its own off switch. The objects you use constantly had nothing useful on hover. Now they do, each one led by its name so you always know what you're looking at. Generators. Running or off, fuel level, condition — up front instead of three clicks into a menu. Fridges & Freezers. Power state, preservation, a capacity bar per compartment. Says it plainly when the grid's down and your food's on the clock. Stoves & Ovens. On or off, temperature, timer, broken warnings. Microwaves, toasters, coffee makers too. Fireplaces & Barbecues. Lit, smouldering, or cold. Fuel in hours. Barbecues call out propane vs. charcoal. Reads from across the room. Lamps. On or off, bulb or no bulb, grid or battery, battery level. Catch a dying bulb before it dies. Containers. How full, how many items, locked or not — anything with storage. Farm Plants. Growth phase, water, health, disease, fertilizer. More shows the higher your Farming. Replaces the vanilla farming tooltip. Rain Collectors. Water level, exact amount, tainted warning. TVs & Radios. On or off, power source, channel, volume. Radios flag whether they transmit. Ore Deposits. Iron, copper, flint, limestone — deposit size, expected yield, the Masonry level it wants, whether you've got a pickaxe in hand. Clocks. Wall and standing clocks read out the time. Food. Freshness bar, green to yellow to red, with a spoilage estimate ("~36h", "~2d"). Poison and cook-before-eating warnings that only fire when they should. Canned goods say "Non-perishable" instead of faking a full bar. Drainables. "~12 uses left" for lighters, spray cans, glue. Charge percent for batteries. Seeds. When to sow, plus best and risky months once your Farming comes up. Bait & Traps. Which animals a bait draws and what a trap catches, scaled to your Trapping skill. Item Tags. Flags what you can dismantle or smelt. Evolved Recipes. Hold Shift on an ingredient to see where it goes — Soup, Stew, and the rest. Weapon Stats. The raw combat numbers the game hides: min-max damage, crit chance and multiplier, attack speed, reach, break-chance odds, endurance cost, max targets per swing, tree-chopping stats — and for guns, hit chance, recoil, aiming time, magazine and jam chance. Hold the detail key for the skill-adjusted numbers. Vehicle Parts. Condition color-coded so a whole car reads at a glance, install skill requirements, storage space. Crafting Recipes. Hold Shift for base craft time next to your skill-reduced time, and the yield on recipes that make more than one. NEW — The Full Card (beta) As of v1.4.0 the mod can rebuild the game's own tooltip rows too: weapons, food, clothing, containers, literature, the lot. The whole card becomes one piece instead of a mod strip stapled under a vanilla box. It also double-checks itself. The first time you hover each kind of item, it compares its card to the tooltip vanilla would have drawn. If they disagree, it steps aside and you get the plain vanilla tooltip for the rest of the session. Every row was verified against the full item catalogue (about 5,000 items) before shipping. If you'd rather sit the beta out, it's one toggle in Mod Options. The look Accent rails. A colored strip on every card, using the same colors as the other Sauce mods. Firearms blue, melee red, food green. A generator's rail is green when it's running and red when it's off. Names on top. World-object cards lead with the object's name on an accent-colored rail — a running generator's header glows green, ore reads gold. Range gating. Cards respect distance: close for containers, a bit further for generators, across the room for a fire. Detail mode. Hold Left Shift for the extra layer. Rebindable in TooltipLib's options. The dress. Every card wears the kraft label: paper body, a colored rail under the name, dot leaders between labels and values, dotted section rules, and real gauges instead of flat bars. It ships in this mod — no other mod needed — and there's a toggle if you prefer the plain vanilla box. When Sauce Inventory Rendering is installed (our inventory mod, coming to the Workshop), its card takes over so tooltips and inventory stay in step. Playing with other tooltip mods: if another tooltip framework takes over the card (StarlitLibrary and friends), nothing is lost — their content renders untouched and ours appends below it. By default the skin steps aside for the session so every tooltip matches; TooltipLib's options have a switch for the mixed look if you'd rather keep the kraft where we own the card. Options > Mods > Sauce Tooltips Tooltip Range — how far away object tooltips read. Full card replacement (beta) — the vanilla-row rebuild, on by default. Dressed tooltips (kraft card) — the label skin, on by default. Options > Mods > TooltipLib holds the per-label switches — one tickbox per source (Fridges, Stoves, Food, Vehicles, and the rest). Never touch vehicles? Turn that one off and those rows stop existing. The detail-info key and the other-tooltip-framework option live here too. description: FIRST IN MOD LOAD ORDER Compatibility Notice for Inventory Overhaul Mods Most of this mod will work with other mods as long as Better Pause is loaded early in your mod load order. However, complete inventory overhauls can overwrite vanilla inventory files and may bring the pause restriction back into the inventory context menus. Clean UI Compatibility - Build 42.19 Clean UI is supported in Build 42.19+ when the Better Pause Clean UI compatibility file is loaded after Clean UI. Recommended load order: 1. TwisTonFire - Better Pause 2. Clean UI 3. Better Pause Clean UI Compatibility File This allows the inventory right-click menus to work while paused, even when Clean UI replaces the inventory menu files. If another mod fully overwrites the inventory system after the compatibility file, that mod may still reintroduce the pause restriction. TwisTonFire - Better Pause This mod removes the pause-related restrictions that Project Zomboid normally enforces. In vanilla, a number of actions are explicitly blocked while Active Pause is enabled. In many cases, the player could otherwise simply queue actions, plan the next step, and continue playing when ready. This mod removes all pause restrictions currently known to me, allowing you to queue actions even while Active Pause is enabled. It also includes an optional Mod Option that can automatically pause the game right after you enter your world. This option is disabled by default and works in Singleplayer only. Important Load Order Information This mod must be placed at the very top of your mod load order, before all other mods. The reason is simple: This mod uses full vanilla file overrides. Those files must load first in order to cleanly replace the original game files. If another mod loads before this one, its changes may not work properly or may not appear in-game at all. Why I made my own version There are already similar mods on the Steam Workshop. However, I do not want to depend on whether another mod is updated or abandoned. Because of that, I created and maintain my own version, so I can make sure it continues to work the way I want. Why this mod can be updated quickly Whenever Project Zomboid receives an update, I only need to run a script on my own PC. That script automatically takes the new vanilla files and removes the pause restrictions for me. This makes it easy for me to update the mod as quickly as possible after a game update, without manually editing every file by hand again. Why full file overrides are necessary Unfortunately, complete file overrides are the only sensible way to remove these restrictions. In most cases, the pause checks are placed very high up inside very long functions. Because of that, they cannot be cleanly removed with lightweight hooks or small compatibility patches. My goal with this mod My goal is to keep this mod updated as quickly as possible whenever the game changes, so the functionality remains available. I also make sure that each version of this mod only patches the exact Project Zomboid version it is intended for. Summary Removes all pause restrictions currently known to me Lets you queue actions while Active Pause is enabled Optional automatic pause after entering your world Auto-pause option is disabled by default Singleplayer-only auto-pause option Must be placed at the very top of the mod load order Uses full vanilla file overrides Designed for fast maintenance after game updates Version-specific patching for the intended Project Zomboid version Is this mod better than X? I cannot say whether this mod is better than another one. What I can say is that this mod is very clear about how it is meant to be used: It must be loaded before all other mods. Nothing breaks when the game updates. The patches only apply to the specific game version this mod was made for. Its translation files also clearly warn that it must be placed at the very top of the load order. 12 current translations of the in-game mod description. Another important difference is how this mod is maintained. It does not simply comment out these restrictions — it removes them entirely. Compatibility FIRST IN MOD LOAD ORDER Your support helps me keep going — thank you very much in advance! Workshop ID: 3696291148 Mod ID: twistbetterpause Mod ID: twistbetterpause_cleanui_compat

description: Meat Expansion 2.0 (ﾉ◕ヮ◕)ﾉ*:･ﾟ✧ By Yumi Hi! Meat Expansion was my very first mod. (´｡• ᵕ •｡`) I’m Yumi, a proud meat lover, and I always felt like Project Zomboid was seriously lacking when it came to animal drops. You would go through all the effort of hunting, raising, and butchering an animal, only to receive an amount of meat that never really felt worth it. So, naturally, I decided to enter the meat dimension and fix it myself. (ง •̀_•́)ง When I first uploaded this mod, it was very much a learning project. It worked, but it was simple, messy in some places, and I still had a lot to learn. Since then, Meat Expansion has grown into a much larger mod with 43 distinct cuts of meat, proper 3D world models, custom textures, raw and cooked versions, burnt variations, expanded animal drops, and a completely reworked hunger and portion system. It took me a lot of time to learn Blender, 3D modeling, textures, UVs, scaling, scripting, and how to make everything actually appear correctly in-game. I broke things, fixed them, broke them again, and somehow survived. (｡•́︿•̀｡) But I am honestly really happy with how far this mod has come. Meat Expansion was originally inspired by Vanilla Foods Expansion, specifically the way it allowed pigs to drop different kinds of meat. I thought that idea was really cool and wanted to create my own much larger version covering several animals and many more cuts. This is still my first mod, so please go easy on me. I’m always learning, but I have put a lot of time, effort, and love into it. <3 What This Mod Does (っ◔◡◔)っ Meat Expansion reworks and expands animal butchering drops to make hunting, farming, and raising animals feel more rewarding. Instead of receiving only a small selection of generic meat, animals can now provide multiple recognizable cuts based on their species. The mod currently includes beef, pork, chicken, turkey, lamb, sheep, and venison cuts, including steaks, ribs, roasts, organs, wings, legs, shoulders, brisket, tenderloin, and much more. Lard Drop Values (づ｡◕‿‿◕｡)づ Lard drops have been reworked and are now exclusive to cows and deer. Adult Cows → 12 Lard Calves → 5 Lard Adult Deer → 5 Lard Fawns → 2 Lard Vanilla Foods Expansion Notice (´｡• ᵕ •｡`) You do not need Vanilla Foods Expansion to use this mod. Meat Expansion has its own expanded animal drops and can be used completely by itself. If you still want to use Vanilla Foods Expansion alongside this mod, that is entirely up to you. Just understand that both mods alter animal meat drops. Using both may result in much larger meat yields than intended because Vanilla Foods Expansion can add its meats while Meat Expansion also adds mine. So, if your butchered animal suddenly explodes into a grocery store worth of meat, that is probably why. (╥﹏╥) If there is another type of meat you would like to see in the future, feel free to let me know. I may add more whenever I have the time and energy. Build 42.20 Compatibility (ง •̀_•́)ง Compatible with Build 42.20 Works with most mods Mods that edit animal loot tables may conflict Vanilla Foods Expansion is not required Using Vanilla Foods Expansion alongside this mod may produce very large meat drops The Workshop poster has also been refreshed and updated for Build 42.20. Final Notes I’m a mom to a two-year-old, I work full-time, I run a household, and I have a life that exists well beyond this game. So updates won’t always be instant—I fit this in when I can, and I appreciate your patience. If you run into a glitch or bug, please let me know with as much detail as possible (what happened, any error messages, steps to reproduce). That genuinely helps me fix things faster. And about the images: yes, I use AI to make them. I don’t draw, I’m not paying someone to create art for a hobby project, and I’ve got far bigger things to deal with than pixel-perfect illustrations. I like the images I generate—they bring my OC to life in a way that makes me happy. That’s the point. So if you’re here to drop “AI slop” comments, save it. I don’t care. Move on. I’m here to have fun, share something I love, and build a little community around it. If that’s not your vibe, the door’s right there. ✌️ Final Thoughts (≧◡≦) This mod has been a huge learning experience, and I’m incredibly proud of how far it has come. Learning Blender, fixing 3D models, creating textures, adding raw, cooked, and burnt variations, expanding animal drops, and rebuilding the hunger system was definitely not easy. There were many moments when I broke something, fixed it, and then somehow broke something completely unrelated—but seeing everything finally come together made it worth it. If you enjoy Meat Expansion, liking and favoriting the mod means everything to me. <3 Thank you for checking it out! — Yumi ^v^ WARNING Any hateful or disrespectful comments towards me or my family will be deleted and reported. I don't care if you disagree with me using AI to make my images, that's my choice, and that does not mean you should harass me for it. Workshop ID: 3700009701 Mod ID: MeatExpansion2.0 ❤️ Taking a Mental Break from Modding ❤️ I’ve decided to take a mental break from modding for a little while. I truly love creating mods, but lately, updating them has started to feel more like a chore than something I genuinely enjoy. I don’t want to push myself until I’m completely burned out or lose my love for something that has brought me so much happiness. Unless an issue is genuinely serious or causing the game to break, I won’t be working on or updating my mods for the time being. However, if you encounter something truly game-breaking, please feel free to send me a DM. I’m also planning to create my own Discord server very soon, where you’ll be able to find information, updates, and support for all of my mods in one place. For now, I’ve temporarily turned off the comments. Please don’t worry—they will be turned back on once I feel ready to regularly check in on everything again. Right now, I simply want to enjoy playing other games, relax, and spend more time with my daughter without feeling like I constantly need to work on something. Thank you all so much for your patience, understanding, and continued support. It genuinely means more to me than you know. This isn’t goodbye—I just need a little time to rest and enjoy the things that matter most. ❤️ — Yumi <3

Shared Global Map Share one single map between all players on the server. Shared Global Map is a global map sharing mod for Project Zomboid Build 41 and Build 42. It is not faction-based: shared map information is available to every player using the mod on the server. Main Features - Map annotations are shared between all players. - Placing, editing, moving, resizing or removing annotations is synchronized. - Text and symbol annotations keep their assigned size. - Reading a paper map shares the revealed map area with everyone else. - Annotated-map markers are imported into the shared map when the game exposes them. - General map exploration is shared. - Players joining later receive the current shared map state. - Shared map data is stored server-side to reduce the risk of annotations disappearing after reconnecting. World Map Tools - Improved annotation palette with Favorites and Recent symbols. - Quick favorite toggle with right click. - Free drawing tool directly inside the map annotation interface. - Free drawings are shared and can be removed with the remove marking tool. - Compact SGM map legend with a show/hide button. - World-map shortcuts for faster annotation use. GPS Navigation - Adds a GPS interface and on-screen direction arrow. - Text annotations can be used as destinations. - Remaining distance is displayed while navigating. - The destination is cleared automatically once reached. - You can follow another online player locally without sharing that follow target. - GPS currently points directly toward the destination. Road-aware route calculation is not active yet. Build 41 note: GPS destinations can be private or shared with players using the same marker color. Build 42 note: GPS has been adapted to the new map UI, but old marker-color team routing is not treated as a B42 core feature while the new system is being stabilized. Dedicated SGM Mini-Map - Adds a dedicated Shared Global Map mini-map. - Works independently from the vanilla mini-map server option. - Shows shared text and symbol annotations. - Shows player markers with direction. - Includes recenter and local player-follow controls. - Build 42 support includes vanilla street-name data on the SGM mini-map. Shared Notes - Adds a shared notes panel from the world map. - Notes support titles and multiline text. - Checklist-style text can be written manually. - In Build 41, shared notes use marker-color groups. Player Markers - Player markers can appear on the world map and SGM mini-map. - Each player can choose their marker color. - Your own name is hidden on the map and mini-map, while other players' names can still be shown. Build 41 note: marker color is also used for GPS sharing and shared notes. Build 42 note: marker color is currently kept mainly as a visual player marker preference. City Names - Build 41 can show discovered city names through SGM. - City labels can also appear after reading city maps. - City label size can be configured. - Build 42 already has native map labels, so extra SGM city labels are disabled by default. Mod Options - Enable or disable Favorites / Recent palette sorting. - Enable or disable extra SGM city labels. - Change city label size. - Configure player marker display and marker color. Map Reset Menu The ? button on the world map opens a reset menu. - Clear shared annotations. - Clear map discoveries. Important: for the host / admin, clearing discoveries can also reset the shared discovered map state for everyone. The menu clearly warns about it. Compatibility / Conflicts - Supports Project Zomboid Build 41 and Build 42. - This mod is not designed for faction-only map sharing. - This mod edits the world map annotation UI. - It may conflict with other mods that heavily modify map symbols, annotation tools, or symbol size controls. - Compatibility with extra symbol mods has been improved, but conflicts are still possible depending on how those mods patch the world map UI. - For map mods, shared annotations, discoveries, mini-map display and direct GPS destinations should still work. description: Adaptive Wear System A dynamic clothing and equipment degradation system designed to bring realism and long-term survival consequences into your gameplay. This mod introduces a fully immersive wear system where your gear reflects how you play, how you survive, and how much you neglect it. Core Features Dynamic durability system for clothing and backpacks Visual and mechanical degradation tied to real gameplay actions Progressive damage instead of instant condition loss Fully compatible with singleplayer and multiplayer How It Works Your equipment no longer degrades randomly. Instead, it reacts to your behavior: Blood accumulation increases wear over time Repeated washing weakens fabric durability Overused items become fragile and unreliable Environmental interactions affect your gear condition Every action has consequences. Survival is no longer just about staying alive, but maintaining what keeps you alive. New Mechanics Blood Wear System Heavy blood levels gradually damage clothing and backpacks. Washing Degradation Cleaning your clothes repeatedly will slowly reduce their structural integrity. Hole Creation System Items with high wear have a chance to develop holes, reducing protection and effectiveness. Environmental Damage Walking through dense vegetation (trees, bushes) can damage clothing and create tears. Backpack Degradation Backpacks are no longer immune — they wear down just like clothing. Design Philosophy This mod is not about punishing the player. It is about creating meaningful consequences over time. Neglect your gear, and it will fail you when you need it most. Take care of it, and it will last. Why Use This Mod Adds depth to survival gameplay Makes looting and repairing gear more meaningful Encourages strategic decision-making Enhances immersion without breaking vanilla balance Compatibility Works in both Singleplayer and Multiplayer Designed to integrate naturally with vanilla mechanics Safe to add to existing saves It is not compatible with mods that add dirt to the character or clothing/backpack. It is not compatible with mods that clean clothes with rain. Requires: RealismV4 Growing Up is a challenge scenario where you begin the apocalypse as a child and have to survive long enough to become an adult. You don't start with a profession, useful skills, or anything resembling combat confidence. You start young, weak, frightened, and out of your depth. Your body grows over time. Your fear changes over time. Your skills unlock over time. If you survive long enough, the scared kid you started with slowly becomes a capable survivor. What Growing Up adds Start as a child — begin between ages 8 and 14 instead of as a normal adult survivor Grow into adulthood — age over time until 18, with changing body scale, height, weight, and movement Child archetypes — choose from Scout, Jock, Nerd, Shy, Bully, or Crybaby, each with different starting traits, items, and milestones Age-based progression — body and capabilities change as you grow, including speed, milestone trait changes, and skill access Persistent fear system — panic floor, night fear, nightmares, and emotional vulnerability that slowly ease with age and experience Comfort items — teddy bears and similar items help calm panic when things get bad Literacy progression — kids begin with limited reading ability and have to work up to advanced books through simpler material Age-gated skills — some skills are throttled or locked until you're old enough, so progression feels earned Driving restrictions — too small to drive properly as a young child; older kids may stall while learning Firearm penalties — heavy recoil punishes young survivors until they build experience Custom school escape intro — scripted opening with blocked exits, scavenging pressure, and a desperate escape sequence Kid zombies — child-sized infected appear in the world and inside the challenge setup Growth HUD — tracks age, height, kill count, fear level, XP rate, and upcoming milestones Custom voice system — large set of voice lines reacting to fear, growth, milestones, sleep, wounds, weather, cooking, books, zombies, and more The experience You are smaller than everyone else. You learn slower. You scare easier. Some things are physically harder. Some things are mentally harder. The early game is designed to feel unfair in exactly the way surviving as a kid in Project Zomboid should feel unfair. But the run changes with you. You get older. You get calmer. You unlock new abilities. You stop reacting like a terrified child to every single thing. And eventually, if you make it that far, you stop being a kid at all. description: Loot Sense is a handy little utility that lets you add items or whole recipes to a "shopping list" so it's easier to remember all the things you need while out and about. It can also scan nearby containers for you and alert you by rolling the window down and highlight the item in blue and/or highlighting it in the loot window (can be turned on/off in options), making finding a particular item as fast as running past a group of containers. Features Add singular items from the building/crafting UI to your shopping list. Search box to find, and add any in-game item Notes section for general note-taking. "Don't forget to loot the house on the corner!" description: ﻿ApocalipseBR - Projeto Nemesis Build 42 - Multiplayer Compatible A Resident Evil–inspired boss zombie mod that brings the relentless Nemesis to Project Zomboid. He will find you. What Does This Mod Do? This mod adds a boss-tier zombie wearing the iconic Nemesis outfit that the server automatically spawns near players using an escalating pressure system. The longer you survive without encountering him, the more inevitable his arrival becomes. It works by converting a zombie inside a range to the infamous Nemesis, and he's not like any other zombie: Sprinter - he runs. Always. Superhuman toughness - takes up to 10 hits to bring down (configurable). Hawk vision & pinpoint hearing - he detects you from far away. Long memory & navigation - he remembers where you are and pathfinds toward you. Active redirect - even if distracted, he re-targets the nearest player every few seconds. Doors and barricades - Nemesis does an icreased damage to doors and barricades, there's no stopping him. Also includes the Mr. X outfit as a secondary visual variant. Mr. X is slightly less armored but still uses the same boss module stats. Players cannot equip the Nemesis or Mr. X suits - the mod blocks wearing them from context menus, drag-and-drop, and as a safety net on clothing update events. Pressure Spawn System The server runs a background pressure loop every in-game minute: Pressure increases by a configurable amount each minute (default: +3). When pressure reaches the threshold (default: 30), a spawn roll is attempted. The roll has a configurable success chance (default: 10%). If the roll succeeds, Nemesis spawns 30–45 tiles away from a random eligible player. On spawn or failed roll, pressure resets to zero and the cycle begins again. There is no limit on how much Nemesis can be active at a time - too frequent spawn chances in the sandbox and you may be getting swarmed by Nemesis. With default settings, expect roughly 10 minutes of calm before the first threshold hit, and then it's a dice roll each cycle. Tension builds because you know he's coming - just not exactly when. Sound Design Nemesis has a full 3D positional audio system. All vanilla zombie sounds are suppressed on Nemesis-outfit zombies and replaced with custom ones: Theme music - a looping ambient track audible within 60 tiles. You'll hear him before you see him. "S.T.A.R.S." voice line - plays when Nemesis first detects you (40-tile range). Unmistakable warning. Roars - periodic roars (3 variants) on an 8-second cooldown with a 40% chance per cycle, audible up to 80–100 tiles away. Grunts - plays when Nemesis takes a hit (2 variants, 50% chance), audible within 40 tiles. New features (14/08/2026) Nemesis roars also create an AI sound pulse that can attract nearby zombies, making the fight messier, and harder to ignore. All sound ranges, cooldowns, and chances are configurable through Sandbox Options. You can tune or mute any layer. Boss Corpse & Loot When Nemesis dies: Nemesis can roll up to 3 bonus loot items from a weighted loot table. Ammo boxes, magazines, weapons, Resident Evil gear, and rare ammo cartons can appear depending on the roll. Ammo cartons have the lowest drop chance because they are the rarest reward tier. Optional Bonus Drops Some loot entries are soft-integrations with other ApocalipseBR mods. These mods are not required. If you do not have them installed, their item IDs are skipped safely and Nemesis simply rolls from the items that exist in your mod list. If you have Raccoon City B42, Nemesis can also drop items such as Samurai Edge magazines, Adapter Clips, Resident Evil backpacks/suspenders, and special Raccoon City weapons. If you have ZVirus Vaccine / LabItems, Nemesis also drops biological lab loot: one high-quality infected human brain and 3–10 infected blood samples. This keeps Projeto Nemesis compatible with servers that do not run those extra mods while still rewarding players with thematic crossover loot when they are installed. Sandbox Options Everything is tunable from the server sandbox settings page: What to Expect A slow-burn tension loop that keeps you on edge throughout your session. Audio cues that let you gauge distance and react - or panic. A genuine threat that forces you to think about escape routes, weapon durability, and positioning. Works on dedicated servers with multiple players - Nemesis picks a random target each spawn. Fully configurable difficulty - dial him up for horror, or tone him down for a manageable challenge. A genuine pure rush of adrenaline, specially when it comes unexpected. Known Issues Nemesis zombies can get stuck attacking doors and windows easily. [FIXED] - He breaks doors and barricades despite roleplay state Nemesis may fail to pathfind correctly when spawned too far away from the target player. [Not something i can fix] - I've limited the maximum range in sandbox to an acceptable value to avoid missconfiguration In roleplay zones where door attacks do not deal damage, zombies attacking doors can still be converted into Nemesis, causing Nemesis to get stuck inside those roleplay areas. [FIXED] - the same fix of Nemesis getting stuck on doors and windows easily apply here No knwon issues are in place anymore, if you have any issue feel free to share! Future planned features [IMPLEMENTED] Rare item drop table: guns, ammo, magazines, optional crossover loot, and rare cartons. [IMPLEMENTED] Nemesis corpse cleanup: keeps the boss suit and removes immersion-breaking underwear/clothing. [IMPLEMENTED] Nemesis roar attraction: roars can pull nearby zombies through the game's AI sound system. Credits Original B41 ResidentEvilNemesis assets: Nemeth Workshop ID: 3706463588 Mod ID: ApocalipseBrProjetoNemesis

description: The Ark The Ark is a direct sequel to the Bandits: Week One mod, continuing the story after the dramatic events of the first chapter. You awaken from a coma; disorientated, changed and discover that the world — and your place in it — is no longer the same. Unlike Week One, The Ark delivers a quite different experience. This is a narrative-driven adventure focused on progression, discovery, and atmosphere. The story unfolds step by step, drawing you deeper into a world filled with mystery and unanswered questions. The story will lead you to the answer for the ultimate question about the Knox Infection. Expect rich lore, unexpected twists, and carefully placed surprises as you explore new locations and encounter new events. The mod introduces original gameplay mechanics designed specifically to support the story and immerse you in its themes. Your choices, observations, and persistence matter. The Ark is not just about survival and not about you only — it’s about uncovering the truth, forming connection with other human, and facing moments of challenge. This is a slower, more deliberate journey meant to be experienced, not rushed, but there is also a lot of intense action moments. What is the Ark? The Ark is a SINGLE-PLAYER ONLY mod for Project Zomboid Build 42. It is a total conversion of PZ that revamps the entire map and adds custom elements including NPC's. It is intended to be played through slowly, and offers a story-driven campaign that has probably never been attempted at this scale. This mod cannot be played like vanilla Project Zomboid, it is meant to be explored slowly and methodically. What to expect? This mod is an immersive story that has hundreds of quest lines, where you will explore the ruins of Knox Country, discover the lore of the mysterious Arks, the outbreak of the Knox infection and your place in this apocalypse. But, this story is not just about you: You have others to consider, and their survival is important as your own. This mod is difficult and even the most seasoned PZ players will struggle with some of the changes in the world. Be on your toes at any moment. How to play? This mod requires stable B42 version of the game as well as [B42] Bandits NPC and [B42] Waterpipes mods to run. It is recommended that you play through this mod without any additional mods, ESPECIALLY mods that will overwrite zombie behaviour, zombies, and survival items such as gas masks/hazmat suits. It is also recommended that you do not change the default settings in Sandbox for your first playthrough. It is recommended that you back up your saves frequently. Death comes knocking at every door and at every opportunity. Copy the files in your X:\Users\YourName\Zomboid\Saves\Sandbox\ARK_vX.XXX_Date-Time to a separate folder. If you die, replace the files in that folder with the backup files and overwrite them. Similar to Week One, you can talk with NPC's by pressing the T key, however you will not be expected to type out what you want to say to other NPC's. You can also interact with other NPC's by holding down the Q key, which will give you commands such as to follow/stay and other opportunities to interact with them. The Ark features a central computer, called NOAH, that gives you information about the situation within the Ark. You can interact with it by right clicking on the terminal. You can exit the interaction window by either walking away from the terminal or by closing the terminal by exiting all of the menus. It is vital that you maintain the Ark. This means keeping it fueled, stocked and functioning to ensure survival deep underground. Things such as generators, decontamination chambers and vents all need maintenance to keep running smoothly. Radiation exposure is a major hazard when travelling out of the Ark. It is essential that you prepare for the nuclear winter that has followed the nuclear detonation. Wearing an intact hazmat suit and a gas mask with working filters is important. If you are exposed to radiation, taking Potassium Iodine pills can help to lower your radiation levels, but it is a gradual process and will not take away radiation right away. Do not eat irradiated items without taking them through decontamination first. Lore documents can be explored by clicking on the arrow buttons at the bottom of the page. Important items will be highlighted once you get close to them. Please do not post spoilers here. I reserve the right to delete them. I ran into an error, what should I do? The Ark has been in testing for months, however errors are expected to come up due to how complex the mod is. If you encounter errors, please report them to Slayer's Discord. Please do not report errors that are due to mod conflicts. Donations If you like my work, be sure to give it a LIKE or: Known Issues Player body or some body parts are invisible - restart the game Emma is stuck - hold Q, select Movement and Follow me, go with her to some other location and then hold Q, select Movement and Don't follow. Enabling Living Skeletons can cause issues with targeting. It is recommended that you do not enable this option. Endure. Music Here is a playlist of all tracks in the mod. Anti-Dark-Spawn System - Singleplayer Only for now Every survivor starts with a lighter in their inventory to ensure you're never trapped in total darkness. Additionally, the mod will attempt to automatically flip the light switch in your starting room if the power is still on. Compatibility There should not be any issues with other mods. If you still want to add these spawns to your server, please take a look at the "Multiplayer Instructions" discussion. But please be aware, that i will not be offering support for issues you run into. Known Issues None. How to Spot a Broken Spawn & What to Do To maintain the quality of this mod, please look out for the following: Placement: You should always spawn inside a building. Clipping: You should not be stuck inside furniture or walls. If you encounter a spawn point that breaks these rules, please report it! How to report Provide the coordinates of the location (and ideally a screenshot), and I will fix it in the next update. Future Updates Let me know what you want to see. description: About this mod: This mod makes your diet actually matter by having a simulated gut health, and adds two of the most basic human needs, urinating and defecating. ------------------------------ FEATURES ------------------------------ Fully simulated gut health that tracks what you eat and drink over a period of time, and either improves or damages your gut health based on what you've eaten. Good gut health gives higher endurance regen and slower fatigue, bad gut health gives the opposite. Food related illnesses. Eating too much greasy/sugary/fat foods or drinking too much soda too fast can cause stomach cramps and heart burn. Consistent bad diet can cause frequent diarrhea or constipation. Bladder and bowels that fills up as you play. Drinking and eating will fill it up faster, with simulated digestion meaning it's not an instant fill when you ingest something, but builds up faster the more you eat. Urinate and defecate in toilets, on trees or bushes, in a fluid container, or on the ground. Where you relieve yourself matters, use toilets to avoid unhappiness, if you can't find one then a tree or bush is better than just out in the open. Make sure to wipe using toilet paper, rags, socks or towels to avoid a mess after. Control system for bladder and bowels. Based on what you eat/drink, your health, traits, and panic level, you have varying control over your bladder and bowels, which makes you more or less likely to have accidents. System for urine and feces getting on clothing. Visible dynamic stains for urine and feces on clothing. Leaving soiled clothing to dry can cause permanent damage to the clothing and the stains won't wash out. System for urine and feces getting on your body. If you don't clean urine or feces from your body in time, then you can get a rash that will turn into an infection. Custom smell system. Soiled clothing, unflushed toilets or urine/feces on the ground will leave a bad smell that attracts nearby zombies. The smell travels realistically in buildings and can be cut off by closing doors. Custom UI as a tab in the health panel. Track your intake, see your current gut status, your control level, any illnesses or statuses. Also take actions like checking your pants and wiping/washing yourself. New items. Medications and supplements to help manage your gut health and illnesses. Custom animations for all actions. Sounds for all actions. New moodles and traits. Fully MP compatible. ---------------------------- MOD INCOMPATIBILITIES ---------------------------- It's FULLY COMPATIBLE with Take a Shower and Bath (just needs a tweak to the moodle positions because we use different moodle frameworks) For Lifestyle: Hobbies do this: 1. description: What it does Your character sees more than your screen shows. Walls hide the corner they're staring down, a tree crown covers the zombie on the road, and a staircase is a blind climb into whatever waits at the top. PeekAView closes that gap in three places: Wall cutaway: walls start cutting away at greater distance, so doorways and corners open up as you approach instead of at the last step. Tree fade: trees between you and where you're looking turn see-through, on foot and behind the wheel. Stair view: the upper floor draws while you climb, so you see what's waiting before you get there. Zombies in the room you're climbing into stay visible through the whole climb, anywhere in that room. To be clear: no wallhack. Your character's line of sight still decides everything, the mod only draws what the game already counts as seen but keeps hidden. Every feature has its own toggle under Options → Mods → Peek a View, and F8 switches the whole mod on and off in game (rebindable). About the vanilla tree fade: build 42.20 added one, and it's decent. Mine replaces it with whole-tree fading around your character that opens into your view direction while you aim, knows how big each tree actually is, and comes without the dithered circle around your character. If you'd rather keep the vanilla version, untick "Active on foot" and PeekAView will only fade trees while you drive. Requirements PZ Build 42.20 or later ZombieBuddy, one-time install for any Java mod Compatibility Safe to add or remove mid-save, the mod stores nothing in the save. Runs alongside the Staircast Workshop mod: PeekAView detects it and yields its own stair view. Works well with Wind Sway, my foliage sway mod. Multiplayer / dedicated servers PeekAView is client-side: the server runs none of its code, each player only sees the effect on their own screen. Two things still have to be in place: On the server: both mods go into the server's .ini, so joining clients download and enable them (keep your other entries, separate with semicolons; 3619862853 = ZombieBuddy, 3710281407 = Peek a View): Mods=ZombieBuddy;PeekAView WorkshopItems=3619862853;3710281407 On every player's PC: ZombieBuddy's one-time setup (its installer puts the Java agent into the game folder). The server can't do that part for you. Without it, Options → Mods → Peek a View shows a warning that the Java component is not loaded, and nothing fades. The first time PeekAView loads on a PC, ZombieBuddy asks for approval of the mod's JAR, tick Allow. FAQ What does "Fix B42 Wall-Hiding Bug" do? Vanilla B42 can hide upper-floor walls next to player-built structures, leaving wall holes from certain angles. The toggle (off by default) suppresses that. Trade-off: player-built decks attached to vanilla walls render more visibly at the facade, so enable it only if you actually see the holes. Added it to an existing save and nothing changed? Subscribing doesn't switch a mod on in saves that already exist. Load Game → select the save → "Choose Mods..." → tick ZombieBuddy and Peek a View. I declined PeekAView in the ZombieBuddy prompt. Can I undo it? Edit %USERPROFILE%\.zombie_buddy\mod_approvals.json: in the "id": "PeekAView" block, flip "decision": false to true (or delete the block to be re-asked). Restart PZ. Maintenance & Source This is the mod in its finished shape. I play with it myself, so breakage from game updates gets fixed when I run into it, but no new features are planned. Last tested against PZ build 42.20.2. MIT-licensed, fully open source: github.com/armakupub/PeekAView. Forks welcome. Attribution Cutaway-on-stairs idea + FakeFrameState pattern + choice of patched render classes: copiumsawsed/pz-Staircast (MIT, original Workshop mod). Read-path implementation fork: armakupub/staircast-rp (MIT). PeekAView extensions on that foundation: upper-floor zombies reveal during the climb, limited to your character's forward view and the room you're climbing into. description: Backpack Barnyard Let’s be honest for a second. You ever look at a full-grown cow and think: “Yeah… I’m putting that in my backpack.” No? …well now you can. This mod lets you pick up animals and store them in your inventory, backpacks, fanny packs — pretty much wherever you want in single player. Pigs, sheep, cows… if it exists, it’s going in the bag. And yes… they only weigh 0.01. Because honestly, driving miles moving animals one at a time got old real fast. Now you can just carry your entire farm with you. How To Use — Single Player After a LOT of trial and error, this is the most stable way to use it: To pick up an animal, right-click slightly UNDER the animal Do NOT click directly on it because that opens the vanilla menu You’ll see: Pick Up Animal Your hands must be empty Once it’s in your inventory, right-click the animal item Choose Move Animal To Select where you want to move it: Main Inventory Backpack Fanny Pack Other worn containers If the animal is already inside a backpack, fanny pack, or another container, right-click the animal and choose: Move Animal To Main Inventory This lets you move animals back and forth without needing to click and drag. Putting Animals Down — Single Player The custom “Place Animal Down” option has been removed because it caused instability and bugs. To drop an animal, click and drag the animal from your inventory onto the ground or use the normal drop option This is currently the only reliable method Multiplayer — IMPORTANT Multiplayer finally works, but it works differently from single player. To pick up animals in multiplayer, use MP Pick Up Nearby Animals (#) The number shows how many animals are nearby Do not use the regular Pick Up Animal option in multiplayer After the animal is in your inventory, right-click it and use Move Animal To You can transfer animals between your main inventory, backpack, fanny pack, and worn containers using the right-click menu Important: Drag-and-drop can be unreliable in multiplayer, so use the right-click transfer options instead. How To Transfer Animals Between Inventories Once an animal is in your inventory: Right-click the animal item Choose Move Animal To Select the inventory you want: Main Inventory Backpack Fanny Pack Other worn containers If the animal is inside a backpack or fanny pack and you want it back in your regular inventory: Right-click the animal item Choose Move Animal To Main Inventory This was added because click-and-drag can be annoying or unreliable, especially in multiplayer. Compatibility Build 42.20+ Single player supports inventory, backpacks, fanny packs, and containers Multiplayer supports pickup using MP Pick Up Nearby Animals (#) Right-click animal transfer works for moving animals between inventories Trailer capacity works in multiplayer Credits This mod is inspired by the original work from Swamp Fox. All credit goes to them for the original idea. Final Notes I’m a mom to a two-year-old, I work full-time, I run a household, and I have a life that exists well beyond this game. So updates won’t always be instant—I fit this in when I can, and I appreciate your patience. And about the images: yes, I use AI to make them. I don’t draw, I’m not paying someone to create art for a hobby project, and I’ve got far bigger things to deal with than pixel-perfect illustrations. I like the images I generate—they bring my OC to life in a way that makes me happy. That’s the point. So if you’re here to drop “AI slop” comments, save it. I don’t care. Move on. I’m here to have fun, share something I love, and build a little community around it. If that’s not your vibe, the door’s right there. ✌️ — Yumi <3 Check Out My Other Mods! Feel free to check out my other Project Zomboid mods! description: EBF Chainsaw Standalone Chainsaw System for Project Zomboid Build 42.20 This mod adds a standalone and fully functional chainsaw system for Project Zomboid Build 42.20. The chainsaw can be equipped, started, turned off, refueled, emptied, used as a weapon, and used to cut trees. It has its own fuel system, chain condition system, radial menu support, context menu actions, custom icons, sounds, animations, and multiplayer-focused behavior. MAIN FEATURES Standalone chainsaw item. Actions to start and turn off the chainsaw. Fuel system with gasoline capacity. Add gasoline using a fuel can. Remove gasoline from the chainsaw. Chain system with install and remove actions. Chain wear when cutting trees and attacking zombies. Broken chains can fall off during use. The chainsaw can still be started without a chain, but it cannot cut properly or deal full damage. Custom radial menu using the V key while holding the chainsaw. Context menu actions with proper icons. Multiplayer-compatible client-side processing. Compatible with saves using Authentic Z, while keeping the EBF chainsaw mechanics independent. CRAFTING The mod includes a manual that teaches the chainsaw recipes: Start Chainsaw Turn Off Chainsaw Remove Chainsaw Chain Install Chainsaw Chain Create Chainsaw Chain Create Heavy Chain Link You can craft chainsaw chains using metalworking tools and materials. Chainsaw chain crafting uses welding animations, welding sound, and requires a valid crafting surface. GAMEPLAY NOTES The chainsaw uses gasoline and chain durability separately. Fuel is consumed during use. The chain wears down when cutting trees or hitting zombies. If the chain breaks, it will be automatically removed from the chainsaw. The chainsaw makes noise while turned on. The chainsaw becomes even louder when cutting trees. CHAIN SYSTEM The chainsaw chain is an important part of the system. Without a chain: The chainsaw can still be started. It cannot cut trees properly. It does not deal full damage. With a chain installed: The chainsaw can cut trees. It can be used more effectively as a weapon. The chain loses condition during use. A damaged chain can break and fall off. COMPATIBILITY Designed for Project Zomboid Build 42.20. Standalone mod. Does not require Authentic Z. Does not require any other chainsaw mod. Designed to work safely alongside Authentic Z. This allows players to use the EBF chainsaw mechanics without depending on other mods. AUTHENTIC Z COMPATIBILITY NOTICE This mod includes compatibility support designed to work alongside Authentic Z variations, while keeping the EBF chainsaw system independent. Important: EBF Chainsaw does not depend on Authentic Z to work. Compatibility only exists so that players using Authentic Z can also safely use the EBF chainsaw mechanics. MULTIPLAYER SUPPORT This mod was designed with multiplayer compatibility in mind. Chainsaw actions, the fuel system, chain system, sounds, and animations were created to work safely in multiplayer environments. IMPORTANT NOTE This is a standalone EBF chainsaw system. It does not replace the mechanics of other chainsaw mods. It adds its own chainsaw logic, recipes, sounds, animations, and gameplay behavior. description: KR CoreOS The shared foundation of every KR mod — and a distribution API open to any modder. KR CoreOS is a backend library. It adds no items or gameplay mechanics on its own — it provides the shared infrastructure that powers loot distribution, vehicle spawning and cross-mod extensibility for the whole KR ecosystem. Install it alongside any mod that requires it. No configuration needed. ⚙️ What It Provides Item Distribution API — Register items into world loot using 140 thematic groups that cover every one of the 1418 B42.20 loot containers (military, firearms, medical, electronics, food, clothing, tools, books, warehouse crates and more), each container in exactly one group. One function call — KRCore does the rest. Distribution Combos — Ready-made combined groups. The old coarse names (ELECTRONIC, MEDICAL, CRATES...) still work as combos, plus cross-cutting concepts: WAREHOUSE (every crate), POWER (power + batteries), FOOD (food + cold storage), COLD_STORAGE (fridges + freezers), COOKING (kitchens + stoves), WARZONE (guns + ammo), TACTICAL, LAW and WORKSHOP. Vehicle Distribution API — Register custom vehicles into the world spawn zones (parking lots, traffic jams, junkyards...). Care Package Protocol — A lightweight extensibility system that lets future mods register themselves and receive additional content without modifying each other's code. 🛠️ For Modders — Why use CoreOS instead of writing your own distribution Hand-writing distribution means touching ProceduralDistributions directly: hunting container names one by one across 1400+ entries, repeating the same block for every item, maintaining two versions of the code if you support both B41 and B42, and praying no other mod stomps on your table. CoreOS removes all of that. Registering an item looks like this: KRCore.dist.add("Base.MyItem", { TACTICAL = 0.20, -- military + survival (combo) ELECTRONIC = 0.10, -- electronics stores }) What CoreOS handles for you: Complete, verified coverage — 140 thematic groups map every loot container in the game (all 1418, re-verified against B42.20), each in exactly one group with no overlap. You don't need to know a single container name. One codebase for B41 and B42 — Groups mix container names from both builds; each version uses its own and silently skips the rest. You write the call once. No conflicts between mods — Registrations are queued and flushed together at the right point of the load cycle. Nobody overwrites anybody. No duplicates — If two groups share a container, CoreOS deduplicates automatically. Precise overrides — custom containers take priority over groups: you can pin a special probability on one specific container without giving up the whole group. Future-proof — When the game renames containers, it gets fixed once in CoreOS and every dependent mod is fixed without publishing anything. Full documentation — groups, combos, probability table, basic and advanced examples, and common mistakes — is available in the mod discussion. GitHub Repository KR CoreOS - Shared Library & Modding API 📦 Mods Using It KR FriOS — Portable fridges, freezers, electric stoves, a charger and the refrigerated FriOS StepVan. KR SolarOS — Solar chargers that work as generators: the large one charges car batteries and powers your base; the small one charges regular batteries. Check out my other mods! 🔧 Compatibility Build 41 (41.78.7) ✔ — CoreOS B41 support is here to stay Build 42 (42.20.2) ✔ Singleplayer ✔ Multiplayer ✔ No known mod conflicts 🔭 Future Content KR CoreOS is the foundation of every upcoming KR mod. As new mods release, they will declare KR CoreOS as a dependency and register through its API — no updates to existing mods required. BetterPush — The Domino Effect Fully Compatible with : Buttstroke / Gun Stock Attack [B42] MAJOR FIX : Domino Effect should now only trigger on pushing animations, not on weapon swinging or bumping players Turn your shove into a weapon. One push. A whole line falls. Ever wished your character's raw strength actually mattered when you push zombies? BetterPush adds a satisfying chain-reaction mechanic to the shove action. At high strength levels, shoving a zombie has a chance to trigger a domino effect — the zombie you pushed stumbles into the one behind it, which stumbles into the next, and so on. Each zombie falls one after another with a realistic staggered delay, just like real dominoes toppling in a line. Features Dynamic Strength Scaling — As your character gets stronger, you become deadlier. Both the chance to trigger a domino push AND the maximum number of zombies you can knock down dynamically increase as you level up your Strength! Domino Chain Reaction — When triggered, zombies behind your target fall one by one in the direction you pushed. The chain only continues through zombies that are physically close to each other — if there's a gap, the chain breaks. Chance-Based — It's a reward, not a guarantee. Every trigger feels earned. Staggered Knockdown — Zombies don't all drop at once. Each one falls roughly 0.6 seconds after the previous, creating a smooth, cinematic cascade effect. Singleplayer & Multiplayer — Fully compatible with both. In multiplayer, knockdowns are synchronized through the server so all players see the effect. Fully Customizable Sandbox Options — Every parameter is adjustable in-game through the Sandbox Settings menu, complete with hover-over descriptions. Sandbox Options BetterPushMinStrengthLevel — The Strength level where the push effect first becomes possible (0–10, default: 5). BetterPushMaxStrengthLevel — The Strength level where you reach your absolute maximum push potential (0–10, default: 10). BetterPushMinChance — The base chance to trigger a domino push when at minimum strength (0–100%, default: 5%). BetterPushMaxChance — The maximum chance to trigger a domino push when at max strength (0–100%, default: 30%). BetterPushMinZombies — The base maximum number of zombies knocked down in a chain when at minimum strength (1–20, default: 1). BetterPushMaxZombies — The absolute maximum number of zombies knocked down in a chain when at max strength (1–20, default: 4). BetterPushLineDistance — How close zombies must be to each other (front to back) to continue falling in the chain (0.6–5.0 tiles, default: 0.8). BetterPushLineWidth — How wide the lateral tolerance is when finding the next zombie in the chain (0.6–5.0 tiles, default: 0.8). How It Works You shove a zombie (Spacebar). The mod checks your Strength. If you meet the minimum level, it rolls a chance to trigger based on how strong you are. If successful, it calculates how many zombies you can push down (which also scales with Strength) and traces a line from you. It looks for the closest zombie behind the target — they must be nearly touching. That zombie falls. Then the next. Then the next. Each one drops with a slight delay, creating the domino cascade. Compatibility Build 42.17 Unstable Singleplayer ✔ Multiplayer ✔ Should be compatible with most other mods — BetterPush only safely hooks into the OnWeaponHitCharacter event and does not override any vanilla files. Tips Works best against tightly packed hordes — the zombies need to be shoulder-to-shoulder for the chain to connect. Pairs well with traits and mods that boost Strength. One push. Watch them fall. If you would like to support me, I would appreciate it :) <3 Workshop ID: 3715137752 Mod ID: BetterPush

description: Dynamic Horde Events Once the streets around a base are cleared, Project Zomboid can become very quiet. Dynamic Horde Events adds occasional horde encounters to bring some danger back to long-running worlds. Hordes can approach from outside the immediate area, pass close to your base, or actively hunt a chosen player. They do not run constantly, and every event type has its own sandbox settings. Horde types Normal Horde A group spawns outside the player's immediate area and is attracted toward the player's location by an event sound. Normal hordes can also use optional direct pursuit. With this enabled, only zombies created for that event keep tracking the selected player for about one in-game hour. Existing zombies in the world are not added to the pursuit group. Wandering Horde A wandering horde travels across the area instead of attacking the player directly. It spawns on one side of the player and moves toward a point beyond them: Spawn point -> Player area -> Exit point Stay quiet and it may pass without becoming your problem. Gunshots, vehicles, alarms, and other loud noises can still pull the horde off its route. Cataclysm Horde A rare event intended for long-running worlds. Cataclysm hordes are much larger and can be configured to pursue their selected player directly for a limited number of in-game hours. If the player gets far enough away, the mod can spawn a limited catch-up group near the player. The original zombies are not deleted from the world, and catch-up stops when the pursuit event ends. Cataclysm events can also trigger temporary storm, rain, wind, fog, cloud, and desaturation effects. Every part of the weather effect can be adjusted or disabled. Scheduling Each horde type has its own schedule and can be disabled separately. Random interval: the next event is rolled between the configured minimum and maximum time. Fixed days and hour: run an event at a predictable interval, such as every day at 22:00 or every seven days at 18:00. Warnings and indicator When an event starts, the mod can show a movable direction indicator with: event type direction distance approximate zombie count Warning sounds, the direction indicator, survivor voice lines, and the Cataclysm screen effect can be disabled. The master notification option turns all player-facing warnings off while leaving the event itself active. Multiplayer Horde events use a shared world schedule. When an event begins, one active player is selected as its target. The optional MP spawn clamp keeps new hordes inside the active server area. For example, if a horde is configured to spawn 80-100 tiles away while the clamp is set to 70, the multiplayer spawn distance is capped at approximately 70 tiles. Sandbox settings You can configure: event schedules and fixed event day/hours (7 Days To Die Mode) horde sizes and spawn distances normal horde scaling over survived days or months direct pursuit and path assistance wandering route distance and spread Cataclysm pursuit duration and weather warning sounds, speech, indicator duration, and notifications indoor and multiplayer spawn restrictions Water tiles and active safehouses are avoided automatically when the mod searches for a spawn point. Normal Horde Pursuit Disabled by default. When enabled, the spawned normal horde keeps receiving the selected player's current position instead of relying only on the initial attraction sound. Path assistance can help with buildings, upper floors, and obstacles, although zombie pathfinding is still controlled by the game. Performance Very large hordes can be demanding, especially on multiplayer servers or in dense map areas. If performance drops, reduce the maximum horde size, Cataclysm size, attraction radius, or event frequency. Build and compatibility ✅Project Zomboid Build 42.20 Should work with most maps, zombie variants, and gameplay mods. Mods that heavily replace zombie spawning, networking, or AI may affect horde behavior (Tested with Wandering Zombies and it works ok tho zombies may change course if they spawn too far away). It can be added to an existing save. New event timers are created the first time that world is loaded with the mod enabled. Recommended mods CDDA Zombies adds more zombie variety to the hordes. Cheval de Frise adds more options for defending a base against them. My Other Mods: Project Parkour Extensive Health Rework Evolved Survival Planner List (TO DO List) Cut That Tree! (Tree Chopping Minigame) One Clean Jaw Stab Workshop ID: 3716405632 Mod ID: DynamicHordeEventsB42

Project Zomboid Needs More Bugs Spawn real-time rendered bugs around outdoor lights Bugs are active in the summer months Bugs are most active when it's warm and not raining Bugs are attracted to active light sources Mod Options control the number and size of bugs Mod Option to toggle if bugs are active all year Mod Option to turn off temperature and rain limited spawn rates Mod Option so bugs can spawn both day and night Includes an "addBug™ function" to add your own bugs Safe to add at any time or remove, but why? For B42 SP & MP Check out JB's Fireflies for even more bugs! Adding your own bugs model: This is the name of the 3D item model used for the bug, like "Base.Plushabug" size: This determines the scale of the 3D item. 1.0 represents the full size of the item, a good range would be 0.05 to 0.8 for bugs speed: This sets the base velocity applied to the bug during movement. A good range is 0.0001 to 0.01, since higher values can cause the bug to move too fast to see yawOffset: This is a degree adjustment used to ensure the "front" of your 3D model faces the actual direction of travel. The range is 0 to 360, and typical values are 0, 90 or 180 depending on how the model was exported crazyFactor: This controls the amount of random "jitter" or "crazy"" added to the bug's velocity every frame. A good range is 0.00001 to 0.02; higher values create frantic, crack-head movement, while lower values looks like a steady drift lightAttraction: This is how strongly the bug is "pulled" toward the light source. A range of 0.001 to 0.5 is good. Higher values make the bugs stick too close to the light source areaOfInterest: This is the radius in squares/tiles around the light source where the bug will spend its life. A good range is 0.1 to 1.5 minFrames and maxFrames: This defines the lifespan of a single bug instance in update ticks before it despawns. A suitable range is 30 to 600, which is roughly 1 to 10 seconds of activity at 60 FPS Example mod put in lua/client: local BugPattern = require("jb_BugPatterns") local bug = { model = "Base.Plushabug", size = 0.06, speed = 0.001, yawOffset = 90, crazyFactor = 0.01, lightAttraction = 0.001, areaOfInterest = 0.5, minFrames = 180, maxFrames = 600, } BugPattern.addBug(bug) Workshop ID: 3717902500 Mod ID: JB_BugsInLights

description: Common Sense - Community Compatibility Fix Current version: Project Zomboid Build 42.20 Mod ID: BB_CommonSenseFix Single Player and Multiplayer About This Version This mod is based on the original Common Sense mod, created by Braven. This release is not intended to steal the original work, credits, or authorship. It is a community compatibility and maintenance version created so players can continue enjoying this excellent mod on newer Project Zomboid builds. The original concept, foundation, and all corresponding credits belong to Braven. If the original author would like this version to be changed or removed from the Workshop, please contact me through the comments or by direct message. What Does the Mod Do? Common Sense adds several quality-of-life improvements and interactions that feel natural within Project Zomboid. Its purpose is to enable small, logical actions that the game normally does not provide, without completely changing the gameplay experience. Main Features Prying with a crowbar: force open building doors, garage doors, reinforced doors, windows, and vehicle doors. Configurable difficulty: adjust the success chance, minimum Strength required for reinforced doors, and the possibility of breaking glass after a failed attempt. Weapon interface: displays useful information about the equipped weapon, including ammunition, status, and condition. Equip directly from the ground: equip weapons, clothing, and backpacks through the context menu without transferring them manually first. Belt flashlights: attach compatible handheld flashlights to the tool slot while respecting known mods that alter attachment points. Color filter: provides a more accessible interface option for color-blind players. The obsolete Build 41 manual collecting action was removed from this B42.20 version. Ground items must be collected through the native Project Zomboid interaction. Recipes and Utilities Open canned food using knives, screwdrivers, forks, and spoons as improvised tools. Configure the chance and severity of injuries caused by opening cans without a proper can opener. Disinfect dirty bandages and ripped sheets using alcohol. Create sheets from compatible clothing and materials. Craft engine parts with the appropriate materials and skills. Combine damaged pairs of gloves to recover one usable item. Repair additional items, including nightsticks and plungers. Pour the contents of compatible containers and cans onto the ground. Experimental Feature: Remove a Bullet by Hand This version includes an experimental mechanic for manually removing a lodged bullet through the Health panel. The mechanic is completely disabled by default. The action can be enabled separately through Sandbox settings. When completed, the removed bullet is returned to the inventory and marked as bloody. Removing the bullet increases pain, bleeding, and wound severity. The character must remain still while performing the action. The custom BulletOut animation option is retained for settings compatibility but is unavailable on Build 42.20.2. Current status: the action logic is available for testing without a custom animation. The BulletOut asset was removed from the active package because Build 42.20.2 includes it in the multiplayer animation checksum even while the Sandbox option is disabled, which could prevent the mod or server from loading. Sandbox Options Administrators can configure: The general prying mechanic. Building doors, garage doors, reinforced doors, windows, and vehicles separately. Minimum Strength required for reinforced doors. Difficulty of prying attempts. Chance of breaking glass. Weapon statistics interface. Color filter. Chance and severity of injuries caused by opening cans. The action to remove a bullet by hand. A reserved compatibility option for the currently unavailable bullet-removal animation. Installation and Compatibility Made for the stable Build 42.20. Works in Single Player and Multiplayer. This version is standalone: the original Common Sense mod is not required. Do not enable this version and the original Common Sense mod at the same time. On a dedicated server, add BB_CommonSenseFix to the Mods list. All players must use the same version installed on the server. Credits Original mod and creator: Braven / BitBraven. Original mod: Common Sense. Build 42.20 compatibility, fixes, and community maintenance: Malaio. This version exists to keep the mod accessible to the community throughout the API and structural changes introduced in Build 42. No credit for the original work is being claimed. Support and Bug Reports When reporting a problem, please mention whether it occurred in Single Player or Multiplayer, which action was used, the active Sandbox settings, and the relevant section of the console log. Workshop ID: 3717968421 Mod ID: BB_CommonSenseFix
