description: OVERVIEW Anomalies is a HARDCORE mod that introduces randomly generated anomalous events, bringing entirely new challenges to your exploration in Knox Country. MULTIPLAYER SUPPORT Thanks to the awesome community member Ricky, there is now an official standalone Multiplayer Compatibility Patch available! If you are playing on a server, make sure to subscribe to it: >> DOWNLOAD THE MULTIPLAYER PATCH HERE << EMISSIONS A devastating anomalous event that alters the atmosphere! When the sky takes on a reddish overlay, an Emission is imminent. You have exactly 1 minute to find a secure indoor shelter and hide. Your Anomaly Radar is crucial. It provides continuous warnings (12h, 6h, 3h, 2h, 1h, and 1 min before it starts) and notifies you when it is safe to go out. Beware: During an active Emission, your radar will suffer heavy interference. Disabled by default (activate via Sandbox Options). RADIOACTIVE ANOMALOUS ZONES Toxic: A deadly radioactive zone. Wear your gas mask and monitor filters. Frost: A freezing microclimate. Bundle up, wear a gas mask, and check filters. Thermal: Extreme heat where objects and zombies engulf in flames. Wear light clothing and a gas mask. These zones dissipate as you move away. A safe place might become radioactive later, and vice-versa. Encountering all 3 at once is possible. Good luck! GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALIES Step too close, and you are violently thrown to the ground! The anomaly itself deals no direct damage to the player, but the fall might break your Anomaly Radar. Driving through one will short-circuit your engine. Mutated Threat: Zombies walking over a gravitational anomaly receive a temporary buff, turning into a Sprinter for 30 seconds! Sandbox Options: You can disable the random spawning of standalone gravitational anomalies (they will still naturally spawn inside radioactive zones). The mechanic that buffs zombies into sprinters is a separate option (disabled by default). If this buff is disabled, gravitational anomalies will have absolutely zero effect on zombies. ANOMALOUS MUTANTS Toxic Walkers: The most common mutation. These zombies exude radiation. Use a gas mask with filters for close-quarters combat, or eliminate them from a distance. Squealer: Essentially a Sprinter, but with a unique, terrifying look and custom sound effects. Volatiles: DO NOT GET CLOSE. If they feel threatened by your proximity, they will explode. The explosion deals damage and has a 1% chance to severely injure you. Avoid combat or take them out from afar. Shooting them has a chance to hit their attached gas tanks, triggering a massive explosion that draws attention within a 50-tile radius. Being inside a car reduces the damage taken, but the shockwave might stall your engine. Shadows: Creatures born from the night that lurk in dark spots. They are immune to physical damage, so save your ammo. Do not let them get close, or you will be dragged into the darkness. Run toward the light or shine your flashlight directly at them to purify them. Watcher (Optional Sandbox): Weighed down by heavy frequency antennas on its back, this crawler is harmless on its own. However, if it spots you, it will emit a frequency that alerts all nearby zombies to your exact location! You will know you've been seen by an eye icon on your screen or by the static interference on your Anomaly Radar. Kill it quickly or run away to break its line of sight. Gravitational Mutant (Sandbox): Surrounded by anomalies. In combat, it spawns gravitational anomalies directly on top of you (watch for the red visual alert!). Its anomalies will also buff regular zombies into sprinters for 30s. Killing this mutant will immediately clear all active gravitational anomalies from the world. Disabled by default. Flaming Bull (Optional Sandbox): A mutant bull altered by extreme exposure to Thermal Anomalous Zones. It has a highly unstable temperament and will prepare a devastating charge if you get too close. A direct hit deals damage and has a chance to cause lacerations. It uses hit-and-run tactics, keeping its distance between strikes. At 20% health, it enters a fury state, leaving a trail of fire to block your pursuit while it attempts to escape and heal. A thick anomalous fog makes it immune to firearms—you must face it in melee combat! Butchering its corpse yields no meat, but you can recover the weapons of past victims embedded in its thick hide. *Disclaimer: Because it relies on the game's base animal system, its animations may occasionally glitch, causing it to run sideways during a charge.* SURVIVAL GEAR Wipe out hordes in radioactive fog to scavenge the Aurorabh and PA10 gas masks. AntiRad: Removes -40 radiation. If in an anomalous zone, it must be used while wearing a gas mask with active filters, otherwise it fails. Protection Artifacts: Secure your base by preventing anomalous zones. Place it on the ground and right-click its base (where it touches the ground) to bring up the 'Activate Protection Artifact' option. Max 5 active artifacts. Use a Stabilizer to boost or stabilize them. Anomaly Radar Find or craft one to hear when you are near radioactive zones or measure distance from anomalies. NEW FEATURES: Mini UI Radar: A resizable interface (use mouse scroll). It tracks nearby mutations: Red (Volatile), Cyan (Watcher), Green (Toxic Walker), Orange (Squealer), Purple (Gravitational Mutant), Black w/ White Outline (Shadow), Brown (Flaming Bull), and Yellow (Gravitational Anomaly). Map Integration: Press 'M' with a radar equipped to see active Gravitational Anomalies and Radioactive Zones on your world map. MID-SAVE COMPATIBILITY Safe to add mid-save, but a zone might spawn inside your base! To be safe, backup your save, enter debug mode, spawn and activate a Greater Stable Protection Artifact in your home. PERMISSIONS & DEVELOPMENT Modifying & Publishing: You are free to modify this mod for personal use or publish a tweaked version. All I ask is that you give proper credit to the original author and include a direct link back to this Anomalies mod page. Multiplayer Collaboration: The base mod remains singleplayer-focused since I lack MP network sync experience. Ricky developed and maintains the official standalone MP patch. If you wish to help integrate MP fixes directly into the core files, feel free to reach out to me! description: The Director [B42.18 MP and SP] "It's not just spawning zombies. It's deciding what to do about you." A cognitive AI for Project Zomboid. Server-side overseer that watches every move you make, builds a Bayesian model of who you are as a player, and writes a different scenario for every survivor it meets. Inspired by Left 4 Dead's AI Director, but pushed several decades forward in capability. What it actually does Every cycle, an 18-module cognitive pipeline runs end to end: Perceive - events tagged with semantic context (loud, aggressive, vulnerable, at_night, in_storm_phase) Remember - short-term episodic memory consolidates into long-term narrative beats (firefight, hubris, near-death recovery, betrayal) Model you - Bayesian Beta distributions track paranoid, confident, methodical, aggressive, hoarder, explorer, expert beliefs that tighten as evidence accumulates Predict you - a Theory-of-Mind layer models what you think the Director will do next, so it can subvert your expectations Deliberate - generates 5-10 candidate plans, simulates your likely response via Monte Carlo rollout, scores them on 7 competing objectives Learn - a UCB1 multi-armed bandit Q-table records what works on you specifically across 420 state buckets; persists across save/load Reflect - every 30 in-game minutes, the Director self-critiques and adjusts strategy Narrate - procedural taunts reference your actual history ("You came back to that street. Brave. Or stupid.") Action vocabulary The Director picks from 12 tactical levers each cycle, weighted by a learned-reward bandit: spawn_horde - walker / fast_shambler / fake_shambler / sprinter / crawler / mixed. The two new tiers landed in v1.2.0 via B42.18's per-zombie speed API. Tier is gated by belief: fake shamblers (look slow, then run when you commit) are reserved for players who actually scout before engaging - a charger would read them the same as walkers, so the trick has no audience. Fast shamblers fill the buildup band; sprinters are saved for the climax. lure_existing / redirect_zombies - pulls or nudges nearby zombies via a world-sound source siege_phase - sustained multi-cycle pressure at intensity 1-5 ambient_sound / phantom_gunshot / broadcast_static - atmospheric cues that don't spawn anything but make you check the corners meta_event_nudge - bumps a Knox Event helicopter (or similar) at a thematically-fitting moment weather_nudge - pushes weather toward whatever the persona prefers taunt - procedural chat referencing your actual profile and history wait - enforced relax windows (the same trick L4D uses) cull_distant - removes off-screen zombies to make room for fresh pressure Personas Pick the Director's voice in sandbox options: Patient - long lulls, rare big strikes Sadistic - targets your weakest moments (low HP, sleeping, low ammo) Tactical - methodical, consistent pressure Narrator - heavy taunting, theatrical pacing Cross-mod awareness The Director auto-detects every active mod on the server and adapts. Hand-written adapters ship for Warlord, Calm Before The Storm, Here They Come!, Bandits NPC, Helicopter Event Framework, and Hordes Alpha. Mods we've never heard of get conservative defaults via name-keyword detection. Other mod authors can ship their own adapter without forking The Director - drop a ZT_Adapter_YourName.lua file in the Adapters folder and it auto-loads. See the Discussions tab for the adapter protocol. Persistent across sessions Every belief, every Q-value, every narrative beat, every persona drift is saved. Load your save a week later and the Director continues the campaign it was running. Tactician Notes Right-click in the world, "Zombie Tactician", "Open Tactician Notes" for a live, color-coded panel showing the Director thinking in real time. Watch each cycle's perception, beliefs, projected outcomes, decision rationale, and self-reflection scroll by like an LLM monologue. Other admin tools in the same menu: Dump Brain State, Force Cycle Now, Reset Learned Data. Compatibility Build 42.18 unstable Singleplayer and dedicated MP (per-player belief tracking) Pure Lua. No external services, no API keys, no network calls Save-safe: persistence migrates between schema versions automatically A note on what this is This mod is the result of building, from scratch in Lua, what an LLM would have done if Project Zomboid's kahlua sandbox allowed network access. It mimics LLM-style cognition (multi-step reasoning, persistent beliefs, theory-of-mind, reflection) without being one. Every implicit LLM capability is an explicit module. It is also early. Beliefs may drift in unexpected ways. Personas may need tuning. The Tactician Notes panel is your friend - open it, watch the brain reason, and report what feels off. Credits Architecture inspired by Mike Booth (L4D AI Director), Dave Mark (Behavioral Mathematics for Game AI), Jeff Orkin (F.E.A.R. GOAP) Step right up. Support If my mods saved your save (or your sanity), a coffee keeps the late-night debugging going. Every tip funds more time spent reverse-engineering kahlua quirks so you don't have to. Buy me a coffee on Ko-fi: https://ko-fi.com/grphx Workshop ID: 3720305815 Mod ID: ZombieTactician

description: Please read the description before leaving a comment. This mod adds friendly survivors. There are no hostile survivors. Build a base, gather companions, and create a small community. This is not a detailed life simulation mod for living together with NPCs. It is a compact and intuitive player-support mod designed to make lonely survival a little easier with the help of NPCs. You cannot give NPCs detailed commands, and they do not need food. The available commands are limited to having them defend the base, follow the player and assist in combat, and exchange items. However, each NPC occupation has its own traits. Depending on their occupation, NPCs can support you with things such as vehicle maintenance, farming, water collection, healing, and item gathering. ───── How to Play ───── 1. Set a Base Set a safe location as your Base from the right-click menu. You cannot recruit NPCs until a base has been set. 2. Find and Recruit Survivors NPCs wander around the world. After setting a base, you can recruit them from the right-click menu. Recruited NPCs can either follow you or wait at the base. Following NPCs stay near the player and try to fight nearby enemies. You can also encounter NPCs by consuming a walkie-talkie. 3. Custom NPC You can create one Custom NPC. After setting a base, you can create them from the right-click menu while you are inside the base. 4. Shared Storage Shared Storage is a withdrawal-only container used to receive items collected by NPCs. It can only be opened from the right-click menu while the player is inside the base. NPCs stationed at the base have a low chance to collect items. The collection interval and amount can be adjusted in the sandbox settings. In addition, some occupations may bring back extra items through their base traits, separate from normal collection. 5. NPC Management Tag The NPC Management Tag stored in your key ring is an item that contains NPC records. It is used to restore companions’ names, status, equipment, and inventory. There is an automatic recovery system in case it is lost, but please be careful with it. 6. Base Support Abilities Some occupations have base support abilities such as healing, vehicle maintenance, generator maintenance, crop watering, and item generation. These abilities generally only work while the player is inside the same base. Game balance can be adjusted in the sandbox settings. 7. Guard Patrol System If you set guard points and assign NPCs to guard duty, they will move to the guard points. If there are empty guard points, they will patrol between them. ───── Occupation Abilities ───── Each NPC occupation has different combat traits, follow abilities, and base support abilities. Some abilities work while the NPC is following you, while others work when the NPC is stationed at your base. Fire Officer ・Combat: axe attacks always knock down zombies. ・At base: refills rain barrels. Police Officer ・Combat: firearms may knock down zombies. ・At base: rarely collects ammunition. Park Ranger ・Combat: firearm range +10%. ・Following: improves nearby foraging support. Construction Worker ・Following: increases the player’s carry capacity. Security Guard ・At base: melee damage x1.5. ・At base: improves firearm damage and accuracy. Carpenter ・At base: has a chance to add nails. Burglar ・Following: can help unlock doors and vehicle doors. Chef ・At base: has a chance to add cooked meals. Repairman ・At base: repairs doors, windows, and barricades. Livestock Farmer ・At base: waters crops. ・At base: has a chance to add meat. Crop Farmer ・At base: waters crops. ・At base: has a chance to add vegetables or fruit. Fisherman ・At base: has a chance to add fish. Doctor ・Combat: blade damage x1.5. ・At base: heals the player and NPCs inside the base. Veteran ・Combat: improves firearm damage and accuracy. ・At base: rarely collects ammunition. Nurse ・At base: improves healing if a doctor is at the base. Lumberjack ・Combat: axe damage x1.5. ・At base: has a chance to add planks. Fitness Instructor ・Combat: sports weapon damage x1.5. ・Following: increases the player’s carry capacity. Burger Flipper ・At base: has a chance to add a fast food set. Electrician ・At base: repairs and refuels generators. Engineer ・At base: repairs and refuels generators. Metalworker ・At base: has a chance to add metal materials. Blacksmith ・At base: has a chance to add a katana. Mechanic ・At base: repairs vehicle parts. ・At base: has a chance to add spare vehicle parts. Tailor ・At base: has a chance to add thread or ripped sheets. ───── Player Death ───── By default, even if the player dies, NPCs stationed at the base and the contents of Shared Storage will be preserved. Contaminated fermentation produces: Distilled Liquor Distilled Liquor can still be consumed or used later to produce Ethanol. 3. Distillation Stage Fermented liquids must be transferred into the Still. Biofuel Refining Ethanol can be stored inside industrial tanks to begin the refining process. Attachments are limited to weapons that realistically support them, and every firearm was balanced around believable handling and performance rather than arcade gameplay. description: 2026.08.18 v1.9 Ōdachi now has its own Saya (scabbard) — 15 authentic lacquered variants plus a plain wood/replica version, worn on the back Tantō now has its own Saya as well — a plain wood/replica version, worn on the hip on the opposite side from the Katana/Wakizashi daishō so it doesn't visually clash New recipes: craft, lacquer and stain the Ōdachi Saya; craft the Replica Tantō Saya Translation fixes and additions across all supported languages (CN, DE, ES, JP, PL, PTBR, RU) 2026.07.29 v1.7 Replica scabbards and Saya can now be carried on the back The Motivation behind NIHONTŌ I created this mod to address several issues with the vanilla Katana and the Long Blade skill: Rarity: The vanilla Katana is a unicorn on default settings. It is entirely possible to loot the entire map and never find a single one. Condition: Even if you are lucky enough to find one, it has the longevity of a glass ornament. It will break when a zombie looks at it the wrong way. Repair: In the vanilla game, you cannot sharpen them. Crafting: Vanilla blade crafting feels more like a chore than progression. Welding together scrap swords that break almost instantly or progressing to a master-level blacksmith only to craft slightly better swords didn't feel right. Lack of Variety: Progression & Gameplay What started as a personal fix evolved into a passion project. While the default settings reflect my own preferences, I have added Sandbox Options to accommodate different playstyles, with more configuration options coming in the future. In the current version, you can hunt for high-end Katanas for end-game mayhem. However, until you find or forge one, you can hone your skills with lower-tier variants. These are easier to craft, spawn more frequently in low-tier locations, and bridge the gap in your skill progression. Current Weapons & Features A standalone, immersive overhaul for Japanese bladed weapons, specifically designed for Build 42. ⚔️ Weapons Bokutō – Hand-carved wooden training sword. Your starting point. Decorative Katana – Aluminum wall-hanger. Better than nothing. Scrap Katana – Forged from scrap metal. Rough but functional. Replica Katana & Wakizashi – Iron blades, Mall Ninja grade. Found in pawn shops and schools. Nihontō Katana – Authentic steel. The endgame blade. Nihontō Wakizashi – The shorter companion blade. Tantō – A compact dagger for close quarters. Nagamaki – A long-handled blade/spear hybrid for reach and power. Ōdachi – A massive great sword. Slow, devastating. 🗡️ Customization Modular Crafting: Every part – Blade (Tōshin), Guard (Tsuba), Hilt (Tsuka) – is a separate, interchangeable component. Hilt Colors: 9 Tsuka color variants for Katana and Wakizashi. Replica Scabbards: A single dyeable Saya per weapon – color it any way you like. Every weapon in the mod, including the Tantō, has one. Authentic Saya: 15 historically accurate Urushi-lacquered and natural wood Shirasaya variants – now including the Ōdachi. Custom Assets: Hand-crafted icons for every component and color variant. ⚙️ Mechanics Sharpness System: Every time the game attempts to decrease a blade's condition, there is a chance to reduce its sharpness instead. A razor-sharp blade protects itself – a dull blade does not. Keep your blade sharp! Character Feedback: On-screen warnings when sharpness drops below critical thresholds. Skill Scaling: Higher Long Blade and Maintenance skills improve condition protection. Sandbox Options: Tune spawn rates, condition values, sharpness mechanics and more. The sharpness mechanic can also be extended to all bladed weapons. New Literature: The "Nihontō Tanren-ho" crafting book and the "Mall Ninja Monthly" magazine unlock advanced recipes. Full Localization: CN, DE, ES, JP, PL, PTBR and RU. Cultural Appreciation & Authenticity I have always been deeply inspired by Japanese culture and traditional martial arts. My goal with this mod is to pay tribute to the incredible craftsmanship and heritage of the Nihontō. I have put a great deal of effort into researching and using authentic historical nomenclature—from the specific parts of the koshirae to the distinct eras of swordsmithing—out of deep respect for Japanese traditions. While the "Mall Ninja" items in this mod represent a specific Western pop-culture phenomenon, the Nihontō themselves are intended to be as culturally and historically accurate as possible within the limits of the game. Acknowledgments I want to thank Michonne and Akyohunter for inspiring me. Before I created this, I used Michonne's Katana and Akyohunter's Legendary Katanas and Wakizashis extensively. They are great mods, and I highly recommend them if you prefer a simpler way to obtain a Katana or if you aren't interested in my specific sharpness mechanics and obsession with historical accuracy! :D I hope you enjoy the mod. Please feel free to leave comments regarding bugs or suggestions for improvements. Technical Background & Credits Big thanks to Paddlefruit from the official TIS Discord for the awesome Character rig! When I started this project, I had zero experience with 3D modeling, so this mod is based on a 3D model by mSameja. Since then, I have learned a lot and reworked almost every aspect of it, but nonetheless, all credit for the original 3D work goes to the artist mSameja. Original Model: "Katana and Sheath" Author: mSameja License: CC BY 4.0 Developed by Corvus Workshop ID: 3723127305 Mod ID: Nihonto

description: Tired of single-click building? Queue up multiple placements while one is still in progress. Built and statically validated against the local Build 42 Lua source. In-game multiplayer feedback welcome. Workshop ID: 3724301960 Mod ID: BuildingQueue

description: READ BEFORE ANYTHING !! For Any Bug Report For Any Suggestion Before saying "it's not working", unsubscribe, then resubscribe. If it still fails, post your bug on Discord with your console file "C:\Users\you\Zomboid\console.txt" and your mod list "C:\Users\you\Zomboid\mods\default.txt" => Discord : https://discord.gg/vJay7GQ92B ☀️ Plysken Solar Revolution Harness the sun to keep your base running long after the grid goes dark. A complete off-grid solar energy system for Project Zomboid Build 42: solar panels, battery banks, a Solar Computer to manage your devices, and a failsafe backup generator relay. Solo & Multiplayer (Host/Coop and Dedicated Server). 🔋 Getting Started 1. Learn the recipes. Read the magazine New Advancements: Energy From The Sun — found as loot or inside a Solar Box crate. Everything unlocks at once — check your crafting menu. 2. Build the parts. Craft Make Solar Panel (part) first, then Make Flat Solar Panel (or Wall-Mounted / Floor-Mounted), plus Create Battery Bank — the bank also needs an Inverter. 3. Put the Battery Bank indoors. It needs a room with walls AND a roof. Anywhere else the placement cursor stays red and you get Battery Bank must be placed in an enclosed room! — a walled yard with open sky will not do. 4. Put the panels outdoors, with clear sky above them. A wall-mounted panel also needs a wall to hang on. Wrong spot gives Solar panels must be placed outdoors! 5. Wire them together. Right-click the bank, Battery Bank, Connect Panels, then click each panel in turn. It worked when that panel's own right-click menu now reads Disconnect from Battery Bank. 6. Load batteries, then switch on. Open the bank like any container and drop batteries inside, then right-click it, Battery Bank, Turn on. 7. Check it. Right-click the bank, Open Status Window. Working OK with a battery level climbing during the day means you are charging. ⚡ Living Off Solar A running bank powers every vanilla appliance in the whole building — lights, fridges, freezers, TVs — like a generator, without the noise or the fuel. At night or under heavy cloud it drains the stored charge instead. Linking banks. Right-click a bank next to another one, Battery Bank, Link bank — they then share one pool of charge and one set of panels. Backup generator. Place a Failsafe Trigger on top of a vanilla generator that is already plugged in. When the banks run low it starts the generator on its own, and stops it once they recover. One Failsafe is enough for a whole linked network. Extensions you built yourself. Stand inside the extension, right-click the floor, Connect this area to the Power Bank. You will see Area connected to the Power Bank and its appliances start counting toward your draw. Fumes. A battery bank clears toxic fumes from its room only while it is running. A flat bank stops clearing, so a generator left indoors will gas you overnight. Keep real generators outside. 🖥️ Solar Computer Place a vanilla Desktop Computer on a tile right next to a Battery Bank, right-click it, Solar Computer, Connect to Battery Bank. Then simply left-click the computer to open Device Management. description: Computer Mod A Project Zomboid mod that turns useless computers into fully functional machines. B41 HERE! About This Mod Computers in Project Zomboid usually do not do much besides being dismantled. This mod changes that. Computer Mod adds usable computers with their own operating system. You can install an OS, set passwords, browse websites, download and install games, read magazines and newspapers, watch video files, use apps, burn CDs, store files, and communicate with other players. Features Playable Games There are currently 24 playable games. Some computers may already have games installed, while others may have none. Games can be installed in two ways: Game CDs: Find a game CD, insert it into a computer, and install it through My Files. Internet downloads: Open the browser, visit knoxshare.bbs, download a game, then install it from the Downloads folder. Downloads take time. You do not need to stay next to the computer while downloading, but shutting the computer down will cancel the download. Playing games reduces boredom, stress, and sadness. Losing a game slightly increases stress. Applications A fresh OS includes My Files, Notepad, Browser, Paint, Calculator, Mail, Board, Chat, Market, Settings, and Music Player. Mail: Create an account, log in from different computers, send mail, reply, and delete messages. Board: Post public messages that other players with computers can read. Chat: Create an account, send requests, and privately message other players. Market: Create a market account, buy rotating shop items, and complete jobs for money. Shop items and jobs refresh over time and are shared across computers on the server. Paint: Draw simple images and save them as desktop files. Folder, File and CD System Computers now have a more functional file system. You can create folders, rename them, delete them, move files, restore files from Trash, and organize your desktop. Folders can contain notes, paint files, magazines, newspapers, video files, and other readable or downloadable files. Blank CDs can be found in the world. CDs can be opened from My Files, renamed, wiped, used to store files, or used to burn installed games. Removed CDs keep their name and stored content. Applications cannot be copied into folders or CDs, but files can. Magazines, Newspapers and Videos Computers found in the world may contain recipe magazines, newspapers, or video files. Reading or watching them takes time and can affect your character. Recipe magazines can teach the same things as their physical versions. Some hidden websites also allow you to download magazines or videos. Hidden site addresses may be found naturally inside notes or emails. Passwords, BIOS and OS Installation Some computers may be password protected. There are three ways to access them: Know the password. Find the password. Reset the disk from BIOS. Use a Password Hack CD. To hack a password, insert a Password Hack CD and start the hacking process from the login screen. Complete the mini-game to remove the password. By default, hacking requires Electrical level 1. Warning: Resetting the disk deletes the operating system and local data. If a computer has no OS, it cannot boot normally. Find a PZ OS 3.1 CD, insert it, enter BIOS during boot, and install the operating system from the CD. Internet Outage System Internet access can be affected by world power. If the power grid goes down, the internet backbone can go offline depending on sandbox settings. To restore the network, players must find special relay terminals around the map and repair them with Electrical skill and electronic parts. If relay power is required, the active relay must keep receiving electricity, such as from a generator. If that generator runs out of fuel, the network can go offline again. This system can be adjusted or disabled in sandbox options. Terminal Locations Customization You can change the computer name, profile picture, password, desktop background color, date format, clock format, and file layout. Desktop icons and folders can be moved on a grid. Translations The mod includes translation files for: English, French, Italian, German, Spanish, Danish, Dutch, Hungarian, Norwegian, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Turkish, Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Brazilian Portuguese, Finnish, Korean, Thai, Traditional Chinese, and Ukrainian. Roadmap & Known Bugs Full Roadmap Known Bugs List Upcoming Mod Permissions Please do not reupload, redistribute, or share modified versions of this mod without my permission. You are free to use this mod on your server through the original Steam Workshop page. Editing the files and distributing them through Discord, modpacks, private server packs, or any other platform without permission is not allowed. For compatibility patches, translations, server-specific edits, or addons based on this mod, please contact me first. Unauthorized edits or reuploads may be reported. My Other Mods: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2795331647 Thank you for checking it out. Workshop ID: 3725497089 Mod ID: ComputerModkum

description: This mod expands the medical side of Project Zomboid with new diseases, symptoms, treatments, diagnostic tools, blood-related mechanics, medical knowledge progression, and a more punishing survival experience. Project Zomboid health is often simple enough: patch the wound, disinfect it, take some pills, hope the bite was not that bite. This mod makes your character’s body feel more fragile, unpredictable, and dangerous to ignore. 🖥️EHR Health Monitoring New health monitoring UI with disease information, active medication and body status. To open new health panel press H (can be configured in Mod Options, not sandbox) Vanilla health panel still can be used, check mod options to configure what your primary health panel will be. EHR panel opens in compact mode by default, you can change that in mod options as well The mod adds a wide range of new illnesses and medical conditions designed to fit naturally into Project Zomboid’s survival loop. Diseases can be caused by wounds, corpses, contaminated food or water, poor conditions, temperature exposure, toxins, infection, untreated injuries, mental and other survival-related risks Some illnesses are mild and manageable. Others can slowly spiral out of control if ignored. Symptoms may overlap, making diagnosis less obvious and forcing the player to pay attention instead of treating every problem like “just take antibiotics.” For more detailed info of every disease please read pinned topic in discussions Extensive Health Rework Evolved adds new medical items, medicines, tests, and treatment tools. Some treatments are designed for specific conditions. Others may reduce symptoms, slow disease progression, or help recovery. Using the wrong treatment may be useless, risky, or simply a waste of supplies. The mod introduces more detailed medication behavior. Different medicines can affect different symptoms and conditions. Some may help reduce fatigue, endurance penalties, infection risks, or specific disease effects. Medication can have active states, doses, side effects, durations, and condition-specific usefulness. The goal is to make treatment feel more intentional instead of turning every illness into a one-button fix. Some medication can be found in houses, more advanced in clinics and hospitals, and top tier experimental ones in secret research facility and military bases. New Medical Crafting New recipes to make survival in wilderness more manageable but it will not replace clinical items. Medicinal Plant Search Players with enough medical and foraging knowledge or read the special flyer can inspect suitable bushes for useful plants. Search spots are hidden at first, so you must identify promising signs by hand. Some spots may hide thorns and can scratch your hands unless you wear intact gloves. Hive & Spiderweb Search Some trees may contain honeycomb or spiderwebs. Not every tree is useful, and inspected trees cannot be searched again for some time. Move your hand carefully through the tree area, avoiding bees and spiders. Collected honeycomb and spiderwebs are used in medical crafting. The mod expands blood-related gameplay with new mechanics connected to blood loss, blood types, transfusions, and dangerous complications. Blood is no longer just red decoration on your shirt after missing one fence swing. Blood level can be tracked by new special medical watches 🪡New Suturing minigame Vanilla suturing system is really forgiving and does not require player skill or medical skill practically at all. New suturing system adds depths to this mechanic and respect your character's first aid skills. If your suture is not good enough, there is a 40% chance of triggering cellulitis that if untreated will give severe complications. So keep your hands steady and don't rush(unless you bleeding to death and running from zombies. Then cellulitis is the least of your problems) The more First Aid you have the easier it's become (Can be turned off in sandbox settings, but why?) 🤧Immune System EHR now includes a dynamic Immune System that reacts to your character’s physical condition. It does not grant complete immunity or cure active diseases. Instead, it slightly increases or decreases the risk of contracting supported diseases. Your immune condition is displayed in the Immune System tab of the EHR Medical Panel. 📻The mod includes atmospheric radio content connected to health, survival, and the collapse of the world. A daily broadcast on 47.0 Mhz features Amelie Crowe, a radio host whose story progresses over time. Her transmissions may include medical advice, survival warnings and personal reflections 9 AM – medical advises which gives small first aid xp 3 PM – Storry progression 9 PM – Useful knowledge of different diseases The broadcast is intended to add atmosphere, worldbuilding, and a sense that someone out there is still trying to explain the end of everything — badly, beautifully, and probably while running out of supplies. 👩‍⚕️ A new perk with unique skill EHR surgeon gives you First Aid 10, special perk that works with scalpel and full knowledge of all diseases 📑Diagnosis and Medical Knowledge Not every condition is immediately obvious. Press J to open handbook and see what knowledge you have about diseases The mod gives more value to medical skill, books, and proper diagnosis. Some diseases may share similar symptoms, and the player may need specific knowledge or tools to better understand what is happening. Specialized medical flyers can help the character identify illnesses, understand symptoms, and choose the correct treatment. description: Required Dependency Toxic Sky is required for this mod to function properly. It Came Without Warning You heard rumors about them. And it seems they were true. The Monoliths are anomalous structures that appeared during the Knox Infection and seem to share a mysterious connection with the infected. But that’s not all. Each Monolith emits its own hazardous zone capable of taking a heavy toll on survivors — though the zones themselves do not directly kill. Gas masks and SCBA equipment have proven useful when dealing with prolonged exposure. Some survivors even claim that destroyed Monoliths leave behind valuable loot, indispensable for those willing to take the risk. And as if that weren’t enough, many report strange radio transmissions originating from the Monoliths themselves. Which only makes it easier to find them — and destroy them. A Brief Overview Toxic Sky Anomalies adds randomly spawning Monoliths that permanently persist on the map until destroyed. As usual, the mod includes extensive sandbox and configuration options. Use the vanilla Project Zomboid military tracking system found in Military Walkies and Military HAM Radios to determine the radio distance to anomaly targets. Each Monolith transmits on two frequencies: 11.2 MHz — a strong long-range signal transmitted twice per day across the region 11.4 MHz — a more active short-range signal intended for nearby survivors The Monoliths function as stationary anomaly bosses that continuously spawn waves until destroyed. Survivors who manage to overcome them may be rewarded with valuable loot. The system uses Toxic Sky core logic, meaning every Monolith creates a Hazard Zone with unique environmental dangers. However, these zones only deal indirect damage. You will not be instantly poisoned or continuously lose health — though there are plenty of other ways for the anomalies to make your life miserable. A unique VHS tape can also be discovered through event drops in both SP and MP. It contains radio frequencies and fragments of lore surrounding the Monoliths. They are also fully compatible with MP and SP. Otherwise, the new hazard zones are fully compatible with the Toxic Sky ZoneUI and can be placed and controlled by admins directly via the TS ZoneUI. Mods that gives you a different TSA experience: Toxic Sky Anomalies (Guns of Marz add-on) - by IronLungs (Thanks dude!) Q&A Question: I don´t see any monoliths appearing - what am I doing wrong? Answer: Monoliths have the same gate protection as Toxic Sky. Only when Water and Power is shutdown, the Event-Manager will start it´s work. Mods that manipulate Water&Power (Let you restore it) can interfere with that state. Best solution is to switch off the condition in the mod options! Question: Dude, I hear them on the radio with weird messages mixed in! But I can´t find them?! Answer: Monoliths transmit on two radio frequencies: 11.2 and 11.4. On 11.2, a strong, map-wide signal is transmitted twice a day, which can be detected using military walkie-talkies and military radios (the rangefinder from Project Zomboid) – this allows you to determine the distance to the source. 11.4 is a weaker signal with a range of up to around 2,000 metres and transmits every 30–40 minutes. This signal can also be tracked, but you need to be much closer to the source to get a clear reading. The frequencies are fixed and do not change. Finding them can be part of the challenge! And they do even send out RP valuable bits and snippets :3 Question: Help, weird stuff happens with my character and I see strange colors around my screen Answer: Congrats, you found a monolith zone. Each zone has it´s own hazard specific effect. Gasmasks work fine if a monolith is still young, but they loose effectivness the older it gets. Question: Dude, I pumped 5 magazines into the monolith and nothing happens?! This is broken! Answer: Technically - no. Monoliths are bulletproof by design. If you want to take them down, you have to get up close and personal. Two-handed weapons deal significantly more damage than one-handed weapons, so if you try to stab it to death with a knife... be prepared. That may take a LONG while! Question: What do you mean - the OLDER IT GETS? Answer: Haha, Monoliths can mature if you don´t take them out. If they are fully matured, they will drop more loot (Usealy 4-5 days) but their zone effect will grow stronger and only a SCBA gear will protect you fully then. Question: I got a ton of beans from my monolith kill and some aviator shades - wtf Answer: Yeah well I did try to keep the loot table as usefull as possible - but sometimes you can be unlucky. You find the loot table under TSA_LootTables.lua and can adjust the items, and the weights of common, uncommon and rare items. Question: I want to use this for my server! Will the Monoliths spawn in Johns bedroom?! Answer: It depends. TSA uses, like TS itself now, a native recognition of Project Zomboids Safehouse System in Multiplayer. If you use that, you are fine. The Event Manager will not place monoliths in your living room or garden. But I cannot guarantee that it might, some day, spawn in such a way that a town is partialy disrupted by it´s vicinity. Doing a automated spawn system is hard enough, and I never intended it to work with MP. I tried my best to guardrail it. Question: How do I place that as an Admin/GM/Mod on my server? Answer: Easy! Use the Toxic Sky Zone Panel - It´s a button in your admin tools, clearly labeled. If the button isn´t there, well, then another mod has overwritten it. Use the chat command /ts zoneui or /ts panel instead. it will open the pannel. TSA is a addon for TS, so it loads nativly into the Zone UI and can be choosed from the dropdowns. Question: OH GOD WILL THE MONOLITHS SPAWN THE ENTIRE WORLD?! Answer: No, there can only be 10 Monoliths active, at any given time - but you can adjust it in the mod options / sandbox options Question: I want the Monoliths to drop more and I want bigger waves and I also want them to spawn each hour! description: If the vehicles on your street are looking absolutely chopped, it is time to open a chop shop. Dismantle those clapped cars for spare parts and scrap metal. No cap, it is the best way to clean up the map. Multiplayer compatible. Safe to add to existing saves. CHOPPED VEHICLE SALVAGE This simple mod expands the vanilla wrecked vehicle dismantling mechanic to include all normal vehicles and trailers. While similar mods exist, this mod was born out of frustration with compatibility, or lack there of, these have with popular vehicle claiming and respawn mods. The goal was to make this as lightweight as possible. By relying mostly on base game mechanics and only adding a thin layer on top, this mod maximises compatibility and minimises the chance of breaking during future game updates. HOW IT WORKS Vehicles can be salvaged using a welding mask and a propane torch. Doing so destroys the vehicle, yields metalworking materials, and optionally recovers installed parts. Welding skill level 3 or higher is required to salvage normal vehicles or trailers (configurable in sandbox options). Higher Welding levels yield more materials upon dismantling. Normal vehicles take 2x as long to dismantle as burnt wrecks (configurable in sandbox options). Higher Welding levels increase dismantling speed. Installed parts drop upon salvage (min/max parts dropped can be configured or disabled in sandbox options). COMPATIBILITY Vehicle salvage action is derived from base game's burnt wreck dismantling, only adding skill requirements, part drops, and claim checks. It should work out of the box with most mods. Another Vehicle Claim System (AVCS) - Claimed vehicles cannot be salvaged. Vehicle Life Cycle Systems (VLCS) - Derives "ISRemoveBurntVehicle", meaning a respawn ticket is created when a vehicle is salvaged. Disable "Allow Scrapping Normal Cars" (AllowScrapNormal = false) in VLCS sandbox settings. Vehicle Repair Overhaul - Disable "Full Vehicle Salvaging" (VRO_EnableFullVehicleSalvaging = false) in VRO sandbox settings if you are using "Vehicle Salvage Overhaul" mod. If you use a vehicle claim system that is not listed here, a small compatibility patch might be required. Drop a comment and I will look into it. ⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀This mod was created for the Second Dawn server. Free for all This mod can be added to and extended by the whole community. description: Read and Recall Vanilla skill books in Project Zomboid give you XP just for finishing them. This mod adds an end-of-book check: after every skill-book chapter, you take a short quiz or play a hands-on minigame to KEEP the full XP multiplier. Skip or fail and you only get half the bonus. Ace it and the multiplier is yours. The result: skill books feel like LEARNING, not page-flipping. And every chapter ends in something memorable - drive a nail, read a horse's mood, dope the wind, choose the right quench for a sword, place primal cuts on a beef carcass. What's new Dedicated server / co-op support - quizzes and minigames now trigger in multiplayer. Compatible with "I Learn What I Read Too" - the two mods run side by side without conflict. Fixed the double popup - enabling both editions no longer opens two windows per book. Resizable quiz window - drag to resize; long question lists now scroll. 2 versions available Read and Recall (Real-Life) - real-world educational content. Each chapter teaches honest technique: hammer grips, food preservation chemistry, the working-temperature window for steel. Pass the quiz to prove you read it. Read and Recall: Knox Edition - the same skill books reimagined as in-universe Knox County textbooks, with Project Zomboid game mechanics woven into the narrative. Carpenter trait benefits, generator runtimes, the day the grid drops, magazine spawn locations - referenced in-story. The two editions are incompatible. Enable only ONE at a time. How it works Finish reading a vanilla skill book as normal. A Summary screen pops up with a recap of the chapter and two buttons: Take the Test or Skip (Half XP). Pass the test (a quiz or a hands-on minigame, depending on the volume): you keep the full vanilla XP multiplier for that level range. Skip or fail: you get the half multiplier ("floor") so reading is never a total waste. Progress is saved per character per book, so you can come back and re-test later. Features 24 skills supported - every craft, survival, and combat skill that has vanilla books. 120 volumes of content: 72 written quizzes (11 hand-written questions each) and 48 hands-on minigames. Sandbox-tunable: pick the test format, XP curve, and floor reward to match how you want the mod to feel (see below). No XP cheese by default: the maximum multiplier is the vanilla one. Opt-in Bonus mode is available in sandbox if you want above-vanilla XP for acing. Per-character progress stored in ModData. Multiple characters on the same save each track their own claims. Themed UI: each skill has its own colour palette and emblem on the summary/test banner. Sandbox options Four toggles on the New Game settings page (both editions): Test format - keep the mix of minigames and quizzes (default), or convert every minigame slot into a written multiple-choice quiz. Every minigame volume has an alt MC quiz authored - 96 across both editions. XP mode - Default (linear graded curve from floor to vanilla), Lenient (90%+ instantly gives full vanilla XP), or Bonus (90%+ gives ABOVE vanilla XP for the perfectionists). XP bonus multiplier - how much above vanilla the Bonus mode awards. 1.0 to 2.0, default 1.20 (20% above vanilla). Floor percent - XP fraction kept when skipping or failing. 0.0 to 1.0, default 0.5 (half XP). Set to 0.0 if you want no reward for failing. Skill-by-skill book index Every volume ends in a written Quiz or a named minigame. Full breakdown here: Read and Recall - quiz & minigame index (Google Sheets) Compatibility Compatible with any mod that does not replace that class wholesale. Singleplayer supported. Multiplayer/co-op newly added - please report any issues. No save corruption risk. Known issues / caveats Quizzes draw fresh questions each attempt, but pools are 11 deep per volume - re-reading the same book several times will revisit some questions. PZ's font does not render some Unicode dashes cleanly; all summaries use plain ASCII hyphens by design. Wind direction in Dope the Wind follows hunter convention - "left-to-right wind" means wind moving from your left to your right. Have fun. Read carefully. Pass the test. Also check out my other mods in my collection! Your support is much appreciated! Workshop ID: 3728582856 Mod ID: ReadAndRecall Mod ID: ReadAndRecallKnoxEdition

description: Better Vehicle Dynamics A drivetrain and traction overhaul for Project Zomboid Build 42. Every vehicle gains a torque-curve driven engine, surface- and weather-aware grip, and a stack of optional realism systems - all sandbox-tunable, all multiplayer-safe. What it changes Torque-curve acceleration - engines pull from a real power curve instead of a flat number. Low-end grunt for shoving wrecks, a proper top end. Surface & weather grip - independent traction on sealed road, rain, snow and off-road. Lose the back end if you push it. Tyre-type grip model - worn / standard / modern tyres each get distinct grip per surface, not one flat value. Load affects handling - a heavily loaded vehicle is slow to pull away from a stop, as if the engine is straining against the weight. Strength is a sandbox slider. Load affects fuel - hauling heavy burns extra fuel while driving. Configurable drag - air drag and rolling resistance (road and off-road) are separate, tunable knobs. Reference power & weight (opt-in) - researched HP/mass figures for the vanilla fleet; modded vehicles can register their own. Cargo-capacity rescale - per-body-type storage multipliers instead of one blanket override. Drift mode (opt-in) - hold a bindable key to break the rear loose for an arcade slide. Off by default. Tyre marks - vehicles leave a ground decal when a tyre breaks loose; marks fade out on their own. Vehicle info panel - a docked readout beside the mechanics window showing the active profile, per-surface grip, tyre type and cargo load. Ground-clip guard - a server-side safety net that snaps a vehicle back onto its floor if it ever sinks into the ground (a multiplayer desync class). Only ever acts on an impossible state, so normal driving, ramps and basements are unaffected. Tuning Everything is exposed in Sandbox Options, grouped into Handling, Tyres & Load, Drivetrain and Readout & Misc pages, plus quick tuning presets. Defaults aim for a grounded, readable feel; dial it toward arcade or hardcore to taste. Multiplayer Built for dedicated servers and co-op. Load-sensitive fuel and the ground-clip guard are server-authoritative so they behave consistently for everyone. Installation (players) Better Vehicle Dynamics is split between this Workshop subscription (Lua, sandbox options, UI) and a small one-time Java-side install (the deep physics - engine code Steam Workshop cannot patch). The subscription alone is not enough; do the manual step once and you are set. Tuning, tyre and guard updates after that are pure Workshop updates with no further manual install. Subscribe to this mod and let Steam finish downloading it. Open the mod folder: Steam\steamapps\workshop\content\108600\3728775267\mods\BetterVehicleDynamics\B42.20_Manual_Install\ Copy the zombie sub-folder from there into your Project Zomboid install directory (right-click Project Zomboid in Steam -> Manage -> Browse local files). Restart Project Zomboid. When Project Zomboid itself updates, recopy the zombie folder to refresh it. Dedicated server hosts Server-side install is the same idea: copy the whole zombie sub-folder from B42.20_Manual_Install\ into your server's <server>/java/zombie/ directory (merge it into the existing tree). It carries the full package layout - physics, world (iso) and texture classes - so copy the entire folder, not just one sub-path. Both the server and every connecting client need the install - a bytecode mismatch between sides will cause vehicle-related packet desync warnings. For modders A public Lua API lets other mods register vehicle reference data, tyre-grip profiles and content packs without touching this mod's files. Full reference: Better Vehicle Dynamics - Public Lua API Compatibility Works alongside vehicle-skin and content mods. Run only one vehicle-physics overhaul at a time. Build 42.20+. description: Automatic Lights Add a timer or motion sensor to any light — like real-world wall-outlet timers and porch sensors. Save electricity, stretch your bulb supply, light your perimeter hands-free. What it does Craft one of four new devices, right-click a light to install it, then Configure the light to set its behavior. Each light holds one device at a time. Light Timer — daily on/off schedule. Set ON and OFF times independently or use only one side. Indoor Motion Sensor — turns the light on when a player enters the same room; off after an idle period. Walls block detection. Outdoor Motion Sensor — turns the light on for any player within a configurable tile radius; off after an idle period. For porch and patio fixtures with no enclosed room. Night Outdoor Motion Sensor — same as the outdoor sensor but only active between dusk and dawn. Saves bulbs and electricity by ignoring motion during daylight. Note: for performance reasons the "motion" sensors actually detect presence, not movement. The light stays on for as long as you remain in the room (indoor) or inside the radius (outdoor), and the idle countdown only begins once you leave the area. Lights will turn off while you sleep, however. Features Four craftable devices in the Electrical category. Timer at skill 1, motion sensors at skill 2. Per-light configuration — every light has its own schedule or idle-minutes setting. Independent ON / OFF for timers — set only one side if you only want dusk-on or dawn-off. Manual override respected — toggle a timer light by hand and it stays in that state until the next scheduled transition fires. Returns to schedule when you walk back into range, even across an on/off boundary. Motion lights are event-driven — they react immediately when someone enters detection range. Optional zombie detection on motion sensors — early-warning porch lights. Server-authoritative — all light state lives on the server, same code path in SP, hosted MP, dedicated MP, and split-screen. Crafting Light Timer (Electrical 1) — salvaged kitchen timer or alarm clock, electronics scrap, electric wire, screws. Screwdriver required. Indoor Light Motion Sensor (Electrical 2) — vanilla MotionSensor (electronics loot), electronics scrap, wire, screws. Screwdriver required. Outdoor Light Motion Sensor (Electrical 2) — same as indoor plus 2 duct tape for the weatherproof housing. Night Outdoor Motion Sensor (Electrical 2) — upgrade an existing Outdoor Motion Sensor with a wrist watch (provides the timekeeping element), electronics scrap, and wire. Screwdriver required. Worn watches are ignored. Skill gates live in the recipes. Once a device is built, anyone can install and configure it (configurable in sandbox). Requirements Build 42 (versionMin 42.18). Not B41-compatible. A working light bulb installed in the light. Configuration (Sandbox Options) Look for the Automatic Lights page in Custom Sandbox. Each option has a hover tooltip. Timer Enabled — master toggle for the entire mod (default on). Require Timer item — require a crafted Light Timer installed on a light before it can be scheduled (default on). Turn off to configure any light directly, gated only by Electrical skill. Required Electrical skill — minimum skill to configure a light timer; applies only when Require Timer item is off (default 1, range 0–5). Default ON / OFF time — prefilled in the timer dialog (default 19:00 / 06:00). Catch up on chunk load — reconcile timer lights when their chunk reloads (default on). Motion sensor Motion sensors enabled — toggle for the motion-sensor feature (default on). Off = installed sensors stop reacting and new installs are blocked. Require Motion Sensor item — require a crafted Indoor or Outdoor Motion Sensor installed on a light (default on). Motion Sensor Electrical skill — minimum skill when the item requirement above is off (default 2, range 0–5). Default idle-off minutes — prefilled in the motion-sensor dialog (default 5, range 1–60). Outdoor sensor radius (tiles) — detection radius for the outdoor sensor (default 6, range 1–20). Indoor sensors use room boundaries instead. Motion poll interval (frames) — how often sensors check for nearby players (default 10). Sensors detect zombies — also trigger on zombies, useful as an early-warning porch light (default on). Compatibility Build 42 only. Not B41-compatible. Singleplayer, hosted MP, dedicated MP, split-screen — same code path, all supported. Light state is server-authoritative. Server admins — adding to an existing world PZ does not merge new sandbox options into existing world saves. New worlds pick up defaults automatically. Existing worlds need an AutoLightTimers block hand-spliced into <servername>_SandboxVars.lua: AutoLightTimers = { Enabled = true, RequireTimerItem = true, RequiredElectricalSkill = 1, DefaultOnHour = 19, DefaultOnMin = 0, DefaultOffHour = 6, DefaultOffMin = 0, CatchUpOnChunkLoad = true, MotionSensorEnabled = true, RequireMotionSensorItem = true, MotionSensorSkillLevel = 2, MotionSensorDefaultIdleMinutes = 5, OutdoorMotionSensorRadius = 6, MotionSensorPollFrames = 10, MotionSensorDetectZombies = true, }, Server config: add to WorkshopItems= and Mods=AutoLightTimers. description: Gore's SVU4 is a vehicle survival and customisation framework for Project Zomboid Build 42.20.2, expanding the vanilla fleet with an armour and upgrade system built around keeping vehicles alive long after the roads have stopped being friendly. Supported vehicles can be fitted with multiple grades of armour, bull bars, plows, engine scoops, filtered air intakes, roof equipment, tire chains, auxiliary fuel storage, Auto Tune radio antennas and selectable wheel-rim styles. The Vehicle Upgrades interface keeps installation, removal, repairs and material requirements together in one place, while the established vehicle-paint system adds another layer of customisation without replacing the underlying vanilla vehicles. The current Vanilla Cars build brings SVU4 support across the supported vanilla vehicle families with family-specific armour and upgrade visuals, Gold armour variants and scoop-cut hood armour where appropriate. This update also includes a substantial visual-routing cleanup for Build 42.20.2: PickUpVan bull bars, plows and scoop hoods have corrected positioning and refresh behaviour, PickUpTruck hood armour has been realigned to the current body model, ModernCar02 and service-vehicle roof equipment use the correct family visuals, and vehicles with factory emergency light bars no longer offer roof racks that would occupy the same space. SVU4 also includes optional survival-focused crafting modules. Vanilla Vehicle Parts Crafting lets players manufacture a broad selection of replacement car parts, now including Old, Regular and Performance mufflers that require a compatible standard, crafted or recharged filter. Spare Engine Parts Crafting provides Old, Regular and Performance fabrication tiers with progressively higher skill requirements and repair efficiency while rewarding Mechanics, Metalworking and Electrical XP. These systems are intended to make long-term vehicle maintenance possible without turning replacement parts into free loot. For larger bases and multiplayer worlds, the optional Industrial Fluid Infrastructure module adds industrial and player-buildable fluid storage with native liquid handling and propane support. SVU4 is designed as a modular package: use the Core framework and Vanilla Cars support as the foundation, then enable the crafting and infrastructure components you want for your world. Existing Workshop and Mod IDs are retained, so this release is a direct production update to the existing SVU4 ecosystem rather than a separate branch. description: Build 42.20 ready - fully tested in single player, on a dedicated server and in co-op host. Still works on earlier Build 42 versions. READ BEFORE ANYTHING !! For Any Bug Report For Any Suggestion Before saying "it's not working", unsubscribe, then resubscribe. If it still fails, post your bug on Discord with your console file "C:\Users\you\Zomboid\console.txt" and your mod list "C:\Users\you\Zomboid\mods\default.txt" => Discord : https://discord.gg/vJay7GQ92B ❄️ Plysken Frost Revolution Turn any small room into an industrial cold storage. Build a Cold Unit, mount it on a wall, power it up, and the room temperature drops. Perishable food kept in containers inside the room stays frozen — indefinitely — as long as the unit has power. The post-apocalypse just got cooler. Solo & Multiplayer (Host/Coop and Dedicated Server). ❄️ Getting Started 1. Learn the recipe. Read Sub-Zero Solutions: Industrial Cold Storage, found as loot — or reach Electricity 7 and it comes on its own. Crafting needs Electricity 5. 2. Craft the Cold Unit. At any surface, with a screwdriver and a wrench in your bag. If the craft button stays greyed out, scroll the ingredient list — the screws are the last line and are easy to miss. 3. Mount it on a wall, indoors. The room needs walls AND a roof; any of the four walls works. A covered terrace is not a room, and the cursor will stay red. 4. Switch it on. Right-click the unit, Open Control Panel, set the target with the rotary knob (−30 °C to 0 °C) and press power. The room cools progressively — a large room with a single unit takes a while, several units cool it much faster. 5. Store your food. Anything perishable in any container in the room freezes once the room sits at or below 0 °C, and stays frozen while the unit has power. Carcasses on a butcher hook are preserved the same way. Items dropped loose on the floor are not. Extend the cold next door: stand in the neighbouring room, right-click the floor and pick "Add this room to the cold room". The two rooms must share a real opening — a doorway, or a wall you broke down. Up to 12 rooms per cold room. Full step-by-step, every placement rule and a "nothing is freezing" checklist: Getting started & troubleshooting 🖥️ Control Panel Live room temperature, an adjustable target on a rotary knob (drag it, or roll the mouse wheel over it), and an on/off toggle with startup, ambient hum and shutdown sounds. If the unit is on but gets no power, the panel says so. Draughts from open doors and smashed windows slow the cooling down, so seal your room well. Your character feels the cold inside (vanilla Hypothermia, toggleable). Works in vanilla buildings and in rooms you build yourself. 📦 Items Cold Unit — the wall-mounted cooling unit. Built from engine parts, plastic pipes, electronics scrap, sheet metal, scrap metal, electrical wire and screws. Sub-Zero Solutions: Industrial Cold Storage — the skill magazine. ⚙️ Sandbox Options Default target temperature (−30 °C to 0 °C, default −10 °C) Cooling speed multiplier (0.25 to 4.0 — raise it if you find the wait too long) Insulation strength (0.0 to 3.0 — set 0 to disable the breach mechanic) Player feels the cold (on/off) Temperature unit — Celsius or Fahrenheit 🤝 Companion Mod (optional) Lua Digital Watch UI by RedChili — when you wear a digital watch, it shows the cold room temperature instead of the outdoor climate. Auto-detected, no setup needed. ⚠️ Engine Limitations Your in-game watch reads the vanilla climate by default — the Control Panel is the source of truth (or install the companion mod above). The placed unit is named "Air Conditioner" in the pickup and dismantle menus. It reuses the vanilla air-conditioner sprite, and the game builds that label from the sprite, not from the item — renaming it would rename every air conditioner on the map, so it stays as is. In your inventory and on the Control Panel it is correctly called Cold Unit. If you also carry a salvaged air conditioner, be careful: once placed the two look identical, and the game places whichever comes first in your bag. The mod now warns you when that happens, so you don't end up waiting on a unit that was never yours. 📋 Requirements Project Zomboid Build 42. No other mods required. Safe to add to an existing save — you craft the unit when you're ready. As with any mod, test on a spare save first; I'm not responsible for conflicts with other mods. 🌍 Translations English and French are complete. German, Spanish (plus the Argentinian, Chilean and Mexican variants), Italian, Portuguese, Brazilian Portuguese, Dutch, Russian, Ukrainian, Simplified & Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Thai, Polish and Turkish cover most of the interface; anything not translated falls back to English. Catalan, Czech, Danish, Finnish, Hungarian, Indonesian, Norwegian and Romanian are still largely English. These translations are mine, not a native speaker's. If something reads wrong in your language, tell me on Discord and I'll fix it — with credit. 🙏 Credits & License Original mod by Plysken. The Cold Unit reuses the vanilla industry_01_4 sprite (Air Conditioner) but is mechanically a brand-new item with its own behavior, sounds and UI. © 2026 Plysken. All rights reserved. description: Realistic Eye Adaptation to Dark You step into a Build 42 room without lights and see nothing. Real eyes don't work that way - and now your character's eyes don't either. This mod simulates real dark adaptation. The first seconds in a pitch-black room, you can't see a thing. Over the next 20 in-game minutes (configurable), your night vision builds up until you can navigate the room. Step into bright daylight afterwards and a brief glare flash washes the screen - your dilated pupils paying the price. Features Gradual dark adaptation - eyes adjust over ~20 in-game minutes Three-zone awareness - outdoor / lit indoor / dark indoor each affect adaptation differently Soft decay, not snap-reset - leaving a dark room doesn't instantly cost you all your adaptation (10 min outdoor, 40 min lit indoor) Glare effect - per-player warm flash when dark-adapted eyes hit bright light, cooldown-gated against door spam Adapted vision moves with you - soft warm ambient light follows your character in dark rooms (singleplayer only - see below) 7 tunable sandbox options - adaptation time, decay rates, brightness cap, trigger sensitivity, glare on/off, glare duration, cooldown Multiplayer The world-light effect is disabled in multiplayer by design - a shared lighting buff would x-ray hiding teammates and break ambush gameplay. Adaptation is still tracked internally so the per-player glare flash still fires on your own screen. Not compatible with Room Light Boost Both mods spawn ambient light; running them together stacks the effect. Pick one: instant boost (RLB) or gradual realism (this mod). Compatibility Project Zomboid Build 42. Safe to add to existing saves. Safe to remove. Türkçe Build 42'de ışıksız bir odaya giriyorsun ve hiçbir şey göremiyorsun. Gerçek hayatta gözler böyle çalışmaz - artık karakterinin gözleri de çalışmıyor. Bu mod gerçek dark adaptation'ı simüle ediyor. Zifiri karanlık bir odaya girdiğin ilk saniyelerde hiçbir şey göremezsin. Sonraki 20 in-game dakika boyunca (ayarlanabilir) gece görüşün gelişir, odada hareket edebilir hale gelirsin. Sonra parlak gün ışığına çıkarsın ve ekranda kısa bir göz kamaşması patlar; genişlemiş pupillerinin bedelini ödersin. Özellikler Yavaş alışma - gözler ~20 in-game dakikada uyum sağlar Üç ortam algısı - dışarı / aydınlık iç mekan / karanlık iç mekan adaptasyonu farklı etkiler Yumuşak decay, anında sıfırlama yok - karanlık odadan çıkmak adaptasyonunu hemen yakıp atmaz (dışarıda 10 dk, aydınlık iç mekanda 40 dk) Göz kamaşması efekti - adapte gözler parlak ışıkla karşılaşınca ekranda sıcak flaş, kapı spam'ine karşı cooldown korumalı Adapte görüş seninle hareket eder - karanlık odalarda karakterini takip eden yumuşak sıcak ışık (sadece singleplayer - aşağıya bak) 7 ayarlanabilir sandbox option - adaptasyon süresi, decay oranları, parlaklık tavanı, hassasiyet, glare on/off, glare süresi, cooldown Multiplayer Dünya-ışığı efekti MP'de tasarım gereği kapalı - paylaşımlı ışık buff'ı saklanan takım arkadaşlarını x-ray ederdi ve pusu mekaniğini bozardı. Adaptasyon yine internal olarak takip edilir, per-player glare flash hâlâ senin ekranında patlar. Deutsch Du betrittst in Build 42 einen Raum ohne Licht und siehst gar nichts. Echte Augen funktionieren nicht so - und jetzt deine Spielfigur auch nicht mehr. Dieses Mod simuliert echte Dunkeladaptation. In den ersten Sekunden in einem pechschwarzen Raum siehst du nichts. Über die nächsten 20 Spielminuten (konfigurierbar) baut sich deine Nachtsicht auf, bis du den Raum erfassen kannst. Trittst du danach in helles Tageslicht, blitzt eine kurze Blendung über den Bildschirm - deine geweiteten Pupillen zahlen den Preis. Funktionen Allmähliche Anpassung - Augen passen sich über ~20 Spielminuten an Drei Zonen - Außen / hell innen / dunkel innen wirken jeweils anders auf die Adaptation Sanftes Abklingen, kein sofortiges Zurücksetzen - der Gang aus einem dunklen Raum kostet nicht sofort die ganze Anpassung (10 min außen, 40 min hell innen) Blendungseffekt - adaptierte Augen treffen helles Licht: warmer Blitz auf dem Bildschirm, Cooldown gegen Tür-Spam Adaptierte Sicht folgt dir - sanftes warmes Umgebungslicht im dunklen Raum (nur Einzelspieler - siehe unten) 7 konfigurierbare Sandbox-Optionen - Anpassungszeit, Decay-Raten, Helligkeitsgrenze, Empfindlichkeit, Blendung an/aus, Blendungsdauer, Cooldown Mehrspieler Das Welt-Licht ist im Mehrspieler bewusst deaktiviert - ein geteilter Lichtbuff würde versteckte Mitspieler durchleuchten und Hinterhalte zerstören. Die Anpassung wird intern weiter verfolgt, und der per-player Blendungseffekt erscheint trotzdem auf deinem Bildschirm. Русский Заходишь в Build 42 в комнату без света - не видишь ничего. Настоящие глаза работают не так. И теперь глаза твоего персонажа - тоже. Этот мод симулирует настоящую адаптацию к темноте. Первые секунды в кромешно тёмной комнате ты ничего не видишь. На протяжении следующих 20 игровых минут (настраивается) ночное зрение нарастает, и ты можешь ориентироваться в комнате. Затем выходишь на яркий дневной свет - экран ослепляет короткая вспышка: расширенные зрачки платят свою цену. Особенности Постепенная адаптация - глаза привыкают за ~20 игровых минут Три зоны - улица / освещённое помещение / тёмное помещение по-разному влияют на адаптацию Плавное затухание, без мгновенного сброса - выход из тёмной комнаты не лишает тебя адаптации мгновенно (10 мин на улице, 40 мин в освещённом помещении) Эффект ослепления - адаптированные глаза попадают на яркий свет: тёплая вспышка на экране, кулдаун против спама дверей Адаптированное зрение следует за тобой - мягкий тёплый свет следует за персонажем в тёмных комнатах (только одиночная игра - см. ниже) 7 настраиваемых sandbox-опций - время адаптации, скорости затухания, максимальная яркость, чувствительность, вспышка вкл/выкл, длительность, кулдаун Сетевая игра Мировой свет по дизайну отключён в сетевой игре - общий световой бафф просвечивал бы прячущихся союзников и ломал засадную механику. Адаптация по-прежнему отслеживается внутренне, и per-player вспышка по-прежнему срабатывает на твоём экране.

description: Extensive Power Rework (Community fork) A community continuation of Hunter's Extensive Power Rework for Project Zomboid Build 42. Hunter stepped back from PZ modding and publicly invited community forks; this is one of those forks. What it does Power and water infrastructure overhaul. Substations and water treatment facilities are real, repairable objects. Players restore utilities to entire zones by completing repair tasks at the right locations. Stations The mod ships with 6 facilities scattered across Knox County. Each one must be repaired to restore power or water to its zones. Louisville Power Plant is the master prerequisite - bring it online before any other substation can carry power downstream. Louisville Power Plant (12120, 1617) - powers Louisville. Prereq for the whole grid. Louisville South Substation (14732, 4083) - powers West Point, Valley Station, Louisville Airport. Muldraugh Substation (10389, 10060) - powers Muldraugh, Rosewood, March Ridge, Fallas Lake. Riverside Relay (4832, 6279) - powers Riverside. Irvington Substation (2210, 13914) - powers Irvington, Echo Creek, Ekron, Brandenburg. Rosewood Water Treatment (8044, 15360) - waters every zone. What's in this fork The full v1.0.4 codebase carried forward B42.18 compatibility (sandbox JSON translations, current API) Additional Features (Community Fork additions) Everything below is new in the Community fork on top of Hunter's original. Original codebase and gameplay design remain Hunter's; this list tracks only what the fork adds. Gameplay Storm Blackouts - during thunderstorms, online substations have a configurable chance per 10-minute tick of being knocked offline by a lightning strike, forcing repair through the normal EPR flow. Three sandbox options to tune frequency and whether thunder is required (vs heavy rain). Server-side, sandbox-gated. Admin tooling EPR Debug Panel - admin / SP / -debug-only right-click submenu opens a tabbed window: Zones (per-zone power+water toggles), Facilities (Teleport, Flicker, Repair, Activate, Deactivate per substation + water plant), World (global override, noise burst, Force vanilla shutoff, Lightning strike random / ALL online). Mirrors the pattern of The Director and Better Vehicle Dynamics. Compatibility Pure Lua, no Java patches No item-script overrides - safe to remove without orphaning inventory Uses ModData on world objects: removing mid-save reverts repaired zones to non-functional but does not corrupt the save Server-friendly: drop into the Mods= line, restart Credits Original concept, codebase, and all of the work: Hunter, who opened the project for community forks when stepping back. Source Source code is on GitHub: github.com/grphx/extensive-power-community. Issues, suggestions, and pull requests welcome. Mod info Mod ID: EPR_Community Workshop ID: 3733603053

description: Moonlight Mayhem Moonlight Mayhem is a quality-of-life mod… if your preferred quality of life is living in constant fear, checking the clock every five seconds, and treating 6 PM like a scheduled execution. This mod changes zombie speed based on the time of day. During the day, things can stay somewhat normal. But once the moon rises and the timer hits your chosen start time, the dead stop dragging their feet and start running. During the day, you prepare. At night, you survive. What This Mod Does Moonlight Mayhem lets you set a daily time window where zombies become much more dangerous. By default, zombies become sprinters at night and return to a slower speed in the morning. You can change the start time, end time, night zombie speed, off-hours zombie speed, refresh behavior, tracking options, cleanup settings, and optional extra night spawns through sandbox options. No-Spawn Area Tool This update adds a new in-game tool that lets you mark areas where Moonlight Mayhem’s optional night spawns will not place zombies. To use it: Right-click the ground. Open the Moonlight Mayhem menu. Choose Enable Click-and-Drag No-Spawn Zone. Click and drag over the area you want protected. Release the mouse button to save it. The menu also includes: Show Saved Area Briefly — shows saved no-spawn areas for about 10 seconds. Clear All Saved No-Spawn Areas — clears all protected areas so you can redo them. Important: This only blocks Moonlight Mayhem’s own optional night zombie spawns. It does not control vanilla Project Zomboid respawns or zombies spawned by other mods. Build 42.20 Night Hunt Options This update adds more sandbox control for how dangerous nights become. You can enable Night Player Tracking Pulse, which makes zombies within the selected radius detect and move toward your location during active night hours. For example, with the default time window: 6:00 PM to 6:00 AM Zombies can be made to know where you are and start hunting toward your area. This does not update every zombie in the entire world at once, because that would probably make your PC file for divorce. Instead, it uses a controlled radius around the player. Default Behavior By default, the nightmare begins at: 6:00 PM And ends at: 6:00 AM Because once night hits, the dead start running. If tracking is enabled, they may also start moving toward you like you personally insulted their entire bloodline. If optional night spawns are enabled, use the No-Spawn Area Tool to protect your base or other important areas from this mod’s custom spawns. Compatibility Designed for Build 42.20 Includes an in-game right-click no-spawn area tool Made mainly for single player Multiplayer may work, but it is not my main focus Mods that heavily change zombie behavior may conflict Multiplayer Note My main focus with this mod is single player.
