Seed Season Indicator A mod that overlays markers on seed and seed packet icons in your inventory to indicate the current month's sowing season status. Lets you tell at a glance whether each seed is ready to plant right now. In vanilla, checking the sowing season requires opening the Info → Discovered Recipes and Media → Agriculture tab. This mod overlays the indicator directly on seed icons in the inventory, so you can tell whether a seed is plantable right now without opening any other window. Update (2026-08-06, v1.3.5): Added Brazilian Portuguese translation. Marker Types Green ★ — Best month (bestMonth): peak yield period Green ● — In season (sowMonth, excluding best/risk): safe to plant Yellow ● — Risk month (riskMonth): plantable, but with a risk of reduced yield Red ● — Out of season (outside sowMonth): cannot plant now Display Condition (Vanilla-Compliant) Markers appear only on seeds and seed packets for which you have read the seed packet and learned the corresponding sowing season recipe. Season Info in the "Category" Column The "Category" column in inventory detail view also shows the season status, and can be sorted by it. Display examples: Gardening (Best) / Gardening (In Season) / Gardening (Risk) / Gardening (Out of Season) Edible seeds categorized as "Food" — such as "Sunflower Seeds" and "Pumpkin Seeds" — also get the season status, shown as Food (Best) and so on Clicking the "Category" column header sorts by Best → In Season → Risk → Out of Season → Unread → Gardening (others). Seeds in the "Food" category group together in season order right after the other food items Useful for bringing "seeds ready to plant right now" to the top of the list Season Info in the Tooltip (v1.3) Hovering over a seed or seed packet appends season info to the end of its tooltip. This month (July): Out of Season — the current month's status, color-coded the same as the markers Planting Season / Best Month / Poor Month — the list of plantable months, using the same wording as the farming menu An image of the fully grown crop is shown on the right Display conditions are the same as the markers (only seeds whose packet you have read; empty seed packets show nothing) Options Configure from Options → Mods → Seed Season Indicator. Enable Indicator (default: ON): toggles marker rendering and category column extension Show season info in tooltip (default: ON): toggles the tooltip season info Markers not showing? This mod follows the sandbox setting PlantGrowingSeasons. If it is disabled, your world has no growing seasons, so all markers are intentionally hidden (there is no "in/out of season" to show). In particular, the "Outbreak" difficulty preset has this PlantGrowingSeasons setting disabled. Also note that markers only appear on seeds whose seed packet you have already read (see "Display Condition" above). Compatibility Supports: Build 42 Languages: English / Japanese / Russian / French / Korean / Spanish / Brazilian Portuguese (Russian translation provided by HoloBucket, French translation provided by Seijun, Korean translation provided by Hagaren, Spanish translation provided by Salve Sithis, Brazilian Portuguese translation provided by Yhan113) Standalone — works with vanilla, no additional mods required When used together with mods that draw "read" markers on seed packets, the markers from both mods may appear side by side on the seed packet icon (no functional impact) When Show Sowing Season In Seed Tooltip is active, this mod's tooltip section is automatically disabled to avoid duplicate info (markers and the "Category" column keep working) Not compatible with inventory UI overhaul mods that completely redefine the ISInventoryPane class (neither marker rendering nor category column extension will function) Technical Notes Wraps ISInventoryPane:renderdetails to overlay marker textures on seed/seed packet icons via drawTexture Wraps ISInventoryPane:refreshContainer to overwrite the sort key (v.cat) with custom category keys Category column display text is replaced via drawText interception (non-destructive approach, does not call item:setDisplayCategory) The tooltip section wraps ISToolTipInv:render and appends rows and the crop image right after the vanilla drawing (temporary DoTooltip swap, always restored) Settings are saved via PZAPI.ModOptions to ~/Zomboid/ModOptions.ini Workshop ID: 3734639991 Mod ID: SeedSeasonIndicator

Absolutely no disrespect to the original creator. MethylEniMine did an amazing job with the original mod, and all original credit goes to them. This version is my Build 42.20 repair, compatibility pass, and storage chaos update. This mod is for survivors who want massive fridge and freezer storage without turning their base into a cursed warehouse full of 80 refrigerators. If you hunt, farm, cook, hoard canned food, stockpile meat, or collect random junk because “I might need it later,” this mod is for you. (´｡• ᵕ •｡`) Included Mods This Workshop item includes: Fridge Expansion Deluxe — the main mod focused on refrigerators and freezers Fridge Expansion Deluxe: Storage Boost Add-On — optional add-on for expanded container/backpack storage features Use only the main mod if you just want huge fridges and freezers. (ﾉ◕ヮ◕)ﾉ*:･ﾟ✧ Boosts many supported containers to massive storage values Helps backpacks and storage containers feel extremely lightweight This add-on is intentionally overpowered. If you want a cleaner fridge-only experience, enable only the main mod. Multiplayer Support Note I do my best to make my mods work in multiplayer, but multiplayer can be extremely complicated and sometimes unpredictable. I work long hours during the week and only really have weekends off, plus I have a husband and a two-year-old daughter, so unfortunately I do not live in a magical world where I can spend unlimited time troubleshooting Project Zomboid multiplayer issues. I will still try to keep things working when I reasonably can, but if this mod ever breaks in multiplayer or has multiplayer-only problems, I am very sorry, but it will no longer be my main priority. Singleplayer and general stability will be my focus going forward, because I am not going to stress myself out or pull my hair out over multiplayer anymore. Credit All original credit goes to MethylEniMine, the creator of the original Methyl’s Furniture mod. This mod exists because I genuinely loved that mod and wanted to help bring that wonderful storage chaos into Build 42.20. This mod was also heavily inspired by Dane, the creator of Customizable Containers. Customizable Containers was honestly one of my favorite mods because of how much freedom it gave players with storage, backpacks, weight, and container capacity. The huge sandbox menu and all the extra options could cause lag, glitches, and multiplayer weirdness, so I wanted to implement some of that same storage convenience directly into this mod in a much simpler way. No giant sandbox setup, no crazy settings maze, just cleaner storage boosts that are easier to use without breaking the game. The server creates one active airdrop event at a time, spawns a lootable crate vehicle/container, fills it with controlled weighted loot, adds event zombies around the area, sends temporary markers to the correct players, and safely cleans everything up when the event expires or is removed. Important Compatibility Notice Built for Project Zomboid Build 42.20.2. Designed for multiplayer and dedicated server use. Not intended for older Build 42 versions. The chat commands are available only in client/server multiplayer. How The Event Works The server runs the airdrop scheduler. By default, the server attempts one airdrop every 24 real-life hours. Only one airdrop can exist at a time. If an airdrop is already active, the next cycle is skipped. Each event has a limited lifetime, configured in Sandbox options. When the timer ends, the crate marker is removed and the active event state is cleared. Drop Modes Mode 1 - Private Player Drop The server chooses one random online player. The airdrop is spawned near that player, not directly on top of them. The chosen player receives the timer, direction arrow and approximate map zone. Other players can still find the crate naturally, but they do not receive the private marker. Mode 2 - Global Fixed Point Drop The server chooses one fixed map point from the configured list. All online players receive the global map zone and direction arrow. The same fixed point is not selected twice in a row. If the selected chunk is not loaded yet, the zone is still announced. The crate is spawned only when a player gets close enough to the marked area. This keeps the event optimized and avoids forcing unloaded map chunks. Location Validation The mod validates the drop location before spawning the crate. It avoids invalid or unsafe squares such as: water, rivers and lakes tiles without floor indoor rooms and buildings roofs and constructions above the square walls, doors, stairs and trees solid or blocked tiles vehicle intersections unloaded chunks Loot System The crate uses a weighted loot system with configurable categories: Military Food Medical Tools Ammo Survival Military clothing Rare loot Items are validated before being added to the container. Invalid items are logged instead of breaking the event. Loot Levels Level 1 - Simple: basic loot, up to 30 zombies. Level 2 - Medium: medium/good loot, up to 60 zombies, with a small sprinter chance. Level 3 - Top: stronger loot, 80 to 120 zombies. Level 4 - Elite Military: military-focused loot, 135 to 200 zombies, larger spawn radius. Loot levels can control zombie count, zombie radius, item count, item repeat limits, loot weight multipliers and category weights. You can also disable level defaults and manually tune many values through Sandbox options. Markers And UI Small vanilla-style countdown timer. Direction arrow pointing to the approximate zone. Approximate blinking circle inside the in-game map. No ground circle is created in the world. The map marker color is configurable in Sandbox options. The marker does not reveal the exact crate location. Zombies And Decorations Event zombies spawn around the crate according to the selected loot level or manual Sandbox values. Zombies are distributed around the area instead of stacked on one tile. Optional impact decorations can add dead bodies, blood and crater/scorch marks near the airdrop. The mod does not create explosions, fire or destructive map damage. Admin Commands /drop - force an airdrop event. /drop1 or /drop 1 - force a Level 1 airdrop. /drop2 or /drop 2 - force a Level 2 airdrop. /drop3 or /drop 3 - force a Level 3 airdrop. /drop4 or /drop 4 - force a Level 4 airdrop. /nodrop - remove the current active or pending airdrop. Commands require admin/moderator-style access. Forced drops bypass the scheduled timer, but they still respect the one-active-airdrop rule. Sandbox Options The mod includes Sandbox options for: enabling or disabling the mod event interval in real hours airdrop lifetime drop mode loot level manual loot limits loot categories zombie count and radius marker radius and marker color direction arrow and map marker toggles location search attempts Mode 2 fixed-point search radius optional /chopper trigger impact decorations debug logs Performance Notes The system is designed to be light on dedicated servers: No heavy per-frame map scans. No constant OnTick spawn checks. Server-side scheduling is handled in real time. Location validation runs only when a spawn is attempted. Pending Mode 2 drops materialize only when players approach the zone. The server keeps one active event state at a time. Summary Airdrop Mod is a multiplayer-focused event system for Project Zomboid Build 42.20. It creates timed, configurable and server-controlled airdrop events with loot, zombies, map guidance, admin tools and safe cleanup. Did you like the mod? Support the development! Build a pipe network, hook it up to your rain collectors, and let it water your farm automatically — drawing from the barrels you already have. A clean, Build 42 take on the classic irrigation pipes, rebuilt from the ground up. Singleplayer & Multiplayer — works in co-op and on dedicated servers. 🔧 How It Works 1. Craft the pipes. A metal pipe with a hammer and a screwdriver in your bag gives you Irrigation Pipe — four per craft. A fired clay pipe segment gives you Clay Irrigation Pipe, one per segment and no tools at all: once you have a pottery wheel and a kiln, that route is renewable. 2. Lay a pipe on the ground. Right-click the tile you want it on, then Irrigation Pipe → Place Pipe, and pick the shape you need — Pipe Line (E-W), Pipe Cross, Pipe Corner (NE), Pipe T (North) and so on. They lay on bare ground and on built floors alike. You know it took when the pipe is on the tile and that same right-click now offers Remove Pipe. 3. Reach a rain collector. There is nothing to click for this one: run your pipes until one of them sits next to a rain collector and the connection is made for you. To see what is actually linked, right-click any pipe and choose Show Network — the pipes light up blue and every barrel feeding them turns green. Hide Network clears it. 4. Then leave it alone. Every cycle the network waters the farming plots within its reach, drawing from the barrels of that same network. Each plant is filled to its own optimal level and no further, so nothing is wasted, and barrels on one network share and even out their water between them. 5. Feed the crops too, if you want. With a bag of Fertilizer or Compost on you, right-click a rain collector that is part of the network and choose Pour Compost into irrigation water (or Pour Fertilizer into irrigation water). Right-click that barrel again and it tells you what is left — Reservoir — Fertilizer: x, Compost: y (doses). Right-click a crop and it reads Crop — Composted, Crop — Fertilized or Crop — Fertilized & Composted. One safe dose per plant, never more: it cannot over-fertilize or kill a crop. Compost is spent first because it is renewable; fertilizer is kept as the backup. 🔎 Network View Right-click any pipe and choose Show Network to highlight every pipe (blue) and barrel (green) in that network, with a quick readout: number of pipes, number of barrels, and total water in the pool. 📦 Items Irrigation Pipe — crafted from a Metal Pipe + Hammer + Screwdriver (4 per craft), or from a Clay Pipe Segment with no tools (1 per segment). One item; the shape (line / cross / corner / T) is chosen when you place it. ⚙️ Sandbox Options Enable Auto-Watering (on/off) Watering Interval (1–60 in-game minutes, default 10) Watering Radius (0–10 tiles; 0 = the pipe’s own tile) Smart Pipes (fill to optimal vs fixed small amount) Smart Pipes Max Fill (per cycle) Shared Water Pool (on/off) Enable Fertigation (on/off, default on) Fertigation Quality (simulated Farming skill 0–10 — higher = better chance of a yield bonus) Doses per Fertilizer/Compost bag (how many plants one poured bag fertilizes) 📋 Requirements & Notes Project Zomboid Build 42. No other mods required. Works with vanilla rain collectors (not lakes, rivers, wells or blue barrels). Safe to add to an existing save — you’ll find the new items in areas you explore after installing. As with any mod, test on a spare save first; I’m not responsible for conflicts. 🌍 Translations 18 native languages: EN, FR, DE, ES, IT, PT, PT-BR, NL, RU, UA, CN, CH, JP, KO, AR, TH, PL, TR. Others fall back to English — contributions welcome via the comments. 🙏 Credits Thanks to aeoris2000 for giving me the idea to do this port to B42. Irrigation Pipes / Cluster Barrels — the Build 42 implementation whose code was adapted (placement, network, watering). Irrigation Pipes FIX! by Si’rrakx — pipe sprites reused. Huge thanks to all of them. If you’re one of the original authors and want a change to the credits, reach out on the Discord. 📜 License Created by Plysken for Build 42, based on the mods credited above. You’re welcome to reuse, port, translate or build on this mod — just keep a credit and, ideally, drop by the Discord so we can stay in touch. Built to be shared, not locked down. description: 🚰 Water Pipes Bring real plumbing to Knox County. Project Zomboid lets you hoard water in barrels and pray for rain — but never move it where you need it. Water Pipes changes that: lay a real pipe network through your base and let water (and other liquids) flow exactly where you want it. 🔧 What you can do 🧩 Build a pipe network across floors and walls — pipes snap together into straights, corners, junctions and crossings. Go vertical: run pipes up walls so rooftop rain collectors feed the kitchen below. 💧 Share your water. Barrels and rain collectors join the network as one shared supply. 🚰 Plumb your fixtures. Sinks, showers, toilets and even washing machines pull straight from your network — no more hauling water bottles. 🧱 Hide your plumbing. Concealed pipes work exactly like normal ones but are invisible once placed. Built with a bucket of cement, revealed any time with Show pipe network. ⛽ Pump any liquid. Pipe petrol to your generator and keep it topped up automatically; your taps serve whatever the network holds (tap water only comes out clean if it has been purified first — with the default Realistic Purification setting, dirty water stays dirty until it passes a purifier). 🔀 Direct the flow with Fluid Routers — one-way valves the water flows through: in through the green band (IN), out through the red band (OUT), never back, capped at the pressure ceiling you set. Put a vessel on the router's tile and the two sides exchange only through it — that is how the purifier works. Rotate with R to aim the red end. 🧪 Purify tainted water with the Electric Water Purifier — a powered tank that turns dirty water clean as it flows through. ⛏️ Pull water from wherever it is. An Electric Water Pump beside a well or on a river bank feeds your network non-stop: wells give clean water, rivers give dirty water for the purifier. It sucks from a couple of floors down at most, so place it low. Right-click it to switch it on or off and read its power, source and pressure. 🌊 Pressure matters. Height, distance and pumps decide what reaches each tap; chained pumps add up, and a Pressure Gauge reads any point. The sandbox also offers a Simple and an Off mode. 🌱 Irrigate your crops. A Drip Emitter waters its own tile and barely sips; a Sprinkler blankets its 3x3 but needs pump pressure, pays for all nine tiles whether or not anything grows, and is loud. Both spend water whenever they run — pick your trade. Mind the pressure: too much bursts a drip (the sprinkler shrugs it off) — keep pumps off the drip line or cap it with a router, and patch a burst one with duct tape (right-click → Repair). 🚒 Tap the town water. Open a fire hydrant with a wrench for clean, pressurised water until the day the mains is cut — and its gush waters any crops in its own 3x3. ⏳ Water goes stale. Standing water turns contaminated over time and rain spoils uncovered water — keep it moving or purify it. Fully tunable, and optional. 🧰 How to use it 🔧 Grab a Pipe Wrench and some Pipes. The Pump and Purifier also need welding gear (blowtorch and rods) plus some Electricity and Metal Welding skill; the emitters need a little Farming. 🏗️ Build menu → Piping category. Floor pipes route the network; the vertical pipe climbs between floors. 🔗 A pipe on the same tile as a barrel, rain collector or sink hooks it into the network. 🪛 With the wrench in hand, plumb a sink or connect a generator from its right-click menu. 🔍 Right-click any pipe → Show pipe network lights it all up: pipes red, sources green, taps and generators blue. ♻️ Dismantle pipes to recover your materials. 🧪 Electric Water Purifier ⚡ Build the 2x2 tank on a Fluid Router. While powered it pulls tainted water in through the router's green (IN) side and sends clean water out the red (OUT) side. 🪣 Runs on a charcoal-and-cloth filter that wears with use: right-click → Repair filter with charcoal and ripped sheets. Wear is tunable (or off) in sandbox options. 📊 Right-click → Open Purifier to read it live: levels, power, filtering rate and filter condition. 💡 Tips from the plumber 🏺 Give your water somewhere to live. Pumps push water IN, but barrels, amphoras and tanks HOLD it. Don't pipe a river pump straight into a sink — put a container or two on the line and let the taps drink from those. 🧪 River water arrives dirty. Purify it before it reaches the kitchen, or keep the dirty line for the crops — they don't mind. 🔀 Zone big bases with Fluid Routers. Each side of a router is its own network, computed on its own — a huge base split into zones costs the game the same as several small ones, so plumbing stays smooth as you expand. ✅ Good to know 👥 Multiplayer ready · 🌍 English, Spanish and Simplified Chinese · 🧱 Designed for Build 42. 🧩 Tested with other mods 🛁 Take A Bath And Shower — full integration: its bathtubs and showers plumb into the network like any vanilla fixture. Tried another mod alongside? Tell me in the comments and I'll add it here. 🤝 Collaborations 🎨 Tileset and sprite art by aariak_einherjer — Steam · ArtStation. 🇨🇳 Simplified Chinese by rakkasumi. Thank you both! If you draw, translate or have ideas worth trying, get in touch right here — there is still room. ⚠️ Before you remove the mod Like most Build 42 buildable mods, removing this from an existing save can trigger a "WorldDictionary" load error. Fixable — follow this guide — and always back up your save before adding or removing mods. 🐞 Bugs & requests 💬 Report anything here: github.com/carthon/WaterPipesModPZ/issues ☕ Support the mod ❤️ Enjoying Water Pipes? You can buy me a coffee on Ko-fi: ko-fi.com/carthonrules — thank you! 🖥️ Server setup Workshop ID: 3739595559 Mod ID: waterpipes

description: Zombie camouflage BitBraven's camouflage mod always felt like a mechanic that belonged in the vanilla zombie apocalypse experience, and now it returns to Project Zomboid Build 42 in a much more immersive and balanced form. Grab your frying pan, smash a zombie's skull, and blend into the horde. How does it work? Right-click a zombie corpse and select "Use Camouflage". Your character will gather the zombie's entrails and cover themselves with them to conceal their scent and appearance. Once applied, the camouflage lasts for a limited time and makes it harder for zombies to identify you. However, the process is exhausting: your character will become slightly fatigued and nauseous—just as anyone would. Needless to say, they'll also be covered in blood and begin to walk like the undead. But be careful: if you get too close to them, they'll start to suspect that you're not one of their own. And if you stay there for too long or one of them manages to touch you, they'll quickly realize there's fresh meat hiding beneath those rotten guts! New Features 💠 You now walk like the undead while camouflaged. A configurable hotkey can be assigned in the mod options to toggle this animation. 💠 Reworked zombie detection system: Zombies no longer stand around staring blankly at the player. They now build suspicion over time when you stay too close to them. Their behavior feels much more natural and immersive, simulating them tracking the player's scent. For players who prefer the original behavior, it can be restored through the Sandbox options. 💠 New sniffing animation: Zombies will sniff the player when they start becoming suspicious. Walk away when you see it. 💠 Camouflage can deteriorate if you run or climb wallks within a zombie's line of sight. These actions attract too much attention and reduce the effectiveness of your disguise. Needless to say, zombies don't talk. 💠 You can remove the camouflage by washing your clothes or yourself. 💠 Now compatible with mods like Rain Cleans Blood. F.A.Q. Does it work in multiplayer? 🛑 Use in multiplayer at your own risk. This update is for SP. Does it work with existing saves? Absolutely! Is the mod compatible with [...]? This mod shouldn't have any incompatibilities with other mods, but if you find one, please let me know. 🔴 If you are using the mod Starving Zombies and the zombies feel too aggresive, disable the Sandbox option "Zombies can smell player". So Camouflage remains a useful tool for confusing zombies, but it no longer guarantees complete safety. If you stay too close to them or perform suspicious actions, they'll eventually figure out that you're still alive. Use it wisely... or end up becoming part of the horde. Recommended mods If you want blood to fade when it rains, you would use a mod like this one, which will affect your camouflage! Credits Originally developed by BitBraven. description: Companion Dogs [ALPHA] Adopt a stray. Feed it, earn its trust, and you end up with a dog that follows you around, warns you about things you cannot see and throws itself at zombies for you. It also has to eat every day, and it can die. After that come the German Shepherd for fighting, the Golden Retriever for hunting, the Husky for hauling cargo through the cold, and the Border Collie for the farm. They breed and raise puppies too. Known issue: dog looks crumpled / has no texture Fix: enable Companion Dogs in the main-menu Mods list, then fully restart the game (quit to desktop) before loading your save. Co-op hosts must do the same and restart the server. Details & reports: this discussion thread. Removing the mod? Read first Zomboid stores every animal of a whole map region in one file. Remove the mod (or one breed addon) from a save that still has dogs and the game hits a dog it cannot read, gives up on the rest of that file and rebuilds the region -- your livestock goes with it. Kill your dogs and save before uninstalling. If animals already vanished, reinstall the mod before saving again and they most likely come back. >> Full removal guide << What your dog does Find strays on the street and waiting inside houses, pet shops, vet clinics and barns Inspect a stray before you commit: breed, sex, age and traits up front Tame a stray with food and earn its loyalty Follow, Stay and Guard, from a radial or the right-click menu Early warning for zombies you cannot see Combat that knocks zombies down and buys you time Assisted hunting, and a wider foraging Search Mode Saddlebags for extra cargo, with the weight truly off you Livestock care that keeps your herd calm while you are away Needs, loyalty and a companion moodle per breed Five skills with XP and inborn trait genes Obedience tricks: walk to a tile, distract, sniff out an item, fetch it Breeding and puppies, with pedigree and cross-breed mutts Rides with you in any vehicle A management window for all of it >> Details in the wiki << The catch Barking warns you and pulls zombies in. A stressed or starving dog barks whether you want it to or not. An untrained dog will sometimes just ignore you, and then it stays deaf for a couple of seconds before it will take an order again. description: Signature Weapons Turn your favorite weapon into a legendary artifact! The Signature Weapons mod allows survivors to claim a weapon as their own, track its kills, and watch it grow in power the longer they survive. Key Features Claim Your Arsenal: You can claim up to 2 signature weapons per account. Custom Naming: Give your weapon a custom name (using letters, numbers, and spaces) via the right-click context menu. The name will proudly display in brackets, such as [Old Reliable]. Infinite Durability: Your signature weapon will never break in your hands. Striking a zombie or swinging the weapon instantly restores its condition to maximum. Psychological Comfort: Holding your trusted weapon calms your nerves. Wielding a signature weapon grants a passive stress reduction and a panic recovery bonus that scales with your kill count, capping at a 25% recovery bonus at 12,500 kills. Strict Anti-Theft: Your weapon is soulbound to you. Non-owners are completely blocked from moving, dragging, or picking up your claimed weapon from the world or containers. (Note: Server staff such as admins and moderators bypass this restriction.) Custom Tooltips: Hovering over a weapon reveals a custom interface detailing the owner's name, the current number of zombies slain, and total legacy kills. NEW: Added an experience bar to the tooltip. Weapon Evolution & Damage Scaling As you slay the undead, your weapon levels up. description: The Trample Steam from Call of Duty: Black Ops 2 zombies, rebuilt for Project Zomboid Build 42(Backported to B41). An engine powered spring-loaded floor trap you weld together and place on a tile. Anything that steps on it gets launched. Zombies ragdoll, land, and die. The board flings its victim, ratchets itself down, dings, and waits for the next one. By default, this is intended for use in Singleplayer / Co-Op multiplayer as a zombie/animal trap, but can be adjusted to work and be balanced in PvP servers, a method of travel(chaining), simple zombie deterrence, or many other usage scenarios with sandbox settings. It should be lightweight enough to allow for several dozen to be simultaneously deployed. (Placing trap is different from deploying, placing does nothing but spawn the static model on the ground and does not allow the trap to work) The Trap Craft it with welding gear and scrap (Requires skills: Mechanics 3, Welding 3, Electrical 2). The recipe comes from a magazine, "How to Use: Trample Steam", which spawns about as rarely as the generator manual. Engineers and Welders know it from the start. Deploying one requires Mechanics 2, a technical occupation(Mechanic, Engineer, Electrician or Welder), or having read the magazine. Both crafting recipe and deployment have sandbox toggles if you just want to fling zombies. Click-to-place deployment with a live preview. It faces you by default; press R to rotate or click and drag to aim the launch direction. Launches use the same hit reaction as getting run over by a car, ragdolls and all. Multiple zombies on the pad go flying together on a single charge. It wears out. Each launch costs a charge, and a worn trap can jam. Repair broken ones with welding rods, or reinforce a working trap with extra sheet metal for a much bigger charge pool. Pack it up and redeploy it anywhere. It remembers its wear, fuel, upgrades, and kill count. Power Runs on gasoline, generator/grid power, both, or nothing at all, your choice in sandbox (default: both, preferring grid and saving its gas). Gas traps deploy with an empty tank and sip about one tank per week; refuel from any container holding gasoline. When a trap loses power it fires itself dry and sits with the board stuck up until the power comes back, then re-deploys on its own. It's possible to siphon a trap's stored gasoline back into a gas can. Noise The launch bang, the ready ding, and the idle hum are real noise that zombies investigate. Left alone, a trample steam baits its own victims. Sabotage Using a screwdriver and Electrical 2 you can try to jam an enemy trap - success quietly breaks it, a botched attempt makes a loud clank that draws zombies, and higher Electrical skill improves the odds. Camouflage Wrap a trap in ripped sheets in one of five colors (woodland green, dead-grass olive, mud brown, road grey, winter white). Each color fully repaints the trap with a blotch camo pattern so it genuinely blends into grass, dead lawns, mud, pavement or snow, and its engine is muffled, so no more idle hum. Survives pack-up; removing the wrap is free. Useful for genuinely catching players off guard in PvP. Multiplayer Built for MP: deployment, state, animations, sounds, and launches all sync, with the server validating everything. One engine note: Project Zomboid disables ragdoll physics in multiplayer, so MP uses the regular death animations. Ragdoll also disabled in B41, since that engine feature doesn't exist. Sandbox Options Presets A one-click Settings preset at the top of the sandbox page switches the whole trap between play styles: Custom, Co-op, Casual, and PvP. Sandbox options Notes Built for Build 42, made on 42.19. Backported to B41, All art is original, rendered from my own model. Not ripped from inspiration game. Safe to add to an existing save. Updating the mod will not break already-deployed traps. Sounds are not mine, pulled from inspiration game. Can be replaced by changing .ogg files Permissions All code and art in this mod are original and remain the property of the author. All rights reserved. Do not reupload, repackage, modify, or reuse any part of it without written permission. This mod can only be added to and extended with the permission of the original creator. description: if you enjoy this mod, please consider supporting it... :) 🔥 FRONT PAGE FEATURED! A huge thanks to the community for pushing Zombie Camouflage - Build 42 into the Most Popular list! PSA: for more information on updates, please check the changelog. About This Mod Cover yourself in the blood of the dead and walk right past them. This is the Build 42 version of "Zombie Camouflage", rebuilt from the ground up for B42's new systems while keeping the spirit of the original intact. This is based on my version of "Zombie Camouflage", its a full Build 42 port from my build 41 version with alot of improvements and reworks. If you still play the build 41, i got you covered: Zombie Camouflage - Edited - B41 Only! TL;DR — What's new in the Build 42 version Rebuilt for Build 42 (new mod folder structure, JSON translations, updated APIs). Completely reworked zombie reaction — no more frozen "statue" zombies. The horde wanders and shambles around naturally and simply ignores you while you're covered. Level-based recognition distance: the higher your camouflage, the closer you can get before a zombie makes you out. The moodle icon is now color-graded (amber -> yellow -> lime -> green) and updates live, so a glance tells you how covered you are. Strip off a bloodied piece of clothing and the icon visibly steps down a level to warn you you're losing cover — instead of vanishing all at once. You can now drag the icon anywhere on screen, like other HUD windows (right-click it to reset). Reworked, realistic wear-off: wash your body, wash/lose the bloody clothes, or get caught in the rain. The nausea from wearing corpse blood is now mild and hard-capped — it can NOT make you seriously ill, get you infected, or kill you. Huge list of supported cutting tools (most knives, axes, cleavers, machetes, saws, spears and improvised blades). How to use Grab any supported cutting tool (a kitchen knife, hunting knife, cleaver, axe, machete... see the list below). Right-click a fresh corpse on the ground and choose "Cover Yourself with Corpse Blood". Your character smears the gore over themselves — you're now camouflaged. Walk (or crouch-walk) calmly among the dead. Keep your distance and you'll pass right by them. Stay calm. Standing still, walking, aiming and sneaking keep you hidden. Running, sprinting or firing a gun blows your cover and alerts everything nearby. Multiplayer 1. in the game main screen go to HOST > manage settings > Edit Selected Settings > Choose Mods.. 2.the Choose Mods option is in the down part of your screen right in the middle of it. 3. there you select the mod and hit ACCEPT, then hit NEXT. 4. in the next screen, before you hit SAVE, you have to select the mod in the Steam Workshop tab and make sure it also appears on the "Mods" tab that is right under the Steam Workshop tab. 5. hit SAVE and you're good to go. uncheck the new stealth system check box in the Zombie tab.⚠️ Follow every step. If you have done everything correctly, then you're all set and good to go. Camouflage levels There are four levels, shown by the color of the moodle icon. Each time you cover yourself you go up roughly one level (about four applications to max it out). The higher the level, the closer you can get to a zombie before that zombie recognizes you: Level 1 — amber: keep a wide berth (~3.5 tiles). Level 2 — yellow: you can get noticeably closer (~2.6 tiles). Level 3 — lime: close quarters (~1.8 tiles). Level 4 — green: practically shoulder-to-shoulder (~1.1 tiles) — you can crouch and weave right through a crowd. Higher levels also make you look more drenched in blood and make zombies lose interest faster after you've made noise. How zombies react While you're covered, quiet, and no zombie is point-blank, the dead wander and roam normally and just don't come for you — no freezing, no unnatural standing around. Let a zombie get closer than your level allows and that one recognizes you and locks on. Put distance back between you (or put it down) and your cover settles back in. Run, sprint or fire a weapon and you're exposed — the area stays alerted for a short while even after you stop. How the disguise wears off Strip the bloody clothes — peel off soaked pieces and the level (and icon color) steps down as a warning; take them all off and it's gone. Wash your body at a sink, river or bath and the disguise comes off completely. Rain and wet clothing gradually wear it down over time. When you're dry and keep your bloodied clothes on, the cover lasts a good long while. description: Working, map-wide text messaging network for Project Zomboid, built for co-op. Find a pager, get your own number, and stay in touch with your group from anywhere on the map. Designed around an immersive communication ladder: use proximity voice chat up close, walkie-talkies at medium range, and pagers for everything beyond that. The pager is your long-range tier. Intended when global text chat is off and not in an external voice call. Other pager mods are depreciated, and the main issue with using in game voice chat among a group of friends is the long distance barrier where you simply cannot contact someone. This bridges that gap, while still being time period accurate. Additionally, this is a great option for in game Server Browser Discovery / PvPvE servers. If you are using this in a large scale server feel free to directly work with me for additional features, and please consider supporting my development, as well as anyone else that is able! Core Every pager has a unique number (XXX-XXXX). Send and receive short text pages to any number, anywhere on the map. Offline delivery: pages queue on the server and arrive the moment the recipient reconnects. Messages live on the physical pager, so they travel with the device. Talk to your group Contacts - save names to numbers and reply with one click. Channels / Groups - define a group of numbers and page the whole team at once. Broadcast - page every pager on the network (toggleable). SOS beacon - emergency broadcast that pages everyone and attaches your location. Quick pages - fire preset phrases ("On my way", "Need backup!", "All clear"...) straight from the right-click menu, no typing. Location & awareness Optionally attach your coordinates to a page; the recipient sees the position plus distance and a compass bearing (e.g. ~340t NE). Sharing is your choice per server: Off, ask-per-page, or always on. An SOS still shares location unless it's fully off. Share my number nearby adds you to nearby players' contacts automatically for first meet-ups. Say my number makes your character read it out loud for voice chat. Batteries Pagers run on a battery that lasts about three in-game months (tunable in sandbox). When it dies the pager goes quiet until you Replace battery from the right-click menu using an ordinary Battery. Remaining charge shows on the screen as BAT %. PvPvE Faction scoping - optionally stop rival factions from paging (or eavesdropping on) each other. Factionless players are never cut off. Block list - block a number and its pages never reach you. Block a griefer straight from your inbox. Anti-spam - optional per-player send cooldown for busy servers. Quality of life Holster the pager in the walkie-talkie belt slot. Rebindable hotkey (default P) opens the pager you're carrying and auto-activates a fresh one in a single press. Beep + on-screen message preview when a page arrives, an unread badge on the item, and a per-pager mute / Do-Not-Disturb. Read receipts, so you know your page was actually seen. Difficulty/Realism Presets: Custom, Convenient, Almost Realistic, and Ultra Realistic. Pager Tower System(Only enabled in Ultra Realistic) Craftable relay tower — requires Electrical 5 and is learned only from the Pager Tower Schematics magazine, which only appears in loot when a tower is actually needed(receive only pagers and/or required for signal). Multiple towers, each its own network node with an incrementing number (000-0001, 000-0002), its own coverage circle, inbox, and console. Towers auto-add as a contact to any pager that comes within range. Rename a tower at the tower — the new name syncs everywhere. Power source option: Grid or Generator / Generator only / None. Tower comms option: send-and-receive or send-only. Per-player tower limit (0 = unlimited; admins exempt). Sandbox options Multiplayer Built for co-op first: all routing is server-authoritative - number allocation, delivery, offline queueing, signal range and faction checks all live on the host. Notes Built for Build 42; backported to Build 41. Uses the base game's Pager item, so it fits in naturally and turns up in normal electronics loot. Electricians can also craft one. Safe to add to an existing save. Permissions All code, UI, networking and sandbox logic in this mod are original. The poster art is original; the inventory icon and world model are derived from the base game's vanilla pager. Please ask before reuploading, repackaging or reusing parts of it. description: Claimable Outposts Claimable Outposts adds useful locations across the world that can be cleared, powered, claimed, supplied, and defended. Instead of looting a place once and leaving forever, this mod gives you a reason to secure important spots and return to them later. A claimed outpost can become part of your survival route, but it will still need attention if you want to keep it running. How It Works Find an outpost, clear the area, bring power back with a working generator, and make sure there is a crate nearby for supplies. Once everything is ready, you can claim the outpost from the right-click menu. After claiming it, the outpost becomes active and can generate loot over time depending on what kind of location it is. Outpost Types Different outposts are focused on different survival needs: Food locations can help with food supplies. Fuel locations can support fuel-related survival. Medical locations can provide medical supplies. Ammo and weapon locations can help with combat supplies. Keeping an Outpost Active An outpost is not just a free loot spot. It needs power, a supply crate, and a safe area around it. If the generator runs out of fuel, the crate is missing, or the area becomes dangerous, the outpost may stop working until you fix the problem. Infestations Claimed outposts can attract trouble over time. Nearby locations may become infected and will need to be cleared. If you ignore these problems, the danger around the outpost can grow and eventually lead to bigger attacks. Horde Attacks Outposts can be attacked by zombie hordes. When trouble is coming, nearby players will be warned. The outpost owner can also receive a warning even when away from the area, as long as they are online. If a horde reaches the outpost, you will need to defend it. If the defense fails, the outpost can be lost or disabled until you deal with the situation. Bandits V2 Compatibility Claimable Outposts now includes compatibility with the Bandits V2 mod. Bandits can now control their own outposts throughout the world. These locations may become dangerous enemy-controlled areas that survivors will need to approach carefully. A bandit outpost attack system is also currently being developed. In a future update, bandits will be able to organize attacks against player-controlled outposts. Please note that the bandit outpost attack system is still a work in progress and may change during development. Friendly outposts now support trading, supply deliveries, reputation, and radio support. You can buy and sell items using local vouchers, deliver requested supplies for rewards, and improve your reputation with friendly outposts. Higher reputation gives better trade discounts. If you have a working radio, you can use the Radio Network to request friendly support when one of your claimed outposts is under attack. World Map Support Outposts are marked on the world map with simple icons, making them easier to find and plan around. Each icon matches the general type of outpost, so you can quickly tell what kind of location you are looking at. Singleplayer and Multiplayer The mod works in both singleplayer and multiplayer. In singleplayer, outposts can still be claimed, maintained, supplied, and attacked. In multiplayer, players can use outposts as shared survival objectives, supply points, or dangerous places worth fighting over. Localization Supported languages: English Turkish Spanish Russian German Simplified Chinese Summary Claimable Outposts is built for long-term survival. It gives you useful places to secure, but those places are not permanently safe. You will need to maintain them, clear nearby threats, defend them when the dead come knocking, and watch out for bandit-controlled outposts. Forge a grenade shell, build the fuze assembly, weld yourself a striker lever, then assemble everything together with gunpowder into a working Mk2, M26 or M67 grenade. Producing a grenade is not a trivial task, so the recipes require very high skills to produce and are additionally locked behind a new manual: "TM 9-1300-214: Military Explosives" - look for it where you would expect to find such a thing and maybe as contraband somewhere? If you're playing with the "Delayed Fuse" sandbox option enabled: grenades that don't detonate on impact can now bounce once or twice before coming to rest and arming for real. The bounce depends on the actual calculated throw energy. Heavier throws bounce further, heavier grenades bounce less, and it roughly follows the direction you threw it in - with a little natural randomness so it doesn't look robotic. Also lowered the minimum for the "Loot Multiplier" sandbox option from 0.1 to 0.01, for anyone who wants grenades to be even rarer than before. Also fixed a crash that could happen when an explosion needed to shatter several nearby windows at once, and a visual bug where a bounced grenade would snap to the center of its tile instead of staying exactly where it landed. --- Update 2.0 - This was a big one and a LOT of work, but I think you will like it. --- On squares that are visible to the player but invisible to the character the aim marker turns red. I don't hard-block the throw, you can still throw at a red marker if you really want to. Just know you're throwing blind at that point: you don't actually have eyes on what's there, so the grenade might not land where you expect - and if you're standing close to whatever's blocking your view, that could get dangerous real fast. Added a sandbox option to disable instant-exploding grenades. You can decide if you want instant explosions or more realistic behaviour. Set the "Delayed Fuse" option to true, and decide how long the grenade sits armed after landing before it explodes. Threw the grenade against a wall by accident? ... You now have some time to escape your doom :D If a delayed-fuse grenade gets stuck against a wall above ground level, it now falls down to the real floor below. Completely reworked how the game figures out where you're actually aiming. Changed fence/obstacle recognition from a blacklist to a sprite based getLastPicked. What this means: prior to today's change, the mod checked passability using a square collision check, then checked the tile, and if it was a fence, let the grenade pass if it had enough ballistic height. This turned out to be very unreliable - there are often small objects near fences, and other things I can't fully explain, that incorrectly triggered "obstacle" detection. I've gone further and thrown that whole approach out. Targeting now uses the exact same depth-correct picking the game itself uses to highlight objects under your cursor. On top of that, the precise height on whatever you're aiming at is now taken into account too - aim partway up a wall and the grenade actually targets that exact spot. With targeting this precise I added window demolishon - a grenade punches straight through glass without losing momentum, but shatters it on the way through. Explosions now also shatter nearby windows in a radius around the blast (plus the floor above and below) - on buildings and on vehicles alike. Also reworked throwing down from height - the drop trajectory now properly accounts for the extra range the fall itself gives you, so tossing a grenade off a rooftop actually reaches further than a flat throw would. This is a much safer approach to a problem the game engine gives me no clean way to solve 100% - and at least now you can safely throw grenades over fences and even low buildings, and through windows! The system is not perfect by any means. I am trying to calculate a 3D trajectory using 2D blocking sprites. This is a faulty system by default. Throwing straight up onto a higher floor especially can still land a bit off. But I will try to improve it as I go along. And here I need your help!!! Please test the grenades! Throw them into walls, buildings, doors, windows, up onto roofs, anything you like. If you think something should have stopped the grenade and it didn't (or the other way around), report it to me with as much detail as possible - a description of the obstacle and its location, if you can. With your help, I'll keep tightening the ballistics and make them as realistic as possible. I realize that in their current state (not craftable), grenades are a rare and valuable commodity. To help with testing, I've added a debug-spawn key that doesn't require switching to full debug mode: hold Shift + Numpad "+" (rebindable in Mod Options) to spawn a single flashbang directly into your inventory, whenever you want to do some trajectory testing. --- My other mods Nihontō - Authentic Katana Overhaul Weapons of the Orient - Eastern Martial Arsenal Accelerated Leather Processing Food Drying Functional Car Wash Enjoy my mods? description: The Best Lockpicking [B42.20+] A complete lockpicking overhaul for Project Zomboid Build 42.20. Good for servers that want faster gameplay. Controls: A / D to adjust tension — Mouse to move the pick Crowbar Unlocking Force open locked doors and vehicle doors. description: Zombies can trip. Pack a horde behind you and they start tripping over each other. Now they stumble when they bump, lose their footing randomly, and pile up over other tripped bodies. The faster they are, the harder they fall. Good for sprinter runs to add a more natural balance to it. Intended to drop in to any save, including regular zombies. Rebuilt from the ground up for Build 42, with extra QOL, ragdolls, full multiplayer support and far more control. Backported to B41. Compatible with "Skully's Zombie Collision" and "Zombies Trippin'", which I recommend as they add to the experience. How it works Bump trips: a moving zombie that touches another while grouped up can lose its footing, and the denser the horde, the more of them go down. Random trips: even with a clear path, a moving zombie can roll to trip on its own, on a randomised cooldown. Pile-ups: a zombie that walks onto another already sprawled on the ground trips over it, so one fall cascades into a dogpile. Trip over corpses: bodies on the ground become real obstacles and corpse piles trip the horde. Speed: sprinters, fast shamblers and shamblers each have their own trip chances, so you can make runners clumsy without touching slow hordes. Radgolls: For singleplayer in B42, ragdolls are automatically enabled Features & Improvements over original Zombies can trip anytime, not just when they see you Zombies can trip while actively lunging Zombies can bump each other in groups, causing them to trip Zombies can pile up in a chain reaction from other zombies that tripped Makes use of new ragdolls system When running into a zombie, they are also likely to trip now too Standalone, no dependencies Multiplayer ready: all logic runs on synced server authority Highly configurable. Safe to add or remove mid-save. Compatible with various NPC mods such as Bandits. Sandbox options(default) Please note that defining how often a trip occurs is different from what percent of trips are going to be ragdolls! Ensure 'Use Physics Hit Reactions' is on in game for ragdolls(it's on by default) I don't recommend using "Injured Zombies Stumble" at the same time as you'll make zombies trip significantly more and lose most ragdoll support. This mod is an all-encompassing gameplay feature and is designed as a replacement. B42 remaster by turnip. Original by Monkey: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2856413047 Workshop ID: 3746603021 Mod ID: TrippingZombies

description: Bundle Up Ready for B42.20!! Meant to organize our excessive amounts of stuff! Put 99 Nails in a box and now half your base is missing from server chunk rot? No More! Item weights for each bundle/box can be adjusted in the Sandbox Options menu if the defaults don't suit your game :D What's New Stacks go one level deeper. Cartons now pack into Cases, so a hoard that used to bottom out at "a shelf of cartons" collapses one more time. Food Cases (4 cartons): all 166 food cartons, dry goods and produce alike. That's 48 items in a single slot. Magazine Cartons (12 boxes) & Cases (4 cartons): your spare B-F, JS-14, M16, M1911, M1A and M9 mags, up to 240 per case. Carton of Caps (12 boxes): caps were the only ammo in the game that never got a carton. Now they have one. Everything you drop is finally visible. 565 of the mod's items had no world model and rendered as thin air when dropped on the ground. Every one of the 780 items now has one. Rope bundles look like rope bundles. Tied plank, sheet metal, pipe and bar bundles used to render as a single loose plank. They're now actual strapped bundles, and the 10-count ones look bigger than the 5-count ones. Perishable Timer: Food keeps spoiling while it's packed away, so a carton is storage, not a stasis pod - and that now holds however deep you stack it. Age carries all the way up and down the stack, so a case of cartons ticks exactly like a lone carton does, and a rotten carton can't be laundered into a fresh-looking case. Rotten food can't be packed in the first place, and the spoilage rate is adjustable in Sandbox Options - set it to 0% if you'd rather cartons preserve. Cartons you loot start their clock when the area first generates, same as loose food on the shelf next to them. Do note that fridges and freezers don't slow a carton down, and that anywhere you'd already explored before updating keeps its old cartons as they were. New loot: magazine cartons turn up in gun stores, army and SWAT storage at about a quarter the rate of the boxes, and cap cartons in the Wild West sheriff furniture that already carried the boxes. What's Inside This mod bundles, boxes, and bags up the clutter so your base (and your sanity) can breathe. A quick taste of what's covered: Bundles (5/10, rope or sheet rope): Planks, Sheet Metal, Iron Pipes, Iron Bars, Wire, Small Metal Sheets Boxes & Bags: Nails, Screws, Gold/Silver Scrap, Pens, Sack of Sacks, Jewelry Pouches Six-Packs: Ginger Ale, Blueberry, Bubblegum, Grape, Lime, Orange, Pineapple, Strawberry, Variety Pack Scrap Bags: Aluminum, Brass, Copper, Iron & Steel Scrap, Broken Glass, Wood Charcoal/Splinters, and more Parts Boxes: Iron & Steel Bars/Blocks/Chunks/Pieces, Circular Sawblade, Rake Head, and more Medical Boxes: Bandages (incl. Dirty), Painkillers, Sleeping Pills, Caffeine Pills, Alcohol Wipes, Disinfectant, and more Ammo (5/60/240): B-F, JS-14, M16, M1911, M1A and M9 magazines in Boxes, Cartons and Cases, plus a Carton of Caps. Note: vanilla already boxes and cartons loose rounds, so this rounds out your spare clips instead Seed Pouches (10): all 55 vanilla seed packet varieties, because your farming stash deserves the same treatment as your nail jar Books & Paperbacks (10): every genre in the game, plus Leatherbound editions and the Bible Magazines (10): every topic, old and new print runs, plus Crossword, Wordsearch, HottieZ, and TV Monthly Reading Material (10): Notebooks, Diaries, Journals, Newspapers (incl. the 4 named city papers), Comics, Catalogs, Phonebooks, Photo/Picture Books, RPG Manuals, Menus, and Loose Paper 166 Food Items & 84 Supply Items via Food Cartons and Supply Boxes from Balsamic Vinegar to Box of Batteries - and every food carton now packs again into a Case of four ...and many more!!! On the Way Alcohol Packs Gas Cans Engine Parts Coke (the blacksmithing kind) Clay Bricks In the UK, our online safety laws are all wonky right now, so we can't use Imgur to post pictures in descriptions. description: Version 1.7 deployed Drying Rack now has dedicated overlay art for berries, fruit and vegetables — previously all three showed the mushroom overlay as a placeholder while drying. Salt licks can now be harvested directly while placed in the world (right-click the installed salt lick → Harvest Salt Shavings). No need to pick it back up first anymore. Version 1.6 deployed Reworked salt lick harvesting: the shavings you hammer off a salt lick are no longer directly usable as salt (they were basically raw metal-laced rock dust before, which never made sense). Now you dissolve the shavings in a pot of water, boil it into a raw brine, then filter it through either Cheesecloth (yields regular Salt) or a Respirator Filter (finer filtration, yields more Salt per batch). Makes it a proper multi-step process instead of "hit rock with hammer, get seasoning". Version 1.5 deployed Fixed dried meat/fish losing their real nutrition values (calories, carbs, fat, protein) after coming off the Drying Rack — they were falling back to generic placeholder numbers instead of reflecting what you actually put in. New: Wheat and Sunflower Heads can now be dried in the oven (Baking Tray), same as fruit/veg/berries/mushrooms. Baking Trays now correctly rename to show "Dried" once they're actually done, instead of permanently showing "Fresh" even after finishing. (Icons still don't change - this is impossible to do sadly) Added a recipe to harvest "drying salt" from salt licks. The resulting item can only be used in this mod's recipes and not for cooking. This is to help with the lack of table salt in Knox County. New sandbox option: Enable Salt Harvesting (on by default) — lets you disable salt lick harvesting if you do not want it easier. New sandbox option: Enable Oven Drying (on by default) — lets you disable the oven/Baking Tray drying path entirely, independent of the Drying Rack. If you thing oven drying is "too easy" you can now disable it. This mod started as a request from my subscriber herrhiskelig – and honestly, it's one of those ideas that made me think "why isn't this in the game already?" So here it is. The baking trays and skewers are custom modelled (fresh and dried variants for mushrooms, fruit, berries and now wheat/sunflower). Vegetables currently share the fruit tray/skewer look until dedicated art is made. The Drying Rack also has its own custom overlay art for mushrooms, meat, fish, berries, fruit and vegetables showing drying progress. Most dried food items themselves still use vanilla models and icons – this will be gradually improved. Features Dry wild mushrooms (all 7 generic variants + button mushroom) Dry berries (blackberries, blueberries, winter berries, holly berries, beauty berries and all wild variants) Dry fruits (apple, banana, cherry, grapefruit, grapes, lemon, lime, mango, orange, peach, pear, pineapple) Dry vegetables (tomato, bell pepper, carrots, onion, corn, radish, broccoli, cauliflower, kale, leek, eggplant, peas, daikon, edamame, spinach) Dry wheat and sunflower heads Salt and dry meat (bacon, chicken, turkey, mutton, pork, venison, beef, steak, frog meat, rodent and small bird meat) and fish (all vanilla fish species) – salting is a required first step before drying Salting meat and fish doubles their shelf-life, so you have a bit more time to reach your drying rack Drying rack support: dry mushrooms, berries, fruit, vegetables, salted meat and salted fish directly on a farm drying rack, no oven or tray needed (takes longer than the oven method) Dried Tomatoes and Bell Peppers can be processed with vanilla's Collect Seeds recipe to get seeds Dried food lasts indefinitely All item properties are preserved when drying: poison status, nutrition, age and remaining food amount How to use Oven method: place mushrooms, berries, fruit or vegetables on a baking tray (or on a skewer), put it in the oven, turn it on, and wait for the food to dry Drying rack method: place any of the above directly on a farm drying rack and wait – slower, but needs no oven, tray or fuel Meat and fish need to be salted first (Salt Meat and Fish recipe) before they can be dried Planned for future description: TwisTonFire - WANTED Ever searched through piles of containers, corpses, bags, shelves or dropped loot just to find one specific item? TwisTonFire - WANTED lets you create your own personal wanted list of items. If one of those items exists nearby, the mod highlights the matching container, corpse or dropped item with an outline. This makes looting faster, cleaner, and much less annoying — especially when you are looking for rare items, tools, magazines, weapons, clothing, or anything else you do not want to miss. Why is this useful? Project Zomboid can have a lot of loot in many different places. Sometimes the item you need is hidden inside: A normal container A corpse A backpack on the ground A wallet inside another container A nested container inside another item WANTED helps you find the item without opening and checking every single container manually. Main Features Create your own WANTED list: Add any item type you want to search for. Nearby scanner: The mod scans loaded tiles around your character. Outline highlights: Matching loot locations are highlighted clearly. Nested container support: Items inside bags, wallets, backpacks, and other containers can still be found. Corpse support: Perfect for checking large piles of corpses after fights. Dropped item support: Items lying on the floor can be highlighted too. Inventory context menu: Add or remove selected items directly from the inventory right-click menu. Custom outline color: Change the WANTED outline color in Mod Options. Custom UI hotkey: Open or close the WANTED UI with a configurable keybind. Adjustable radius: Set how far around your character the scanner should search. Adjustable refresh interval: Control how often WANTED updates its search. Complete disable option: Fully disable the scanner, UI, highlights, and context menu from Mod Options. Scanner Modes You can choose how WANTED should scan the world. Default: Normal scanner. Includes containers, corpses, floor items and nested containers. Corpse Only: Only scans corpses, including nested containers inside corpse inventories. Corpse and Floor Only: Scans corpses and dropped floor items, including dropped bags with nested containers. Fixed world containers such as shelves, cupboards, crates, and counters are ignored. This is useful if you only want help with corpse piles or floor loot without highlighting every fixed container in a building. WANTED UI The WANTED UI gives you a simple overview of: All available item types Your current WANTED list Search radius Refresh interval Current scanner status Current highlight count Loaded tiles scanned Last scan duration You can add or remove items directly in the UI. Your WANTED list is saved locally and persists between sessions. Default WANTED UI hotkey: KP_4 / Numpad 4 The keybind can be changed in: MAINMENU -> OPTIONS -> MOD OPTIONS Inventory Button WANTED adds a small toggle button to the inventory title area. This lets you quickly enable or disable the scanner without opening the full UI. If the scanner is disabled, current WANTED highlights are removed. Blacklist Compatibility WANTED includes compatibility logic for TwisTonFire - Blacklist. If Blacklist filtering is active, WANTED respects it. Items that would be hidden or filtered by Blacklist will not trigger WANTED highlights. This also applies to blacklist rules such as damaged clothing filters. Important: If TwisTonFire - Blacklist is loaded, Blacklist handles the shared inventory title button area. WANTED will integrate with that setup instead of replacing it. Clean UI Compatibility WANTED includes a dedicated Clean UI compatibility adjustment. The Clean UI compatibility file is only loaded when Clean UI is active. If you do not use Clean UI, the compatibility adjustment will not be loaded and has no effect on your game. Clean UI: No known incompatibilities. Performance Notes WANTED is designed to scan in small steps instead of checking everything at once. Default settings: Search radius: 15 tiles Refresh interval: 4 seconds You can lower or raise these values in the WANTED UI depending on your preference. Higher radius or faster refresh can increase scanner work. The default values are intended to be a good balance between usefulness and performance. Current Translations Traditional Chinese Simplified Chinese German Spanish French Japanese Korean Polish Portuguese (Brazil) Russian Turkish Ukrainian If you have suggestions for better translations, feel free to tell me! Compatibility Your support helps me keep going — thank you very much in advance! Workshop ID: 3747641501 Mod ID: twistwanted

description: Build Support: B42.12 to B42.20 — Build 42 only Moodle Effects Explained replaces vague vanilla moodle descriptions with clearer, effect-focused tooltips based on checked Project Zomboid Build 42 game files. The goal is simple: when a moodle appears, its tooltip should help you understand what it actually means for your character. Useful links FAQ, Questions and Bug Reports - report bugs, tooltip issues, compatibility problems or translation mistakes. Expanded Moodles - optional supported mod for the Expanded Moodles variant. Moodle Descriptions Expanded - Patch B42.15+ - separate compatibility patch for the original Moodle Descriptions Expanded mod. What this mod does Adds clearer descriptions to vanilla moodles. Explains practical effects such as movement penalties, combat penalties, panic, stress, tiredness, sickness, temperature, wetness, hunger, thirst, endurance, pain, windchill, noxious smell and more. Uses quantified descriptions where practical. Keeps the vanilla moodle system intact. Does not add new moodles. Does not change actual gameplay effects, moodle values, character stats, sandbox settings, recipes, items or save data. Included variants This Workshop item includes two separate mod variants. Moodle Effects Explained Use this version for vanilla moodles. Recommended for most players. Moodle Effects Explained - Expanded Moodles Use this version if you also play with Expanded Moodles. Includes extra notes for moodle effects modified or expanded by Expanded Moodles. Requires Expanded Moodles enabled and sorted before this variant in the mod load order. Important: choose only one variant Do not enable both Moodle Effects Explained variants at the same time. They edit the same vanilla moodle description keys, so only one should be active: Use Moodle Effects Explained without Expanded Moodles. Use Moodle Effects Explained - Expanded Moodles with Expanded Moodles. Mod Options Client-side Mod Options are included: Moodle tooltip font size: Small, Medium, Large. Default: Small. Fallback tooltip background shadow: enabled or disabled. Default: Enabled. Moodles in Lua compatibility This mod can work with or without Moodles in Lua. description: OVERVIEW This mod is a complete reimagining of how skill books work in Project Zomboid. Instead of simply fast-forwarding time while your character sits in silence, you can now actually read the books you find. Each book consists of 15 interactive pages. Because of this new system, the overall time it takes to finish a whole book is noticeably shorter than in vanilla. READING SPEED & TRAITS The time it takes to read each page is directly affected by your character's traits, but you can now fully customize these values in the Sandbox Settings! Fast Reader: 20 seconds per page (Default). Slow Reader: 35 seconds per page (Default). No reading traits: 27 seconds per page (Default). You can choose exactly how many seconds each page takes. If you want to freely flip through pages with no cooldown, just set the values to 0 in the Sandbox options. DARK MODE For those who prefer reading with a darker background, there is a toggle switch located in the bottom left corner of the reading interface. You can easily switch between the default light theme and a dark mode (black background with white text). The mod will remember your preference for the next books you open. LIMITATIONS & MULTIPLIER VALIDATION Due to limitations in how the base game registers reading to grant the XP bonus, there is an extra step required after you finish reading the book through our custom UI: Solo Play: When you finish reading all 15 pages and close the UI, the book will be marked as finished, but the XP multiplier won't appear immediately. To get your buff, just double-click the book in your inventory. This acts as a quick validation for the game to understand that the reading is over. Multiplayer: The process is similar, but requires a small trick. (Please note: Multiplayer was tested using the in-game "Host" local server option, not on a dedicated server). When you finish the 15 pages and close the UI, the book will be marked as finished. Double-click the book (your character will start the vanilla reading animation). Take a step or do any action to cancel this animation. Then, double-click the book again; they will start the animation once more. Wait a few seconds, you will receive your multiplier, and the game itself will end the reading animation on its own. MID-SAVE COMPATIBILITY It is completely safe to add this mod to an ongoing game (mid-save). You can enable it at any time without breaking your current run! However, it is recommended to make a backup of your save file if you are using any other mods that alter, modify, or interact with book functionalities to prevent any unexpected conflicts. description: READ BEFORE ANYTHING !! For Any Bug Report For Any Suggestion Before saying "it's not working", unsuscribe, resuscribe. Then post your bug on discord with you console file "C:\Users\you\Zomboid\console.txt" and you mod list "C:\Users\you\Zomboid\mods\default.txt" => Discord : https://discord.gg/vJay7GQ92B 🎒 Plysken Attachments Reborn Stop stuffing everything inside your pack. Strap your weapons, tools, flashlights and small containers to the OUTSIDE of your backpack — and see them hang there in 3D on your character. A clean, Build 42 revival of the classic attachments system. Singleplayer & Multiplayer — works in co-op and on dedicated servers. 🔧 How It Works 1. Wear the backpack — put a supported bag on your back. The mod only sees the bag worn there, not one held in your hands or in another slot. 2. Attach something — right-click the item in your inventory, open Attach, and pick a slot: Weapon, Utility Left, Left Side, Flashlight, Bedroll, Container and so on. The item stays in your inventory, but it now hangs on the outside of your pack, visible on your character. If the slot you want is missing from that list, the bag does not have it yet — that is step 3. 3. Sew on more slots — take the backpack off first (the game will say so if you forget), right-click it and pick Add Attachment Slot, then the slot you want. You need Leather Strips and Thread, plus a Needle and anything that cuts — scissors, shears, a multitool or a sharp knife — and Tailoring 2 by default. The new slot appears in the Attach list straight away. Remove Attachment Slot takes one back off. 4. Move it if it sits oddly — right-click the attached item and pick Adjust attachment position. The sliders move the spot on the bag while you watch, no reloading. That spot is shared by every item that goes to it, so nudging it moves them all. Your settings are saved outside your save file, so they follow you to every character and every world, and there are Reset buttons if you overshoot. Purely visual and local to you — nothing is sent to the server, so it is safe in multiplayer. 🎯 What You Can Attach Weapons — axes, machetes, knives and more, slung on the side of your pack. Tools — hammers, saws, crowbars and other everyday gear. Lights — flashlights and lamps, clipped on and ready. Small containers — pouches and small bags for a little extra organisation. Face masks — gas masks, respirators, dust, hockey and welding masks, hung on the side slots and visible on your back. Gloves & headwear — every pair of gloves in the game, plus balaclavas, shemaghs, head sacks, every hockey mask and the NBC masks: 37 pieces of headwear in all. Two honest notes: hard hats, army and firefighter helmets have no 3D model in the game files, so there is nothing to hang on a pack; and dyed gloves show in their base colour once attached. Bedrolls & tents — packed sleeping bags and tents ride on top of your pack, rolled and ready. Instruments — acoustic and electric guitars, bass, banjo and keytar, carried on the pack instead of your back. 🎒 Supported Backpacks Works on most vanilla backpacks — around 46 bags, from school bags and duffel bags to hiking packs and the ALICE pack. No other mods required. 🧩 Mod Compatibility PAR adds attachment slots to other mods' backpacks automatically — no setup, just have the mod active. The full list, kept up to date, is here: Supported bags and gear On modded bags, placement is approximate — each one borrows the layout of the closest vanilla bag. Use step 4 above to put it exactly where you want; it stays that way. Suggest a mod in the comments and I'll look at adding it. ⚙️ Sandbox Options Require Slot Cost (on/off) — whether sewing a new slot costs thread / needle and Tailoring skill, or is free. Slot Tailoring Level (0–10, default 2) — the Tailoring level needed to sew on a new attachment slot. Allow players to adjust attachment position (on/off, default on) — lets each player fine-tune where attached items sit. Purely visual and local to that player. Switch it off if you'd rather everyone saw the mod's default placement. 📋 Requirements & Notes Project Zomboid Build 42. No other mods required. Safe to add to an existing save. As with any mod, test on a spare save first; I'm not responsible for conflicts. 🌍 Translations Supports 28 languages: AR, CA, CH, CN, CS, DA, DE, EN, ES, ES-CL, ES-MX, FI, FR, HU, ID, IT, JP, KO, NL, NO, PL, PT, PT-BR, RO, RU, TH, TR, UA — every one of them fully translated, no more English fallback. Spanish was done by a player; the rest I did myself, so some wording may be a little stiff in places. If something reads oddly in your language, tell me the exact line and I'll fix it — and I'll credit you for it. 🙏 Credits A Build 42 revival by Plysken, built on the original Noir's Attachments by Noir / NockaOut — the mod this one is based on. Huge thanks to them. If you're the original author and want a change to the credits, reach out on the Discord. Spanish translation by Choko — a full pass over the Spanish files. It's the first language other than English that's genuinely complete, and it's entirely their work. 📜 License The original Noir's Attachments and its concept belong to their authors, credited above. The Build 42 port, all the reworks and the original code written for it are Plysken's own work. You're welcome to reuse, port, translate or build on this mod — just keep the credits and, ideally, drop by the Discord so we can stay in touch. Built to be shared, not locked down. Craft it with an electronics soldering iron and any screwdriver, plus a GS network floppy disk found in the world. No computer? The Home Computing Digest magazine teaches Get PC, which drops one straight into your inventory. With the reader and disk in your inventory, right-click the disk next to the computer to install (or open the mod's window: it tells you what's missing). Create a new network or join an existing one. Reader and disk aren't consumed: use them to install as many terminals as you want. Container management Mark zones from the Nodes tab: a whole room, an entire building, or draw by hand, tile by tile, exactly what you want included. Configure each container: categories, custom filters, fill priority and label. Search Works from Storage: find any item instantly, deposit or withdraw in bulk, with filters. 🛡️ Reliability and performance Reliable transfers: confirmed micro-batches, bounded retries, and optional progress on your character. Built for big networks: cached container opening and budgeted scans, no hitching when opening the terminal. Controlled auto-sort: only the network owner or admin can trigger it, with a clear summary of what moved and where. Deterministic routing: match, affinity and priority never contradict each other, category by category. Fast setup: copy/paste rules from one container to a whole zone, and set priority for an entire zone. Built-in diagnostics: structured logs and a server-to-client relay, so you can debug without chasing files by hand. 🎮 Game modes ✅ Singleplayer · ✅ Multiplayer (dedicated server and hosted games). ✅ Requirements NeatUI Framework. Our entire interface is built on it. 🧩 Official addons Extend the terminal by installing any of these separately or combined: 🧷 Other SiK mods 🌍 Languages [EN], [ES], [LATAM], [CH], [DE], [FR], [PTBR], [PL], [RU], [IT]. English is the fallback for any other game language. All translations besides English and Spanish use AI assistance and may have mistakes - let us know in a comment and we'll fix it, or contribute your own correction. 🐞 How to report a bug Restart the game after the Steam update. Enable Debug Mode in the sandbox options (in MP, the relay already brings server logs to your own console). Reproduce the bug and note what you expected versus what happened. Comment with the visible version, the steps, and your console.txt. We also appreciate ideas, likes and favorites. This mod was developed with AI assistance. If you disagree with that, nothing obligates you to install it.

Pack Mule (cattle) - carry your gear; stash items in the pack and they haul them for you. Real animal character Genetics matter - a companion's real genetic traits shape it. A Strong animal is a steady, sturdy companion; a Craven one is a nervous wreck near danger; a Blind one makes a poor lookout. The higher your Animal Handling, the more of an animal's quirks you can spot. Acceptance - see how much an animal genuinely accepts you, the game's own taming stat. Family & breeding - view lineage (mother, offspring, pregnancy, mating season) and a genetic pairing advisor that ranks your companions as mates so the offspring trend better. Care, safety & control No friendly fire - while a companion is actively following you, your own swings can't hurt or kill it, so you can fight zombies right beside it (toggleable). Soothe & care - calm a stressed companion to build a little extra bond. Assign roles - re-assign a companion's ability (turn a cow into a lookout, make any animal a Pack Mule). In-game Settings - tune protection, bonding thresholds, follow distance and more from the F9 window, no file editing.
