Press F8 (or the Herd button) and see the lot. Worst-off first - every animal in one list, sorted so whatever needs you is at the top. Your own companions are highlighted. Tells you what is actually wrong - sick or hurt, starving, dehydrated, stressed, ready to milk (or overdue), ready to shear, pregnant or in heat, genetic disorder, or sitting outside any zone. Read-only - it looks, it never touches. Nothing about your animals or companions is changed or saved by this page. This was previously a separate mod of mine called Animal Overview. It lives here now - if you were waiting for it, you already have it. Built right Easy on weak machines - config-first and lightweight; it does nothing at all when no animal is following you. Works with the vanilla animal system - it adds a relationship layer, it doesn't replace anything. Compatibility: Project Zomboid Build 42 - including the current stable/default branch (no beta opt-in needed). Single-player and co-op (host-and-play) are what I can vouch for. Companions used to be remembered only on the machine hosting the world, which meant that on a dedicated server each player's roster lived on their own client and was lost on reconnect - befriended animals appeared to vanish. That has been rebuilt: a companion's record now lives on the animal itself, so it is part of the world and saves server-side like anything else, and older saves are migrated across the first time each animal turns up. Run it on one at your own risk for now; if you do, I would genuinely like to hear how it goes on the Discord below. Use the in-game feedback to report bugs - every bug will be patched. description: PZ Pulse is a live status dashboard to keep track of your character's numerous details. Open it in any browser to have everything you need visible at a glance. 42.20 update If you had this mod on 42.19, your BOOKMARK needs updating. Old bookmarks will open but sit on "connecting" forever no matter what the game is doing. To fix it: in game, open the mod's options and click Copy dashboard URL, paste that into your browser, and re-bookmark. That's the whole fix - nothing is lost, and your saved layout is untouched. Choose panels Most panels are a somewhat faithful recreation of the in-game character window: Info - name, profession, traits, weight, favorite weapon, kills, time survived Skills/XP - every skill, level + progress to next, with level-up and XP flashes Health - overall + per-body-part damage and wound flags Protection - bite/scratch defense per body part from your clothing Body Temperature - core temp, body heat, and per-part skin temp / insulation Moodles & Needs - the full HUD moodle stack plus hunger, thirst, fatigue, stress, panic, etc. Extra panels beyond the character window: Weapon Condition - in-hand durability, sharpness, jam/ammo/chamber, attachments Clothing - per-garment condition, holes, and protection - a keep-or-toss view Quickload Slots - your equipment-hotbar loadout Encumbrance - carry load vs. capacity with the HeavyLoad tier Open Wounds - a worst-first triage list of active, untreated injuries Recent Recipes - a transient note when you learn something new Customizable Drag panels by their title bar to move them between columns or reorder them. Choose the column count and show/hide any panel. Per-panel font and icon sizes, animation toggles, and flash timings. Layout is saved in your browser, so your preferences stick. How to use Enable the mod and load a save. Open the mod's options screen and use the Copy dashboard URL button, then paste it into your browser's address bar and bookmark it. Drag the page to your second monitor (press F11 to fullscreen it). It updates in real time, the refresh rate is adjustable via the in-game mod options. This is NOT online The heartbeat / data lives in your Zomboid\Lua\PZ_Pulse folder. The webpage lives in your mod folder. It makes no network connections. It contacts no servers. Can I share it to my phone / tablet / laptop / OBS? Here is a script for this on github It's on GitHub because Steam forums strip slashes from posts. Windows will give you security warnings and you will have to say ok. Only run this on private networks. Translation? The game translates many of the words for free. For the rest here's a: Language Pack Can I have a panel that does X? Anyone can add a panel with their own mod, and it does not need any permission from me. There is a small API for it, plus a complete demo panel to copy and rename: PZ Pulse extension API on GitHub Your mod adds one Lua table and (optionally) a small .js file. Your panel then gets the same title bar, drag, collapse, hide and font-size controls as the built-in ones. Example: FireBjorne's Nutrition Panel is a separate mod that draws itself inside PZ Pulse. Notes Read-only - unfortunately it cannot be interactive. Needs a second monitor (or a spare window) to be useful. Project Zomboid Build 42 only. No dependencies. Singleplayer and multiplayer. description: Vietnam War Rations — Historical MCI / LRRP / Field Ration Mod Taken inspiration from the experience with USMRE mod from the link below: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3738115503 Vietnam War Rations adds a historically inspired collection of Vietnam War-era U.S. military rations to Project Zomboid. This mod focuses on the experience of using old military rations, not just finding a food item and instantly eating it. Instead of behaving like a simple food pack mod, Vietnam War Rations lets you open ration cases, unpack individual meal cartons, inspect unknown rusty cans, open cans with proper tools, heat meals, prepare drinks, use field accessories, and deal with old-stock loot that has survived into the 1993 Knox Event. These are not modern MREs. These are older canned and dehydrated military rations from another era — heavier, rougher, less convenient, and sometimes unpleasant. Core Features: Adds the full historical 12-menu MCI lineup, including: - Beefsteak - Turkey Loaf - Chopped Ham and Eggs - Ham Slices - Meat Chunks with Beans - Ham and Lima Beans - Beef Slices with Potatoes in Gravy - Beans with Frankfurter Chunks - Beef in Spiced Sauce - Boned Chicken or Turkey - Chicken with Noodles in Broth - Pork Steak Also includes the historical alternate: - Spaghetti with Meatballs in Tomato Sauce - Each carton follows the correct MCI-style structure, with an entrée can, B-unit, spread unit, dessert/bread unit, accessory packet, spoon, and gameplay-support items. - LRRP / LRP Rations The mod also includes the full 8-menu LRRP ration lineup, representing lightweight dehydrated long-range patrol rations: - Beef Hash - Beef and Rice - Beef Stew - Chicken and Rice - Chicken Stew - Chili Con Carne - Pork and Scalloped Potatoes - Spaghetti with Meat Sauce LRRP meals do not behave like canned MCIs. They are dehydrated field rations and must be prepared differently, giving them their own identity and gameplay loop. Indigenous / Field Ration Content The mod also includes field-style indigenous ration items such as: - Indigenous ration packets - Freeze-dried rice - Dried fish packets - Dried shrimp packets - Rehydrated rice - Rice and fish/shrimp field meals This mod provide a different survival-food style because it revolve around interactive ration system. It is designed around process and immersion. You can: - Open full MCI ration cases - Open individual MCI meal cartons - Unpack historically matched ration components - Inspect rusty unknown MCI cans - Reveal unknown cans into actual ration items - Open cans using proper tools - Heat canned meals - Prepare LRRP meals with water - Rehydrate rice and field meals - Make black coffee, sweet coffee, creamed coffee, cocoa, and sweet cocoa - Use accessory packet contents - Use a C-rat boonie stove - Use trioxane fuel tablets for field heating To open the can, you can use: - P-38 can opener - Vanilla can opener-style tools where appropriate - Knives or sharp tools where supported - Other valid opening tools depending on the recipe The P-38 can opener is included as a gameplay-friendly exception so players are not completely locked out of using the ration system. For Heating and Cooking Canned meals are not heated by simply combining them with bottled water. Instead, they can be heated using more believable heat sources and field methods. Heating food improves the experience, but not every meal becomes pleasant. Some historically infamous meals, such as Ham and Lima Beans, can still carry mood penalties even when cooked. The mod treats mood and player reaction as part of historical flavor, not just balance. For Beverage Preparation Accessory packets include ration drink components such as: - Instant coffee - Cocoa powder - Sugar packets - Creamer packets - Chewing gum - Leave empty beverage packets after use You can prepare different field drinks depending on what you mix: - Black field coffee - Sweet field coffee - Creamed field coffee - Field cocoa - Sweet field cocoa Old-Stock 1993 Loot Logic Project Zomboid is set in 1993, long after these Vietnam War-era rations would have been current military issue. Because of that, the loot balance is built around old surplus logic. You are more likely to find: - Rusty unknown MCI cans - Loose old cans - Forgotten ration components - Old storage/surplus finds You are less likely to find: - Pristine complete cartons - Full MCI ration cases - Clean LRRP packets - Well-preserved complete ration sets Rusty unknown cans are intentionally the most common ration find. Complete cases and clean unopened meals are rare, especially outside military, surplus, warehouse, storage, or survival-related locations. The general concept for this mod: You do not just eat a ration. You open the carton, check what is inside, open the can, decide whether to eat it cold or heat it, prepare drinks from accessory packets, use field fuel, and deal with the fact that some of this food is decades old. description: Bring authentic indirect fire support to Project Zomboid with a fully functional M224 60mm mortar system. A realistic, multiplayer-compatible mortar platform for Build 42: full deployment, deterministic wind ballistics, a rotary airburst fuse setter, a laser-rangefinder fire-control instrument, tube maintenance, and late-game improvised ammunition manufacturing - all fully configurable in Sandbox. FEATURES - Fully deployable M224 60mm mortar, up to 1000 tiles range - Detailed 3D world models: tube assembly, baseplate, ammunition crates, shells - Interactive firing HUD: azimuth / elevation / range control with per-gun learnable dispersion - Deterministic wind ballistics - the round rides the weather, frozen at ignition - IMPACT and TIMED AIRBURST detonation: program the M734-style fuse setter with a real click-and-drag rotary dial - Directional airburst fragmentation - being under a roof matters - Laser rangefinder fire-control instrument: live impact prediction, target marking, and a shot stopwatch to measure travel time - World-map fire mission plotting with persistent plot lines - Tube condition, cleaning (solvent recipes), field repairs, and realistic misfires: failure to fire, dud, hang fire, low-power - with barrel clearing - Shell moisture: rounds soak in the rain and misbehave - Ammunition crate logistics with auto-feed at the gun and world crate spawns - Launch, flight, impact and UI sound design; dust rings, blast gases, shell trails - Multiplayer compatible, server-authoritative firing - 20+ Sandbox options IMPORTANT - Do NOT pick up the deployed mortar parts. Always pack up the mortar using the interaction menu before moving it. AMMUNITION - 14 ROUND TYPES Factory: HE-Light, HE, HE-Heavy, Fragmentation (airburst anti-personnel, folding-fin 3BK18 model), Incendiary, Smoke, Illumination. Improvised (magazine-researched, crafted): HE, Smoke, Illumination, Incendiary - plus craftable Mechanical Airburst Fuse variants. IMPROVISED MANUFACTURING Find Improvised Mortar Ammunition Vol. 1 and Vol. 2, fabricate empty shell bodies (Metalworking), fill them with scavenged payloads (Electrical / Mechanics gates), and hand-build airburst fuses. Improvised rounds fail more often - the crew's Maintenance skill eases the risk, and cleared duds are sometimes recoverable. Factory ammunition stays significantly more reliable. MORTAR CREW EQUIPMENT Military: Plotting Board, Aiming Circle, Firing Tables, Laser Rangefinder. Civilian: Orienteering Compass, Map Ruler. Proper military fire-control equipment significantly improves accuracy; civilian tools work with more dispersion. THE SPOTTER LOOP Bind the rangefinder to a gun, mark targets in first person or on the map, read the full firing solution off the device, time a ranging round with the shot stopwatch, subtract the round's burst lead, dial the fuse, and fire for effect. SERVER FEATURES Administrators can tune wind, dispersion, reliability, moisture, loot rates, effects and the UI through Sandbox. Built for Build 42 with performance and multiplayer synchronization in mind. Thank you for downloading and supporting the project. Feedback, bug reports and suggestions are always welcome. [previewyoutube=oIF3-7l5rI4;full][/previewyoutube] Subscribe! https://www.youtube.com/@mr.brollow Join my Discord! discord.gg/NWvyA3PArw Disclaimer: This mod is a TOTAL OVERHAUL of the base game and is not combatable with other map mods. Its HIGHLY RECOMMENDED to play this mod as a Standalone. It is NOT safe to remove or add this into an existing save. You can add other workshop mods to your Skyblock playthrough. However there may be some conflicts, or compatibility issues. This mod is my own rendition of Skyblock. Taking inspiration and mechanics from the well known MC Skyblock and other games. It is not intended to be a 1:1 of MC Skyblock as I wanted to preserve the charm and style from Zomboid. If you are developer who wants to make addons or upload content to the workshop for this mod. Please reach out to me via my discord first! Multiplayer Compatible for B42.20 Stable Release Recommended Sandbox Settings for Multiplayer & Servers Tree Growth Speed = Minimum 5 Cobblestone Gen. Min Seconds Per Reward = Minimum 5 - 10 Cobblestone Gen. Max Seconds Per Reward = Minimum 10 - 15 You can adjust the day & night length to your preference. We also added an option to allow zombies to spawn in Darkness instead of spawning at certain times. Feel free to adjust the Sandbox settings to your preferred experience New Game Start: Create your save with any desired preset {or custom sandbox} YOU MUST Select the "Skyblock" world for the full experience You may modify the Sandbox settings. However some Sandbox settings will be adjusted automatically for you such as grow speed, zombie corpse removal, and more. When creating your Character, it is recommended to select the Skyblock Survivor Occupation. It is a 0 cost occupation with some needed starting traits and recipes. - Smoker is probably not the best trait to pick When you spawn, you will have a Watch and Skyblock Guide Book in your inventory. This guidebook will contain more information and goals. It is recommended for new players to review this Guide Book. Falling off your island will result in absolute death and loss of all items on you. However, dying in Skyblock is not the end! You should maintain and keep all or most your skill levels & recipes. When respawning, you will be given back the lost Skills and a new Guide Book and Watch. Features: Replant Trees Replant trees from Saplings! They will passively regrow. Consisting of 4 stages, with each stage providing a different range of resources. Saplings can be obtained from cutting down trees. Mine Resources Mine for Stone, Flint, Limestone, Salt and Iron Ore at the 'Cobblestone Generator!' The 'Cobblestone Generator' has an infinite supply of resources. Use these resources for all sorts of crafting and building. Notice: When Building the Cobblestone Generator: be careful not to drink from, or lose the Starting Water Bucket or Lava Bucket. This can brick your run. Similar to how this can happen in MC Skyblock. Stone = Guaranteed Drop Bonus Drops Chance: Limestone = 40% Flint Nodule = 47% Salt = 10% Iron Ore = 3% Expand Your Island You can expand your island using a range of available resources. Locate and reach 3 other potential islands! 1. Desert Island 2. Farm Island 3. Mechanical Island Farm Zombies This mod features fully custom Zombie Spawning Mechanic along with a custom loot pool for Zombies. Zombie Spawning Mechanics: Spawn Times = [8PM - 6AM] Same Floor as you [Must be at least 12 tiles away] One Floor Above [Must be at least 6 tiles away] Maximum distance from player = [ 75 tiles ] Max zombie spawn cap: 100 The tile must have a light level of ≤ 0.5 The surrounding area (4 tile radius average) must also average ≤ 0.5 Must have a floor, no water and no blocking objects Zombies contain Emeralds for Trading (65% Chance to Drop) Fishing Mini Game This mod features a fully custom Fishing Mini game Mechanic. WHY? Because Zomboid does not support having water above the Ground Floor. To to make this possible we created a custom Water Tile and hooked up a mini-game inspired by Stardew Valley. I want to expand on this mechanic in the future but right now it features 3 different difficulty tiers, with each one having their own loot pool. [Green=Easy / Yellow=Normal / Red=Hard] You must have a Fishing Rod with Bait attached in inventory or equipped in order to begin fishing. All you would need to do is just Right click the water tile(s) near you. Care For Animals This mod has a fully custom Animal spawning mechanic, with modified behaviors. There will be a few ways to locate or obtain animals in your playthrough. Firstly; Animals can be found at the Farm Island. There will be a custom Animal Cage Tile. The Trader's stock refreshes periodically and is never the same twice. Each visit offers a randomised selection across four categories: Resources = essential crafting and survival materials. description: Yu-Gi-Oh! Trading Card Game Bring the world of Yu-Gi-Oh! Trading Card Game to Project Zomboid! ** WORKS ON BUILD 42 AND BUILD 41 ** Single dual-build mod - works on both branches automatically. NEW in 2.0.0: the GX generation is here! Over 1,000 new cards join the collection, taking it past 2,500 cards in total. Elemental HEROes, Destiny HEROes, Evil HEROes, Cyber Dragons, Ancient Gears, Dark World, Lightsworn, the Sacred Beasts, Rainbow Dragon and the rest of the GX era are now out there waiting to be found. 30 new products come with them: expansion packs from The Lost Millennium through Light of Destruction, seven Duelist Packs built around a single character, three big Collections, and seven new Starter and Structure Decks. Two new card types show up with their own icons - Union and Gemini monsters - and two new rarities can be pulled: Gold Rare from Gold Series, and Ghost Rare, the rarest pull in the mod (only four cards in the whole collection can appear as one). The Card Album now groups sets into tabs by generation, so tracking 41 sets stays readable. ⚠ Please back up your save before updating. This version changes how cards are stored internally so the mod stops clashing with other mods. Your collection is designed to carry over untouched and it's been tested on existing saves - but with a change this size, a backup costs you one minute. Step-by-step guide in the Discussions tab. Cards are scattered as loot throughout the world (containers, school bags, even the occasional student zombie). You'll also find sealed Booster Packs and Decks you can open - right-click them or use the crafting menu - to reveal new cards. Each booster gives you 4 commons plus one guaranteed rare-or-better card, weighted by rarity. Open packs in style Opening a pack triggers a reveal screen: your cards appear face-down and flip over one by one, with sound. Rarer cards shine with a foil effect - Rare, Super, Ultra, Secret, Ultimate, Gold and Ghost each look different. Collect them all The Card Album is a binder that only holds cards (no duplicates - one slot per card). Equip it in your hands to open it and store cards, and right-click it and choose View Collection to track your completion set by set: owned cards in full color, missing ones greyed out. Find it as loot or craft one. It's time to duel! Play duels against an AI opponent on any table in the world - or against another player in multiplayer. First, find and read two magazines: Yu-Gi-Oh! Basic Info teaches you to read cards (ATK/DEF, level, attribute and type appear in the card tooltip), and Yu-Gi-Oh! Duel Rules teaches you how to duel - then just right-click a table. Look for them in comic book stores, magazine racks, schools, libraries and bedrooms. Duels are turn-based on a full playmat: summon in attack or defense position, set monsters face-down, tribute for high-level monsters, play spells and traps, and bring your opponent's 8000 Life Points down to zero. Right-click your cards to choose what to do. Cards flip and rotate with smooth animations, and the AI plays out its whole turn step by step so you can follow every move. Build your own 20-30 card deck from cards you actually own with the deck builder - or duel with a loaner deck until your collection grows. In PvP duels, right-click a table and pick Challenge to a duel to invite a nearby survivor. There you also choose your own targets and decide when your Traps go off, so you can save that Sakuretsu Armor for the second attacker. The mod must be installed on the server, and both players need to have read the duel rules magazine. Fair warning: this is a SIMPLIFIED, old-school ruleset - think kitchen-table duels from the early anime, not the full modern TCG. Monsters battle with their ATK/DEF stats, and only the spells and traps with listed effects do something so far - the rest are collectibles. No chains, no effect timing. More card effects arrive with each update. Fusion Monsters Polymerization and the Extra Deck. Play Polymerization with the right materials in your hand or on the field, pick which Fusion to summon, and bring out monsters like Gaia the Dragon Champion, Black Skull Dragon or Flame Swordsman. All 38 Fusion Monsters of the first two generations have working recipes, and you build your Extra Deck from the fusions you own. Note: the GX Fusion Monsters are collectible and can be added to your Extra Deck, but their summoning recipes aren't implemented yet - they're coming in a future update. Card vending machines Yu-Gi-Oh! card vending machines appear in towns across Knox County - outside schools, shops and gas stations. Right-click to buy sealed packs and decks with cash, dispensed straight to you. Each machine's stock rotates weekly, so it's worth checking back. description: Adds a farming element that grants accessories random bonus stats. Ever felt like you needed more challenges, goals, progression, and loot to chase? Want to get even more enjoyment out of killing zombies? Now you can get magic items from zombies! Features Enchanted items can drop while looting or killing zombies from 6 accessory types: necklaces, long necklaces, rings, wristwatches, bracelets, and earrings. By default, the options are necklaces, long necklaces, and rings. You can toggle them on or off in the mod settings. Works on ANY vanilla necklace, long necklace, or ring - gold, silver, ruby, diamond, and every other variant, not just one specific item. Enchanted items are determined at the time of item creation. If you added the mod to a world you are already playing in, try visiting areas you haven't been to yet. There are 3 enchantment tiers: Magic (70%, 1 option), Unique (20%, 2 options), and Legendary (10%, 3 options). Each option has up to 5 tiers, ranked from White (65%), Green (20%), Blue (10%), Purple (4%), to Yellow (1%) in increasing rarity. There are 4 possible option types: Full-Body Scratch Defense, Full-Body Bite Defense, Combat Movement Speed, and Carry Capacity. Since it uses vanilla accessories directly, it's safe to add mid-save. Each item's rolled stats are unique to that specific item, so even if you remove and re-add the mod, your existing items keep their original values. Safe to remove at any time - rolled stats are stored on the item itself, so uninstalling won't corrupt your save. Compatible with tooltip-related mods like BetterClothingInfo and Tempo_PerfKit - tested to make sure their tooltip enhancements keep working alongside this mod's. Drop chances and option values can be tuned directly in the mod options. (Values on items you've already found won't change.) Built for Build 42 Compatible mode There are many reports of conflicts with 'Tooltiplib'. While I don’t use this mod myself, I’ve done my best to minimize issues, though complete compatibility isn't guaranteed. For the best compatibility, load order is important: Tooltiplib should generally be placed near the top of your mod list (below only mods that rewrite the tooltip render hook entirely, like Starlit Library), while my mods should be placed towards the bottom. In my testing, placing Tooltiplib at the very bottom also worked, but load order conflicts can still happen. Please use them with caution, and if conflicts persist, choose between using Tooltiplib or my mod. Note I wanted to add more option types (attack damage, endurance, etc.), but unfortunately the only stats available were ones clothing items can natively have. And as you may know, the movement speed stat doesn't even work right now, which narrowed things down even further. ;( For the sake of balance and to avoid farming fatigue, I kept it to 6 accessory slots (2 necklace types + 4 ring types) by default. Now, this feature has also been added to wristwatches, bracelets, and earrings. By default, only necklaces and rings are checked, so if you want to add or remove them, you can configure it in the mod settings. Up to 9 slots are supported through the settings. I'm considering an update that lets you dismantle unwanted accessories for materials, which could then be used to re-enchant or upgrade other items. If possible, I'm also considering adding a dedicated Enchanting skill. My All Mods Workshop ID: 3760442018 Mod ID: MagicAccessories

description: Quartermaster Tired of manually sorting every loot haul into your storage containers? Designate containers and then let your character sort everything automatically. How it works Designate your storage. Right-click a crate, locker, or container and pick "Configure sorting...". Tick the item categories (or specific items) that box should hold. Distribute. Open any container (a car trunk, a looted crate, even your own backpack) and hit the Distribute Loot button. Watch (optionally Fast Forward). Your character physically carries the loot to the matching boxes, nearest first, looping back until everything's sorted. Features Sort by the game's own item categories, or pin specific items by name (additive: a box can hold both, and a specific-item box wins over a category box). Presets: save reusable bundles of categories/items and apply them to any box - set up "Kitchen", "Armory", etc. once and reuse across all your worlds. Editing a preset updates every box that uses it. Overflow cascades to the next box of the same category. Real hauling: auto-walks within a configurable range, multi-trip, as one continuous (fast-forwardable) action queue. Works from world containers (hauled in trips) or straight from your own inventory (walked box to box). Searches nearby floors too, not just your current one. Craft from storage: tick "Storage" in the crafting menu and recipes light up from what's in your designated boxes; your character hauls the ingredients over, then crafts (batches and crafting-surface recipes too). Works with vanilla crafting and Neat Crafting. Storage Manifest: craft one (a notebook/notepad + a pencil) and right-click it to open a read-only window listing the combined contents of every designated box - searchable, sortable by item / category / count, and updated live. Controller support: distributing, the designation window, and the manifest are all usable with a gamepad. Never touches gear you're using: equipped, favorited, and hotbar/holstered items (holstered pistol, sheathed knife, etc.) are left alone. Anything with no matching box is left where it is. Settings (Options - Mods - Quartermaster) Walk range (tiles) Floors to search up / down Max carry load (% of capacity) - cap or overburden how much is hauled per trip Craft from designated boxes (also toggled by the "Storage" checkbox in the crafting menu) Notes Safe to add to an existing save. Build 42 only (will not run on 41.x). Works in single-player and multiplayer. On a server, designated boxes and presets are owned by the world, so everyone shares them. The Storage Manifest is single-player only for now. Early beta - bug reports and feedback very welcome! Changelog v0.23 (beta) - Single-player presets now survive being shared with someone playing in a different game language. v0.22 (beta) - Works properly with mods that merge nearby containers into one view (e.g. Proximity Inventory). v0.21 (beta) - See what's in a category before designating it. Item icons in the picker. v0.20 (beta) - Box fill priority: higher fills first, 0 is normal, distance decides ties. Copying a box's sorting carries it. v0.19 (beta) - Copy a box's sorting and paste it onto another. v0.18 (beta) - Fixes a blank main menu on PZ 42.20.1 and newer, caused by a "%" in a settings label. v0.17 (beta) - Multiplayer. description: Nuclear Protocol Nuclear Protocol introduces a dangerous end-game objective for players who have already conquered the apocalypse. You may have a fortified base, enough supplies to last for years, powerful weapons, and a secure territory. However, one final objective is still waiting to be completed. Find the military credentials, protective equipment, and sealed launch codes required to access the nuclear command terminal. Choose your target carefully, authorize the launch, and face the consequences of changing the world forever. End-Game Objective A nuclear strike is not something you can carry out immediately after starting a new world. The equipment and authorization documents required for the launch are extremely rare. You will need to search dangerous military locations to find them. You will need: Military Access Card Nuclear Authorization Card Sealed Nuclear Launch Codes Nuclear Command Terminal Once all requirements have been met, you can use the terminal to enter the target coordinates and authorize the nuclear strike. Nuclear Strike A nuclear strike is much more than a large explosion. The targeted area will be permanently devastated within a massive 500-tile radius. Buildings will burn, collapse, and suffer permanent structural damage. Vehicles inside the blast zone may be heavily damaged, destroyed, or completely burned out. Trees, fences, roads, and other parts of the environment will be scorched. Zombies caught inside the affected area will be destroyed. Fires will spread throughout the ruins. Ash, smoke, and fog will cover the devastated region. The destruction becomes a permanent part of the world. The city you target may never return to its former state. The Aftermath The explosion is only the beginning. Radiation spreads far beyond the physical destruction zone and becomes weaker as you move farther away from the impact point. Powerful post-blast winds, abnormal temperatures, heavy clouds, reduced visibility, ashfall, and dangerous weather conditions can continue for days. Entering the affected area without proper preparation can be fatal. Surviving Radiation Radiation cannot be seen. Survivors must therefore rely on proper equipment and careful preparation. A Geiger Counter can be used to measure nearby radiation levels and determine whether an area is safe to enter. Protective equipment includes: Nuclear Hazard Suits Gas Masks Replaceable Gas-Mask Filters Geiger Counters Potassium Iodide Tablets An undamaged nuclear hazard suit combined with a working gas mask provides the highest level of protection. Damaged protective clothing becomes less effective, while gas-mask filters gradually lose their protective ability through use. Always inspect your equipment before entering a radioactive area. Potassium iodide can help reduce accumulated radiation in the body, but it cannot replace proper protective equipment. Preparation Matters Before authorizing a nuclear strike, consider preparing: A secure shelter outside the radiation zone Enough food and clean water for several days Medical supplies and potassium iodide Spare gas-mask filters An undamaged nuclear hazard suit A Geiger Counter A safe evacuation route Singleplayer and Multiplayer Nuclear Protocol works in both singleplayer and multiplayer. In singleplayer, the nuclear launch can serve as the final objective of a long-term survival world. In multiplayer, survivors can work together to recover the required credentials, prepare shelters, organize an evacuation, and decide where—or whether—the strike should be launched. The consequences affect everyone in the world, turning the launch into a major server-wide event. Localization Supported languages: English Turkish Spanish Russian German Simplified Chinese Important Warning A nuclear strike permanently changes the affected part of the map. Do not launch a strike near an area you wish to preserve. Creating a backup of important worlds before using the terminal is strongly recommended. Since many new tiles were added in the latest update, the mod will still work with the current version, but the newly added tiles will not appear burned or destroyed after the nuclear explosion. I won’t be updating the mod, but you’re free to update it and publish your own version. Workshop ID: 3764265933 Mod ID: NuclearProtocolB42

description: World Item Removal List [SP] Take full control of the automatic World Item Removal List in your Singleplayer save — without Debug Mode and without reopening the Sandbox settings. World Item Removal List [SP] provides a clean interface for viewing, adding, removing, and manually entering items that should automatically disappear from the ground after a specified amount of time. The mod directly uses the World Item Removal settings of your current save, keeping its interface synchronized with the corresponding Sandbox values. Why is this useful? Project Zomboid can leave many unnecessary objects behind during a long-running game: Branches and other leftovers after cutting down trees Broken or unwanted weapons Discarded clothing Unwanted crafting materials Items dropped by other mods Removing all of these objects manually can become tedious. You should not have to carry every unwanted item to a garbage bin or place it inside a corpse simply to remove it from the world. The World Item Removal List exists to clean up this clutter automatically, reduce unnecessary persistent world objects, and help protect the performance of long-running saves. Main Features View the current removal list: Every existing entry is displayed individually inside the UI. Browse all loaded items: Search through available Vanilla and modded item types. Add items: Select items from the complete item catalogue and add them to the removal list. Remove items: Delete individual entries from the current list. Manual entries: Enter exact FullTypes or item-family entries yourself. Item-family support: Entries that represent groups of similarly named items are recognized and clearly marked. Missing mod-item support: Entries from currently unloaded mods remain visible and can still be removed. Removal time control: Change how many hours an item must remain on the ground before it can be removed. Blacklist and whitelist modes: Change how the removal list should be interpreted. Sandbox synchronization: The interface reads from and writes to the current save's World Item Removal settings. No Debug Mode required: Everything can be managed during normal gameplay. Optional world context entry: The right-click menu option can be enabled or disabled in Mod Options. Configurable UI keybind: Assign a key for opening and closing the interface. Manual Entries and Item Families The manual entry field allows you to add values that may not appear as individual items in the catalogue. Exact item example: Base.Axe This targets one specific item type. Item-family example: Base.Hat or: Base.Hat_ An item-family entry can affect multiple items that share the corresponding Vanilla naming prefix. For example, a hat-family entry may include several items whose FullTypes begin with the same hat prefix. The UI clearly distinguishes between: Exact loaded items Item-family entries Manual or currently unloaded entries Important: Do not use an asterisk such as *. Use a valid FullType or supported item-family format instead. The Three Supported Settings The mod provides access to the three relevant World Item Removal settings: World Item Removal List: Determines which item types are affected. Hours for Removal List: Determines how long matching items must remain on the ground. Removal List as Whitelist: Reverses how the item list is interpreted. These values remain synchronized with the corresponding settings of the currently loaded Singleplayer save. There is no separate duplicate list stored in Mod Options. Blacklist and Whitelist Modes Normal mode / blacklist behavior: Items included on the list may be automatically removed after the configured amount of time. Whitelist mode: The list is reversed. Items included on the list are protected, while items outside the list may become eligible for removal. Warning: Whitelist mode can affect a very large number of world items. Always check the current mode and your list carefully before applying major changes. Opening the UI The interface can be opened through the world right-click context menu. The context-menu entry can be enabled or disabled under: MAIN MENU -> OPTIONS -> MOD OPTIONS You can also assign a keybind for opening and closing the UI. Default UI keybind: Unassigned The keybind can be configured in: MAIN MENU -> OPTIONS -> MOD OPTIONS No key is assigned by default to avoid conflicts with other mods or personal control layouts. Save-Specific Settings The mod works with the settings of the currently loaded Singleplayer world. This means different saves can use different: Removal-list entries Removal times Blacklist or whitelist modes Changes are applied to the active save instead of being used as one global list for every world. Singleplayer Only This mod was intentionally designed exclusively for Singleplayer. It does not load its interface or functionality in Multiplayer and contains no networking, server commands, or Multiplayer synchronization. Multiplayer is not supported. Performance Notes The item catalogue is prepared for the management interface, while the actual automatic removal process continues to be handled by Project Zomboid's existing World Item Removal system. Its purpose is to provide a convenient interface for configuring the existing system. Compatibility Your support helps me keep going — thank you very much in advance! description: MRT.NoisyNeighbors: Multiple Generators More generators, more brrrr. Allows multiple generators to work together. Returned from a run to find your only generator has stopped? No lights, no powered refrigerators — because your entire system depended on a single point of failure. MRT.NoisyNeighbors turns multiple generators into one automatic system. Install a controller, link nearby generators, and leave one in reserve. When the active generator runs out of fuel, becomes damaged, or is destroyed, the controller automatically hands power over to the next one. A controller currently supports up to two generators: one runs while the other protects your base. What the system gives you Automatic handoff between active and reserve generators. Manual load transfer to another connected generator. Combined fuel reserve, consumption, and estimated runtime in the controller window. Atmospheric controller sounds for starting, running, and switching power, plus a metal electrical-panel interface sound. The controller window shows which generator type is connected to each system line. State persists through server restarts and world loading. Refrigerators and freezers work correctly. The controller is outdoor equipment and can only be installed outside. Full support for single-player, multiplayer, and dedicated servers. Optimised for multiplayer: the server processes only this mod's controllers and their events, with no constant world scans or unnecessary network sync. New in 0.3.0 This update includes major optimisation work on the server side of the mod. Controllers, refrigerators, and their visual objects are now handled through targeted lookups instead of broad repeated checks of loaded squares. I expect the mod to run noticeably better, with much less lag, on large servers and servers with weaker hardware. Please share your test results and send bug reports - feedback from busy dedicated servers is especially valuable. Crafting and setup Craft a Generator Controller Kit with Electrical 4. Install the controller outdoors, link generators within three tiles, then start the system. Linked generators can be refuelled through their context menu. Admin power A server administrator can enable infinite power for an individual controller. In this mode no linked generators are required, fuel is not consumed, and the controller does not wear out. The setting persists through restarts, making it useful for public shelters, trading zones, and other shared locations. Important Do not power the same refrigerator from a controller and a separate active vanilla generator at the same time. These overlapping setups have not been tested enough yet and may cause incorrect refrigerator behaviour. Compatibility Build 42 only. Confirmed working on Build 42.20 Stable and 42.19. Earlier Build 42 versions have not been tested. Can be added to an existing save. The mod can be removed from an existing save: controllers and their tiles will disappear. Planned Next update: a controller for a three-generator backup system. A four-generator tier will follow. A more atmospheric interface: a skeuomorphic controller window that feels like part of the game world. Enjoying the mod? Buy me a coffee ☕ Every coffee helps make the mod better. description: Beyond Ten The apocalypse does not stop teaching at level 10. Every trainable skill can continue from level 10 to level 15. The normal Skills panel expands to fifteen slots, with mastery levels 11-15 shown in gold and using the familiar XP tooltip. Build 41 + Build 42 One subscription contains separate implementations for Build 41.78 and Build 42.19+, including Build 42.20 stable. Project Zomboid selects the correct files automatically, including the matching Skills UI and gameplay adapters. How progression works Reach level 10 normally Vanilla skill books and their XP multipliers continue working normally through level 10 Keep earning XP from the same actions, recipes, combat and supported mods Fill five new mastery levels without requiring new mastery books, tokens or a separate menu Mastery XP and levels are saved with the character Each new level continues the skill's late-game XP curve. For a standard vanilla skill the costs are 10,500 / 12,000 / 13,500 / 15,000 / 16,500 XP. Fitness and Strength keep their appropriately larger passive-skill curve. Mastery bonuses Weapon skills and Aiming: +3% damage per mastery level Strength: +1 carry capacity and +2% melee damage per mastery level Fitness: improved endurance efficiency and recovery Sprinting, Nimble, Sneaking and Lightfooted: activity-specific endurance efficiency Reloading: the vanilla reload-speed formula continues through level 15 Maintenance: up to a 30% chance to prevent condition loss at level 15 Crafting, medical, survival and mechanical skills: 2.5% faster relevant timed actions per mastery level Combat mastery is applied inside the normal weapon calculation, so zombie, NPC and PvP hits keep the game's usual death handling, kill credit and multiplayer hit packets. Server owners should account for the additional PvP damage when balancing mastery progression. Mod compatibility Custom perks are discovered from the live PerkFactory list instead of a vanilla whitelist. Conventional parented custom skills appear automatically; top-level custom skill leaves are also added to the Skills panel. Recipe skills receive mastery action-speed bonuses, and compatible custom weapon categories can receive combat bonuses. Other mod authors can use the public BeyondTen.GetEffectiveLevel(character, perk) API or register action and bonus providers. Mods that keep using the normal XP-award path for the running game build progress automatically; a mod that stops awarding XP when getPerkLevel() reaches 10 needs a small API integration. Tested together on Build 42.20 stable The following combinations were loaded and played without Beyond Ten runtime errors: Detailed Skill Tooltips - the 15-slot bar and mastery progression work. Beyond Ten now keeps its normal level-1-to-10 breakdown and adds the concrete Beyond Ten effect for levels 11-15. CleanUI with NeatUI Framework - the expanded Skills panel and scrollbar remain usable. More Traits, its Dynamic Traits module and Unified Carry Weight Framework - normal XP multipliers continue feeding mastery. Dynamic Traits was verified by gaining Well-Fitted when Nimble advanced from level 7 to 8. Character-creation levels remain capped at native level 10, and dynamic rules that listen only for native level-ups do not react to virtual mastery levels 11-15. I Learn What I Read Too - normal level-9 book progression and the vanilla book multiplier remain intact. ILWIR's books and level settings end at native level 10, so it coexists with Beyond Ten but does not award mastery levels 11-15; ordinary XP sources continue mastery progression afterward. Someone called RPG? with TooltipLib - inventory tooltip rendering does not interfere with the Skills panel or mastery progression. Optional compatibility adapters Skill Recovery Journal is detected automatically. Mastery is transcribed and read through its normal timed actions, including partial progress, cancellation, XP multipliers, native levels 1-10 before mastery, and cumulative one-time-use behavior. Build 42 keeps the full journal mastery state server-side in multiplayer; Build 41 follows SRJ's legacy client-authoritative action flow. Journals created before Beyond Ten 1.2.0 contain no mastery snapshot and must be transcribed again. The Build 42 single-player path has been played end to end with partial transcription, resume, a full game restart, fresh-character recovery and different writer/reader XP multipliers. Build 41 and multiplayer lifecycle paths also have extensive automated coverage. Known compatibility limits Keep Skill Level currently preserves native skill progress only and does not restore Beyond Ten mastery after death. Build 41 Skill Recovery Journal inherits that mod's legacy client-authoritative multiplayer design. Build 42 refuses missing or ambiguous journal identity data instead of guessing and duplicating mastery. Very large, long-running public servers should monitor save growth because live journal records are preserved rather than automatically deleted. Safe by design Both supported builds keep native skill tables capped at level 10. Beyond Ten stores levels 11-15 separately and applies their progression through build-specific adapters, so engine tables and save data never receive invalid native levels. No game files are replaced. Multiplayer Install the mod on the server and every client. Build 41 forwards the owning client's final post-multiplier mastery award to the server. Build 42 captures its server-authoritative XP award directly. In both builds the server saves and synchronizes the mastery total. Requirements Project Zomboid Build 41.78.x or Build 42.19+ (tested on Build 42.20 stable) No other mod is required. Workshop ID: 3765241705 Mod ID: BeyondTen

description: Completely rewritten from scratch with many new features! Confirmed to work with B42.20.2 SP. Works for MP. Free to add and remove from your current save. What does this mod do? MRE Mod adds 36 different Meals Ready to Eat to the game. It includes 2026 Menus 1–24 from Boxes A and B, plus 1993 Menus 1–12 from Box C. The mod is designed to keep MREs simple and treat each one as a complete meal, without the extra packaging items you’d usually find in a real MRE. MRE Loot Boxes are also added to loot distribution. When you find an unopened box, you can open it to receive 12 MREs based on the box type you found. The mod includes several sandbox options so you can customize it to your liking. You can choose to spawn only 1993 MREs, only 2026 MREs, or both. You can also disable loot boxes entirely, adjust MRE spawn rates, and choose between balanced vanilla-style nutrition or more realistic nutrition values. It also includes craft able MRE boxes, letting you make your own storage box for MREs. Craft the boxes and collect them all! Stability You should have a bug and error free experience. If you encounter any issues please reach out. This was built on B42.19 and will be updated to work for B42.20 and beyond. Roadmap My goal with this mod is absolute stability for a long term no wipe server. This mod is feature complete. The only updates will be to fix bugs and to ensure smooth operations for each game update. For the latest updates and to view the changelog visit my personal Gitlab Features: Can add mid save Spawns 36 different MREs in the world. Craft 3 different MRE Boxes to store your MREs. Rare MRE Loot Boxes that provide 12 MREs when opened. Sandbox options to control the nutrition stats of each MREs. Sandbox options to choose what MREs you want in the game, 1993 only, 2026 only or both. Sandbox options to disable MRE loot boxes. Sandbox options to adjust the MRE spawn rates. custom 3d modeled MRE and MRE boxes. ability to convert MREs from my older B42 MRE Mod if necessary Bugs: Currently when eating a MRE it is not properly in your hand. This is only cosmetic. B42.20 MP when opening a loot box MRE you only get 1 MRE. This is for MP only SP still works. Support Me If you like my mods support me by liking and awarding the mod. If you want to give more, you can buy me coffee! Mod Info Workshop ID: 3765409550 Mod ID: bdtmre

description: Custom Start Complete control over your start. Custom Start extends Project Zomboid's vanilla character creation with a dedicated fullscreen setup menu, allowing you to configure nearly every aspect of your survivor before entering the world. Instead of replacing the game's existing character creation, Custom Start adds a new Custom Start button alongside the normal Play button. Use the expanded setup menu or continue using vanilla character creation exactly as before. The dedicated setup menu guides you through your survivor's configuration with a page-based interface while keeping every stage accessible at any time. Features Extended character setup Occupation and trait selection Skill customization Starting inventory configuration Equipment and backpack management Interactive map-based spawn selection Optional zombie clearing around custom spawn locations Reusable presets Complete setup summary before entering the world Dedicated Interface Custom Start uses its own interface designed specifically for survivor setup. The vanilla Sandbox, World, and Character Creation menus remain untouched. Inventory & Equipment Choose exactly what your survivor begins with. Configure: Starting inventory Item quantities Worn backpack Backpack contents Primary hand equipment Secondary hand equipment The Equipment page works together with the Inventory page to make organizing your starting gear quick and intuitive. Spawn Selection Select your starting location directly from an interactive world map. Presets Save complete survivor configurations for future games. Presets store your entire setup, including: Character Occupation Traits Skills Inventory Equipment Spawn settings Load a saved preset at any time or use it when creating a replacement survivor after death. Summary Before entering the world, review every part of your survivor's setup on a single page. Compatibility Custom Start is designed to work alongside Project Zomboid's existing character creation without replacing it. The normal Play button remains available, allowing players to use either the vanilla setup or the expanded Custom Start workflow. The mod also dynamically detects compatible content added through Project Zomboid's standard systems, allowing traits, occupations, items, and other supported content from compatible mods to appear automatically. Frequently Asked Questions Does this replace vanilla character creation? No. Custom Start adds a new Custom Start button beside the normal Play button. Vanilla character creation remains fully available. Can I still start a normal game? Yes. Simply press the standard Play button. Can I use this for replacement survivors after death? Yes. Custom Start is available both when creating a new game and when creating a replacement survivor. Are presets saved? Yes. Presets are stored and remain available between game sessions. Does this work with other mods? Custom Start is designed to detect and use compatible content added through Project Zomboid's standard systems. Compatible occupations, traits, items, and other supported content will automatically become available within the Custom Start interface.

description: Archery mod - Bows and Crossbows This mod has been updated for B42.20 and is working so far. It's been tested in Singleplayer and Co-op, but multiplayer (dedicated servers) may still have some rough edges. If you run into issues on a dedicated server, please report them and I'll take a look. Original mod by javim3 https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3518662691 DO NOT USE THIS MOD AND THE ORIGINAL MOD AT THE SAME TIME. You only need this one, plus JM3 utils. NOTE: This mod should work on Multiplayer but more testing is appreciated. If you find a bug, please feel free to report it. 📦 NEW ITEMS: 6 crossbows: wooden, metal, hunting, military, tactical and a special repeating crossbow. 4 bows: wooden, metal, hunting, and military. Arrows: for all models. Archery accessories: flashlights, lasers, sights, quivers. 🛠️ NEW RECIPES: Recipes are available in the JM3 section and allow crafting of several items included in the mod. 🔅 ADDITIONAL FEATURES: - If you run out of arrows, you can use shafts as improvised projectiles, though with reduced range and damage. You need to adapt the weapon using the corresponding recipe. - Arrows or shafts can be recovered from zombies, but may break if your aiming skill is low. Materials can be salvaged through a broken arrow recycling mechanic. - Shooting at close range increases the chance of instant kill (only with bows and crossbows). - Some zombies may spawn equipped with a bow or crossbow. - The quiver includes an automatic storage function for arrows, materials, and knives (Singleplayer only). It must be equipped, marked as favorite, and activated from the options panel. 🌎 AVAILABLE LANGUAGES: Spanish: AR, ES Chinese: CN English: EN Russian: RU Ukrainian: UA Polish: PL 📢 CONFLICTS: Advanced Trajectory Realistic Overhaul: potential conflicts (if you see 2 shots, follow ATRO's instructions) Other versions of JM3 Archery Mods that autoloot items from corpses may interfere with arrow recovery 🔄 CHANGES FROM THE ORIGINAL MOD: - Tied the arrow breakage chance to the aiming skill. It starts at 40% (configurable via Sandbox options) and is reduced by 10% every 2 levels of aiming. - Fixed the recipes for switching ammunition types. By default, the weapons use arrows, but you can adapt them to use shafts. The tactical crossbow can be adapted to special arrows like incendiary or explosive. - Implemented a mechanic to recover some materials from broken arrows. - Expanded the number of fletchings you can get from some items, and added new items to the list for crafting fletchings, such as playing cards. - Added a new leather quiver that can be crafted with Tailoring 2. It has better capacity than the normal quiver. It doesn't have a model when equipped. - Added a bow quiver accessory. It can be mounted on bows and crossbows, increasing their weight but reducing reloading time by 15%. - Rebalanced the range of bows and crossbows. They were shorter-ranged than a shotgun, which didn't make much sense for a bow. Higher tiers now reach considerably further. - Added a recipe to craft a Repeating Crossbow. You need a Hunting Crossbow and some welding materials. It has a max ammo capacity of 3 arrows, but is heavier, less durable and more likely to jam. - Added recipes to craft incendiary and explosive arrows. The recipes require a high Aiming level. - Rebalanced and fixed some bugs on distribution tables for archery related items. - Fixed weapon conversion recipes not working correctly in multiplayer (items could vanish or fail to sync). - Fixed material yield recipes (extra shafts/fletchings) not triggering in multiplayer. - Rebalanced bow and crossbow ranges. - The quiver auto-sort feature is now Singleplayer only, with an option to include knives and an option to toggle the on-screen message. - Various fixes for B42.20 compatibility (loot distribution, ammo boxes, crafting). description: Works on v42.20! Safe to add midgame! Compatibility version works in MP IF YOU ARE EXPERIENSING ISSUES WITH THE MOD TRY: 1) RESUBBING AND RELOADING THE GAME 2) WHEN THE VERSION IS UPDATED (HAS COMPATABILITY VERSIONS IN MOD LIST) AND YOU STILL HAVE ISSUES USE THE COMPAT VERSIONS This mod adds practice recipes to train crafting skills using tools and materials. This makes early-level grind more tolerable and reduces the risk of carpal tunnel syndrome. The intention behind this mod is for your character to practice more difficult actions. Features Supported skills: Knapping, Carving, Pottery, Blacksmithing, Carpentry, Electronics, Glassmaking, Masonry, Mechanics, Tailoring, and Welding Three difficulty tiers: Simple (lvl 0), Intermediate (lvl 2 or 3), Advanced (lvl 4 or 6) Some recipes consume resources, some don't Some higher tiers require more/different resources and/or more/different tools Customizable XP gains in Sandbox Options XP & Sandbox Options You can choose the regular or harder version of this mod in your mod list. Harder version's tiers are at lvl 0, 3 and 6, while regular is at lvl 0, 2, 4. Might add a sandbox option for that instead later. Each tier of recipes gives an amount of XP which can be adjusted in Sandbox Options under "Practice Crafting": Practice XP Base (Simple) - default: 30 Practice XP Base (Intermediate) - default: 60 Practice XP Base (Advanced) - default: 100 These values are the base XP before game multipliers (skill books, traits, etc.) are applied. Notes on pottery Pottery can be done on surface or on wheel: Wheel: 60s, regular XP Surface: 75s, 75% XP If you want to hand build pottery without a wheel you can check out my mod No-Wheel Pottery. Neat UI Compatibility If you use Neat Crafting from Neat UI, this mod automatically integrates with their XP display addon. The practice XP will be shown correctly in the recipe list with full multiplier breakdowns. Other Crafting UI Mods Compatibility There might be conflicts / display issues with other UI mods. Try them out, tell me how it goes. I can't promise that I will add compatibility with them, Neat Crafting was already a lot of work. Sorry (but only a little). RECIPE LIST 🪨 Knapping: Consumes any stone; requires hammer/mallet/knapping tool; no output. 🪵 Carving (Wood): Consumes wood; requires sharp knife; produces Splinters. 🦴 Carving (Bone): Consumes bones; requires sharp knife; no output. 🏺 Pottery (Surface): 25% longer (75s), 25% less XP; consumes water, keeps clay. 🏺 Pottery (Wheel): 60s; consumes water, keeps clay. ⚒️ Blacksmithing: Consumes charcoal, keeps Iron/Steel Chunk; requires tongs, hammer (ball peen for higher tiers), metalworking chisel for Adv.; no output. 🔨 Carpentry: Consumes planks and nails; requires hammer (+saw at Interm., +drill at Adv.); produces broken wood. ⚡ Electronics: Consumes battery charge; keeps electronic scrap, electric wire (+lightbulbs at Interm., +receivers/transmitters/amplifiers/motion sensors at Adv.); requires screwdriver; no output. 🍷 Glassmaking: Consumes molten glass from a crucible; requires glassblowing pipe and pliers; produces broken glass (equivalent volume to used glass). 🧱 Masonry: Consumes stones (FlatStone/LargeStone for higher tiers); requires hammer and chisel; no output. 🔧 Mechanics: Keeps Engine Parts/Car Brake/Car Battery; requires wrench and screwdriver; no output. 🧵 Tailoring (Sewing): Consumes thread; keeps fabric (rags, denim, leather, burlap) at Simple, consumes fabric in higher tiers; requires needle/awl (+scissors at Interm.); no output. 🧶 Tailoring (Knitting): Keeps Yarn/Twine; requires knitting needles; no output. 🔥 Welding: Consumes metal items and blowtorch fuel; requires welding mask and blowtorch; produces scrap metal. description: About this mod: Black Powder Gunsmithing adds new 18th and 19th century firearms, fully craftable from scratch, including the bullets and black powder. This mod requires the Gunworks framework to handle its reloading. Make sure it is enabled and loaded before this mod. Credits: Nik - Models and textures RedChili - Code and animations Charlie - Concept and research ------------------------------ FEATURES ------------------------------ A collection of historically accurate black powder firearms: Charleville Musket (1770) Springfield percussion rifle Kentucky long rifle 1875 Springfield Trapdoor Double barrel flintlock shotgun Revolvers (Colt Walker, Remington Army and Schofield) New ammo and consumables like paper cartridges and percussion caps that are needed to reload. New maintenance logic, needs to be regularly wiped with oil/grease and a rag to keep it from breaking. Barrel and stock are worn out separately, and you can break the gun down and smelt it to get most of the metals back. description: WELCOME TO AEGIS PANEL The admin panel you didn't even dare to dream of. Built this for my own server because I simply did not like how the vanilla admin tools look. Plain, tiny and I kept getting lost in them. It grew into a full admin suite, so here it is. Only real admins (/setaccesslevel) can see the panel at all. This is not just another admin panel with a few buttons. The screenshots show you every page and what it does. A few things you should know: Events: are in and tweakable through sandbox settings. Building fully custom events is not unlocked yet. The vehicle system: goes deep. Try it: right click a car or hit Edit in the panel you will see what I mean. (No, not every car has paintable colors that is the game, not the panel. But it is right there and it makes life easier.) Custom head tags: I personally hated having "admin" next to my name. Now you change it in a few clicks pick a color right on the role you created a small color window pops up. (This is not 1ms magic, give the system and your server a moment to work!) Server tools: scheduled restarts, auto restarts, change the ingame time and date. It is winter and you are not feeling it? Skip it or jump back to July. Power and water: on and off, whenever you want. Zones are free-form now, not just rectangles: Your player wants those two extra corners in his safehouse? Paint it. He wants the whole street protected so nobody walks on it? Paint it. Sandbox settings: right in the panel. Why? If a panel exists it should do this too. The Full Editor button still takes you to the vanilla sandbox screen anytime. Evidence screenshots: whenever you kick, ban or tempban someone, the panel takes a screenshot automatically and puts it into the Screenshots folder of the admin who did it ("C:\Users\yourname\Zomboid\Screenshots"). Aegis never deletes those. That is your backup if you ever wonder why you banned someone. Spawn animals: Nothing more needs to be said. Factions and safehouses: get their own detailed page. Construction radar: ever had trouble with players over who built what? Not anymore. Weather and time: need a moment to settle in, let the system and your server work. Item spawning: made easy, just type the item name. Area clearing: go try it :) Only the last 2-3 actions can be undone and yes you could wipe all of Louisville with it.( i try it, finally revange) Powerful tool. Do not overdo it. If you overdo it, that is on you. You have been warned. I could not test this with 50 players online, so a request to the big servers: please report any performance issues or anything else you can trace back to Aegis. Thank you. GIVING SOMEONE LIMITED ADMIN ACCESS Set their vanilla level to observer: /setaccesslevel "name" observer. Aegis only shows the panel to levels that carry the admin tool, so observer is the lowest one that works. On its own it grants no Aegis rights. In Aegis open Roles, create a role, tick only the areas that person should have, save. Assign the role to the player at the bottom of the same page. An Aegis role can only narrow what a vanilla admin may do, it never grants anything by itself. Leave the Roles area unticked and they cannot change permissions, not even their own. Only the vanilla admin level keeps role management no matter what, so nobody can lock themselves out. HOTKEYS F7 opens the Aegis Panel, F6 opens the Player Area. Both can be rebound under Options, Mods. SINGLEPLAYER Some options do not work in singleplayer, the powers in particular. To use them there you have to start the game in -debug mode. Big thanks to everyone who dug this up and posted it in the comments :* Multiplayer comes first. Once I am done with MP and have more time, I will move on to singleplayer, so please bear with me a while longer. FINAL WORDS Play with it. Do not overdo it. (Do it.) I think I did not forget anything, and if I did, find it and enjoy it :) Questions, bugs, feedback, bring it on. Remember: v2.5 IMPORTANT Admin Panel 2.5 and Player Area 1.4 are out now. The panel now teaches itself Workshop ID: 3766508989 Mod ID: AP

description: LOGISTICS TERMINAL The first centralized container management mod for Project Zomboid. Turn a vanilla Desktop Computer into a complete logistics network for your safehouse. Browse every container from one interface, find items instantly, and transfer them without running from room to room. MAIN FEATURES • Access every safehouse container from one terminal • Search and sort stored items • Transfer items between inventories, containers, backpacks, and vehicles with visible progress • Access nearby vehicle storage • Create custom Storage Profiles • Include or exclude specific items and categories • Assign profiles to multiple containers • Automatically sort items into profiled containers with Transfer All • Try compatible containers alphabetically and skip full containers • Display container weight and capacity • Use custom vanilla container names • Skip rejected items without stopping the transfer queue • Prevent transfers to unsuitable or full containers • Allow access to the owner and faction members • Server-side multiplayer validation • Resizable and responsive interface • Built-in help for every tab • French and English support • Vanilla-friendly design • Access containers located in basements, including extended basement areas • Browse large storage networks with paginated loading and complete search results • Double-click an item from All Containers to open its source container • Rename containers directly from the terminal using Project Zomboid’s vanilla naming system • Grant or revoke terminal access for individual faction members • Save faction permissions separately for each safehouse HOW TO USE Claim a safehouse. Place a vanilla Desktop Computer inside it. Right-click the computer. Select Logistics Terminal. Use the three tabs to manage your storage: • Logistics Terminal — Search and transfer items. • Profile Manager — Create storage rules. • Profile Assigner — Assign profiles to containers. Automatic sorting To automatically sort an inventory using your Storage Profiles: 1. Create a Storage Profile in Profile Manager. 2. Add the accepted or excluded items and categories. 3. Click Apply Changes. 4. Assign the profile to one or more containers in Profile Assigner. 5. Return to the Logistics Terminal tab. 6. Select All Containers on the left. 7. Select the inventory, backpack, or nearby vehicle storage on the right. 8. Click inside the right-hand item list to use it as the transfer source. 9. Click Transfer All. Only containers with an assigned profile are used. If several containers accept the same item, they are tried in alphabetical order. Full containers are skipped and the next compatible container is used. Items without a compatible destination remain in the source inventory. STORAGE PROFILES Create rules that control what each container accepts. For example: • Allow only ammunition in a specific cabinet • Exclude food from a tool container • Allow one specific item even when its category is denied • Deny one specific item from an otherwise allowed category Specific item rules always take priority over category rules. Remember to click Apply Changes after modifying a profile. Storage Profiles are also used by the automatic sorting system. A container without an assigned profile is never selected as an automatic destination. SOLO PLAYER SETUP Solo mode is detected automatically, including on existing saves. No Sandbox option or new game is required. 1. Place the terminal Place a vanilla Desktop Computer inside or near the building you want to use. 2. Start the setup Right-click the computer and select Set My Zone. This uses Project Zomboid’s native safehouse system. 3. Set the first corner Stand on the first corner of the storage area and click Set First Corner Here. 4. Set the final corner Walk to the opposite corner while keeping the computer and desired containers inside the rectangle. Click Apply: your current position becomes the second and final corner. 5. Open the terminal Right-click the computer again and select Logistics Terminal. Every container inside the selected area, on every floor, can now be detected. Use the ? button if you need help during the setup. Moving to another location Select Erase Safehouse from the computer’s context menu, confirm the deletion, then use Set My Zone again at the new location. IMPORTANT This mod is made for Project Zomboid Build 42. If you encounter a bug, exploit, or possible duplication issue, please report it with as much information as possible. Thank you for your feedback and support! © Deltasubject. Unauthorized redistribution, reuploading, or reuse of this mod’s code is prohibited without permission. Item Arrange V2.7. Build 42.20. Single player and Multi Player What does this mod do? This mod changes how items are placed when dropped on the ground, tables, shelves, countertops, and other surfaces. Instead of being scattered randomly, items are arranged in an orderly and visually pleasing way. The result is a cleaner-looking world that's both more practical and more immersive. Why is this interesting? More practical – No more messy piles. Items are easier to find and organize. Better looking – Project Zomboid's 3D item models look great, and displaying them neatly opens up many new decoration possibilities. More realistic – The number of items that can be placed on a surface is no longer limited by the container's weight capacity, but by the actual space the items occupy. How to use the mod HOLD SHIFT KEY WHEN DROPPING ITEMS Items are arranged automatically when you drop them from your inventory. Simply drag the items holding shift keY onto the desired surface before releasing it. You can place items on the ground beneath your character or on any adjacent surface, such as tables, shelves, and countertops. Just drag them to the ground of the current tile or adjacent tile. Donations / Payments / Gifts Limitations Not every item can be arranged. Currently, only items with simple, regular shapes (such as boxes or cylinders) are supported. Not every surface is supported yet. Each surface must be configured manually, which is a time-consuming process. Support for additional furniture and objects will be added over time. Zombies bleed. A solid hit from a bladed weapon, a piercing tool, or a firearm doesn't just deal damage. It opens a wound. Bleeding Zombies layers a bleed-out effect on top of normal combat damage: some hits are a shrug-off graze, some are a solid wound that finishes the job over time, and some are simply fatal. Why? The idea of this mod came from the work done on my main project called Slow Burn: Infected Survivor [B42] . A gameplay overhaul mod based on a popular book series where the "zombies" are more infected living humans rather than the Undead. I liked how it played so i decided to release it as a standalone mod too for those interested in a playthrough where the undead felt a little more living infected humans rather than undead zombies. its a personal preference of-course and it wont be for everyone but for those that would enjoy it i hope it provides some enjoyment. *NEW*Cosmetic Mode Don't want zombies to die from bleed damage? set the sandbox settings to cosmetic mode to disable the damage part of the mod. How It Works Every qualifying hit rolls how deep the wound is: Graze (weak, can clot shut on its own), Normal (a solid wound, usually lethal given time), or Devastating (always fatal). A hit to the head carries noticeably worse odds for the zombie than a hit to the torso. Grazes bleed for a while before they're even eligible to clot. No more resolving themselves away instantly. Bladed weapons, firearms, and piercing tools (screwdrivers, ice picks, and the like) all qualify. Blunt weapons don't, except for a lucky critical hit to the head. A bleeding zombie leaves a growing blood trail behind it as it's chased. Your Skill Matters The better you are with the weapon in your hand, the deeper the wounds you cause. Short Blade, Long Blade, Axe, Spear, Blunt, Small Blunt, or Aiming for firearms: a higher level in that specific weapon skill shifts the odds away from a harmless Graze and toward a Normal or Devastating wound instead. Only the one skill governing the weapon you're actually holding counts. A Short Blade 6 / Aiming 1 character gets the level 6 bonus with a knife, and only the level 1 bonus with a pistol. No blending. A max-level fighter is noticeably deadlier, but a torso hit is still never a guaranteed kill. Tuned to feel earned, not overpowered. Every number here is sandbox-adjustable if you want a sharper or gentler curve. Debug Mode Press V (rebindable in Settings > Controls) to toggle live combat text showing exactly what happened on each hit. Handy for dialing in your own sandbox settings. Fully Sandbox Configurable Enable/disable the mechanic entirely Wound-tier odds, set separately for head and torso hits How much skill level shifts those odds Damage scale per wound tier Clot timing and chance, for both Graze and Normal wounds Critical hit multiplier Compatibility Works on both Build 41 (stable) and Build 42 (unstable) from the same Workshop item. Workshop ID: 3767935128 Mod ID: BleedingZombies Note: I am currently learning to code in Lua. Some aspects of this mod have been assisted with AI tools to help me in that process. All the code is tested, and reviewed and maintained by me. I make these mods because I love this game and want to create fun things for the community. If you have feedback or find an issue, I'd really appreciate hearing it. Please be kind and constructive. Check out my new mod!

description: Turn the horde into heat. Cut up zombie corpses with any axe, hatchet, or butchering knife, then burn the parts as fuel. How it works Right-click a zombie corpse with a chopping or butchering tool equipped (or anywhere in your bags) and choose "Cut up corpse". Each corpse yields a torso, two arms, and two legs. Every part works as fuel in campfires and other fire sources. A whole fresh zombie burns for about 2 hours: torso 30 minutes, each limb 15 minutes. Clearing a big pile? Pick "All zombie parts" in the Add Fuel menu to toss every part you're carrying into the fire in one go. Parts rot like meat, and the more rotten a part is, the shorter it burns. Use them fresh, or stash them in a fridge or freezer to keep them burnable longer. Rotten and skeletal corpses yield already-rotten parts. [NEW in v1.1] Bundle up: tie one zombie's parts - the torso, both arms, both legs - into a single Zombie Parts Bundle at half the weight of the loose parts. No rope needed, and you can craft it straight off the floor (in singleplayer the bundle stays on the ground where the pile was). It still burns about 2 hours fresh, keeps rotting like the parts inside, and is only as fresh as its oldest part. Double-click it in your inventory to untie. [NEW in v1.1] Parts clean themselves up: parts and bundles left lying on the ground crumble away a few days after rotting completely - about 12 days after the kill, anywhere on the map, even in places you haven't visited in a while. Anything in your inventory or a container is never touched. No more fields of ancient limbs cluttering your base and dragging performance down. The corpse's clothes and loot are always recovered before the body is destroyed - nothing is ever lost. In singleplayer everything is laid out on the ground where the corpse fell; in multiplayer the parts and loot go into your inventory instead (like vanilla animal butchering), ready to drop wherever you like. Facing a pile? "All corpses" cuts up everything on the spot in one go. Maggots can also be tossed into a fire as fuel - though mostly just to be rid of them. Works in singleplayer and multiplayer, tested on dedicated servers. Available in 15 languages. Fully verified against Build 42.20. Workshop ID: 3767942451 Mod ID: CorpseBurn
