description: Fishing Panel Plus A rebuild of the Build 42 Fishing Panel (the window that opens when you right-click the water). It fixes the panel's display issues and gathers everything you need for fishing — info and controls — into a single panel. The vanilla panel only gives you verdicts like "Time: Normal" or "Temperature: Unknown" — no current values, no ideal conditions, no hint of why something is Unknown. This mod reworks the same information into a form you can actually use, and adds bait, line, catch log, and speed controls right inside the panel. One gameplay change is included — see "Gameplay Change" below. Vanilla Display Fixes Fixed the panel rendering as "??: ??" in Japanese, Chinese, Korean, and Thai — every language now displays correctly Fixed a mistranslation where the "Good" rating reused a health-UI translation key (in Japanese the panel literally said "Time: minor wounds"). Dedicated fishing keys are now used instead Fixed fonts rendering one step smaller than intended — the panel also follows your UI Font Size option now Removed stray blank lines at the top of the Guide tab Info Tab, Upgraded Fishing skill row — your current level plus a progress bar to the next one, and a note like "Next: Lv 4 unlocks Temperature" showing what unlocks next The four environment factors (Time / Weather / Temperature / Wind) — each verdict now comes with the current value and the ideal condition (e.g. "Now 15h / Best 4–6h, 18–20h"). Locked factors say "Unlocks at Lv N" instead of leaving you guessing (the unlock levels themselves are vanilla — this mod does not change them) Shore check — shows whether your bobber landed near the shore Bait status row — the attached bait with its icon. Right-click it to attach or remove bait without digging through your inventory Line status — line wear percentage and line type, always visible. When the line breaks, the row warns you in red: "Line: snapped" Fish Dex (Dedicated Window) All fish species (21 as of the current build) in a two-column list. Each species you catch fills in its icon and name The panel header shows your collection progress (e.g. "Fish Dex 14 / 21") — click it to open or close the window At Fishing Lv 6, each species' description appears right in the list (until then, the window tells you the unlock condition) Updates instantly while open. Window position is remembered Quality of Life While Fishing Today's catch log — every fish (and piece of junk) is logged automatically. Scrollable, collapsible, and kept across restarts within the same in-game day In-panel speed controls — four buttons: Pause / Normal / two fast-forward speeds. Change game speed without moving your cursor to the top-right corner; the current speed is highlighted No more camera shake — the screen no longer sways with your mouse while waiting for a bite or reeling. Right-click aiming still works exactly as in vanilla Fishing net feedback — collecting fish from a net shows the same "+1 fish name" speech bubble as rod fishing (singleplayer only) Fishing net info — the net's right-click menu now shows time since placement, remaining bait, and break risk Scales with your font — the panel and the Fish Dex size themselves to your UI Font Size and language, so text never overlaps Both windows remember their positions; the panel auto-resizes to fit the active tab Gameplay Change (One, and Only One) This mod is primarily a display overhaul, but it changes one piece of fishing behavior: Temperature checks now follow the world temperature — vanilla judges fish activity by the local temperature at the player's feet, so lighting a campfire at the waterside makes fish bite like it's summer in the middle of winter. With this mod, local heat sources such as campfires no longer affect the fish in the water; the temperature check follows the world temperature for more realistic behavior. The panel's temperature row shows both values ("Local / World"), so you can always see which one applies. Note that this change applies to all fishing at all times, whether or not the panel is open. Mod Options Panel width — Auto (default, recommended) or a fixed width from 400 to 700 px Languages English, Japanese, and Russian included. Other languages fall back to English Russian translation contributed by RedLink-kam — thank you! The display fixes (garbled text, etc.) work in every language Translations are welcome — let me know in the comments Compatibility Supports: Build 42 Client-side only. Does not touch server-side fishing logic Safe to add to or remove from existing saves Replaces the vanilla Fishing Panel, so it may conflict with other mods that modify the same panel Developed and tested in singleplayer. Multiplayer is untested Multiplayer limitations by design: the speed control buttons only work for the host; fishing net feedback is singleplayer only Workshop ID: 3768207575 Mod ID: FishingPanelPlus

description: This is a continued version of Water Pipes (aka Plumbing) – B42 Edition. I’ve updated the mod for the current version of Project Zomboid Build 42 and fixed several issues that were preventing parts of it from working as intended. The goal is to keep the original plumbing system available while the original version is no longer being maintained. Multiplayer has not been tested yet. It may work, but until it has been properly tested, please expect possible issues and report anything you run into. I don’t claim ownership of the original mod, its code, or any of its assets. All credit belongs to the original creator and everyone who contributed to the original release. If the original author returns and wants to maintain the mod again, use anything from this update, or ask for this version to be removed, they’re welcome to contact me. Source code: GitHub If you enjoy these continued mods and would like to help support the time spent updating and maintaining them: Support me on Ko-fi Water Pipes (aka Plumbing) – B42 Edition Multiplayer supported! Ever wanted to plumb your base in Project Zomboid? Water Pipes lets you install pumps, run pipelines, and bring water directly from rivers, lakes, or wells into buildings and barrels. Build sprinklers for your crops, control flow with valves, and monitor output with flow meters. This B42 rewrite is built from scratch with new features, optimizations, and improved building tools. Features - Pump water from lakes, rivers, or wells. - Supply entire buildings with running water. - Fill rain barrels automatically. - Build sprinklers to irrigate crops. - Install valves and flow meters for full control. - Unlimited pipe length – connect anything, anywhere. Quick Start - Build a pump next to a water tile or well, make sure it has electricity, and turn it on. - Lay pipes from the pump to a building or barrel. - Add sprinklers for crops, valves for control, and flow meters for monitoring. - Expand with forks, crossroads, or multiple pumps for a large network. Donations / Payments / Gifts If you like the original author’s work, be sure to give the original mod a LIKE or support them here: Original author’s Ko-fi Advanced Details Pumps - Must be next to a water tile containing tainted water or a well containing fresh water. - Require electricity and can be turned on or off. - Efficiency degrades over time. Repair the pump to restore its output. - Damaged pumps may stop working or catch fire, so keep them away from your base. - Charcoal can filter tainted water into fresh water. - Remove with a sledgehammer. Pipes - Automatically connect and change shape to match neighboring pipes. - Forking splits water flow, while merging increases it. - To move pipes up a level, build a pipe on the upper floor first and then place one below it. - Connect pipes to barrels or buildings by placing a pipe next to them. - Buildings must be part of the original map and cannot be player-made. - There is no pipe-length limit. - Pipes block vehicles. - Remove with a sledgehammer. Flow Meters - Install on an existing pipe. - Right-click to check the current water flow. Valves - Install on an existing pipe. - Right-click to open or close the valve. - Valves are either fully open or fully closed. - Closed sections use no water, allowing more water to reach open routes. Sprinklers - Install on an existing pipe. - Automatically water crops within an eight-tile radius. - Currently do not affect players, such as making clothing wet. Troubleshooting & Bugs For help with the original version, contact the original author through their Discord: Original author’s Discord Original Workshop page: Water Pipes (aka Plumbing) – B42 Edition Workshop ID: 3546314080 Mod ID: Waterpipes Workshop ID: 3768656166 Mod ID: WaterpipesContinued

This mod is designed to bring more realism to the weight system in Project Zomboid b42. In the new b42 version, many items have been added or changed, but we still have a major problem with the game’s unbalanced weight system. Simple pieces of clothing that weigh as much as lead, a cotton ball as heavy as a strip of fabric, a box of nails heavier than a metal bar; And we can’t fail to mention the effect that volume has on an item’s storage capacity—for example, a small backpack can hold 150 “Cotton Balls” or 10 “Iron Pipes” (assuming each item “Cotton Ball” containing 3 cotton balls, which would total about 0.45 kg and 4.5 L in real life. The “Metal Pipe,” on the other hand, would weigh ~16 kg and occupy 2.5 L) yet carry the same penalty (3.8 Encumbrance, 15 backpack capacity with a 70% reduction) in the game’s weight system. This disproportionately affects the overload mechanic and, consequently, wears down the character’s body more than it actually should. This is just one example, but there are hundreds of other similar situations that are frustrating and cause a lot of inconvenience for us players, which is why I created this mod. The mod introduces changes to the main unbalanced items used by players, such as clothing, medicines, books, bottles, tools, and much more. We have 1,629 balanced items (modified presets) and up to 5,092 items that can be modified across all 136 categories in the game. These include individual changes (unique ID), partial changes (ID containing a specific value), and modifications to entire categories (Literature, Skill Books, and Magazines). NOTE: *Due to the search mechanism used (category and character filters on IDs), there is a possibility that the mod may automatically affect the weight of another item added by a mod or if new items are added in future versions.* If you have any questions or feedback, please post a comment or start a discussion so we can talk about improvements to this mod; I'd be extremely grateful to discuss it. This mod is still in development, and we’re continuing to add new improvements. We appreciate your understanding if any changes occur that affect your current gameplay. If you encounter any errors or crashes, please let us know so we can resolve them as quickly as possible. I’m just one person working on this mod, so future updates may not be very extensive, and it might take a while to fix any bugs. I appreciate everyone’s patience. description: Easy Exercise Automatic strength and fitness training that actually behaves itself in Build 42 - and reads your skill books during the rest breaks. Open the Fitness panel, pick an exercise, tick AUTO and press Start. Your character trains, sits down when the endurance runs out, gets back up when it has recovered, and repeats - until you stop it or something gets in the way. It drives the vanilla fitness action underneath, so XP, stiffness and animations are exactly what the base game gives you. What it does Exercise, rest, repeat - paced by your actual endurance, not a timer. You choose the endurance % to sit down at and the % to stand back up at. Reads books while it rests - bookmark a skill book and those breaks stop being dead time. Details below. Works through soreness (optional) - when the Pain moodle climbs it can take a painkiller, or a tiny sip of alcohol. The game grants the full painkiller effect no matter how little you drink, so a sip barely makes you tipsy. Both are off by default and fully tunable. Stops itself when it should - zombie in sight, taking damage, low health, overloaded, or you grab the controls. Each one ends auto mode with a short note telling you why. Optional fast-forward hold - the game normally drops to 1x every time an action ends, which during auto exercise is constantly. This keeps your chosen speed, and releases it the instant anything dangerous happens. Tells you what it is waiting for - exhausted, in pain, resting - as a speech bubble or floating text, your choice. It makes no sound, so it will not draw zombies. Reading while resting Right-click a skill book or recipe magazine and choose "Read this while resting". It gets a blue star, and your character reads it every time auto exercise sits them down. This is free progress: sitting recovers endurance at exactly the same rate whether you read or not, and sitting even makes reading slightly faster. Keep bookmarked books in your main inventory - books inside a bag are not read. Only books that are actually worth reading right now are picked up. Above your level, already used up, recipes you already know, or simply too dark - it waits instead. Skill books are closed the moment you have recovered enough to train again, and pick up exactly where they left off on the next break. Recipe magazines are finished in one sitting instead. The game never saves partial progress on a magazine, so interrupting one would throw the whole read away - they are short, so this only delays the next set a little. The bookmark is remembered per book type, so dropping one copy and picking up another keeps it. Turn it off entirely, or limit it to skill books or magazines, in Mod Options. Settings (in-game Mod Options) Everything below is adjustable live - no file editing, no restart: Stamina - sit-down %, stand-up %, minutes per set, exhausted-moodle limit Pain - when to treat pain, pills and/or alcohol, sip size, intoxication cap, cooldown, when to give up Reading - read while resting on/off, skill books on/off, recipe magazines on/off Safety - stop on manual input / heavy load / zombie / low health / taking damage / panel close Game speed - hold fast-forward, and the health level that releases it Notifications - speech bubble, floating text, or off, plus how often to repeat the reason Compatibility Build 42 (42.20). English and Korean included. Safe to add or remove on an existing save - it only drives vanilla actions. The one thing it writes to your save is your list of bookmarked books, which simply goes unused if you remove the mod. Plays nice with UI overhaul mods - the bookmark entry is added through the game's own context-menu event rather than by replacing menu code. Single-player and multiplayer (each player runs it for their own character). Local split-screen second player is not supported. Do not run more than one auto-exercise mod at once - they hook the same fitness panel and will conflict. Changelog v2.2 New: reading during rest breaks. Right-click a skill book or recipe magazine and pick "Read this while resting". Bookmarked books get a blue star and are read whenever auto exercise sits your character down - which costs nothing, since sitting recovers endurance at the same rate either way. Books you cannot use yet or have already finished are skipped. Skill books are put down as soon as you are rested enough to train again and resume next break; recipe magazines are read through in one sitting, because the game does not save partial progress on them. Keep the books in your main inventory. All of it can be turned off in Mod Options. v2.1 Fixed: your character could freeze in the exercise pose and stop responding. Between one set and the next, the character could get stuck mid-exercise - lying on the floor still doing push-ups or sit-ups, earning no XP, and no key would make them stand up. The mod now closes the set down properly before starting anything new, waits for the character to be fully settled before queueing the next one, and if it ever does get stuck anyway it detects it within a second and frees the character on its own. That safety net runs even while auto mode is off, so a character that is already stuck will get up as soon as the mod is updated. Fixed: with the exhausted-moodle limit turned down, the character could stand up and immediately sit back down over and over. If you hit a bug, please leave a comment. description: Build a Smoker out of a salvaged grocer's freezer, then cure butchered meat into bacon, jerky, ham, sausage, salami and pepperoni. Named for TidierMouse, who inspired it. Update 2.0.4 Made the crafting and placing more in-line and reasonable. The Smoker is a welded metal unit, so it is built like one now: no planks, no nails, no hammer. It takes a fridge, a barrel or drum, scrap metal and welding rods, plus a welding mask and blowtorch - safety first - and you weld it together. It no longer asks for Carpentry to pick up or put down either; if you can build it, you can place it. The recipe is called "Make Smoker" in the menu instead of showing its internal name. Update 2.0.0 - curing is a real process now The Smoker used to be a workbench you crafted at. Now it is a smokehouse you load, light and walk away from. Two stages Prep, anywhere. Salt and season your meat on any table or counter. That gives you uncured meat - bacon, jerky, ham, sausage, salami or pepperoni, raw and waiting. Smoke, in the Smoker. Load the uncured meat in, add wood, light it. A progress bar shows the cure, and it keeps going while you are off looting - you do not have to stand there. Come back to finished, smoked meat that never rots. It only works in the Smoker. An oven or a campfire will not cure meat, and the Smoker will not take anything except prepped meat - no cooking dinner in it. It is a smokehouse, not a stove. The Smoker is now built as an item and placed where you want it, so you can pick it up and move it later instead of tearing it down. Single tile. On sausages: they are the fast option and they are meant for scraps. Rabbit, squirrel, birds, rodents, the odd chicken foot - things you would otherwise throw away. Feeding prime venison or beef into a sausage works, but you will lose most of the value doing it. Save the good cuts for jerky, ham and salami, which return far more of the meat you spend. Nothing creates food. Every cure returns a little less than it costs - you are trading calories for meat that keeps for good. Previously bacon and ham actually generated calories, which made pork the only sensible choice; that is fixed, and every recipe now sits within a hair of the same trade. Base meats only. Butchering gives a base meat and sometimes a named cut as well (cow gives Beef and Steak, pig gives Pork and Pork Chop, poultry carves into fillets and wings). Cuts are for eating as cuts - only base meats go into curing: Beef, Venison, Pork, Mutton, Rabbit, small animal, small bird, and skinned rodents. One exception: chicken feet. They are a butchering byproduct rather than a cut, and the only butchered food in the game with no crafting and no cooking use whatsoever - so they finally earn a job as mixed sausage filler. Recipes - prep on any surface, then cure in the Smoker. Herbs and spices matter Every cure needs salt plus at least one herb; salami wants garlic and pepperoni wants a hot pepper. The herb list accepts fresh, dried and seasoning forms of basil, chives, cilantro, oregano, parsley, rosemary, sage, thyme and mint - all farmable, and all foragable too. Preserving your meat gives you a reason to keep a herb garden and to forage. Balance: every recipe returns about 85% of the calories you put in, whichever one you pick, so there is no single best meat to farm. What you gain is meat that keeps forever, not more of it. WARNING - this mod adds a world object and new items. Once you build a Smoker, cure any meat, or pick up a fridge, that save depends on the mod. Adding it to an existing save is fine; removing it afterwards is not. Treat it as permanent for any world you use it in. Build 42 only. 2.1.0 Ground beef can now be used to make sausages. description: A banded chest that holds nothing but treasure. Gold and silver, cut gems, jewellery, coins and cash go in. Everything else stays out. --- UPDATE: MORE TREASURE ACCEPTED --- Raw precious metal now goes in Small gold and silver ingots, gold and silver fragments, and gold and silver sheet were being turned away. Their item tags are identical to the full bars the trove already accepted, so this was an oversight rather than a decision - and gold and silver fragments are the very material you build the trove out of. All six now go in. Clearer wording on silverware The old description said silverware was refused. Ordinary kitchen forks and spoons are, but SOLID gold and silver tableware - cups, goblets, cutlery - has always counted as treasure and gone in. The list below now says so properly. --- THE TROVE --- A one-tile lockbox built from planks, nails, hinges and the gold and silver scrap left over from breaking down jewellery. It holds 60 units and it can be padlocked. Build it with: 6 planks, 12 nails, 2 hinges, 2 scrap metal and 4 gold or silver scrap, plus a hammer and a saw. Needs Carpentry 3. Found under Furniture in the build menu. It only accepts treasure This is the point of the mod. The trove refuses anything that is not a valuable, so your hoard stays a hoard instead of slowly filling up with nails and canned beans. The refusal is enforced properly, not just hidden in the interface. Accepted: gold and silver bars, small ingots, fragments and sheet; loose diamonds, rubies, sapphires, emeralds and amethysts; gem bags; gold and silver coins; cash; any gold, silver or gem-set jewellery - rings, necklaces, earrings, bracelets and piercings; and solid gold or silver tableware such as cups, goblets and cutlery. Also accepted: the gold necklaces from Authentic Z, which carry no item tags of their own and would otherwise be turned away. Not accepted: everything else. Ordinary kitchen silverware stays out, and so does anything that is merely gold-COLOURED - gold-framed glasses, sports medals, gold star boppers. Gold-coloured sports shorts do not count as treasure. Marigolds are not made of gold. WARNING - this mod adds a world object. Once you build a Trove, that save depends on the mod. Adding it to an existing save is fine; removing it afterwards is not. Treat it as permanent for any world you use it in. Build 42 only Workshop ID: 3769346349 Mod ID: tidiertrove

description: Grid-based inventory for Build 42.20, repaired for single player and multiplayer. Version 2.09 Fixes shotgun reload, rack, eject, insert-magazine, and unload actions after equipping firearms from equipped bags. Stages held firearms safely for Build 42.20's root-inventory checks without requiring free pocket-grid space. Fixes shotguns and other weapons failing to equip or open their interaction menus when stored in an equipped bag. Equips carried weapons directly before relocating them for Build 42.20 ownership and multiplayer synchronization, without requiring free pocket-grid space. Fixes trap placement from equipped bags by consuming the trap from its actual nested container on both client and server. Removes the right-click developer grid/item/container editor from the release build, including when the game is launched with -debug. Restores furniture/moveable placement and trap context menus when items are stored in equipped bags. Prevents inventory hover events from leaving unrelated floor items outlined in blue. Prevents early-load errors when Build 42.20 loads moveable and trap UI classes lazily. Removes the remaining startup trap-menu warning by waiting for vanilla trap UI to load. Lets carried bags go straight into their worn slot even when the pocket grid is full, with matching client and multiplayer-server validation. Fixes the missing inventory/equipment UI caused by B42.20 compatibility changes. Fixes the _sendModData crash that spammed errors while opening inventories or moving items. Fixes ghost icons and duplicated stacks during MP transfers. Fixes shelves, crates and other world containers losing or rejecting their saved grid data. Fixes zombie inventories appearing only after selecting Move to Floor. Removes the per-tick isNPC error loop and repairs MP inventory synchronization. How it works Every container is a grid and every item has a footprint. Press R while dragging to rotate. Modded items receive sensible sizes automatically from their weight and category. Bags can go inside bags, and empty soft bags use less space. Items that do not fit go into the overflow list. They are not deleted. Grid space and weight limits work together. Both are configurable. Organized and Disorganized change grid space instead of carry weight. Required setup Requires Equipment UI: Workshop ID 2950902979. Do not enable the original Inventory Tetris alongside this fork. Dedicated servers: Mods=EQUIPMENT_UI;INVENTORY_TETRISP_MP Dedicated servers: WorkshopItems=2950902979;3769773293 Settings Settings are available under Inventory Tetris, Inventory Tetris: Inventory Space, and Inventory Tetris: Search when creating a sandbox. Clothing Pocket Size Bonus: 1 Bag and Backpack Size Bonus: 1 World Container Size Bonus: 3 Organized Bonus: 1 Disorganized Penalty: 1 Item Weight Multiplier: 0.10 Grid bonuses are added to both width and height. A +1 bonus adds much more room to small containers than large ones. Setting all bonuses to 0 restores the original mod's grid sizes. Solo players can also edit TetrisMPConfig.lua. Dedicated servers should edit the nested InventoryTetris = { } section in their SandboxVars file while the server is stopped. See CONFIG_README.txt for details. What this fork includes Inventory Space settings for pockets, bags, world containers and traits. Item Weight Multiplier built in; no separate Feather Weight mod is needed. MP Patch, Outlier Fixes and Load All Mags compatibility merged into one mod. Stable item sizes between sessions and support for modded items. Repairs for empty crates, partial Grab All transfers, worn clothing transfers, nested bags, hotbar transfers and animation lockups. Correct Equipment UI labels in all bundled languages. Notes Safe to add to an existing save. Do not remove it from a save after using it. Shrinking a grid does not delete items; anything that no longer fits moves to overflow. Grid scale, click actions and stack shadows are per-player options. Support: https://discord.gg/kWqp33FsA8 Credits Inventory Tetris was created by Notloc. The B42.19 fix, MP patches and Easy Mag Container work are by Royadin. This fork combines and updates that work for Build 42.20. Original mod Workshop ID: 3769773293 Mod ID: INVENTORY_TETRISP_MP

description: Cye's Crafted Melee Rebalance Crafted weapons now properly reward the effort required to make them. Rebalances 150 vanilla craftable melee weapons according to material cost, required skills, workstations and crafting complexity. Nominal durability uses ConditionMax × ConditionLowerChanceOneIn as a comparative estimate. v1.2.X – Server Controls & Interface Update Global Sandbox scaling: use a quick progression multiplier from x0.50 to x10.00 or set precise CMR intensity from 0% to 200%. Unified scaling: all 944 stat changes and CMR Short Blade risks follow the active server profile; comparison windows show the effective values. Server-managed panel access: hosts can lock local settings, disable weapon or crafting access, and exempt selected players. Co-op hosts and admins remain exempt. Neat Crafting support: right-click integration works in list and grid views. It is optional and safely ignored when Neat Crafting is absent or incompatible. Redesigned comparison panel: automatic width, game icons scaled to the UI font and displayed values limited to two decimal places without changing internal precision. Expanded and compact views: switch layouts with one button. The selected view is reused by new weapon, Vanilla crafting and Neat Crafting windows during the current session. Enjoying the mod? If CMR improved your experience, leave a positive rating or add it to your favorites to help other players find it. Thanks for the support! Multiplayer and existing saves - Safe to add to or remove from existing saves. Fully restart the game or server after changing the mod list or global CMR profile. - Adds no weapons, recipes, loot entries or persistent world data. - Supports single-player, co-op and multiplayer. Global balance and access rules come from the active world/server profile. - Compact/expanded view preference remains local to each player and resets to expanded after a full game restart. Report issues in Discussions → Bug Reports & Issues. Include your game version, CMR Sandbox profile, steps to reproduce, other active mods and console.txt whenever possible. description: PZ Map keeps your map handy without covering your view. Use a browser to display your live game map on a second screen or window. 42.20 update If you had this mod on 42.19, your BOOKMARK needs updating Old bookmarks will open but sit on "connecting" forever no matter what the game is doing. To fix it: in game, open the mod's options and click Copy map URL, paste that into your browser, and re-bookmark. That's the whole fix - nothing is lost, and your saved settings are untouched. Features Same zoom-based detail as the in-game map - streets, place names, forest, water. Your real time position is tracked on the map as you move. Fog of war is lifted as you walk, read maps, and find flyers. Your in-game map notes show up as you make them. Isometric view - toggle to the game world's tilted perspective. Map key - the vanilla building/land-use color legend. Flyers and brochures - their icons and labels show on the map, but not the flyer content. Annotated maps - click their icons to see their notes. Extra fancy features Direction indicator - keep a compass in your inventory for your heading to show up in-map. Darkness overlay - you need a light source to read the map (just like in-game). Follow mode - camera glides to keep your marker centered as you move. Theme: Dark map - can switch to a darker color scheme. Optimized - tuned to run smoothly. Customizable Cell grid, labels, notes, fog, and darkness are all independently toggleable. UI size slider can change your settings and map key sizes. Layout preferences are saved in your browser. How to use Enable the mod and load a save. Open the mod's options screen and use the Copy map URL button, then paste it into your browser's address bar and bookmark it. Drag the page to your second monitor (press F11 to fullscreen it). It updates in real time, the refresh rate is adjustable via the in-game mod options. Multiplayer Other players show up on your map live, as colored squares with names. Your server decides who you can see. Most servers hide everyone by default. Red squares are your side - same faction or safehouse. Amber is everyone else (if visible). Multiplayer - for server admins To let players see each other, set MapRemotePlayerVisibility in your server settings to Friends (same faction or safehouse), Friends and nearby, or Everyone. This is a vanilla setting and it also controls the in-game map. Bandwidth: about 54 bytes per second for each player shown on someone's map. A 5 person faction costs the server roughly 1 KB/s. That is per pair, so it grows with player count. A large server set to Everyone can add up. You can switch it off: the sandbox option Send player positions (on by default) under the PZ Map page of the server settings screen. Or in <server>_SandboxVars.lua: PZ_Map = { SendPlayerPositions = false } Switching it off stops PZ Map streaming positions and nothing else. The in-game map is completely untouched. This is a world setting, so it cannot be changed mid-session. Multiplayer works, and your webpage is still not online The heartbeat / data lives in your Zomboid\Lua\PZ_Map folder. The webpage lives in your mod folder. It makes no network connections of its own and contacts no third-party servers. In multiplayer it rides your game's existing connection to the server you already joined. Can I share it to my phone / tablet / laptop / OBS? Here is a script for this on github It's on GitHub because Steam forums strip slashes from posts. Windows will give you security warnings and you will have to say ok. Only run this on private networks. Notes Read-only - unfortunately this cannot be interactive. Needs a second monitor (or a spare window) to be useful. Project Zomboid Build 42 only. No dependencies. Singleplayer and multiplayer. Steam Workshop Meta It's dangerous to go alone. Press this: A similar mod for character stats: PZ Pulse Check out: my other mods. Workshop ID: 3770149036 Mod ID: PZ_Map

description: Respawns loot in containers ANYWHERE on the map, not just towns. Fixes vanilla loot respawn being silently disabled in rural/farm/forest areas and most map-mod regions. Everything else - farms, forests, rural roadsides, and many custom-map areas - never respawns loot, no matter what your sandbox settings say. This mod removes the zone restriction and runs its own respawn logic everywhere. How it works - When a chunk loads (a player gets close), eligible containers older than the configured interval are refilled using the vanilla loot tables (ItemPickerJava), so a gun store still spawns gun store loot. - Player-built containers (pl crates etc.) are never filled - your storage is safe. Furniture relocated with the moveable system is treated the same and never refills. - Construction in the area does NOT block respawn (vanilla ConstructionPreventsLootRespawn is bypassed). - Only containers that were opened and actually looted by a player, and that hold fewer items than the configured maximum, are refilled. An optional sandbox toggle also refills completely empty containers even if never seen or looted - off by default. - Safehouse containers are skipped by default (configurable). Sandbox options Interval hours, max items per container, safehouse handling - all configurable under the "Full Map Loot Respawn" page. Compatibility Build 42. Single player and multiplayer (server-side only). Works with map mods. Offline Survivor Offline Survivor changes the way players disconnect from your server. Instead of instantly disappearing, your character remains physically present in the world while you are offline, creating a much more immersive multiplayer experience for Project Zomboid. Logging out stops being a safe escape and becomes a real decision: where you disconnect matters, and someone may find you. Whether you're running a Hardcore, PvP, Survival or Roleplay server, Offline Survivor gives that moment real weight. ✔ Compatible with Project Zomboid Build 42.20+ 🛏 How It Works When a player disconnects, their character no longer vanishes. A sleeping survivor is left behind, using the player's real in-game model, clothing and equipment. If a bed or a large sofa is nearby, the survivor lies down on it, correctly aligned with the furniture. Otherwise they rest on the ground where they logged out, in one of several natural sleeping poses. While offline, other players can search the sleeping survivor through a dedicated panel, limited by your server's Sandbox rules. Nobody can open the body like a normal corpse or strip its clothing. Players can also drag a sleeping survivor to another location using the game's own body-dragging animation. When that player reconnects, they wake up exactly where their body was left. When the owner returns, the sleeping survivor is removed and control is handed back. ✨ Features Players remain physically present after disconnecting. Uses the player's real in-game model. Preserves appearance, clothing, backpack and equipped items. Automatically detects nearby beds and large sofas, with correct orientation. Randomised sleeping poses so no two survivors look identical. Integrated search panel with real item icons. Configurable loot limit and cooldown. Drag sleeping survivors using the native animation. Optional: zombies can find and devour sleeping survivors. Server-authoritative: theft and deaths are validated by the server, never the client. Fully customizable Sandbox settings. English and Portuguese (BR) translations. Dedicated Server compatible. Multiplayer compatible. ⚙ Sandbox Settings Offline Survivor is built to be tuned per server. Every option below is available in the Sandbox menu: Enable Offline Survivor — turn the whole system on or off. Enable Search and Theft — allow players to search sleeping survivors. Maximum Items per Search — how much can be taken at once. Search Cooldown (Real Hours) — how long before the same player can search again. Interaction Range (Tiles) — how close a player must be. Bed Search Radius (Tiles) — how far to look for a bed. Large Sofa Search Radius (Tiles) — same, for large sofas. Despawn Delay (Real Minutes) — decimals allowed; 0 keeps the body until its owner returns. Zombies Can Kill Sleeping Survivors — off by default. Minutes Zombies Need To Kill — how long zombies must feed before the player dies. Allow Dragging Sleeping Survivors — off by default. Hide Administrator Bodies — staff leave no body behind. ☠ Offline Survivor: Silent Death Looking for an even more unforgiving experience? Offline Survivor: Silent Death is a separate version of the mod, included in this same Workshop item, that allows players to assassinate sleeping offline survivors. Instead of being limited to searching another survivor's belongings, an attacker carrying a knife can end them where they sleep. Without a knife, the option never appears. The sleeping body then becomes a real lootable corpse holding the victim's actual belongings — it can be searched, moved and burned like any other body. When the victim reconnects, they are already dead, and a red on-screen warning tells them they were killed in their sleep and who did it. Zombie kills are reported the same way. Silent Death adds one extra Sandbox option: Protect Sleeping Survivors in Safehouses, enabled by default, which blocks assassinations inside any safehouse. Important: the two versions share this Workshop item but use different Mod IDs. Enable only one of them at a time: Standard: OfflineSurvivor PvP version: OfflineSurvivorSilentDeath ✅ Compatibility Project Zomboid Build 42.20+ Dedicated Servers Multiplayer Sandbox Clothing Mods Equipment Mods Backpack Mods Jaxe Revival — detected automatically, no setup required Note: because the sleeping survivor is a real body, the game counts it like any other corpse for smell and flies. This is a Build 42 engine behaviour and cannot be changed from a mod. Servers that prefer to avoid it can use the Despawn Delay option. 📜 Permissions You are free to use this mod on public or private servers. The following is NOT permitted: Reupload this mod to the Steam Workshop. Reupload modified versions without permission. Redistribute any files from this project. Use this mod or any of its assets in another project without proper credit. If you would like to use any part of this project, please contact me first. 🐞 Bugs & Suggestions If you find any bugs or have suggestions for future updates, feel free to leave a comment on the Workshop page. When reporting a problem, the server console log helps enormously — it usually points straight at the cause. Your feedback helps improve the mod and shape future releases. ❤️ Thank You Thank you for downloading Offline Survivor. I hope you enjoy the experience, and thank you for supporting the project! 🛠 Custom Mod Commissions I also create custom mods on request. If you need a specific mod for your server — a unique mechanic, a private feature or an adaptation of an existing system — feel free to get in touch and we can discuss it. description: BLOODSLICK The apocalypse is messy. Now the floor can fight back. Blood-covered floors are no longer harmless. Running or sprinting across visible blood can cause your character to lose their footing, stumble forward, or fall face-first. Sprinting carries a greater risk, while experienced characters are better at keeping their balance. FEATURES Slip hazards caused by visible blood on the floor. Walking is safe; only running and sprinting can trigger a slip. Separate probabilities for running and sprinting. Two possible outcomes: a forward stumble or a full fall. Uses Project Zomboid's vanilla animations and fall consequences. Full falls stain the character's body and worn clothing with blood. Running and Nimble skill levels reduce the chance of slipping. Different surprised character reactions for stumbles and falls. 12 localized reactions: 6 for stumbles and 6 for falls. Prevents the same reaction from playing twice in a row. English and Spanish translations. Fully configurable through native Sandbox options. No dependencies required. HOW IT WORKS Bloodslick checks the floor whenever your character enters a new tile while running or sprinting. If blood is present, the mod performs a slip roll. A successful slip then performs a second roll to determine whether the character merely stumbles or completely falls over. Full falls use the vanilla bumped and falling states, so all normal Project Zomboid consequences are handled by the game itself. The mod does not apply artificial or duplicate damage. When a full fall occurs, the torso and the side of the body that hits the floor become bloody. The game's native blood system stains both exposed skin and every worn clothing layer covering those areas. Stumbles do not cause blood stains. SKILL INFLUENCE Both Running and Nimble reduce the final slip chance. Their modifiers are calculated separately and then combined. With the default settings, a character at level 10 in both skills is left with only 25% of the original base risk. DEFAULT SETTINGS Slip chance while running: 6% Slip chance while sprinting: 14% Full fall after a running slip: 30% Full fall after a sprinting slip: 65% Risk reduction per Running level: 5% Risk reduction per Nimble level: 5% Cooldown between slips: 4 real-time seconds Character reactions: Enabled Blood stains after full falls: Enabled Every value can be changed or disabled from the Bloodslick page in the Sandbox settings. COMPATIBILITY Made for Project Zomboid Build 42.13+. No custom animations or external frameworks required. Uses the game's native floor-blood detection and movement states. Can be added to an existing save. Blood detection follows the player's Blood Decals graphics setting. If blood decals are disabled, invisible blood will not become a hazard. Although the mod is designed around zombie blood, Project Zomboid does not record the source of individual blood decals. As a result, any visible blood on the floor may be slippery. CREDITS Inspired by the movement-hazard concept of Watch Your Step, with a separate implementation focused specifically on blood-covered floors. description: SMB RUNTIME Some mods change what you see. SMB Runtime is the quiet foundation that lets them reach deeper without turning every project into a different workaround. I built SMB Runtime because I did not want every ambitious SMB project to ask players to trust a new installer, a new patch or another fragile shortcut. One shared foundation is easier to understand, audit, maintain and remove. Each mod remains its own mod. Runtime only provides the bridge it actually needs. If another SMB mod sent you here, you are in the right place. On its own, SMB Runtime adds no items, characters or gameplay mechanics. It works quietly in the background, and that is exactly what it is supposed to do. WHAT IT DOES Gives compatible SIMBAproduz mods access to systems a normal Workshop mod cannot safely reach on its own. Accepts only compatible SIMBAproduz modules built and signed for this Runtime. Keeps that shared foundation separate from the features, saves and identity of every dependent mod. Provides a guided way to install, verify, repair or remove the Runtime whenever needed. SMB Runtime does not replace or patch the Project Zomboid executable or projectzomboid.jar. Its only installation change is a verified, reversible entry in the game's official startup configuration. SETUP, ONE TIME ONLY After subscribing, close the game and open: mods/SMB_Runtime/Tools/INSTALL.html The guide explains every step in English or Portuguese and normally takes about a minute. You usually only need to complete it once. SUBSCRIBING ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH. Complete the local setup before launching any mod that requires SMB Runtime. DEDICATED SERVERS Dedicated servers running dependent mods need the Runtime too. Open the Dedicated Server section inside INSTALL.html for separate Windows and Linux instructions. Every player connecting to that server must also complete the local setup on their own game. WHY IT EXISTS I want to keep creating ideas that feel natural inside Project Zomboid without making players choose between possibility and trust. SMB Runtime is the part I maintain once, carefully, so every compatible SMB mod can stay focused on its own purpose. When it works, you should barely have to think about it. USING IT Players and fully non-monetized community servers are welcome to use SMB Runtime freely. If your server makes money in any way, reach out to me first and receive written permission before using it. Built and audited for Project Zomboid Build 42.20. RELEASE NOTES OPEN THE SMB RUNTIME CHANGE NOTES Workshop ID: 3771291698 Mod ID: SMB_Runtime

description: SMB TATTOO Give your survivor tattoos that actually belong to their body. Choose from 26 original tattoos directly in character creation. Combine several designs, place more than one tattoo on the same body region and see everything on your character before the game even begins. The tattoos stay beneath clothing, dirt, blood, wounds and bandages. They remain through save and reload, multiplayer, death and reanimation, and they are still there on the body left behind. This is not a temporary texture placed over the screen. The tattoo becomes part of that survivor. CHOOSE, COMBINE AND PREVIEW The tattoo selector is built into Project Zomboid's character creation screen. Browse by body region, wear several tattoos at once and use the live preview to build the exact look you want. Full-body view temporarily removes clothing, hair and beard so you can see the complete design, then restores every original choice. The included tattoos support Vanilla male and female bodies, with optional mappings for supported Tomb bodies. CREATE YOUR OWN TATTOOS SMB Tattoo also includes Tattoo Studio. Import a transparent PNG, position it directly on a 3D body and export a complete Project Zomboid Workshop mod. No coding. No folders to assemble. No metadata to understand. I built the Studio because a tattoo mod should not end with the tattoos I made. If you can create the artwork, you should be able to put it into Project Zomboid and share it with other players. Open: Options > SMB Tattoo Studio 1. START YOUR PACK Fill in the three required fields: Tattoo name: the name players see in character creation. Author: the creator shown beside the tattoo. Addon name: the Workshop pack that can hold one or several tattoos. When all three fields are complete and the Studio is ready, IMPORT IMAGE turns green. 2. IMPORT AND PLACE THE ARTWORK Import a transparent PNG. Natural Ink can soften solid black into a more believable charcoal tone while colored artwork keeps its identity. This happens once during creation, not as a gameplay filter, so it adds no gameplay rendering cost. Controls Left mouse button + drag: rotate the body. Alt + left mouse button + drag: move the view up or down. Right mouse button + drag over the body: move the selected tattoo across the skin. Mouse wheel: zoom in or out. Sliders: fine-tune Scale, Rotation, Width, Horizontal and Vertical placement. Ctrl is not used by the Studio. A tattoo can contain several image pieces, and the movement controls affect only the active piece while the others remain visible. 3. CONFIRM THE BODY PROFILES The Studio guides you through Vanilla male, Vanilla female, Tomb male and Tomb female. Each body keeps its own placement. Tomb is not required to create a pack. Those mappings are simply used when a supported Tomb body mod is present during gameplay. 4. ADD MORE OR EXPORT Choose CREATE ANOTHER TATTOO to add another design to the same pack. The completed tattoo stays safe while the Studio keeps the author and addon selected for you. You can also open a verified pack under My Packs and add more tattoos later without losing its Workshop ID or existing content. When you press EXPORT PACK, Tattoo Studio automatically creates: A complete local Project Zomboid Workshop mod. Full-resolution textures for every supported body. The Workshop metadata and internal mod files. The standard icon, poster and preview. The correct body-region registration for every tattoo. SMB Tattoo as the in-game dependency. When the export finishes, the mod is ready for you to review and publish. HOW TO PUBLISH YOUR TATTOO PACK The Studio saves the exported mod inside the active Project Zomboid Workshop folder. On the current Build 42.20 stable for Windows, the usual location is: C:\Users\<YOUR WINDOWS NAME>\Zomboid_B42_Unstable\Workshop\ Depending on the active game profile, it may instead be: C:\Users\<YOUR WINDOWS NAME>\Zomboid\Workshop\ Look for a folder beginning with: SMB_TattooPack_ Then open Project Zomboid's Workshop publisher from the main menu: Select the tattoo pack created by the Studio. Review its title, description, preview and visibility. Choose whether to create a new Workshop item or update the verified pack. Confirm the upload when everything looks right. FINAL STEAM STEP After the pack is published, open its Steam page and add SMB Tattoo under Required Items. SMB Tattoo already requires SMB Runtime, completing the dependency chain for subscribers. Tattoo Studio creates the mod, but it never uploads or publishes anything without your decision. INSTALLATION SMB Tattoo requires SMB Runtime. Subscribe to SMB Runtime and SMB Tattoo. Close Project Zomboid. Complete the Runtime setup through mods/SMB_Runtime/Tools/INSTALL.html. Enable both mods in the Mods menu. Restart the game whenever you enable or change tattoo packs. Subscribing to SMB Runtime without completing its local setup is not enough. MULTIPLAYER AND COMPATIBILITY The server and players need compatible versions of the same Workshop items and collections. Every player completes the local Runtime setup; dedicated servers complete the server setup too. SMB Tattoo was built and audited for Project Zomboid Build 42.20. Build 41 is not supported. Players, creators and fully non-monetized community servers may use SMB Tattoo freely. If a server makes money in any way, contact me first and receive written permission before using it. The complete terms are included inside the package. RELEASE NOTES OPEN THE SMB TATTOO CHANGE NOTES Workshop ID: 3771292051 Mod ID: SMB_Tattoo

description: A suite of animations that make your character feel more alive. It never did anything on Build 42 - the functions it tried to call do not exist in the game any more - so it has been dropped entirely. One way to fix it: Open that mods.txt in a text editor and delete the AnimSet Fix line Multiplayer People needs to test it. The vehicle entry, clothing reported on earlier versions are fixed. Known limitation An item in the off hand shifts during a handgun's recoil. This is vanilla behaviour - it happens without this mod too, with a handgun and a flashlight. description: About this Mod The world is entombed in a thick, unnatural fog that never lifts. visibility drops to almost nothing. This is an early Alpha release!. the fog, wildlife, and survival-pressure systems below are playable now. Expect rough edges and ongoing balance changes. I need feedback!! If anyone wants to be a play tester for the mod please feel free to reach out. How to Play During development i have tailored the gameplay as best i can to some specific sandbox settings. Some i have hard coded into the mod to be forced but some i have left open for the players to select. I would Highly recommend you set the following. In the early game, make sure you right click rags to craft a bandana for the lowest level of protection. the mod is intended to be a bit of a challenge but not too overly difficult its not fun. I am currently working on the default settings to get the "out of the box" sandbox settings just right. Sandbox Settings Zombie Toughness - Tough Zombie Count - Low Zombie Sight, Hearing & Memory - unless turned off in the fog sandbox settings these will be forced onto the lowerst settings Key Features Permanent Fog - locked to maximum intensity year-round, regardless of season or weather. Undead Wildlife - every animal in this world is already dead. 38+ custom hostile "skeleton animal" species (cows, rats, deer, sheep, and more) replace all living vanilla wildlife, individually balanced by size. a rat dies in a hit or two, a bull is a genuine fight. Zombie Sight & Hearing - on a new game, Zombie Lore Sight/Hearing are forced to Poor and Memory to Short automatically, low population but individually tougher. No Minimap, Ever - forced off regardless of sandbox settings. A Blank World Map - the map opens, tracks your position, and still supports vanilla's own pen/note tools, but never auto-reveals terrain. Two new hand-drawing tools (freehand pen, click-drag lines) let you map the fog yourself. The Fog Spawn - a merged spawn-location option pooling every vanilla town's spawn points into one "recommended" choice, used to give the random start more meaning. Fog Exposure Sickness - prolonged time outdoors unprotected gradually builds sickness (a mild fever, never fatal). A quick dash between buildings is safe; loitering isn't. Real vanilla masks all count as protection, scaled by how good they actually are, a gas mask with a working filter is a full hard counter. Work In Progress The mod is in heavy development right now. specifically a lot of work is going into the undead animals part of the mod. its taking a lot of playtesting to try and get it right. so feedback on that would be great. Requirements None -- this mod has no dependencies. Workshop ID: 3771665235 Mod ID: TheFogMod Note: I am currently learning to code in Lua. Some aspects of this mod have been assisted with AI tools to help me in that process. All the code is tested, and reviewed and maintained by me. I make these mods because I love this game and want to create fun things for the community. If you have feedback or find an issue, I'd really appreciate hearing it. Please be kind and constructive.

How It Works Select Spawn Selector from the vanilla starting-location menu. Complete sandbox settings, occupation, traits, and character creation normally. Features Choose any mapped location instead of selecting from a predefined list. Supports solo and multiplayer. Automatically displays compatible enabled map mods. Supports panning and zooming across the complete available world map. Switch between the standard map and Build 42's detailed terrain view. Switch between floors to select if you are spawning on the ground floor (default) or upper floors/lower basements. Displays town names while zoomed out to make navigating the world map easier. Includes toggleable, colour-coded points of interest for identifying building types while zoomed in. Server owners can disable this feature through the sandbox settings. description: Knox Buildworks Plan it. See it. Build it. Knox Buildworks is a complete building experience. It brings construction into one searchable catalogue, makes recipes easier to understand, supports real multi-tile structures and wall finishes, and adds a persistent blueprint planner for projects of any size. It is independent from the vanilla Building Menu and can safely live beside it. Use Knox when you want it, keep the original menu available, or let a server make Knox the primary building action. Build 42 only | Single-player and multiplayer | Requires ElyonLib Enable Knox Buildworks for the framework and converted Build 42 construction. Enable the included Knox Buildworks - Vanilla Expanded mod as well for the much larger, carefully organized building collection. Everything in its place Open the catalogue with F7 or from the Building Menu drawer on the left. Search by recipe name or required item, browse in grid or list view, and filter by category, subcategory, material or skill. Favourites, recent recipes and pinned recipes keep the things you actually build close at hand. Construction qualities that belong together appear as one family instead of separate Level 1, Level 2 and Level 3 cards. Model variants, colours and material choices are grouped the same way, and your selection carries into blueprint placement. More than 1,700 buildable definitions across the core and Vanilla Expanded collection. Clear requirements for materials, tools, uses, alternatives, skills, recipes, time and light. Directional and multi-tile placement for walls, floors, stairs, gates and irregular objects. Plaster, paint, wallpaper and signs using the correct tools, colour, pattern and wall shape. Persistent blueprints with rooms, Z levels, ghosts, gather areas, totals and build queues. Multiplayer integrity with synchronized plans and server-side validation. Choose it, place it, build it Each catalogue entry represents a complete construction recipe, not merely a sprite. Choose the buildable family and quality, then select any available model variant, material set or wall finish. Knox resolves that combination into its exact footprint, directional sprites, requirements, skills, construction stage and placement rules. Select Build to use the construction cursor immediately. The preview rotates and snaps according to the object, marks valid and invalid placement, and supports repeated building while the required materials remain available. When construction begins, the game performs the timed action, uses or drains the selected ingredients, preserves required tools, awards configured XP and creates the appropriate world object. In multiplayer, the server validates the same selection again before anything is consumed or placed. Select Place Plan instead to save that exact configuration as a non-blocking ghost without spending materials. The planned object remembers its position, direction, Z level, quality, variant, material and finish until you are ready to construct it. Know what the recipe will use Materials and tools are separate from skills and knowledge, so a missing hammer never looks like a missing Carpentry level. Recipe rows explain whether an item is consumed, kept, drained by uses, destroyed or allowed to degrade. Select a requirement to see Available Ingredients / Possible Items, including what you own and every valid alternative. You can choose the specific item to use, or pin the recipe to a configurable HUD tracker with icons or text. Build naturally Knox placement follows Build 42 rules for floors, wall edges, frames, previous stages, collisions, distance, support and footprints. Compatible objects remain on the cursor for repeated placement while materials are available, and native entity-backed objects retain their specialized game behaviour. Build supported walls bare or plan their plaster, exact paint colour or wallpaper in advance. Standalone finish actions can also target compatible existing walls. Knox only shows finishes supported by that surface. Plan the whole project first Planning Mode lets you design before spending materials. Create independent blueprints, draw named and coloured rooms, choose a Z level, and place non-blocking ghosts with their direction, quality, variant, material and finish remembered. Draw walls in lines and floors in areas while large objects remain safe single placements. Floors, walls, furniture and finishes can share a planned tile, and plans can be moved, edited or erased later. A gather area can include world containers and vehicle storage. Review whole-project totals, build one ghost, or queue the plan. Blueprints can be exported as JSON, imported at a new origin, or written onto an in-game blueprint item. Planning Mode in action Designed for multiplayer The server rechecks buildable choices, requirements, skills, recipes, finishes, position and permissions. Integrity checks prevent mismatched clients from building with incompatible definitions. Blueprint owners can grant view, contribute or build access to their faction or individual players. Server options cover Planning Mode, the primary Building Menu action, blueprint limits, construction XP, and infinite or limited wells that refill from groundwater and rain. Vanilla Expanded The bundled Vanilla Expanded add-on turns the Build 42 tile library into a practical catalogue. Walls are grouped by family, quality, model and available colour, alongside a broad selection of roofs, doors, windows, floors, fences, containers, furniture, architectural details, decorations, road pieces, vegetation and survival structures. It remains optional, so you can enable the focused core or the full collection. For add-on creators Knox is also a data-driven framework. Add-ons can define templates, material groups, stages, variants, multi-level geometry, recipes, skills and wall finishes through JSON, while still referencing native entities when engine components are needed. AI USAGE DISCLAIMER This mod was developed entirely with code generated by Claude. There is not a single line written by hand. My work was designing the whole logic of the system, providing the game and modding knowledge, reading the debug output, giving context and steering the development until it did what I wanted. The project was supervised, tested and optimised throughout, including the multiplayer port, always aiming for efficient code with no unnecessary performance cost. The tiles and sound effects are my own work. Water Pump — running water after the end of the world, at last! A fuel-powered motor pump and a 3000 litre tank. You draw water from a river, a well or some barrels, lift it into a tank up high, and from there gravity feeds the taps of the whole house. No electricity needed. It also does something much simpler: moving water from one place to another without hauling cans by hand. Getting water running, step by step Put the pump down near a water source and connect it to that source (river, well, barrels, another tank) and to an output container. Fuel it and turn it on. Water starts moving on its own. Build the tank up high — your roof is the natural spot — and connect it from its menu. Install a water connection on each fixture with a pipe wrench. Plumb the fixture with the game's own "connect to water source" option. This step is not optional: until you do it, the tap keeps serving its own leftover water and ignores your tank. How to tell it worked: a tap running off your tank reads 40/40. If it still reads 20/20, that is the tap's own leftover water and it is not on the tank yet. And if the tank is empty, a plumbed tap has nothing to give and shows no water options at all — exactly like an empty rain barrel. The pump Heavy: it takes both hands to carry. Place it from the menu to pick the facing, or just drop it on the floor and install it later. Fuel: 20 litres, filled from cans or bottles. It burns about half a litre per hour while running, whether it is pumping or not. Flow: 5 litres per in-game minute. Range: draws from 3 tiles away on its own level, pushes up to 20 tiles away and 4 floors higher. Condition: wears down with use, repaired with a pipe wrench and scrap. Do not run it dry. Left on with no water at the intake, the engine overheats in a couple of in-game hours. Below 20% condition it can burn out for good: it will not start and cannot be repaired. It only moves water. Petrol, bleach or anything else is refused, and if you force it the engine coughs, will not start and loses 15% condition. Rainwater is fine, but the pump does not purify — lift rainwater and rainwater is what you get up there. The info window shows status, fuel, condition and connection count, and while it is open it highlights the connections in the world: green for outputs, blue for sources, red for a contaminated one. The fast way to read a big setup. The tank Built from the construction menu with Welding 4 and the recipe learned. It holds 3000 litres and takes sheet metal, scrap and pipes. It starts disconnected, so you can fill it before it begins distributing. Once connected it feeds by gravity, with no fuel and no electricity: 20 tiles around, and downwards with practically no floor limit — a rooftop tank can supply a whole building or a bunker. Lifting water up is the pump's job, and that does have a limit of 4 floors. The water connections With a pipe wrench and a tank in range you can install a connection on any tap, toilet, shower, bathtub or washing machine. It is invisible: it does not clutter the house and you can keep building over it. It behaves like a rain collector sitting above the fixture — except one tank supplies every fixture at once. It has to be an enclosed space. The game's plumbing only works inside a space closed off by walls, a map house or one you built yourself. A roof alone is not enough: a covered patio will not do. That is the game, not the mod, so the menu tells you the reason instead of letting you waste the wrench. One connection covers a 3x3 area, so a sink and a toilet next to each other share one. If a spot is already covered the mod says so — including when what covers it is your own rain barrel, in which case you do not need the mod there at all. You can remove a connection from the same menu. While one is installed you cannot pick the fixture up, and if the fixture is destroyed the connection goes with it. Going further: cascading A tank can be the output of one pump and the source of another at the same time. Chaining pump → tank → pump → tank lifts water as high as you want: tested in the tallest buildings. Barrels work too. Every stage costs fuel, so it is a real decision. The highest tank fills first, then the ones below. With several pumps around, the menu lets you pick which one each thing connects to, showing position and status, so you never have to guess. How to get it The pump shows up mostly in hardware stores, and at a lower rate in garages and industrial warehouses — roughly where you would find a generator. Sometimes it is lying on the floor of a garage. The magazine "Off-Grid Water Systems" teaches both the tank and the pump. Hardware and electronics stores, and with less luck libraries, bookshops, magazine racks and house shelves. Operating the pump is also learned on its own at Electrical 3 — but for the tank you do have to find the magazine. Multiplayer It works in multiplayer. Ported and tested against a real dedicated server: placing, installing, turning on, fuelling, connecting, the tank, the connections and the water transfer are all synced. If you hit a bug, leave it in the comments. Removing the mod from a save Straight answer: on a world where the water tank was built, you cannot fully remove the mod. Zomboid registers the tank's script in that save's WorldDictionary, and after that the client refuses to load the world without it — Missing dictionary script: WaterPump.WaterTank. I tested it: with the mod on both sides it loads; missing on the server, or on both, it fails. That is a Zomboid limitation, not a choice of the mod, and no mod can reach it. Nothing is lost, though. Put the mod back and the world opens again; Zomboid reinstates the entry by itself. So if what you want is a world with none of the mod's stuff in it, run the cleanup and just keep the mod in your load order — once the cleanup has run it does nothing at all. In the Lua console with debug mode on: Single player: WPM.desinstalar() Multiplayer, as admin: WP.pedir(getPlayer(), "desinstalar", {}) It wipes every pump, tank, connection and mod item from the loaded area, and lists whatever sits in an unloaded chunk with its coordinates. In multiplayer the report prints to the server log. If you truly need it gone, back up the save and look up Project Zomboid WorldDictionary missing dictionary script. Never just delete that .bin file: it scrambles the save's IDs. Tested on Build 42.20 (stable branch), single player and multiplayer with a dedicated server. Available in Spanish and English. description: This mod is created mainly for compatibility with Extensive Health Rework Evolved, since Realistic Temperatures mod has it's own systems that hard to make fully compatible, especially body temperature Just like Realistic Temperatures this mod makes indoor temperatures respond to outdoor weather. Temperature depends on central heating systems(shut's off after power goes down), the condition of the building, and open/broken/barricaded windows or doors. It works quite different tho and performance wise is much lighter If you want purely indoor temps simulation it's probably better to use Realistic Temperatures mod (tho it can be quite performance heavy). My mod just fully compatible with EHR unlike RT Main Features Separate temperatures for individual rooms within the same building. Heat gradually moves between rooms through doors, open passages, and stairways. Open or broken exterior doors and windows increase heat exchange with the outdoors. Barricaded windows still cause a small amount of leakage, but retain heat much better. After the power shuts off, buildings gradually cool down or warm up toward the outdoor temperature. Unvisited buildings begin close to the current outdoor temperature, with a configurable +2 °C buffer by default. To avoid offline simulation and keep performance high. Supports vanilla buildings, multiple floors, and roofed player-built structures. Room temperatures are preserved while moving through the building and when returning later. Adds several placeable heating and cooling devices. Simulation speed, heat loss, opening leakage, and other values can be configured through Sandbox settings. IC changes ambient air temperature only. IC does not directly overwrite the character's core temperature. IC does not modify clothing or item insulation. IC does not replace vanilla thermoregulation. IC uses room-based simulation, cached building data, and scheduled updates. IC can provide its ambient temperature data to EHR for a more complete health simulation. Items Cheap Heater A basic electric space heater with a 6-tile radius. Best suited for small rooms. Premium Heater A powerful electric heater with a 12-tile radius. It attempts to maintain a temperature of approximately 25 °C. Standing Fan An electric standing fan with an 8-tile radius. It can reduce the local temperature by up to 10 °C near the device. Propane Heater A propane-powered heater with a 10-tile radius and a target temperature of approximately 25 °C. It uses vanilla propane tanks. Tanks can be inserted, removed, or replaced through the object's context menu. Electric devices require grid or generator power and automatically stop working after losing electricity. Devices powered by a generator add to its fuel consumption. All devices can be found in appropriate loot locations, including electronics stores, household departments, garages, warehouses, U-Store-It facilities, camping suppliers, and residential storage. Electronics Stores, warehouses and U-Store-it has highest chances where you can find it. description: One Clean Jaw Stab This mod allows you to perform "stealth kill" aka "jaw stab" whenever you want In vanilla, the jaw-stab attack depends heavily on zombie awareness and combat conditions(you can't perform jaw stab if more than 1 zombie pursuing you). One Clean Jaw Stab turns it into a deliberate combat move: get close, pick your target, and attempt the kill when you decide the moment is right. Unlike similar mods it doesn't change chances or interfere with mechanic. It gives you control whether to use it or not with dedicated rebindable button. And it does not require manual installation! How It Works Equip a short blade in your primary hand. Hold aim and approach a standing zombie until your character raises their free hand. Press the Middle Mouse Button to attempt the close kill. But be careful because there is customizable chance that zombie will push you away leaving you exposed or you can lose your weapon during the attack The hotkey can be changed under Options > Mods > One Clean Stab. Zombie awareness and the number of pursuing zombies do not prevent the attempt, but positioning still matters. You must be aiming, close enough, and facing a valid standing target which makes you open. So plan your stabs with right timing. Features A dedicated and fully rebindable close-kill button. Works with every short-blade weapons Configurable success chance. A failed attempt makes the character pushed away by zombie and fall backward, leaving them exposed. Optional Short Blade skill requirement for unlocking the mechanic. Optional endurance, fatigue, and cooldown restrictions to prevent careless spam. description: Mini Compass [Build 42] A lightweight, customizable compass HUD with live direction and heading information for walking and driving. Overview Mini Compass is a client-side navigation HUD for Project Zomboid Build 42. It provides clear directional information without changing inventory, XP, vehicles, character stats, world data, or gameplay balance. Choose between a circular compass dial or a compact text display, then customize its size, degree display, dragging, and screen position through Game Options. Key Features Two display styles: Circular Compass Dial or Simple Text. Live heading: Displays 0°–359° with N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, and NW. Walking and vehicle support: Updates on foot and while driving. Optional degrees: Show or hide the numerical heading. Three HUD sizes: Small, Medium, and Large. Draggable HUD: Move the compass anywhere on the screen. Per-player saving: Each player keeps their own settings and position. Reconnect and restart persistence: The HUD returns to its last saved location. Reset position: Restores the default placement beside the in-game clock. How It Works Enable Mini Compass in the Mods menu. Open Game Options → Mods → Mini Compass. Choose the style, size, degree display, and dragging preference. Drag the HUD to the preferred position. Its location and settings are saved locally. Single Player and Multiplayer Single Player: Supported. Hosted Multiplayer: Runtime-tested and confirmed working. Different players keep separate settings and HUD positions. Dedicated Server: The mod is client-side and performs no authoritative gameplay changes. Separate dedicated-server runtime validation is still pending. Confirmed hosted multiplayer behavior: Independent settings and positions for different players. Position survives reconnecting and restarting the game. Fresh players receive the default upper-right placement. Reset Position remains saved after reconnect or restart. No shared gameplay or server state is modified. Configuration Game Options → Mods → Mini Compass Enable Mini Compass: Show or hide the HUD. Compass Style: Select Circular Compass Dial or Simple Text. Show Degrees: Show or hide numerical heading values. Allow Dragging: Enable or lock manual HUD movement. Compass Size: Select Small, Medium, or Large. Reset Compass Position: Return the HUD beside the in-game clock. Settings are personal and local. No Sandbox Options are required. Compatibility Compatible with: Existing Single Player saves Hosted Multiplayer servers Common resolutions and window-size changes Other mods that do not block the same HUD area Possible conflicts: Other HUD mods may overlap the compass in the upper-right corner. Interface overhauls may move or resize the in-game clock. Enable dragging and move the compass when overlap occurs. Mini Compass adds no world objects or permanent gameplay data. Current Limitations No waypoints, map markers, GPS routing, or minimap features. HUD overlap may occur with other interface mods. Dedicated-server runtime validation is pending. Troubleshooting Confirm that the Workshop item and MiniCompass Mod ID are enabled. Restart the game or server after updating. Remove stale or duplicate local copies of older versions. Use Reset Compass Position when the HUD is off-screen. Test with only Mini Compass enabled when checking a conflict. Keep it close, train it well and it will become a sharp little warning system—with teeth. Breed features Tiny but alert Chihuahuas detect zombies slightly earlier than other breeds. Their wider perception radius makes them excellent early-warning companions. Keen Eye / Ojo al detalle While a fed and loyal Chihuahua is by your side, it helps you notice small details around you and increases your foraging vision in Search Mode. A starving or disloyal Chihuahua provides no bonus. Fast obedience, limited combat Chihuahuas gain Obedience experience quickly, but their Combat experience develops more slowly. They can attack zombies and help knock them down, but they normally cannot finish zombies on their own. Urban spawning Stray Chihuahuas can appear around houses and urban locations. They have an increased chance of appearing near pet shops, veterinary clinics, hair salons, barber shops, beauty salons, spas and densely populated city areas. Breeding and puppies Chihuahuas can breed with each other and participate in the Companion Dogs breeding system, including Chihuahua puppies. Part of the Companion Dogs family This is an optional breed add-on. Dynamic Missions Dynamic Missions gives established survivors a reason to leave the comfort of a finished base, geared-up stash, and dream garage by adding fresh objectives to the mid and end game. Missions can be expanded, balanced, and customized through a config file or managed in-game with admin/debug powers. How To Use Right-click in the world and open: Player Missions > Manage missions When a mission is offered, open the mission window, accept the job, follow the markers, complete the objective, then return to the mission window to claim your reward. Mission Types Clear Buildings - Sweep an infested building and eliminate the zombies inside. Courier Runs - Recover a marked mission package and deliver it to the assigned crate. Supply Runs - Gather requested items and drop them off at a mission cache. Vehicle Delivery - Pick up a vehicle and drive it to the delivery zone. Trailer Delivery - Tow a trailer from one location to another. Features and Customization Create your own missions: Add even more mission variety editing a config file (or with admin/debug) No hardcoded missions: They are never the same place or type. World map markers and in-world markers for mission locations. Customize mission items, mission rewards, distances, its up to you to make missions as you want them! How to Customize Mission file The easy way is to use Admin (in MP) or debug (in SP). In the same Player Missions you will see a Mission config option. In this screen you can: Disable/Enable missions Change mission parameters Create new missions The manual way - Advanced users only! You may break the mod if you don't know what you are doing! The game will expect a config file 'cbb_missions.json' in server Lua/ folder (not the mod lua folder. If you don't know the folder I'm talking about, use the admin/debug mode). You can use the existing server script \
