description: SquareGrail's Simple Occupations Hello! I am SquareGrail and this is my mod of simple occupations. This is my first ever mod on any game. I fell in love with Project Zomboid last year and wanted to give something back to the community. Please keep in mind, this mod was created for people like myself. People who wish to have a balanced experience without any crazy overpowered or game-breaking traits or occupations. Please leave a thumbs up, favorite, and award if you enjoy my mod! It helps with my exposure. This mod uses version 42.19.1 & 42.20.3. Works in Singleplayer & Multiplayer. Recommended to be used in a fresh game. Using in an ongoing run may cause bugs. Features This mod doesn't come with a lot of occupations or traits, but it comes with simple, lore-friendly traits and occupations that add more variety to the game while still keeping it balanced. This mod comes with five different occupations for you to play and three traits that can be purchased: Occupations: Private Eye A nocturnal sleuth, skilled in guns and staying light on their feet. Wanderer A battle-hardened nomad proficient in venturing the wilderness, and an expert of spear combat. Pizza Courier Proficient in pizza cutter combat, and faster driving. Football Player Adept in running, fitness, and melee combat. Researcher An astute observer trying to understand the world and the oddities of the Knox Virus, they wield knowledge in first aid and are great at absorbing information. Traits: Skulker +1 Sneaking Ranch Hand +1 Animal Care Speed Loader +1 Reloading This is an all-in-one mod. You do not need any other mods or anything else to make it work. Possible Incompatibilities 10 Years Later Professions and Occupations Occupations Expertises & Balance Mar Traits Compatibilities SOTO More Traits Some What Traits Redundancies Please be aware that this mod was create for a more Vanilla friendly experience. If you play with other trait and occupation mods, you may see additional traits or possible similar occupations that may do the same things that you see in this mod. For example; our mod provides Ranch Hand; which gives you +1 Animal care. SOTO also has a trait called Animal Friend which gives you +1 Animal care. These overlaps do not break the game, just be aware of overlap. Meet the Creators and Artists Absolutely no AI was used in the creation of the art of this mod. The sprite art of all the occupations and traits was done by the_jack. He was the main artist and my partner in helping me create this mod. Court Jester created both the Private Eye Spiffo and Wanderer Spiffo. L0st_illusi0n colored both the Private Eye Spiffo and Wanderer Spiffo. The code for the mod was done by myself, SquareGrail. I am entirely new to coding and this took a lot of trial and error. I used VScode for most of my work and learning. It's not perfect, and I'm sure its flawed in many ways, but it all works and I'm glad I was able to give back to the community in this way. Thank You Support me on Ko-fi! Modpacking or reuploading is not allowed as long as the original version is present. We disapprove of any of the art being taken and put into AI, however we cannot stop you. Otherwise, this mod is open source and can be built upon and code can be used if you wish. I want to thank Somewhatfrog for talking with me about my mod and helping me understand some of the code a bit better. I also want to thank HydetheBooty98 and G00SE_ for their amazing work and inspiring me to try creating something myself. Disclaimer I am new to this community and coding as a whole. Any mod that changes occupations, traits, or overwrites them may cause this mod to be incompatible or possibly throw errors. The mods listed in the compatibilities and incompatibilities are what I know for sure works and what will more than likely will throw errors. Workshop ID: 3773667690 Mod ID: SquareGrailProfession

It is recommended to start a new save to install or update the map. Old saves may contain cached chunks from the previous version. description: Who were you before the world ended? READ ME - DISCLAIMER This mod is a WIP. as new features are introduces there is always a likelihood you might lose your saves or they might become corrupted. As much as is possible i will attempt to avoid this from happening but as I work on it, it cannot be guaranteed currently. Project Zomboid tells you how you died. This Is Your Life gives you a life worth remembering first. This Is Your Life replaces vanilla character creation with a fully themed, in-world experience. File and reload complete profession-and-trait builds for future characters. Kentucky Identification Record — Create your name, body, voice, hair, clothing, and final appearance through a complete DMV-inspired replacement for the vanilla appearance screen. Responsive Presentation — Every custom screen scales with the game window and resolution. Your Hometown Matters Every origin: Spawns your character in the selected town. When Origin Traits are enabled, reveals local map knowledge your character would reasonably possess. When Origin Traits are enabled, grants an Origin: Town trait visible on the character sheet. This Is Your Voice This Is Your Voice is an optional roleplay system that gives your survivor contextual internal thoughts and spoken reactions as they interact with the world. Responses are shaped primarily by your survivor's personality, traits, and growing experience. The system reacts to combat pressure, zombie kills, injuries, skill gains, survival needs, weather, buildings, vehicles, looting, crafting, repairs, reading, wound treatment, and other tracked actions. Personality-Driven Reactions — Cautious, practical, and aggressive survivors respond differently to the same experiences, with additional trait- and profession-sensitive lines where appropriate. Varied Dialogue — Large dialogue banks, probability, cooldowns, repetition limits, and situational rules keep reactions from becoming constant or predictable. description: Working Tarot Cards! Feel like Madame Nazar. About the mod: Adds functionality to an existing in-game item: tarot cards. The mod lets you draw cards through the UI and show them to other players. The mod also features its own card guide, detailing card meanings and how to interpret them. You can check out the mod's features in this video! User Guide: First, you need to find the cards in the game. Once you do, you'll be able to explore all the mod's features. Right-click on the Tarot deck, and two additional options will appear in the context menu: “Draw a card” and “Open the catalog of cards.” Draw a card: When you click this option, the mod's main interface will open: - The card you drew - The name of this card - A brief description of the card's meaning And 4 buttons: - "Show the card to nearby players" - "Open the card in the catalog" - "Draw another card" (and the number of cards remaining in the deck) - "Close" Show the card to nearby players: By tapping this button, you'll show your card to every player within a 3-tile radius. In turn, the player will only see the card, its name, and a close button. However, this button has a 5-second cooldown. The button shows when the cooldown ends Open the card in the catalog: When you click this button, a card catalog will appear, with the page open to the card you drew. There, you can find the full, more detailed, and comprehensive meaning of the card, as well as its reversed interpretation. Draw another card: You will draw a new card from the deck. At the same time, the card counter on the button will update to the current value. New cards drawn using this button will never be repeated. If you draw a card, regardless of which side it shows, it won't appear again. When you run out of cards in your deck, the interface will close. Close: Close the menu. You can also close menus from this mod by pressing the ESC key. Open the card catalog When you click this option, the mod's interface will open, displaying a catalog of all the cards in the mod. There, you can find the full, more detailed, and comprehensive meaning of any card, as well as its reversed version. If you've drawn cards, an additional option will appear in the context menu: “Draw the last card again.” When you click it, you'll see the card you drew last. In this mode, you can't draw any more cards from the deck. The mod has been translated into English, Russian, and Ukrainian. !!!Inaccuracies are possible!!! description: v42.20_2.46 由于一直想体验一下末世系统，但是没找到和我想的比较像的，就用AI做了一个。当前测试环境 B42.20，100%纯AI制作，修复维护听天由命。 纯正义mod，可以考虑加点提难度的一起玩。虽然我什么都没加，也天天开饭。 【这是什么】 一个把任务、商店、回收、银行、成长、自动装填、机器人同伴、家园传送放进同一套界面的中文系统型 MOD。 使用实体系统币作为主要货币。系统币可以通过击杀、任务、回收和交易获得，也会用于购买、升级、传送、医疗和其他系统服务。 【怎么打开】 进入游戏后点击屏幕上的 GS 悬浮入口，或按默认 N 键打开/关闭主系统。顶部“设置”中可以修改按键；常用动作也可以放在系统快捷栏中。 第一次使用建议先看主界面的“说明”，再按需要领取空间终端、仓库核心或购买自动装填机。 【任务与成长】 任务包含待接取、进行中、追踪、倒计时、奖励和失败惩罚；可以手动放弃，也可以开启按游戏小时自动提交已完成任务。 升级页提供人物负重、属性成长、天赋改造和医疗服务。人物负重升级会按当前角色实际接口测算和刷新，不需要死亡后重新购买。 天赋可以购买正面效果或移除负面效果；医疗提供感染检查、伤势治疗和病毒治愈。 【商城与回收】 商城支持分类、搜索、分页和批量购买。回收解锁的商品可以隐藏、恢复或在隐藏管理中确认删除。 原版物品栏多选后右键可“回收”“回收并上架”或“仅上架”。保护物、钥匙、无价值物、不可回收物和已上架物会按模式智能跳过。 家具按具体世界贴图区分，床、货架等不同组件不会再只按同一个物品类型混在一起。 新增了抽奖券 【银行】 支持活期存取、自动存现金、贷款、提前还款和稳健/平衡/激进风险理财。 旧存档中的死期存单仍可支取，但当前版本不再创建新死期。 银行页可整理背包中的零散系统币，尽量换成大面额；死亡只影响活期规则，不直接扣除理财。 【系统自动装填机】 商城可购买自动装填机。它把随身散装弹药按具体弹种保存为数字账本，支持存入、取出和手动装填随身独立弹匣。 快速换弹动作完成后可自动补充弹匣；多台装填机按同弹种余额从低到高消耗。不会修改枪械内置弹仓。 【机器人同伴与维护】 单人模式可培养代码绘制的像素战斗无人机，包含跟随、守卫、攻击、灵视、守护和爆裂等能力；多人当前不运行机器人战斗逻辑。 商城提供系统修复组件、耐久强化核心和车辆修复模块，可处理手持装备或车辆的对应耐久问题。 【家园、快捷与管理】 可设置家园、回家、返回出发点和临时传送点；传送包含确认、费用和安全落点检查。 沙盒选项负责新世界初始规则，系统管理页负责当前世界运行时配置。诊断页可查看同步、等待命令和错误状态，方便多人排查。 【多人说明】 商城、回收、银行、任务、升级、医疗和自动装填等关键操作由服务端重新验证，并带操作防重。 Workshop ID: 3773949382 Mod ID: GodSystem_CN

Fork of Bandits by Slayer. Original mod: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3268487204 All credit goes to the original author. This fork only patches errors, never behaviour. Rebased on the author's 42.20 update: every version folder is upstream's own with the fixes below on top. Anything the author has since fixed himself is dropped rather than kept. Still broken in 42.20 Missing square on the per-frame path A character has no square while it is between tiles, while its chunk unloads, and while its corpse is processed. About thirty places assumed one is always there, on code that runs every frame for every bandit - a single one of them threw 713 times in 90 seconds. Each throw aborts whatever the bandit was doing, so it stops fighting, reloading and retreating until its square resolves. On the task path it is worse: the task is never cleared, so it throws again every following frame and the bandit is stuck for good. In multiplayer only the client that owns the bandit runs this, so it looks broken for one player and fine for everyone else. All thirty are guarded; nothing is rewritten and no behaviour changes. Bandits working on a vehicle at the edge of the loaded world The vehicle task reached for its square without checking it existed, and threw once per frame for as long as the bandit held the task. It now ends the task cleanly instead. Bandit bases had no water The water barrel was filled using two methods build 42 no longer has, and the failure happened before the barrel was placed - so it never appeared on the square at all. It is now placed first and filled through its fluid container, the way vanilla fills a rain barrel. A night check that could never fire The hour condition was impossible to satisfy, and the trait test used a form build 42 ignores. The branch was dead twice over. Bandits kept the weapon they looted The death loot was rebuilt from a stale copy of the bandit's gear, so a newly picked up weapon never reached it. The server never rebuilt the list at all - its copy stayed as it was at spawn. Both now update, on a weapons change only. Bandit corpses: empty, then random, then missing the weapon Death loot goes into an engine queue that is emptied into the body once, at death. Nothing in the mod ever filled it at the right moment, so corpses came up empty. The first fix drained that queue by hand, which also rolled fresh vanilla loot into any bag the bandit carried - and it repeated on every shot fired, so identical bandits dropped wildly different things. The second wiped the inventory before refilling it, which deleted real gear whenever it ran with an incomplete picture, and it does run that way: a bandit that swung once and then fired lost the weapon it was holding. Now nothing is ever removed. What is already there is left alone, and rebuilt items are added only when an equivalent is missing, so repeated calls neither duplicate nor delete. Clothing becomes real lootable gear instead of a texture. The ID card, which used to be thrown away by the same cleanup, is built on the same path as everything else. A bandit filling water or fixing a generator got stuck for good Three call sites passed no bandit data at all, on the worst possible path: the failure skips the task cleanup, so the task stays finished-but-not-removed and throws again every frame. The data is now looked up when it is missing, and a zombie that has none simply returns. Corpse handling on the server Build 42.20 removed the method the mod used to lay a bandit down, and its replacement is not reachable from Lua. It fired every time a bandit lay on the ground at zero health, so the error counter climbed constantly and corpses could be left unresolved. Guarded, with the author's own earlier fallback - still present in 42.20, and still sitting as a comment right above the call. Smashing a vehicle window threw in multiplayer The message telling the server about the damage was sent with no sender and no damage value, so it failed every time a bandit hit a car window with someone inside. The sibling function that sends the same message gets both right; this one was written from it and lost them. Fixed upstream in 42.20, so dropped from this fork - the removed corpse method in two more places - a missing room-id check - an item transmit call that no longer exists, at 14 sites - a player check that used the wrong capitalisation and so never matched The author's update did not touch the 42.12 to 42.18 folders, so those keep every fix they already had. Only 42.20 was rebuilt. Notes - Drop-in replacement: mod id is still Bandits2, so existing worlds and server configs work unchanged. - Unsubscribe from the original mod to avoid a duplicate mod id. - Multiplayer: every player on the server needs this same version (Lua checksum must match). - This fork will be retired as soon as the original author picks the rest of these up. Since 42 unstable released it always frustrated me that Zombies can't attack animals. IndieStone prevented that direct targeting at a lower level in the game engine. This mod works around that (best effort) to provide a more realistic animal / zombie interaction sequence. Now, zombies, in addition to being attracted to animal noise (and simply stressing out the animals), will actually chase them down and attempt to kill the animals and eat the carcasses afterwards. "If you enjoy this mod, please take a second to give it a thumbs up! It helps with steam's workshop visibility scoring immensely." Key Features Zombies pursue nearby animals, close in, and kill them. They speed up as they close on livestock, the same way they do on a player - without this, shamblers could never catch a healthy animal in the open. Animals slow down when wounded, so a chase actually ends instead of running forever. After a kill, zombies gather and feed on the carcass. (single player only atm) Zombies that feed become satiated: they sit down to rest and are slow to notice you for a couple of in-game hours (configurable, wakes if approached or hurt). (single player only atm) Meat from a zombie-killed animal is unsafe to eat. Wild animals - deer, rabbits and the rest - are hunted too, not just livestock. Animals (males from aggressive species) will fight back Male animals - Bulls, rams, boars and roosters (and Stallions from horse mod) charge zombies once they are wounded, goring and knocking them down. Enraged animals can be dangerous to the player as well, so stay away from a charging bull.... The herd defends its own (single player only atm) Males answer for their herd: when a female or young animal is chased, the nearest male of its species enrages and comes for the attackers - a charging bull shrugs off bites and can floor a whole crowd. Mothers defend their young too: a cow, sow, ewe, hen or turkey hen stays near her juvenile, escorts it when zombies give chase, and rams the zombie that closes on it. If the young dies, the mother flees, broken. Zombies prefer to chase juveniles, but the young are small and shifty - hard for a zombie to land a clean bite on. Both defenses have their own sandbox toggles, and every species can be individually included or excluded from targeting. Sandbox options Zombie speed-up when locked on an animal target, aggro radius, damage that zombies and animals inflict (to each other, and animals to player) and whether animals fight back at all is configurable Sandbox settings are stored per save, so changing a default only affects NEW saves. To change these on an existing save, edit them in the in-game Sandbox Options and then restart the game. Mod Compatibility Companion Dogs is supported. Companion dog is targetable if configured in sandbox. Wild and stray dogs ARE valid targets, provided wild animals are included and their "Wild Dogs Invincible" option is off. Horse Mod is also supported, considered livestock. Defaults to not being a valid target, which can be changed in sandbox. Ridden horses are not covered, the horse mod already has a targeting solution in place for horse/rider damage. Cat Mod is supported - zombies won't attack cats because cats won't flee zombies. Notes B42.20+ only. Can be added to an existing save. Safe to remove mid-save, restores anything it changes on a zombie or animal, and cleans up after itself if disabled. By default any zombie hunting an animal becomes faster by 1 tier (slow shambler -> fast shambler -> sprinter), returns to normal speed the moment it gives up - without that, shamblers simply cannot catch a healthy animal in open ground. Set "Speed near livestock" to "all become sprinters" for a more exciting experience, or Off if you would rather livestock only be at risk when cornered. Multiplayer ALPHA support is in, see Discussions for details. Future Plans Possibly make compatible with 'infected animals' mod (not sure though, install base is low so even though there is synergy there, it might not be worth the effort). Have initial support for velociraptor mod ready, but that mod is rapidly changing so I'm holding off deploying since support might get broken by new changes. I use Claude for help writing the code, I am a software tester by occupation and I design all the features and rigorously test every build. In my job everyone on the dev team uses claude every day for help with our work - prototyping, coding and testing. I am not an expert with PZ code (although to be fair I am learning a ton each day) and I never could have built out everything myself without leveraging these tools. If you absolutely can't stand anything that uses AI for building mods then look elsewhere or build your own mod..... Workshop ID: 3774007514 Mod ID: ZombiesTargetAnimals

Multiplies every player's carry capacity. Default is 2.5x, configurable from 0.25x to 10x in the sandbox settings. Read this first: the game applies a hard cap of 100 to how much a character can physically carry, and re-applies it every time the value is read, so no mod can lift it. A multiplier of 2 already reaches that cap. Anything higher still raises the capacity shown in your inventory and pushes the encumbrance penalties further out - so you carry the same 100 with no slowdown instead of being weighed down - but it cannot fit any more in. Works in singleplayer and multiplayer. How it is done Carry capacity is two separate numbers in this game, enforced by different code. The one the inventory header draws is what the encumbrance moodle and the movement penalties use - scaling it moves the point where you start slowing down. The one that decides whether an item will physically go in is a different field entirely, and vanilla leaves it at 50 for every character. Scaling only the first is what produces the classic "the bar says 125 but it still stops at 50". Both are scaled here, so the number you see is the number you get. The hard limit is capped at 100 by the game itself, on every read, so it cannot be modded past that. A multiplier of 2 already reaches it. Higher settings still raise the displayed capacity and push the encumbrance penalties further out, they just cannot move the wall any further. Item weights are NOT modified. Older carry-weight mods worked by shrinking every item in the game, which leaks into vehicle mass, fishing, fuel burn times and crafting, and needs a pile of patches to hold together. Nothing of the sort is needed here. Sandbox options Carry Capacity Multiplier (default 2.5) - capacity as a multiple of the normal amount. Keep Strength Trait Bonuses (default off) - when off, every character gets exactly the multiplier above whatever traits they picked. When on, the Strong / Stout / Weak / Feeble carry bonus is applied underneath it, so a Strong character at 2.5 ends up on 3.75x. Either way the traits keep all of their other effects. Notes Safe to add to an existing save. Before uninstalling, set the multiplier to 1.0 and load your character in once. The displayed capacity is never written to the save and reverts on its own, but the hard limit is part of the save file, so it keeps whatever value it had when the mod was last active. Setting 1.0 first puts it back to the vanilla 50. Sandbox values are baked into a world when it is created, so an existing world keeps the settings it was made with. For multiplayer the mod has to be installed on the server as well as the clients, like any other mod. Build 42.20+. Mod ID: CarryWeightMultiplier Workshop ID: 3774013360 Mod ID: CarryWeightMultiplier

description: Down But Not Out : Alternate Death and Revival Mechanics A Multiplayer oriented, Roleplay First, highly customisable mod for knockdowns, wounds and revival. Tired of bleeding out after a nasty scratch to your neck or being pumped full of lead? Now, instead of dying, you'll drop to your knees. You can wait, you can crawl to safety. But someone will have to pick you up, or you'll die all the same. Knockdowns Fatal damage puts you on the ground with a timer instead of killing you. You can still crawl, use some of your gear, and give up if nobody is coming. On the floor, you're impervious to damage from players and zombies alike. If you get picked up, you'll carry a Knockdown Moodle. Each one fades after five minutes. Get knocked down three times in quick succession and the fourth one will kill you instead of knocking you down. Getting dragged down is the exception, that will kill you on the spot. How long you can survive without being picked up, how long knockdowns take to fade amongst others can be modified and the system itself can be turned off. Wounds Every real death leaves a Wound behind, and they take an hour to fade. Die three times in a short span and the fourth is permanent. Just like knockdowns, fade time continues while you're offline, so you don't have to AFK in-game for it to pass. How long Wounds take to fade, carrying your injuries through a revive, amongst other things can be adjusted, and the system can be turned off. Saving and respawning You can use a bed to save and restore your progress, and to set a respawn point. You can toggle the respawn mechanic and adjust what can be used for saving, restoring and respawning, instead of a bed. Loot You leave behind a loot cache where you die. For a while, nobody else can open it and take it away. You'll have a window of opportunity to get your items back before the cache unlocks, and eventually despawns. Whether or not the cache is locked, how long it'll be locked for, and how long the cache exists before despawning can be adjusted. Works in co-op and on dedicated servers, singleplayer not yet supported. Requests, suggestions, comments, bugs? Feel free to post in the comments. Looking for a place to RP? Come join us on Deadline Update 1.4: Fixed an issue causing non-vanilla traits and skills not being saved and loaded properly, causing the loading to break Fixed a rare issue causing the knockdown screen to persist after death. Update 1.3: Potential fix for rare cases where respawning with the sandbox setting 'Clothing Only' doesn't spawn bags/containers in inventory. Added a new moodle that makes it more obvious if you are on your final Wound / Life Added Sandbox options for the following: - Revive with entire inventory / Disable Loot Cache - Wound Amount / Life amount. Set to 0 for no lives. If set to 0, any full death is a permanent death. Alternatively disable the 'Enable Wounds' setting if you want permanent deaths with no lives. - Count knockdowns. If disabled, the mod no longer puts a limit on how many knockdowns you can have in a short period of time. - Bleedout timer. If disabled, there's no timer when knocked down. Update 1.2: Potential fix for rare cases where moodle data isn't loaded from the server Added Sandbox options for the following: - Health Drain when knocked down - Death Cache never unlocks - Death Cache never despawns Keep clothes on revival or set a custom outfit that is spawned and worn when revived Update 1.1: Skill XP from Books are now properly calculated. Books and Recipes read, VHS watched are now stored when saving your character Added two new Sandbox Options, allowing you to enable being attacked by zombies or players while downed. Credit where it's due This mod can be added to and extended by anyone in the community, but credit must be given to the original author within the files of the mod - and posted alongside the mod wherever it roams. description: Gives you a VISUAL indication of the direction and volume of nearby world sounds. A coloured arrow flashes around your character pointing toward the sound; colour and flash rate indicate distance. This is an updated build 42.20 port of Nolan Ritchie's original Sound Direction Indicator. All credit for the mod itself goes to the original author. What was fixed Build 42 removed the old HasTrait("Deaf") string API in favour of the CharacterTrait enum, so the mod threw an exception on every single world sound and no indicator ever appeared. The trait checks now use hasTrait(CharacterTrait.DEAF / KEEN_HEARING / HARD_OF_HEARING). Also fixed: the arrow now re-aims as you move while it is on screen (the original had a dot-vs-colon call bug that silently disabled this), a leftover debug keybind on the Home key was removed, and the player reference is now resolved live so death and respawn no longer leave the arrow aiming from your old position. Accessibility If you play without sound, this is the mod that makes ambient audio cues legible. Deaf, Hard of Hearing and Keen Hearing traits all scale the detection radius as intended. Survival Planner List Survival Planner adds customizable planning journal with tasks, sub-tasks and automated completion if you set it Create plans, split larger goals into subtasks, track the items you need, mark destinations on the world map, and let the planner automatically recognize your progress while you play. Main Features Create and organize plans Create active or planned objectives, edit their titles, assign custom icons, reorder them by dragging, and move completed plans into a separate archive. Subtasks Break larger plans into smaller steps and complete them individually. Multiple item goals Attach several required items to a plan or subtask and set a separate quantity for each one. Inventory and loot highlighting Tracked items are easier to notice in your inventory and nearby containers. Automatic completion Optionally complete a plan when all of its item goals have been reached. World map integration Select a destination on the world map and link it to a plan. Navigation indicators Tracked destinations can display movable on-screen indicators with a directional arrow, distance to the target, and the linked plan name. Arrival goals Optionally complete a plan after reaching its destination. The default arrival radius is 5 tiles. Custom plan icons Choose from vanilla item icons or a collection of custom-purpose icons. Customizable interface The planner window is movable and resizable and includes several selectable color themes. Quick access Use the movable on-screen planner button or press K to open the journal. The hotkey can be changed in the Mod Option settings. Sandbox settings Inventory scanning and navigation systems can be adjusted or disabled through sandbox options. How It Works First craft a Survival Planner and keep it in your main inventory or an equipped bag. Open it using the on-screen planner icon, the context menu, or the configurable K hotkey. Press create plan Set it's name, link an items if needed, select icon, optional map marker and optional automatic completion You can add sub-tasks to the main plan by pressing add subtask button on active plan Subtasks supports only item tracking Plans are divided into several categories: Active — plans you are currently working on. Planned — objectives saved for later. Done — completed plans. Item Tracking — Just specific items highlight. To edit the contents of the planner, your character needs a suitable writing tool and an eraser. Once editing is available, change everything or add new sub-tasks. ❗NOTE: when choosing icon or item there will be a little lag due to actual number of items and icons. Map Navigation A plan can be linked to a location selected on the world map. When navigation is enabled for that plan: A custom marker appears on the map. description: Any lifeform that disrespects anime and otaku culture is not welcome here. If you have the time to insult me, you might as well spend that time finding a mod you actually enjoy. After all, I'm not holding a gun to your head and forcing you to play this one! 【Introduction】 To transcend time and space is humanity's only path to survival in this vast galaxy. ---Father of Lilies--- Mod Overview This is an anime-style mod designed for Project Zomboid Build 42 Stable. This mod has been in development for a very long time. It continues the style of my previous Project Anime mod while incorporating an immeasurable amount of passion and effort into this anniversary release. With 120+ clothing items, 25+ weapons, and countless miscellaneous items covering clothing, melee weapons, firearms, food, backpacks, and a trading system, it is a comprehensive content mod. There are currently 16 unique outfit sets with distinct styles, and more are still being added! The Anniversary Edition of Project Anime has already integrated the KKS library directly into the mod, meaning no prerequisite mods are required anymore. (Anime Shader, Cute Girl Voice, and Clothing Holes not Display are NOT required. However, I highly recommend using them together for the best experience!) English Language Support Available! Core Features 1. Anime Body: Essentially, it is a full-body outfit that transforms you into a cute anime girl once equipped. It can also be upgraded to improve its performance, so make sure to check your crafting menu! There are currently six adorable characters available. Two of them are the cute Moelotl race from RimWorld: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3292351432. You may also discover more... easter eggs related to the Moelotl. In addition, there are experiences waiting for you involving the chairwoman of a futuristic military-tech corporation, the young lady of a fallen noble family, her personal maid, an incompetent shinigami, and more. 2. Various Outfits: To clearly distinguish Project Anime clothing from vanilla or other modded clothing, every outfit has a strictly corresponding numerical ID in its name. One important thing to note: due to the massive body proportion differences between the Anime Body and vanilla character models, these outfits are not compatible with vanilla clothing or clothing mods designed around Project Zomboid's default body shape. However, the number of outfits currently included is already enough to keep your eyes entertained for quite a long time. Thanks to updates to my KKS engine, creating new outfits has become significantly easier, and more clothing will continue to be added in future updates. If there are outfits you particularly like, feel free to provide me with Koikatsu (Sunshine) character cards (Koikatsu 1 or 2) along with the corresponding clothing ZIP mods or clothing cards. Perhaps one day your favorite outfit will appear in a future update! 3. Trade with WESTTECH® Corporation: When enter the game, players automatically receive a pager that allows them to trade with WESTTECH® Corporation. Many items from both this mod and the vanilla game can be traded. If you're missing something or want a specific item, why not ask them if they have it? How to Properly Play This Mod 1. New Save: When creating your character: Step 1: On the occupation screen, choose any scenario story marked with [Project Anime] according to your preference, and select any additional traits you want. Step 2: It is recommended to wear nothing during character creation. After entering the game, you will receive the items related to the chosen story. 2. Existing Save: After adding this mod, you may notice zombies dropping items called "WESTTECH® Credit" when killed. Using just one credit allows you to directly exchange it for the pager used for trading in this mod. Use the pager along with more credits to obtain additional items! Mod Compatibility This mod is compatible with the vast majority of other mods. However, please note that it may conflict with other weapon mods, especially those that include suppressor scripts. Quick Q&A Q: Will there be more outfits? A: Absolutely. Q: Where do I obtain credits? A: Zombies can drop them, and selling valuable items through the pager can earn you a large amount of points. Q: How do I obtain the other outfits? A: Zombies have a small chance to drop clothing packs. WESTTECH® Corporation also offers complete outfit pack trading services. Q: Can all characters wear all outfits? A: Yes. Since all characters use the same body model, every outfit can be worn by every character. For example, the young lady can wear the maid outfit. Q: Can outfits from different clothing packs be mixed and matched? A: Of course. (Some combinations may have clipping.) Q: Is multiplayer supported? A: Multiplayer works perfectly fine. This mod contains very little Lua scripting, so you generally don't need to worry about script errors or updates breaking functionality. Q: What type of players is this mod intended for? A: First of all, this is a Japanese anime-style mod, not a realistic Western animation style. The characters and clothing models are highly stylized, cute, and cartoonish. Aside from firearms, the overall balance is fairly close to vanilla. However, since scenario stories grant starting equipment, increasing the survival difficulty is still recommended. Gameplay Tips from the Mod Author 1. WESTTECH® Corporation is far more powerful than you imagine. If you have any questions, try asking them through your pager. 2. Nearly all consumables in this mod can be repeatedly obtained through trading. 3. Energy weapons reload extremely quickly. However, there are times when you shouldn't rely on them too much. 4. Use the "Repair Toolbox" and "Fuel Battery" from this mod to restore weapon durability. 5. You should obtain and equip the WESTTECH® Assisted Targeting System as soon as possible. 6. WESTTECH® Corporation does not sell a cure for the zombie virus. 7. Carefully consider whether you truly want to sell rare items from this mod. 8. There is an item called Thermal Lining. Once equipped, you can dress lightly even during the coldest winter. 9. Need better protection but don't want to wear clipping armor from other mods? Try Protective Lining! It's invisible and can be upgraded for even greater protection. 10. Please treat Chairwoman Rironn kindly and cherish your life. Do not exploit suicide to farm unique items. 11. The body models and backpack equipment in this mod can both be upgraded to improve their performance. Check your crafting menu! 12. Before upgrading any backpack, please take out all items in the backpack. Otherwise, they may disappear. 13. If one firearm must be crowned the strongest, it is unquestionably the H-02r Charged Rifle. However, its price is extremely high. If luck is on your side, you might find one on a corpse. description: Dark Presence My first big mod :) Something got into the Knox County dark, and it doesn't want you to see. After nightfall some of the dead come back wrong. They're wrapped in a skin of darkness that swallows bullets and blades whole. You can put a full magazine into a Taken and it won't so much as stumble. The one thing that touches them is light. Hold a flashlight beam, a road flare, your headlights, or plain daylight on one long enough and the dark burns off it. Then it dies like anything else. Taken carry a darkness shield you have to burn down with light before you can kill them. A steady beam held on one drops it fast. Ambient light does it slowly. A faint ring marks the one you're burning and tightens as the dark comes off it, so you can see how close you are. They own the dark. Shielded Taken don't scare off, and the night hides them. How fast one reaches you depends on what it is: some sprint, some come at a walk, all of them take the same light to break. Finish what you start. A Taken you burned but didn't put down will knit its shield back together once it's in real darkness again. Burn one all the way and it's done for good — that part is permanent, no matter how dark it gets. Light is a refuge. Stand in a well-lit doorway or room and the Taken will not come in after you; they gather out at the edge of the light and wait. Step back out into the dark and they are on you immediately. Your own aimed beam is the exception — that's the weapon, and they'll press through it. Weather matters. In rain, fog and storms the dark bleeds in early and only the light you're carrying will cleanse a shield. A lantern in a lit house won't cut it in a downpour. There's a story being written about your survivor. Eleven pages, third person, by a man at a typewriter who died a long time ago and can't stop typing. The Taken carry it. Kill one and it might drop the next chapter you haven't read. If you'd rather not go looking, there's a dead radio frequency that only speaks in the small hours. Sit by it and the author will read you a page himself. Every page tells you something that's already on its way, and every page costs you. One turns the dead toward your light. One kills the power. One teaches the dark the sound of your breathing. The further you read, the harder it wants you, and the ending it has written for you is a small, tidy death, alone in the last of the dark. The more of the manuscript you read, the more the dark drinks the daylight. Colour bleeds out of the world, the nights get deeper, and the sun starts setting earlier and rising later. Read enough of it and you'll lose real hours of daylight off both ends of the day. The author has an ending in mind for you, and it isn't a kind one. But the margins of the manuscript argue with him. There's a second hand in there, scared and hurried, and if you read far enough it leaves you a way to write a different ending than the one the dark wrote. Getting there is its own thing. So is what it asks of you. Read all eleven pages and find out. Sandbox options for most of it: when the dark arrives, how fast shields burn and whether they heal, how many Taken, ambient spawns, the radio, the Leak, walker possession, dread, the shield rings, and the rest. You can switch the whole story off and keep just the light-versus-Taken survival if that's all you're after. The mod's own music and the Taken's voices have their own volume sliders, on a rebindable key (F8 by default), so you can set them where you want them without touching the rest of the game's sound. You also decide what's left when it's over. By default, seeing the story through ends it: the dark leaves for good and Knox County goes back to an ordinary apocalypse. If you'd rather it never quite let go, set it to linger instead, and a weaker shadow of the dark stays with you for the rest of the run. In the base mod, a Taken can still perceive you while you're standing in light — it just won't walk into it. The optional True Dark add-on removes that last gap: with it, a Taken in light genuinely cannot see or hear you at all, full stop, and one out in the dark sees further than it should. To do that it has to reach deeper into the game than a normal mod can, so it runs on the ZombieBuddy framework and needs a launch-option tweak. It's fiddly to set up and completely optional. Important Notes Build 42 (42.20). Built and tested for singleplayer. Multiplayer supported but only with Story Mode option being off. Safe to drop into an existing save. If you want it gone, do it after the story's finished rather than mid-run. Plays nicely with most things. Anything that hard-overrides the climate or the lighting could clash. Mods For Better Experience Music from the Alan Wake Original Score by Petri Alanko. All rights to Alan Wake and its music belong to Remedy Entertainment; this is a non-commercial fan mod. Stay in the light. Good luck surviving. Bug reports and feedback welcome. Also check out my other mods in my collection! Your support is much appreciated! description: The world ended. The trains didn't. ✔ Built for Build 42.20 stable WHAT · WHERE · HOW One drivable locomotive (EMD GP7) + 61 working switches across the map's rail network Location: Muldraugh engine shed (spawns on first approach, safe to add mid-save) To drive her: the Railroader profession (4 pts) — or read the operating manual she carries in her cab. Any survivor can learn. Quick start: board with E, tap W to crank the diesel, press R to set the reverser forward, then W/S throttle notches and Space brake Fuel: diesel only (depot tank, Valley Station tank, or jerrycan) Controller / Steam Deck: the whole cab is on a gamepad since 1.1 — not yet tested on real hardware, so reports are welcome Singleplayer only for now. No multiplayer or split-screen yet English & Russian throughout, including the notebook and the album One locomotive: an EMD GP7 in weathered Knox & Louisville navy, road number 800, cold in the Muldraugh engine shed. Nobody left it running for you. Not a car with a train skin (no BaseVehicle): the 800 is a world entity riding authored routes over the actual Knox County track, a rigid body on two trucks that overhangs the curves the way 112 tonnes should. WHAT YOU FIND The 800 spawns on your first approach, once per world, and her state is rolled then: diesel from dry to full (enough to go somewhere about two times in three), a battery self-discharging since day one, fuel gone stale, condition as the last crew left it. TWO WAYS INTO THE CAB Take the Railroader profession (4 points; XP toward Mechanics, Maintenance and Electricity) and you know her from minute one, with a photo album of the life before and a pocket notebook that is the mod's whole manual. Or find her and read: every locomotive carries her own operating manual in the cab, and forty minutes with it qualifies you on that model — the last engineer's notebook is aboard too, so you learn which lever is which. No driving skill and no level to grind: an engineer is a certified job. What the profession still buys is the cold morning — a railroader catches a dead diesel more reliably and burns half the battery finding out. RUNNING IT A cold start is an attempt, not a menu option: prime, crank, and it catches or it doesn't. Cold, stale fuel and a tired battery cut the odds, and every crank drains the charge — rain does not, a diesel has no ignition to soak. Once running: eight throttle notches, an interlocked F·N·R reverser, an independent air brake — from notch 8, count your braking distance in hundreds of metres. The HUD is a GP7 control stand: six dials, every needle a real number. Full sound, including a horn and bell fed by the compressor — silent on a dead engine. WHAT GETS IN THE WAY Parked, it is a wall. Rolling, it knocks the dead down; above ~4 m/s (≈15 km/h) it kills. Trees are felled, fences flattened, a car on a crossing is thrown clear. Every hit debits condition; at zero she is OUT OF ORDER — stalled on the rails, and there is no repair in the game yet. Running off a broken rail end at speed or hitting rolling stock hard means DERAILED — permanent in ordinary play, and saved. Drive like the track matters. CAB, STORAGE & FUEL Roof, no wind, warmth once the block is warm (the WATER dial is your comfort gauge); anyone can sleep in the seat, no licence needed. The cab is storage too — 50 units that ride with her, reachable only from the seat, and what you drop from the cab lands beside the track, not under the wheels. Fuel: diesel only — jerrycan, or the finite tanks at the Muldraugh depot and Valley Station. A flat battery needs a running generator nearby. CONTROLS E board / leave · V cab menu (sleep, headlight) · W/S notches 0–8 (tap W with the reverser in neutral to start; tap S at notch 0, stopped, to shut down) · R reverser (neutral, forward, reverse) · Space air brake · Q horn · L bell · F headlight · Shift+F dome light · RMB look around · Right-click a switch to throw the points. On a controller: D-pad up/down throttle (with the diesel off, start and shut down) · D-pad left reverser · D-pad right (hold) cab menu · right stick, click air brake · left bumper horn · right bumper bell · interact climbs in and out. Any binding can be moved from the console. Not yet tested on real hardware — if something sits wrong, say so in the comments. FAQ — short answers Safe to add mid-save? Yes. Back up before removing the mod. Throttle does nothing? You are not qualified yet. Take the Railroader profession, or read the operating manual waiting in her cab. Do I need a new character? No — since 1.1.1 any survivor can read his way into the cab. Derailed — can I put it back? Only with the game's own debug mode on (-debug in the Steam launch options), then right-click the wreck. In a normal game there is no such option, by design — proper re-railing is a later stage. Multiplayer / split-screen? Not yet. Singleplayer only; MP is on the roadmap. Full manual, detailed FAQ and console commands: pinned Manual & FAQ discussion. THE ROAD AHEAD Next: rolling stock — freight cars and a caboose first, then a business car you can couple behind the 800 and live in. Then: a lootable track chart, more spawn points, and multiplayer (a server-authoritative locomotive — a big rebuild, no dates). The pinned Suggestions & Roadmap discussion is where the next line gets written; the best ideas get built and credited. MADE WITH Full transparency: design, mechanics, balance, story and months of testing — me, solo, evenings. Code — AI-assisted under my direction. 3D model — a CC BY asset, heavily modified (see Credits). The album in the film is real, shot with a real camera; the photos printed inside are AI-generated, as is some film artwork. CREDITS EMD GP7 model: "EMD GP7 Western Pacific 713" by Jesper Landin (Sketchfab), CC BY 4.0 — decimated, retextured into the K&L livery, converted for the game engine. Community code review: ifchan — the v1.0.1 optimization pass exists because of it. Cold-start realism consulting: ferreirajc87, a real conductor from the comments. The rebuild: timoshq3 — the Reddit wireframe post that started it. He was right. Supporters: Gunter, Sample, Koralex, Mudyan — they paid for a locomotive nobody charged them for. THE FILMS Every mod I make comes with a short film — watch The Railroader above (the album in it is real and hand-filmed; details in Made With). More stories: The Family Photo · The Window Washer If the 800 earned its keep in your apocalypse: buymeacoffee.com/slavapo · из России: boosty.to/slavapo 112 tonnes, and a licence you had to pay four points for. Take it out of the shed. Workshop ID: 3774360904 Mod ID: Railroader

Lockpicking Skill Lockpicking Skill adds a dedicated Lockpicking skill with level-based failure chances, paperclip break chances, action speed progression, XP rewards, skill books, and extensive Sandbox configuration. Lockpicking is built around a simple and reliable setup: a trusty screwdriver and a paperclip. FEATURES Lockpicking Skill The mod adds a dedicated Lockpicking skill that improves as you successfully and unsuccessfully attempt to pick locks. Your Lockpicking level affects: - Lockpick failure chance - Paperclip break chance - Lockpicking action speed - Overall progression through the skill Vehicle doors can also be lockpicked. TOOLS Lockpicking requires: - Screwdriver - Paperclip The screwdriver is used as part of the lockpicking process while the paperclip acts as the lockpick. Paperclips can break when an attempt fails, making them an expendable resource. FAILURE SYSTEM Lockpicking has a configurable failure system. Failure chances can be configured individually for each progression tier. The failure system can also be completely disabled through the Sandbox settings. LOCKPICKING PROGRESSION The Lockpicking skill is divided into five progression tiers. | Skill Level | Failure Tier | Failure Chance | Break Chance | |-------------|--------------|----------------|--------------| | 1-2 | Tier 1 | 35% | 100% | | 3-4 | Tier 2 | 30% | 95% | | 5-6 | Tier 3 | 20% | 90% | | 7-8 | Tier 4 | 15% | 85% | | 9-10 | Tier 5 | 10% | 80% | The values above are the default settings and can be changed through the Sandbox options. As your Lockpicking skill increases, your chance of successfully picking a lock improves and your paperclips become less likely to break. ACTION SPEED PROGRESSION Higher Lockpicking skill levels also reduce the time required to pick a lock. Default action speed progression: | Skill Level | Speed Multiplier | |-------------|------------------| | 1 | 0.25x | | 2 | 0.50x | | 3 | 0.60x | | 4 | 0.80x | | 5 | 1.00x | | 6 | 1.20x | | 7 | 1.40x | | 8 | 1.60x | | 9 | 1.80x | | 10 | 2.00x | Higher levels allow experienced characters to work through locks considerably faster. The action speed system can also be switched to use a single default multiplier instead of level-based progression. XP SYSTEM Lockpicking provides experience for both successful and failed attempts. Default XP rewards: | Result | XP | |--------|----| | Successful Lockpick | 20 XP | | Failed Lockpick | 10 XP | XP values can be changed through the Sandbox options. An optional XP indicator can display the amount of Lockpicking XP gained after an attempt. SANDBOX CONFIGURATION The Lockpicking system is designed to be highly configurable. Available options include: - Enable or disable lockpick failure - Enable or disable the paperclip break system - Enable or disable the XP indicator - Configure successful lockpicking XP - Configure failed lockpicking XP - Configure failure chance for each skill tier - Configure paperclip break chance for each skill tier - Configure the default action speed - Configure action speed for each skill level - Use either default or level-based action speed This allows the mod to be configured for a more forgiving experience or a much more difficult survival experience. SKILL BOOKS The mod includes five Lockpicking skill books designed to support progression through the skill. Beginner's Bend: Paperclip Tactics Wiggle & Lift: A Novice's Guide to Tumblers Quiet Hands: Intermediate Lock Manipulation The Subtle Click: Advanced Pin Control Master of the Mechanism: Professional Lock Defeat CURRENT DEVELOPMENT This is my first Project Zomboid mod, and the mod is still actively being developed and balanced. Current development is focused on: - Playtesting and balancing the Lockpicking progression - Balancing XP progression - Balancing failure and paperclip break chances - Testing action speed progression - Multiplayer testing - Fixing bugs and compatibility issues - Testing the mod with the current B42 stable release FUTURE PLANS Possible future additions include: - Actual lockpicks as a more durable alternative to paperclips - A very rare Skeleton Key - Skeleton Key providing extremely fast lockpicking - Additional ways to gain Lockpicking XP - Security doors being significantly harder to pick than standard doors - Different lock difficulties based on the type of door or security level - Additional Lockpicking-related items and mechanics - Further progression and balancing options The goal is to keep Lockpicking useful without making it an easy replacement for keys or other methods of accessing secured areas. FEEDBACK As this is my first mod, feedback, bug reports, balance suggestions and ideas for future features are very welcome. Thanks for giving the mod a try! Limited Propane Supply Refill your propane tanks and blowtorches directly from tanks found in the world — but each one now holds a limited, random amount of propane that runs dry with use. How it works Right-click a propane tank or blowtorch lying on the ground to refill it from a nearby source. Works with large Fossoil / Gas2Go storage tanks, small industrial propane tanks, and (optionally) gas station pumps. Automatically finds the closest eligible source within a configurable search radius. The context menu option shows exactly how much propane is left, and greys out once the source is empty. Fully multiplayer-compatible, with server-side stock tracking so every player sees the same numbers. Finite capacity Capacity is measured in portable propane bottles, not liters: a capacity of 50 means the tank can fill 50 full bottles (refilling a blowtorch only costs a small fraction of one bottle). Each tank starts at a random percentage of its capacity (50–90% by default) instead of always full, so not every source you find is guaranteed to be useful. Once a source runs dry, it stays dry — go find another one. Crafting an empty tank Can't find one lying around? Craft an empty propane tank: 2x Sheet Metal, 1x Metal Pipe, 4 uses of a Blowtorch, and a welding mask (kept, not consumed). Requires Welding level 4. The result is an empty tank, ready to be filled at any propane source. Sandbox options Allow refilling at gas pumps (off by default) Allow refilling at small industrial tanks (off by default) Search radius for a nearby propane source (default: 2 tiles) Large storage tank capacity, in propane bottles (default: 50) Small industrial tank capacity, in propane bottles (default: 5) Minimum / maximum initial fill percentage (default: 50–90%) Compatibility Built and tested for Project Zomboid B42.20. Safe to add to or remove from an existing save. Workshop ID: 3774499542 Mod ID: LimitedPropaneSupply

description: Adds the right-click options Climb up the ladder and Climb down the ladder on any ladder in the game, including ones you place yourself. Works in singleplayer and multiplayer. Want to build your own ladders as well? Get the companion mod Build Ladders. The problem it solves In Build 42, several ladders in the base game have the ladderN or ladderW property but not the climbSheetN / climbSheetW flag, which is what the engine checks to let you climb. The result is that the same ladder can be climbed in one orientation but not the other. This affects the metal ladder (industry_railroad_05_37), as well as sewer ladders, wooden ladders, and billboard ladders. How to use it To climb up: stand next to the ladder and right-click on it, or hold E for about half a second. It's a hold rather than a tap because E is the game's Interact key. To climb down: stand at the top, within one tile of the opening, and right-click on the ground. You don't need to see the ladder. The key is rebindable under Options > Key Bindings > Climb Ladders. How it behaves Ladders spanning several floors take you all the way to the top instead of dropping you off halfway. It checks there is somewhere solid to step off before moving you, using the same check the game uses to decide if you can walk onto a tile. If there is nowhere to go, the option is greyed out and says why. You can't climb up with an unsplinted broken leg, or when you're out of breath. Being over your carrying capacity makes it slower and more tiring. Climbing down is never blocked, so you can't get stranded on a roof. Ladders are detected by reading the sprite's ladder properties at runtime, not from a fixed list, so ladders added by other mods work too. Multiplayer Fully supported. The move is confirmed by the server and broadcast to the other clients, so everyone sees you climb rather than watching you walk around below. The server validates each request and rejects anything further than a ladder could reach. Add it to your server's Mods list as usual. Where to get ladders Ladders in the world can be picked up with a crowbar (Carpentry 2) and placed anywhere with a hammer, using the base game's moveable furniture system. This mod then lets you actually climb the one you placed. Companion mod: Build Ladders Build 42 lets you build staircases - wooden, log and welded - but no ladders at all. The sprites have been sitting in the game the whole time, in the carpentry tileset, with their ladder properties already set, and nothing ever used them. Build Ladders adds the recipe they were missing: a wooden ladder in the Carpentry build menu, 4 planks and 8 nails at Carpentry 3, in four orientations. Build it again on the same tile and the new section stacks on top of the last one, so a three-storey building is three builds - and you do all three from the ground. You never have to be up there, which is the whole point, because the build cursor only reaches the level you are standing on. Cheaper and lower level than a staircase on purpose. A ladder is the cheap way up, and in exchange the dead can't follow you. Subscribe to Build Ladders here Details Does not modify the saved world, and adds no items, recipes or tiles. English, Spanish, French, German, Polish, Portuguese (BR), Russian and Chinese. Requires Build 42.15 or newer. Support If this saved you a few rooftop jumps, you can buy me a coffee on Ko-fi. Completely optional - the mod is free and stays free. Workshop ID: 3774776279 Mod ID: SubirEscaleras

Trunks stay visible, so anything you could hit remains in view. Higher speed extends the look-ahead distance, so wrecks and zombies hidden under a canopy are far less likely to catch you by surprise While moving on foot, canopies of XL / XXL trees around you are thinned in all directions. They return to normal when you stand still L-size jumbo trees are not affected by default while driving and on foot to keep the forest scenery intact (indoors covers all three sizes). While on foot, a Mod Options setting can include them When you stop, trees return starting with the ones closest to you. Trees you have already passed are restored automatically as well Trees that do not block your view — such as those on the far side of the road — stay visible Entering a building automatically hides jumbo trees (L / XL / XXL sizes) within 24 tiles. They reappear immediately when you go back outside Normal-sized trees are not affected. Turn it off and apply to restore vanilla rendering instantly for comparison Canopy hiding style (Fade / Trunk only, default: Fade) — how canopies look while driving and on foot Hide road-covering canopies while driving (default: on) — only the canopy is affected; the trunk stays visible Look-ahead distance while driving (Long / Short, default: Long) — choose how far ahead canopies are affected Hide canopies around you while on foot (default: on) On-foot hide range (Standard / Narrow / Minimal, default: Standard) — choose how far around you canopies are affected Include smaller jumbo trees while on foot (default: off) — also fades L-size jumbo trees in addition to XL / XXL. description: Reload All Magazines Reloading a full loadout of magazines one by one is a right-click marathon. This mod collapses it into a single click. Magazines are topped up fullest-first, so you get a complete magazine as early as possible. When ammo is short, this also gives you the highest possible number of full magazines instead of a pile of half-empty ones. Ammo is pulled just in time. description: Get bitten in vanilla and a number starts counting down. Take a pill and it stops. That's the whole of it. I wanted wounds you have to look after. So infections have stages now, antibiotics work as a course, a bone poking through your skin gets worse while you keep walking on it, and you sew your own cuts shut by hand. Most of it can be done badly. The Health tab becomes an examination The body is coloured by how bad it is. Not by what it is. Pain tells you where. What it actually is takes a look: left-click to examine, right-click to treat. Until you've looked, you've got "something is wrong with that arm" and not a diagnosis. First Aid decides how long that takes and how much you get out of it - twelve seconds at zero, three by ten. And it trains itself while you look. Sepsis Leave a wound dirty and it goes bad. Leave it long enough and it's in your blood. You'll feel run down about twelve hours in. That's the warning and it's early enough to act on. Then fever, then you can barely stand, then it kills you. Three days or so if you ignore it. Antibiotics aren't something you swallow once. One pill covers about sixteen hours, the course needs three back to back, and if you let a gap open you lose the ground you gained. Take them too close together and you'll poison yourself instead. Change the dressing while you're at it. A fresh one quarters how fast the wound picks up infection; a rotten one does nothing. Open fracture Bone through skin. Worse every hour it's unsplinted, quieter under a splint, and feeding the infection the whole time. A splint cuts that feed threefold, a clean dressing quarters what's left. Painkillers treat nothing at all, they only hide it. Arms and legs. Needs the Bone Fracture sandbox option, or nothing can break in the first place. Blood loss Costs more than the health bar. You dress it, the bleeding stops, and you stay weak for days afterwards. Poisoning and organs Treatment is something you can get wrong too. Take more than the body can clear and you'll be ill for longer than the overdose lasts: the drug is gone and you're still shaking. And it leaves a mark. A damaged liver clears slower, so the next overdose lands on what's left of the last one. Damaged kidneys flush less away. Alcohol on top of a course is harder on the liver than alcohol alone. Water helps: a hydrated survivor clears twice as fast, and that's the kidneys doing it. Two medicines at once are work for the liver even when neither is over its limit. Nobody tells you any of this. Organs read at First Aid 3; below that you get a bitter taste and yellow hands and have to work it out. Stitching The needle goes in one side and out the other, and you're the one pulling it through. Press on the mark, drag across, release on the far one. Skill sets how much your hand shakes. The instrument sets the margin: a surgical needle can close a wound cleanly, a sewing needle and thread can't, however well you aim - it caps at 80%. A stitch is only as good as its weaker end. A bad closure tears open when you run or fight, and then it bleeds again. You can walk away mid-job, but with fewer than half the stitches in the wound counts as open and the needle and thread are spent anyway. Settings Its own sandbox page. Every condition switches off on its own, sepsis and examination speed are adjustable, and the examination requirement comes off entirely if you want. A condition switched off is paused, not cured. Turn it back on and it carries on from where it was. Notes Singleplayer and multiplayer. Pure Lua - no items, no tiles, no map changes. Remove it whenever: the mod puts back everything it borrowed before the game saves. Don't run it with other health or blood overhauls. Two mods holding healing down will fight. For admins Workshop ID: 3775026731 Mod ID: WoundsOverhaul Multiplayer is tested on somebody else's live server, not mine. Illnesses, examining, treating and sewing another player, the minigame, the drug model, and state surviving a relog. How this was made The Lua is written with an AI assistant - I don't write Lua. The design, the balance and the testing are mine: I play every version before it ships, and most of the bugs were found on my own character. The art isn't. No generated images. The limb sprites are built in Figma over photographs of my own arm; the wounds and stitches are vector. 0.3.16 • Sterilized bandages now actually work: an alcohol bandage or sterilized rag suppresses infection growth like a full disinfectant application for the bandage's whole life, and speeds up clearing once the wound closes. They previously gave nothing over a plain bandage. Reported by Alan. • Broken bones now show when other players examine you. Vanilla never sends a fracture to the server - splinting syncs the splint but not the bone - so exams showed a healthy leg with a splint on it. Your client now reports its own wound changes, which also makes injuries from falls, crashes and animals visible to others. Reported by Dark. • Wound infection no longer drifts apart between players in multiplayer. Reported by Flam3MaSTerr. • Examinations have gestures now: the character reaches for what they are examining - face, torso, waist, legs, feet - and holds and works the specific arm. Suggested by DaniAngione. • New artwork: shoulders, chest and head with their own skin and wounds in the suture window. No body part borrows another limb's picture any more; the head has four wound variants. • For server owners: this update changes shared files, so the server must update too - clients on the new version cannot join a server on the old one. 0.3.15 • Stitching without the skill is genuinely hard now. The needle trembles on screen, the stitch lands exactly where the needle shows, and the press itself jerks the hand - so waiting for the wander to cross the mark no longer buys a perfect bite. Skill steadies the hand; stress and exhaustion shake anybody's; pulling the thread through is harder than lining it up; a surgical needle forgives more. Asked for by Franky Dank, tuned with advice from a working medic. • Examining a patient no longer flickers. The panel was rebuilding its body feed every few seconds and the picture blinked with it. • CDC Rapid Response 2: the sickness their cures simulate is no longer billed to your liver as drinking. Their needle still leaves a real wound - treat the injection site. Reported by Yuri-chan. • The Health tab takes its place even when translations load late, so the tab row stops growing by one and pushing other mods' tabs - Armor Makes Sense's Burden - off the right edge. • German and Spanish get the two treatment-menu lines that were still English. • A week away clears your blood: drug levels are worked out from the world clock, not counted by a running game, and a test now keeps it that way. • For server owners: this update changes shared files, so the server must update too - clients on the new version cannot join a server on the old one. mod_name: Potato textures - better fps for low-end pcs and steam deck (B42 stable)
description: Made this mod for personal use. Inspired by Every Texture Optimized made by maceleet. Heavily compressed textures for better performance: greatly compresses textures from all 3d models in the game at the cost of some texture quality loss/artifacts. (yes this will make some textures uglier, but should not be too noticible) Helps low end machines run the game, especially since B42 made the game more demanding to your pc. How to install Just activate the mod and you are ready to go. For multiplayer, the server needs Potato Textures active on the server modlist. But theres a workaround for people who want the mod on servers that do not have potato textures enabled. You can read the workaround at the end of the mod description on this page. This mod works great for potato pcs/laptops (low vram gpus, integrated gpus, 8/16gb ram, old cpus) steam deck/machine 16x pop players heavily modded saves (using mods add up and increase usage of your pc resources. this mod helps mitigate that a bit) Mod compatibility Potato Textures is compatible with all mods as long as those mods DON'T modify zomboid's original textures. Mods that add new textures (like new vehicles, weapons, clothing) are compatible but Potato Textures do not optimize other mods (this means adding too many mods that add textures will keep adding strain to pc resources, which will affect negatively FPS) Here is some mods that do not work properly with Potato Textures: Every Texture Optimized: You should NOT use both this mod and every texture optimized at the same time. Just pick one. Both mods replace pretty much the same textures with compressed versions, enabling both mods will make one override the other. (both Potato and ETO will boost performance, but Potato textures delivers harsher compression for maximum FPS gains at cost of quality. If you dont care about some mild loss of quality and want more FPS gains, I recommend using Potato instead of ETO) How can I tell if the mod is working? Go to character creator (quickly pick random game mode, location and traits to open the character creator Pick male Pick first skin option Take all his clothing off If you can see the Spiffo, the mod is active and working Additional info and troubleshooting Should be safe to add/remove from any existing saves (since this mod only replaces existing textures when its active). If you have a problem with cars having flat color/no shading textures, set the "Maximum Vehicle Texture Size" to 512 (it will impact performance a bit tho) If you think the mod is somehow not working while active, restart the game. If the mod is not showing up on Zomboid after downloading: verify game files, clear steam's download cache (settings>downloads>clear cache) and restart steam. Also verify if Potato Textures show in game proprieties>workshop tab. Other things you can do and other mods for FPS/stuttering improvements on B42 stable Lock the game to 60 FPS using the "Lock Framerate" option in zomboid performance settings (this helped me with random drops and 1% and 0.1% lows) Allocate additional RAM (if you have enough free RAM) Undying Optimizer: mod that optimizes the UI NEEDS MORE TESTING ON STABLE B42:Tempo - A Performance & FPS Optimizer: mod that does some render/chunk optimization. Have not been updated after B42 stable release but so far on my testing its working fine. NEEDS MORE TESTING ON STABLE B42:Horde Optimizer: mod that optimizes larger hordes of zombies (more more noticible on Louisville or everywhere if you play on high pop settings). Its a new mod so it might have some bugs. So far on my testing theres no problems. Also we can wait for other performance mods to be updated to Stable 42 BetterFPS. But most importantly, we need an optimization update from indiestone for the game. Workaround for using the mod on multiplayer servers that do not have Potato Textures on the modlist -Download my mod -Copy texture files from mod folder: \------------> steamapps\workshop\content\108600\3775173406\mods\Potato textures - better fps\42\media\textures -First I recommend to make a backup (preferably outside zomboid game folders). After the backup, paste the mod textures on original textures game folder: \------------>steamapps\common\ProjectZomboid\media\textures -The game has now the mod by default, no need to activate Potato Textures -Join server To revert the texture files to their original state, use the backup you made OR verify game files (steam will download them back) Workshop ID: 3775173406 Mod ID: potatoFPS

An add-on for Hemp Roll, which it requires. Subscribe to that first, or this will not load. Glass bongs, six colours Blown on a glassmaking bench from a crucible of molten glass, using pliers and a glassblowing pipe. Clear needs Glassmaking 3; the coloured ones need Glassmaking 4 and a can of the matching paint. Pack one with 2 Smokeable Hemp and smoke it - Stress, Unhappiness and Boredom -10. That is the best return on hemp of anything in the mod, which is the point of owning one. You get the empty bong back afterwards to refill. They are ordinary items, not built furniture, so you can right-click and Place Item to stand one anywhere you would put a bottle - the floor, a table, a counter, a shelf. Rolled Dogbane Hemp dogbane is a different plant to hemp - vanilla ships it as rope fibre. Rolled with a paper and smoked, it stops the heart. It exists because people asked for an alternative to bleach that the character does not have to suffer through: no sickness, no drawn-out ending, it is simply over when the smoke is. Deliberately unmistakable - its own name, its own icon and a tooltip that says outright what it does. Nobody should ever smoke it by accident. v1.2 changes Rebalanced alongside Hemp Roll 1.3. A bong used to cost 3 Smokeable Hemp for -18, which was worth exactly three joints - so building one gained you nothing. It now takes 2 for -10, the best return on hemp anywhere in either mod. Requires Hemp Roll 1.3.0 or later. Update both together or the numbers will not line up. v1.1 changes Bongs now turn up in the world at a rare rate - bedroom dressers and side tables, living room shelves and side tables, and closet shelves. Roughly one per thousand containers, so finding one is a small event rather than a given. Only affects places you have not already looted. Notes Smoking a bong reuses the vanilla pipe animation. I am not an animator, and I would rather reuse one that works than fumble a new one. Favourited items cannot be placed - that is a vanilla rule, not this mod. Adds no buildable world objects. Safe to add to an existing save. Requires Hemp Roll 1.3.0 or later. Build 42 only. Workshop ID: 3775174705 Mod ID: BongsAndByes

description: You can play as a zombie. How to become a Zombie-Player Whenever you are infected by the zombification, there is a percentage of chances that you become a Player-Zombie instead. Whenever you are hit by another Zombie-Player, there is a percentage of chances that you become a Player-Zombie (instantly) instead. Both percentages can be modified from sandbox options. Once infected by a zombie, the transformation occures when the player's health falls down at or below 15 percent (modifiable from sandbox options). Movement Animations Idle, Walk, Run and Sprint animations are now those of the zombies. Crouch animations are replaced by zombie Crawling animations (for Idle, Walk and Run). Aiming & Strafing animations are replaced by Lunge animations. Turn animations are adapted to zombies. Window and small fence vaults use partially zombies animations. Combat Animations Shove animations is replaced by Bite-Attack animation. Bite-Attack animation is validated on the Victim side if the attacker is closer than 1m. Bite-Attack distance can be modified from sandbox options. Lunge animation is fun but not practical: any movement direction request will make the Zombie-Player follow the mouse cursor. I recommend to attack with Shove from normal movement without activating the new Aiming/Lunge mode. Other Animations A death animation occures when the player transforms. Zombie-Player specifics Capacity to equip any weapon is removed. Can be deactivated from sandbox options. Nothing can stress you anymore. Can be deactivated from sandbox options. (solo only) Feast on corpse: [Contextual Menu] consume a dead body to heal, eat, drink and decrease boredom and get happiness. Increases drunkenness. Rest on ground: [Contextual Menu] decreases exhaustion and fatigue. Increases boredom. Bang on door/window: [Automatic] Basic zombie instinct of banging stuff takes on when you are doing nothing next to a door or window. No damage is done. Shouts: credits to Poltergeist and their Shout sound mod. Zombie Skin: credits to Authentic Peach as this function is based on what is shown in AuthenticZ. Bandits crossover Zombie player attacking Bandits now transfer the infection (initial infection state can be tuned from sandbox options. default=instant). If you wanna try it, play it while it's hot. It may be hard to maintain a crossover. Technical details Zombies do not attack Zombie-Players. Can be reactivated from sandbox options. If you activate weapons wielding, get ready for animations inconsistencies. There is no cure. But you can use the one from They Knew or Zombie Cure B42 versions (if they maintained B41 interface). It works in solo and multiplayer (coop untested). Once you have been infected (vanilla virus), consecutive zombies attacks will not trigger the Zombie-Player infection chance anymore. Unless your cure it. On Multiplayer, quit the server properly to save the infection status. Admin and debug level players are godlike by default. Remove god powers for a normal experience. Debug level players can use a test panel to add / remove the infection (a new tab on character panel). This mod can safely be added to, removed from your saves (except for Zombie immunity that requires you to die or be cured before removing the mod). Works for B42 and further versions. Use this other mod for B41 and previous versions. If you still have questions, ask on Official PZ Discord: mod_support channel. Incompatibilities Incompatible (at some degree) with all mods that use IsoGameCharacter.ZombiesCantAttack. Incompatible (at some degree) with all mods that use IsoZombie.setUseless. You can still play with those mods but need to turn off following sandbox option: Zombie-Players are not attacked by zombies. On Lockdown This mod cannot be modified by anyone else, for anything else, at all, ever. Even if the user disappears, he or she would much rather you didn't touch the fruits of their hard labour. If you wanna support, kind words are very welcome. If you don't have any, you can still give constructive criticism on discord. Workshop ID: 3775179328 Mod ID: InfectedPlayer
