description: What is it? Family Z Core is a shared dependency framework for Project Zomboid Build 42.20+. It provides common runtime, compatibility, networking, persistence, diagnostics, security and integration services for Family Z modules and compatible external integrations. It is not a standalone gameplay overhaul. Its purpose is to provide a stable technical foundation that other mods can build on without having to recreate the same core infrastructure. How does it work? Family Z Core initializes a controlled runtime layer before dependent systems use its services. It identifies the current environment — Single Player, Host, Client or Dedicated Server — and exposes shared systems through a versioned public API. Its main capabilities include: Module, capability and service registration with lifecycle and ownership tracking. Event bus, routed messaging and request/response communication. Server-authoritative networking, permissions, commands and message validation. Schemas, serialization, persistent stores, migrations, integrity checks and recovery mechanisms. Compatibility scanning, feature detection, adapters, conflict declarations and active-mod awareness. Extension manifests, dependency graphs and dynamic provider discovery. Centralized errors, diagnostics, runtime auditing, health telemetry and performance monitoring. Generation-safe lifecycle handling for reloads, reconnects, world changes and long sessions. The current v10.x public baseline is frozen at 36 public facades and 777 production contracts, allowing dependent mods to target a defined interface instead of relying on unstable internal implementation details. For Developers Mods can load the framework with require "FamilyZCore" and integrate through the read-only FamilyZ.Core.API boundary. The public API exposes versioned contracts for services such as Events, Modules, Capabilities, Services, Config, Schema, Persistence, Migrations, Network, Permissions, Commands, Messages, Routing, Compatibility, Authority, Extensions, Dependencies and Discovery. Developers can query API availability and contract versions before using a feature through functions such as API.getVersion(), API.supports(), API.getContract() and API.listContracts(). Returned table data is defensively copied and direct writes to the public API boundary are blocked. External integrations can register their own modules, capabilities, services and extension manifests, declare required resources, negotiate Core/game-version compatibility, expose discoverable providers and use controlled adapters for interaction with other mods. Compatibility adapters can account for runtime type, game-version ranges, required mods, conflicting mods, target modules and validation probes. Dynamic Discovery allows integrations to resolve compatible providers at runtime instead of maintaining direct hard references, while ownership and lifecycle systems provide controlled cleanup, revocation and recovery. For compatibility work, integrations should target FamilyZ.Core.API rather than FamilyZ.Core.Internal. Family Z Core provides the integration infrastructure, but does not automatically make unrelated mods compatible without an appropriate adapter, provider or contract implementation. Differences from Other Mods Family Z Core is designed as infrastructure rather than as a visible gameplay feature. Instead of adding a specific mechanic, interface or content pack, it centralizes technical systems that would otherwise be duplicated across multiple mods: networking, authority, permissions, persistence, recovery, diagnostics, compatibility, lifecycle management and service discovery. Its contract-first architecture also differs from integrations based mainly on direct global-table access or uncontrolled runtime patching. Public functionality is exposed through a read-only API boundary with versioned contracts, defensive return copies, ownership rules and compatibility negotiation. This allows dependent mods to remain separate modules while sharing the same technical foundation. It also gives external developers a standardized integration surface without requiring access to Family Z Core's internal implementation. Mods That Depend on Family Z Core Advanced Server Control — A centralized server-administration and gameplay-management platform covering moderation, world controls, diagnostics, persistence safeguards and other server systems. Advanced Mod Maintenance Center — A main-menu maintenance utility for detecting mod updates, dependency problems, errors, regressions and compatibility risks before loading a save. Advanced Admin Tools — A unified administrative framework for controlled item, world, entity, environment, diagnostic and moderation operations. Advanced Veterinary — A veterinary medicine expansion that adds persistent animal health records, diagnostics, treatment, disease, reproduction, genetics, welfare and herd-management systems. Advanced Medicine — A medical expansion connecting wounds, diseases, symptoms, vital signs, medication, diagnosis, procedures, immunity, nutrition and recovery. Advanced Universal Mod — A compatibility platform designed to analyze and bridge supported legacy Build 41 mod behavior toward Build 42 through validated profiles, adapters, conflict analysis and evidence-based compatibility. Languages English (EN) Español (ES) Português Brasileiro (PTBR) Deutsch (DE) Français (FR) Русский (RU) 简体中文 (CN) 日本語 (JP) Support (for all dependent mods) Family Z Core — Discord Donation and extra services Patreon Workshop ID: 3775194569 Mod ID: FamilyZCore

Lemon's Vehicle Claims lets players claim cars and trailers for their account and decide exactly who is allowed to use them. During normal play, claims are protected from unauthorized driving, towing, siphoning, looting, mechanics work, and player attacks. Owners also receive a last-known map marker for each claim. HOW TO CLAIM A CAR Sit in the driver's seat, start the engine, and press the gray dashboard claim control or select Claim Vehicle from the vehicle radial menu. Once owned, the dashboard control turns green: left-click it from inside that exact vehicle to reset its timer, or right-click it and confirm to unclaim. Proximity and Refresh Location do not reset ordinary vehicle timers. Dashboardless trailers retain owner-proximity renewal. Each player also has one reserved trailer claim that does not use a normal vehicle slot. Stand next to a trailer, right-click it, and select Claim Trailer. VEHICLE AUTHORIZATIONS Ride - Allows the player to use passenger seats, but does not grant access to stored items. Drive / Tow - Allows driving or starting a car and attaching, towing, or detaching a trailer. Open Trunk - Allows the player to open vehicle storage and move items in or out. Repair - Allows normal repairs and maintenance without removing or deliberately damaging parts. Replace - Includes Repair and grants the full mechanics experience, including installing, removing, or damaging parts. Trailer claims use the same access options except Ride, which is not shown. Build 42.20 MP limitation - A driving crash is ignored for a linked pair if either vehicle is claimed, and a claimed vehicle ignores client-reported hit-character damage, because Workshop Lua receives no authoritative server collision value. Wholly unclaimed vehicles keep vanilla collision damage. Fire, zombies, environmental damage, ordinary wear, and server-owned player attacks still apply. ADMIN CONTROLS Lemon's Aid is not required for basic administration. An admin can right-click any claimed car or trailer and choose Manage Claim to view its owner, change its access list, or release the claim. Admins always have full access and are not restricted by vehicle or trailer claim limits. EXTRA FEATURES WITH LEMON'S AID Players receive a My Vehicles tab showing all car and trailer claims, separate claim totals, last-known locations, access lists, and the time remaining before claim expiry. They can refresh a selected claim's map location, manage permissions, or release it directly from the tab. Location refresh never resets an ordinary claim timer. The standalone Manage Claim window also includes the location refresh action. Admins receive a Vehicle Claims tab with a full list of claimed cars, trailers, and their owners. From there they can inspect or edit claims, release them, adjust individual ordinary-vehicle claim limits, and change the claim-expiry time. Workshop ID: 3775276785 Mod ID: VehicleClaims4220MP

description: Author's Notes This is my first mod, so it is not perfect. It worked when I tested it alone, but thanks to the community I keep finding exploits and rough edges. A huge thank you to everyone who has reported something -- you are helping me grow as a modder in this beautiful game. Z-LLEGRO A craftable delivery terminal & buy-back scanner for the apocalypse economy. Order what you need. Sell what you don't. No traders required -- only time is your enemy here! Craft a Mini Tablet to order supplies that arrive by courier drop, or a Scanner to sell loot back for cash. Identical in singleplayer and multiplayer, with a full in-game admin panel so server owners can shape the economy without ever opening a config file. ✔ Build 42+ ✔ Singleplayer & Multiplayer ✔ No other mods required 🆕 New in v1.1 The community-feedback update -- safe to add to an existing save. Waiting deliveries are marked on your map, and the marker clears when you collect the crate. Sell-only / Buy-only items -- give loot a cash value without putting it on the shelf. Sell several stacks at once with Ctrl/Shift+click and checkboxes. Big payouts arrive as money bundles, not a fistful of notes. Type prices directly in the admin panel. Plus many fixes -- recipes now auto-learn correctly, any screwdriver works, the sell window resizes and keeps its place, sub-hour ETAs show minutes, and orders are validated server-side. Full list in the change notes. 🛠 How To Use It 1. Craft it. Both are in-hand recipes -- no workbench -- learned automatically at Electricity 3: Mini Tablet -- 2x Battery, 2x Electronics Scrap, 1x Sheet Metal, 1x Screwdriver (kept) Scanner -- 1x Battery, 1x Electronics Scrap, 1x Sheet Metal, 1x Screwdriver (kept) Any screwdriver counts -- Multitool, Handiknife, improvised/old, or modded. The Tablet buys, the Scanner sells. Craft both to do both. 2. Keep it on you -- in your inventory or a carried bag. Nothing to place or build, and it need not be in your hands. 3. ⚠ RIGHT-CLICK THE GROUND to open it. The step most people miss. Right-click any floor tile or object next to you: Open Z-llegro Terminal -- browse and order (needs the Tablet) Open Z-llegro Scanner (Sell Items) -- sell loot for cash (needs the Scanner) Manage Z-llegro Catalog (Admin) -- admins/moderators only, needs the Tablet No hotkey, no placed object. If the options are missing, you are not carrying the Tablet or the Scanner. 4. Your order arrives as a crate where you stood when you pressed Buy, once the delivery time passes. Loot it like any container; right-click an empty one for Remove Empty Z-llegro Box (anyone can), or leave it and the mod clears it shortly after. 🛒 Ordering Supplies The Terminal has a category sidebar and Favorites tab (auto-updating for modded items), search, 5 sort modes, an adjustable grid, and a weekly stock rotation so the shelf actually changes over time. Check out with Express, Standard or Economy delivery -- each shows ETA, shipping and grand total up front. Bigger orders take longer to pack, bad weather adds delay, night orders cost more. My Deliveries Track every order and cancel your own pending ones (goods return to stock; cash is not auto-refunded). Anything still waiting out in the world is marked on your map, and the marker clears as soon as you collect the crate. If the courier arrives while you are away, the order is held and delivered when you return -- never lost. 💰 Selling Loot Back Carry the Scanner and open it from the ground menu. It lists every catalog item you carry (worn bags included) plus anything sellable in nearby containers. Pick a quantity, sell, get paid instantly. Only catalog items sell, so it is never a junk-dump exploit, and a configurable limit caps how many of one item a player can sell per in-game day (15 by default). Clearing a big haul is quick: tick the boxes, Ctrl+click to add or Shift+click for a range, then Sell All Selected. Payouts over $100 arrive partly as money bundles. ✨ Why It's Good For Your Game Gives cash a purpose instead of letting it pile up in your pocket. A safety net, not a shortcut -- nothing arrives instantly or for free. 🙂 Duplicate loot becomes currency; almost everything sells back for a share of its value. Early/Mid/Late tiers and weekly rotation -- worth checking, not memorising once. Zero setup: craft it, use it. ⚙ For Server Admins All of this is a real sandbox setting or in-game tool -- no file editing, and every label has a tooltip. 202-item tiered starter catalog Tools & Building Materials, Survival, Clothing, Weapons, Ammo, Medical and Jewelry, split into Early, Mid and Late (scarce -- the full firearm lineup, a katana, a 4-step vest progression up to SWAT). Jewelry is graded silver/gold/gemstone/diamond, so pieces looted off zombies become real income. All re-priceable live from the admin panel. Sandbox Options (21 settings) Delivery -- per-tier hours and price, rain delay, night surcharge, packing delay. Shop -- daily buy limit, cart cap, restock timing, rotation count and length. Trade-In -- sell-back %, daily sell limit, separate sell-only limit, stock-flood cap, "in-season items only" mode. Admin Catalog panel Browse every loaded item (vanilla or modded) by category, mod or search; add or remove with one click, modded categories tagged (Mod). description: Tracks which skill books, recipe magazines and tapes you actually own, and where they are. I made this because I kept looting books I already had. I was keeping notes on a literal sheet of loot paper every save, and I still ended up with two copies of Farming Vol 5 in my bag. So I finally wrote a mod to do the bookkeeping for me. Demo video: youtube.com/watch?v=OW-KBpi1hTo (also up in the carousel) The main idea: when a container gets scanned near you, any book, magazine or tape inside is marked as seen, with the time and place. You don't have to pick anything up. Later, when you actually need Carpentry 4, the list shows where you left it. A bookcase at your base, or some house across town, with coordinates. Since 1.6 you can jump straight there: right click the row to see the spot on the world map, or pin it with a pen. Scanning runs about once per second while containers are around, and corpse piles are skipped by default (you can change that). The Summary tab is the overview. Skill books by volume, magazine progress, and per-skill VHS/CD counts. Skills tab: every volume with its level range and read state. Books you can't read yet because your level is too low are marked as well, so you know what to shelve for later. Right click a bookcase or crate to register it as base storage. You can register as many containers as you want, they all pool into one base. Anything inside counts as BASE, anything in your bags as HAND. That's the anti-duplicate part. Since 1.4 that check follows you into the field: books you already own get a small dot on their inventory icon (green means at base, blue means on you), and the tooltip tells you where your copy is. Plays fine alongside other book mods, the badge keeps to its own corner. And when you drag-select a pile of books, right click has "Grab only what's needed": it skips what you already own and takes one copy per book. I can't carry everything either, my overflow lives in a car trunk, and the tracker used to just lose it there. Since 1.4.2 you can right click a vehicle and register the whole car as base storage: trunk, glove box, seats, everything in it counts as BASE wherever the car ends up. Recipe magazines and schematics work the same way, with the recipe count per magazine. Settings: hover icon (drag it anywhere, or turn it off and use the hotkey - Numpad * by default, rebindable in Key Bindings), scan scope, corpse exclusion, and an optional Collector tab for non-skill tapes and music CDs. That one is off by default. It exists because I am that kind of person. Some notes: Build 42 only, tested on 42.20. Safe to add to an existing save, data is stored per character. Since 1.5 your next character inherits it when you die (sandbox option to turn off). Skill tapes show their base XP values. English, Korean, Simplified Chinese and Russian, follows your game language. Works at 4K and large font sizes, the window scales with your font size setting. You can lock a row as owned or ignored, and write a memo on any item. Multiplayer: personal tracking should work, but I had nobody to test with, so treat it as half-tested. Death inheritance covers respawning in the same session, rejoining later starts fresh. Shared base view is planned. If something breaks or you have an idea, leave a comment. Thanks bella (filter memory), Ritar (stacked crate reports), Nephiro (show-on-map idea), and everyone leaving feedback in the comments. The Base tab got a Map button too. 1.5 - Records survive death: your next character inherits them (sandbox option to disable). 1.4.9 - Cleaned up the harmless translation warnings 42.20.2 started printing to the console log. 1.4.8 - Preventive safety guards for the B42.20.1 hotfix. 1.4.7 - The window hotkey can now be rebound in game options (default Numpad *). description: Adds archery to Project Zomboid Build 42. Five bows, six arrows, a full set of custom bow animations, and a brand-new Archery skill that levels alongside your other perks. Three bugs that quietly cost you materials, six new clips, and a lot more things you can build an arrow out of. FIXED - Arrows could be dismantled into GUNPOWDER. Same for dental floss, and same for the twine on all three carved bows. The craft worked and the arrow was correct, so the only sign was your twine quietly going missing. A roll hafts five arrowheads now, as it always said it did. - Item names were NEVER TRANSLATED - not once, in any release. Bows and arrows showed their English names in Italian, Portuguese and Chinese, because the item-name file was keyed in a shape the game does not read. English looked perfect throughout, since the fallback is the English name, so nothing ever looked wrong from here. ADDED - Diagonal strafing. Strafing has nine directions and the bow only had five clips, so every diagonal borrowed the sideways one - step back and to the left with the bow up and you sidestepped left. Four new clips, forward and backward diagonals on both sides. - Raising and lowering the bow. Bringing the bow up and letting it back down were still the vanilla RIFLE transitions. Two new clips. That is 30 authored bow clips now, up from 24. - More things to make arrows out of. The recipes did not change, only what they accept. Fletch with a chicken or turkey feather, a credit card OR ANY ID CARD - nine materials. Fit a metal head with scrap metal OR ANY EMPTY CAN - tin, water ration, beer or pop. Lash it on with twine, dental floss, SINEW THREAD OR THREAD. The cordages are priced by what they actually hold, so none of them is the obvious answer: twine and dental floss bind 5 arrowheads per roll, sinew thread 10, and a spool of thread 10. FOR MOD AUTHORS Arrows now carry the item tag radarchery:arrow. It is there for you rather than for us - nothing in this mod reads it - so a quiver or storage mod can match on the tag instead of hardcoding six item IDs, and keeps working when a seventh arrow arrives. PLANNED Still on the list: - More transitions, and smoothing the ones that are there - Skill books and archery traits, and possibly an archery occupation - Draw time and reload time - More arrow types and better recipes - A crossbow. It is the single most requested thing, and it is coming, with animations of its own. SUGGESTIONS AND BUG REPORTS - COME TO THE DISCORD https://discord.gg/EgNPzTQzH7 I am open to suggestions - if there is something you want out of an archery mod that is not here yet, tell me and it goes on the list. And please report bugs rather than quietly uninstalling: what you were doing, your mod list and anything odd in console.txt is plenty to get me started. WHAT IT SHIPS WITH - 5 unique bows across 2 lines - 16 compound bow colour variants (8 colours x 2 tiers), for 19 bow items in total - 6 arrow types - 30 custom animation clips - 11 crafting recipes - 1 new skill: Archery, ten levels - 4 languages: English, Italian, Brazilian Portuguese and Simplified Chinese BOWS Carved line - craft-only, made with the vanilla Carving skill: - Crude Carved Bow (Carving 1) - Carved Bow (Carving 4) - Fine Carved Bow (Carving 9) Each tier is tougher than the last. The Fine Carved Bow outlasts every other bow in the mod, trading damage, range and accuracy for durability. Compound line - loot only, in Red, Blue, Green, Tan, White, Black, Yellow and Pink: - Compound Bow (mid tier) - Heavy Compound Bow (high tier, half as common) The colours are purely cosmetic. Every colour within a tier shoots identically. ARROWS Arrows are made from real wood, not twigs, and crafting them is an upgrade chain - you carve a shaft, fletch it, then fit a head to it. - Carved Arrow - the shaft, and the only recipe needing no skill. Carve it from a plank, a branch or scrap wood. Survives about 25% of hits. - Fine Carved Arrow - a carved arrow fletched with a feather, a credit card or an ID card. Flies straighter and comes back far more often. Survives about 40% of hits. - Stone-Tipped and Bone-Tipped Arrows - a sharp flint flake or a sharp bone fragment, lashed on with cordage. Both hit hard. Survive about 50% of hits. - Tipped Carved Arrow - a head beaten out of scrap metal or an empty can. The toughest of the crafted arrows, surviving about 55% of hits. - Carbon Hunting Arrow - loot only, the biggest damage bonus. Survives about 90% of hits. Twine and dental floss haft five arrowheads per roll; sinew thread and a spool of thread haft ten. Plain carved arrows are cheap and disposable; every step up the chain hits harder or comes back more often. FEATURES - Arrows lodge in what you shoot. An arrow that survives the shot stays in the body, so you get it back by looting the corpse rather than hunting the floor - and a zombie that walks away is still carrying it. Every arrow's recovery chance is a sandbox slider. - The Archery skill. A full ten-level perk beside Aiming and Reloading, with its own XP multiplier in sandbox. As it rises, hit chance, critical chance and range go up. Firearms still train Aiming. - A visible nocked arrow. Draw a bow with ammunition and the arrow is genuinely there on the string, and it leaves on the exact frame the shot releases. - Carry it on your back. Bows slot into the Back hotbar slot exactly like a rifle, and stay visible whether or not you wear a backpack. - A full animation set - 30 clips authored for the bow, not borrowed from the rifle: idle, movement at every speed and crouch, eight-way strafing, raising and lowering the bow, the aim, draw, release, nock, and limping on an injured leg. - Bows tire your arms, by draw weight, eased by Archery - with its own sandbox slider. - Custom fire sound, custom 3D models and custom inventory icons throughout. WHERE TO FIND IT Compound bows and carbon hunting arrows turn up in hunting cabins and ranger stations first, then gun stores, pawn shops, sporting-goods and camping stock, and survivalist and criminal stashes - with a small chance in a garage and a smaller one in household shelving. Hunter, ranger, ghillie, camper, backpacker, survivalist, redneck and farmer zombies can carry archery gear too. Colours within a tier are equally common; the heavy tier is half as common. The carved bows and all five crafted arrows are craft-only and spawn nowhere. You make those yourself. NOTES - Build 42 only. No dependencies, and safe to run alongside other weapon mods. - Item IDs live in module Base (for example Base.CarvedArrow). - Adding this mod mid-save is fine. Removing it will strip any RadArchery items from that save. - Multiplayer is supported, and every multiplayer bug found so far is fixed. Reports from a server are still very welcome. mod_name: Inventory Tetris - Grid Based Items and Equipment Overhaul
description: Inventory Tetris completely replaces Project Zomboid’s normal list-based inventory with a grid system where items actually take up space. Bigger items need more room, things can be rotated to fit, and organizing your bags becomes part of the game instead of just sorting a list. This version is being actively maintained for Build 42.20 with a pretty heavy focus on Singleplayer, Multiplayer, Dedicated Servers, persistence, compatibility, and fixing the weird edge cases that come from changing such a core part of the game. Equipment UI is also included directly with Inventory Tetris now, so you do not need to install the old discontinued version separately. The goal is to keep everything feeling like one cohesive inventory system while staying as compatible with vanilla Project Zomboid as we reasonably can. Build 42.20 | Singleplayer | Multiplayer | Dedicated Servers | Equipment UI Included FEATURES Grid-Based Inventory Every item has a physical size and has to actually fit inside the container you’re putting it in. You can move things around, rotate them, stack compatible items, and organize your inventory however makes sense to you. Different bags and containers have different layouts, so what you carry and how you pack it actually matters. Containers, Pockets & Equipment Inventory Tetris goes a lot deeper than just replacing the main inventory window. Backpacks, nested containers, pockets, worn equipment, and the Equipment UI all work together as part of the same system. Moving something from your backpack to a pocket or onto your character should still feel like one connected inventory rather than a bunch of unrelated menus. Vanilla Trait Integration Inventory traits have been adapted to work with the grid system. Organized and Disorganized affect container capacity when weight limits are enforced, while Disorganized also makes automatically placed items less neatly packed. With Search & Discovery enabled, Dextrous searches containers faster and All Thumbs searches them slower. Search & Discovery (Optional) You don’t always have to immediately know what is inside a container. With Search & Discovery enabled, containers have to be searched before their contents are fully revealed. It makes looting a little slower and more deliberate, and gives searching through houses, vehicles, bodies, and storage areas a lot more personality. You can enable it in the Sandbox Options under Inventory Tetris: Search. Turn on Enable Search Mode there. SETTINGS Inventory Tetris has quite a few ways to customize how the system plays. Here are some of the settings that make the biggest difference. Global Bonus Grid Size Add extra width and height to all Inventory Tetris container grids. The default is 0, with up to 8 additional grid spaces available globally. Item Weight Multiplier Adjust the actual weight of items without changing how much physical grid space they occupy. 1.0 keeps normal item weights, while lower values make items lighter. Grid Scale Adjust the size of the Tetris inventory grid to better fit your resolution, UI scale, and personal preference. Global Stack Size Multiplier Increase or decrease Inventory Tetris stack limits globally. 1.0 is the default. Values below 1.0 reduce stack sizes, while values above 1.0 increase them. Items that are not already stackable remain non-stackable. The multiplier can be set from 0.01 to 100.0. Enable Search Mode Hide the contents of eligible containers until your character searches through them. Search Time controls how quickly items are revealed, while Corpse Search can be set to Disabled, Some Items, or Enabled. Use Item Transfer Time Enable calculated transfer times when moving items between containers. This setting is Singleplayer only. Item Transfer Speed Multiplier Adjust how quickly timed item transfers are completed in Singleplayer. This setting is Singleplayer only. Enforce Carry Weight Enforce vanilla container capacity limits alongside the Tetris grid. In Multiplayer, these capacity checks are enforced for server authority. We cannot override this behavior because Project Zomboid enforces it! Encumbrance Slowdown Slow your character when carrying a very heavy load, allowing weight to remain an important part of inventory management even with the grid system. ...and Quite a Few More! Additional settings are available for controls, UI scaling, visual options, container stacking rules, and other fine tuning. FAQ Does Inventory Tetris work in Multiplayer? Yes. This version supports Singleplayer, hosted Multiplayer, and Dedicated Servers. Multiplayer and persistence are areas we continue to actively test, so if you find something strange on a server we definitely want to hear about it. Do I need another version of Inventory Tetris installed? No. This Workshop item contains Inventory Tetris itself. You should not load multiple versions of Inventory Tetris at the same time. Do I need Equipment UI installed separately? No. Equipment UI is now included directly with Inventory Tetris. If you still have the old standalone Equipment UI installed or enabled, please disable or unsubscribe from it. Can I use this on an existing save? The current version is designed to preserve Inventory Tetris’s existing persistence data. That said, this is Project Zomboid and Inventory Tetris changes a pretty fundamental part of the inventory system. Backing up an important save before any major mod update is always a good idea. Can I remove Inventory Tetris from an existing save? We do not recommend treating Inventory Tetris as a mod that can be freely added and removed from an active save. It changes inventory behavior and stores additional information about container layouts and items. If the save matters to you, make a backup before changing your mod list. How do key rings work? Key rings are treated differently from normal Tetris containers. The key ring itself still takes up space in your inventory, but the keys stored inside it do not need individual Tetris grid positions. You can open the ring and move keys in and out normally, including dropping keys directly onto it. Why can’t I move items in my inventory? If items can’t be moved to/from containers, or simple inventory actions are freezing in place, you are almost certainly experiencing an incompatibility issue with another mod that changes Project Zomboid’s vanilla interface behavior. Is this compatible with other inventory mods? Inventory Tetris replaces a large part of Project Zomboid’s inventory interface and behavior, so mods that replace or heavily modify the same systems may conflict. We try to preserve vanilla behavior and compatibility wherever practical, but we cannot guarantee compatibility with every inventory, equipment, or container overhaul. CREDITS Inventory Tetris is currently maintained by Naneek and Smangsty. None of this would be possible without the original mods created by Notloc. We’re very thankful for the work that made this entire mod possible. Thanks to everyone testing the mod, reporting weird behavior, and helping us make the Build 42 version better. MOD INFORMATION Mod Name: Inventory Tetris Mod ID: INVENTORY_TETRIS Workshop ID: 3775513231 Build 42.20 | Singleplayer | Multiplayer | Dedicated Servers | Equipment UI Included Workshop ID: 3775513231 Mod ID: INVENTORY_TETRIS

description: What is Advanced Medicine? Advanced Medicine is a modular medical framework for Project Zomboid Build 42.20+ that expands vanilla BodyDamage with persistent systems for diseases, wound infection, pharmacology, diagnosis, procedures, sterility, nutrition, immunity and multiplayer treatment. How Does It Work? Advanced Medicine reads vanilla health data and adds a deeper clinical layer without replacing BodyDamage. Synchronizes wounds, bleeding, burns, bites, pain and body-part damage. Tracks temperature, heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure, SpO2, hydration and consciousness. Runs staged diseases with severity, complications and recovery. Uses symptoms, vitals and examinations for diagnosis. Adds bacterial-load progression affected by contamination, hygiene, bandages, foreign bodies, immunity and antibiotics. Adds medication onset, duration, dose limits, interactions, adverse effects, overdose and antibiotic resistance. Adds timed examinations and procedures with success/failure conditions. Persists medical state through Family Z Core. Uses server-authoritative validation in multiplayer. Interface Right-click → Family Z Core → Medicine Core Features Diseases & Symptoms Primary conditions: Influenza Gastroenteritis Wound Infection Bronchitis Dehydration Food Poisoning 15 primary symptoms include fever, chills, cough, headache, fatigue, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dizziness, breathing difficulty, pain, confusion, appetite loss and weakness. Diseases support incubation, staged progression, severity, risk factors and complications. Medication & Pharmacology Registered medications include Acetaminophen, Ibuprofen, Amoxicillin, Diphenhydramine, Ondansetron, Loperamide, Chlorhexidine, Albuterol, Oral Rehydration Salts and Lidocaine. Pharmacology manages onset, duration, exposure, dose limits, interactions, adverse reactions, overdose, tolerance, dependence and simplified antibiotic resistance. Wounds & Infection Supported wounds include superficial, deep, laceration, puncture, burn, bite, contaminated and infected wounds. Wounds track contamination, bleeding, inflammation, pain, tissue damage, healing, foreign bodies, sutures and bandage condition. Infection stages: Risk Localized Established Severe Disseminated Sepsis Recovered Complications include suppuration, abscess, cellulitis, necrosis and sepsis. Diagnosis Diagnosis uses known symptoms, vitals, examinations, instruments and medical skill. Examinations include temperature, pulse, respiration, blood pressure, SpO2, hydration, consciousness, wound inspection, abdominal palpation, chest auscultation and pain assessment. Results may return a probable condition, alternatives or insufficient data. Procedures 21 procedures are validated. Basic care includes cleaning, irrigation, disinfection, bandage changes, antiseptic use, oral medication assistance, IM injection and immobilization. Advanced care includes debridement, suturing, abscess drainage, foreign-body extraction, local anesthesia, IV access/fluids, nebulization, oxygen therapy and hemorrhage control. Equipment & Sterility 20 equipment definitions cover diagnostic tools, sterile supplies, syringes, sutures, surgical tools, IV equipment, nebulizers, oxygen equipment and medical kits. Equipment may track condition, uses, quality, sterility and expiry. Sterility states: Sterile, Clean, Contaminated, Dirty. Immunity, Nutrition & Transmission Immunity considers baseline resistance, acquired immunity, vaccination and suppression from hunger, fatigue or stress. Transmission supports respiratory, direct-contact, fomite, food, water and fluid exposure. Masks, gloves, washing, disinfection and isolation can modify risk. Nutrition tracks hydration, electrolytes, energy, protein, iron, micronutrients and glucose. Skills & Crafting Six tracks are defined: Diagnosis, Pharmacology, Procedures, Infection Control, Natural Medicine and Pharmaceutical Crafting. Medical books provide progression and knowledge unlocks. Natural Medicine includes plants and preparations. Pharmaceutical Crafting supports common medical formulations and treated supplies. Medical Loot Items use vanilla procedural distributions across medical, first-aid, veterinary and military locations. Basic supplies are more common than antibiotics and advanced equipment. Multiplayer Multiplayer treatment is server-authoritative and includes synchronization, consent, access control, distance/skill/inventory validation, action locks and persistent history. How Is It Different from Other Mods and Vanilla? Advanced Medicine is a connected clinical framework rather than only an item pack or wound overhaul. Vanilla remains relevant: BodyDamage injuries are read and synchronized. Persistent simulation: wounds, infections, diseases, medications and history continue over time. Evidence-based diagnosis: conditions are inferred from available clinical data. Connected systems: drugs, equipment, procedures, sterility, immunity and nutrition share the same patient state. Server authority: multiplayer treatment is validated server-side. Family Z architecture: integration is handled through Family Z Core. Frequently Asked Questions Does it replace vanilla First Aid? No. It extends BodyDamage. Are wounds more likely to become infected? Not through a simple vanilla multiplier. Advanced Medicine adds bacterial-load progression based on wound condition and care. What increases infection risk? Contamination, dirty bandages, open wounds, foreign bodies and poor hygiene. Can infections be treated without antibiotics? Yes. Cleaning, hygiene, wound care and immunity contribute, but antibiotics become more important as bacterial load increases. Can infections become severe? Yes. They can progress to abscess, cellulitis, dissemination and sepsis. Can medication relieve symptoms? Yes. Drugs target specific symptoms or clinical processes. Can I overdose or combine drugs incorrectly? Yes. Dose limits, interactions, adverse reactions and overdose states are implemented. Does antibiotic resistance exist? Yes, as a simplified mechanic linked to repeated exposure. Are medications rare? Basic supplies are more common than antibiotics and advanced equipment. Does hygiene matter? Yes. It affects contamination, procedures and infection pressure. Can procedures fail? Yes. Skill, fatigue, stress, hygiene, lighting and equipment affect outcomes. Can I suture, drain abscesses or remove foreign bodies? Yes. These are advanced procedures. Can I instantly identify a disease? No. Diagnosis depends on available evidence and may remain uncertain. Can players treat each other? Yes. Multiplayer treatment supports consent and server validation. Can I craft medicine? Yes. Can Advanced Medicine cure the Knox infection? No. Is this real medical guidance? No. All medical mechanics are gameplay abstractions for Project Zomboid. description: Simple and immersive: migrating zombie hordes occasionally pass through your area. No warnings, no HUD, no chat messages. Every couple of in-game days (tunable), a horde approaches the area around a randomly chosen player. Hordes approach on foot from one or two directions as a coherent group, then disperse and linger as ordinary zombies. You might not even notice one passing through. That's intentional. Zombie speed, abilities and outfits follow your world's lore settings. Hordes tend to grow as survivors make their way through the apocalypse. Their size also varies each time - sometimes a handful, sometimes a flood. Works in singleplayer and multiplayer (B42 42.20+) - at its best on a small server with a few friends. Can be added to an existing save. Sandbox Options - Horde Size: how large hordes get, from a rare-event Easy up to Crazy - Horde Size Variation: how much each horde's size is randomized - Horde Frequency: how often hordes occur - Hordes Come For You: whether hordes simply pass through, sometimes follow their chosen survivor on the way in, or always do - Extra Sprinters: opt-in. Veteran survivors may rarely attract faster zombies (only if your lore settings already allow them) - No Horde Spawns Within 60 Tiles: experimental, for keeping hordes away from large fenced bases Admin Chat Commands (multiplayer) - /inuhorde now: trigger the next horde immediately - /inuhorde status: check the current or next event - /inuhorde reset: end the horde event in progress (its zombies stay put as ordinary zombies) How It Works (For the technically curious) - Hordes are real zombie entities, created server-side in loaded areas out of player sight - They walk in using the game's own pathfinding. The mod only sets destinations along the way - In B42 multiplayer the server can't steer zombies directly - movement is owned by clients. The mod syncs its guidance to whichever client owns each zombie - Zombies far from any player get virtualized and can't be guided, which is why a horde can't start its journey from across the map - Unlike most horde mods, there are no world sounds or other bait that would drag existing zombies around. Only the horde itself is guided FAQ Q: Does it spawn new zombies, or use the ones already on the map? A: It spawns new ones. Existing zombies and respawn settings are unaffected. Q: Can you share more details about how it works? A: Not knowing is part of the fun, so I keep the details unspoiled. If you're curious, read the source code. description: See how your survivor is doing at a glance, without opening any menu. Press ; (semicolon) to show or hide the panel - that's it, nothing else to set up. Enable the mod, load in, it's already there. (Want a different key? Options - Key Bindings - "Toggle Status HUD".) Quick start: ; toggles the panel - right-click it for Settings - drag it anywhere and lock the position once you like where it sits. Adding it to a save you already started? Build 42 gives every save its own mod list, so ticking the mod in the main menu does not switch it on in an existing world - load the save and enable it there too. Otherwise nothing appears and the key does nothing, which looks exactly like a broken mod. It is the most common reason it "doesn't work". What it shows 32 stats in 4 groups. Turn any of them on or off. Survival - Health, Food, Water, Rest, Endurance, Fitness Mental - Stress, Panic, Pain, Unhappy, Boredom, Anger, Morale, Nicotine Withdrawal, Idleness, Sanity Body - Body Temperature, Body Heat Generation, Wetness, Discomfort, Sickness, Infection, Fever, Drunk, Food Sickness, Poison Nutrition - Carry Weight, Body Weight, Calories, Proteins, Carbs, Fat Each row: icon, a bar that turns yellow then red as it gets worse, and the exact number. Hover a row for the full name. Make it yours Right-click the panel - Settings, in four tabs. Everything updates live, so you see the change before you close the window. Hover anything in Settings for a one-line explanation of what it does - every stat and every option Vertical list, or a horizontal strip along the top/bottom edge Text sizes read from your machine's own fonts, marked * where they are drawn perfectly sharp; 16 width steps; background down to fully invisible Choose where the stat name goes: off, auto (trimmed so the bar keeps a usable width), full, or drawn inside the bar Put the number beside the bar, or inside it so the bar runs the full row Group stats by category or order them freely; headings on or off, with a gap or a divider line between categories. Folding a category by clicking its heading can be switched off if you keep catching it while dragging. Turn bars and icons on or off, grayscale mode if you don't want colour Only show problems - hides every stat that's currently fine Hide the vanilla moodle icons too, since this panel already covers them Resize from any edge or corner, drag anywhere, lock the position once you're happy Optional second keybind to open Settings directly, no right-click needed (Options - Key Bindings - "Open Status HUD Settings") Reorder stats with the up/down arrows in the Stats tab. Grouped keeps a stat inside its own category; Free order lets it go anywhere. An "Order" button per group undoes just that group's reordering, and Reset to defaults restores your stat selection as well as the appearance. Extra Threshold ticks - marks on the bar showing exactly where the next moodle level kicks in Diagnose stats (right-click) - compares the game's raw value with what the HUD shows, for when a stat looks wrong. Off by default; a server can enable it. Knows what your server disabled - hides those stats instead of showing them stuck and broken Server admins A sandbox page under CH Status HUD lets you lock which stats players can see, and switch off threshold ticks or the diagnose tool for everyone. Add the mod to the server's mod list too, not just your own subscription - the page only appears if the server itself loads it. Installation Client-side only - no server-side Lua, no network traffic, nothing written into the save. That also means every player who wants to see the HUD needs it installed and enabled on their own machine - the host or a server doesn't hand it to anyone automatically. Singleplayer: enable it in the Mods menu, then load in - it appears on its own. On a save you already started you must also enable it inside that save's own mod list (see Quick start), since Build 42 keeps one per world. Otherwise it works fine on an existing save; you only need a fresh one for the server admin sandbox page (see above), which is fixed at world creation. Hosting (the in-game Host button): check both the regular mod list AND the separate Steam Workshop items list in the host setup screen. This mod has to be enabled in both, or it won't load at all - no panel, no keybind, nothing, and it can look like the mod is just broken. Dedicated server: add it to the server's own mod list, not just your own subscription - both Mods= and WorkshopItems= in the server's .ini need this mod (id CHStatusHUD, Workshop ID 3776182375). Every player connecting still needs it installed on their own end too, same as hosting. Languages Fully translated into every language the game ships (28), including the new hover explanations. AI-assisted - if something reads wrong in your language, comment what it should say instead and I'll fix it. Update - 16 August The warning sliders now show the real value, not a percentage. Proteins reads "below -300", Calories reads "below 0" - the same numbers the panel itself shows you. There are - and + buttons either side of each slider that move it one point at a time, since dragging to an exact figure with a mouse was guesswork. Fixed: the Settings window opens where you left it instead of jumping back to the middle of the screen every time. In the update before this one: nutrition warnings started working at all (Carbs and Fat could never count as a problem), the panel stopped moving after a relog, the toggle key gained a cycle mode, and the default key changed from U to ; because U is vanilla's Vehicle Info key. Existing players keep the key they have. Not working? The mod writes one line to console.txt when it starts, beginning with [CH Status HUD] panel created. Paste that line in the comments and I can tell you exactly what happened. If instead you find PANEL CREATION FAILED, paste that one - it names the cause. Also check console.txt for mods you thought you had disabled - a save keeps loading whatever it was created with, and one running unnoticed has been the answer before. Mod ID CHStatusHUD Workshop ID: 3776182375 Mod ID: CHStatusHUD

description: READ BEFORE ANYTHING !! For Any Bug Report For Any Suggestion Before saying "it's not working", unsubscribe, then resubscribe. If it still fails, post your bug on Discord with your console file "C:\Users\you\Zomboid\console.txt" and your mod list "C:\Users\you\Zomboid\mods\default.txt" => Discord : https://discord.gg/vJay7GQ92B Plysken Underground Revolution Dig your own bunker. Not a prefab basement that appears when you place a block - an actual hole in the ground that you open one shovel pass at a time, ladder down into, and close behind you. A room you dig out becomes a real interior: it stays dry, it is lit, and below ground the temperature stops swinging with the weather, the way a cellar does. Being straight with you about one thing. To make your gallery count as indoors, the mod borrows an interior from a cellar already on the map. Near a town that works, and the walls you build down there hold. Far from everything, there may be nothing close enough to borrow from - and then rain still reaches your ears, and a zombie can climb over an underground wall. Do not make one your only defence until you have seen it hold. This is a limit of the game engine, not something a mod can fix. ⚠️ Single-player mod. It may simply not work on a server, and there is no multiplayer support for now. See Requirements below before you try. ⛏️ How it works Everything happens around a worksite bench, and the order matters - each step opens the next one. If a button is greyed out, the panel tells you why underneath it. 1. Craft the Bunker Worksite Bench. Carpentry 3. You need a hammer and a saw in your bag (they are not consumed), plus 10 planks, 30 nails, a notebook and a pen or pencil. It is in the Carpentry tab of the crafting menu. 2. Put the bench down where you want to dig. It anchors the whole worksite. Everything you do afterwards has to happen within 10 tiles of it by default - you can raise that in the sandbox options, up to 100. 3. Clear the ground. Right-click the patch you want to open. If something is in the way the game says so, and offers what to do about it: Chop down the tree, Dig out the stump, Cut down the bushes, Clear the grass. Bare soil is what you are after. 4. Open the panel and start digging. Left-click the bench, or right-click it and pick Open construction panel. Press Start to dig, then click the square you want to sink. You need a digging tool - a shovel, trowel, hoe or pickaxe. Road and pavement have to be broken with a pickaxe before you reach the soil underneath. One square takes 24 passes by default, and each pass fills part of a sack. You carry that soil out yourself - sacks are heavy, and hauling them up costs endurance. The panel tracks you as Continue digging (5/24), so you can stop and come back. 5. Build the ladder. Once the first shaft is sunk, the panel offers Build the ladder. Carpentry 2, 5 planks and 20 nails, hammer and saw. Stand on one of the eight squares bordering the hole - not on the hole itself. 6. Go down and widen from below. Right-click the shaft and pick Climb down the ladder. From then on you dig sideways: right-click a wall of earth, choose Dig from here, then Dig north, Dig south, Dig west or Dig east. The first shaft is the only one you sink from the surface - after that the bunker grows underground. 7. Close it behind you. The panel offers Build a trapdoor. Carpentry 3, 4 planks, 2 hinges, 1 doorknob and 10 nails. Once it is in, right-click it to Open, Close, Lock or Unlock it. 🔧 Things worth knowing before you start The bench is the worksite. Pick it up and the whole project stops, at every level - not just the one you are standing on. Leave it standing, or put it back where it was. An open trapdoor is an open hole. Locking it keeps people out; it does nothing to the dead, who break rather than open. What protects you is closing it. And there is no safety rail - walk into the shaft and you fall in. You cannot build a wall on a wall of earth. Earth is not a square you can build on, it is ground you have not opened yet. Dig it out and the earth wall disappears on its own. You build in the space you have made, never in what is still solid. For a 5x5 room with your own built walls, dig 6x6. The game stores a wall as the north or west side of a square, so a “south” wall is really the north wall of the square below, and an “east” wall the west wall of the square beside. You need that extra row and column open to put walls there. If you only want an enclosed room, digging 5x5 is enough - the earth around it already closes it, and it holds. 📦 Items Bunker Worksite Bench - the only thing the mod adds to your crafting menu. Carpentry 3. It is a placeable worksite, not decoration: it anchors the whole project and every action happens within range of it. Everything else is vanilla - shovel, hammer, saw, planks, nails, hinges, a doorknob. The soil you dig fills sacks, which you carry yourself. ⚙️ Sandbox options Nineteen settings under a PUR page: digging passes and speed, soil per pass, endurance costs, how much you can haul up the ladder, worksite radius, underground temperature, and what the ladder and trapdoor cost to build. If you would rather build than dig, raise the digging speed and drop the passes. One catch, and it is the game’s, not mine: a world freezes its sandbox settings when it is created, so these options stay at their defaults in a save you already started. Start a new world to change them. ❓ FAQ Common questions are answered in #pur-faq on our Discord. Got one that isn’t there? Ask there and I’ll add it. 📋 Requirements Project Zomboid Build 42.20 or newer - the build it was developed and tested on. It relies on engine behaviour that changed during the 42.x line, so older builds will misbehave. No other mods required. ⚠️ Single-player only, and I mean it. Every system was written and tested for a solo game, and I have never run it on a server or in co-op. Nothing stops you trying, but it may not work at all - and if it breaks there, I will not be able to help. Multiplayer is not planned for now: it depends on a change on the game's side, which I have already asked the developers for. You can add it to a save you already started. As with any mod, try it on a spare save first. I am not responsible for conflicts with other mods. 🌍 Languages 26 languages. English is mine; the rest were written for this release and may read a little stiff to a native speaker. If a line sounds wrong in yours, tell me and I will fix it - and credit you. ⚖️ License Original mod by Plysken - built from scratch for Build 42, with its own tiles, sprites, systems and artwork. © 2026 Plysken. All rights reserved. Subscribing grants a personal, non-transferable licence to play only. Without written permission: do not reuse, copy, port, translate, fork, repackage, re-upload (Workshop / GitHub / Nexus), bundle inside another mod, or use any portion for AI training. Unauthorised re-uploads will be reported under DMCA. FrenchWork Workshop ID: 3776279483 Mod ID: PUR

TARKOV COMBAT STIMS Thirteen single-use injectors inspired by Escape from Tarkov. Each one delivers a short, powerful buff -- and most make you pay a price for it. Built for moments when regular medicine won't cut it. NEW Seven new stims joining the original six: Morphine (pure painkiller), xTG-12 Antidote (anti-nausea, cures colds), Trimadol (kills panic and stress), Meldonin (mood boost, hunger cost), AHF1-M (sustained beta blocker for combat), ETG-c Stimulant (heavy regen, you feel every wound), and Obdolbos Cocktail (gamble on inject -- 60%% hit, 30%% bad trip, 10%% jackpot). Also new: seven matching craft recipes, per-stim duration sliders for every timed stim, and tiered loot rarities so common stims spawn more often than premium ones. HOW TO USE Right-click any stim in your inventory and select "Inject" for a ~0.5 second injection with a syringe sound. Durations use in-game time, so fast-forwarding compresses the stim (and its crash). Re-injecting refreshes the timer -- effects never stack past a single dose. THE STIMS -- THE ORIGINAL SIX -- SJ6 Tactical -- 20 min: Sprint god-mode. Full endurance, no fatigue. Crash: endurance collapses to 5%%, fatigue slams in. Propital Regen -- 30 min: Pain to zero, ~2 HP/min regen on every wounded part. Crash: hunger and thirst surge. Zagustin Hemostatic -- instant: Seals every open wound (bleeding, cuts, deep wounds, bites, bacterial infection) on inject, permanently. Foreign objects block it -- pull them first. Does NOT cure zombie infection or restore HP. Side effect: panic maxes one minute after the shot. M.U.L.E. Strength -- 30 min: +30 kg carry weight. Drops instantly when the timer ends -- if you're still overloaded you go straight into over-encumbrance. Crash: fatigue and thirst spike. Adrenaline -- 20 min: Fatigue eliminated and held at zero, even against natural drowsiness. Crash: fatigue rebounds hard, thirst rises. SJ12 Sustenance -- 30 min: Hunger and thirst drop 2%% per minute -- up to -60%% recovery. The safe one: no penalty when it wears off. -- NEW -- Morphine -- 45 min: Pain to zero, longest analgesic in the pack. Crash: fatigue spike and drowsy for 15 min. xTG-12 Antidote -- 30 min: Clears queasy, food sickness, poisoning, and colds on inject, blocks them for the window. Deliberately doesn't touch zombie infection -- Knox stays yours. Crash: mild stress bump. Trimadol -- 30 min: Panic and stress dropped to zero and held. Calm through gunfire and hordes. Crash: +30%% fatigue. Meldonin -- 30 min: Unhappy zeroed. Good mood no matter what. Cost: hunger drains 3x faster -- happiness is calorie-funded. AHF1-M -- 25 min: Sustained beta blocker. Panic zeroed for the full window -- laser focus in firefights, no shaky aim. Crash: hard stress spike. ETG-c Stimulant -- 30 min: 4 HP/min regen on every wounded part, ~120 HP restored across the window (double Propital). Pain stays -- you feel every wound while it heals. Combo with Morphine for both. Crash: heavy hunger, thirst, and fatigue. Obdolbos Cocktail -- rolls on inject: The gamble stim. 60%% full effect of one random original stim. 30%% bad trip (panic, fatigue, stress, endurance drain, pain, or bleeding). 10%% jackpot -- ALL six original stims at once, with all six crashes on the way out. INJECTOR CASE A dedicated case with a 30%% weight reduction on its contents. Only stims fit inside. Right-click and "Wear" to strap it on; while worn it becomes a tab at the top of your inventory panel for one-click access. Also spawns in medical loot, rarer than the stims. Worn on the arm with its own 3D model. Occupies the ammo-bandolier slot -- conflicts with an ammo bandolier only. No conflicts with fanny packs, satchels, belts, backpacks, jackets, or webbing. ACTIVE-STIM ICONS While a timed stim is running, a HUD icon shows which stim is active with a shrinking progress bar. Hover for effect summary and remaining minutes. Icons vanish the moment a stim wears off. Right-click any icon (or any stim in your inventory) and pick Injector Settings to toggle icons, anchor them to any screen edge, and nudge the offset. Settings save per-user across every world. WHERE TO FIND THEM Rare finds in medicine cabinets, pharmacies, hospital storage, first-aid kits, nurse lockers, ambulance kits. Don't expect to be swimming in them. FIELD MANUAL Rarely found alongside the stims themselves. Read it to unlock all 14 crafting recipes on the spot -- one book, one character, permanent. No manual? Reach First Aid Level 3 and the recipes auto-learn instead. CRAFTING YOUR OWN Once the recipes are unlocked (via manual or First Aid 3), they appear under the Medical crafting tab (all grouped as "Make - ..."). You just need a Mortar & Pestle in your inventory -- craft at any surface. Every stim needs an Empty Injector (broken glass, glue, twine). Injecting a stim returns the empty injector to your inventory, so one injector keeps cycling. Ingredients lean thematic (painkillers and sleeping tablets for Morphine, antibiotics and mint for xTG-12, comfrey and antibiotics for ETG-c, every pill in the cabinet for Obdolbos) with alternatives so you're not hunting one specific item. mod_name: Skill Legacy - Keep Your Skills Through Death
description: Your next character carries on from where the last one left off, minus a share of what that life earned. Books you finished and recipes you learned carry too, and are never reduced by the penalty. Single player and dedicated servers. Safe to add mid-world and safe to remove. How it works kept = inherited + (earned this life x (1 - penalty)) The penalty only ever applies to what you earned, never to what you inherited, so repeated deaths cannot spiral to zero. At the default 30%, a character who took Carpentry from 2 to 8 hands on level 7. What players see After dying they land on the normal character creation screen with one addition: a CONTINUE LAST SURVIVOR button that fills in the profession and traits they died with. The profession decides whether they inherit. Pick the job you died as and your skills, books and recipes come with you. Pick a different one and you are a new survivor with none of it. Nothing is decided until the character spawns, so changing your mind costs nothing, and doing nothing at all inherits. A first character has nothing banked and sees no button. Settings Sandbox options under Skill Legacy, changeable on a running world. Penalty (% of this life's gains) - default 30, range 0-100. 0 is full retention; 50+ makes death sting. 100 forfeits the life that ended but keeps everything inherited before it. Legacy replaces starting skills - default ON. Wipes the skill levels a profession and traits grant, so a legacy cannot be stacked on top of a fresh profession. Traits keep everything else. First characters are untouched. Carry books read and recipes learned - default ON. Character creation: legacy button - default 1. 1 shows it, 2 fills the build in automatically, 0 removes it (skills still carry, the profession still decides). Log every skill change - default OFF. See Troubleshooting. There is no on/off switch: unticking the mod is already exactly that. Installing Mod ID SkillLegacy. No dependencies. Single player - enable it and play. A legacy belongs to the save, so skills carry across deaths within a world and stop at its edge. Two saves are two separate banks. Dedicated server - add it to your mod list and restart. Server and clients both need it. Legacies are stored server-side and keyed by username. The data file <Zomboid>/Lua/SkillLegacy_data.txt - on the server for multiplayer, in your own Zomboid folder for single player. One line per player, written on every death plus a ten-minute flush. Back it up with your saves; it is the only copy. Delete the file to wipe everyone, or a single line to reset one player. Removing the mod leaves every character exactly as they are. Troubleshooting Turn on Log every skill change for a per-skill breakdown on every death and restore: levels started and ended at, what was kept, XP earned and lost. Nothing happens on a fresh install - expected. Nothing is banked until someone dies with the mod already running. The button does not appear - either nothing is banked yet, or another mod has replaced the character creation screen. The log says which. Skills still carry either way, and the profession still decides. Requirements Build 42, tested on 42.20. Workshop ID: 3776561019 Mod ID: SkillLegacy

description: # WATER TRAILER B42.20 FIX - USER GUIDE Attention: it is very important to use this loading order for it to work perfectly. * **Do not enable this fix together with the original Water Trailer mod.** Both mods define the same trailers and will conflict with each other. ## INCLUDED TRAILERS The mod adds **small and large water trailers**, plus the **M967 water tanker** if the **Water Semi-Trailer** module is enabled. ## USING THE TANK 1. Approach the trailer and open its **radial menu**. 2. Open the tank cap. All actions that involve filling, draining, drinking, or transferring water require the cap to be open. 3. Choose an action: * Add water from a nearby river. * Add water from a container in your main inventory. * Transfer water from a nearby rain barrel or drum. * Fill a container from the tank. * Drink directly from the tank if the water is safe. * Drain the tank onto the ground. 4. Close the tank cap before driving. Water transfer is interrupted if your character walks or runs. Stay next to the trailer until the action is complete. ## CLEAN AND CONTAMINATED WATER * Water collected from rivers is contaminated. * Tanks found in the world may contain clean water, contaminated water, or be empty. * The water status is shown in the **Mechanics** window only when the tank contains water. * If the water is contaminated, install a filter in good condition to safely drink from the tank or fill containers with clean water. * The filter wears out with use. If it breaks, it will no longer purify contaminated water. * If contaminated water is mixed into the tank, the entire tank becomes contaminated. Use a filter in good condition whenever drawing water for drinking. ## PUMP, FILTER, AND PART CONDITION * The pump speeds up filling from rivers, rain barrels, and other large water sources. It also produces more noise and may wear out over time. * The pump and filter can be installed or removed through the **Mechanics** menu. A wrench and the required Mechanics skill level are needed. * The tank's capacity depends on its condition. ## WATER SPILLING WHILE DRIVING Water will spill if you drive with the tank cap open. description: Project Lottery Turn everyday cash into a reason to keep looting. Have you ever felt that the cash, credit cards, and other money-related items found throughout Project Zomboid are almost useless? Project Lottery gives them a brand-new purpose. Collect cash, convert valuable financial items into money, build a Lottery Machine, and spend your hard-earned cash on randomized rewards. Main Features Spend cash to draw randomized rewards from multiple item categories. Use the new Lottery interface to select a category and choose x1, x5, or x10 draws. Optional Skip Animation mode instantly shows all results in one result window. Batch draws charge the full cost when the draw begins, preventing unpaid draws midway through a sequence. Includes a Lottery animation for players who prefer the full draw experience. Extensive Sandbox Settings let you customize prices, quantities, machine durability, crafting requirements, natural spawning, and more. Supports fully customizable lottery pools with configurable rewards, weights, quantities, prices, and independent miss chances. Supports multiplayer. Custom lottery pools in multiplayer use the host/server configuration. Lottery Machines can naturally spawn directly in selected world locations. Winning Scratch Tickets and Stock Certificates can be exchanged for cash. How to Play Search the world for cash, credit cards, Scratch Tickets, Stock Certificates, and other useful valuables. Convert supported financial items into cash using their crafting recipes. Collect the materials required to craft a Lottery Machine: 6 Small Metal Sheets, 1 Wire, 5 Electronics Scrap, and 1 Glass Panel. Train Metalworking and Electrical. By default, the machine requires Metalworking Level 3 and Electrical Level 2. These requirements can be changed in Sandbox Settings. Craft and place your Lottery Machine. Right-click the machine and select Lottery to open the draw interface. Choose a lottery category, select x1 / x5 / x10, optionally enable Skip Animation, and start drawing. Built-in Lottery Categories Clothing Melee Weapons Ranged Weapons Weapon Attachments & Magazines Food Skill Books Ammunition Most built-in categories can be enabled or disabled individually, and their prices can be adjusted through Sandbox Settings. Custom Lottery Pools You can create your own lottery categories containing vanilla or modded items. Configuration file: Contents/mods/Project_Lottery_B42/42.20/media/ProjectLottery/CustomLotteryPools.txt You can edit this file with Notepad, Notepad++, VS Code, or any other plain-text editor. Each custom pool can configure: Pool name Whether the pool is enabled Cash cost per draw Independent chance of receiving nothing Vanilla and modded item IDs Relative item weights Minimum and maximum reward quantities Important notes: Item weights do not need to add up to 100. Draw probability is calculated from relative weight. A custom pool's miss chance is independent from the Sandbox miss-chance setting. The Sandbox option only affects the built-in lottery categories. The configuration file already contains instructions and examples. After changing the file, completely exit and restart the game or server before testing the changes. In multiplayer, custom lottery pools use only the host/server configuration. Steam may overwrite this file when the mod is updated or downloaded again. Back up your custom configuration before updating. Natural Lottery Machine Spawns Lottery Machines can optionally spawn directly in the world instead of inside loot containers. Sandbox Settings allow you to control: Whether Lottery Machines can spawn naturally Natural spawn chance Allowed spawn locations: garages, gas stations, and convenience stores Naturally spawned machines receive randomized durability, with middle-condition machines being more common than nearly broken or perfect-condition machines. Financial Item Exchanges Credit Cards can be converted into a random amount of cash. Minimum, maximum, and crafting time can be adjusted. Stock Certificates can be converted into a random amount of cash. Minimum, maximum, and crafting time can be adjusted. Winning Scratch Tickets can be redeemed for the exact cash amount shown on the ticket. Update History v1.6 Added a completely new Lottery interface. Lottery type is now selected from the interface instead of the old right-click submenu. Added x1, x5, and x10 draw options. The full cost of a multi-draw is charged immediately when the draw begins. Added a Skip Animation option. When Skip Animation is enabled, all results from a multi-draw are displayed together in a single result window. v1.5 Added cash redemption for winning Scratch Tickets. Added Stock Certificate-to-cash conversion with configurable random minimum, maximum, and crafting time. Thanks to TheWWworld, NickMillion, and Rappolt for the suggestions. v1.4 Added optional natural Lottery Machine spawning. Added configurable natural spawn chance. Added selectable spawn locations: garages, gas stations, and convenience stores. Naturally spawned machines use randomized durability. v1.3 Credit Card exchanges now reward a random amount of cash. The minimum and maximum Credit Card exchange values can be adjusted in Sandbox Settings. v1.2 Increased the Lottery Machine interaction range, making it easier to right-click. Removed packaged Skill Book sets from the Skill Book lottery pool. v1.1 Fixed multiplayer custom lottery pool loading. Multiplayer now uses only the host/server configuration. v1.0 Added multiplayer support. Removed magazines, boxed ammunition, and ammunition cases from the Ammunition lottery pool. Added the Weapon Attachments lottery category, including magazines and ranged-weapon attachments. v0.9 Added a Sandbox option for starting new characters with a Lottery Machine. Disabled by default. Added a Sandbox setting for Lottery Machine weight. v0.8 Split Weapon Draw into Melee Weapon Draw and Ranged Weapon Draw. Added an Ammunition Draw. Added Sandbox options to enable or disable the built-in lottery categories. Mod ID: Project_Lottery_B42 Workshop ID: 3776979836 Mod ID: Project_Lottery_B42

description: 补档！ 这里不欢迎不尊重二次元文化的任何生物，如果你有闲心在这骂我，不妨节省你的时间去找你喜欢的mod，毕竟我没拿枪抵在你脑袋上逼你玩！ 【前言】 -- 跨越时间与空间，是人类生存在这广袤银河的唯一选择。 ---------------- ---------------------------------------------------------- 莉莉丝之父 ------ 开始游戏前的注意事项 如图所示，请将最大纹理尺寸调整至1024及以上.否则可能会导致部分角色模型渲染异常。 前排：更新日志 26.8.8：重要更新 详见讨论区。 26.8.9： 1.交易价格平衡性调整：因许多可出售的工具及武器都可以通过制造大量获取，为了不让玩家短时间内获得大量点数而降低游戏性，削弱了大部分可出售工具及武器的售卖价格。 2.同时新增多种可出售的工具，详情可进入游戏出售配方一栏查看。 3.降低了口衔面包片的升级难度，可以用多种调味料升级，不再局限于黄油/果酱两种。 3.修复了远程武器无法修复/充能的问题。 4.感谢群友的反馈，修复了出售背包类道具需要消耗传呼机电力的问题。 模组总览 此模组是适用于僵尸毁灭工程B42稳定版的日漫二次元类型模组。此模组历经长时间开发，是延续我之前的Project Anime模组风格，并融入无尽心血的周年巨献。130+衣物数量、25+武器以及数不尽的各类物品，涵盖服装、近战武器、枪械、食品、背包、交易系统各方面，是一个综合类的模组。现有17套风格不同的服装套装，并且仍在更新！周年版的Project Anime已经将KKS前置库融合到模组中，因此不再需要任何前置模组。 （Anime Shader, Cute Girl Voice以及Clothing Holes not Display模组并非必须，只是我推荐你一起装上游玩，以得到更好的体验！） Mod Has In-Game English Support Now. Enable Project Anime English Sub Mod to Get English Support. 核心内容 1. 动漫身形：本质上是一件包裹全身的衣服，穿上后即可变身为可爱的动漫少女。此外，它可以升级以提升性能，请检查你的制作菜单！现有6位可爱的角色，她们2位是来自《边缘世界》中的萌螈族：https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3292351432。此外，你也许会发现更多有关萌螈族的...彩蛋？此外，还有来自未来科技军工企业董事长、没落家族中的大小姐、大小姐的专属女仆、废柴死神等你体验。 2. 各种服装：Project Anime的服装为了做好与原版或其他模组中服装的区分，服装名称前都有严格对应的数字编号。很重要的一点：由于动漫身形和原版服装的体型差距过大，因此不兼容原版或其他模组根据原版僵毁的人物体型做出来的服装。不过，现本模组中的服装数量，已经可以供你养眼很长一段时间了，并且，得益于我KKS引擎的更新，现在服装的制作变得特别容易，后续的更新中也会不断添加新的服装。如果你有喜欢的衣服，可向我提供Koikatsu（Sunshine）（恋活1或2）的人物卡以及对应的服装zip mod或服装卡，或许有朝一日，你喜欢的服装会更新到新版本中！ 3. 与WESTTECH®企业进行交易：选好开局故事剧本后，玩家进入游戏后便自动得到一个可以和WESTTECH®企业进行交易的传呼机。许多本模组和原版的物品都可以进行交易，如果你缺了或者想要什么，不妨问问他们有没有吧！ 如何正确地游玩本模组 1. 你是新建的存档：建立角色时，第一步：在选择职业的界面，根据自己的喜好选择带有【Project Anime】字样的剧本故事，可根据自己的需求挑选其它特质；第二步：建立人物界面建议什么都不要穿。进入游戏后，你会得到对应故事中相关的物品。 2. 你是现有的存档：加入本模组后，当你毁灭丧尸时，你会发现它们身上可能会掉落“WESTTECH®点数”的物品。使用5个点数即可直接兑换用于本模组中交易的传呼机。再使用传呼机和更多的点数兑换其它物品吧！ 关于模组的兼容性 本模组和绝大部分其它模组都能和谐相处。但请注意：可能会和其它武器类模组冲突，尤其是带有消音器脚本的模组。 快速问答 Q：会有更多的服装吗？ A：会的哦。 Q：点数要去哪里获得呢？ A：丧尸会掉落，通过传呼机出售有价值的物品可大量获得。 Q：其他的服装要怎么获取呢？ A：丧尸会有小概率掉落服装包。同时WESTTECH®企业提供完整的服装包交易服务。 Q：模组里的服装，所有角色都可以穿戴吗？ A：可以。因为身形模型都是一样的，所有角色都可以穿戴。例如：大小姐也可以穿女仆装。 Q：不同服装包里的服装可以混搭吗？ A：当然可以。（有些会穿模） Q：可以联机游玩吗？ A：联机游玩是没有问题的，毕竟本模组里含的lua脚本代码是非常少的，不用太担心脚本报错、游戏更新导致代码失效的问题。 Q：本模组适合什么风格的玩家呢？ A：首先，本模组是日漫二次元风格，并非欧美写实动漫风格。人物、衣服建模非常卡通化，很萌很可爱。另外，本模组除枪械方面外，强度比较贴合原版。但由于开局会根据剧本故事赠送开局装备，还是建议大家调高生存难度。 同时，欢迎加入Project Anime周年纪念版交流群（群号1074301899）！加入群聊以第一时间获取补档以及体验最新内容！ Workshop ID: 3777364365 Mod ID: ProjectAnimeAnniversaryStable Mod ID: ProjectAnimeEnglish
