[B42.20] Brita Combined Compatibility Port About This Mod This is an unofficial compatibility project that combines and rebuilds content from Brita's Weapon Pack and Brita's Armor Pack for Project Zomboid Build 42.20. Features previously handled by Arsenal GunFighter have been reviewed and replaced with native Build 42 systems wherever possible. This project is currently undergoing compatibility testing. Some features and behaviors may differ from the original Build 41 mods. Installation Subscribe to this Workshop item. Wait for Steam to finish downloading it. Enable Brita Combined B42 in the in-game Mods menu. Starting a new world is recommended for reliable item distribution. When added to an existing world, new items may appear only in unexplored areas and newly generated containers. Multiplayer servers and all joining players must use the same version of the mod. Important Compatibility Information This is a standalone mod and does not require any additional Brita or GunFighter mods. The following original mods are not required: Brita's Weapon Pack Brita's Armor Pack Arsenal GunFighter Do not enable these original mods alongside this port. Doing so may cause duplicate items and conflicts between firearm systems. This mod does not load or depend on files from the original mods during gameplay. This version is intended exclusively for Project Zomboid Build 42.20. Main Features Combines compatible content from Brita's Weapon Pack and Armor Pack into one mod. Uses Build 42 systems for reloading, chambering, fire modes, and aiming. Restores dedicated magazines and feed systems where required by individual firearms. Supports compatible standard, extended, drum, clip, cylinder, belt, and ammunition-container feed types. Uses available Build 42 reload actions and animation families wherever possible. Updates armor and special-equipment body locations for the Build 42 clothing-slot structure. Adjusts weapon range, accuracy, sound radius, knockdown, and muzzle-effect positions. Applies firearm and caliber-appropriate normal and suppressed firing sounds. Converts supported optics, weapon lights, suppressors, lasers, and night-vision equipment to Build 42 systems. Ammunition Policy To reduce ammunition duplication and conflicts with other Build 42 firearm mods, this port currently uses compatible vanilla ammunition families. Dedicated Brita magazines are retained when their shape or capacity is required, but they consume the corresponding mapped vanilla ammunition. The current primary mappings are: .380 firearms use the 9mm ammunition family. 5.45 and .223 firearms use the 5.56 ammunition family. 7.62 rifle families and selected large-caliber rifle cartridges use the .308 ammunition family. Supported shotguns, including 20 gauge and .410 bore weapons, use vanilla shotgun shells. Legacy Brita loose ammunition and ammunition boxes do not spawn naturally. These ammunition mappings are a temporary Build 42 compatibility solution. They may be revised if a stable shared ammunition framework becomes available in the future. Attachments and Special Equipment Scopes and red-dot sights use Build 42 aiming modifiers. Weapon lights use the Build 42 lighting system. Suppressors reduce gunshot noise and zombie-attraction range. Lasers provide aiming bonuses, but visible laser beams are not rendered. Night-vision equipment uses Build 42's native night-vision effect. Thermal optics provide low-light bonuses but do not provide a separate thermal display. Bipods function as fixed recoil-reduction attachments and cannot be deployed. Bayonets provide their visual model and stat modifiers but do not provide a separate stabbing mode. Gas masks, oxygen equipment, radios, and headsets are connected to Build 42 systems wherever possible. Grenade-launcher attachments are currently disabled and do not spawn naturally. Special Weapons The XM214, GAU-17, and GAU-19 miniguns are included as simplified automatic firearms. They use dedicated ammunition containers filled with mapped vanilla ammunition. GunFighter's barrel spin-up, heat system, and custom rotary animations are not included. Excluded Features The following features are currently excluded because they cannot be implemented reliably in Build 42 or depend heavily on GunFighter-specific systems: RPGs and rocket launchers Flamethrowers Custom grenades and special projectiles Mines and selected explosives Bows and crossbows The GunFighter HUD Folding-stock transformations GunFighter-specific animations Legacy crafting recipes Known Issues The following areas are still being reviewed: Spawn rates for certain weapons and armor Weapon-specific magazine and ammunition compatibility Reload actions and magazine models for some firearms Weapon-specific firing and suppressed sounds Long-range aiming and crosshair behavior Some muzzle effects and visual-effect positions Zombie hit reactions and knockdown behavior Some attachment models and functions Multiplayer synchronization Bug Reports If you discover a problem, please report it in the comments. When possible, include the following information: Weapon and magazine names Ammunition type Installed attachments Steps required to reproduce the problem Whether you were playing single-player or multiplayer Whether the test was performed in a new world Detailed reports are extremely helpful when identifying and fixing compatibility problems. Original Creators and Rights Notice This is an unofficial Build 42 compatibility-testing project. All original assets, designs, names, and associated rights belong to their respective creators. This project is not an official update and is not affiliated with or endorsed by the original creators. If you are one of the original creators, know a verified official contact method, or know of an official statement regarding Build 42 ports, please leave a comment or contact me. I would be happy to share technical findings and migration notes or cooperate with an official Build 42 project. This project is not intended to replace or compete with an official Build 42 release. If an official version becomes available, I would prefer to support and use that version. If requested by the original creators, this Workshop item may be unpublished or made private at any time. Please do not harass, insult, spam, or repeatedly contact the original creators or other port developers on behalf of this project. Keep all discussions respectful and focused on compatibility testing and technical feedback. Workshop ID: 3777433827 Mod ID: BritaCombinedB42 Workshop ID: 3777433827 Mod ID: BritaCombinedB42

description: Easy Engine Repair Vanilla engine repair is brutal. On most Build 42 vehicles you need Mechanics 5 just to unlock the option, and once you get there each engine part restores about 1 point of condition. Even at Mechanics 10 you are looking at 3.5. The formula has a cap of 5 that you can never actually reach. Emptying a whole crate of engine parts to move the bar a few percent is not a challenge. It is a chore. This mod replaces that formula with one you control. What it changes Vanilla: 1 + ((Mechanics - vehicle's required level) / 2), capped at 5 This mod: Mechanics x Multiplier, clamped between a minimum and a maximum With the default settings, on a typical vehicle (required level 5): The skill requirement is untouched. You still need Mechanics equal to the vehicle's required level before you can repair its engine at all. This mod only changes how much each part gives you once you qualify. A beginner still cannot fix a sports car. Sandbox options Everything is configurable under the Easy Engine Repair tab in the sandbox settings, both when starting a solo game and when creating a server. Multiplier per engine part and skill level - multiplies your Mechanics level. Default 3, range 0.1 to 100. Minimum condition per part - floor for the result, so a part never feels wasted. Default 3, range 1 to 100. Maximum condition per part - ceiling for the result. Default 30, range 1 to 100. Want something closer to vanilla but without the grind? Set the multiplier to 1. Want engine parts to actually fix an engine? Leave the defaults. Want it absurd? Raise the maximum. Multiplayer Works on servers, but the mod has to be installed on the server, not only on your client. The sandbox values are server-authoritative, so every player automatically plays with the settings the admin chose. For server admins: Mod ID: easy_engine_repair - goes in Mods= Workshop ID: 3777460879 - goes in WorkshopItems= Compatibility Build 42 only. It will not show up in your mod list on Build 41. Safe to add to an existing save and safe to remove. It adds no items, no map data and no saved state. It overrides the ISRepairEngine:complete() function, so it will conflict with any other mod that rewrites that same function. Languages English, Spanish, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Japanese, German, French and Italian. More translations are welcome, they are small JSON files under media/lua/shared/Translate/. AI transparency As a programmer I watch AI move into my field every day, and most of the time nobody even tells you which content was AI-generated. So here is a short section making clear what part it played in this project. AI was used for: As a learning guide for modding Project Zomboid. The translations (manual corrections from native speakers are welcome). The Workshop description in every language. AI was not used for: Writing or fixing the code. Functional analysis and design decisions. Workshop ID: 3777460879 Mod ID: easy_engine_repair

description: English Tired of clicking every single tree, every single tile of grass, one at a time? Zone Tools lets you draw a rectangle on the map and have your character handle the whole area automatically - using the exact same actions and requirements as the game's own right-click menu, just applied to many tiles in one go. Features Chop trees - cuts down every tree in the area with the axe in your inventory. Saw logs into planks - walks to every pile of logs in the area and saws them into planks, leaving the planks at the pile instead of loading you down. Clear bushes - cuts down every bush in the area with a cutting tool in your inventory. Clear grass - clears grass and weeds from every tile in the area, using your scythe when you're carrying one. Till soil - digs/plows every tillable dirt tile in the area for farming, with a hoe or shovel. Collect items - picks up every loose item lying on the ground in the area and carries it to one tile you pick, making return trips whenever your character can't carry any more. Move corpses - drags every corpse in the area to one destination tile you pick, one at a time. How to use Press F8, or click the toolbox icon in the bottom-left corner of the screen. Pick a tool from the menu. Click one corner of the area, then click the opposite corner. For Collect items and Move corpses: after the area, click one more tile - that's where everything gets taken to. Sit back and watch, or press ESC / the Cancel button any time to stop. Notes Every action uses the same tools/requirements as doing it manually - no axe, no tree chopping, no saw, no plank sawing, and so on. Moving with WASD (or anything that normally interrupts an action) while a batch is running cancels the rest of it - it won't quietly pick back up later. Selection is capped at 40x40 tiles per use. You can lower that limit, globally or per tool, in Sandbox Options > Zone Tools. Compatibility Client-side only, and every action is queued through the game's own vanilla functions (the same ones the right-click menu uses) - nothing is done "by hand," so it should behave normally around other mods and in multiplayer. Should be safe to add/remove mid-save. Build 42 only. Questions, bugs, or ideas for more tools? Drop a comment below. Türkçe Her ağacı, her çim karosunu tek tek tıklamaktan sıkıldın mı? Zone Tools (Alan Araçları), haritada bir dikdörtgen çizmene ve karakterinin tüm alanı otomatik olarak halletmesine izin verir - oyunun kendi sağ tık menüsüyle birebir aynı eylemleri ve gereksinimleri kullanarak, sadece aynı anda birçok kareye uygulanmış halde. Özellikler Ağaç Kesme - Envanterindeki baltayla alandaki her ağacı keser. Kütükleri Kalasa Çevirme - Alandaki her kütük yığınına gidip onları kalasa çevirir, çıkan kalasları üzerine yüklemek yerine kestiği yerde bırakır. Çalı Temizleme - Envanterindeki kesici bir aletle alandaki her çalıyı keser. Çim Temizleme - Alandaki her karodaki çim ve yabani otları temizler; yanında tırpan varsa onu kullanır. Toprak İşleme - Çapa veya kürekle, alandaki işlenebilir her toprak karosunu tarım için kazar/sürer. Eşya Toplama - Alanda yerde duran tüm eşyaları toplar ve seçtiğin tek bir kareye taşır; karakter daha fazla taşıyamaz hale geldiğinde gidip bırakır ve kaldığı yerden devam eder. Ceset Taşıma - Alandaki her cesedi, seçtiğin tek bir hedef kareye, birer birer sürükler. Nasıl kullanılır F8'e bas, ya da ekranın sol alt köşesindeki alet çantası ikonuna tıkla. Menüden bir araç seç. Alanın bir köşesine tıkla, sonra karşı köşesine tıkla. Eşya Toplama ve Ceset Taşıma için: alandan sonra bir kare daha tıkla - her şey oraya götürülecek. Arkana yaslanıp izle, ya da istediğin an ESC / İptal butonuna basarak durdur. Notlar Her işlem, elle yapıldığındaki aynı alet/gereksinimleri kullanır - balta yoksa ağaç kesilmez, testere yoksa kalas kesilmez, vs. Bir işlem sürerken WASD ile hareket etmek (veya normalde bir eylemi kesen herhangi bir şey), işlemin kalanını iptal eder - daha sonra sessizce kaldığı yerden devam etmez. Seçim, kullanım başına 40x40 kare ile sınırlıdır. Bu sınırı, genel olarak veya araç bazında, Sandbox Ayarları > Zone Tools kısmından düşürebilirsin. Uyumluluk Yalnızca istemci (client) tarafında çalışır ve her işlem, oyunun kendi orijinal fonksiyonları üzerinden (sağ tık menüsünün kullandığı aynı fonksiyonlar) sıraya konur - hiçbir şey "elle/ham" yapılmaz, bu yüzden diğer modlarla ve çok oyunculu modda normal şekilde çalışması beklenir. Kayıt ortasında eklenip çıkarılması güvenli olmalıdır. Sadece Build 42. Sorular, hatalar veya yeni araç fikirleri mi var? Aşağıya yorum bırak. description: A bugfix and stability patch for Bandits, written from the Build 42.20 source. The community already had one of these - BanditsFix by MCZGabriel - but it targets 42.13.x and has not been updated since February. This is a fresh implementation for 42.20, with the same goal and a few fixes it never had. Credit to MCZGabriel for the idea; none of that mod's code is used here. Safe to add to a world already in progress, safe to remove. Every fix has its own switch in the in-game Mod Options panel. Dedicated servers: add it to the server's mod list as well, not only to the clients. Bandits are dressed and their corpse loot is decided on the server, so the clothing fix has to run there. Everything else is client side and works either way. The warning arrow actually works Bandits aims the red "hostiles nearby" arrow exactly once, at the tile the group spawned on, and then never touches it again - it does not even turn as you walk around, and it hangs there for half an hour after you have killed everybody. Now the arrow points at the nearest living bandit's current position, and the warning disappears the moment there is nothing left alive to warn you about. Corpses keep their clothes Bandits are zombies wearing a costume. They are spawned in a "Naked" outfit and dressed with item visuals, which are graphics with no real item behind them, so the corpse comes out bare. The code that was supposed to put the clothes on the body is still sitting in the mod, commented out. This puts it back. No loot is duplicated - the death loot list is rebuilt from scratch every time it is written. Companions stop wrecking your base Most of the demolition code checks whether the NPC is hostile first. Three branches do not: a barricaded door, a locked double door, and any other locked door. That is why your own ally walks up to your front door and chops it down. Friendly NPCs now leave player-built walls, doors, windows and barricades alone, and you can tighten that to "never damage anything" or turn it off entirely. Hostile raiders still break in. That is the whole point of them. No more running on the spot A light watchdog measures whether an NPC on a move order is actually covering ground. If it has not moved for a few seconds its path is dropped and it picks a new goal. No teleporting, no forced pathfinding. Soft guard posts A guard post is one exact tile, and pathfinding does not reliably land on one exact tile - so the companion is never quite "at" its post, goes back to following you, walks away, takes the post again, forever. Posts now have a tolerance of a tile or two, and a post somebody is already holding does not count as free. Nobody gets snapped into position. Bandits do not know where you are You are supposed to have the advantage of knowing where they are. They should not have the same advantage over you. Out of the box a Tracker hears you through walls from fifty-five tiles away, and in multiplayer the engine's own zombie AI keeps pathing bandits straight to players across the map. Now they find you the way zombies do: line of sight, sound at close range, or getting shot. They also remember where they last saw you and search there for a while, instead of forgetting you the instant you step behind a wall - so breaking line of sight is worth doing, and firefights do not fall apart. Gunshots and alarms still pull them in. Hearing a rifle three streets away and coming to look is fine; knowing which room you are standing in is not. Requirements Bandits by Slayer (Workshop 3268487204) is required. Do not run this together with the old BanditsFix - they patch the same things. Works with the companion mods True Companions and Bandits Creator are both supported, and were checked against line by line rather than assumed. Nothing here overwrites a function either of them overwrites. The stealth rules apply only to NPCs that are actually hunting you - a companion following you, standing in a passive stance or knocked down is never treated as a threat, so orders and following keep working when you break line of sight. Bandits Creator is untouched: nothing in this mod hooks a context menu or sits anywhere in the debug spawn path. Available in every language the game ships with. Corrections from native speakers are very welcome, drop them in the discussions and I will fold them in. Notes Does not alter the base AI - every patch keeps a reference to the original function and calls it, so with a fix switched off the behaviour is bit for bit the base mod's. Does not duplicate loot. Low performance impact: the heavy work runs a few times a second, not every frame. When a bandit is infected and killed by a zombie, a temporary zombie can appear without clothes; killing it restores the real body with its loot. That is how Bandits works internally and it is not a bug. Workshop ID: 3777752751 Mod ID: BanditsFixPlus

description: A loot run mode you switch on. While it is on, every building you go into is circled in red on your world map and dated. Three days into a town you cannot tell, looking at the map, which of forty houses you already stripped. So you re-walk them, and you only find out the second visit was wasted once you are inside staring at empty shelves. You had that information at the time. It just had nowhere to live. Press F7 to start a loot run Rebindable. While loot run mode is on, any building you actually stop in gets a red circle with today's date inside it, at the building's centre on the world map and the minimap. Go back a week later and the mark re-dates itself. Press the key again to stop. Marks are drawn with the vanilla annotation system, so they look like something you drew yourself, they show up everywhere your own marks do, and they save with your game. While the mode is off the mod does nothing at all. Why a mode and not always-on Marking every building you ever walk into makes the map useless - a wall of red over everywhere you have sheltered, fought through, or cut across on the way somewhere else. A mark is only worth something if it means I searched this one, and only you know when that was true. The switch is how you say so. Taking marks off again One at a time - rub it out on the map. These are ordinary annotations, so the world map's own eraser removes them exactly like a symbol you drew by hand: open the map, pick up the eraser, click the mark. The mod notices and forgets the building properly, so it stays gone rather than coming back next time you load. Rubbing out either half takes the whole mark with it. Erasing needs an Eraser in your inventory, the same as erasing any other map annotation. That is vanilla's rule and these are vanilla annotations; the mod does not carve out an exception for its own. All of them - Clear all loot run marks in the options. Erases every mark this character has placed. Does not touch symbols you drew yourself, and needs no eraser. There is a short delay before a building is marked A door is a thing you walk through, not only a thing you go in. Cutting across a lobby to reach the street behind it would otherwise leave a mark saying you looted the place - which is worse than no mark, because you will believe it. So a building has to still have you in it a minute later. The delay is in in-game minutes, so it means the same thing at every day length: long enough that you stopped. Configurable, or switch it off. Works with Container Cleanup If you also run Container Cleanup, loot run mode arms it too - one key, one decision, for the whole run. Mark where you have been, and bin the junk where it stands. No dependency either way. Container Cleanup does not know this mod exists and works exactly as before without it; this mod looks for Container Cleanup and does without. Turn the handshake off in the options if you want the two modes separate. Requires Container Cleanup 1.1.0 or later for the handshake; older copies simply ignore it. Safehouses are never marked Buildings on protected ground are skipped entirely - no mark, and no record that you were there. Mostly this is about your own base. A loot run mark means stripped, do not come back, which is the exact opposite of what a safehouse is. Keeping out of other people's is the side benefit. Two systems are covered, because the admin panel builds them with two different tools: Safehouses - player claims, and the admin panel's Safezone tool, which creates an ordinary safehouse under the hood. One and the same thing. Non-PVP zones - the admin panel's Non PVP Zone tool and the Zone Editor's NonPVP mode. A separate system with no owner, usually drawn over a spawn town or a trade hub. The check runs against the square you are standing on and the building's corners and centre, so a warehouse straddling a zone boundary is skipped even when you are in the unclaimed half. Share marks with your group In multiplayer, everyone in your safehouse can see the buildings you have marked, and you see theirs - a wasted second visit is wasted whoever makes it. Faction sharing works the same way and can be combined with it. Both mean the same safehouse or the same faction - that is how the engine compares them. If you play as a group without one claimed building between you, tick Share marks with everyone instead and the whole server sees them. Sharing is off-by-default in the sense that matters: nothing leaves your map unless you ask it to. Sharing is decided when a mark goes down, so switching it on leaves the marks already on your map private. Share marks I have already placed brings those along too. This rides on Build 42's own annotation sharing, the same mechanism behind the sharing panel on the world map. No custom server component. Players without the mod see shared marks as ordinary map annotations. Settings Options -> Mods -> Loot Run Assistant, per player: Loot run mode key - F7 by default, rebind to anything. Mark buildings I enter - on. Wait before marking - 1 in-game minute. Immediately, 1, 2 or 5. Skip small structures - on. Sheds and outhouses are not worth a mark. Show the date on the mark - on. Arm Container Cleanup too - on. Does nothing if that mod is absent. Share marks with everyone - off, multiplayer only. Overrides the two below. Share marks with my safehouse - on, multiplayer only. Share marks with my faction - off, multiplayer only. Share marks I have already placed - shares the marks that went down before you switched sharing on. Press Apply first. Clear all loot run marks - erases every mark and forgets them. Server Settings -> Loot Run Assistant, sandbox: Enable loot run marking - on. Master switch for the server. Allow sharing marks - on. Off forces every player's marks private. What it writes to your save Map annotations, in the same per-save store as symbols you draw by hand, and one small record per marked building on your character. Adds no items, no recipes and no tiles. Uninstalling leaves the annotations behind, since by then they are ordinary map symbols. Clear all loot run marks removes both halves and is the clean way out before you go. Credit The technique for reaching the map symbols without opening the map is lifted from TwisTonFire's Quick'n'Auto Mark, which proved it at scale. If you want automatic marking without a mode, a dock UI and a symbol picker, go and look at that one - it is a different design for a different taste and it is good at what it does. description: Skill Recovery Journal - Build 42.20 Respawn Fix Let a respawned character recover journal XP normally after death. On Build 42.20.1, SRJ's life-bound XP ledger can survive a local character's death and be copied to the respawned character. The journal item still contains the recorded XP and recipes, but SRJ treats that XP as already recovered, so reading the journal silently skips XP while recipes still restore. This patch fixes the issue as an independent compatibility add-on and does not modify any files of the original SRJ mod. What It Fixes Clears SRJ's life-bound player state (read-XP ledger, flat XP, deductions, starting skill levels) when the player dies. Resets the matching server ledger for multiplayer deaths. Performs a one-time cleanup for saves that were already affected before the patch was installed. Leaves XP and recipes stored in journal items untouched. Installation & Load Order Install the original Skill Recovery Journal mod first. Copy the patch into the Zomboid/mods folder. Enable the patch after Skill Recovery Journal in the mod list. description: Preface This mod is inspired by Immersive Looting: Search Mode and the gradual search-and-reveal looting experience in Escape from Tarkov. Based on that idea, I rebuilt it for Build 42 and added my own design ideas and features. Introduction Turns "opening a container and instantly seeing everything inside" into a looting process that actually takes time to confirm. When opening a container, the items inside will not be revealed immediately. Instead, they will first appear as unknown items. The player must search gradually to identify the contents of each item stack. This gives looting a bit more process, pacing, and tension; and before a container has been fully searched, Transfer All cannot be used directly. Searching creates a small amount of noise and may attract zombies. Holding Shift during searching allows fast searching, but it creates louder noise and may also cause sudden mishaps. If the darkness search penalty is enabled in Sandbox Settings, dim or dark environments will slow searching down, while player light sources can reduce this penalty. Darkness can also make fast-search mishaps more likely. Search time is affected by item value and rarity. More valuable or harder-to-identify items may take longer to reveal. The Foraging skill also affects looting speed. At high Foraging levels, low-value items may even be revealed instantly. Searching can grant a very small amount of Foraging XP. The Foraging skill does not affect item generation inside containers. Item generation still follows the vanilla logic completely; this mod only adds an unknown overlay and search process on top of existing items. Most of the settings above can be enabled, disabled, or adjusted individually in Sandbox Settings. Features Gradual item reveal (default key Z, configurable in key bindings) Fast search (default key Shift, configurable in key bindings) Optional darkness-based search slowdown and fast-search mishap multipliers Basic controller support (Interact to search, Run binding for fast search) Search time affected by item value and rarity Noise risk (normal, fast, mishap) Further noise reduction based on the Dextrous trait and/or Sneaking skill Foraging XP Right-click search nearby containers (optional) Exclude safehouse containers Language support: EN / CH / CN / JP / KO / ES / RU Multiplayer Notes In multiplayer, search states for wild containers are shared through container and item modData within the range that the game itself can synchronize. In other words, the state is not stored on a single player. It is bound to world objects, container items, and items inside containers. As long as the server and game synchronize these objects correctly, other players arriving at the same location will see the same search progress. Even after leaving the area, the search state will still be remembered the next time you return. This helps you tell which of the countless zombie corpses along a fence have already been searched. For containers that have been fully searched, anyone opening them will see the revealed state instead of Unknown. If a container has only been partially searched, other players should theoretically see the same partial reveal state: revealed items display normally, while unrevealed items still appear as Unknown. Safehouse containers use a looser handling method to avoid turning base storage into a repetitive daily chore. Compatibility Notes This mod changes container and looting UI behavior, so it may conflict with the following types of mods: Mods that replace the Loot Window Mods that modify container buttons or Loot All behavior Mods that change world object double-click interactions Other UI/interaction mods that modify inventory, containers, or the looting process Compatibility testing with CleanUI has been completed; in the future, I will only maintain compatibility with CleanUI Author Notes Essentially, this is a mod made for myself, my friends, and private servers. I will not actively reply to every comment, but if there is a bug caused by this mod itself, rather than a compatibility issue, I will maintain and fix it. You can leave feature suggestions, but I most likely will not reply and may not implement them. If there is an interesting idea, I may shamelessly take it for myself. That said, I am very willing to hear UI/UX feedback. I do not mind anyone using the source code, modifying it, integrating it into their own mods, creating and publishing derivative versions, or adding other languages. I give full permission here, and you do not need to ask beforehand. But if you are willing to leave a comment and let me know, I would be very happy, because I simply want to know whether this mod has actually helped someone. description: Adds a buildable wooden ladder to the Carpentry build menu. Build it again on the same tile and the new section stacks on top of the old one, so you can reach the roof of a two- or three-storey building without ever being up there. Companion to Climb Ladders, which is what lets you actually climb it. The gap it fills Build 42 lets you build staircases - wooden, log and welded - but no ladders. The sprites have been in the game all along, in the carpentry tileset, with their ladder properties already set, and nothing uses them: they only ever appear placed by hand on the map. This mod gives them the recipe they were missing. No new art, no new tiles. The recipe Carpentry, level 3. 4 planks, 8 nails, and a hammer you don't use up. Four orientations, rotated with the build cursor. They are four different sprites, not one mirrored: two are drawn with a bit of wall behind them and sit well against a building, two are bare and sit well on their own. Cheaper and lower level than the base game's staircases on purpose. A ladder is the cheap way up, and in exchange the dead can't follow you. Two and three storey buildings One section reaches the level above. A three-storey building needs three sections, and you build all three from the ground, aiming at the same tile every time: Build on the ground tile against the wall. Section goes to level 0. Build again, same tile. Section appears at level 1. Build again, same tile. Section appears at level 2. You never have to be up there, which matters, because the build cursor only reaches the level you are standing on. One section, one payment - no discount for height. You need a climbing mod In Build 42 these sprites carry the ladder properties but not the climbSheet flag the engine checks, so without a mod that does the movement itself, a ladder you build is decoration. This mod no longer forces which one. It used to list Climb Ladders as a hard requirement, which meant it silently refused to load for anyone who preferred a different climbing mod. That was the wrong call and it's gone: use whichever you like. Mine is Climb Ladders, and version 2.4 or newer also fixes a related bug: a ladder that stopped short of the roof used to drop you inside the building, through the wall. Taking them down Destroy or dismantle the bottom section and the whole column comes down with it, refunding the materials for every section. This is because the build and destroy cursors only work at the level you are standing on, so stacked sections can't be selected from the ground - and to get up there you would need the very ladder you are trying to remove. Before, that left ladders you could only delete through debug mode. Details Adds no items and no tiles. One build recipe, using sprites already in the game. Doesn't require a wall behind it. Plenty of player-built bases are loose floors and platforms with nothing to lean on. English and Spanish. Requires Build 42.20 or newer. Support If this saved you a trip around the building looking for a way up, you can buy me a coffee on Ko-fi. Completely optional - the mod is free and stays free. description: Stable Corpse Driving Your vehicle keeps full control when driving over zombie corpses at speed. In vanilla, running over zombie corpses at speed launches the vehicle into the air with upward wheel impulses, briefly leaving it uncontrollable while the dashboard flashes. This mod keeps the car planted so steering, throttle, and brakes always respond — while collision detection and damage behave exactly like vanilla. Features The vehicle is no longer launched into the air when driving over zombie corpses; steering and throttle stay responsive at any speed. No corpse is moved or removed; corpses and their items stay exactly where they are. Vanilla collision is preserved: run-over hits, impact sounds, and normal vehicle wear (such as wheel damage) still occur. Real collisions (walls, trees, live zombies) behave exactly like vanilla; the car can still flip or take damage. The dashboard only flashes red for severe damage or a destroyed part, instead of blinking on every minor run-over scratch. Zombies, animals, items, and other game rules are unaffected. Works in single-player and multiplayer. How It Works Vanilla applies an upward impulse to each wheel that runs over a corpse. The strength is scaled by the corpse's corpseSize mod data (zombie corpses have none, so it defaults to 1.0). At high speed, or with several corpses in one tile, the impulses stack and launch the car off the ground. This mod sets zombie corpses' corpseSize to 0.1, making the launch impulse nearly disappear so the car stays grounded — the collision itself still happens. Compatibility Project Zomboid Build 42.20+ Single-player / Multiplayer Can be added to an existing save No required mods Adds no items, recipes, or sandbox settings Mod Information Mod ID: StableCorpseDriving Version: 1.0.0

On Build 42.20, when a vehicle towing a trailer collides with a zombie, an obstacle such as a fence or tree, or a building, the trailer automatically detaches from the towing vehicle with a metal break sound. Even if a hard collision still trips the vanilla detach check, the trailer is automatically re-hitched while you keep driving. While backing up with a trailer, steering is eased to stop the fold from deepening; a flung trailer is gently pulled back, and if it detaches during a jackknife it is re-hitched once the rig is straightened out. Please rate! Skully's Zombie CollisionA mod that adds proper collision between zombies, preventing them from phasing through each other while chasing the player. Internally tested and balanced. Reported by other players to work in multiplayer for extended sessions without issues (see comments for feedback). The issue: In vanilla, zombies usually go through one another when they are chasing you, especially if you hit or push the zombie at the front. The solution: This mod aims to fix the lack of collision that zombies have when they are chasing the player in a way that doesn't ruin your performance. It only considers the zombies close to you and only a small amount, which is what matters. Whether you have 10 zombies or 100 zombies around you, the additional performance strain remains roughly the same. Multiplayer tested: (With 200 ping and the usual MP desync. When fighting alone, feels like in single player) Shoutout to goco for helping me test, much apreciated Zombies dont go through walls! Ambient City Lights SINGLEPLAYER & MULTIPLAYER – BUILD 42.20 When the power grid goes down, the atmosphere of Knox Country's towns does not have to disappear with it, right? What does the mod do? Ambient City Lights preserves the nighttime atmosphere in towns after the power shuts down. Streetlights, illuminated signs, and supported outdoor lamps continue to light up the streets and make these places feel alive after dark. Only the ambient city lighting is affected. Houses, appliances, fuel pumps, and all other electrical devices still require a proper power source. Features Streetlights and other fixed city lighting stay active at night after the power grid fails. Supported outdoor lamps can still be switched on and off through the context menu, direct interaction, or a controller. You can choose how many supported lights should remain available. Every supported light has a very rare chance to flicker, dim, or go out for a while. Optionally, more and more lights can fail over time. Lamps powered by generators or batteries remain fully controlled by the base game. Works in both singleplayer and multiplayer. Sandbox Settings The sandbox options let you decide how brightly your towns remain lit after the power grid fails and whether that lighting should slowly fade over time: Active Lights (0–100%): Controls how many supported lights stay lit. At 100%, the full city lighting remains. Lower values create dark gaps and make the streets feel less perfectly maintained. Flickering Lights: Every supported lamp has a very rare chance to develop a fault. Most only flicker briefly or become dimmer. In rare cases, a lamp may show warning signs and then remain dark for one to four in-game hours. Two neighboring lamps can occasionally be affected at the same time without turning a large town into one constant light show. Flickering can also be switched off completely. Gradual Light Failures: Optionally allows more lights to fail after the power grid shuts down. You can choose whether the amount set under Lights Remaining is reached after 365, 180, or 90 in-game days. Set it to Off to keep the number of lights unchanged. Lights Remaining: Sets how much city lighting will always remain despite the gradual failures. The preset value is 25%. It can never leave more lights working than the value chosen under Active Lights. Which lights stay dark at a lower percentage is not rerolled every time you load the game. The selection stays the same in your save and is shared by every player in multiplayer. Existing Saves & Multiplayer The mod can be added to existing saves and servers. The save or server simply needs to be restarted normally after adding it. If you enable gradual light failures for the first time in an older world, they only start counting from that moment. The age of the world and the original day of the power outage are never counted retroactively, so an older server will not suddenly lose most of its lighting. If you switch gradual light failures off later, the lighting temporarily returns to the value chosen under Active Lights. Switch them back on and they continue from where they stopped. On multiplayer servers, these settings are shared by every player. FAQ Q: Is a failed light permanently broken? A: No. It has simply failed for Ambient City Lights and otherwise returns to normal base-game behavior. Regular grid power, a generator, or a battery can still power it if that fixture supports them. Q: Can I repair failed lights? A: The mod does not add a separate repair system. Since the fixture itself is not destroyed, no special repair is needed. Q: What happens during sleep or fast-forward? A: Flickering and gradual light failures follow in-game time. Sleeping and fast-forwarding move them ahead as well. Any flicker that would have happened during that time is simply skipped instead of being replayed afterward. Compatibility Note Ambient City Lights changes the light that supported outdoor fixtures cast into their surroundings. The lamp sprite itself can still appear dark or switched off after the power grid fails. Flickering also changes only the surrounding light, not the visible fixture. Feel free to leave feedback in the comments. Workshop ID: 3778621107 Mod ID: AmbientCityLights

description: Play real pool in Project Zomboid. Every pool table in the world becomes a fully playable billiards minigame: put a Pool Cue in your hands, right-click a table, and a physics-driven game of 8-ball opens in a top-down 2D window. Play solo, against an AI opponent, or head-to-head with another survivor in multiplayer. ⭐ If this mod made your Project Zomboid gameplay easier, don't forget to rate it and add it to your favorites! This helps the mod reach more players! ⭐ Not a decoration and not a timed action with a progress bar - an actual pool simulation with cue control, aiming guides, spin-free realistic ball physics, fouls and a full ruleset. Two rulesets 8-Ball - the classic game, by the book. Break from behind the head string, open table until the first legal pot, solids and stripes, fouls, ball in hand, and winning (or losing) on the black. Play it 1v1, or in teams with up to 8 people. Most Balls - a fast, casual free-for-all. No groups and no 8-ball penalty: every ball you pocket is a point, and whoever has scored most when the table is cleared wins. Three ways to play Solo Practice - free table, no rules, no turns. Just pot balls and relax. Vs AI - a computer opponent that aims with the ghost-ball method, checks both halves of every shot for blockers, and plays safeties when nothing is on. Easy, Normal and Hard. Multiplayer - a real match against up to seven other survivors at the same table. Up to 8 players, teams, and spectators Open a lobby, invite people, and hit Start - the game counts who actually turned up and sizes the match to fit. In 8-Ball, extra players join as teams (odd seats against even), so a group of four can play doubles. Only the host needs a cue. The table is set up with it and everyone passes it around, exactly as they would in a real bar, so your friends can join empty-handed. Anyone else can right-click the table and choose Watch Pool Game to spectate: no cue needed, no seat taken. Perfect for a bar night on a roleplay server. Leaderboards Finished matches are recorded. See who rules one specific table, compare it against the server-wide ranking, or track your own career record in singleplayer - games, wins, win rate, pot rate and fouls. None of it touches your save file, so the mod stays safe to remove at any time. Built for multiplayer The server is the authority and the physics are deterministic. Only the shot vector travels over the network - every client replays the identical simulation and lands on the identical result, so everyone watches the exact same shot. No position streaming, no rubber-banding, a couple of dozen bytes per shot. You can also watch whoever is shooting line their shot up in real time, so the table is never just sitting still while you wait. Toggleable in Options - Mods. Learn to play New to pool? There is a built-in How to Play guide right in the game window covering aiming, power control, fouls, ball in hand and both rulesets. No need to alt-tab. Sound Custom-made audio for the cue strike, ball-on-ball contact, cushion hits and balls dropping into pockets. Project Zomboid has no billiard sounds of its own, so these were made for the mod. They play through the UI channel, so a game of pool will never attract zombies. Rewards Boredom ticks down in real time while you play. Finishing a match also eases Unhappiness and Stress, at the cost of a little Fatigue. The payout scales with how long you actually played and how many shots you took, so the window is not a one-click mood reset. Requirements A Pool Cue (Base.Poolcue) in your primary or secondary hand to play. Spectating needs nothing at all. Balls and chalk are assumed to live with the table. Works on any vanilla pool table - they are common in bars and pool halls. Compatibility Safe to add mid-save. Adds no items, no recipes, and modifies no vanilla files. Safe to remove mid-save. The mod stores nothing at all in your save file - no ModData, no world objects, no global state. Remove it and the tables simply go back to being ordinary furniture. Singleplayer, co-op and dedicated servers. Should not conflict with anything: it adds one context menu entry and one UI window. Languages Fully translated - interface, messages and the complete in-game guide - into every language Project Zomboid supports: English, Portugues (PT and BR), Espanol, Francais, Deutsch, Italiano, Nederlands, Polski, Russian, Ukrainian, Turkce, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Japanese and Korean. Community Suggestions, bug reports or just a chat - there is a Discord button right in the game menu, or join at https://discord.gg/XJMKptpphq Controls Move the mouse to aim - the cue follows your cursor. Click and drag away from the cue ball to pull back, release to shoot. The farther you pull, the harder the shot. Mouse wheel or the [ and ] keys for fine aim. Right-click to cancel a shot you have started. Found a bug or have a suggestion? Leave a comment - I read them all. By: Portal Viciados Workshop ID: 3778877053 Mod ID: UsablePoolTables

description: Write down what you know. When you die, your next character reads it back. Craft a journal, transcribe your progress into it, and stash it somewhere safe. Your next character reads it and gets that progress back - once, exactly, and never more than you actually had. How to use it Bind a journal. All three recipes are known from character creation, under the Skill Journal crafting category. Transcribe into it. Right-click and take Transcribe into journal. Your character sits down and writes. Do it again any time to bring the journal up to date. Die. Stash it first, or fetch it back off your corpse. Read it. Your next character right-clicks, takes Read journal, and the progress comes back. Three journals Which one you carry decides what it can hold. Skill Notebook - the skill half. XP and levels, the skill books you read (finished or not) and their reading bonus, and the tapes that teach. Skill Notepad - the recipe half. Magazines, photo schematics, seed packets. Much quicker to fill. Skill Journal - both, bound from one of each, and it keeps whatever is already written in them. The Journal is the one you hand down. It survives being read and stays with your successor, where the other two are used up. It comes out looking like whatever book you bound it from, and it keeps the penlight you built it with, so it's the only one you can write or read in the dark - about a thousand in-game minutes on a charge, then the light dies mid-sentence and it's an ordinary book until you put a battery in. It takes as long as it should Writing and reading are both priced in pages, at the same speed your game reads a book - so a server that has already tuned reading speed gets journals to match for free. A whole skill is 220 pages and a passive one 550, on a steep curve: level 5 is about 19 pages, level 10 the full 220. Books, magazines, schematics, seed packets and tapes cost what they cost to read or watch. You can stop. Walk away mid-sentence and the journal remembers the page, then charges you only for what's left. Updating is cheap. Transcribing again bills only what you've learned since. Reading is billed the same way, but only for what you'd actually gain, and nothing is granted until the last page - so a part read can't be farmed. Every vanilla skill book runs 220 to 380 pages, so a well read character can owe more time for their books than for every skill they have. Eight sandbox options weight all of it from 1 to 1000 percent if that's too steep. No XP duping The part other journal mods get wrong, so I'll be specific. Totals, not gains. Reading grants the difference between what's written and what you have, so a second journal grants nothing. They can't be stacked into free levels. Reading bonuses can't get stuck on. A book's bonus only comes back for tiers you haven't outgrown. One you're already past would run for ever, and that's where "I suddenly had max XP" comes from. Tapes can't be farmed twice. The XP comes back and the tape is marked watched in the same moment. Nothing to gain, nothing to lose. A journal with nothing left to give you says so, and isn't destroyed. A half written journal can't be read at all - it doesn't describe anybody yet. And no journal ever spawns in the world. Whose journal is it In singleplayer the lock is your character's name, so a successor with the same name reads it as though the character never died. In multiplayer it's the character name and your account. Nobody loots your corpse and absorbs your skills, and re-crafting can't launder a journal into someone else's hands. It's all worked out on the server, so a client can't fake it. Somebody in the comments pointed out that this makes your next character wear a dead one's name, so the name half is now a sandbox option. Turn Lock a journal to one name off and your account alone owns the journal: your successor inherits it whatever they're called, and everyone else is still locked out exactly as before. In singleplayer there's no account to fall back on, so off there means any character in that save can read any journal in it. Other mods Books, tapes and recipes from other mods are sorted by what they actually grant rather than by a hardcoded list, so a modded tape, book or skill that teaches is picked up on its own - I don't need to know your mod exists. No vanilla file is replaced and no vanilla behaviour patched. Options A journal carries two things, and each has its own switch at the top of the list: Restore skill XP and Restore what was read. Both start on. Turn the XP one off and a successor inherits the books, recipes and tapes but earns their own levels; turn the other off and they get the XP and nothing else. A journal that gives less back costs less to write and less to read. Twenty-two sandbox options in all, under Skill Journal, read live so a change lands on the very next transcribe or read: the time costs and a weight per kind of knowledge, how much skill XP comes back, which kinds of progress return at all, whether a journal can be rewritten, who it's locked to, and whether each one survives being read. Safe to add mid-save - the recipes are known the moment it loads, with no new character and no relog. Safe to remove, but read your journal first, since any you're carrying go with the mod. Singleplayer, hosted multiplayer and dedicated server. Needs Build 42.20 or newer, on the server as well as the client. Workshop ID: 3779162647 Mod ID: LGSkillJournal

description: Mod Folders Too many mods? Stop scrolling through hundreds of entries and organize your mod list into folders. Mod Folders adds a lightweight folder management system directly to the Project Zomboid mod selection screen. Create your own categories, collapse large groups, reorder them by dragging, batch-enable or disable a folder, and move multiple selected mods at once. Example folders: Weapon Mods Map Mods UI Mods Vehicle Mods Translation Mods Frequently Used Mods Test Mods Core Features Create up to 99 folders and freely customize their names. Folders are displayed above uncategorized mods. Click the + button on a mod to place it into a folder. Mods already inside a folder also show a - button for quickly returning them to the uncategorized list. Expand or collapse individual folders at any time. Use the global expand/collapse button to open or close all folders at once. Drag a folder by its drag handle to freely change folder order. Folder order, names, expanded state, and mod assignments are saved locally. Folder Controls Drag Handle — Hold the drag area and move the mouse up or down to reorder the folder. ✓ / × — Enable or disable every installed mod inside that folder. A confirmation window is shown before the batch action is applied. T — Rename the folder. Trash — Delete the folder. Mods inside it are released back to the uncategorized list. Hover over folder action buttons to see a short description of what each button does. Multi-Select & Batch Move You can select multiple mods first, then move all of them into the same folder with a single + operation. Ctrl + Click — Add or remove individual mods from the current selection. Ctrl selection can include mods from different folders and uncategorized mods at the same time. Shift + Click — Select every mod between the current anchor mod and the clicked mod. Shift range selection only works when both mods are inside the same folder, or when both mods are uncategorized. Batch Move — After selecting multiple mods, click the + button on any selected mod, choose a folder, and all selected mods will be moved there together. Selected mods are highlighted with a yellow selection frame for easier visibility. Global Controls Folder Icon — Create a new folder. Three Vertical / Horizontal Lines — Expand all folders or collapse all folders with one click. Configuration Sharing Your folder configuration is stored locally in: C:/Users/<YourUsername>/Zomboid/Lua/ModFolders.cfg To share your folder layout with another player: Exit the game first. Send your ModFolders.cfg file to the other player. The other player places it in their own Zomboid/Lua/ folder and replaces the existing file. If the other player does not have some of your mods installed, those missing mods are simply ignored. Shared mods will still be placed into their configured folders, and extra mods that are not listed in the configuration remain uncategorized. Compatibility Compatibility support is included for: Mod Load Order Sorter [B42] Mod Manager Mod Tag Mod Manager Reforged Notes Folders are used to organize how mods are displayed in the mod list. Putting a mod into a folder does not automatically enable or disable it. Mods are only batch-enabled or batch-disabled when you explicitly use the folder ✓ / × action. This mod does not modify saves or game content. It can be safely enabled or disabled without affecting existing saves. Bug Reports If you encounter an unexpected error, please try to reproduce it with as few unrelated mods enabled as possible, then send the relevant console.txt / error information together with your active mod list. description: Don't forget to like it, if you enjoy! Switching from Accessory Skill Bonuses Lootbound is a separate successor to Accessory Skill Bonuses, not a direct update. The two mods are marked as incompatible and cannot be active together. Disable Accessory Skill Bonuses before enabling Lootbound for your save. Existing saves are supported, but bonuses previously assigned by Accessory Skill Bonuses are not transferred. After enabling Lootbound, eligible equipment will be processed using Lootbound's new item families, skill pools, and sandbox rules. Previously annotated accessories may therefore receive different results. Back up your save before switching. A new save is not required, although starting fresh provides the cleanest and most consistent equipment progression. Updates / Fixes 8/9/2026: v1.0.2 - Added the new Bonus Quality sandbox setting. Choose from Very Low, Low, Default, High, or Very High to control how frequently stronger bonuses appear without changing the overall number of bonus items. Default preserves the existing balance. Current saves automatically remain on Default, and previously processed equipment keeps its original bonus permanently. 8/7/2026: v1.0.1 - Removed the [No XP Bonus] label from regular items for cleaner inventory names. No-bonus results are still stored permanently and cannot reroll. Every Piece of Gear Can Shape Your Build Lootbound: RPG Equipment Bonuses is the ambitious RPG successor to Accessory Skill Bonuses. It expands the idea from accessories into a complete equipment-driven progression system for Project Zomboid. Clothing, armor, bags, jewelry, underwear, watches, belts, conventional melee weapons, and firearms can become permanent finds with themed XP bonuses. The result is a world where checking one more wardrobe, corpse, locker, or weapon rack can genuinely change the build you are creating. Build a Survivor Through Their Equipment Every supported item family has a deliberate skill pool. Technical gear can favor crafting and maintenance. Field clothing can support survival skills. Bags can reward physical or practical development. A conventional weapon supports its own weapon skill, while firearms favor Aiming or Reloading. Jewelry and underwear are the wild cards: their bonuses can reach across the complete skill list, creating unusual combinations and giving collectors a reason to inspect even the smallest finds. Permanent, Individual Loot Each eligible item is processed from its own unique game identity. Its result is stored permanently and does not change when it is dropped, transferred, equipped again, placed in a container, or carried across a server restart. Most equipment remains ordinary. Useful bonuses are uncommon, stronger results are rare, and exceptional pieces can become the center of an entire loadout. Features More than 1,700 explicitly selected vanilla equipment definitions Wearable clothing, armor, accessories, bags, underwear, and conventional weapons Themed skill pools based on equipment family and weapon type Permanent deterministic bonuses unique to each individual item Matching equipped bonuses stack additively Weapons provide their bonus only while held Works with ordinary XP, skill books, television, VHS, and trait-modified XP Colored item annotations show bonus strength at a glance Total equipped bonuses appear directly in the Skills panel with tooltips Inventory, worn-item, opened-container, and loot-generation scanning Single-player and multiplayer support English interface text with no forced replacement of vanilla translations Explosives, traps, throwables, bare hands, and ambiguous improvised objects are intentionally excluded. Your World, Your Rules Lootbound includes five Bonus Frequency presets. The default setting keeps bonuses small and rare, while higher settings make equipment progression increasingly noticeable. Additional sandbox controls let you: Include or exclude conventional weapons Include or exclude protective equipment Allow or remove the rare +10% item tier Enable or disable a nearly impossible mythical discovery Changing these options affects newly processed items. Equipment already discovered keeps its permanent result. A Secret Worth Searching For There are rumors about an extraordinary piece hidden among the world's belly-button jewelry. Most survivors will never see it. The stubborn, the lucky, and the truly obsessed may want to keep looking. Adding Lootbound to a Game For a new game, subscribe, restart Project Zomboid if it is running, enable Lootbound: RPG Equipment Bonuses in the Mods menu, and make sure it is enabled for the new save. description: A sink you install in a house should be plumbed into that house, the same as the sink that came with it. In vanilla it can't be. The moment you place a sink, bath, shower, toilet or washing machine, the game marks it as connected to nothing, and the only thing you're allowed to attach is a rain collector on the floor above. Do I need this if I already have LG Extended Plumbing? Only if you fit your own fixtures before the water shuts off. That mod is about rain barrels feeding a whole building. This one is about putting a fixture back on the town supply while there still is one. Two different problems, and they stack. How to use it Right-click the fixture and take Plumb ... to main, with a pipe wrench. It sits under the existing Plumb option rather than replacing it. From then on the fixture is one of the building's own, as far as the game is concerned. Not "behaves like one": unlimited water, reading Water: Unlimited, the same as any sink the house came with shuts off on the same day the rest of town does keeps the same 20 litres standing in its pipes afterwards, and drains them the same way can still be given a rain collector later, like any other fixture I set one flag and stop. None of it is reimplemented or run on a timer. Where it works Indoors, in a building that came with the map - which includes any original building you've renovated, since it keeps its room data. Not in a structure you raised in an open field, because there are no pipes under a field. Rain collector plumbing still works there exactly as it does now. Some buildings never had a supply whatever the calendar says. The orphanage is the well known one, and derelict buildings are the same, so a fixture you connect in one of those is dry for the same reason its own sinks are. That's the map's decision, not mine. You can only do this while the town water is still on. Once it shuts off there is nothing at the far end of the pipe, so the option goes away. That is the normal end of it, not a fault: an empty pipe is all a fixture connected then would ever have. If you start a world a month or more after the apocalypse the water can already be off on day one, and you'll never see the option at all. It covers every fixture the game itself treats as plumbed - kitchen and bathroom sinks, baths, showers, toilets, washing machines and combo washer/dryers. Modded fixtures are picked up on their own if they're flagged the same way. Other mods It overrides nothing. It adds one option and one action under their own names and leaves the vanilla plumbing code alone, so a mod built on top of vanilla plumbing won't collide with it - rain collector mods included. LG Extended Plumbing - they stack. A fixture you connect here draws on the mains until the town runs dry, then falls back to the building's shared barrels like any other fixture. No sandbox options and nothing to configure. Safe to add mid-save, since it does nothing to a fixture until you connect one, and safe to remove, because a connected fixture is left in a state vanilla produces on its own. Singleplayer, hosted multiplayer and dedicated server. Needs Build 42.20 or newer, on the server as well as the client. Workshop ID: 3779251515 Mod ID: LGMainsWater

description: Vanilla only plumbs a sink to a barrel in the 3x3 right above it. Barrel on the roof, sink downstairs, no option, however full it is. So: plumb a barrel in with a wrench and it feeds every fixture in the building. Twelve 400 litre barrels on the roof read as 4800 litres at the kitchen tap. I built it for a server I run with friends, so it gets tested hardest on a dedicated server. How to plumb a barrel in Right-click the barrel and pick Plumb into house supply. You need a pipe wrench, and it takes a moment, the same as plumbing a sink. Nothing happens until you do it, so a barrel you put down for its own sake stays yours. The option shows up on a building's roof, against its outside wall, or standing inside it. Then two rules decide what it reaches: Down is free. A barrel feeds every floor below it, basement included. On the roof, that's the whole house. A generator pushes it up. Power the barrel's own square and it feeds its floor and above as well. That's the only way a barrel in the yard reaches anything. Generator only, mains doesn't count. No roof to stand it on? Build a floor over the room, go up, and put the barrel on that. What else you get Barrels add up and drain together, so none sits brimming while another runs dry. They all keep catching rain. Hold back as reserve saves a barrel for last, once the others are empty. Disconnect from house supply takes one back out - no tool for that, and it keeps its water. Whiskey on tap. Dirty asked for this in the comments, so: right-click a fixture, pick Plumbed liquid, and run whiskey, beer, wine, milk or juice to it instead. A barrel belongs to what's in it, so the bar sink and the kitchen tap can't touch each other's supply. A mix is a drink of its own. Bleach in a barrel, topped up by the rain, is a barrel of Bleach + Water - and the tap pours it in the same proportion your barrels are in. Hover Plumbed liquid and it lists the litres of each. Water dispensers fill up instead. Plumb an office cooler in the other way round and the barrels keep it topped up, with clean water even where they're tainted. Pick it up to undo it. Clean and tainted are one supply, because a plumbed fixture cleans the water as it pours. Want them apart anyway? Set the clean barrels as reserve. Mapped basements, bunkers and roofs all work, and so does a base you built yourself or a room you added on to a house. Two things I can't do. A basement you dug has no room record, and the game won't plumb below ground without one. And wall showers, the deluxe bath, dishwashers and chemical toilets aren't water fixtures in vanilla at all, so nothing can plumb them. Other mods I don't replace any vanilla function or rewrite any action, so most mods never notice this one is there. If a mod still plumbs its barrel the vanilla way, from overhead, it works with this - the worst you should see is a duplicate right-click option. Mods that add barrels or tanks work for the same reason: I ask the game whether a thing holds fluid, so there's no list to be on and I don't need to know your mod exists. What fights it is a mod that plumbs fixtures itself, because that's the same question answered twice. Useful Barrels - compatible. Its barrels join like any other, as whatever is in them, so a fuel barrel never turns up at the kitchen tap. PlumbingFixed - compatible from v2.2.3. DuongC patched their mod to stand down and use this one's supply instead of pooling its own 3x3, so nothing is counted twice. Update it first, and thanks to them. Immersive Water Shutoff - compatible. Its author tested the pair and confirmed it. Mains water mods - different job, no conflict. A building on the mains uses that until it runs dry, then the barrels take over. LG Extended Electricity - a barrel is either the water supply's or a generator's, never both, and the two mods agree which. Water Pipes - not compatible on the same fixture. It sets the same flag this is built on. Give each fixture to one system or the other. Pipe mods that only add containers are fine. Options Sandbox, under Extended Plumbing: an off switch, how far a fixture looks when it isn't in a real building, which containers get filled instead of feeding, a fix for washing machines on servers, and a log that says why each fixture did or didn't connect. Safe to add mid-save. Any barrel already feeding a plumbed sink is connected up for you on the first load, so nothing that worked stops. Singleplayer, hosted multiplayer and dedicated server. Taking it off again: switch it off in the sandbox options first. To feed a tap from across a building I park a hidden water store on the square above it, and that store is a real object in your save. Delete the mod while one is standing and your game is left holding something it cannot make sense of - the tap still thinks it has a barrel overhead, so it runs dry and stays dry. Turning Extended plumbing off is how you tell me to pack up. Do it in this order and it comes away clean: switch Extended plumbing off in the sandbox options walk your base so every part of it loads, and give it a moment - I take the hidden stores out as I reach them then remove the mod Switching it off is not destructive on its own: turn it back on and your plumbing comes straight back, so it is safe to use just to see what the mod is doing. If you have already removed it and your sinks are dry, put the mod back, switch it off in the sandbox options, walk the base, and then remove it. Needs Build 42.20 or newer, on the server as well as the client. Workshop ID: 3779561845 Mod ID: LGExtendedPlumbing

Turn the tile range up and the neighbours get your electricity before your own upstairs does. So this makes a generator power the whole building it reaches. Every floor, the roof, the basement, from a generator standing anywhere its range touches the place. How to wire a building up Plug the generator in, switch it off, then right-click it and take Wire up the building. No tools. Turning it off first is the habit the base game already teaches - you stop a generator before you change what it's connected to. Unwire the building puts it back, and vanilla's own Disconnect generator undoes the lot. Out of the box a generator does nothing until you wire it up, so nothing lights up or starts costing fuel behind your back. A sandbox option wires them up the moment they're plugged in. What you get Everything comes on. Lights, fridges, freezers, stoves, microwaves, TVs, radios, washers, dryers, chargers, fuel pumps, the food spoilage clock. There's no coverage list to keep, so modded appliances work without me knowing they exist. Power isn't water. A generator on the ground floor lights the attic, one on the roof lights the cellar. The fuel adds up. Everything it powers is charged at the game's own rates, so lighting a warehouse costs what a warehouse should. The generator's panel shows where it's going, and nothing is charged twice. Two generators split the load evenly, so two tanks last twice as long instead of emptying twice as fast for the same light. If one runs dry the others pick up its share. A bit of the yard as well, so a porch light or an outdoor freezer works. You set how far in sandbox. Power stops at the building it's wired to, with that bit of yard around it. It can't run down the street. The breaker Dragon Slayer Ornstein asked in the comments for generators you could overload, and they were right. Put too much on one and its breaker flips, taking every generator on the same buildings with it. Every generator is rated on its own, off how well built it is: ValuTech 5400 W, Old 5625 W, Lectromax 6750 W, Premium Technologies 8100 W. A modded one is rated the same way, from its durability. A light is 20 W, a TV 300, a fridge 800, a stove 900, a fridge-freezer 1300, and the generator burns 200 just idling. A stacked washer/dryer is 9000 W for each half of it, which will take a breaker down on its own. Getting it back isn't meant to be a fight. While the breaker is out those generators behave exactly as base game, so walk round, start them all, then take Reset the breaker on whichever one you're standing next to. That's what makes a second generator a real answer instead of a second fuel bill. Fuel lines A generator runs on ten litres. A rain barrel holds four hundred, and vanilla already lets you pour a petrol can into one - it just can't get it back out again. This adds that last hop. There are two ways to feed one, and they stack. A barrel standing next to it. Roll a drum up to the machine and take Connect to generator with a pipe wrench. Any of the eight squares around it, or its own. No pump, no height rule, nothing to power - they're touching. Station pumps connect the same way, so a generator parked at a filling station runs off the tanks underneath it. The whole base, if you also run LG Extended Plumbing. Plug the generator in and take Plumb generator - indoors, on the roof, or against an outside wall - and it refuels out of any barrel plumbed into that building and holding petrol, under that mod's own rules: a barrel above it feeds by gravity, one on its level or below needs its own square powered. The drum beside it is always drained first, and the building is the reserve behind it, so the base's shared petrol stays the base's until the local drum runs out. Other mods Mods that add appliances or generator types are fine, because the test is the game's own and not a list of sprites. What fights it is a mod that rewrites which squares a generator powers - that's the same question answered twice. Generator Powered Buildings is the same idea as this one, so pick one or the other. Solar Revolution - not compatible yet, and that one's mine to fix. Its power banks are generators as far as the game is concerned, so this mod bills one for the building and the breaker trips it off - which Solar Revolution undoes on its next tick, so you get flicker rather than a clean failure. Plumb a fuel barrel near one and it'll pour petrol in for nothing as well. Until the patch is out, right-click each bank and take Unwire the building, and keep fuel barrels away from banks. Modded barrels and tanks work as fuel vessels on their own, for the same reason. There's a quick test: if you can pour a petrol can into it by hand, the fuel line can use it too. Empty it first, since petrol won't mix with water. LG Extended Plumbing - better together, and the two agree about barrels. Install it and a generator can be plumbed into a building the way a sink is, drawing on the whole base's petrol. A barrel only ever does one job - the water supply's or a generator's - and one already plumbed into the water isn't offered a generator connection. Neither mod needs the other. Options Sandbox, under Extended Electricity: an off switch, whether generators wire up as soon as they're plugged in, whether the extra rooms cost fuel, load sharing, the breaker and its rating, fuel lines, whether station pumps count, how far power reaches outside the walls, and a log. Safe to add mid-save, safe to remove mid-save. Only the generator remembers anything - nothing is written to a building, a room or an appliance. Singleplayer, hosted multiplayer and dedicated server. Needs Build 42.20 or newer, on the server as well as the client. Workshop ID: 3779562002 Mod ID: LGExtendedElectricity

description: Purpose-built rain collectors should not collect rain slower than a bucket. In vanilla B42, purpose-built rain collectors gather water far slower than ordinary buckets (~2.5x slower), which makes no sense to me. This mod adjusts the four vanilla rain collectors so they collect rain at the same rate as a bucket. Capacity is unchanged. So far as I'm aware, no other mod fixes this issue. Help Others Find This Mod: Click "Like" If you'd like to help others find the mod, click like. If you favourite it, please like it too. Steam's "Most Popular" rankings have a big impact on mod visibility. For several days now the mod has averaged around 70% of visitors subscribing. However, the mod has had very limited visibility since release, I don't think I would have found it myself yet, if I didn't create it. Broad Compatibility The mod has a very small footprint and only changes the rain-collection rate of the four vanilla purpose-built collectors. It's very unlikely to cause issues with any mod that doesn't change the same values, and I've not seen any other mod that changes them. Specifically confirmed working with other popular or companion mods: • PlumbingFixed • LG Extended Plumbing with thanks to Ocean Of Notions (see comments) • Common Sense • Rain Cleans Blood • My modestly large list of other installed mods Designed for B42.19 and B42.20. Safe to Add or Remove from an Existing Save Existing vanilla rain collectors are corrected as their squares load, so there is no need to start a new game or rebuild existing collectors. I tested installing and removing it mid-save on my long-standing B42.19 game with no issues. Ocean Of Notions tested and confirmed the same on B42.20, with thanks (see comments). Multiplayer Compatibility Designed for multiplayer compatibility. The mod runs server-side and synchronises the changed rain-collector values.
