description: [ML] All 29 languages the game ships with. This is The Zims - Menu Style itself. Right-click the world and the options fan out around your survivor's head, the way a certain life simulator did it. This is a DLC and needs The Zims Subscribe to The Zims How it works Rounded buttons around the head - each option is a button with its icon in the orb on the inner end, exactly where you expect it. An option without an icon just gets a clean button with the text centred. The button in focus shows its full name - the others are shortened, so a long name never breaks the wheel. Submenus swap in place - open one and the wheel becomes that submenu. What you clicked sits in the middle - its own picture when it has one, its name when it does not - so a glance tells you where you are. Click the middle to go back a level. It never piles up on itself - up to seven options curve around the head in an arc; a full page of eight lays them out in two even columns. Both come from a table, not from a formula, so options can never land on top of each other no matter how long their names are. Long menus page - past eight options, Back appears above the wheel and More... below it. Those two slots are navigation only, never an action, so you never misclick one for the other. The mouse wheel pages too. Click away to cancel - and the same right-click opens the menu on the next object, with no extra step. Plays on a controller compatibility Every DLC in this family is built to work for controller players. Left stick, or the d-pad - move the highlight. Something is highlighted from the moment the wheel opens, so the confirm button always has a target. A / Cross - confirm. B / Circle - back one level, or close the wheel. LB and RB / L1 and R1 - previous and next page. Your survivor stands still while the wheel is open. The left stick would otherwise aim and walk at the same time, and choosing an option turned into a stroll away from the very thing you were trying to use. There is a setting to turn that off. A direction only ever moves the highlight - it never confirms and never opens a submenu. One gesture, one meaning, so nothing fires that you did not ask for. DLC Settings Press K in game and pick The Zims - Menu Style DLC in the window. The key can be changed under Options > Key Bindings > [The Zims]. Colours - pick the background and the text with a colour picker, and a third button puts both back to default without touching anything else. Border, highlight, orbs and the darker submenu button are all derived from your background colour, so one change recolours the whole wheel and it still looks designed. Volume - a slider for the mod's own sounds: the soft click as the highlight moves between options, the one when you choose, and the one when the menu turns a page. It is a volume of its own, not a shortcut to the game's - turning it down does not touch anything else you hear. Size - compact, normal or large. The head - show it or hide it, and turn the follow-the-mouse motion on or off. Opening animation, and an optional marker on the active direction. Hold still on a controller - on by default, and switchable here. It is a client-side UI mod. It changes nothing about game state, so a player without it is not out of sync with one who has it - they just get the old vertical menu. Listing it is what makes Steam push it to everyone; it is not a correctness requirement. Support These mods are free and always will be. If they made your game better and you want to buy me a coffee, the door is here - but the mod never asks twice. Built for Build 42. Workshop ID: 3779890822 Mod ID: ZimPie

description: [B42] Machinery Powered workstations, replaceable parts, custom interfaces - and the foundation for much more. Machinery adds three table saws, a Standing Drill Press, Bench Grinder Station, Metalwork Lathe, Hydraulic Press, Metal Bandsaw, and bulk propane storage. Each is a functional workstation with power, serviceable parts, recipes, sounds, and a custom interface. How to obtain the machines Machines do not spawn naturally yet. Construct them through either: PZ's vanilla Building Menu The enhanced catalogue provided by Knox Buildworks Knox Buildworks is fully supported but optional. New: five powered metalworking stations Standing Drill Press - all eight dormant vanilla drilling conversions for iron and steel stock Bench Grinder Station - restores the selected axe, wood axe, machete, or hunting knife without replacing it Metalwork Lathe - turns steel bar stock into round rods and precision slugs Hydraulic Press - compacts scrap and metal stock and reforms circular sawblade blanks Metal Bandsaw - cuts tires, sawblades, iron stock, bars, bands, and sheets with the base-game bandsaw workflow All five reuse base-game art, sounds, electricity, and player animations. Their resizable UIs provide live machine displays, clear requirements, and action progress. The Lathe and Hydraulic Press include green and blue variants. Jobs award server-authoritative Metalworking XP with the normal XP halo. Service parts and machine oil The new stations need Machine Oil and their own fitted consumable: Drill Press - Machine Drill Bit Set Bench Grinder - Grinding Wheel Metalwork Lathe - Lathe Tool Set Hydraulic Press - Hydraulic Service Kit Metal Bandsaw - Metal Bandsaw Blade Parts wear through use and show their exact condition in the service panel. Replacements can be found in industrial loot or crafted through the Repair recipes. Installed parts and their remaining life stay with a machine when it is moved. Three functional table saws Industrial Table Saw - powered by grid or generator electricity Contractor Table Saw - powered by grid or generator electricity Cabinet Table Saw - gasoline-powered, with a native 8 L fluid tank Each model rotates in all four directions and tracks its power, fuel, installed blade, blade condition, materials, and operating state. A proper machine interface Live preview of the placed machine Readable recipe cards and drag-and-drop material or service-part slots Controller-friendly service and machine controls Selectable batch quantities, direct entry, and MAX Automatic materials from inventory, bags, nearby containers, and the ground Choose results from an organized menu: inventory, floor, carried bags, or nearby containers Output, XP, time, accident-risk, part-life, electricity, and fuel previews Custom cutting and servicing sounds with timed animations Skill matters Carpentry affects yield, speed, XP, and safety. At Carpentry 6, a log job has only 1% accident risk; most accidents are scratches and cuts are much rarer. At Carpentry 10, an expert can produce up to five planks per log with no accident risk. Large branches can also become planks, with the expected result shown before starting. Power, fuel, and serviceable blades Industrial and Contractor saws need an active electrical supply. The Cabinet saw trades electricity for gasoline and consumes fuel per job through B42's fluid system. The Cabinet model also produces dangerous exhaust indoors. Repeated enclosed operation can become fatal; the panel warns you, and sandbox settings can disable or scale the danger. Every saw needs a circular blade fitted with a wrench. Recipes show the required skills, tools, and materials before construction. Table saws require Metalworking 4 and Electrical 3; service parts are installed separately afterward. description: Reading Reworked Reading Reworked is a quality-of-life mod that makes reading faster and less tedious while allowing you to keep moving through the world. The goal is simple: reading should remain useful and meaningful without bringing your gameplay to a complete halt, especially in multiplayer. Be sure to rate the mod if you enjoy it. It greatly helps with visibility and exposure to the community. Features Reworked Reading Times Reading times are adjusted around a 220-page Level 1 Skill Book. Normal Reader: ~2 minutes 30 seconds Fast Reader: ~1 minute 40 seconds Slow Reader: ~3 minutes 20 seconds Reading times scale with the number of pages in the book. The Fast Reader and Slow Reader traits continue to have a meaningful effect on reading speed. Reading While Walking You can continue reading while walking. This allows you to stay productive while moving between locations instead of having to stop and stand still whenever you want to read. Running will still interrupt reading. Your reading progress is preserved when switching between standing still and walking. Aiming While Reading You can aim while reading and moving. This allows you to keep your weapon ready while reading, giving you a better way to stay aware of your surroundings without completely stopping what you're doing. Whether aiming interrupts reading can be configured through the Sandbox Options. Reading Bonuses Reading glasses provide a 10% reading speed bonus by default. Sitting provides a 10% reading speed bonus by default. Both bonuses can be customized through the Sandbox Options. Multiplayer Reading Reworked is designed with multiplayer in mind. The reading system, walking functionality, aiming behavior, reading progress, and skill-book behavior are designed to work properly in multiplayer. Sandbox Options Reading Reworked includes its own Sandbox Options page, allowing players and server owners to customize the reading experience. You can adjust: Normal reading time Fast Reader reading time Slow Reader reading time Allow reading while walking Whether aiming interrupts reading Reading glasses reading-speed bonus Sitting reading-speed bonus Debug output The default settings provide the intended Reading Reworked experience, while the Sandbox Options allow you to tailor the mod to your preferred playstyle or server. Development Reading Reworked is actively being developed and refined. The focus is on keeping the mod simple, reliable, and convenient rather than adding unnecessary penalties or mechanics. Feedback If you encounter bugs, unexpected behavior, multiplayer issues, or have suggestions for improving the mod, please leave a comment. Feedback and testing are especially helpful as the mod continues to develop. Thanks for checking out Reading Reworked! Workshop ID: 3780124271 Mod ID: ReadingReworked

description: Modern Firearms System — B42.20 Community Fix Patch - 08/21/2026 An unofficial bug-fix/enhancement patch for Modern Firearms System on Project Zomboid Build 42.20. NOT a standalone mod — it requires the original Modern Firearms System and must load after it. This patch now also include some fix/improvement for BackpackSystemB42 and BladesmithSystemB42 which comes with the original MFS mod steam package. Please enable those two and place this patch after those. Credits FIRST AND FOREMOST — 布偶旧猫, creator of Modern Firearms System. Every firearm, model, texture, sound and animation is their work. This patch only repairs and extends what they built. Without their mod there is nothing here. Please support the original. SECOND — owo, author of the Modern Firearms System Multiplayer Fix for 42.19. This patch already carries a substantial amount of their work — the multiplayer magazine synchronisation, server-side validation, client state confirmation, action guards and performance safety layers all originate from that patch and were merged in rather than reinvented. Their protocol and version strings are preserved. THIRD — ChatGPT and Claude, used for code review, diagnosis and revision, and myself for direction, testing, and the texture and mesh work. ⚠ Please read before installing If you are uncomfortable with AI-assisted modding, please do not install this patch. Wait for the original author to release their own update instead. That is a completely reasonable position and no explanation is needed. It exists because the original mod has open issues on 42.20. It is not a replacement for, or competitor to, the original author's work. What this patch fixes Flashlight on/off revive (SP fully tested, MP still require multi clients test) Rewrite the weapon light control function. Now gunlight install on the weapon can charge/discharge using vanilla battery, and the light switch on/off is default using "F". Amount of power will show up when you hit the key on top of your head. To charge the light, has battery in your inventory, and with a firearm with less than 100% battery in the weapon light, you will right click the weapon to see an option to charge/remove battery option. Interface -weapon inspect GUI Numeric weapon instantly reflected stats in the inspection window, restored attachment position editor, attachment offset value now survive both SP/MP reboot and log in The Sound value now reads the weapon's true effective sound radius instead of a fixed −40 modifier, updating immediately when a suppressor is fitted. Fully fixed weapon sound issue Fixed tooltip flicker on long compatibility lists. Now with cursor on weapon/weaponparts, press "Alt" key to show extra detail info including item ID, and allowed weapon attachment option. Fix weapon GUI part offset not aligned with hand-held model issue. Now both pistol and long-gun has correct offset display on hand and in weapon inspection GUI. Add support for individual part with their own mounts. Attachments appear and disappear immediately on install/removal, and now render on holstered handguns. Actively fixing weapon attachment render issue. Most problems (a lot of) are now fixed, new reported issue will be investigated and address. Firearm Rate of Fire (RoF) Control Finish the audit and research on Firearm auto mode RoF study. Now assigned all long guns with Calibrated RPM value in the table has minimum RPM differences between the stand and crouch. All auto pistol/SMG now use global 900 RPM in auto mode. Potentially a new RoF system is under investigated for better control. Default hotkey to toggle single/auto mode is "Backspace", configurable in keybinding page. Firearm sounds Repaired case-sensitive sound keys, adding working profiles for guns without audible firing path, completely fix weapon sound missing issue for all guns Caliber-based suppressed fallback for weapons keeping their vanilla sound; AS VAL's integrated suppressor preserved. Fixed the first suppressed pistol shot leaking the unsuppressed sound, and gunshot behaviour at different zoom levels. Models and visuals Fixed dropped weapons showing a flat 2D icon instead of a 3D model when a recoil pad, sling or ammo strap was fitted — affecting most weapons in the mod. Same for dropped magazine. Also fixed all parts world model orientation. Corrected M240, URG-S, HK416, NoveskeN4, M4A1S, M4Mk18 held-model mirrored issue. — Fixing every weapon would mean authoring a mirrored mesh for all guns, so only worked on selected 6 guns. The mirrored_gun folder includes instructions if you want to correct a specific gun yourself.) Fixed exact-case mesh/texture references for 11 weapons including 98K, M1918, M82, Minigun and Luger P08, several of which showed only an icon when dropped. Actively investigate mesh/texture issue for improvements. Crafting — new content 50 conversion recipes between vanilla and MFS attachments, both directions. 63 crafting recipes for MFS-only parts: stocks, foregrips, barrels, muzzle devices, suppressors, bipods, bayonets and empty M203/GP-25 launchers. Costs scale with family and tier. Ammunition, magazines and balance M240 now uses a dedicated 7.62×51mm 100-round belt box on .308 ammunition, replacing the mislabelled 7.62×54R drum. URG-S correctly uses 5.56mm — 30-round mag, 60-round drum. Capacities corrected: M14 7→20, FAL 7→20, USP45 drum 7→50. Repaired four magazines referencing models that do not exist, and the SG553 magazine, invisible because its model was an empty stub — new mesh and texture included. Six rifles — Kar98k, RSC, Berthier, Lebel M1886, M1 Garand, M1903 — fired three projectiles per shot, copied from a shotgun template. Every other non-shotgun fires one. Corrected, removing a large unintended damage advantage at long range. Resolved four weapons defined twice in separate files, where the copies disagreed and the winner depended on load order. Backpack/bladesystem change Add water container function to some of the backpack in BackpacksysteB42, and fix some model issue. Adjust some blade function in BladesmithsystemB42. Complete EN/CH/CN translation Known limitations — please read MULTIPLAYER IS NOT FULLY VERIFIED. Basic function are all working in MP, but some MP specific issue is still pending report and under investigation. Attachment positions apply to the weapon in your hands. Other players see default positions — the game stores attachment points on the weapon model, shared by every weapon of that type, not the individual weapon. A proper fix is planned, not done. Installation & Compatibility This mod is not compatible with most of other gun mods: Example include any mods that use Gun Fraemwork, and itself. Install the original Modern Firearms System, then this patch. Both MFS and this patch should be at the very end of your mod order. This patch does work with my other MFS-MTK-AM compatch. description: Elevators Every office block, hospital and hotel in Knox County has them. Polished steel doors, a call button worn smooth by a decade of thumbs, and a floor indicator frozen where it stopped. You have walked past a hundred of them and taken the stairs every time. The elevators work now. Press the button. Built for Build 42.20+. Works in new games and existing saves. How it works Right-click an elevator door or its call button, pick a floor, wait for the car, and step out. That is the whole mod. It uses the elevators that were already there. The doors in the vanilla map are recognised on sight. No new tiles, no new items, no map edits, nothing added to the world. Every floor the shaft actually serves. Floors are read off the building itself and numbered from the bottom of the shaft, so towers, split levels and basements all list correctly. A tower that skips its mechanical floors will skip them in the menu too. It knows which side the doors open. Some shafts open on one side downstairs and the other side upstairs, and the mod puts you out at whichever doors serve the floor you asked for, in the lobby rather than in the shaft. description: Context Menu Cleanup Right-click menus get crowded fast when playing with a lot of mods, and many of the entries are rarely, if ever, used. List the entries you want removed or hidden, separated by semicolons: Sleep;Take Nap;~Teleport Matching is based on the text you actually see in the menu and ignores capitalization. Start an entry with ~ to match anything containing it, so ~Teleport catches "Teleport Here", "Teleport to Base", and anything else containing that word, while a plain entry has to match the whole name. description: Dynamic Hordes BC Ultimate Survival [all screenshots taken in debug mode] [update 0.4.7 live performance fixes, horde zombie de-spawning fix] [since updates went live, hordes will no longer track the players position to use as a spawn anchor, horde members should not idle around the hordes last spawn location, moving away from the horde for two in-game hours will force remaining zombies to rejoin the horde] I wanted hordes in Zomboid that actually feel like hordes. Not just 100 zombies suddenly appearing because a timer went off, and not hundreds of zombies randomly wandering between bits of countryside with no real destination. Large persistent hordes exist around the map, move from town to town, stay in towns for a while, then move on somewhere else. It is heavily inspired by the large travelling herds in The Walking Dead and is built specifically around Build 42.20. What the mod does • Adds between 1 and 8 persistent roaming hordes, configurable in Sandbox Options. • Hordes travel between actual named towns, rather than picking random groups of buildings and calling them settlements. • Includes the legacy towns and newer Build 42 areas including Brandenburg, Echo Creek, Ekron and Irvington. • Hordes continue migrating around the map even when the player is nowhere near them. • When a horde reaches a town it remains and roams there for 1 to 3 in-game days before moving on. • Hordes exist abstractly when far away and gradually become real zombies when they enter the player's loaded area. • Zombies materialise off-screen before you reach the herd rather than suddenly appearing around the player. • Killing physical herd zombies genuinely reduces that herd's persistent population. • Surviving hordes can slowly rebuild their numbers over time. • If a herd falls below the configured collapse percentage, it breaks apart and the remaining zombies become normal stragglers. • Destroyed hordes can eventually be replaced by a new generation elsewhere on the migration network. • Replacement hordes are distributed around the world rather than deliberately spawning near the player. • Individual hordes can be reset from the debug menu and recreated with a fresh migration. Onslaught Mode There is also an optional Onslaught Mode. Turn this on and every active horde stops following its normal town route and begins migrating towards you. They do not teleport. If a horde is on the other side of Kentucky, it has to migrate across the map to reach you. Move somewhere else and the destination moves with you. Turn Onslaught back off and the hordes return to their normal town-to-town migrations. The mod accounts for • Player-built bases - An outdoor courtyard inside a completely walled compound is technically still outdoors. The mod checks Build 42's enclosure regions so a properly enclosed compound is rejected as a spawn area. The horde has to appear outside and get through your defences normally. • Buildings- Horde zombies are not allowed to materialise inside rooms or houses. They can enter them afterwards like normal zombies. • Visible spawning- If a potential spawn square is on-screen, the mod rejects it. • Open wilderness- Forest and countryside squares without a world-region object remain valid if they pass the normal spawn checks. • Saving and loading- Physical herd representatives and persistent abstract population are handled separately to avoid duplication through vanilla zombie virtualisation. • Chunk unloading- Herd zombies are deliberately accounted for before they leave the loaded world. • Horde population- The population shown for a herd is meaningful. Killing herd zombies reduces it. • Horde collapse- A nearly destroyed herd does not continue wandering around pretending to contain hundreds of zombies. • Player detection- One member spotting the player can alert nearby herd zombies, they are pursuing you. • Town distribution- Long-distance migration uses a hand-authored named-town network instead of treating farms, warehouses or random building clusters as towns. • Build 42's expanded map - The migration network includes major newer settlements as well as the legacy towns. Debug tools Debug Mode is off by default. When enabled you can: • See H1, H2, H3 etc on the world map. • See herd population, state, route and destination. • See normal migration lines. • Select and test individual hordes. • Bring a herd near the player for testing. • Reset an individual herd and give it a fresh migration. • Force replacement of a destroyed herd. • Inspect generation and replacement information. During Onslaught Mode the normal migration lines are hidden because the destination is continuously moving with the player, but the individual herd icons remain visible. Sandbox Options Pretty much everything important can be adjusted: • Enable or completely disable Dynamic Hordes. • Number of active hordes. • Minimum and maximum herd population. • Maximum physical zombie representatives per herd. • Horde movement speed. • Horde replacement and replacement delay. • Horde regeneration, delay and speed. • Collapse threshold. • Town roaming and town stay duration. • Collective alert radius. • Player warning dialogue. • Onslaught Mode. • Debug Mode. Why another horde mod? There are already some really interesting horde mods for Zomboid. This is not meant as a dig at any of them. I made this because most of them are trying to solve a slightly different problem, and I wanted to avoid some of the limitations reported on their own Workshop pages and changelogs. Hordes Alpha B42 has reported limitations hordes becoming stuck around buildings with some navigation settings, and inherited notes around player-built structures/custom-map navigation. Dynamic Hordes instead gives its persistent herds known named-town destinations and controlled materialisation rules. Horde Night fundamentally an event/attack mod. Its changelog has historically included fixes for Build 42 spawning, spawn distance, safehouse spawning and multiplayer visibility. Dynamic Hordes is not based around creating a fresh attack because a particular night arrived. The hordes already exist elsewhere on the map and have somewhere they are going. Dynamic Horde Events creates encounters relative to the player's position. Dynamic Hordes is instead a persistent world simulation: normal-mode hordes have their own map position and migration whether you are near them or not. Living Hordes takes the larger approach of replacing the normal spawning and migration simulation. Dynamic Hordes deliberately adds persistent travelling mega-herds on top of the existing apocalypserather than replacing the entire vanilla zombie population system. Important notes • Currently designed for single player. • Built and tested against Project Zomboid Build 42.20. • No external framework dependency. • Normal zombie behaviour still applies once herd zombies are physically present. • Base protection stops a travelling herd from materialising inside a properly enclosed compound. It does not make the compound safe once the horde arrives outside it. The basic goal I want clearing a town to matter, but I don't want it to mean that town is safe forever. You might clear Rosewood completely. A few weeks later there could be 200 zombies coming down the road from somewhere else. That's the mod. description: Vanilla Fishing Fix — Build 42.20 Stable A vanilla-friendly fishing overhaul that makes every cast, fish and piece of equipment matter. Vanilla Fishing Fix rebuilds fishing balance without adding mandatory items or replacing the vanilla capture minigame. Fish become useful food, casting becomes skill-based, bait attracts different species, equipment has meaningful strengths and every catch can become part of your personal record—or a server-wide fishing tournament. Weight-Based Nutrition Calories, protein and fat are calculated from the fish's real weight and species profile. Small fish are common but modest meals; large fish can provide roughly 900–1800 kcal before Sandbox bonuses. Fish fillets correctly divide and preserve the nutrition of the original fish. Food bait is consumed in 5-hunger portions instead of deleting an entire fillet or piece of meat. Sandbox calorie bonuses range from 0% to 400%. Skill-Based Casting Before the vanilla capture minigame begins, a separate blue-and-yellow distance meter controls your cast from approximately 1 to 16 tiles. Fishing skill progressively slows the moving cursor. Higher skill slightly widens the precision zone. Higher skill reduces the maximum deviation of a failed cast. Immediate results: Perfect, Great, Good, Poor or Miss. The original vanilla fish-tension minigame remains intact after casting. More Dynamic Fishing Species-specific behaviour: carp are calmer, trout escape more often, catfish strain the line and pike are aggressive. Escapes, line breaks, very rare rod failures, exceptional catches and double catches. Expanded junk catches and very rare treasure made from vanilla items. Hidden rich fishing areas improve catches but become temporarily depleted with use. Rod wear scales with fish weight instead of applying the same damage to every catch. Fishing XP is awarded in stages: bite, control and successful capture, with a bonus for exceptional fish. Bait, Equipment and Conditions Bait choice and freshness now influence what you attract. Insects favour smaller fish, fresh fish bait attracts predators and meat is especially effective for catfish. Stale bait discourages demanding species, while rotten bait attracts scavengers and more junk. Hooks, line strength, line condition, rod type and rod condition all matter. Dawn and dusk are the best periods, weather has a stronger effect, and long fishing sessions gradually cause fatigue until the character rests. description: AllTheInfo Project Zomboid keeps track of far more than it ever puts on screen. It works with exact figures for damage, durability, spoilage, protection, growth and skill progression, then shows you a bar, a vague word, or nothing at all. AllTheInfo shows you the numbers, across the whole game, from a single mod. Every figure on screen is one the game itself is using, read out of the B42.20 code rather than estimated. What it adds Items Numbers on every bar vanilla draws without one: condition, damage, insulation, wind and water resistance, blood, dirt, wetness. Melee: crit chance, swing type, real attack speed, knockback, and the exact odds of losing a condition point per hit. Firearms: accuracy, effective range, jam chance, magazine size. Clothing: the discomfort value, which the base game never shows anywhere. Food: hours until stale and rotten at the current rate, accounting for fridge, freezer and sandbox spoilage speed. Cooking: how long anything cookable still needs, at the temperature the thing it is sitting in actually reaches: 200 C in an oven, 130 in a microwave, 80 on a barbecue or campfire. Once it is cooked the row turns red and counts down to the moment it burns instead. Books: reading time with Fast Reader, Slow Reader and glasses applied. Also: seeds, firewood burn time, bed quality, gas mask filters, torch runtime and light range, radio battery life, fishing rods, lines, hooks and baits, and which skill a tape or CD teaches and how much XP it gives. Compare against what you are using. A coloured difference next to each value. Weapons compare against what is in your hands; clothing against the piece worn in the same slot, following the game's own exclusive-slot rules, so a shirt correctly compares against the t-shirt it would replace. Crafting. Hover a recipe's result and get the full item block, comparison included, before you spend the materials. World Generators: fuel hours left, noise radius, average time until 20% condition and until it breaks, hourly odds of a backfire or fire. The powered area is outlined on the floor. Structures: health as a number under your cursor, no clicking. The build menu also shows what health you would get with the relevant skill at 10. Gas pumps: right-click one and hover Info for the fuel left in the tank and whether the mains or your own generator is keeping it alive. The game has that number and only prints it as a debug option. Crops: health out of 100, growth phase, hours to the next one, water level against what the plant needs, time since watering, pest levels. Vanilla hides most of this behind Farming levels or debug mode. Animals: right-click any animal for its panel. Butchering yield, blood in litres, feathers, old age and the weight ceiling -- figures that appear on no screen, cheat mode included -- plus health, hunger, thirst, attitude, milk, wool and pregnancy as numbers instead of words. Hover any row for what that stat actually does, thresholds included. Fishing: the panel rates four things as "Normal" or "Good" and never says what they are worth. Every row now carries its real multiplier, fog and wind get told apart from the weather, and the two factors the game never showed you get rows of their own: your hook and the fish in that spot. Plus bite chance, waiting time and trash odds. Hover a species for the Fishing level it needs, its size range and the odds it takes the bait you have on. Character What each skill level is for: hover a level and see every recipe and build that requires it. Read live from the game's own recipe list, so recipes added by other mods show up too and nothing goes stale after a patch. Skills: per-level descriptions with real figures, on fifteen skills. A weapon skill multiplies damage by 0.3 + level x 0.1, so x0.3 untrained and x1.3 at 10. Strength, Fitness, Nimble, Running, Sneaking, Lightfooted, Aiming, Reloading and Maintenance each get their own table, level by level. Traits and professions: starting skills with their true XP multiplier, traits granted, recipes taught by name, foraging bonuses per category. Plus written-out effects for the ones hardcoded in the game's Java that nothing can read at runtime: 79 traits and professions covered. Moodles: all 26, every level, as a list of numbers: the exact threshold that triggers it and every effect it has. XP boost fix: the game shows "+75%" for a level 1 boost. The real figure is x4, because a skill with no boost runs at a quarter rate. Why one mod instead of eight Several of these features already exist, each in its own mod. Getting the full picture today means installing eight of them and hoping they do not collide. No conflicts. Those mods overlap. More than one wraps the same tooltip, the same generator window, the same XP screen, and whichever loads last wins while the rest quietly stop working. Here there is one implementation of each hook. The parts talk to each other. One codebase, so comparisons, formatting, colours and options behave the same everywhere instead of looking like eight mods stapled together. Built for B42.20. Every formula re-derived against the current build. Most of the mods this replaces were written for B41 and several of their numbers are simply wrong now. You choose what you see Every feature is a toggle in the mod's own All Info tab in the game options, not buried in the Mods list. Grouped by theme with a master switch per section, so you can turn off a whole area or one row inside it. Want the weapon numbers but not the food timers? The XP fix and nothing else? Two clicks. Every option says what it adds and where, and a disabled one is never even called. Compatibility Build: 42.20 and up. Multiplayer: client-side only. Nothing is sent to the server, so it works on any server without the server having it. Saves: safe to add or remove at any time. Nothing is stored in your save. Splitscreen: supported. Languages: English, Simplified Chinese, Russian, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, German, Turkish, French, Japanese and Polish, the ten biggest on Steam. Not a partial job: all 506 strings in each. Most rows also reuse the game's own labels, which are already translated into all 29. AllTheInfo does the same job as these. Do not run them alongside it: More Item Information, Fix XP View, Generator Time Remaining, GeneratorRange, Show Wall Health, More Description for Traits, Clear description for Moodles, Descriptive Tooltips for Skill Levels, Detailed Skill Tooltips, Detailed Descriptions for Occupations and Traits, Moodle Effects Explained. Overlaps but does not break: Better Generator Info wraps the generator window properly, so both blocks render and you will just see some figures twice. Under the hood Each provider runs isolated: if one ever breaks on some odd item, that item loses its rows and everything else carries on. There is also a self-test in the options tab that checks over 100 assertions against the live game and says loudly if a patch moved something. Still a beta Feature-complete and tested in game, but young. Under active development: more detail, more derived values, and fixes for whatever you report. Bug reports in the comments are welcome. Tell me the item, the screen and what looked wrong. Translation corrections just as much: every language comes from one phrase table, so a single fix lands everywhere at once, and the numbers are never translated -- they pass through untouched. Mod ID: AllInfo Workshop ID: 3781129962 Mod ID: AllInfo

description: Companion fix for [B42]PROJECT RV Interior. Weather leaks straight through the cabin walls - this stops that, while still respecting whether the RV's own AC/heater is actually on. More fixes planned; see the roadmap at the bottom. The bug RV interiors are plain map tiles placed far outside the normal playable map, with no roof geometry for the engine's room/roof detection to find. That leaves every cabin permanently flagged "outdoors" by the engine itself, so full outdoor rain and temperature apply exactly as if you were standing in a field - worst during rain. (The base mod's own code even fills rain barrels placed inside the room from "rain" - the same bug, visible from the inside of the author's own logic.) The fix The "outdoors" flag itself can't be changed from a mod, so this corrects its effects on you directly, about once a second, while you're inside any RV interior: Wetness (body and every worn item) is always driven back down, since the interior's rain simulation keeps re-wetting the room every tick. The cabin has a roof regardless of power - rain shouldn't reach you either way. Body temperature is corrected only if the RV actually has a real Heater part switched on with power available - the same part behind the vanilla driver-seat "Heater On/Off" radial toggle, which doubles as AC via a negative target temperature. No heater, heater off, or no battery charge means no correction at all: a desert-parked RV with the AC off still cooks you, a snowed-in one with no heater still freezes you. Reaching the heater/AC from inside The vanilla heater/AC toggle only works from the driver's seat, which you're not in once teleported into the interior. Adds a right-click option, "Toggle RV Heater/AC," while you're inside, so you don't have to walk back out to the cab to switch it on or off. Works in singleplayer and multiplayer alike - the fix runs authoritatively on whichever process actually owns your character (the server on a dedicated server, your own game in singleplayer), never on a remote client. An optional sandbox setting ("Respect vehicle Heater/AC for cabin temperature," default on) turns the whole temperature behaviour off server-wide, leaving only the wetness fix. Notes Safe to add or remove mid-save. No new items, recipes or save data. Requires [B42]PROJECT RV Interior. Load after it. Workshop ID: 3781225795 Mod ID: ProjectRVFix

description: THIS MOD IS NOT DEPRICATED AND HAS BEEN MERGED WITH THE MAIN COMPANION DOGS MOD IN THE MOST RECENT UPDATE SO IT WILL NO LONGER BE UPDATED AS OF 2026/08/18 Companion Dogs - Performance Patch [B42] Unofficial performance add-on for Companion Dogs [ALPHA]. This mod reduces traversal stutter caused by repeated building classification inside Companion Dogs' LoadChunk processing. Requirements Project Zomboid Build 42 Companion Dogs [ALPHA] Companion Dogs Workshop ID: 3740052292 Companion Dogs Mod ID: CompanionDogs What the patch does Companion Dogs classifies buildings while chunks are loaded. A single building can occupy many squares, which can cause the same static building checks to be performed repeatedly during one chunk load. This add-on wraps the existing Companion Dogs building classifiers and caches their boolean result by stable building bounds. It currently caches the base classifiers for: Houses Police buildings Pet/vet buildings Farm buildings What it does NOT change Dog spawn chances Breed selection Dog behavior or AI Taming, bonding, breeding, skills, or genetics Persistence Companion Dogs assets The original Companion Dogs LoadChunk callback and spawning logic remain in place. Performance testing In the test environment that led to this patch, Companion Dogs' LoadChunk callback produced hundreds of calls above 10 ms, with repeated stalls in the 250-330 ms range while driving through populated areas. With this add-on enabled, the same instrumented route produced zero Companion Dogs LoadChunk callback warnings at or above 10 ms, while driving remained smooth. Results will vary by save, hardware, map area, and mod list. Compatibility Tested: Project Zomboid 42.20.2 with Companion Dogs [ALPHA]. The patch performs a runtime compatibility check before wrapping anything. If the expected Companion Dogs building classifiers are missing after a future update, the patch disables itself and logs the reason instead of guessing. Multiplayer: The patch does not alter networking, but co-op and dedicated-server behavior has not yet been independently validated for this add-on. Installation Subscribe to Companion Dogs [ALPHA], subscribe to this patch, and enable both in the main-menu Mods screen. Companion Dogs should load before this patch. The dependency metadata handles that automatically. Because Companion Dogs uses custom animals, follow the base mod author's recommendation and fully restart Project Zomboid after enabling the mods before loading a save. Credits and permissions Companion Dogs [ALPHA] is created by Bjorn. This is an independent, unofficial performance add-on and is not affiliated with or endorsed by the original author. This Workshop item contains no Companion Dogs source code, models, textures, animations, sounds, or other assets. It interacts only with runtime tables/functions exposed by the installed Companion Dogs mod. Thanks to the Companion Dogs author for the excellent companion-dog mod that made this optimization worth pursuing. Zero to Chad (Build 42.20) Start as a coward. End as the guy zombies have nightmares about. Every zombie you kill hardens you. Kill milestones permanently lower your maximum panic, grant Brave and Desensitized, and cure your phobias along the way. A character progression system built on the kill counter you already have. Default progression Every 100 kills - your maximum panic drops permanently. The reductions stack. 500 kills - you earn Brave. This milestone counts double toward the reduction. 1000 kills - you earn Desensitized, which removes Cowardly, Agoraphobic, Claustrophobic and Hemophobic. By then your maximum panic has already reached zero: the trait just makes it official. Features Clumsy is cured too. At the Brave milestone your combat experience steadies your feet. Optional, like everything else. Your phobias are cured, not ignored. Take Cowardly, Hemophobic or Claustrophobic at character creation for the extra points - your survivor will grow out of them. The cap beats the multipliers. The reduction applies to your final panic value, so it works even on a character whose panic is inflated by Cowardly. A trait that shows your progress: Hardened - Bronze, Silver, Gold, with its own icon in the character sheet. It is informational, cannot be picked at character creation, and disappears once you become Desensitized. In-character notifications: a floating thought when you cross a milestone, not a wall of numbers. Can be turned off. Death resets it. Progress belongs to the character, not the save. A new survivor starts from zero. Costs nothing to run. Milestones are checked once per in-game day at midnight and on login. Sandbox options Nine options. Change the kills per milestone, the thresholds for each trait, and turn any part off: run it as traits-only, as panic-reduction-only, or make the whole thing brutally slow. The reduction rescales itself to whatever thresholds you pick. Multiplayer Works in singleplayer and multiplayer. Traits are granted by the server, so they survive relogs and server restarts - tested on a dedicated server, not just assumed. Each player progresses on their own kills. description: 10 YEARS LATER v2.0.0 - Restructure & Cluster Update Check changelog if you want to know all the changes! For server owners who have experienced various issues, you can use this PLAYTEST BUILD to test the latest fixes and verify whether the issues have been resolved. INTRODUCTION An unofficial Build 42 Stable adaptation and continuation of Dane's original 10 Years Later mod. This is not intended to be a better version of the original mod but rather an unofficial continuation and adaptation of Dane's work for Build 42 Stable. Since we deeply respect and admire Dane and the work he put into creating the original mod. To the point 10 Years Later has become an essential part of how my girlfriend and I enjoy Project Zomboid. The goal is to preserve the visual and gameplay effects of 10 Years Later while making the environment feel more naturally reclaimed and giving multiplayer servers and lower-end PCs more control over how much processing is performed. MY UPDATES FROM THE ORIGINAL VEGETATION ENVIRONMENT Added clustered environmental spawning for a much more natural and realistic distribution of trees, bushes, grass, and trash. Vegetation now spawns much closer together in natural groups and clusters instead of being evenly scattered across the environment. Added support for large/JUMBO trees using appropriate tree and foliage components. Improved vegetation density and distribution to better resemble how plants naturally reclaim abandoned areas over time. Added optional controls for indoor vegetation and overgrowth. Changed grass sprite to prevent overlay cutoff issues. Grass and vegetation use appropriate animated sprites where available. Fixed vegetation that could not be removed properly. URBAN ENVIRONMENT Fences can now use Build 42 Stable's damaged, bent, and destroyed fence variants. Added automatic vine removal from fences that become completely destroyed. Reworked vegetation, vines, fence damage, ruined windows/doors, barricades, and generic objects into dedicated processing systems. PERFORMANCE Added a performance preset system designed around different hardware levels. Added Potato, Low-end, Mid-range, High-end, NASA, and Custom performance presets. Added individual controls for optional performance-heavy systems such as vines, cracks, wall damage, roofs, generic objects, stories, and animals. Reworked square processing for better performance and reliability. Improved processing behavior for multiplayer servers. TWEAKS & FIX Improved animal spawning to prevent excessive spawning attempts and dedicated-server errors. Fixed barricades not spawning or working properly. Various fixes and adjustments I forgot lol. FEATURES FROM THE ORIGINAL Adjustable abandoned story/event spawn frequency. Configurable tree spawning, including separate tree spawning rates for roads. Configurable vine growth and vegetation reclaiming. Adjustable grass spawning, including separate rates for roads. Adjustable fallen leaves spawning, including separate rates for roads. Configurable custom grass and natural debris, including separate rates for roads. Adjustable bush spawning, including separate rates for roads. Configurable road and dirt crack overlays for environmental deterioration. Adjustable trash spawning, with separate settings for interiors. Configurable barricade spawning. Adjustable wall deterioration and decay. Adjustable roof deterioration and decay. Configurable fence damage. Adjustable abandoned vehicle spawning. Adjustable animal spawning. THANK YOU This is an unofficial adaptation and continuation made with genuine respect for Dane. My girlfriend and I are forever grateful for the work you put into 10 Years Later. It has given us countless hours of enjoyment in Project Zomboid, and this project would not exist without the original work. If Dane ever wishes for this project to be taken down, or releases an updated version of 10 Years Later, I will happily respect his wishes and remove or step aside from this project. REPORTS & SUGGESTIONS All reported issues and reasonable feature suggestions will be considered. If you encounter a problem, please provide as much information as possible. However if you are being a dickhead, don't expect us to reply. I’d rather make love than communicate with the likes of you. description: Sleep in multiplayer without waiting for everyone else, and without breaking the night. How it works Go to bed the normal way. While asleep an overlay lets you pick how you sleep, and you can switch at any time without waking up: Wait for team (default) - plain vanilla. As soon as everyone is asleep the server fast-forwards the night, exactly like it always did. Solo nap - rest at accelerated speed while the world keeps running at normal time. A full rest takes a few real minutes instead of twenty. The overlay also shows your sleep level 0-100 with a marker for the nap limit, your fatigue, and a wake button. A small HUD indicator shows how many players are currently asleep, so you know when the group is ready for the night. Not overpowered Solo naps stop at a configurable fatigue remainder (15% by default) - handy, but not a full night. Full rest is what a proper night with the group is for. Bed quality matters, and rest follows the vanilla recovery curve, just faster. The mod never touches world time The only fast-forward is the vanilla one. When everyone is asleep the mod stands down completely and lets the server run the night, so nights cannot be cut short by the mod. Server setup (required) In your server settings: SleepAllowed=true and SleepNeeded=true. Without both, Build 42 servers wipe fatigue every tick and force-wake sleepers after about three in-game hours - sleep will not work with or without this mod. Recommended: FastForwardMultiplier=5 (the default 40 makes a shared night pass in about 15 seconds; 5 gives roughly 2 minutes). Sandbox options Nap speed, fatigue floor, endurance recovery, auto-wake, bed quality multipliers and the HUD indicator are all configurable. Build 42.13+ only. Multiplayer focused. English, Russian and Brazilian Portuguese. Workshop ID: 3781533687 Mod ID: TrueSleep

description: V's Judo Takedowns - SP & MP Okay, maybe not exactly Judo, but close enough. This mod simulates throwing zombies to the ground, giving you another way to control zombies at close range. Works in Singleplayer and Multiplayer. 1,000+ Subscribers & Top 10 Weekly Most Popular! We somehow made it. V's Judo Takedowns has passed 1,000 current subscribers and reached the Top 10 Weekly Most Popular B42 mods in less than a week. I honestly didn't expect this little mod about throwing zombies to grow this quickly. Thank you to everyone who subscribed, shared the mod, tested it, left feedback, and helped it get here. I really appreciate the support. Please Rate - Ratings and feedback help me know whether people actually enjoy the mod and what I should focus on next. What this mod does V's Judo Takedowns allows you to perform close-range takedowns that force zombies to the ground with very little damage. The idea was inspired by the John Wick series, where Judo and grappling are frequently used to control an opponent and create an opportunity to finish them. Think of it as an alternative to vanilla shoving: Instead of pushing the zombie away, you take it down. Recommended Use & Current Limitations V's Judo Takedowns currently works best when fighting small groups of around 3–5 zombies. The current takedown system can become less reliable when surrounded by larger groups, particularly when 6 or more zombies are competing for targeting at close range. For now, I recommend using Judo as a tool for controlling small groups and creating openings when slightly outnumbered, rather than as a way to fight entire hordes. This is a limitation of the current architecture. How to use the mod - Subscribe and enable the mod. - Multiplayer servers should use VJudoTakedownMP. - Aim near a zombie and press the Judo key. - Default key: Left Alt - The hotkey can be customized through Project Zomboid's Key Bindings. - The takedown works regardless of what you are currently holding, including firearms, melee weapons, bags, or bare hands. Balance & Sandbox Options Takedowns use stamina and can be configured through Sandbox settings. Server owners and players can adjust: - Minimum Strength - Minimum Fitness - Minimum Stamina Required - Takedown Stamina Cost - Whiff Stamina Cost - Play Animation on Whiff The core takedown range and cooldown are intentionally fixed. Notices \*The mod is designed to simulate throws regardless of the item you are holding. Its behavior is therefore intended to remain similar to vanilla shoving rather than functioning as a conventional weapon attack. \*The mod currently uses vanilla Project Zomboid animations. Animation choices prioritize keeping the player mobile and avoiding unnecessary animation locking. \*Multiplayer and Singleplayer are both supported. Roadmap to 1.0 - Complete [strike]- Directional throws using existing animations[/strike] Done [strike]- Multiplayer support[/strike] Done [strike]- Stamina system[/strike] Done [strike]- Balance / Sandbox options[/strike] Done [strike]- Takedown audio[/strike] Done The original roadmap for V's Judo Takedowns is now complete. Future Grappling Project More advanced grappling features, including custom takedown animations and direct player-zombie grappling interactions, will not be added to V's Judo Takedowns. Instead, these ideas are planned for a separate future mod. The concept will require further research and development to determine what is technically possible within Project Zomboid, particularly for synchronized player-zombie interactions, custom animations, and more advanced grappling mechanics. There is currently no release date. Development will begin only after the necessary R&D has been completed. Development V's Judo Takedowns will continue to receive maintenance, fixes, and improvements where necessary. Feedback is welcome, particularly regarding: - Balance - Multiplayer reliability - Situations where a takedown feels like it should have connected but did not Videos and GIFs will continue to be added as I get good footage. Special Thanks A special thank you to Alice & Elise for their help throughout development. Workshop ID: 3781547420 Mod ID: VJudoTakedown Mod ID: VJudoTakedownMP

description: Undead Wildlife Kentucky's wildlife did not escape the infection. Disclaimer: Multiplayer support is experimental. The core systems work in multiplayer, but animal movement, attacks and reanimation are currently much smoother in single-player. Use on a server at your own risk and please report any issues. Undead Wildlife allows the outbreak to spread through Kentucky's animal population. Living animals begin normally, but zombies can pursue, grab and attack them. Animals killed during these attacks rot, die and may rise again as hostile infected wildlife. The Outbreak Spreads The mod no longer converts every animal immediately by default. Zombies now hunt living animals and continue attacking until their prey dies. The corpse changes to its infected texture, remains on the ground during the reanimation delay and then rises as undead wildlife. Animals that survive an attack may still succumb to their wounds or infection later. Zombies can feast on fallen animals and become available to pursue other living animals once the corpse reanimates. Immediate conversion remains available as an optional sandbox setting for players who prefer the original gameplay style. Features Bloody and decaying infected variants with new rotten textures Undead deer, cattle, pigs, sheep, chickens, turkeys, rabbits, raccoons and their young Zombies visibly pursue, grab and attack living animals Zombie-killed animals can decay, reanimate and turn against survivors Optional outdoor encounters that send infected wildlife towards the player from outside immediate view Encounter frequency rises as the outbreak progresses through in-game weeks Undead animals pursue the player and commit to close-range attacks instead of repeatedly strafing through them Successful weapon hits interrupt and stagger animal attacks Animals can be pushed away, while smaller creatures such as chickens and rabbits can be stomped without a weapon Firearms and ordinary weapons can damage infected wildlife Infected wildlife cannot be butchered, harvested for meat or bones, or placed on butcher hooks Custom corrupted animal audio without replacing the sounds of living vanilla animals Fair Infection Rules Animal combat can be rough at close range, so attacks from undead wildlife cannot cause bites or transmit the Knox infection. Scratches, lacerations, bleeding, pain and ordinary wound infection can still occur. Large animals remain extremely dangerous. Bulls are excluded from supplemental encounters, making them exceptionally rare, but infected livestock created through the outbreak can still pose a serious threat. Progressive Outdoor Encounters Supplemental encounters only progress while a survivor is outdoors. Animals will not quietly accumulate around your home while you spend time inside. By default, each outdoor survivor receives one encounter roll every 10 real-life minutes. The chance begins at 5%, rises by 3 percentage points after each completed in-game week and stops at 40%. Encounter animals are capped and despawn when they are far from every active survivor. These values can be adjusted or the encounter system can be disabled entirely in the sandbox settings. Sandbox Settings Enable or disable the mod Enable immediate replacement of existing animals Enable or disable supplemental encounters Starting encounter chance Weekly encounter increase and maximum chance Real-time encounter check interval Maximum active encounters and despawn distance Detection range, damage and health loss Knockdown chance and animal shoving Enable or disable zombies hunting living animals Zombie detection range for animal prey Zombie-kill reanimation chance and delay Multiplayer Undead Wildlife supports single-player, hosted multiplayer and dedicated servers. Spawning, zombie predation, targeting and player damage are validated by the server. Single-player is currently the most polished experience. Multiplayer is playable, but network delay can make animal pathing, attack alignment and reanimation less seamless than in solo play. Continued multiplayer feedback is welcome. Requirements Project Zomboid Build 42.20.2 or newer No other mods required Existing Saves The mod can be added to an existing save. Living animals remain alive by default and can become infected through zombie attacks. Supplemental encounters begin at the chance appropriate for the world's current age. The optional immediate-replacement setting can convert already loaded animals and redirect future ranch and wildlife spawns to infected variants. Removing the mod from an active save has not been fully tested. Back up your save before attempting removal. This is still a work-in-progress mod. Balance feedback and detailed bug reports are welcome. When reporting a problem, please include whether you were playing single-player, hosted multiplayer or on a dedicated server. description: ⚠ Ki5 Support For everyone who wants to see full Ki5 vehicle support with exclusive custom snow textures — I’m opening a fundraiser to make it happen. You can support the development with a donation starting from just €1. Creating full Ki5 support will require a lot of work and could take several weeks, or even a month. Snow1, Snow2 and Snow3 - from light snow to heavy coverage. • Temperature matters. The warmer it gets, the faster accumulated snow melts. • Engine heat. A running engine melts only part of the accumulated snow, even in cold temperatures. It cannot completely clear the vehicle. • Manual cleaning. Vehicle snow states continue to update outside your current chunk. • Original states are preserved. Existing visual states such as blood remain intact. • Multiplayer supported. Other players can see the changing snow stages. Snow accumulation Snow1 - 60 in-game minutes Snow2 - 180 in-game minutes Snow3 - 360 in-game minutes Each stage uses specially prepared snow-covered vehicle textures. description: Cut the busywork out of magazine reloading with four handheld speed loaders and a furniture-grade Loading Station, built for Build 42.20. This mod NEVER creates ammunition. It only automates the physical loading of detachable magazines: loose rounds are consumed from your ammo boxes (handheld loaders) or from the station's 30kg internal store (deposited from ammo boxes), and the rounds are pressed into your magazines. HANDHELD SPEED LOADERS Four universal loaders: Civilian (1.10×), Professional (1.25×), Military (1.40×), Spec-Ops (1.50×). NOT caliber-specific: compatible detachable magazines work automatically. Loader speed is property-driven (LoaderSpeedMultiplier). Carrying multiple loaders applies only the highest multiplier. Other mods can add compatible loaders simply by defining the same property. The Spec-Ops loader is exceptionally rare and intended as a high-end find. LOADING STATION Place the station through the right-click context menu like furniture. After placement, the station takes a short moment to initialize before its inventory can safely be used. Internal store holds up to 30 kg of loose ammunition deposited from ammo boxes. Custom panel UI displays stored ammunition and compatible magazines with live round/capacity readouts. Select individual magazines or use Load Selected / Load All / Cancel. Sequential, server-authoritative loading queue: each magazine is placed on the station, loaded through a timed action, then returned to your inventory. No ammunition is ever generated. Four visual states: Empty / Low / Medium / Full, with optional magazine-on-station visuals. MULTIPLAYER Multiplayer-safe: station state, inventory changes, and loading operations are server-authoritative. Client requests are validated and applied on the server. Timed actions and station synchronization work correctly in hosted and dedicated-server multiplayer. SANDBOX Speed Loader Reload XP: 100% / 75% / 50% (default) / 25% / 0%. Applies to magazine loading performed through both handheld loaders and the Loading Station. COMPATIBILITY Compatibility-first: the mod never identifies magazines by hardcoded item names. It inspects magazine properties such as ammo type, capacity, and current rounds, allowing vanilla and modded detachable magazines to work automatically. No ammo generation. No caliber-specific restrictions. Just faster magazine loading. Workshop ID: 3781855943 Mod ID: MagazineSpeedLoaders

description: Immersive Solar Arrays Harvest solar power for the needs of your base. Wire car batteries into a battery bank, put panels on the roof, and run your fridges and freezers off the sun instead of a generator that has to be fed. This is a fork of RadX5 and Poltergeist's Immersive Solar Arrays, rebuilt for build 42. Support for build 41 has been dropped. Build 42.20 or newer. Singleplayer and multiplayer. What it does Battery banks. Wire car batteries, build a bank, and it powers everything a generator would, in the same radius, without fuel. Solar panels. Flat, wall mounted and floor mounted. Connect them to a bank and they charge it through the day. Cloud, fog, temperature and the length of the day all move the number. Status window. Right click the bank. The summary tab says whether the panels are keeping up and how long the charge lasts at the current draw. The details tab lists what is actually pulling power. Generator backup. A generator plugged in near a bank becomes its backup. Put a failsafe trigger on the generator's square and the bank starts it when the charge runs low, then stops it once the panels have caught up. Loot and world spawns. Panels, batteries, inverters and the skill magazine spawn in the containers you would expect. Pre-placed crates and battery banks appear around the map, and five stash houses hide a solar cache behind an annotated map. What this fork fixes The build 42 branch loaded and appeared to work, but most of it quietly did nothing. None of the below wrote anything to the log. Every string showed as its own key. Build 42 reads only JSON translations. The mod still shipped build 41 text tables, which are not loaded at all. All 27 languages converted. Every item had no item type. The field that declares one was renamed, and the old name is not parsed any more. Every recipe was impossible to perform. Item tags are matched literally and are namespaced now, so the tools the recipes asked for matched nothing. Battery banks never became generators. Two property accessors removed in build 42 threw on every placement, so banks powered nothing, their window closed on open, and panels could not see them. Base game loot tables were being corrupted. A misspelt field put a weight into vanilla item lists with no item in front of it, shifting every pair after it. Stash houses errored on load and their caches were never placed. Multiplayer did nothing. Plugging a generator, flipping the bank switch, connecting a panel and moving a battery all reached for a server object that does not exist on a client. Tile fixes. Flat panels no longer draw over your feet, and the failsafe no longer hides under the generator it is wired to. Requirements Target Square: On Load Commands is needed for the pre-placed crates that spawn around the map. Without it everything else still works, you just do not get those crates. It is safe to add or remove on an existing save. Options Sandbox options cover panel efficiency, how quickly batteries wear out, DIY battery capacity, how often the bank charges, how power draw is calculated, loot rarity for each item group, world spawns and stash houses. Making a solar panel and making an inverter from scratch are off by default. Turn on expanded recipes in the sandbox options if you want them. Notes Only run one version of this mod. The mod id is ISA. Some options need a game reload, and stash houses want a new save to appear properly. Mods that replace the default inventory transfer or generator interactions can cause problems. Test on a save you are willing to lose before adding it to a long running one. Reporting a bug Reproduce it with only this mod enabled and write down the steps. If it only happens alongside other mods, narrow down which ones. Check the console log for errors and post those with everything else. Credits Original mod by RadX5 and Poltergeist, with thanks to everyone who contributed to it over the years, translators included. Licensed under the Apache License 2.0. Original: github.com/radx5Blue/ImmersiveSolarArrays This fork: github.com/aspctt/ImmersiveSolarArrays Workshop ID: 3781944805 Mod ID: ISA

mod_name: Scenarios [B42.20] - Where I Was When It Happened
description: Where I Was When It Happened Tired of always spawning in a house? Want to experience what it was like for other citizens of Knox Country, those first few hours of the outbreak? Try all that, and a few new map areas, with "Where I Was When It Happened"! Escape from the sanatorium, respond to the outbreak as a police officer, find yourself trapped in prison, live out your doomsday prepper fantasy, or shelter from a storm at a remote radio outpost. Each scenario changes your starting location, clothing, equipment, condition, or surrounding world to create a different opening story. Optional challenges can also be enabled for players who want a defined objective. Important Information Requires Project Zomboid Build 42.20 or later. Currently designed for single-player only. Scenarios are applied when creating a new world. Existing worlds are not converted into scenarios. The default setting is "No Scenario," which preserves the ordinary Project Zomboid start. Optional Challenge is disabled by default. No other mods are required. How to Select a Scenario Enable the mod, begin creating a new Custom Sandbox world, and open the Where I Was When It Happened page in the Sandbox settings. Choose your starting scenario and optionally enable Optional Challenge. Scenarios The scenarios below appear in the same order as the Sandbox settings. Commune The rapture came and went, and it didn't even go down the way your leader said it would. Optional Challenge: Your faith is unyielding. Remain alive without leaving the compound for 14 days. Sunderland Hills Sanatorium The sanatorium has been abandoned. You wake in a patient room wearing only a hospital gown and slippers. Find a way out. Optional Challenge: Find and escape through the sanatorium tunnel. Police Response You were approaching the scene of a reported shooting when all hell broke loose. You begin as a police officer beside a working cruiser with its lights and siren active. Optional Challenge: Check on your wife and children—reach and clear your marked Louisville home. Prison Break Only one way out: through loads of undead. You begin inside the Rosewood prison cell block. There should be a way out. Optional Challenge: Escape the prison area. Critical Condition Inspired by CDDA's Really Bad Day challenge. You wake in a hospital sick, exhausted, starving, dehydrated, and severely injured. Optional Challenge: Get rid of every negative moodle and restore your body to full health. Barricaded – Running Low You successfully barricaded your house when the outbreak began, but it has been a while and now you are running low on everything. The house has been lived in, picked over, and barricaded, with only a small collection of supplies remaining. Optional Challenge: Become self-sufficient by reaching level 3 in Farming or Animal Husbandry. Barricaded – Doomsday Prepper They all laughed. Well, who's laughing now? You begin inside a fully barricaded house stocked with food, water, medicine, weapons, ammunition, tools, and reading material. Optional Challenge: Survive for at least 30 days and reach level 5 in five skills. Fitness and Strength do not count. Storm Shelter You were working the graveyard shift at a remote ranger radio outpost when the outbreak hit. A severe thunderstorm is raging outside, and the power has gone out. You receive storm gear, basic emergency supplies, and a small snack pack. Optional Challenge: Restore power to the ranger radio outpost. The Tourist You chose the worst possible time to take your PTO. You begin in a nice hotel. Optional Challenge: Reach Coalfield Historic Reenactment Town within one week while keeping your camera. Lost Hiker You were hiking and got completely lost. You begin in the wilderness with hiking clothing, a backpack, a compass, and basic outdoor supplies. Optional Challenge: Reach civilization within four days. Prison Break – Probably Impossible Only one way out: through loads of undead. Unlike the standard Prison Break scenario, the prepared escape-route doors remain locked. I have no reason to think this one is possible. Left it in cause there's always someone who might try anyway. Optional Challenge: Escape the prison area. Alpha Release If a scenario fails to initialize safely, the mod attempts to return the character to the ordinary starting position without applying destructive inventory or injury changes. This is an alpha release for Build 42. The scenarios have been tested individually, but unusual sandbox combinations or other mods may cause unexpected behavior. This is my first mod ever, so, hope you like it! When reporting a problem, please include: The selected scenario Whether Optional Challenge was enabled Whether the problem happened before or after reloading the save Any relevant lines beginning with [WhereIWas] from your Project Zomboid console log Feedback about balance, starting equipment, map placement, and challenge conditions is welcome. You can customize: Sidebar; Clock and alarm button; Time-speed controls; Moodles; Hotbar. The edit panel can also be moved anywhere on the screen or completely hidden while you position the interface. CUSTOMIZE THE SIDEBAR Choose which sidebar icons remain visible and adjust the sidebar to match your preferred layout. Primary and secondary hand items scale together with the sidebar, and additional multiplayer buttons are supported. 5 INDEPENDENT HUD PRESETS Create and save up to five independent HUD presets. Each preset stores its own: Interface positions; Interface sizes; Sidebar icon selection; Clock and time-control configuration; Moodle configuration; Hotbar configuration. Unused presets begin with the original Project Zomboid positions, 100% sizes, and default icons. Switching presets restores the exact layout saved in that preset. SAVE AND RESET CONTROLS Save the active preset or reset only the part you want to restore: Save the current configuration; Reset positions to the original game locations; Reset sizes to the original game sizes. SMB AUTOHIDE INTEGRATION This edition adapts the movable interfaces to SMB AutoHIDEhud instead of forcing animations to use the game's original HUD positions. Supported panels fade in and out in their customized locations, including while the game is paused. Mouse detection, visibility restoration, and animation behavior continue working after an element has been moved or resized. The F10 menu includes independent animation controls for the sidebar, clock and time controls, moodles, and hotbar. These controls take priority over SMB AutoHIDEhud for those four interfaces: disabling an animation in Movable HUD keeps that interface permanently visible even if the corresponding SMB option is enabled. The same HUD profile is restored after leaving the game or switching to another world or server. In multiplayer, the profile remains local and personal to this installation. description: In this mod, you will find a wide Variety of MREs And by wide variety, I mean a total of 86 functional MREs All MREs are fully custom with new custom made items ============================================== There's sanbox settings to enable / disable the MREs you want / don't want. Every theme has it's own settings = 9 themes in total = 86 MREs in total. So, if you only want the Military MREs to spawn, disable all other themes. If you only want the Neo-Noir and Post-Apocalyptic MREs to spawn, make sure that only those 2 themes are enabled. Etc. Toggle for The Straw of Life and toggle for the Medical MRE In case you only want those 2, or just the Water Straw. ----------------------------------------------- Themes include - Military (Normal MREs like we all know) Nature Inspired (Most meals and drinks will be natural items, no chemicals, etc.) Vault-Stasis (Cryo-Preservation, Food that lasts for centuries) Neo-Noir (Bright Neon and Futuristic, and sometimes drab and dreary) Post-Apoc (This is the stuff that keeps the Wasteland fueled) Deep-Space (Rations that are "Out-of-this-World") Deep-Sea (Ocean floor scraps and Underwater meals you never knew existed) ElderTarkov (Gaming related, but it includes only Tarkov and Elder Scrolls for now) Misc. (At the moment this only includes a Roman MRE, Japanese MRE and a 100% Vanilla-Friendly candy pack) Books (Books to raise some skills and make you happier while reading) ---------------------------------------------------- The Straw of Life This mod includes a Water Straw, to drink tainted water safely. When you have the straw and a tainted water container in your inventory, you will get the option to "Drink with Water Straw". That means you can use the straw to drink the tainted water directly out of the container, which purifies as you drink. So that's clean, safe water just like that. The straw has 20 uses. That's 20 sips of 100ml water each time used. One straw supports 2L of clean, purified water before it dissappears. The straw sometimes spawns in the world in Medical containers, but the only other place to find it, is in the Medical MRE. (Military spawns and Medical spawns) There's also some new Water Purification items. Some can be used as a spice in your meals as well. Your choice what you want to use it for. ------------------------------------------------------- The Flameless Ration Heater (FRH) We all adore our ration heaters. MREs are not complete without this beauty. So yes, this mod includes a working FRH, to heat those cold scraps again. Just note, not all MREs will include an FRH, only the ones with relavent meals will include one. It kind of seems silly to warm dried food or a loaf of bread, etc. You just need a bit of water in your inventory, fresh or tainted, and the FRH, along with the meal you want to heat. If you opened a meal before warming it up, don't worry though, you CAN heat the opened meals as well. You are welcome. ------------------------------------------------------- Now, the Condiment saga This mod includes a LOT of condiments. That includes Sauces, Spreads, Coffees, Teas, Sugars, Salts, etc. All the lovely little Accessory packet trinkets you'll find in MREs. All of them are cross-referenced with all MRE meals. That means, you can use the normal Military HotSauce / Ketchup / etc. in all other themes of MREs, and vice versa. Want a Space age sauce on your Roman bread? Go ahead and spice up that toothbreaking brick. Want your Apocalyptic slurry in your Algae sludge? Mix up that *sheet* and see if your eyes can handle what you just concocted. --------------------------------------------------------- The Accessory Packets All applicable MREs will give you an accessory packet with all the precious goodies to help you cope and survive another 24 hours in this forsaken world of pixels and stupid crazy zombies. It's like opening a Birthday present after opening the Xmas present. --------------------------------------------------------- The Books of Survival This module includes 6 books that raises certain skills when read. One time use per book. Each book covers 3 skills. 18 skills total. Each book is linked to a certain type of MRE theme, so the skills will raise according to the each certain theme. They will spawn in the according spawns for the skills they cover. They will also boost your happiness and lower boredom while being read. ---------------------------------------------------------- So now, let's see, your MRE will include a Main meal, a Side, a Snack / Sweet and a Drink. Sometimes more items as well. IF applicable, it will also include the FRH and an Accessory Packet. One MRE can have up to 20+ items included when opening the Accessory packet as well. That's a damn good deal for a Dead world. An insane amount of time and work went into making this mod. I mostly did it because I am a true MRE lover, and this is something that I have wanted to do for a very long time. All items are completely custom. The color schemes will be off here and there, but 95% of the items will be correct, and everything is 100% functional. Now, understand please, this mod contains over 700 items split across all MREs, and I did put in a lot of effort to make everything custom, to be unique and have never-seen-before items. No loose spawns to clutter the world, except a few medical items, like the Water Straw, Superwater, and medicines to help you survive. All food items will only be found in the MREs, nowhere else. So no, there will be no unnecessary clutter taking over spawn locations. I will continue working on it to make sure everything stays in good working order, and to update items to make sure they stay unique. From time to time I will add new MREs / items as well. Keep your rations dry, your matches lit, and your eyes on the horizon. May your water be boiled, your seal stay airtight, and your calories stay high. Peel carefully, eat well, and live to scavenge another day. May your next pouch be freeze-dried gourmet and your heater pad never fail. Left you the last pouch from my haul. It’s mostly hardtack and bitter root paste, but it’ll keep your belly from screaming across the next stretch of badlands. Watch your back out there.
