description: Important warning! This version is provided as-is and is not currently under active development. Reuploaded with full permission from the original creator, who has officially passed World Decay on to the community as an open-source project. Modding always comes with risks. Managing your mod load order, troubleshooting conflicts and backing up saves is your own responsibility. I cannot guarantee performance or take responsibility for any save/game issues. Note: I’m just a fan of the original creator who was given these files to share. The code itself remains completely untouched from the original release. Please understand that I'm just another player and workshop user like you, not a developer. I would love to learn how to mod myself, but right now I have zero skill. In the future, as I learn more, I might take a crack at maintaining and updating the mod. For now, I'm just happy to keep the files available for everyone. I'm focused on learning the basics and plan to work on smaller projects first before ever attempting anything on this scale. The original creator was an actual programmer and I'm nowhere near that skill level. I want to learn actual modding the real way without using AI as a shortcut. Because of that, building up the technical skills needed for a project this size will be a long process if I ever decide to focus on it. What is this mod? World Decay overrides the base map appearance to show years of urban decay. When each map chunk loads, the mod runs its generators procedurally: vegetation (trees, bushes, grass, vines), structural decay (cracks, burned walls, broken doors and windows, bent fences), trash and barricades. It keeps a persistent chunk cache to skip already visited areas and a batched dispatcher to avoid lag spikes. It includes cleaning tools and full sandbox control over every element. It is a work in progress, so you may run into bugs, unexpected behavior or performance issues. We are not professional modders, just players doing our best to build something good. Key features Vegetation system: Trees, bushes, grass and vines with configurable percentages via sandbox. Urban decay: Cracked roads, burned walls, broken doors and windows, bent and broken fences. Barricades: Leftover barricades from people who held out and lost, scattered across the map. Trash and debris: Piled-up garbage left behind by years of abandonment. Cleaning system: Right-click menu to remove vegetation and clear areas for rebuilding. Full sandbox customization: Every element can be tuned, enabled or disabled. Performance notice Important: This mod changes world generation heavily and adds a large number of objects to every loaded chunk. As a result, it may negatively impact performance on lower-end systems. This is expected given how Project Zomboid handles object rendering, and is not a problem with the mod. First load: You may notice some lag during the first few seconds after loading in, while the mod generates vegetation and objects across all visible chunks. Performance will stabilize once the first pass completes. Recommendations: Allocate more RAM to the game if you can. Lower vegetation percentages in sandbox options if you experience lag. In multiplayer, host and server specs matter a lot. Credits Texture Packs: Manik_Goblyn - Manik's a Decade Later textures. If any texture pack author wants their work removed from this mod, it will be taken down on request. Contributions are welcome. Anyone who has access to the source code of what used to be "World Decay" can upload it, modify it or do whatever they want with it. It belongs to the community and to whoever wants to maintain it. You do not need to give credit to me or to anyone else. Supported languages English (EN) Español / Spanish (ES) Deutsch / German (DE) Português Brasileiro / Brazilian Portuguese (PT-BR) Revive: Okijiu Русский / Russian (RU) Load order priority: This mod should sit as close to the TOP of your load order as possible (use the Auto-Sort feature or move it up manually). If other mods overwrite the same world tiles, the load order decides which one wins. Example load order (Mod IDs): Mods=errorMagnifier;WorldDecay;ModExample1;ModExample2; In the in-game mod manager: 1. Error Magnifier 2. WorldDecay 3. Your map mods 4. Other gameplay mods Mod information Workshop ID: 3782424006 Mod ID: WorldDecay Texture Pack ID: WorldDecay_Maniks_Textures Game Version: Build 42.20+ Save-safe: Yes - can be added or removed mid-save. What it does Trees, grass and bushes sway with the wind, from light breeze to storm. I built this for immersion: in vanilla the vegetation stands still most of the time, and the optional "Wind Sprite Effects" only shear sprites between random poses. Wind Sway replaces the animation and the renderer: Trees bend from the trunk up. Leaves flutter, broad crowns move as a block, evergreens as a stiff cone. Scaled to tree size, jumbos included. Wind has a direction and gusts: crowns lean with the rain, gusts roll through the forest, storms bend crowns over and hold them. Sway in still air: two sliders, plants and trees. Weather adds on top, 0 = vanilla wind only. Every plant moves: bushes and all wind plants, stiffer ones a little less. Render-only: water, sounds and aiming stay on the real weather. Own renderer: grass and trees drawn in batches instead of one draw call per sprite. Options → Mods → Wind Sway, no other setup: the mod turns the game's wind effects on by itself and ignores the vanilla "Wind Sprite Effects" option while it runs. Turn the mod off and your vanilla setting applies again. Requirements PZ Build 42.20 or later ZombieBuddy, one-time install for any Java mod On first launch ZombieBuddy asks whether to load Wind Sway's JAR, tick Allow. Compatibility Safe to add or remove mid-save, the mod stores nothing in the save. Multiplayer / dedicated servers Wind Sway is client-side: the server runs none of its code, each player only sees the effect on their own screen. Two things still have to be in place: On the server: both mods go into the server's .ini, so joining clients download and enable them (keep your other entries, separate with semicolons; 3619862853 = ZombieBuddy, 3782670683 = Wind Sway): Mods=ZombieBuddy;WindSway WorkshopItems=3619862853;3782670683 On every player's PC: ZombieBuddy's one-time setup from its Workshop page. The server can't do that part for you. FAQ What does it cost in FPS? Some, anything that moves is drawn every frame. Wind Sway batches it and stays well below vanilla's wind option; tree-heavy areas even run faster than vanilla on my machine. Why ZombieBuddy, can't this work without it? No. The wind effects and the renderer are Java, Lua can't reach them. Options → Mods → Wind Sway says "Java part did not load"? ZombieBuddy isn't installed, or you declined the prompt. Check the install steps on its Workshop page. To undo a decline, edit %USERPROFILE%\.zombie_buddy\mod_approvals.json: in the "id": "WindSway" block flip "decision": false to true, restart PZ. Added it to an existing save and nothing changed? Subscribing doesn't switch a mod on in saves that already exist. Load Game → select the save → "Choose Mods..." → tick ZombieBuddy and Wind Sway. description: Brew your own alcohol from your crops - ferment in a barrel over real in-game days, distill spirits, age Korean damgeumju, and even refine biofuel. Finished vanilla drinks (beer, wine, cider, whiskey, vodka, brandy) are the actual vanilla items. How to Brew 1. Make your base liquid (crafting menu, Cooking tab - any empty glass bottle or jar works as the vessel): Wort: 2 barley/wheat + 2 hops + yeast + water -> beer Rice mash: rice + yeast + water -> makgeolli Grain mash: 3 corn/barley/rye + yeast + water -> whiskey (distilled) Potato mash: 4 potatoes + yeast + water -> vodka (distilled) Sugar mash: 2 sugar + yeast + water -> moonshine or ethanol (distilled) Grape / apple / fruit must: 5 fruit + sugar -> wine / cider / fruit wine Honey must: 2 honey + yeast + water -> mead 2. Build a Brewing Barrel (build menu, Farming tab: hammer + 4 planks + 4 nails). Right-click it, Start Fermenting, and load your jars - one at a time or all at once, up to 10. You can keep adding jars of the same kind to a running barrel; each addition ferments on its own timer. 3. Wait real in-game days - makgeolli 6, beer/cider 7, fruit wine 10, wine/mead 14 (sandbox-adjustable down to 1 day). Right-click the barrel to check progress; higher Farming skill reads more detail. Collect when ready - but don't forget it: brews left too long spoil and must be dumped (sandbox toggleable). 4. Distill spirits - build a Still (Welding tab, Metalwelding 3: blowtorch + welding rods + metal drum + 2 pipes + 2 small metal sheets). Click it to open its recipe window. Every distillation burns a fire source plus a log or charcoal: soju from 2 makgeolli bottles, whiskey / vodka / moonshine from their mash jars, brandy from wine. 5. Sour it into vinegar - load finished wine or cider back into the barrel and let it ferment a second time (7 days). You get vanilla vinegar, which vanilla pickling recipes accept as-is, so a bad wine year still feeds the pantry. Vinegar never spoils in the barrel - it is already the soured product. 6. Age damgeumju (Korean fruit-infused liquor) - seal an empty jar + lid + 3 fruits + sugar + soju or vodka. Wait (10 days by default), then right-click the jar to open it. Acts as a mild folk medicine: eases pain and colds. 7. Refine biofuel - distill 2 sugar mash jars into a jar of ethanol, then refine it at the still into a jar of real petrol. Fuels vehicles and generators directly, or pour it into gas cans. Features Custom-made barrel and still tiles, drawn to match the vanilla art style Brewing grants Farming XP; makgeolli gives slight fatigue relief Sandbox options: fermentation time scale, damgeumju aging days, spoilage toggle, moonshine sickness toggle EN / KO / FR translations included Works in singleplayer and multiplayer (server-authoritative since 1.0.1) Pairs well with Fruit Farming (fruits + rice for the full farm-to-bottle loop). Built for Build 42.20. Workshop ID: 3782769048 Mod ID: HomeBrewing

description: Stops inventory selections deselecting themselves. This one's annoying as hell. I haven't been able to reproduce the bug on the spot, so testing this fix has consisted of me just running around with items in my inventory selected for a while. It hasn't happened to me so far, so if it does for you, please let me know. What's broken Project Zomboid rebuilds the inventory list constantly: whenever an item ages, gets wet, or a container changes. Each rebuild saves your selection and puts it back afterwards. Putting it back is where it goes wrong: the game restores a single item where it should restore the whole row. The next rebuild then can't find anywhere to put that item, and your selection disappears. Every row in the inventory is a stack internally, even one holding a single item, so this hits regardless of quantity. Compatibility Build 42. Singleplayer and multiplayer. Safe to add or remove mid-save. Replaces ISInventoryPane:restoreSelection(), so it will conflict with any other mod that replaces that same function. Inventory overhaul mods are the ones to watch. Found a bug? Post in the comments. A log excerpt from Zomboid/console.txt makes it much easier to fix. Workshop ID: 3782920935 Mod ID: NicksInventorySelectionFix

Repeated vehicle and foot traffic gradually wears natural ground into persistent dirt roads and walking paths. Bushes are crushed before removal, maintained tracks suppress obstructive regrowth, and abandoned routes slowly fade. Tested for B42.20 single-player and multiplayer. Safe to add to existing saves and servers, but take a backup. This mod contains no custom assets, it uses the vanilla sprites and tile set. But once those sprites are placed in the world, they are part of the map and will remain if the mod is removed. A "Cleanup" option is planned. To get rid of paths for now, turn off Vehicle and Player Traffic and set erosion high (10), and they will fade away on their own over time. For bug reports, please open a discussion thread, describe it as fully as you can. If a screenshot might help please include. Background On the server I play on, we had a base at the Lakehouse / McCoy estate. Which sucks to get in and out of. So we lumberjacked our way to the road north for a faster exit. But then, the saplings grew. And then they grew on the vanilla dirt drive way too. And so this mod was born. Options The following can be independently enabled or disabled: Vehicle paths - On by default. Player paths - On by default. Bush destruction by vehicles - On by default. The first hit damages the bush, the second destroys. Grass destruction by vehicles - Off by default. The first hit damages the grass, the second destroys. This removes the sound of driving over grass and makes for nicer looking roads, but it's a little more destructive so I left it off by default. By default, a vehicle must pass over a location 6 times before a visible path appears. A walking player passes over 60 times. Adjust the multipliers for wear and erosion for each for faster or slower rates. The minimum speed needed to destroy bushes or grass is also configurable. Known issues Dirt roads may appear on top of concrete pads or wooden floors you've built. This doesn't destroy the floor you built, it just gets layered on top of it. This will be fixed in the future. The edges of a dirt road may be visible through snow. Some might call that a feature. Plans Planned changes upcoming. Version numbers to be determined, things may be bundled together, just depends how things go. 0.5.0: Smoothing/blending improvements for the paths. 0.6.0: Option to entirely hide paths while still tracking vehicle traffic and wear to prevent overgrowth. Option to pour gravel on a square to prevent the dirt road from eroding with disuse. "Lock in" the road. Option to "Cleanup" the mod. It will disable all the features and begin removing mod data whenever encountered, to return the world to normal, if someone so chooses. 0.?.0: Optional Snow destruction/tracks Optional Animal and/or zombie path wearing Erosion Rates Roads and walking paths gradually lose wear when they are not being used. Higher Erosion Rate values make tracks disappear faster; lower values preserve them longer. Times below are measured in in-game days and assume the route receives no new traffic. Visual Stage Breakdown At Erosion Rate 1.0, a fully developed 30-wear route fades through its visual stages as follows: Vehicle and foot traffic have separate Erosion Rate settings. When both rates are equal, the table applies directly. Mixed-use routes with different vehicle and foot erosion settings will decay according to how much wear came from each source. Any renewed traffic adds wear and can maintain or rebuild the route. Workshop/Mod ID Workshop ID: 3782929173 Mod ID: ProjectDirtroad

This mod adds more atmosphere to Project Zomboid with dynamic visible breath in cold weather and realistic cigarette smoke during smoking. This is my first Project Zomboid mod, and I have tried to keep it lightweight, unobtrusive, and compatible with both the base game and other mods. The first is Cold Breath. When the temperature becomes sufficiently low, your character will produce visible breath while breathing. The breath is not simply a static texture. It uses an animated particle system with several behaviors: 1) Multiple animated breath-cloud frames. 2) Smooth appearance and disappearance. 3) Breath frequency changes depending on temperature. 4) In mild cold, breath appears less frequently. 5) In extreme cold, breathing becomes much more noticeable. 6) Breathing frequency changes with character activity. 7) Walking, running, and sprinting increase breathing frequency. 8) Newly created breath remains attached to the character briefly before drifting away. 9) Breath reacts to wind direction and strength. 10) Strong wind can stretch the cloud and carry it away faster. 11) Larger clouds gradually break apart into smaller particles. 12) Breath does not appear indoors. 13) Breath does not appear while the character is inside a vehicle. The system is designed to fit the visual art-style of Project Zomboid while adding subtle environmental atmosphere without changing gameplay mechanics. The second is Cigarette Smoke. The mod adds visible smoke when your character is smoking. The cigarette-smoke system is based on the smoking detection system created by @movin in the Cigarette Smoke mod. Special thanks to @movin for creating the original cigarette-smoke system and allowing its implementation as part of this project. The cigarette smoke has its own particle system and works independently from the cold-breath system. Smoke appears during actual puffs rather than simply appearing because the character has a cigarette equipped. The effects are designed primarily to improve immersion and Cold Breath is especially noticeable: 1) At night. 2) During winter. 3) In freezing temperatures. 4) During long journeys outdoors. 5) During intense physical activity. Cigarette smoke remains independent of the ambient temperature, making it a separate visual effect rather than another part of the cold-breath system. Performance: The mod uses a limited number of active particles and does not continuously generate unlimited visual effects. Both systems use their own lightweight particle and rendering logic. The goal is to provide additional atmosphere without unnecessarily affecting performance. Multiplayer: The mod is designed for Build 42.20.3 and is prepared for multiplayer. Most of the visual effects are handled client-side, so they should not create unnecessary network traffic. Compatibility: The mod is designed to interfere as little as possible with existing game systems. Cold breath and cigarette smoke operate as separate systems and do not replace Project Zomboid's core temperature, survival, or smoking mechanics. The mod should not cause compatibility issues with other mods. However, compatibility with third-party mods that directly modify the same smoking actions or related systems cannot be guaranteed in every possible combination. My mod doesnt work alongside original Cigarette Smoke mod from @movin because our mods are using the same systems BUT it works with True Smoking, thanks to @movin Credits: Special thanks to @movin for the Cigarette Smoke mod that was based on mine mod and for the smoking-detection system used to implement cigarette smoke in this project. Thanks as well to everyone who tests the mod, reports bugs, and helps improve the project. Good luck and remember - "This is how you died" Workshop ID: 3783135152 Mod ID: ColdBreath

Neat Lockpicking Break into locked doors, windows, and vehicles with three minigames. UI built on NeatUI Framework. Lockpicking — pin minigame on doors and vehicle doors. Crowbar — skill-check on doors, garages, windows, and car doors. Hotwire — wire minigame from the driver seat. Replaces vanilla hotwire. Skill books Lockpicking I–V and a magazine spawn in the world. How It Works Lockpicking Right-click a locked door, or use the vehicle radial (V) on a locked car door. Push pins from below, in the correct order. A wrong pin can snap the pick. Handmade picks break in one mistake; store lockpicks last several uses. You need the Burglar profession/trait, or to have read Lockpicking Basics. Crowbar and hotwire are not gated. Anyone with the right tool can try. Burglars get a Lockpicking XP boost. They do not start with Lockpicking levels. Crowbar Press SPACE when the marker is in the yellow or green zone. Miss the zone and the attempt fails. Strength sizes the zones. Fitness and stamina decide the cost. You cannot start while exhausted. Works on doors, garages, windows, and vehicle doors. Security doors are harder. Hotwire Sit in the driver's seat of a vehicle that is not already hotwired. Unscrew the cover, cut the wires, join the two matching battery wires, then touch the starter. Wrong connections can spark, shock you, drain the battery, or trigger an alarm. After the battery pair is joined, Test wires helps identify cables. Each test drains the car battery. 1 Spark = AlarmCable 2 Sparks = StarterCable 3 Sparks = ShockCable Items Lockpicking Basics — magazine. Unlocks lockpicking and the handmade pick recipe. Lockpick — several uses. Handmade Lockpick — craft from a paperclip and a screwdriver. Breaks on a snap. Lockpicking I–V — skill books, same rules as vanilla books. Magazine and books spawn in bookstores, libraries, and similar loot. Lockpicks show up in bathrooms, salons, and tool storage. Requirements NeatUI Framework — load before this mod. Compatibility Build 42 Singleplayer and multiplayer Translations English, Polish, Portuguese (BR), Russian, Spanish, Spanish (AR), French, Ukrainian. description: Livestock Panel Plus Turns the livestock zone panel (right-click inside the zone → Check Zone) into a status table for your whole herd. Each animal's row — just a name in vanilla — gains columns for hunger, thirst, mood, health and more. In vanilla, checking on an animal means opening a separate Info window for each one, then hunting through it for the line you need. This mod puts every animal's state side by side in one table — and lets you tend them right from it. Along the way it also smooths a few small rough edges around animal care. It only shows information vanilla already displays on the Animal Info panel; anything your Animal Care level does not reveal yet stays hidden in the table too. Update v1.2 Configurable status dot colors — Mod Options now has color pickers for all 8 status colors, plus a reset-to-default button. Adjust them if the defaults are hard to tell apart Table and tabs Four column tabs — Care / Harvest / Breeding / Class — plus a Zone tab for the zone itself Status cells are colored squares — green = fine / yellow = attention / orange = bad / red = critical / cyan = ready to harvest or a breeding chance / dark cyan = harvestable but low yield / gray = not applicable. Each color can be changed in Mod Options Cells and column headers show tooltips with the same wording as vanilla Columns with no applicable animal are hidden (a chicken-only zone shows no Milk column) The list shows 11 rows instead of vanilla's 5, with the window size unchanged A species icon sits next to each name, and names are tinted light blue for males, pink for females and yellow for young — so custom-named animals stay recognizable at a glance Your Animal Care level and the progress toward the next level are always visible in the header. Higher levels unlock more columns (e.g. pregnancy, mating, weight) and finer stages for mood and health. The Zone tab lists what each level reveals Sorting and filtering Click a column header to sort — once to bring the animals in the worst state to the top, again to reverse, a third time to reset Click a cell to filter the list down to animals with that value; click the same cell again — or the Clear button that appears — to remove the filter The default order groups animals by species, then breed, then male / female / young. A Mod Option restores the vanilla order (by name) Age sorts by life stage (baby → adult → geriatric); weight sorts by the actual number Tend animals from the table Right-click a row to Milk, Shear, Pet, Give Water or Feed — fewer clicks than the vanilla routine of walking up to the animal and opening the radial menu. Everything runs through vanilla's own actions; no checks or effects are changed Your character walks up to the animal and performs the action the vanilla way — nothing happens from a distance When you carry only one suitable container or tool, the action runs directly without a submenu Menu conditions match the vanilla right-click menu (e.g. Give Water is grayed out when you carry no water container) Give Water and Feed on the radial menu The animal radial menu (hold V) offers Milk and Shear, but not Give Water or Feed. This mod adds both, using the same conditions as the right-click menu. Untainted water containers are used first. Zone tab Shows the zone information (size, troughs, food, water, roof area and more) in two columns One row per hutch, with each building's dirt level and egg count; the values change color when cleaning or collecting is due Hover a row to highlight the matching objects in the world — troughs inside buildings show through the walls One row per composter, too — compost level, contents weight and worm count. Only fresh worms multiply, so rotten ones are shown separately in gray parentheses Also shows how much dung is lying on the ground, so the collect-and-compost loop fits on one screen Rename the zone from here (or by right-clicking the panel title) And more Picking up dung now has an animation and a sound — in vanilla your character just stands still until the work is done. Duration and yield are unchanged Animal Care XP earned by tending animals appears above your character's head, in the same style as crafting (singleplayer only) Lambs hop with joy once you pet, water or feed them — an existing vanilla animation you rarely get to see, and only lambs have it in vanilla. It has no effect on any game value Mod Options Sort order — group by species, breed and sex (default: on; off restores the vanilla name order) XP display above your head on/off (default: on) Status dot colors — change each of the 8 colors individually (with a reset-to-default button) Compatibility Supports: Build 42 Extends the vanilla panel instead of replacing it No game values or rules are changed; every action the mod triggers is vanilla's own Safe to add to or remove from an existing save Languages: English, Japanese and French (French translation provided by Kallikah; a few strings remain in English). Most terms in the table reuse vanilla's own translations, so they follow your game language Multiplayer: tested on a co-op host. Zone renaming syncs. Only the XP display above your head does not appear in multiplayer (the vanilla event never fires there; the XP itself is granted normally) If you run into a problem, please let me know in the comments. mod_name: Knox County Smokes - Immersive Tobacco Overhaul [B42]
description: Knox County Smokes Kentucky, 1993 - the tobacco heart of America. When the end came, this county left behind more than the dead: cartons still on the shelves, half-smoked packs in nightstands, butts never stubbed out, and one warehouse nobody ever came back for. A complete, lore-friendly tobacco expansion for Build 42.20+. How big is this, really? Before "16 brands" misleads you into thinking this adds 16 items - that is just the first shelf: 163 new items, every one with its own inventory art, 3D world model, and written description. The full ledger: 96 commercial brand items (16 brands, each with singles, packs, cartons, cases and two kinds of branded butts); 11 cigars, cigarillos and loose tobaccos (the cigars leave their own butts); 22 hidden and legendary items; 21 pieces of recipe literature (growing manuals, blending guides, torn process pages, forbidden manuscripts, a county dossier); 5 ashtrays; 4 assorted-pack containers; 2 street butts; matches and a lighter. That adds up to exactly 163 - feel free to audit us. A dozen interlocking systems: brand effects, loyalty tiers, a smoking ledger, effect data cards, butt scavenging, ashtray interactions, smoldering embers and fire risk, fire-source choice, a dedicated foraging focus, and a full seed-to-cigarette production line. 41 sandbox options and 10 fully translated languages, single-player and multiplayer alike. Sixteen original brands From the local names on the gas station shelf (Knox Standard, Bluegrass Select, Old Mill Reds...) through the mainstream labels to the premium stock kept behind the counter (Golden Crane, Black Oak Reserve, Eastern Star...), every brand ships singles, packs, cartons, cases and its own discarded butts. Add Coal Creek cigars, San Cielo cigarillos, hand-rolling and menthol shag, and Old Homestead chew. Four everyday ashtrays are scattered through bars, diners and homes - the fifth? Try your luck on Spiffo's turf. Every item carries its own description - plus one line of house wit on its hover card. The crane on the Golden Crane pack was drawn from a goose. Nobody ever noticed. Smoking, done properly Brand effects - every label has a personality: the steadying one, the nerve-settling one, the boredom-killer, the painkiller. Smoking while seated earns a little extra. Effect data cards - hover to see the real numbers. By default a brand reveals its data only after you have actually smoked it - a smoker's knowledge is earned by the lungful. Brand loyalty - smokers have their brand. Stick with one and its duration and strength climb through tiered ranks; commercial, hidden and legendary labels each walk their own ladder. The smoking ledger - a collection book of every brand you have tasted, with loyalty ranks. Some slots just say "???". Ashtrays and butts - usable ashtrays, embers that glow in the dark, the choice to stomp or snuff, and a restrained fire-risk system. Naturally spawned world clutter is always extinguished. Butt scavenging - when all else fails, butts plus rolling paper make a smoke. It works. It is not pleasant. Choose your fire - matches, a lighter, or the special one? A "Smoke using..." menu puts it in your hands. No more wasting the irreplaceable. From seed to forbidden manuscript 1.0 ships a complete native B42 production line: grow and harvest tobacco, find growing manuals and blending guides, and reproduce all sixteen commercial brands. Go deeper: assemble paired process and ratio fragments into complete manuscripts and craft five hidden cigarettes that never spawn as finished loot - Night Watch, Silent Hunt, the Old Physician, the Ashen Communion, and Beyond County. Far stronger than anything on a shelf. The bill comes afterward. A county that smokes Spawn rates mirror real 1993 Kentucky: about 33% of male and 27% of female zombies were smokers, still carrying their half-used packs - roughly one in ten unopened, and the ones who fell near a store likely just bought theirs. Nightstands, office desks, diner counters, glove boxes and trunks all show the traces of a smoking county; a shop's backroom stocks what the shop sells; store shelves stay factory-sealed. Search mode gets a dedicated Tobacco focus - craving needs no training, available at level 0. KCS manages its own spawn rates by default: the official presets' brutal global rarity cannot erase cigarettes here - and if you set global loot to Abundant, tobacco rises with it. Collection and legend The rare Spiffo's Alibi set - pack, commemorative lighter, ashtray, carton and case - waits for a completionist, and completing it does something. About that ever-smiling raccoon, the county talks: some swear on their lives that his cigarettes cure the sickness. Medically speaking, utter nonsense, and we decline to comment. Then again - when has Spiffo ever lied to anyone? There is also a brand set aside for the last hours, which leaves something worth keeping when it is gone. And the farther legend: each world is visited, at most once, by a certain something. It looks wrong - as if the world forgot to texture it, a harsh magenta-and-black checkerboard. That is not a missing texture. Do not report it. Some things were never meant to be rendered. If you find it, it is yours. Your save, your rules 41 sandbox options across three tidy pages: spawn multipliers up to 10x, effect strength and duration, loyalty pacing, partial-pack rules, scavenging cost, ashtray capacity, sitting bonus, a packaging weight discount or strict bookkeeping, a flavor text toggle - even the odds of the thing. Nearly every mechanic can be tuned or turned off. The defaults state our design intent; the options respect that your save is yours. Compatibility and a promise Optional True Smoking 42.15+ integration: multi-puff smoking, put-down-and-resume, per-puff effects, KCS brands preserved throughout. No dependency required. Joins existing saves cleanly. Single-player and multiplayer (server-authoritative with full client sync). 10 languages, fully translated: English, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Russian, Spanish, Portuguese, German, French, Polish, Japanese. Every code entry point is defensively fenced. House rule: whatever breaks in your 200-mod load order, it will not be Knox County Smokes. FAQ New save needed? - No. Subscribe and play; everything folds into your world naturally. What about vanilla cigarettes? - Naturally spawned vanilla tobacco is gently replaced with KCS equivalents (sandbox-optional); vanilla items, recipes and crafting chains remain fully intact. Mod conflicts? - KCS only appends; it never overwrites or removes vanilla distributions or items, and its error fencing keeps other mods' failures from dragging it down. I found a magenta-checkered pack - is it broken? - Scroll up to Collection and legend. It is not broken. Congratulations. Why can I see all the numbers? - The data card has three sandbox modes: flavour only, unlock-by-smoking (default), show everything. Mystery run or wiki run - your call. Problems? Leave a comment - we fix fast. Smoking is bad for your health. Though honestly, in Knox County, it does not crack your top ten causes of death. Workshop ID: 3783725847 Mod ID: KnoxCountySmokes

description: The Darkness Is Coming returns for B42! Answers for FAQs Mod is tested only in Singleplayer. This mod works as intended as of 42.20. There may be some little bugs here and there. But the mod works! If it doesn't, you either have a mod conflict or you're doing something wrong. Features Highly customizable experience through Sandbox Options! Adds periods of darkness in Knox County that could go on for days! Adds thick fog during the darkness. Adds ambient sirens and spooked crows that go off to warn of an imminent Darkness Event in handpicked locations in the map! Zombies slowly become sprinters when the darkness falls. Use the Automated Emergency Broadcast System to get warnings and lore about the darkness. [NEW] Adds snow (snow melts and doesn't stay), similar to Silent Hill 1's otherworld. [NEW] The world transforms during the darkness. Trash, blood, grime, overgrowth. You might have to walk some distance away and then walk back if trash and blood is not cleaned up at event end. This is usually needed if you reloaded a save. [NEW] Light sources are very important. Staying in the darkness without any light source (indoors or outdoors) will increase your stress and damage your health, and can even kill you. This gives the player a reason to maintain a light source even in their base. AI Disclosure I am not a huge fan of AI but it is the reality, and it saves time if used well. I have to use it for my professional career and it comes in handy sometimes. I mainly used AI for code reviews and fixing obscure bugs that I encountered by feeding it the decompiled game source code. I also used AI for the radio broadcasts! I suck at creative writing. I was always into math and science, not much into literature. I have a thread about the radio broadcasts and I would love if some creative mind/s would collaborate and create broadcasts that actually fit the lore of the mod and game. I COULD do it myself but it will take me a lot of time and thinking, and frankly they won't be good. I can also spend the time working on other projects. Sorry about this. I understand some of the lines seem a bit cringe and look and sound very AI generated. Lore "The Darkness Is Coming!" became a popular cry for help, with whoever is still alive to experience this supernatural event. Parts of the world started experiencing periods of total darkness. Black clouds would cover the skies. Clouds thick enough that they block completely block out the sun! The air would turn foul. An unexplained, and sometimes hazardous, thick fog would also set in. Scientists started recommending the use of gas masks to stop this anomalous atmospheric matter from invading human bodies. But unfortunately they couldn't find any scientific reasoning behind these events, leading everyone to believe that this event is of a supernatural nature. They did come up with a warning system that could detect traces of this anomalous matter. Authorities set up a number of sensor and sirens to warn everyone about this hazardous phenomenon. A year later, the Knox Event happened. These are truly the end times. Access to the Automated Emergency Broadcast System became essential to survival. Future Improvements Implement non-AI generated radio broadcasts Fix any bugs reported by the community Test in MP Credits Thanks to >>> this guy <<< for copying my B41 mod and creating an AI slop version of it, without even giving me credit. I mainly created this mod out of love for this game and community, but some spite was fuelling the process too. Thanks to the PZ Modding Community for help. Thanks to all the people that left suggestions of possible features. If your requests were not added, I can assure you I did take them in consideration and there's no ruling out that I won't implement them. Thanks to TIS for this highly moddable game and also to Team Silent that create the franchise that was an inspiration for this mod. description: Project Parkour Project Parkour expands movement in Project Zomboid with a dedicated Parkour skill, new traversal mechanics, and a large collection of animations for both vanilla and entirely new actions. The mod does not turn a fresh survivor into a skilled runner. New moves and mechanics are unlocked through progression, consume endurance, and require suitable conditions. Main Features Randomized vaults/climb animations - separate animation pools for walking, running, and sprinting. Every animation unique not only visually they have different speed and distance. Window Dive - You can sprint to a window for a fast and stylish dive instead of breaking it first. Great move if you trying to escape unwelcoming friends. Directional Dodge - a dedicated dodge button with directional dodges! Outside combat stance it performs a dodge in direction your character looking. While aiming(combat stance), movement input selects from direction (WASD and where character looking) forward, backward, left, or right. Every direction have their own animations. Free Jump - An actual jump in Project Zomboid! Jump anything (that makes sense). Distance depends on movement: 2 tiles while standing, 3 while running, and 4 while sprinting. Free Jump can clear low fences, furniture, rocks, small stationary cars, rooftop gaps, and roof edges. Full walls, tall fences, trucks, and other oversized obstacles cannot be jumped. Wall Run Up — run vertically up a wall and climb onto a clear roof one level above. Landings and recovery — fast fall rolls and get-up animations. Progression The mod adds a 10-level Parkour skill. XP is earned by actually moving through the world: low- and high-fence traversal, windows, Free Jump, Wall Run, and genuine sprinting. Every 30 tiles travelled while sprinting awards 5 XP. Built-in anti-farm rules reduce rewards from repeatedly using the same obstacle. Move to another part of your route to earn the full reward again. Level 1 — basic parkour animations: controlled vaulting, window traversal, and fall/stumble recovery. Level 2 — the full 2–4 tile Free Jump system, jumps over small vehicles, landing rolls, Dash Vault, and Corkscrew Vault. Level 3 — four-direction dodge system and the low-fence Dive Roll. Level 4 — sprint window vaulting, new sprint vaults, and an advanced high-fence animation. Level 5 — Front Flip, Backflip Vault, advanced dodge variants, and a high-fence Front Flip. Levels 6–7 — mastery bonuses that gradually reduce endurance costs. Level 8 — Wall Run Up by default, plus further endurance improvements. Levels 9–10 — maximum stamina efficiency for Wall Run, jumps, and dodges. You may find that high levels quite empty content wise and you are correct. I'm planning to add more mechanics and animation later on. Controls The Dodge, Forward Jump, and Climb onto Roof keys are unassigned by default. Configure them under: Options → Mods → Parkour General Info Manual jumps mechanics validate their route and require a safe landing area. Parkour mechanics are unavailable while overloaded. Low endurance and serious injuries may also block specific moves. Dodges do not grant invulnerability and have no I-frames. Mods that replace the same player AnimSet branches may conflict. Higher compatibility priorities are included for common animation replacements. Every animation can be toggled in sandbox settings if you don't like specific one. If there is no alternative - default vanilla animation will play or no animation at all if vanilla does not support it I'm not 3D animator and most of the animations were retargeted to PZ human rig. So some animations will vary in quality. You will definitely see where is mine 🙃 ❗You should really check the videos if you didn't already. Build/MP ✅42.20 Singleplayer 🟡Multiplayer There are currently some sync issues in MP. These will require more time to fix, but the core mechanics are working fine. description: Traits As Skills — Skill based Trait Progression System Say goodbye to static traits. Your character's strengths, flaws, and fears now adapt directly to how you survive. Traits As Skills completely overhauls character progression by adding a dedicated Traits tab to the Character Info window. Gain XP, level up, and watch your survivor dynamically evolve through real-time gameplay actions. Philosophy This mod follows a simple principle: progress, not regression. You are in a zombie apocalypse — surviving always means getting stronger. Every day you stay alive, every threat you overcome, every wound you heal makes your survivor tougher, sharper, and more capable. Weakening over time is not how survival works. Get stronger, or die. That doesn't mean everything only goes up. Some spectra do include negative XP, but the mod never abuses the idea of weakening you just for skipping a meal or a drink — overcoming a genuinely hard situation while hungry and thirsty would hardly make anyone weaker. Neglect your character badly enough and negative traits can still appear, but it is never abusive. Features Traits as True Skills — Track your progress visually with dedicated XP bars, levels, and evolving stages for every trait. Earned Character Evolution — Earn XP through organic survival actions. Kill zombies to build Courage (+5 XP) or simply survive day by day. Dynamic Trait Transformation — Overcome your flaws or unlock new advantages as you progress (e.g., conquer Cowardly or cure Agoraphobia over time). Modder-Friendly Open Framework — Designed from the ground up as a flexible foundation for the community. Easily hook into the API to build your own custom evolutive traits! Framework documentation: github.com/GersonRess/TAS_Docs UI & Inspection Hover to view detailed descriptions, prerequisites, and progression milestones for every trait in your list. description: This is a standalone conversion of the original "NotAlone - NPC Mod" made by tomura for the new, stable version of Project Zomboid (build 42). Since he gave permission to upload any modified versions of his mod I am posting it now, but I want to state it clear that this conversion only modifies the NotAlone mod to the newest versions of the game and it wouldn't be possible to make without the original, so thanks tomura. Link to the original mod (with description how it works, NOT REQUIRED to download): https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3720923377 Note: I highly recommend trying this conversion on a new save. I tested it for 2 days and it shouldn't had any gamebreaking bugs, but it's still early release and I can't guarantee it will work perfectly. It's also SINGLEPLAYER ONLY. IMPORTANT!!!: Due to changes in code with the build 42, this mod requires you to place one file manually in your Project Zomboid's steam folder. Unfortunately it's not possible to automate it. Without it all NPCs in the mod will be invisible and will probably also crash your game. Here is what to do, step by step: 1. After hitting "subscribe" and downloading this mod, locate the mod's folder. It should be located here on your PC: \Steam\steamapps\workshop\content\108600\[This mod steamworkshop's ID]. 2. Inside this folder go to \mods\Tom_NPC_NotAlone\JavaPatch. 3. Copy the "zombie" folder. 4. Go to your Project Zomboid's steam folder: Steam\steamapps\common\ProjectZomboid 5. Paste this "zombie" folder directly here. Do NOT post it inside some subfolder like "media". Paste it directly inside your "ProjectZomboid" folder, where your ProjectZomboid64.exe is located too. Why is it necessary? In short: I had to create the new IsoSurvivor class for this mod to work, and Project Zomboid can only load it when it's inside it's core files. More details are in mod's INSTALLATION.txt file. Adnotation: If you will ever verify your PZ files on Steam or there will be another hotfix update, there is a possibility that the "zombie" folder will be deleted and you will have to repeat this manual process again for this mod. List of known issues: 1. NPC is stuck inside a car. Solution: Approach the car's door next to which the NPC is sitting and try to enter it by pressing "e". Or you can just walk away, the NPC should eventually teleport to you. 2. NPC became invisible. Solution: Yeah it can unfortunately happen especially with older PCs due to VRAM problems. To fix that either send the NPC to your base and then recruit him to follow you again, or exit to menu and reload the save. You can also just ignore it if it doesn't bother you much, the NPC will still follow you, fight the zombies, give you it's occupation bonuses etc, just will be invisible. 3. Park Ranger foraging bonus doesn't work. Honestly I have no idea how to fix that, build 42 changed the foraging system and fixing that now would be quite a mess. Full transparency: I made that build 42 conversion with Claude Code's huge help. Update 1.2 log: -Fixed a critical bug where freezing, hunger and thirst was still applied to NPCs and could kill them over time. Now they should be dying only after being bitten or by bleeding to death during fight, just like in the original version. Update 1.1 log: -Fixed a bug where shared inventory with NPCs didn't worked and was causing many errors. -Fixed a bug where some NPC's occupation bonuses didn't worked (let me know in comments if some still doesn't work except the Park Ranger). Workshop ID: 3785948334 Mod ID: NotAlone_NPC

description: Traits As Skills — More Traits Integration This is not a final product. This addon exists as a reference example of the Traits As Skills framework, showing modders how to plug their own traits into the system. Traits As Skills - More Traits integrates the traits from More Traits (ToadTraits) into the Traits As Skills spectrum system. Your More Traits now show up in the Traits tab with their own XP bars, levels, and evolving stages, exactly like the vanilla traits. Is It Playable? Yes, completely. This addon is fully functional and works out of the box in singleplayer and multiplayer. You can play with it as any other mod: traits evolve, XP is earned, levels are applied, everything works. The only thing that marks it as a reference example is its support status: because it exists mainly to demonstrate the framework, it may not receive the same level of attention to feedback, balance, or updates as a full product. The code and features are complete and playable. Read This First This addon is a reference implementation, not a curated gameplay product. It showcases how to build evolutive traits on top of the Traits As Skills framework. Its real purpose is a complete, copy-pasteable example for modders: spectra definitions, XP actions, server-side hooks, translations, and the framework's extension points. The set of traits covered and their XP tuning are intentionally simple and may not be balanced for serious play. What It Adds New evolutive spectra for weapon masteries, mental health, and survivalism built from More Traits. Handicap traits mapped into existing vanilla spectra (e.g. health, courage, body, detection, hands). Per-weapon-type kill tracking (blunt, blade, axe, spear, firearm, stomp) feeding the mastery spectra. Condition-based passives such as being wounded, driving sickness, and mental distress. Scope New spectra (created by this addon) Nimble — Flexible, Fitted (4-7, 8-10) — Nimble skill. Spear — Pro Spear, Prowess Spear (4-7, 8-10) — Spear skill. Blunt Mastery — Lead Foot, Gordanite, Blunt Twirl, Prowess Blunt (2-3, 4-5, 6-7, 8-10) — Blunt / Small Blunt / stomp kills. Blade Mastery — Practiced Swordsman, Blade Twirl, Prowess Blade (4-6, 7-8, 9-10) — Axe / Long Blade / Small Blade kills. Ranged Mastery — Anti Gun, Prowess Guns, Gun Specialist, Terminator (0-2, 6-8, 8-10, 9-10) — Firearm kills + shooting. Survivalism — Immunocompromised, Unwavering, Super Immune (0-3, 7-8, 9-10) — Bandaging, suturing, wounds, surviving. Mental Health — Depressive, Burned, Blissful (0-2, 0-3, 7-10) — Mood-based passives. Bands added to existing vanilla spectra Movement — Noodle Legs, Gimp, Fast, Evasive (0-4, 0-4, 7-10, 9-10). Detection — Quiet, Incomprehensive (7-10, 0-2). Agility — Swift (7-10). Sprinting — Olympian (7-10). Blunt — Tavern Brawler, Bouncer, Martial, Battering Ram (4-10, 7-10, 6-10, 7-10). Hunting — Pro Gun (6-10). Building — Grunt, Fast Worker, Slow Worker, Quick Worker (5-10, 8-10, 0-3, 8-10). Cooking — Gourmand, Natural, Ascetic (9-10, 4-10, 0-2). Foraging — Vagabond, Graverobber, Antique, Wildsman (5-10, 8-10, 10, 6-10). Repair — Scrapper (5-10). Mechanics — Tinkerer, Generator (4-10, 0-3). Body — Gymgoer, Second Wind (7-10, 9-10). Endurance — Indefatigable, Hardy (9-10, 6-10). Health — Thick Blood, Albino, Anemic, Glass Body (7-10, 0-2, 0-2, 0-2). Courage — Paranoia, Fearful, Action Hero (0-3, 0-2, 9-10). Compulsion — Drinker (0-4). Driving — Expert Driver, Motion Sickness (7-10, 0-2). Hands — Butterfingers (0-3). Stomach — Bad Teeth (0-3). Sleep — Restful Sleeper (7-10). Axes — No XP Axe (0-3). Medic — No XP First Aid (0-3). Learning — Ingenuitive (9-10). For Modders Want to make your own evolutive traits? Study this addon as a working example of every extension point of the Traits As Skills framework, and read the framework documentation (English and Spanish) at: github.com/GersonRess/TAS_Docs Every extension point used here: Registering new spectra (TAS.Spectrum.register). Adding bands to existing spectra (TAS.Spectrum.addBand). Declaring XP actions (TAS.XP.actions) and custom passives (TAS.XP.registerPassive). Server-side kill classification by weapon category. Requirements Traits As Skills (base framework mod). More Traits (ToadTraits). Project Zomboid 42.20+. Incompatible with the "More Traits - Dynamic" submod — its kill-tracking conflicts with this addon. Technical Info Mod ID: TraitsAsSkills_MoreTraits Feedback & Bug Reports: Issues in the addon itself can be reported in the discussions below, but remember — this is a framework example. Balance and trait coverage are intentionally minimal. Learn more about the framework: Traits As Skills Workshop ID: 3786253696 Mod ID: TraitsAsSkills_MoreTraits
